Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Vinayapiṭake

The Vinaya Piṭaka

Cūḷavaggapāḷi

The Pāḷi of the Minor Division

1. Kammakkhandhakaṃ

1. The Section on Formal Acts

1. Tajjanīyakammaṃ

1. The Formal Act of Censure

1. Tena [T 1.0001][P 2.0001][V 0.0001][M 0.0001] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – “mā kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca alamatthatarā ca (syā. ka.). Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā”ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti [V 0.0002] uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā [T 1.0002] kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vakkhanti – ‘mā kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ [M 0.0002] paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattantī”ti.

1. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks were themselves quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, brawlers, and instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha. And approaching those other monks who were quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, brawlers, and instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, they said this: “Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult together on the strong points. By doing so, you will be wiser, more discerning, more learned, and more capable. Do not be afraid of him. We too will be on your side.” Because of this, quarrels that had not arisen arose, and quarrels that had arisen led to greater increase and expansion. Those monks who were of few desires... criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How can the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks, being themselves quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, brawlers, and instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, approach those other monks who are also quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, brawlers, and instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, and say this: ‘Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult together on the strong points. By doing so, you will be wiser, more discerning, more learned, and more capable. Do not be afraid of him. We too will be on your side’? Because of this, quarrels that had not arisen now arise, and those that had arisen lead to greater increase and expansion.”

2. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā [P 2.0002] bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – ‘mā kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [T 1.0003] buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ moghapurisānaṃ ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vakkhanti – ‘mā kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti? Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya. Atha khvetaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānañceva appasādāya pasannānañca ekaccānaṃ aññathattāyā”ti.

2. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having caused the community of monks to assemble, questioned the monks: 'Is it true, as is said, monks, that the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks are themselves quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, brawlers, and instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, and that having approached whatever other monks are also quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, brawlers, and instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, they speak thus: “Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult together on the strong points. By doing so, you will be wiser, more discerning, more learned, and more capable. Do not be afraid of him. We too will be on your side.” And because of that, quarrels that have not yet arisen do arise, and quarrels that have arisen lead to increase and expansion?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: 'Monks, for those foolish men, this is unsuitable, improper, unbecoming, not the conduct of a recluse, unallowable, and not to be done. How indeed, monks, could those foolish men, being themselves quarrelsome... instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, having approached whatever other monks are also quarrelsome... instigators of legal questions in the Saṅgha, speak thus: “Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult together on the strong points. By doing so, you will be wiser, more discerning, more learned, and more capable. Do not be afraid of him. We too will be on your side”? Because of that, quarrels that have not yet arisen do arise, and quarrels that have arisen lead to increase and expansion. This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of the unconvinced or to the increase of the convinced. But rather, monks, this leads to the lack of confidence of the unconvinced and to the alteration of some of the convinced.'

Atha kho bhagavā te paṇḍukalohitake (syā.) bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya dupposatāya mahicchatāya [V 0.0003] asantuṭṭhitāya asantuṭṭhatāya (syā.), asantuṭṭhiyā (sī.) saṅgaṇikāya kosajjassa [M 0.0003] avaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā anekapariyāyena subharatāya suposatāya appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa viriyārambhassa (sī.), vīriyārabbhassa (ka.) vaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā bhikkhūnaṃ tadanucchavikaṃ tadanulomikaṃ [T 1.0004] dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karotu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū codetabbā, codetvā sāretabbā, sāretvā āpattiṃ āpatti (sī. syā.) āropetabbā, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those monks in many ways, spoke in dispraise of being difficult to support, difficult to maintain, of having great desire, of being discontented, of delighting in company, and of laziness. In many ways, he spoke in praise of being easy to support, easy to maintain, of having few desires, of being easily contented, of the effacement of defilements, of shaking off defilements, of being inspiring, of the non-accumulation of defilements, and of exerting effort. Having given the monks a talk on the Dhamma that was suitable and appropriate for them, he addressed the monks: 'Well then, monks, let the Saṅgha perform the act of censure on the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks. And this, monks, is how it should be done. First, the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks should be reproached; having reproached them, they should be reminded; having reminded them, they should be charged with an offense; having charged them with an offense, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

3. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – ‘mā [T 1.0005] kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Esā ñatti.

3. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These monks, Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka, are themselves makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, makers of arguments, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha. And whatever other monks are makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, makers of arguments, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha, they approach them and say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult on strengths and weaknesses. By that, you are wiser, more competent, more learned, and more capable than him. And do not be afraid of him. We too will be of your faction.’ Because of this, quarrels that have not yet arisen do arise, and quarrels that have arisen lead to increase and proliferation. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – ‘mā kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0004] tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These monks, Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka, are themselves makers of quarrels... and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha. And whatever other monks are makers of quarrels... and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha, they approach them and say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult on strengths and weaknesses. By that, you are wiser, more competent, more learned, and more capable than him. And do not be afraid of him. We too will be of your faction.’ Because of this, quarrels that have not yet arisen do arise, and quarrels that have arisen lead to increase and proliferation. The Saṅgha is performing the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka. Let him to whom the performance of the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka is agreeable be silent; let him to whom it is not agreeable speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – ‘mā kho tumhe[V 0.0004], āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For a second time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These monks, Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka, are themselves makers of quarrels... and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha. And whatever other monks are makers of quarrels... and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha, they approach them and say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult on strengths and weaknesses. By that, you are wiser, more competent, more learned, and more capable than him. And do not be afraid of him. We too will be of your faction.’ Because of this, quarrels that have not yet arisen do arise, and quarrels that have arisen lead to increase and proliferation. The Saṅgha is performing the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka. Let him to whom the performance of the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka is agreeable be silent; let him to whom it is not agreeable speak.

“Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho[T 1.0006]. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā, yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – ‘mā kho tumhe, āyasmanto, eso ajesi. Balavābalavaṃ paṭimantetha. Tumhe tena paṇḍitatarā ca byattatarā ca bahussutatarā ca alamattatarā ca. Mā cassa bhāyittha. Mayampi tumhākaṃ pakkhā bhavissāmā’ti. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For a third time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These monks, Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka, are themselves makers of quarrels... and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha. And whatever other monks are makers of quarrels... and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha, they approach them and say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, do not let this one defeat you. Consult on strengths and weaknesses. By that, you are wiser, more competent, more learned, and more capable than him. And do not be afraid of him. We too will be of your faction.’ Because of this, quarrels that have not yet arisen do arise, and quarrels that have arisen lead to increase and proliferation. The Saṅgha is performing the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka. Let him to whom the performance of the act of censure on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka is agreeable be silent; let him to whom it is not agreeable speak.

“Kataṃ saṅghena paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The act of censure has been performed by the Saṅgha on the monks Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelve Unlawful Acts

4. “Tīhi[P 2.0003][M 0.0005], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca adhammakammañceva (syā.) hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

4. Monks, an act of censure endowed with three factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled. It is carried out in absence; it is carried out without questioning; it is carried out without an admission. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ [T 1.0007] hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled. It is carried out for no offense; it is carried out for an offense not expiable by confession; it is carried out for an offense that has already been confessed. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi[V 0.0005], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled. It is carried out without having admonished; it is carried out without having reminded; it is carried out without having charged him with an offense. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done in the absence [of the accused], it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done without having questioned, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Appaṭiññāya kataṃ [T 1.0008] hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done without a confession, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0006], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done for a non-offense, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done for an offense not cleared by confession, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi[V 0.0006], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done for a confessed offense, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Acodetvā kataṃ [T 1.0009] hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done without having made an accusation, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asāretvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done without having reminded, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave[M 0.0007], tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done without having charged with an offense, it is done unlawfully, it is done by an incomplete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is badly settled.

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The twelvefold section on acts not in accordance with the Dhamma is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The twelvefold section on acts in accordance with the Dhamma.

5. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

5. Monks, an act of censure endowed with three factors is an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled. It is done in the presence [of the monk], it is done after questioning, it is done upon his admission. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca [T 1.0010] hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti[V 0.0007], adesitāya [P 2.0004] āpattiyā kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled. It is done for an offense, it is done for an offense that is to be confessed, it is done for an offense that has not been confessed. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled. It is done after making an accusation, it is done after reminding, it is done after charging with an offense. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled. It is done in the presence [of the monk], it is done lawfully, it is done by a complete assembly. Monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is indeed an act in accordance with the Dhamma, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done after questioning, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0008], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca [T 1.0011] hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done upon acknowledgement, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done for an offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena [V 0.0008] kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done for an offense that is to be confessed, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done for an unconfessed offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca [T 1.0012] hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done after accusation, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done after reminding, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi [M 0.0009] samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of censure endowed with three other factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased. It is done after charging with an offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a unified Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, an act of censure endowed with these three factors is a lawful action, a disciplinary action, and is well-appeased.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The twelve lawful acts are concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ

The Sextet on Wishing.

6. pari. 323 “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi [V 0.0009] gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno[T 1.0013], ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

6. Monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against a monk endowed with three factors. He is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, garrulous, and an instigator of disputes in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, full of offenses, and limitless in offenses; he lives associated with householders in ways that are unsuitable. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against a monk endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against a monk endowed with three other factors. With regard to higher morality, he is corrupt in virtue; with regard to transgression, he is corrupt in conduct; with regard to wrong view, he is corrupt in view. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against a monk endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against a monk endowed with three other factors. He speaks in disparagement of the Buddha, he speaks in disparagement of the Dhamma, he speaks in disparagement of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against a monk endowed with these three factors.

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against three monks. One is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, garrulous, and an instigator of disputes in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, full of offenses, and limitless in offenses; one lives associated with householders in ways that are unsuitable. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out an act of censure against these three monks.

“Aparesampi[M 0.0010], bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ [T 1.0014] kareyya.

Monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may also carry out the act of censure on another three monks. One is corrupt in virtue with respect to higher virtue; one is corrupt in conduct with respect to excessive conduct; one is corrupt in view with respect to excessive views. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out the act of censure on these three monks.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya[P 2.0005]. Eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may also carry out the act of censure on another three monks. One speaks in disparagement of the Buddha, one speaks in disparagement of the Dhamma, and one speaks in disparagement of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, should it wish, may carry out the act of censure on these three monks.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Six on ‘Should it Wish’ is concluded.

Aṭṭhārasavattaṃ

The Eighteen Duties

7. “Tajjanīyakammakatena[V 0.0010], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sammati (syā.) sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi na bhikkhū bhikkhūhi (syā.) sampayojetabba”nti.

7. Monks, a monk on whom the act of censure has been carried out should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct: he should not give the higher ordination; he should not give dependence; he should not have a novice attend on him; he should not consent to an appointment as an exhorter of nuns; even when appointed, he should not exhort the nuns. The offense for which the Saṅgha has carried out the act of censure should not be committed, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is worse. The act should not be criticized; those who carried out the act should not be criticized. The Uposatha of a monk in good standing should not be suspended, nor the Pavāraṇā. He should not make it a matter for admonishment, he should not institute a legal complaint, he should not cause permission (to speak) to be requested, he should not accuse, he should not remind (of a fault), and he should not incite the monks against one another.

Tajjanīyakamme aṭṭhārasavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighteen duties regarding the act of censure are concluded.

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The Eighteen Cases in Which the Act Should Not Be Revoked

8. Atha kho saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ akāsi[T 1.0015]. Te saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā sammā vattanti, lomaṃ pātenti[M 0.0011], netthāraṃ vattanti, bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – “mayaṃ, āvuso, saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā sammā vattāma, lomaṃ pātema, netthāraṃ vattāma, kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe…. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

8. Then the Saṅgha carried out the act of censure against the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks. Those monks, on whom the Saṅgha had carried out the act of censure, conducted themselves properly, humbled themselves, and practiced for their rehabilitation. They approached the monks and said: ‘Venerable sirs, we, on whom the Saṅgha has carried out the act of censure, are conducting ourselves properly, are humbling ourselves, and are practicing for our rehabilitation. How then should we conduct ourselves?’ The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha revoke the act of censure for the Paṇḍukalohitaka monks.’

Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Monks, for a monk endowed with five factors, the act of censure should not be revoked. He gives the higher ordination, he gives dependence, he has a novice attend on him, he consents to an appointment as an exhorter of nuns, and even when appointed, he exhorts the nuns. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of censure should not be revoked.

pari. 420 “Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of censure should not be revoked. He commits the offense for which the Saṅgha carried out the act of censure, or another of a similar nature, or one that is worse; he censures the act, and he censures those who carried it out. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of censure should not be revoked.

“Aṭṭhahi[V 0.0011], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ [P 2.0006] nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, okāsaṃ [T 1.0016] kāreti, codeti, sāreti, bhikkhūhi sampayojeti bhikkhū bhikkhūhi sampayojeti (syā.) – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Monks, for a monk endowed with eight factors, the act of censure should not be revoked. He suspends the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, he suspends the Pavāraṇā, he makes it a matter for admonishment, he institutes a legal complaint, he causes permission (to speak) to be requested, he accuses, he reminds (of a fault), and he incites the monks against one another. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these eight factors, the act of censure should not be revoked.

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on the Eighteen Cases in Which the Act Should Not Be Revoked is concluded.

Paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The Eighteen Cases in Which the Act Should Be Revoked

9. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

9. Monks, for a monk endowed with five factors, the act of censure should be revoked. He does not give the higher ordination, he does not give dependence, he does not have a novice attend on him, he does not consent to an appointment as an exhorter of nuns, and even when appointed, he does not exhort the nuns. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of censure should be revoked.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0012], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of censure should be revoked. He does not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha carried out the act of censure, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is worse; he does not censure the act, nor does he censure those who carried it out. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of censure should be revoked.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Monks, for a monk endowed with eight factors, the act of censure should be revoked.

Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno[T 1.0017], tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

He does not suspend the Uposatha of a monk in good standing; he does not suspend the Pavāraṇā; he does not make it a matter for admonishment; he does not institute a legal complaint; he does not cause permission (to speak) to be requested; he does not accuse; he does not remind (of a fault); he does not incite the monks against one another. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these eight factors, the act of censure should be revoked.

Paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on the Eighteen Cases in Which the Act Should Be Revoked is concluded.

10. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tehi, bhikkhave, paṇḍukalohitakehi bhikkhūhi saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘mayaṃ, bhante, saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā [V 0.0012] sammā vattāma, lomaṃ pātema, netthāraṃ vattāma, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācāmā’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

10. And, monks, it should be revoked in this way. Monks, those Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks should approach the Saṅgha, arrange their upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit in a squatting position, raise their joined palms, and speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, we, upon whom the Saṅgha has imposed the act of censure, are conducting ourselves well, we are casting down our pride, we are practicing the conduct that leads to release; we ask for the revocation of the act of censure.’ It should be asked for a second time. It should be asked for a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā sammā vattanti, lomaṃ pātenti, netthāraṃ vattanti[P 2.0007], tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācanti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks, upon whom the Saṅgha has imposed the act of censure, are conducting themselves well, they are casting down their pride, they are practicing the conduct that leads to release, and they ask for the revocation of the act of censure. If the time is suitable for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should revoke the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā sammā vattanti, lomaṃ pātenti, netthāraṃ vattanti, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācanti. Saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks, upon whom the Saṅgha has imposed the act of censure, are conducting themselves well, they are casting down their pride, they are practicing the conduct that leads to release, and they ask for the revocation of the act of censure. The Saṅgha revokes the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks. If the revocation of the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent; if it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi [M 0.0013] etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me[T 1.0018], bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā sammā vattanti, lomaṃ pātenti, netthāraṃ vattanti, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācanti. Saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

A second time I declare this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks, upon whom the Saṅgha has imposed the act of censure, are conducting themselves well, they are casting down their pride, they are practicing the conduct that leads to release, and they ask for the revocation of the act of censure. The Saṅgha revokes the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks. If the revocation of the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent; if it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime paṇḍukalohitakā bhikkhū saṅghena tajjanīyakammakatā sammā vattanti, lomaṃ pātenti, netthāraṃ vattanti, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācanti. Saṅgho paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

A third time I declare this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks, upon whom the Saṅgha has imposed the act of censure, are conducting themselves well, they are casting down their pride, they are practicing the conduct that leads to release, and they ask for the revocation of the act of censure. The Saṅgha revokes the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks. If the revocation of the act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent; if it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ saṅghena paṇḍukalohitakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa,

The act of censure for the Paṇḍuka and Lohitaka monks has been revoked by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha,

Tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Therefore, there is silence. Thus I hold it.

Tajjanīyakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first act of censure is completed.

2. Niyassakammaṃ

2. The Act of Dependence

11. Tena [V 0.0013] kho pana samayena āyasmā seyyasako bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi; apissu bhikkhū pakatā pakatattā (sī. syā.) parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā seyyasako bālo bhavissati abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharissati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi[T 1.0019]; apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

11. At that time, the Venerable Seyyasaka was foolish, inept, had many offenses, and was without interval between offenses. He lived in association with householders, with an association unsuitable for monks. Moreover, the monks were constantly occupied with giving him probation, subjecting him to reversion to the root, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him. Those monks who were of few wishes…pe… criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Seyyasaka be foolish, inept, have many offenses, and be without interval between offenses? How could he live in association with householders, with an association unsuitable for monks? And how could the monks be constantly occupied with giving him probation, subjecting him to reversion to the root, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha [M 0.0014] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, seyyasako bhikkhu bālo abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi; apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, tassa moghapurisassa ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso bālo bhavissati abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharissati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi; apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho seyyasakassa [P 2.0008] bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ niyasakammaṃ (ka.) karotu – nissāya te vatthabbanti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo āpatti āropetabbā (sī. syā.), āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā [T 1.0020] paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assembled, questioned the bhikkhus: 'Is it true, bhikkhus, as is said, that the bhikkhu Seyyasaka is foolish, inept, has many offenses, and is without interval between offenses; that he lives associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders; and that the bhikkhus are constantly occupied with giving him probation, subjecting him to reversion to the root, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: 'Bhikkhus, for that worthless man, this is unsuitable, unbecoming, inappropriate, not befitting a recluse, improper, not to be done. How indeed could that worthless man, bhikkhus, be foolish, inept, have many offenses, and be without interval between offenses; live associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders; and the bhikkhus be constantly occupied with giving him probation, subjecting him to reversion to the root, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of those who lack it... Having rebuked him... he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the bhikkhus: 'Well then, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha carry out the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka—"You are to live in dependence." And this, bhikkhus, is how it should be done. First, the bhikkhu Seyyasaka should be accused; having been accused, he should be reminded; having been reminded, the offense should be placed upon him; having placed the offense upon him, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhu—'

12. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu bālo abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi; apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ kareyya – nissāya te vatthabbanti. Esā ñatti.

12. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Seyyasaka is foolish, incompetent, has numerous offenses, and is indiscriminate in his offenses; he lives associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders; and the bhikkhus are constantly occupied with giving him probation, sending him back to the beginning, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should carry out the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka, saying: ‘You are to live in dependence.’ This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [V 0.0014] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu bālo abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi; apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā. Saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ karoti – nissāya te vatthabbanti. Yassāyasmato khamati seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – nissāya te vatthabbanti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Seyyasaka is foolish, incompetent, has numerous offenses, and is indiscriminate in his offenses; he lives associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders; and the bhikkhus are constantly occupied with giving him probation, sending him back to the beginning, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him. The Saṅgha is carrying out the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka, saying: ‘You are to live in dependence.’ To whichever venerable one the carrying out of the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka, saying: ‘You are to live in dependence,’ is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi [M 0.0015] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu bālo abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi; apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā mūlāya paṭikassantā mānattaṃ dentā abbhentā. Saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ karoti – nissāya te vatthabbanti. Yassāyasmato khamati seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassassa kammassa [T 1.0021] karaṇaṃ – nissāya te vatthabbanti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

A second time I speak on this matter… A third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Seyyasaka is foolish, incompetent, has numerous offenses, and is indiscriminate in his offenses; he lives associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders; and the bhikkhus are constantly occupied with giving him probation, sending him back to the beginning, giving him penance, and rehabilitating him. The Saṅgha is carrying out the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka, saying: ‘You are to live in dependence.’ To whichever venerable one the carrying out of the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka, saying: ‘You are to live in dependence,’ is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Kataṃ saṅghena seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ – nissāya te vatthabbanti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka has been carried out by the Saṅgha, saying: ‘You are to live in dependence.’ It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelve Unlawful Acts

13. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

13. Bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is carried out in the absence of the bhikkhu, it is carried out without questioning him, and it is carried out without his acknowledgment. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with three other factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is carried out for a non-offense; it is carried out for an offense that is not expiated by confession; it is carried out for an offense that has already been confessed. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā [V 0.0015] kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca [T 1.0022] hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with three other factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is carried out without having accused, it is carried out without having reminded, and it is carried out without having charged him with an offense. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out in the absence of the bhikkhu, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi[M 0.0016], bhikkhave…pe… appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out without questioning him, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out without his acknowledgment, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe…[T 1.0023].

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out for a non-offense, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out for an offense that is not expiated by confession, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out for an offense that has already been confessed, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out without having accused, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… asāretvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe…[T 1.0024].

Furthermore, bhikkhus… it is carried out without having reminded, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena [V 0.0016] kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with three other factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is carried out without having charged him with an offense, it is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The twelvefold section on unlawful acts is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelve Lawful Acts

14. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

14. Bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Discipline, and is well-settled. It is carried out in the presence of the bhikkhu, it is carried out after questioning him, and it is carried out upon his acknowledgment. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of dependence endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Discipline, and is well-settled.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0017], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, an act of subordination endowed with three other factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well-settled. It is done for an offense, it is done for an offense requiring confession, it is done for an unconfessed offense—indeed, bhikkhus, an act of subordination endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well-settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti [T 1.0025] – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, an act of subordination endowed with three other factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well-settled. It is done after accusing, it is done after causing one to remember, it is done after charging with an offense—indeed, bhikkhus, an act of subordination endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well-settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done in the presence, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors, …

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done upon questioning, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done upon acknowledgment, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi[V 0.0017], bhikkhave…pe… āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe…[T 1.0026].

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done for an offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done for an offense requiring confession, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done for an unconfessed offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done after accusing, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe…[T 1.0027].

Furthermore, bhikkhus, … it is done after reminding, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors…

“Aparehipi[M 0.0018], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ niyassakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, an act of subordination endowed with three other factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well-settled. It is done after charging with an offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, it is done by a united Saṅgha—indeed, bhikkhus, an act of subordination endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well-settled.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on Twelve Lawful Acts is concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ

The Hexad on Wishing

15. pari. 323 “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya.

15. Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma for a bhikkhu who is endowed with three factors. He is one who creates quarrels, one who creates strife, one who is contentious, one who is talkative, and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is without limit in his offenses; he dwells associating with householders through improper associations with householders. Indeed, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma for a bhikkhu who is endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ [V 0.0018] kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should also carry out the niyassakamma for a bhikkhu who is endowed with three other factors. He is corrupt in higher virtue; he is corrupt in conduct through transgression; he is corrupt in view through extreme views. Indeed, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma for a bhikkhu who is endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno [T 1.0028] saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should also carry out the niyassakamma for a bhikkhu who is endowed with three other factors. He speaks in dispraise of the Buddha; he speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma; he speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma for a bhikkhu who is endowed with these three factors.

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti, abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi [M 0.0019] gihisaṃsaggehi – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma for three bhikkhus. One is a creator of quarrels, a creator of strife, contentious, talkative, and a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is without limit in his offenses; one dwells associating with householders through improper associations with householders. Indeed, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma for these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, for three other bhikkhus also, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma. One is corrupt in higher virtue; one is corrupt in conduct through transgression; and one is corrupt in view through extreme views. Indeed, bhikkhus, for these three bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya. Eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, niyassakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, for three other bhikkhus also, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma. One speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, one speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, and one speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, bhikkhus, for these three bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out the niyassakamma.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ākaṅkhamānachakka is concluded.

Aṭṭhārasavattaṃ

The Eighteen Duties

16. “Niyassakammakatena[T 1.0029], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā [V 0.0019] saṅghena niyassakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kārāpetabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti.

16. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu on whom the act of dependence has been performed should conduct himself properly. Herein is the proper conduct: He should not give higher ordination; he should not grant dependence; he should not have a novice attend on him; he should not consent to an appointment as an exhorter of bhikkhunīs; even if appointed, he should not exhort the bhikkhunīs. He should not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha performed the act of dependence, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is worse than that. The formal act should not be criticized, nor should the performers of the act be criticized. He should not stop the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, nor the Pavāraṇā. He should not make an admonition, he should not initiate a dispute, he should not ask for an opportunity to speak, he should not reprove, he should not remind, and he should not engage in disputes with the bhikkhus.

Niyassakamme aṭṭhārasavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighteen Duties concerning the act of dependence are concluded.

17. Atha kho saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ akāsi – nissāya te vatthabbanti. So saṅghena niyassakammakato kalyāṇamitte [M 0.0020] sevamāno bhajamāno payirupāsamāno uddisāpento paripucchanto bahussuto hoti, āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti – “ahaṃ, āvuso, saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe…. “Tena [T 1.0030] hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

17. Then the Saṅgha performed the act of dependence on the bhikkhu Seyyasaka, saying: 'You must dwell in dependence.' Having been subjected to the act of dependence by the Saṅgha, associating with good friends, keeping company with them, and attending upon them, having the Pāḷi taught and having the commentary questioned, he became learned, a master of the traditions, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikās, wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training. He conducted himself properly, he cast off his pride, he practiced the conduct for release. Approaching the bhikkhus, he said: 'Venerable sirs, having been subjected to the act of dependence by the Saṅgha, I am conducting myself properly, I am casting off my pride, I am practicing the conduct for release. How now should I proceed?' The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… and so on… 'Well then, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha revoke the act of dependence for the bhikkhu Seyyasaka.'

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The Eighteen Cases Where It Should Not Be Revoked.

18. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

18. Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, the act of dependence should not be revoked. He gives higher ordination, he gives dependence, he has a novice attend on him, he consents to the appointment as an instructor of bhikkhunīs, and having been appointed, he instructs bhikkhunīs. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of dependence should not be revoked.

pari. 420 “Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena niyassakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors, the act of dependence should not be revoked. He commits the offense for which the Saṅgha performed the act of dependence, or he commits another similar offense, or one that is worse than that; he disparages the act, he disparages those who performed the act. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of dependence should not be revoked.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.
