Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti[V 0.0020], okāsaṃ kāreti, codeti, sāreti, bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with eight factors, the act of dependence should not be revoked. He suspends the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, he suspends the Pavāraṇā, he makes an admonition, he initiates a dispute, he asks for an opportunity to speak, he reproves, he reminds, and he engages in disputes with the bhikkhus. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these eight factors, the act of dependence should not be revoked.

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighteen Cases Where It Should Not Be Revoked are concluded.

Paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The Eighteen Cases Where It Should Be Revoked.

19. “Pañcahi[M 0.0021], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ[T 1.0031]. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

19. Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, the act of dependence should be revoked. He does not give higher ordination, he does not give dependence, he does not have a novice attend on him, he does not consent to an appointment as an exhorter of bhikkhunīs, and even when appointed, he does not exhort the bhikkhunīs. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of dependence should be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena niyassakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors, the act of dependence should be revoked. He does not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha performed the act of dependence, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is worse than that; he does not disparage the act, nor does he disparage those who performed the act. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of dependence should be revoked.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with eight factors, the act of dependence should be revoked.

Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ [P 2.0009] paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

He does not suspend the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, he does not suspend the Pavāraṇā, he does not make an admonition, he does not initiate a dispute, he does not ask for an opportunity to speak, he does not reprove, he does not remind, and he does not engage in disputes with the bhikkhus. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these eight factors, the act of dependence should be revoked.

Paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighteen Cases Where It Should Be Revoked are concluded.

20. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tena, bhikkhave, seyyasakena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā[T 1.0032]. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

20. And in this way, bhikkhus, it should be revoked. That bhikkhu Seyyasaka, bhikkhus, should approach the Saṅgha, and having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having paid homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his joined palms, should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I, having been subjected to the act of dependence by the Saṅgha, am conducting myself properly, I am casting off my pride, I am practicing the conduct that leads to release, and I request the revocation of the act of dependence.’ It should be requested a second time. It should be requested a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0021] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Seyyasaka, having been subjected to the niyassakamma by the Saṅgha, is conducting himself properly, is letting his conceit fall, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and requests the revocation of the niyassakamma. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should revoke the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0022] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Seyyasaka, having been subjected to the niyassakamma by the Saṅgha, is conducting himself properly, is letting his conceit fall, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and requests the revocation of the niyassakamma. The Saṅgha revokes the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka. Whichever venerable one approves of the revocation of the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka, he should be silent; whichever one does not approve, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time, I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Seyyasaka, having been subjected to the niyassakamma by the Saṅgha, is conducting himself properly, is letting his conceit fall, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and requests the revocation of the niyassakamma. The Saṅgha revokes the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka. Whichever venerable one approves of the revocation of the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka, he should be silent; whichever one does not approve, he should speak.”

“Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ seyyasako bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato [T 1.0033] khamati seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a third time, I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Seyyasaka, having been subjected to the niyassakamma by the Saṅgha, is conducting himself properly, is letting his conceit fall, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and requests the revocation of the niyassakamma. The Saṅgha revokes the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka. Whichever venerable one approves of the revocation of the niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka, he should be silent; whichever one does not approve, he should speak.”

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ saṅghena seyyasakassa bhikkhuno niyassakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The niyassakamma for the monk Seyyasaka has been revoked by the Saṅgha. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent; thus I hold it.”

Niyassakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second niyassakamma is concluded.

3. Pabbājanīyakammaṃ

3. The Act of Banishment

21. idaṃ vatthu pārā. 431 ādayo Tena kho pana samayena assajipunabbasukā nāma nāma bhikkhū (ka.) kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāsikā honti alajjino pāpabhikkhū. Te cūḷava. 292 ādayo evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācaranti – mālāvacchaṃ ropentipi ropāpentipi, siñcantipi siñcāpentipi, ocinantipi ocināpentipi, ganthentipi ganthāpentipi[V 0.0022], ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karontipi [M 0.0023] kārāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, mañjarikaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, vidhūtikaṃ vidhutikaṃ (syā.) karontipi kārāpentipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, āveḷaṃ karontipi [P 2.0010] kārāpentipi, uracchadaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi. Te kulitthīnaṃ kuladhītānaṃ kulakumārīnaṃ kulasuṇhānaṃ kuladāsīnaṃ ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, mañjarikaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, vidhūtikaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, āveḷaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, uracchadaṃ harantipi harāpentipi. Te kulitthīhi kuladhītāhi kulakumārīhi kulasuṇhāhi kuladāsīhi saddhiṃ ekabhājanepi bhuñjanti, ekathālakepi [T 1.0034] pivanti, ekāsanepi nisīdanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, vikālepi bhuñjanti, majjampi pivanti, mālāgandhavilepanampi dhārenti, naccantipi, gāyantipi, vādentipi, lāsentipi; naccantiyāpi naccanti, naccantiyāpi gāyanti, naccantiyāpi vādenti, naccantiyāpi lāsenti; gāyantiyāpi naccanti, gāyantiyāpi gāyanti, gāyantiyāpi vādenti, gāyantiyāpi lāsenti; vādentiyāpi naccanti, vādentiyāpi gāyanti, vādentiyāpi vādenti, vādentiyāpi lāsenti; lāsentiyāpi naccanti, lāsentiyāpi gāyanti, lāsentiyāpi vādenti, lāsentiyāpi lāsenti; aṭṭhapadepi kīḷanti, dasapadepi kīḷanti, ākāsepi kīḷanti, parihārapathepi kīḷanti, santikāyapi kīḷanti, khalikāyapi kīḷanti, ghaṭikāyapi kīḷanti, salākahatthenapi kīḷanti, akkhenapi kīḷanti, paṅgacīrenapi kīḷanti, vaṅkakenapi kīḷanti, mokkhacikāyapi kīḷanti, ciṅgulakenapi kīḷanti, pattāḷhakenapi kīḷanti, rathakenapi kīḷanti, dhanukenapi kīḷanti, akkharikāyapi kīḷanti, manesikāyapi kīḷanti, yathāvajjenapi kīḷanti; hatthismimpi sikkhanti, assasmimpi sikkhanti, rathasmimpi sikkhanti, dhanusmimpi sikkhanti, tharusmimpi sikkhanti; hatthissapi purato dhāvanti, assassapi purato dhāvanti, rathassapi purato purato dhāvanti (syā.) dhāvantipi ādhāvantipi; usseḷentipi, apphoṭentipi[T 1.0035], nibbujjhantipi, muṭṭhīhipi yujjhanti; raṅgamajjhepi saṅghāṭiṃ pattharitvā naccakiṃ naccantiṃ (sī. syā.) evaṃ vadanti – “idha, bhagini, naccassū”ti; nalāṭikampi denti; vividhampi anācāraṃ ācaranti.

21. Now at that time, monks named Assaji and Punabbasu were residing at Kīṭāgiri—shameless, wicked monks. They engaged in such improper conduct as this: they planted flower saplings and had them planted; they watered them and had them watered; they picked them and had them picked; they strung them and had them strung; they made garlands with stems on one side and had them made; they made garlands with stems on both sides and had them made; they made flower clusters and had them made; they made flower bracelets and had them made; they made head-ornaments and had them made; they made ear-ornaments and had them made; they made chest-garlands and had them made. For women of good families, daughters of good families, maidens of good families, daughters-in-law of good families, and female slaves of good families, they delivered garlands with stems on one side and had them delivered; they delivered garlands with stems on both sides and had them delivered; they delivered flower clusters and had them delivered; they delivered flower bracelets and had them delivered; they delivered head-ornaments and had them delivered; they delivered ear-ornaments and had them delivered; they delivered chest-garlands and had them delivered. Together with women of good families, daughters of good families, maidens of good families, daughters-in-law of good families, and female slaves of good families, they ate from the same bowl, drank from the same cup, sat on the same seat, lay down on the same couch, lay down on the same floor-covering, lay down with the same blanket, and lay down with the same floor-covering and blanket. They ate at the wrong time; they drank intoxicants; they wore garlands, perfumes, and unguents. They danced, sang, played musical instruments, and made graceful gestures. They danced, sang, played musical instruments, and made graceful gestures along with a dancing woman; they danced, sang, played musical instruments, and made graceful gestures along with a singing woman; they danced, sang, played musical instruments, and made graceful gestures along with a woman playing musical instruments; and they danced, sang, played musical instruments, and made graceful gestures along with a woman making graceful gestures. They played games on an eight-row board; they played games on a ten-row board; they played a board game in the air; they played a game of circling paths; they played by flicking pebbles; they played dice on a board; they played tip-cat; they played a game of hand-slapping to make figures appear; they played with marbles; they played by blowing on pipes made of leaves; they played with a toy plough; they played by turning somersaults; they played with a palm-leaf pinwheel; they played with toy measures; they played with a toy chariot; they played with a toy bow; they played a game of guessing letters; they played a game of guessing thoughts; and they played by mimicking the deformed. They trained in the art of elephants, the art of horses, the art of chariots, the art of the bow, and the art of the sword. They ran in front of an elephant, they ran in front of a horse, they ran in front of a chariot, and they ran towards them. They shouted challenges, clapped their hands, wrestled, and fought with their fists. In the middle of an arena, they spread out their double-layered robe and said to a dancing girl, ‘Sister, dance here.’ They also snapped their fingers in applause. They engaged in various kinds of improper conduct.

22. Tena [M 0.0024] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu kāsīsu vassaṃvuṭṭho vassaṃvuttho (sī. syā.) sāvatthiṃ gacchanto bhagavantaṃ dassanāya yena kīṭāgiri tadavasari. Atha kho so bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kīṭāgiriṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena [V 0.0023] ālokitena vilokitena samiñjitena sammiñjitena (sī. syā. kaṃ.) pasāritena, okkhittacakkhu iriyāpathasampanno. Manussā taṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā evamāhaṃsu – “kvāyaṃ abalabalo [P 2.0011] viya mandamando viya bhākuṭikabhākuṭiko viya? Ko imassa upagatassa piṇḍakampi dassati? Amhākaṃ pana ayyā assajipunabbasukā saṇhā sakhilā sukhasambhāsā mihitapubbaṅgamā ehisvāgatavādino abbhākuṭikā uttānamukhā pubbabhāsino. Tesaṃ kho nāma piṇḍo dātabbo”ti.

22. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu who had spent the rains in the Kāsī country, while traveling to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One, arrived at Kīṭāgiri. Then that bhikkhu, having put on his lower robe in the morning and taken his bowl and outer robe, entered Kīṭāgiri for alms-food, inspiring confidence in his going forward and returning, in his looking ahead and looking aside, in his bending and stretching, with downcast eyes and endowed with proper deportment. When the people saw that bhikkhu, they said: “Who is this, as if exceedingly feeble, as if exceedingly sluggish, as if constantly frowning? Who will give even alms-food to this one who has approached? But our venerable ones, Assaji and Punabbasu, are gentle, amiable, easy to converse with, preceded by a smile, accustomed to saying ‘Come! Welcome!’, free from frowning, with open faces, and accustomed to speaking first. To them, indeed, alms-food should be given.”

Addasā kho aññataro upāsako taṃ bhikkhuṃ kīṭāgirismiṃ piṇḍāya carantaṃ; disvāna yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ abhivādetvā etadavoca – “api, bhante, piṇḍo labbhatī”ti? “Na kho, āvuso, piṇḍo labbhatī”ti. “Ehi, bhante, gharaṃ gamissāmā”ti. Atha kho so upāsako taṃ bhikkhuṃ gharaṃ netvā bhojetvā etadavoca – “kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo gamissatī”ti? “Sāvatthiṃ [T 1.0036] kho ahaṃ, āvuso, gamissāmi bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vanda, evañca vadehi – ‘duṭṭho, bhante, kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāso. Assajipunabbasukā nāma kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāsikā alajjino pāpabhikkhū. Te evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācaranti – mālāvacchaṃ ropentipi ropāpentipi, siñcantipi siñcāpentipi, ocinantipi, ocināpentipi, ganthentipi ganthāpentipi, ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, mañjarikaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, vidhūtikaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, āveḷaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, uracchadaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi. Te kulitthīnaṃ kuladhītānaṃ kulakumārīnaṃ kulasuṇhānaṃ kuladāsīnaṃ ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, mañjarikaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, vidhūtikaṃ [M 0.0025] harantipi harāpentipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, āveḷaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, uracchadaṃ harantipi harāpentipi. Te kulitthīhi kuladhītāhi kulakumārīhi kulasuṇhāhi kuladāsīhi saddhiṃ ekabhājanepi bhuñjanti, ekathālakepi pivanti, ekāsanepi nisīdanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, vikālepi bhuñjanti, majjampi pivanti, mālāgandhavilepanampi dhārenti, naccantipi, gāyantipi, vādentipi, lāsentipi; naccantiyāpi [T 1.0037] naccanti, naccantiyāpi gāyanti, naccantiyāpi vādenti, naccantiyāpi lāsenti…pe… (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). Lāsentiyāpi naccanti, lāsentiyāpi gāyanti, lāsentiyāpi vādenti, lāsentiyāpi lāsenti; aṭṭhapadepi kīḷanti, dasapadepi kīḷanti, ākāsepi [V 0.0024] kīḷanti, parihārapathepi kīḷanti, santikāyapi kīḷanti, khalikāyapi kīḷanti, ghaṭikāyapi kīḷanti, salākahatthenapi kīḷanti, akkhenapi kīḷanti, paṅgacīrenapi kīḷanti, vaṅkakenapi kīḷanti, mokkhacikāyapi kīḷanti, ciṅgulakenapi kīḷanti, pattāḷhakenapi kīḷanti, rathakenapi kīḷanti, dhanukenapi kīḷanti, akkharikāyapi kīḷanti, manesikāyapi kīḷanti, yathāvajjenapi kīḷanti; hatthismimpi sikkhanti, assasmimpi sikkhanti, rathasmimpi sikkhanti, dhanusmimpi sikkhanti, tharusmimpi sikkhanti; hatthissapi purato dhāvanti, assassapi purato dhāvanti, rathassapi purato dhāvantipi ādhāvantipi; usseḷentipi, apphoṭentipi, nibbujjhantipi, muṭṭhīhipi yujjhanti; raṅgamajjhepi saṅghāṭiṃ pattharitvā naccakiṃ evaṃ vadanti – ‘idha, bhagini, naccassū’ti; nalāṭikampi denti; vividhampi anācāraṃ ācaranti. Yepi te, bhante, manussā pubbe saddhā ahesuṃ pasannā tepi etarahi assaddhā appasannā. Yānipi tāni saṅghassa pubbe dānapathāni tānipi etarahi upacchinnāni. Riñcanti pesalā bhikkhū[T 1.0038], nivasanti pāpabhikkhū. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā kīṭāgiriṃ bhikkhū pahiṇeyya, yathāyaṃ kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāso saṇṭhaheyyā”ti.

A certain lay follower saw that bhikkhu going for alms in Kīṭāgiri. Having seen him, he approached that bhikkhu, paid homage to him, and said: “Venerable sir, have you received alms-food?” “No, friend, I have not received alms-food.” “Come, venerable sir, let us go to my home.” Then that lay follower took that bhikkhu to his home, fed him, and said: “Where are you going, venerable sir?” “I am going to Sāvatthī, friend, to see the Blessed One.” “Then, venerable sir, in my name, bow your head at the feet of the Blessed One and say: ‘Venerable sir, the monastery at Kīṭāgiri is corrupt. The bhikkhus named Assaji and Punabbasu, residents of Kīṭāgiri, are shameless, wicked bhikkhus. They engage in such improper conduct as follows: they plant small flower plants or have them planted, water them or have them watered, pick them or have them picked, string them into garlands or have them strung, make single-stemmed garlands or have them made, make double-stemmed garlands or have them made, make bouquets or have them made, make flower-bracelets or have them made, make chaplets or have them made, make ear-ornaments or have them made, and make chest-garlands or have them made. For women of good family, daughters of good family, maidens of good family, daughters-in-law of good family, and female slaves of good family, they carry single-stemmed garlands or have them carried; and likewise for double-stemmed garlands, bouquets, flower-bracelets, chaplets, ear-ornaments, and chest-garlands. They eat from the same vessel with women of good family, daughters of good family, maidens of good family, daughters-in-law of good family, and female slaves of good family; they drink from the same cup; they sit on the same seat; they lie on the same couch; they lie on the same bedding; they lie under the same covering; and they lie on the same bedding under the same covering. They eat at the wrong time, drink intoxicants, and wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents. They dance, sing, play music, and make merry. They dance with a dancing woman, sing with a dancing woman, play music with a dancing woman, and make merry with a dancing woman... They dance with a woman making merry, sing with a woman making merry, play music with a woman making merry, and make merry with a woman making merry. They play games on eight-squared boards, on ten-squared boards, a game of dice in the air, a game of hopscotch, a game of jacks, a game of dice on a board, a game of tip-cat, a game of hitting bamboo slips, a game of marbles, a game of blowing through toy pipes made of leaves, a game with toy plows, a game of turning somersaults, a game with toy pinwheels, a game with toy leaf-measures, a game with toy carts, a game with toy bows, a game of guessing letters, a game of guessing thoughts, and a game of mimicking deformities. They train in elephant-craft, horse-craft, chariot-craft, archery, and swordsmanship. They run in front of elephants, run in front of horses, and run in front of chariots, and they run towards them. They shout challenges, slap their arms, wrestle, and box. They spread their outer robes in the middle of an arena and say to a dancing girl, “Dance here, sister!” They give her a forehead-gift. They engage in various kinds of improper conduct. Those people, venerable sir, who were formerly faithful and devoted have now become faithless and without devotion. Those former channels of giving for the Saṅgha have now been cut off. The virtuous bhikkhus leave, while the wicked bhikkhus stay. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would send bhikkhus to Kīṭāgiri so that this monastery at Kīṭāgiri might be well-established.’”

“Evamāvuso”ti kho so bhikkhu tassa upāsakassa paṭissuṇitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena sāvatthi tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha [M 0.0026] kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kaccisi appakilamathena addhānaṃ āgato, kuto ca tvaṃ bhikkhu āgacchasī”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ bhagavā; appakilamathena ca ahaṃ, bhante, addhānaṃ āgato. Idhāhaṃ, bhante, kāsīsu vassaṃvuṭṭho sāvatthiṃ āgacchanto bhagavantaṃ dassanāya yena kīṭāgiri tadavasariṃ. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kīṭāgiriṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Addasā kho maṃ, bhante, aññataro upāsako kīṭāgirismiṃ piṇḍāya carantaṃ[P 2.0012]; disvāna yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā etadavoca – ‘api, bhante, piṇḍo labbhatī’ti. ‘Na kho, āvuso, piṇḍo labbhatī’ti. ‘Ehi, bhante, gharaṃ gamissāmā’ti. Atha kho, bhante, so upāsako maṃ gharaṃ netvā bhojetvā etadavoca – ‘kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo gamissatī’ti? ‘Sāvatthiṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, gamissāmi bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā’ti[T 1.0039]. ‘Tena hi, bhante, mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vanda, evañca vadehi – duṭṭho, bhante, kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāso. Assajipunabbasukā nāma kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāsikā alajjino pāpabhikkhū[V 0.0025]. Te evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācaranti – mālāvacchaṃ ropentipi ropāpentipi…pe… vividhampi anācāraṃ ācaranti. Yepi te, bhante, manussā pubbe saddhā ahesuṃ pasannā tepi etarahi assaddhā appasannā. Yānipi tāni saṅghassa pubbe dānapathāni tānipi etarahi upacchinnāni. Riñcanti pesalā bhikkhū, nivasanti pāpabhikkhū. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā kīṭāgiriṃ bhikkhū pahiṇeyya, yathāyaṃ kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāso saṇṭhaheyyā’ti. Tato ahaṃ bhagavā āgacchāmī”ti.

“Very well, friend,” the monk replied, and rising from his seat, he set out for Sāvatthī. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Sāvatthī, Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Now it is the custom of the Blessed Buddhas to exchange greetings with monks who have arrived. Then the Blessed One said to him: “I hope, monk, you are keeping well, I hope you are comfortable, and I hope you have come on your long journey without much fatigue. From where have you come, monk?” “I am keeping well, Blessed One; I am comfortable, Blessed One. And I have come on my long journey without much fatigue, venerable sir. Here, venerable sir, having spent the rains in Kāsi, I was on my way to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One when I turned aside to Kīṭāgiri. Then, venerable sir, in the morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I entered Kīṭāgiri for alms. A certain lay follower saw me wandering for alms in Kīṭāgiri. Having seen me, he approached, paid homage to me, and said: ‘Venerable sir, have you obtained alms?’ ‘No, friend, I have not obtained alms.’ ‘Come, venerable sir, let us go to my house.’ Then, venerable sir, that lay follower took me to his house, fed me, and said: ‘Where, venerable sir, are you going?’ ‘I am going to Sāvatthī, friend, to see the Blessed One.’ ‘Then, venerable sir, bow your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name and say this: “Venerable sir, the dwelling at Kīṭāgiri is corrupt. The monks named Assaji and Punabbasuka residing at Kīṭāgiri are shameless, wicked monks. They engage in such improper conduct: they plant and have others plant a flower garden…they engage in various kinds of improper conduct. Those people, venerable sir, who were formerly faithful and devoted have now become faithless and undevoted. Those former avenues of alms for the Saṅgha have now been cut off. Virtuous monks are leaving, and wicked monks are staying. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would send monks to Kīṭāgiri so that the dwelling there might be restored.”’ From there, Blessed One, I have come.”

23. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, assajipunabbasukā nāma kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāsikā alajjino pāpabhikkhū? Te evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācaranti – mālāvacchaṃ ropentipi…pe… vividhampi anācāraṃ ācaranti? Yepi te manussā pubbe saddhā ahesuṃ pasannā tepi etarahi assaddhā appasannā? Yānipi tāni saṅghassa pubbe dānapathāni tānipi etarahi upacchinnāni? Riñcanti pesalā bhikkhū nivasanti pāpabhikkhū”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave[M 0.0027], moghapurisā evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ [T 1.0040] ācarissanti – mālāvacchaṃ ropessantipi ropāpessantipi, siñcissantipi siñcāpessantipi, ocinissantipi ocināpessantipi, ganthessantipi ganthāpessantipi, ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, mañjarikaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, vidhūtikaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, āveḷaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, uracchadaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi. Te kulitthīnaṃ kuladhītānaṃ kulakumārīnaṃ kulasuṇhānaṃ kuladāsīnaṃ ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi, mañjarikaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi, vidhūtikaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi, āveḷaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi, uracchadaṃ harissantipi harāpessantipi. Te kulitthīhi kuladhītāhi kulakumārīhi kulasuṇhāhi kuladāsīhi saddhiṃ ekabhājanepi bhuñjissanti, ekathālakepi pivissanti, ekāsanepi nisīdissanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭissanti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭissanti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭissanti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭissanti, vikālepi bhuñjissanti, majjampi pivissanti, mālāgandhavilepanampi dhāressanti, naccissantipi, gāyissantipi, vādessantipi, lāsessantipi; naccantiyāpi naccissanti, naccantiyāpi gāyissanti, naccantiyāpi vādessanti, naccantiyāpi lāsessanti; gāyantiyāpi naccissanti[T 1.0041][V 0.0026], gāyantiyāpi gāyissanti, gāyantiyāpi vādessanti, gāyantiyāpi lāsessanti; vādentiyāpi naccissanti, vādentiyāpi gāyissanti, vādentiyāpi vādessanti, vādentiyāpi lāsessanti; lāsentiyāpi naccissanti, lāsentiyāpi gāyissanti, lāsentiyāpi vādessanti; lāsentiyāpi lāsessanti; aṭṭhapadepi kīḷissanti, dasapadepi kīḷissanti, ākāsepi kīḷissanti, parihārapathepi kīḷissanti, santikāyapi kīḷissanti, khalikāyapi kīḷissanti, ghaṭikāyapi kīḷissanti, salākahatthenapi kīḷissanti, akkhenapi kīḷissanti, paṅgacīrenapi kīḷissanti, vaṅkakenapi kīḷissanti mokkhacikāyapi kīḷissanti, ciṅgulakenapi kīḷissanti, pattāḷhakenapi kīḷissanti, rathakenapi kīḷissanti, dhanukenapi kīḷissanti, akkharikāyapi kīḷissanti, manesikāyapi kīḷissanti, yathāvajjenapi kīḷissanti; hatthismimpi sikkhissanti, assasmimpi sikkhissanti, rathasmimpi sikkhissanti, dhanusmimpi sikkhissanti, tharusmimpi sikkhissanti; hatthissapi purato dhāvissanti[M 0.0028], assassapi purato dhāvissanti, rathassapi purato purato dhāvissanti (syā.) dhāvissantipi ādhāvissantipi; usseḷessantipi, apphoṭessantipi, nibbujjhissantipi, muṭṭhīhipi yujjhissanti; raṅgamajjhepi saṅghāṭiṃ pattharitvā naccakiṃ evaṃ vakkhanti vadissanti (ka.) – ‘idha, bhagini, naccassū’ti; nalāṭikampi dassanti; vividhampi anācāraṃ ācarissanti. Netaṃ[T 1.0042], bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā sāriputtamoggallāne āmantesi – “gacchatha tumhe, sāriputtā, kīṭāgiriṃ gantvā assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ karotha, tumhākaṃ ete saddhivihārino”ti.

23. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this matter, had the community of monks assembled and questioned the monks: “Is it true, monks, that the monks named Assaji and Punabbasu, residing at Kīṭāgiri, are shameless, evil monks? That they engage in such improper conduct—planting flowering plants... and so on... and engaging in various kinds of improper conduct? And that those people who were formerly faithful and devoted have now become faithless and undevoted? And that the former avenues of offerings to the Sangha have now been cut off? And that virtuous monks leave, while evil monks reside there?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “It is unsuitable... How, monks, can these foolish men engage in such improper conduct? They plant flowering plants and have them planted; they water them and have them watered; they pluck them and have them plucked; they string them and have them strung; they make single-stem garlands and have them made; they make double-stem garlands and have them made; they make flower bunches and have them made; they make flower bracelets and have them made; they make flower crests and have them made; they make ear-pendants of flowers and have them made; they make breast-ornaments of flowers and have them made. They carry single-stem garlands, double-stem garlands, flower bunches, flower bracelets, flower crests, ear-pendants of flowers, and breast-ornaments of flowers to clan matrons, clan daughters, clan maidens, clan daughters-in-law, and clan female servants, and have them carried. They eat from the same vessel with clan matrons, clan daughters, clan maidens, clan daughters-in-law, and clan female servants; they drink from the same cup; they sit on the same seat; they lie on the same couch; they lie on the same spread; they lie with the same cover; they lie with the same spread and cover. They eat at the wrong time; they drink intoxicants; they wear garlands, scents, and ointments. They dance, sing, play music, and perform. They dance in the presence of a dancing woman, sing in the presence of a dancing woman, play music in the presence of a dancing woman, and perform in the presence of a dancing woman. They dance in the presence of a singing woman, sing in the presence of a singing woman, play music in the presence of a singing woman, and perform in the presence of a singing woman. They dance in the presence of a woman playing music, sing in the presence of a woman playing music, play music in the presence of a woman playing music, and perform in the presence of a woman playing music. They dance in the presence of a performing woman, sing in the presence of a performing woman, play music in the presence of a performing woman, and perform in the presence of a performing woman. They play on eight-row boards, they play on ten-row boards, they play ‘boardless chess’, they play hopscotch, they play games with pebbles, they play dice, they play tip-cat, they play hand-painting games, they play with `gonyin` seeds, they play with palm-leaf pipes, they play with toy ploughs, they do somersaults, they play with pinwheels, they play with toy leaf-measures, they play with toy chariots, they play with toy bows, they play letter-guessing games, they play thought-reading games, and they mimic the deformed. They train in elephantry, they train in horsemanship, they train in charioteering, they train in archery, and they train in swordsmanship. They run before an elephant, they run before a horse, they run before a chariot, and they run back and forth. They shout challenges, they slap their arms, they wrestle, and they box with their fists. They spread their outer robe in the middle of an arena and say to a dancing girl, ‘Dance here, sister,’ and they give a snap of the fingers. They engage in various kinds of improper conduct. This, monks, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired... Having rebuked them... he gave a talk on the Dhamma and then addressed Sāriputta and Moggallāna: “Go, Sāriputta and Moggallāna, to Kīṭāgiri and carry out the act of banishment against the monks Assaji and Punabbasu, banishing them from Kīṭāgiri. They are your disciples.”

“Kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ karoma, caṇḍā te bhikkhū pharusā”ti? “Tena hi tumhe, sāriputtā, bahukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ gacchathā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho sāriputtamoggallānā bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ – paṭhamaṃ assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū [P 2.0013] codetabbā, codetvā sāretabbā, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbā, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Venerable Sir, how should we perform the act of banishment from Kīṭāgiri against the monks Assaji and Punabbasu? Those monks are fierce and rough.” “In that case, Sāriputta and Moggallāna, you should go with many monks.” “Very well, Venerable Sir,” Sāriputta and Moggallāna replied to the Blessed One. And this, monks, is how it should be done: first, the monks Assaji and Punabbasu should be accused; having accused them, they should be reminded; having reminded them, they should be charged with an offense. Having charged them with an offense, a competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

24. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū kuladūsakā pāpasamācārā. Imesaṃ pāpakā samācārā dissanti ceva suyyanti ca. Kulāni ca imehi duṭṭhāni dissanti ceva suyyanti ca. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [V 0.0027] kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti. Esā ñatti.

24. “Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These bhikkhus, Assaji and Punabbasu, are corrupters of families and of evil conduct. Their evil conduct is both seen and heard, and the families corrupted by them are both seen and heard. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the act of expulsion from Kīṭāgiri against the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu, to the effect that: ‘The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu are not to dwell in Kīṭāgiri.’ This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [T 1.0043] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū kuladūsakā pāpasamācārā. Imesaṃ pāpakā samācārā dissanti ceva suyyanti ca. Kulāni ca imehi duṭṭhāni dissanti ceva suyyanti ca. Saṅgho assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ karoti – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti. Yassāyasmato khamati assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These bhikkhus, Assaji and Punabbasu, are corrupters of families and of evil conduct. Their evil conduct is both seen and heard, and the families corrupted by them are both seen and heard. The Saṅgha performs the act of expulsion from Kīṭāgiri against the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu, to the effect that: ‘The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu are not to dwell in Kīṭāgiri.’ Any venerable one who approves of the performance of this act of expulsion from Kīṭāgiri against the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu—to the effect that ‘The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu are not to dwell in Kīṭāgiri’—should remain silent. Any venerable one who does not approve should speak.

“Dutiyampi [M 0.0029] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū kuladūsakā pāpasamācārā. Imesaṃ pāpakā samācārā dissanti ceva suyyanti ca. Kulāni ca imehi duṭṭhāni dissanti ceva suyyanti ca. Saṅgho assajipunabbasukānaṃ [T 1.0044] bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ karoti – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti. Yassāyasmato khamati assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For the second time I state this matter… For the third time I state this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu are corrupters of families, of evil conduct. Their evil conduct is seen and heard, and the families corrupted by them are seen and heard. The Saṅgha performs the act of expulsion against the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu from Kīṭāgiri, to the effect that the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu should not dwell in Kīṭāgiri. Any venerable one who approves of the performance of the act of expulsion against the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu from Kīṭāgiri—to the effect that the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu should not dwell in Kīṭāgiri—should remain silent. Any venerable one who does not approve should speak.”

“Kataṃ saṅghena assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The Saṅgha has performed the act of expulsion against the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu from Kīṭāgiri, to the effect that the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu should not dwell in Kīṭāgiri. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.”

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelvefold Section on Unlawful Acts

25. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

25. “Bhikkhus, an act of expulsion endowed with three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is performed in absence; it is performed without questioning; it is performed without an admission. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of expulsion endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is badly settled.”

“Aparehipi[V 0.0028], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0045] acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti [M 0.0030] …pe… asāretvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

“Bhikkhus, an act of expulsion endowed with another three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is badly settled. It is done when there is no offense, it is done for an offense that is not to be confessed, it is done for an offense that has been confessed... it is done without having accused, it is done without having reminded, it is done without charging with an offense... it is done not in the presence of the accused, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done without questioning, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done without an admission, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done when there is no offense, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done for an offense that is not to be confessed, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done for an offense that has been confessed, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done without having accused, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done without having reminded, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction... it is done without charging with an offense, it is done unlawfully, it is done by a faction. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of expulsion endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is badly settled.”

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelvefold Section on Unlawful Acts is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelvefold Section on Lawful Acts

26. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā [T 1.0046] kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

26. “Bhikkhus, an act of expulsion endowed with three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled. It is done in the presence of the accused, it is done after questioning, and it is done with an admission. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of expulsion endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, an act in accordance with the Vinaya, and is well settled.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0047] āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena [V 0.0029] kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0048] āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ [M 0.0031] hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Monks, an act of banishment endowed with three other factors is also a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and well-pacified. It is carried out for an offense; it is carried out for an offense requiring confession; it is carried out for an unconfessed offense... it is carried out after charging; it is carried out after reminding; it is carried out after imputing an offense... it is carried out in the presence; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out after questioning; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out with an admission; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out for an offense; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out for an offense requiring confession; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out for an unconfessed offense; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out after charging; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out after reminding; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly... it is carried out after imputing an offense; it is carried out lawfully; it is carried out by a concordant assembly—indeed, monks, an act of banishment endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and well-pacified.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelve Lawful Acts are concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānacuddasakaṃ

The Fourteenfold Chapter on Wishing

27. pari. 323 “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

27. Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should carry out an act of banishment on a bhikkhu endowed with three factors. He is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, verbose, and a maker of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is of boundless offenses; he lives in association with householders through unsuitable associations. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should carry out an act of banishment on a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in conduct, and corrupt in view. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He speaks dispraise of the Buddha, he speaks dispraise of the Dhamma, he speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi[T 1.0049], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Kāyikena davena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena davena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena davena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He is endowed with bodily frivolity, he is endowed with verbal frivolity, he is endowed with bodily and verbal frivolity. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0032][V 0.0030], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Kāyikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He is endowed with bodily misconduct, he is endowed with verbal misconduct, he is endowed with bodily and verbal misconduct. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Kāyikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He is endowed with bodily harmfulness, endowed with verbal harmfulness, and endowed with bodily and verbal harmfulness. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Kāyikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena [T 1.0050] micchājīvena samannāgato hoti – imehi, kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He is endowed with bodily wrong livelihood, endowed with verbal wrong livelihood, and endowed with bodily and verbal wrong livelihood. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ[P 2.0014], ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for three bhikkhus. One is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, verbose, and a maker of legal issues in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is of boundless offenses; one lives associating with householders through unsuitable associations. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it should perform the act of banishment for these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, for three other bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment. One is corrupt in higher virtue, one is corrupt in higher conduct, and one is corrupt in higher view. Indeed, monks, for these three bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment.

“Aparesampi[M 0.0033], bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ [V 0.0031] bhāsati – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on three other bhikkhus. One speaks dispraise of the Buddha, one speaks dispraise of the Dhamma, and one speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ [T 1.0051] kareyya. Eko kāyikena davena samannāgato hoti, eko vācasikena davena samannāgato hoti, eko kāyikavācasikena davena samannāgato hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on three other bhikkhus. One is endowed with bodily playfulness, one is endowed with verbal playfulness, and one is endowed with bodily and verbal playfulness. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko kāyikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, eko vācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, eko kāyikavācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on three other bhikkhus. One is endowed with bodily misconduct, one is endowed with verbal misconduct, and one is endowed with bodily and verbal misconduct. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko kāyikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, eko vācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, eko kāyikavācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on three other bhikkhus. One is endowed with bodily destructiveness, one is endowed with verbal destructiveness, and one is endowed with bodily and verbal destructiveness. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment on these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko kāyikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, eko vācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, eko kāyikavācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Monks, on three other bhikkhus also, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment. One is endowed with bodily wrong livelihood, one is endowed with verbal wrong livelihood, and one is endowed with bodily and verbal wrong livelihood. Indeed, monks, on these three bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may perform the act of banishment.

Ākaṅkhamānacuddasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourteenfold Section on 'If Wished' is concluded.

Aṭṭhārasavattaṃ

The Eighteen Duties

28. “Pabbājanīyakammakatena[T 1.0052][M 0.0034], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena pabbājanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā[V 0.0032], tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti.

28. Monks, a bhikkhu on whom an act of banishment has been performed must conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct: He should not give higher ordination, he should not give dependence, he should not have a novice attend on him, he should not consent to the appointment as an instructor of nuns, and even if appointed, he should not instruct the nuns. He should not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha performed the act of banishment, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is worse. The act should not be criticized, nor should the bhikkhus who performed the act be criticized. He should not suspend the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, nor the Pavāraṇā. He should not make a formal statement, he should not initiate an accusation, he should not ask for leave to speak, he should not accuse another, he should not remind another of an offense, nor should he engage in disputes with the bhikkhus.

Pabbājanīyakamme aṭṭhārasavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighteen duties concerning the act of banishment are concluded.

29. Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho kīṭāgiriṃ gantvā assajipunabbasukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kīṭāgirismā pabbājanīyakammaṃ akāsi – na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabbanti. Te saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakatā na sammā vattanti, na lomaṃ pātenti, na netthāraṃ vattanti; na bhikkhū khamāpenti, akkosanti, paribhāsanti; chandagāmitā dosagāmitā mohagāmitā bhayagāmitā pāpenti; pakkamantipi, vibbhamantipi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakatā na sammā vattissanti, na lomaṃ pātessanti, na [T 1.0053] netthāraṃ vattissanti; na bhikkhū khamāpessanti, akkosissanti, paribhāsissanti; chandagāmitā dosagāmitā mohagāmitā bhayagāmitā pāpessanti; pakkamissantipi, vibbhamissantipī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

29. Then the community of bhikkhus, with Sāriputta and Moggallāna at its head, went to Kīṭāgiri and performed an act of banishment from Kīṭāgiri on the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasuka, declaring: 'The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasuka should not dwell in Kīṭāgiri.' Those bhikkhus, on whom the act of banishment had been performed by the Saṅgha, did not conduct themselves properly, did not humble themselves, and did not practice the conduct for their rehabilitation; they did not ask for forgiveness from the bhikkhus, but insulted and reviled them; they fell into courses of partiality, hostility, delusion, and fear; they also departed and disrobed. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasuka, on whom the act of banishment has been performed by the Saṅgha, will not conduct themselves properly, will not humble themselves, will not practice the conduct for their rehabilitation; will not ask for forgiveness from the bhikkhus, but will insult and revile them; will fall into courses of partiality, hostility, delusion, and fear; and will also depart and disrobe?' Then those bhikkhus informed the Blessed One of this matter.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakatā na sammā vattanti, na lomaṃ pātenti, na netthāraṃ vattanti; na bhikkhū khamāpenti, akkosanti, paribhāsanti; chandagāmitā dosagāmitā mohagāmitā bhayagāmitā pāpenti; pakkamantipi, vibbhamantipī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ [M 0.0035]…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakatā na sammā vattissanti, na lomaṃ pātessanti, na netthāraṃ vattissanti; na bhikkhū khamāpessanti, akkosissanti, paribhāsissanti; chandagāmitā dosagāmitā mohagāmitā bhayagāmitā pāpessanti; pakkamissantipi, vibbhamissantipi. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

Then, on that occasion, in that matter, the Blessed One, having had the community of monks assembled, questioned the monks: “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the monks Assaji and Punabbasu, against whom the Saṅgha has carried out the act of banishment, do not conduct themselves properly, do not humble themselves, do not practice the conduct for their rehabilitation; do not ask for forgiveness from the monks, but insult and revile them; and that they fall into wrong courses through desire, hatred, delusion, and fear; and that they also depart and also disrobe?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “... How indeed, monks, can those foolish men, against whom the Saṅgha has carried out the act of banishment, not conduct themselves properly, not humble themselves, not practice the conduct for their rehabilitation; not ask for forgiveness from the monks, but insult and revile them; and fall into wrong courses through desire, hatred, delusion, and fear; and also depart and also disrobe? This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of the unconvinced...” After rebuking them and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha not revoke the act of banishment.”

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The eighteen instances where it should not be rescinded.

30. “Pañcahi[V 0.0033], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [P 2.0015] pabbājanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ [T 1.0054] upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

30. “Monks, for a monk endowed with five factors, the act of banishment should not be revoked. He gives higher ordination; he gives dependence; he has a novice attend on him; he consents to the appointment as an instructor of nuns; and having been appointed, he instructs the nuns. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of banishment should not be revoked.”

pari. 420 “Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena pabbājanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with another five factors should not be rescinded. He commits the same offense for which the Saṅgha carried out the banishment act, or another similar to it, or one even more wicked; he disparages the act, he disparages those who carried out the act—indeed, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with these five factors should not be rescinded.”

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, okāsaṃ kāreti, codeti, sāreti, bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with eight factors should not be rescinded. He suspends the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, he suspends the Pavāraṇā, he admonishes, he initiates a formal charge, he has an opportunity requested, he reproves, he reminds, he associates with monks—indeed, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with these eight factors should not be rescinded.”

Pabbājanīyakamme nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighteen cases concerning the act of banishment that should not be rescinded are concluded.

Paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The eighteen cases where it should be rescinded.

31. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti[M 0.0036], na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa [T 1.0055] bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

31. “Monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with five factors should be rescinded. He does not give higher ordination, he does not give dependence, he does not have a novice attend on him, he does not consent to the appointment as an instructor of nuns, and even when appointed, he does not admonish the nuns—indeed, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with these five factors should be rescinded.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena pabbājanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati [V 0.0034] – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with another five factors should be rescinded. He does not commit the same offense for which the Saṅgha carried out the banishment act, nor another similar to it, nor one more wicked than it; he does not disparage the act, he does not disparage those who carried out the act—indeed, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with these five factors should be rescinded.”

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with eight factors should be rescinded. He does not suspend the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, he does not suspend the Pavāraṇā, he does not admonish, he does not initiate a formal charge, he does not have an opportunity requested, he does not reprove, he does not remind, and he does not associate with monks—indeed, monks, the banishment act against a monk endowed with these eight factors should be rescinded.”

Pabbājanīyakamme paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighteen cases where the banishment act is to be rescinded are concluded.

32. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tena, bhikkhave, pabbājanīyakammakatena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi [T 1.0056] yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

32. “And, monks, it should be rescinded in this way. Therefore, monks, the monk who has been subjected to the banishment act should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and say this: ‘Venerable sirs, I, who have been subjected to the banishment act by the Saṅgha, am behaving properly, I am humbling myself, I am conducting myself for release. I request the rescinding of the banishment act.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. A competent and capable monk should then inform the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, who has been subjected to the banishment act by the Saṅgha, is behaving properly, is humbling himself, is conducting himself for release, and requests the rescinding of the banishment act. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should rescind the banishment act for the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pabbājanīyassa [M 0.0037] kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, upon whom the Saṅgha has carried out the act of banishment, is conducting himself properly, humbles his pride, is conducting himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of banishment. The Saṅgha revokes the act of banishment for the bhikkhu named so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the revocation of the act of banishment for the bhikkhu named so-and-so is agreeable, he should be silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho[V 0.0035]. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, upon whom the Saṅgha has carried out the act of banishment, is conducting himself properly, humbles his pride, is conducting himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of banishment. The Saṅgha revokes the act of banishment for the bhikkhu named so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the revocation of the act of banishment for the bhikkhu named so-and-so is agreeable, he should be silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pabbājanīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā

The act of banishment for the bhikkhu named so-and-so has been revoked by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore

Tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

it is silent; thus do I record this.

Pabbājanīyakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third act of banishment is concluded.

4. Paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ

4. The Act of Reconciliation

33. Tena [T 1.0057] kho pana samayena āyasmā sudhammo macchikāsaṇḍe cittassa gahapatino āvāsiko hoti, navakammiko dhuvabhattiko. Yadā citto gahapati saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā puggalaṃ vā nimantetukāmo hoti tadā na āyasmantaṃ sudhammaṃ anapaloketvā saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā puggalaṃ vā nimanteti.

33. At that time, the Venerable Sudhamma was the resident bhikkhu of the householder Citta in Macchikāsaṇḍa; he was in charge of new works and a recipient of regular meals. Whenever the householder Citta wished to invite the Saṅgha, or a group, or an individual, he would not invite the Saṅgha, or a group, or an individual without first informing the Venerable Sudhamma.

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā therā bhikkhū, āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno, āyasmā ca mahākaccāno, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko[P 2.0016], āyasmā ca mahākappino, āyasmā ca mahācundo, āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca revato, āyasmā ca upāli, āyasmā ca ānando, āyasmā ca rāhulo, kāsīsu cārikaṃ caramānā yena macchikāsaṇḍo tadavasaruṃ.

At that time, many elder bhikkhus—the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika, the Venerable Mahākappina, the Venerable Mahācunda, the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata, the Venerable Upāli, the Venerable Ānanda, and the Venerable Rāhula—wandering on tour in the Kāsi country, arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa.

Assosi kho citto gahapati therā kira bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍaṃ anuppattāti. Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami[M 0.0038], upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cittaṃ gahapatiṃ āyasmā sāriputto dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi.

Citta the householder heard that the elder bhikkhus had arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa. Then Citta the householder approached the elder bhikkhus, and after paying homage to them, sat down to one side. As he sat to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta instructed, roused, inspired, and gladdened Citta the householder with a Dhamma talk.

Atha kho citto gahapati āyasmatā sāriputtena dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito there bhikkhū etadavoca [T 1.0058] – “adhivāsentu me, bhante, therā svātanāya āgantukabhatta”nti. Adhivāsesuṃ kho therā bhikkhū adhivāsesuṃ kho te therā bhikkhū (syā.) tuṇhībhāvena.

Then the householder Citta, having been instructed, roused, inspired, and gladdened by the Venerable Sāriputta with a Dhamma talk, said this to the elder bhikkhus: "Venerable sirs, may the elders consent to my meal for visiting monks tomorrow." The elder bhikkhus consented by remaining silent.

Atha [V 0.0036] kho citto gahapati therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yenāyasmā sudhammo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sudhammaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ sudhammaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, ayyo sudhammo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ therehī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā sudhammo ‘pubbe khvāyaṃ citto gahapati yadā saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā puggalaṃ vā nimantetukāmo na maṃ anapaloketvā saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā puggalaṃ vā nimanteti; sodāni maṃ anapaloketvā there bhikkhū nimantesi; duṭṭhodānāyaṃ citto gahapati anapekkho virattarūpo mayī’ti cittaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, gahapati, nādhivāsemī”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ sudhammaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, ayyo sudhammo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ therehī”ti. “Alaṃ, gahapati, nādhivāsemī”ti. Atha kho citto gahapati ‘kiṃ me karissati ayyo sudhammo [T 1.0059] adhivāsento vā anadhivāsento vā’ti āyasmantaṃ sudhammaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then the householder Citta, having understood the elder bhikkhus' acceptance, rose from his seat, paid homage to the elder bhikkhus, circumambulated them respectfully, and approached the Venerable Sudhamma. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Sudhamma and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the householder Citta said to the Venerable Sudhamma: “Venerable Sir, may the noble Sudhamma accept my meal for tomorrow, together with the elder bhikkhus.” Then the Venerable Sudhamma thought: “Formerly, whenever this householder Citta wished to invite the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual, he would not invite the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual without first informing me. But now he has invited the elder bhikkhus without informing me. Now this householder Citta is ill-disposed, without regard, and estranged from me.” He said to the householder Citta: “Enough, householder, I do not accept.” For a second time… and for a third time, the householder Citta said to the Venerable Sudhamma: “Venerable Sir, may the noble Sudhamma accept my meal for tomorrow, together with the elder bhikkhus.” “Enough, householder, I do not accept.” Then the householder Citta thought: “What can the noble Sudhamma do to me, whether he accepts or does not accept?” He paid homage to the Venerable Sudhamma, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

34. Atha kho citto gahapati tassā rattiyā accayena therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpesi. Atha kho āyasmā sudhammo ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ cittassa gahapatino therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭiyattaṃ [P 2.0017] passeyya’nti pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena cittassa gahapatino nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā sudhammo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā [M 0.0039] āyasmantaṃ sudhammaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cittaṃ gahapatiṃ āyasmā sudhammo etadavoca – “pahūtaṃ kho te idaṃ, gahapati, khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ; ekā ca kho idha natthi yadidaṃ tilasaṅguḷikā”ti. “Bahumhi vata, bhante, ratane buddhavacane bhante buddhavacane (syā.) vijjamāne ayyena sudhammena yadeva kiñci bhāsitaṃ yadidaṃ tilasaṅguḷikāti. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante, dakkhiṇāpathakā vāṇijā puratthimaṃ janapadaṃ agamaṃsu vāṇijjāya. Te tato kukkuṭiṃ ānesuṃ. Atha kho sā, bhante, kukkuṭī kākena saddhiṃ saṃvāsaṃ kappesi. Sā potakaṃ janesi. Yadā kho so, bhante, kukkuṭapotako [T 1.0060] kākavassaṃ vassitukāmo hoti, kākakukkuṭīti vassati; yadā kukkuṭivassaṃ vassitukāmo hoti, kukkuṭikākāti vassati. Evameva kho, bhante, bahumhi ratane buddhavacane vijjamāne ayyena sudhammena yadeva kiñci bhāsitaṃ yadidaṃ tilasaṃguḷikā”ti. “Akkosasi maṃ tvaṃ, gahapati, paribhāsasi maṃ tvaṃ, gahapati. Eso te, gahapati, āvāso, pakkamissāmī”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante, ayyaṃ sudhammaṃ akkosāmi, paribhāsāmi [V 0.0037] na paribhāsāmi (sī. syā.). Vasatu, bhante, ayyo sudhammo macchikāsaṇḍe. Ramaṇīyaṃ ambāṭakavanaṃ. Ahaṃ ayyassa sudhammassa ussukkaṃ karissāmi, cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna”nti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… [T 1.0061] tatiyampi kho āyasmā sudhammo cittaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “akkosasi maṃ tvaṃ, gahapati, paribhāsasi maṃ tvaṃ, gahapati. Eso te, gahapati, āvāso, pakkamissāmī”ti. “Kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo sudhammo gamissatī”ti? “Sāvatthiṃ kho ahaṃ, gahapati, gamissāmi bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, yañca attanā bhaṇitaṃ, yañca mayā bhaṇitaṃ taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocehi. Anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhante, yaṃ ayyo sudhammo punadeva macchikāsaṇḍaṃ paccāgaccheyyā”ti.

34. Then, after the night had passed, the householder Citta had excellent hard and soft food prepared for the elder monks. Then the Venerable Sudhamma thought, 'It would be good if I were to see what the householder Citta has prepared for the elder monks.' So in the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he went to the dwelling of the householder Citta. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the householder Citta approached the Venerable Sudhamma, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. To the householder Citta, who was sitting to one side, the Venerable Sudhamma said: 'Householder, you have prepared a great deal of hard and soft food here, but there is one thing missing—sesame cakes.' 'Venerable sir, while there is such a great treasure in the Buddha's word, the Venerable Sudhamma has spoken only of some trifle, namely, sesame cakes. In a time long past, venerable sir, merchants from the Southern region went to the eastern country for trade. They brought a hen from there. Then, venerable sir, that hen mated with a crow.
