She produced a chick. When that chick, venerable sir, wanted to make a crow's sound, it would sound "caw-cluck"; when it wanted to make a hen's sound, it would sound "cluck-caw." In this very way, venerable sir, while there is such a great treasure in the Buddha's word, the Venerable Sudhamma has spoken only of some trifle, namely, sesame cakes.' 'Householder, you insult me! You revile me! This is your dwelling—I will depart!' 'I do not insult or revile the Venerable Sudhamma, venerable sir. Let the Venerable Sudhamma dwell in Macchikāsaṇḍa. The Ambāṭaka Grove is delightful. I will make an effort for the Venerable Sudhamma’s requisites: robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine for the sick.' For a second time... and for a third time, the Venerable Sudhamma said to the householder Citta: 'Householder, you insult me! You revile me! This is your dwelling—I will depart!' 'Where, venerable sir, will the Venerable Sudhamma go?' 'I will go to Sāvatthī, householder, to see the Blessed One.' 'Then, venerable sir, please report to the Blessed One both what you have said and what I have said. It would not be surprising, venerable sir, if the Venerable Sudhamma were to return again to Macchikāsaṇḍa.'

35. Atha kho āyasmā sudhammo senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sāvatthi tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sudhammo yañca attanā bhaṇitaṃ [P 2.0018] yañca cittena gahapatinā bhaṇitaṃ taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocesi.

35. Then the Venerable Sudhamma, having put his dwelling in order and taking his bowl and robe, set out for Sāvatthī. In due course, he arrived at Sāvatthī, at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sudhamma reported to the Blessed One all that he had said and all that the householder Citta had said.

Vigarahi [M 0.0040] buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, cittaṃ gahapatiṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ dāyakaṃ kārakaṃ saṅghupaṭṭhākaṃ hīnena khuṃsessasi, hīnena vambhessasi? Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā [T 1.0062] pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karotu – citto te gahapati khamāpetabboti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ – paṭhamaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: 'Worthless man, this is unsuitable, improper, unseemly, unworthy of a recluse, unallowable, and not to be done. How could you, worthless man, insult and disparage the householder Citta, who is faithful, devout, a donor, a benefactor, and a supporter of the Saṅgha, in a base manner? This, worthless man, does not conduce to the confidence of the unconfident…' Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha perform the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma: “You must get the householder Citta to forgive you.” And this, monks, is how it should be done: First, the monk Sudhamma is to be charged; having charged him, he is to be reminded; having reminded him, he is to be charged with the offense. Having charged him with the offense, the Saṅgha is to be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

36. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu cittaṃ gahapatiṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ dāyakaṃ kārakaṃ saṅghupaṭṭhākaṃ hīnena khuṃseti, hīnena vambheti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya – citto te gahapati khamāpetabboti. Esā ñatti.

36. 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Sudhamma insults and disparages the householder Citta—who is faithful, devout, a donor, a benefactor, and a supporter of the Saṅgha—in a base manner. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha perform the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma: “You must get the householder Citta to forgive you.” This is the motion.'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu cittaṃ gahapatiṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ dāyakaṃ kārakaṃ [V 0.0038] saṅghupaṭṭhākaṃ hīnena khuṃseti, hīnena vambheti. Saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karoti – citto te gahapati khamāpetabboti. Yassāyasmato khamati sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – citto te gahapati khamāpetabboti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Sudhamma insults and disparages the householder Citta—who is faithful, devout, a donor, a benefactor, and a supporter of the Saṅgha—in a base manner. The Saṅgha performs the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma: ‘You must get the householder Citta to forgive you.’ If it is agreeable to the venerable ones that the act of reconciliation be performed for the monk Sudhamma—‘You must get the householder Citta to forgive you’—let them remain silent. If it is not agreeable, let them speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu cittaṃ gahapatiṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ dāyakaṃ kārakaṃ saṅghupaṭṭhākaṃ hīnena khuṃseti, hīnena vambheti. Saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karoti – citto [T 1.0063] te gahapati khamāpetabboti. Yassāyasmato khamati sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – citto te gahapati khamāpetabboti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time I speak on this matter... For a third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Sudhamma reviles and disparages Citta the householder—who is faithful, devoted, a donor, a benefactor, and an attendant of the Saṅgha—in a base manner. The Saṅgha performs the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma: ‘You must ask forgiveness of Citta the householder.’ If the performing of the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma—‘You must ask forgiveness of Citta the householder’—is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them remain silent. If it is not agreeable, let them speak.”

“Kataṃ saṅghena sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ – citto te gahapati khamāpetabboti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma has been performed by the Saṅgha: ‘You must ask forgiveness of Citta the householder.’ It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I bear this in mind.”

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Dodecad of Unlawful Acts

37. “Tīhi[M 0.0041], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

37. “Monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with three factors is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is performed not in the presence of the accused, performed without questioning, and performed without an admission of guilt. Monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with these three factors is indeed an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0064] asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0065] adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… asāretvā kataṃ hoti[V 0.0039], adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ [T 1.0066] paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

“Furthermore, monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with three other factors is an unlawful act, contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is done when there is no offense; it is done for an offense that is not to be confessed; it is done for an offense that has been confessed… it is done without having accused; it is done without having reminded; it is done without having charged with an offense… it is done in absence, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done without questioning, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done without admission, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done when there is no offense, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done for an offense that is not to be confessed, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done for an offense that has been confessed, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done without having accused, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done without having reminded, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… it is done without having charged with an offense, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly. Indeed, monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with these three factors is an unlawful act, contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.”

Paṭisāraṇīyakamme adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dodecad of Unlawful Acts concerning the Act of Reconciliation is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Dodecad of Lawful Acts

38. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

38. “Monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with three factors is in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and is properly settled. It is done in the presence, it is done after having questioned, and it is done upon admission. Indeed, monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with these three factors is in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and is properly settled.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0042], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0067] paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ āropetvā [T 1.0068] kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

“Furthermore, monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with three other factors is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and is well-pacified. It is done for an offense, done for an offense that should be confessed, done for an offense that has not been confessed… done after having accused, done after having reminded, done after having charged with an offense… done in the presence, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done after having questioned, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done with an admission, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done for an offense, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done for an offense that should be confessed, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done for an offense that has not been confessed, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done after having accused, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done after having reminded, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha… done after having charged with an offense, done according to the Dhamma, done by a complete Saṅgha—indeed, monks, an act of reconciliation endowed with these three factors is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and is well-pacified.”

Paṭisāraṇīyakamme dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dodecad of Lawful Acts concerning the Act of Reconciliation is concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad on Discretionary Acts

39. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ [V 0.0040] kareyya. Gihīnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, gihīnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, gihīnaṃ anāvāsāya avāsāya (sī.) parisakkati, gihī akkosati paribhāsati, gihī gihīhi [P 2.0019] bhedeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya.

39. “Monks, the Saṅgha, if it so wishes, may carry out an act of reconciliation against a monk who is endowed with five factors. He strives for the non-gain of householders; he strives for the detriment of householders; he strives for the non-residence of householders; he insults and reviles householders; he divides householders from one another. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it so wishes, may carry out an act of reconciliation against a monk who is endowed with these five factors.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya. Gihīnaṃ buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati[M 0.0043], gihīnaṃ dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, gihīnaṃ saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, gihī hīnena khuṃseti hīnena vambheti, gihīnaṃ dhammikaṃ paṭissavaṃ na saccāpeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya.

“Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform an act of reconciliation against a bhikkhu endowed with five other qualities. He speaks dispraise of the Buddha to householders, speaks dispraise of the Dhamma to householders, speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha to householders, reviles and disparages householders with base speech, and does not make true a legitimate promise to householders. Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform an act of reconciliation against a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities.”

“Pañcannaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko gihīnaṃ [T 1.0069] alābhāya parisakkati, eko gihīnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, eko gihīnaṃ anāvāsāya parisakkati, eko gihī akkosati paribhāsati, eko gihī gihīhi bhedeti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya.

“Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform an act of reconciliation against five kinds of bhikkhus. One strives for the non-gain of householders; one strives for the disadvantage of householders; one strives for the non-dwelling of householders; one insults and reviles householders; and one divides householders from other householders. Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform an act of reconciliation against these five kinds of bhikkhus.”

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko gihīnaṃ buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko gihīnaṃ dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko gihīnaṃ saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko gihī hīnena khuṃseti hīnena vambheti, eko gihīnaṃ dhammikaṃ paṭissavaṃ na saccāpeti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya.

“Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform an act of reconciliation against five other kinds of bhikkhus. One speaks dispraise of the Buddha to householders; one speaks dispraise of the Dhamma to householders; one speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha to householders; one reviles and disparages householders with base speech; and one does not make true a legitimate promise to householders. Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform an act of reconciliation against these five kinds of bhikkhus.”

Ākaṅkhamānacatukkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tetrad on Wishing is concluded.

Aṭṭhārasavattaṃ

The Eighteen Rules of Conduct

40. “Paṭisāraṇīyakammakatena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā[V 0.0041], tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo[T 1.0070], na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti.

40. “Monks, a monk against whom an act of reconciliation has been carried out must conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct: He should not confer higher ordination, grant dependence, have a novice attend on him, or consent to the appointment to instruct nuns; and even if appointed, he should not instruct nuns. He should not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha carried out the act of reconciliation, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is more serious. He should not disparage the act or those who carried it out. He should not suspend the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, nor the Pavāraṇā; nor should he make a formal statement, nor initiate a formal charge, nor cause a request for an opportunity to be made, nor accuse, nor remind, nor associate with other monks.”

Paṭisāraṇīyakamme aṭṭhārasavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighteen rules of conduct for the act of reconciliation are concluded.

41. Atha [M 0.0044] kho saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ akāsi – “citto te gahapati khamāpetabbo”ti. So saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato macchikāsaṇḍaṃ gantvā maṅkubhūto nāsakkhi cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetuṃ. Punadeva sāvatthiṃ paccāgañchi. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “khamāpito tayā, āvuso sudhamma, citto gahapatī”ti? “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, macchikāsaṇḍaṃ gantvā maṅkubhūto nāsakkhiṃ cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetu”nti. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe…. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno anudūtaṃ detu – cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetuṃ. Evañca pana bhikkhave dātabbo – paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

41. Then the Saṅgha carried out the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma, saying: ‘You must ask the householder Citta for forgiveness.’ Having been subjected to the act of reconciliation by the Saṅgha, he went to Macchikāsaṇḍa but, being sullen, was unable to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness. He returned again to Sāvatthī. The monks asked him, ‘Friend Sudhamma, have you asked the householder Citta for forgiveness?’ ‘Friends, after going to Macchikāsaṇḍa, I was sullen and unable to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness.’ The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha give an accompanying monk to the monk Sudhamma to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness. And, monks, he should be given in this way: First, a monk should be requested. Having requested him, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and able monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ sudhammassa bhikkhuno anudūtaṃ dadeyya cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetuṃ. Esā ñatti.

“‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the monk named so-and-so to the monk Sudhamma as an accompanying monk to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ sudhammassa [P 2.0020] bhikkhuno anudūtaṃ deti cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetuṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sudhammassa bhikkhuno anudūtassa dānaṃ cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetuṃ, so [T 1.0071] tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha gives the monk named so-and-so as an accompanying monk to the monk Sudhamma to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness. To whichever venerable one the giving of the monk named so-and-so as an accompanying monk to the monk Sudhamma to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness is agreeable, he should remain silent; he to whom it is not agreeable should speak.’

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu sudhammassa bhikkhuno anudūto cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetuṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“‘The monk named so-and-so has been given by the Saṅgha as an accompanying monk for the monk Sudhamma to ask the householder Citta for forgiveness. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand this.’

42. “Tena, bhikkhave, sudhammena bhikkhunā anudūtena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ macchikāsaṇḍaṃ gantvā citto gahapati khamāpetabbo – ‘khama, gahapati, pasādemi ta’nti. Evañce vuccamāno khamati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce khamati, anudūtena bhikkhunā vattabbo – ‘khama, gahapati, imassa [V 0.0042] bhikkhuno, pasādeti ta’nti. Evañce vuccamāno khamati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce khamati, anudūtena bhikkhunā vattabbo – ‘khama, gahapati, imassa bhikkhuno, ahaṃ taṃ pasādemī’ti. Evañce vuccamāno khamati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce khamati, anudūtena bhikkhunā vattabbo – ‘khama, gahapati, imassa bhikkhuno, saṅghassa vacanenā’ti. Evañce vuccamāno khamati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce [M 0.0045] khamati, anudūtena bhikkhunā sudhammo bhikkhu sudhammaṃ bhikkhuṃ… sā āpatti desāpetabbāti (sī. syā.) cittassa gahapatino dassanūpacāraṃ avijahāpetvā savanūpacāraṃ avijahāpetvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā taṃ āpattiṃ desāpetabbo”ti sudhammaṃ bhikkhuṃ… sā āpatti desāpetabbāti (sī. syā.).

42. “Then, monks, the monk Sudhamma, together with the accompanying monk, should go to Macchikāsaṇḍa and ask for forgiveness from the householder Citta, saying: ‘Forgive me, householder, I seek to restore your confidence.’ If, on being spoken to thus, he forgives, that is good. If he does not forgive, the accompanying monk should say: ‘Householder, forgive this monk; he seeks to restore your confidence.’ If, on being spoken to thus, he forgives, that is good. If he does not forgive, the accompanying monk should say: ‘Householder, forgive this monk; I seek to restore your confidence.’ If, on being spoken to thus, he forgives, that is good. If he does not forgive, the accompanying monk should say: ‘Householder, forgive this monk on the word of the Saṅgha.’ If, on being spoken to thus, he forgives, that is good. If he does not forgive, the accompanying monk should have the monk Sudhamma—without leaving the range of sight and hearing of the householder Citta—arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit on his heels, raise his hands in añjali, and confess that offense.”

Atha kho āyasmā sudhammo anudūtena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ macchikāsaṇḍaṃ gantvā cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpesi. So sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti [T 1.0072] – “ahaṃ, āvuso, saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

Then the Venerable Sudhamma, together with the messenger monk, went to Macchikāsaṇḍa and asked for forgiveness from the householder Citta. He conducts himself well, lowers his pride, and conducts himself for his release. He approached the monks and said: “Friends, having been subjected to the act of reconciliation by the Saṅgha, I conduct myself well, I lower my pride, and I conduct myself for my release. How should I now proceed?” The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha rescind the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma.”

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The Eighteen Cases Wherein It Should Not Be Rescinded

43. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

43. “Monks, the act of reconciliation should not be rescinded for a monk endowed with five factors. He gives the higher ordination, he gives dependence, he has a novice attend on him, he consents to being appointed as an advisor to nuns, and though appointed, he admonishes the nuns. Monks, the act of reconciliation should not be rescinded for a monk endowed with these five factors.”

pari. 420 “Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Monks, the act of reconciliation should not be rescinded for a monk endowed with another five factors. He commits the offense for which the Saṅgha performed the act of reconciliation, or another of a similar nature, or one worse than that; he disparages the act, he disparages those who performed the act. Monks, the act of reconciliation should not be rescinded for a monk endowed with these five factors.”

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, okāsaṃ kāreti, codeti[M 0.0046], sāreti, bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi [V 0.0043] kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ [T 1.0073] nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ”.

“Monks, the act of reconciliation should not be rescinded for a monk who is endowed with eight factors. He suspends the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, he suspends the Pavāraṇā, he admonishes, he institutes a censure, he makes others ask for an opportunity, he accuses, he reminds, and he associates with monks. Monks, the act of reconciliation should not be rescinded for a monk endowed with these eight factors.”

Paṭisāraṇīyakamme nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section of eighteen cases for not rescinding the act of reconciliation is concluded.

Paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ

The Eighteen Cases Wherein It Should Be Rescinded

44. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

44. “Monks, the act of reconciliation should be rescinded for a monk who is endowed with five factors. He does not give higher ordination, he does not give dependence, he does not have a novice attend on him, he does not consent to being appointed as an advisor to nuns, and though appointed, he does not admonish the nuns. Monks, the act of reconciliation should be rescinded for a monk endowed with these five factors.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Monks, the act of reconciliation should be rescinded for a monk who is endowed with another five factors. He does not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha performed the act of reconciliation, nor another of a similar nature, nor one worse than that; he does not disparage the act, and he does not disparage those who performed the act. Monks, the act of reconciliation should be rescinded for a monk endowed with these five factors.”

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Monks, the act of reconciliation should be rescinded for a monk who is endowed with eight factors. He does not suspend the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, he does not suspend the Pavāraṇā, he does not admonish, he does not institute a censure, he does not make others ask for an opportunity, he does not accuse, he does not remind, and he does not associate with monks. Monks, the act of reconciliation should indeed be rescinded for a monk endowed with these eight factors.”

Paṭisāraṇīyakamme paṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section of eighteen cases for rescinding the act of reconciliation is concluded.

45. “Evañca [T 1.0074][P 2.0021] pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tena tena hi (syā. ka.), bhikkhave, sudhammena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa [V 0.0044] paṭippassaddhiṃ yācāmī’ti[M 0.0047]. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

45. “And, monks, it should be rescinded in this way. That monk Sudhamma, having approached the Saṅgha, should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I, upon whom the act of reconciliation has been carried out by the Saṅgha, am conducting myself properly, I lower my pride, I am conducting myself for release from this act. I request the rescission of the act of reconciliation.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

“‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Sudhamma, upon whom the act of reconciliation has been carried out by the Saṅgha, is conducting himself properly, he lowers his pride, he is conducting himself for release from this act, and he requests the rescission of the act of reconciliation. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should rescind the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma. This is the motion.’”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Sudhamma, upon whom the act of reconciliation has been carried out by the Saṅgha, is conducting himself properly, he lowers his pride, he is conducting himself for release from this act, and he requests the rescission of the act of reconciliation. The Saṅgha rescinds the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma. To whichever venerable one the rescission of the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma is agreeable, let him be silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, let him speak.’”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… [T 1.0075] tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sudhammo bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time I speak on this matter... For a third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Sudhamma, against whom the Saṅgha has performed the act of reconciliation, is conducting himself properly, is showing humility, is conducting himself for release, and requests the rescission of the act of reconciliation. The Saṅgha rescinds the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma. If the rescission of the act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them remain silent. If it is not agreeable, let them speak.”

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ saṅghena sudhammassa bhikkhuno paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The act of reconciliation for the monk Sudhamma has been rescinded by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I bear this in mind.”

Paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth act of reconciliation is concluded.

5. Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ

5. The Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

46. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti [M 0.0048] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo āpattiṃ [V 0.0045] āpajjitvā na icchissati āpattiṃ passitu”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

46. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Kosambi, in Ghosita’s monastery. Now at that time the Venerable Channa, having fallen into an offense, did not wish to see the offense. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the Venerable Channa, having fallen into an offense, not wish to see the offense?” Then those monks informed the Blessed One of this matter.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā [T 1.0076] bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passitu”nti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchissati āpattiṃ passituṃ? Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karotu – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ – paṭhamaṃ channo bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having had the community of monks assembled, questioned the monks: “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the monk Channa, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “It is unfitting… How indeed, monks, can that foolish man, having committed an offense, not wish to see the offense? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha carry out the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha. And, monks, it should be done in this way. First, the monk Channa should be accused; having accused him, he should be reminded; having reminded him, he should be charged with the offense. Having charged him with the offense, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

47. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Esā ñatti.

47. “Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should carry out the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense. The Saṅgha carries out the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha. Any venerable one who approves of the carrying out of the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha—should be silent; any who does not approve should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi [T 1.0077] etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ [M 0.0049] – asambhogaṃ saṅghena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so [P 2.0022] bhāseyya.

“For the second time I speak on this matter… For the third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense. The Saṅgha carries out the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha. Any venerable one who approves of carrying out the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha—should remain silent; any who disapproves should speak.”

“Kataṃ [V 0.0046] saṅghena channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

“The act of suspension—non-communion with the Saṅgha—has been carried out by the Saṅgha for the monk Channa for not seeing the offense. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I bear this in mind.”

“Āvāsaparamparañca, bhikkhave, saṃsatha – ‘channo bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā channo bhikkhu āpattiyā (sī. ka.) adassane ukkhepanīyakammakato – asambhogaṃ saṅghenā’ti.

“And, monks, you should announce this in successive monasteries: ‘The monk Channa has been subjected to the act of suspension by the Saṅgha for not seeing an offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha.’”

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Group of Twelve on Unlawful Acts

48. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

48. “Monks, an act of suspension for not seeing an offense, when endowed with three factors, is an unlawful act, a non-disciplinary act, and is badly settled. It is carried out not in his presence, it is carried out without questioning, and it is carried out without his admission. Indeed, monks, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not seeing an offense is an unlawful act, a non-disciplinary act, and is badly settled.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ [T 1.0078] hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… asāretvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ anāropetvā [M 0.0050] kataṃ hoti, adhammena [T 1.0079] kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, when endowed with another three factors, a suspension act for not acknowledging an offense is an unlawful act, a non-disciplinary act, and is badly settled. It is done for a non-offense; it is done for an offense that does not require confession; it is done for an offense that has been confessed... (abbreviated)... it is done without having admonished; it is done without having reminded; it is done without having charged with an offense... (abbreviated)... it is done in the absence [of the bhikkhu]; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done without questioning; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done without an admission; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done for a non-offense, it is done unlawfully, and it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done for an offense that does not require confession, it is done unlawfully, and it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done for an offense that has been confessed, it is done unlawfully, and it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done without having admonished, it is done unlawfully, and it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done without having reminded, it is done unlawfully, and it is done by an incomplete quorum... (abbreviated)... it is done without having charged with an offense, it is done unlawfully, and it is done by an incomplete quorum. Indeed, Bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors, a suspension act for not acknowledging an offense is an unlawful act, a non-disciplinary act, and is badly settled.”

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakamme adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The twelvefold [section on] unlawful acts concerning the suspension for not acknowledging an offense is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelvefold Lawful Acts

49. “Tīhi[V 0.0047], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

49. “Bhikkhus, an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense, when endowed with three factors, is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and is well-settled. It is done in the presence [of the bhikkhu], it is done after questioning, and it is done upon acknowledgment. Indeed, Bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and is well-settled.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ…pe…. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0080] paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, endowed with another three factors, an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense... (is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and is well-settled). It is done for an offense; it is done for an offense that requires confession; it is done for an unconfessed offense... (abbreviated)... It is done after admonishing; it is done after reminding; it is done after charging with an offense... (abbreviated)... It is done in the presence [of the bhikkhu], lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done after questioning, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done upon acknowledgment, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done for an offense, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done for an offense that requires confession, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done for an unconfessed offense, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done after admonishing, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done after reminding, lawfully, and by a united assembly... (abbreviated)... It is done after charging with an offense, lawfully, and by a united assembly. Indeed, Bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense is a lawful act, a disciplinary act, and is well-settled.”

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakamme dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The twelvefold [section on] lawful acts concerning the suspension for not acknowledging an offense is concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ

The Hexad on Wishing

50. pari. 323 “Tīhi[M 0.0051], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako[T 1.0081]; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

50. “Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense against a bhikkhu endowed with three factors. He is one who creates arguments, quarrels, disputes, and wrangling, and who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is unrestrained regarding them; he dwells associated with householders through unbecoming association with householders. Indeed, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense against a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā [V 0.0048] adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense against a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in conduct through transgression, and corrupt in view through excessive view. Indeed, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense against a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense against a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors. He speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, he speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, and he speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense against a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors.”

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi [T 1.0082] – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense against three bhikkhus. One is one who creates arguments, creates quarrels, creates disputes, and creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is unrestrained regarding offenses; one dwells associated with householders through unbecoming association with householders. Indeed, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense against these three bhikkhus.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti[M 0.0052], eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, for three other bhikkhus also, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense. One is corrupt in higher virtue; one is corrupt in conduct through transgression; and one is corrupt in view through wrong view. Indeed, Bhikkhus, for these three bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, for three other bhikkhus also, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense. One speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, one speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, and one speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, Bhikkhus, for these three bhikkhus, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense.

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakamme

On the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Six on Wishing is concluded.

Tecattālīsavattaṃ

The Forty-Three Observances

51. “Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammakatena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ[V 0.0049]. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā[T 1.0083]. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāro, seyyābhihāro, pādodakaṃ, pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sāditabbaṃ. Na pakatatto bhikkhu sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na diṭṭhivipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na ājīvavipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na bhikkhu bhikkhūhi bhedetabbo na bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedetabbā (syā.), na gihiddhajo dhāretabbo, na titthiyaddhajo dhāretabbo, na titthiyā sevitabbā; bhikkhū sevitabbā, bhikkhusikkhāya sikkhitabbaṃ bhikkhusikkhā sikkhitabbā (syā.). Na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse [M 0.0053] vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ, pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, na pakatatto bhikkhu āsādetabbo anto vā bahi vā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo [P 2.0023] paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti.

51. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct: He should not give higher ordination; he should not give dependence; he should not have a novice attend on him; he should not consent to an appointment as an instructor of nuns; even if appointed, he should not admonish the nuns. The offense for which the Saṅgha has performed the act of suspension for not seeing an offense—that offense should not be committed, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is more wicked than that. The act should not be criticized; those who performed the act should not be criticized. He should not accept from a bhikkhu in good standing: salutation, rising up, the gesture of joined palms, proper duties, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiper, the receiving of the bowl and robe, or the rubbing of the back while bathing. He should not accuse a bhikkhu in good standing of a corruption of virtue, a corruption of conduct, or a corruption of view. He should not cause a bhikkhu to be divided from the bhikkhus. He should not wear the banner of householders, nor should he wear the banner of sectarians. He should not associate with sectarians; he should associate with bhikkhus. He should train in the training of the bhikkhus. He should not dwell with a bhikkhu in good standing under the same roof in a dwelling, nor under the same roof in a non-dwelling, nor under the same roof in either a dwelling or a non-dwelling. On seeing a bhikkhu in good standing, he should rise from his seat. He should not harass a bhikkhu in good standing, whether inside or outside. He should not suspend the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, nor should he suspend the Pavāraṇā. He should not be made subject to an injunction; an accusation should not be initiated against him; he should not be asked to grant an opportunity; he should not be admonished; he should not be reminded; he should not engage in formal acts with the bhikkhus.

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakamme

In the act of suspension for not seeing an offense.

Tecattālīsavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The forty-three observances are concluded.

52. Atha kho saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ akāsi – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. So saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammakato tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tattha bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ na [T 1.0084] sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na sakkariṃsu, na garu kariṃsu na garukariṃsu (ka.), na mānesuṃ, na pūjesuṃ. So bhikkhūhi asakkariyamāno agarukariyamāno amāniyamāno apūjiyamāno asakkārapakato tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tatthapi bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ na sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na [V 0.0050] sakkariṃsu, na garuṃ kariṃsu, na mānesuṃ, na pūjesuṃ. So bhikkhūhi asakkariyamāno agarukariyamāno amāniyamāno apūjiyamāno asakkārapakato tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tatthapi bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ na sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na sakkariṃsu, na garuṃ kariṃsu, na mānesuṃ, na pūjesuṃ. So bhikkhūhi asakkariyamāno agarukariyamāno amāniyamāno apūjiyamāno asakkārapakato punadeva kosambiṃ paccāgañchi. So sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti – “ahaṃ, āvuso, saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe…. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

52. Then the Saṅgha performed the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Channa for not seeing his offense—non-communion with the Saṅgha. Having been subjected to the act of suspension by the Saṅgha for not seeing his offense, he left that monastery and went to another. There the bhikkhus neither paid homage to him nor rose up for him; they did not perform the act of placing their palms together in reverence or the act of proper respect; they did not respect, revere, esteem, or venerate him. Being thus not respected, not revered, not esteemed, and not venerated by the bhikkhus, and being afflicted by disrespect, he left that monastery too and went to another. There too the bhikkhus neither paid homage to him nor rose up for him; they did not perform the act of placing their palms together in reverence or the act of proper respect; they did not respect, revere, esteem, or venerate him. Being thus not respected, not revered, not esteemed, and not venerated by the bhikkhus, and being afflicted by disrespect, he left that monastery too and went to another. There too the bhikkhus neither paid homage to him nor rose up for him; they did not perform the act of placing their palms together in reverence or the act of proper respect; they did not respect, revere, esteem, or venerate him. Being thus not respected, not revered, not esteemed, and not venerated by the bhikkhus, and being afflicted by disrespect, he returned again to Kosambī. He conducts himself properly, humbles himself, and practices the conduct for his rehabilitation. He approached the bhikkhus and said: “Venerable sirs, I have been subjected to the act of suspension by the Saṅgha for not seeing my offense. I am now conducting myself properly, humbling myself, and practicing the conduct for my rehabilitation. How should I now conduct myself?” The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Well then, Bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha revoke the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Channa for not seeing his offense.”

Nappaṭippassambhetabba-tecattālīsakaṃ

The Forty-Three Reasons for Not Revoking

53. “Pañcahi[M 0.0054], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ [T 1.0085] deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

53. O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He gives ordination, he gives dependence, he has a novice attend on him, he consents to the appointment as an instructor of bhikkhunīs, and though appointed, he admonishes the bhikkhunīs. Indeed, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

pari. 420 “Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He commits the offense for which the Saṅgha has carried out the act of suspension for not seeing an offense, or another similar one, or one even more wicked than that; he disparages the act, and he disparages those who carried out the act. Indeed, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ sādiyati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He consents to the salutation, the rising up for, the act of reverential salutation with joined palms, the act of respect, and the offering of a seat from a bhikkhu in good standing. Indeed, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa [P 2.0024] bhikkhuno seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaṃ[T 1.0086], nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sādiyati – imehi kho, bhikkhave[V 0.0051], pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He accepts from a bhikkhu in good standing the bringing forward of a bed, the setting out of water for the feet and a footstool, the placing of a potsherd for rubbing the feet, the receiving of the bowl and robes, and the service of scrubbing the back when bathing. Indeed, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, diṭṭhivipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, ājīvavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, bhikkhuṃ bhikkhū (sī. syā.) bhikkhūhi bhedeti – imehi [M 0.0055] kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He accuses a bhikkhu in good standing of corruption of virtue, of corruption of conduct, of corruption of view, and of corruption of livelihood; and he causes division among the bhikkhus. Indeed, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Gihiddhajaṃ dhāreti, titthiyaddhajaṃ dhāreti, titthiye sevati; bhikkhū na sevati, bhikkhusikkhāya na sikkhati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He bears the insignia of a householder, he bears the insignia of a sectarian, he associates with sectarians, he does not associate with bhikkhus, and he does not train in the training of bhikkhus. Indeed, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vasati, ekacchanne anāvāse vasati, ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vasati; pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā na vuṭṭhāti; pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ āsādeti [T 1.0087] anto vā bahi vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He dwells with a bhikkhu in good standing in a residence under one roof, he dwells in a non-residence under one roof, he dwells in either a residence or a non-residence under one roof, upon seeing a bhikkhu in good standing, he does not rise from his seat, and he harasses a bhikkhu in good standing, whether inside or outside. Indeed, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, okāsaṃ kāreti, codeti, sāreti, bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with eight factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked. He suspends the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, he suspends the Pavāraṇā, he admonishes, he establishes a ground for accusation, he requests an opportunity to speak, he charges, he reminds, and he incites bhikkhus. Indeed, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these eight factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should not be revoked.

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakamme

In the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

Nappaṭippassambhetabba-tecattālīsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Forty-Three Cases Wherein It Should Not Be Revoked is completed.

Paṭippassambhetabba-tecattālīsakaṃ

The Forty-three Cases Wherein It Should be Revoked

54. “Pañcahi[V 0.0052], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa [M 0.0056] bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

54. O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not give ordination, he does not give dependence, he does not have a novice attend on him, he does not consent to the appointment as an instructor of bhikkhunīs, and even when appointed, he does not admonish the bhikkhunīs. Indeed, O monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ [T 1.0088] āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not fall into the offense for which the Saṅgha has performed the act of suspension for not seeing an offense, nor another similar one, nor one more evil than it; he does not censure the act, nor does he censure those who performed the act. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ sādiyati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not consent to the paying of homage, the rising up to greet, the raising of joined palms in salutation, proper service, or the offering of a seat from a monk in a normal state. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sādiyati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not consent to the offering of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a potsherd for rubbing the feet, the receiving of the bowl and robes, or the scrubbing of his back in the bath from a monk in a normal state. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na diṭṭhivipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na ājīvavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na bhikkhuṃ [T 1.0089] bhikkhūhi bhedeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not charge a monk in good standing with corruption of virtue, nor with corruption of conduct, nor with corruption of view, nor with corruption of livelihood; nor does he divide a monk from the monks. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aparehipi[V 0.0053], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na gihiddhajaṃ dhāreti, na titthiyaddhajaṃ dhāreti, na titthiye sevati, bhikkhū sevati, bhikkhusikkhāya [M 0.0057] sikkhati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not wear the emblem of a householder, nor the emblem of a sectarian; he does not associate with sectarians, but associates with monks; he trains in the training of the monks. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vasati, na ekacchanne anāvāse vasati, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vasati, pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhāti, na pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ āsādeti anto vā bahi vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not dwell with a monk in good standing under one roof in a dwelling; he does not dwell under one roof in a non-dwelling; he does not dwell under one roof in a dwelling or a non-dwelling; upon seeing a monk in good standing, he rises from his seat; he does not treat a monk in good standing with disrespect, either inside or outside. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ [T 1.0090] paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for a monk endowed with eight factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked. He does not suspend the Uposatha for a monk in good standing, nor the Pavāraṇā; he does not make one subject to censure, nor initiate an accusation, nor cause an opportunity to be requested, nor admonish, nor remind; nor does he set him at odds with the monks. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a monk endowed with these eight factors, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense should be revoked.

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakamme

In the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

Paṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Forty-three Cases for Revocation is completed.

55. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tena, bhikkhave, channena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

55. And, bhikkhus, this is how it should be revoked. That bhikkhu, Channa, having approached the Sangha, should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined hands, and should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I, for whom the act of suspension for not seeing an offense has been carried out by the Sangha, am conducting myself properly, I am humbling myself, I am practicing for rehabilitation, and I request the revocation of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should then inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyassa [V 0.0054] kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati[M 0.0058]. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, for whom the act of suspension for not seeing an offense has been carried out by the Sangha, is conducting himself properly, he is humbling himself, he is practicing for rehabilitation, and he requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. If it seems fit to the Sangha, the Sangha should revoke the act of suspension for the bhikkhu Channa for not seeing an offense. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā [T 1.0091] vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not seeing an offense, is conducting himself properly, he humbles himself, he is conducting himself so as to be rehabilitated, and he requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. The Saṅgha revokes the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing an offense. If any venerable one approves of the revocation of the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing an offense, let him be silent. If any does not approve, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghena, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

A second time I speak on this matter... A third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not seeing an offense, is conducting himself properly, he humbles himself, he is conducting himself so as to be rehabilitated, and he requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. The Saṅgha revokes the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing an offense. If any venerable one approves of the revocation of the act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing an offense, let him be silent. If any does not approve, let him speak.

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ saṅghena channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The act of suspension for the monk Channa for not seeing an offense has been revoked by the Saṅgha. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.

Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth act of suspension, for not seeing an offense, is concluded.

6. Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ

6. The act of suspension for not making amends for an offense.

56. Tena [P 2.0025] samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… [T 1.0092] te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchissati āpattiṃ paṭikātu”nti? Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.
