56. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Kosambī at Ghosita's monastery. Now at that time, the venerable Channa, having fallen into an offense, did not wish to make amends for the offense. Those monks who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Channa, having fallen into an offense, not wish to make amends for the offense?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha [M 0.0059][V 0.0055] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātu”nti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchissati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karotu – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ – paṭhamaṃ channo bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having caused the community of monks to assemble, questioned the monks: “Monks, is it true, as is said, that the monk Channa, having fallen into an offense, does not wish to make amends for the offense?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “...How indeed, monks, could that worthless man, having fallen into an offense, not wish to make amends for the offense? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... Having rebuked him and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha carry out the act of suspension against the monk Channa for not making amends for his offense, making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha. And, monks, it is to be done in this way: First, the monk Channa is to be accused; having been accused, he is to be reminded; having been reminded, he is to be charged with the offense; having been charged with the offense, the Saṅgha is to be informed by a competent and capable monk:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ [T 1.0093] paṭikātuṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having fallen into an offense, does not wish to make amends for the offense. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should carry out the act of suspension against the monk Channa for not making amends for his offense, making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having fallen into an offense, does not wish to make amends for the offense. The Saṅgha carries out against the monk Channa the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense, making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha. If the carrying out of the act of suspension against the monk Channa for not making amends for an offense—making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha—is approved of by any venerable one, let him be silent. Whoever does not approve, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

A second time I speak on this matter... A third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Channa, having fallen into an offense, does not wish to make amends for the offense. The Saṅgha carries out against the monk Channa the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense, making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha. If the carrying out of the act of suspension against the monk Channa for not making amends for an offense—making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha—is approved of by any venerable one, let him be silent. Whoever does not approve, let him speak.

“Kataṃ saṅghena channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

The act of suspension against the monk Channa for not making amends for an offense—making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha—has been carried out by the Saṅgha. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I bear this in mind.

“Āvāsaparamparañca[M 0.0060][V 0.0056], bhikkhave, saṃsatha – ‘channo bhikkhu, saṅghena āpattiyā channo bhikkhu āpattiyā (sī. ka.) appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato – asambhogaṃ saṅghenā’ti.

And, monks, you should announce from one residence to the next: ‘The monk Channa has had the act of suspension carried out against him by the Saṅgha for not making amends for an offense, making him not to be in communion with the Saṅgha.’

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Group of Twelve on Unlawful Acts

57. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā [T 1.0094] appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

57. Monks, an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense, when endowed with three factors, is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled. It is carried out not in the presence of the monk; it is carried out without having questioned him; it is carried out without his admission. Indeed, monks, an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense, when endowed with these three factors, is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Discipline, and is improperly settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0095] desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… asāretvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, endowed with three other factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled. It is done for a non-offense; it is done for an offense not requiring confession; it is done for an offense that has been confessed... it is done without having admonished; it is done without having reminded; it is done without having charged him with an offense... it is done in his absence; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done without having asked; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done without his acknowledgement; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done for a non-offense; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done for an offense not requiring confession; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done for an offense that has been confessed; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done without having admonished; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done without having reminded; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly... it is done without having charged him with an offense; it is done unlawfully; it is done by an incomplete assembly. Indeed, monks, endowed with these three factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense is an act not in accordance with the Dhamma, an act not in accordance with the Vinaya, and is improperly settled.

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakamme

Regarding the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends for an Offense

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on the Twelve Unlawful Acts is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Section on the Twelve Lawful Acts

58. “Tīhi[M 0.0061], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ [V 0.0057] dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

58. Monks, an act of suspension for not remedying an offense, when endowed with three factors, is a lawful act, a Vinaya act, and is well-settled. It is done in the presence, it is done after questioning, it is done after acknowledgment. Indeed, monks, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not remedying an offense is a lawful act, a Vinaya act, and is well-settled.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0096] codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0097] adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of suspension for not remedying an offense, when endowed with another three factors, is a lawful act, a Vinaya act, and is well-settled. It is done for an offense; it is done for an offense that should be confessed; it is done for an offense that has not been confessed… It is done after admonishing; it is done after reminding; it is done after charging with an offense… It is done in the presence, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done after questioning, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done after acknowledgment, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done for an offense, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done for an offense that should be confessed, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done for an offense that has not been confessed, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done after admonishing, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done after reminding, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly… It is done after charging with an offense, it is done according to the Dhamma, it is done by a complete assembly. Indeed, monks, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not remedying an offense is a lawful act, a Vinaya act, and is well-settled.

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakamme

Regarding the Act of Suspension for Not Remedying an Offense

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on the Twelve Lawful Acts is concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ

The Section of Six on Wishing

59. pari. 323 “Tīhi[M 0.0062], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

59. Monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with three factors, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should perform an act of suspension for an unrectified offense. He is quarrelsome, contentious, argumentative, loquacious, and a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is without limit; he dwells associating with householders in ways that are unsuitable. Indeed, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should perform an act of suspension for an unrectified offense.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā [V 0.0058] appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya[T 1.0098]. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should perform an act of suspension for an unrectified offense. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in conduct, and corrupt in view. Indeed, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should perform an act of suspension for an unrectified offense.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should perform an act of suspension for an unrectified offense. He speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, he speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, and he speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, for a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, should perform an act of suspension for an unrectified offense.

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out an act of suspension against three bhikkhus for not remedying an offense. One is a maker of quarrels, a maker of strife, a maker of arguments, a maker of much talk, and a maker of legal issues in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is without limit in his offenses; one lives associated with householders in ways that are unsuitable. Indeed, bhikkhus, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out an act of suspension against these three bhikkhus for not remedying an offense.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno [M 0.0063] hoti, eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko [T 1.0099] atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out an act of suspension against another three bhikkhus for not remedying an offense. One is corrupt in the higher virtue; one is corrupt in conduct; one is corrupt in view. Indeed, bhikkhus, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out an act of suspension against these three bhikkhus for not remedying an offense.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Bhikkhus, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out an act of suspension against another three bhikkhus for not remedying an offense. One speaks dispraise of the Buddha; one speaks dispraise of the Dhamma; one speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, bhikkhus, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out an act of suspension against these three bhikkhus for not remedying an offense.

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakamme

In the Act of Suspension for Not Remedying an Offense

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Group of Six on Wishing is concluded.

Tecattālīsavattaṃ

The Forty-Three Duties

60. “Āpattiyā [V 0.0059] appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammakatena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāro, seyyābhihāro, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sāditabbaṃ. Na pakatatto bhikkhu sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo[T 1.0100], na ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na diṭṭhivipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na ājīvavipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo, na bhikkhu bhikkhūhi bhedetabbo. Na gihiddhajo dhāretabbo, na titthiyaddhajo dhāretabbo, na titthiyā sevitabbā; bhikkhū sevitabbā, bhikkhusikkhāya sikkhitabbaṃ. Na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā [M 0.0064] anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ, pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, na pakatatto bhikkhu āsādetabbo anto vā bahi vā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti.

60. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu on whom the act of suspension for not remedying an offense has been carried out should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct: He should not give the higher ordination; he should not give dependence; he should not have a novice attend on him; he should not consent to the appointment as an exhorter of bhikkhunīs; and even if appointed, he should not exhort the bhikkhunīs. The offense for which the Saṅgha has carried out the act of suspension for not remedying an offense—that offense should not be committed, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is more wicked than that. The act should not be criticized; those who carried out the act should not be criticized. He should not consent to receiving from a bhikkhu in good standing the paying of homage, rising up for him, the act of reverential salutation, the act of proper respect, the bringing of a seat, the bringing of a sleeping place, the placing of water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-rubbing tile, the receiving of his bowl and robe, or the service of rubbing his back while bathing. A bhikkhu in good standing should not be denounced by him for a corruption of virtue, nor for a corruption of conduct, nor for a corruption of view, nor for a corruption of livelihood. He should not cause a bhikkhu to be divided from other bhikkhus. The banner of householders should not be worn; the banner of sectarians should not be worn; sectarians should not be associated with. Bhikkhus should be associated with; he should train in the training of the bhikkhus. He should not dwell with a bhikkhu in good standing under one roof in a residence, nor under one roof in a non-residence, nor under one roof in either a residence or a non-residence. Having seen a bhikkhu in good standing, he should rise from his seat. He should not disparage a bhikkhu in good standing, whether inside or outside. He should not suspend the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing, nor the Pavāraṇā. He should not be made subject to an injunction; he should not initiate a formal dispute; he should not be asked to grant leave; he should not accuse; he should not remind; he should not associate with the bhikkhus.

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakamme

In the Act of Suspension for Not Remedying an Offense

Tecattālīsavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The forty-three duties are concluded.

61. Atha kho saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ akāsi – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. So saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tattha bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ na sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na sakkariṃsu, na garuṃ kariṃsu, na mānesuṃ, na pūjesuṃ. So bhikkhūhi asakkariyamāno agarukariyamāno amāniyamāno apūjiyamāno asakkārapakato tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ [T 1.0101] agamāsi. Tatthapi bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ na sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na sakkariṃsu, na garuṃ kariṃsu, na mānesuṃ, na pūjesuṃ. So bhikkhūhi asakkariyamāno agarukariyamāno amāniyamāno [V 0.0060] apūjiyamāno asakkārapakato tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tatthapi bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ na sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na sakkariṃsu, na garuṃ kariṃsu, na mānesuṃ, na pūjesuṃ. So bhikkhūhi asakkariyamāno agarukariyamāno amāniyamāno apūjiyamāno asakkārapakato punadeva kosambiṃ paccāgañchi. So sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti – “ahaṃ, āvuso, saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe…. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

61. Then the Saṅgha imposed the act of suspension on the bhikkhu Channa for not remedying his offense—namely, non-communion with the Saṅgha. Having had the act of suspension imposed on him by the Saṅgha for not remedying his offense, he left that residence and went to another residence. There the bhikkhus neither paid him homage, nor rose for him, nor performed the gesture of joined palms, nor performed proper duties, nor honored him, nor respected him, nor esteemed him, nor venerated him. Not being honored, respected, esteemed, or venerated by the bhikkhus, and being subjected to disrespect, he left that residence too and went to another residence. There also the bhikkhus neither paid him homage, nor rose for him, nor performed the gesture of joined palms, nor performed proper duties, nor honored him, nor respected him, nor esteemed him, nor venerated him. Not being honored, respected, esteemed, or venerated by the bhikkhus, and being subjected to disrespect, he left that residence too and went to another residence. There also the bhikkhus neither paid him homage, nor rose for him, nor performed the gesture of joined palms, nor performed proper duties, nor honored him, nor respected him, nor esteemed him, nor venerated him. Not being honored, respected, esteemed, or venerated by the bhikkhus, and being subjected to disrespect, he returned once more to Kosambī. He behaved properly, lowered his pride, and practiced for rehabilitation. Approaching the bhikkhus, he said: 'Venerable sirs, having had the act of suspension imposed on me by the Saṅgha for not remedying my offense, I now behave properly, I lower my pride, and I am practicing for rehabilitation. How should I now proceed?' The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Well then, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha rescind the act of suspension imposed on the bhikkhu Channa for not remedying his offense.'

Nappaṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ

The Forty-three on Not Revoking

62. “Pañcahi[M 0.0065], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

62. “Monks, for a monk endowed with five factors, on account of not making amends for an offense, the act of suspension should not be revoked. He confers ordination, he gives dependence, he has a novice attend on him, he consents to the appointment as an instructor of nuns, and having been appointed, he instructs nuns. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, on account of not making amends for an offense, the act of suspension should not be revoked.

pari. 420 “Aparehipi[T 1.0102], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati…pe… pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ sādiyati…pe… pakatattassa bhikkhuno seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sādiyati…pe… pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, diṭṭhivipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, ājīvavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, bhikkhuṃ bhikkhūhi bhedeti…pe… gihiddhajaṃ dhāreti, titthiyaddhajaṃ dhāreti, titthiye sevati, bhikkhū na sevati, bhikkhusikkhāya na sikkhati…pe… pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vasati, ekacchanne anāvāse vasati, ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vasati, pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā na vuṭṭhāti, pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ āsādeti anto vā [V 0.0061] bahi vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme[T 1.0103], ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should not be revoked. He commits the very offense for which the Saṅgha carried out the act of suspension for not making amends, or another similar to it, or one even more wicked; he disparages the act, he disparages those who performed the act… He delights in a regular monk’s paying of homage, rising up, reverential salutation, proper duties, and offering of a seat… He delights in a regular monk’s offering of a bed, foot-water, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, taking of his bowl and robe, and rubbing of his back while bathing… He accuses a regular monk of corruption in virtue, corruption in conduct, corruption in view, or corruption in livelihood; he causes a monk to be divided from the monks… He wears the banner of a householder, the banner of a sectarian; he associates with sectarians, he does not associate with monks; he does not train in the training for monks… He dwells under the same roof with a regular monk in a residence, under the same roof in a non-residence, or under the same roof in either a residence or a non-residence; on seeing a regular monk, he does not rise from his seat; he harasses a regular monk, whether inside or outside. Monks, indeed, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should not be revoked.”

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, okāsaṃ kāreti, codeti, sāreti, bhikkhūhi sampayojeti [M 0.0066] – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Monks, for a monk endowed with eight factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should not be revoked. He obstructs a monk in good standing from the Uposatha, he obstructs the Pavāraṇā, he makes himself liable to admonition, he institutes a charge, he has an opportunity made, he accuses, he reminds, he involves other monks. Monks, for a monk endowed with these eight factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should not be revoked.”

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakamme

In the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends for an Offense

Nappaṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Forty-three on What Should Not Be Revoked is completed.

Paṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ

The Forty-three on What Should Be Rescinded

63. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

63. “Monks, for a monk endowed with five factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should be rescinded. He does not confer ordination; he does not give dependence; he does not have a novice attend on him; he does not consent to the appointment to advise nuns; and even when appointed, he does not advise the nuns. Monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should be rescinded.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ[T 1.0104]; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati…pe… na pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ sādiyati…pe… na pakatattassa bhikkhuno seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sādiyati…pe… na pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na diṭṭhivipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na ājīvavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, na bhikkhuṃ bhikkhūhi bhedeti…pe… na gihiddhajaṃ dhāreti, na titthiyaddhajaṃ dhāreti, na titthiye sevati, bhikkhū sevati, bhikkhusikkhāya sikkhati…pe… na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vasati, na ekacchanne anāvāse vasati, na ekacchanne [V 0.0062] āvāse vā anāvāse vā vasati, pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhāti, na pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ āsādeti anto vā bahi vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should be rescinded. He does not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha has carried out the act of suspension for not making amends, nor another similar offense, nor one more wicked than that; he does not disparage the act, nor does he disparage those who carried out the act... He does not delight in a monk in good standing’s paying of homage, rising up, reverential salutation, proper duties, or offering of a seat... He does not delight in a monk in good standing’s offering of a bed, foot-water, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, the receiving of his bowl and robes, or back-rubbing while bathing... He does not accuse a monk in good standing of corruption in virtue, nor of corruption in conduct, nor of corruption in view, nor of corruption in livelihood; he does not cause division among monks... He does not wear the banner of householders, nor the banner of sectarians; he does not associate with sectarians, he associates with monks, he trains in the training for monks... He does not dwell with a monk in good standing in a residence under one roof, nor in a non-residence under one roof, nor in a residence or a non-residence under one roof; upon seeing a monk in good standing, he rises from his seat; he does not harass a monk in good standing, whether inside or outside. Monks, indeed, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should be rescinded.”

“Aṭṭhahi[M 0.0067], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā [T 1.0105] appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should be rescinded for a bhikkhu endowed with eight factors. He does not suspend the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing; he does not suspend the Pavāraṇā; he does not make another subject to his instruction; he does not initiate a charge; he does not make another ask for an opportunity to speak; he does not admonish; he does not remind; he does not associate with bhikkhus. Bhikkhus, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense should be rescinded for a bhikkhu endowed with these eight factors.

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakamme

In the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends for an Offense

Paṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Forty-three Cases Concerning What Should Be Rescinded is completed.

64. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tena bhikkhave, channena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

64. And, bhikkhus, it should be rescinded in this way. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu Channa, having approached the Sangha, should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his hands in añjali, and should speak thus: ‘Venerable Sirs, I, having been subjected to the act of suspension by the Sangha for not making amends for an offense, am conducting myself correctly, I am casting off my pride, I am conducting myself for my rehabilitation, and I request the rescinding of the act of suspension for not making amends for the offense.’ The request should be made a second time. The request should be made a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should then inform the Sangha thus:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno[T 1.0106], āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, having been subjected to the act of suspension by the Sangha for not making amends for an offense, is conducting himself correctly, is casting off his pride, is conducting himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. If the time is right for the Sangha, the Sangha should rescind the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense against the bhikkhu Channa. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā [V 0.0063] appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, upon whom the Sangha has imposed the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense, is conducting himself correctly, humbles himself, is conducting himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. The Sangha revokes the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for the bhikkhu Channa. To whichever venerable one the revocation of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for the bhikkhu Channa is agreeable, he should be silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi [M 0.0068] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghena, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter: Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, upon whom the Sangha has imposed the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense, is conducting himself correctly, humbles himself, is conducting himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. The Sangha revokes the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for the bhikkhu Channa. To whichever venerable one the revocation of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for the bhikkhu Channa is agreeable, he should be silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ saṅghena channassa bhikkhuno, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The act of suspension for the bhikkhu Channa for not making amends for an offense has been revoked by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.”

Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth act of suspension for not making amends for an offense is concluded.

7. Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ

7. The Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing an Evil View

65. idaṃ vatthu pāci. 417; ma. ni. 234 ādayo Tena [T 1.0107] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena ariṭṭhassa nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa gandhabādhipubbassa (ka.) evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti. Assosuṃ kho sambahulā bhikkhū ariṭṭhassa nāma kira bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Upasaṅkamitvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etadavocuṃ – “saccaṃ kira te, āvuso ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti? “Evaṃbyā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme [M 0.0069] antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti.

65. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Now at that time, a bhikkhu named Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, had conceived this evil view: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be impediments are not in fact impediments for one who engages in them.’ Many bhikkhus heard that the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, had conceived this evil view: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be impediments are not in fact impediments for one who engages in them.’ Then those bhikkhus approached the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer. Having approached, they said this to the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer: ‘Is it true, friend Ariṭṭha, that you have conceived this evil view: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be impediments are not in fact impediments for one who engages in them”?’ ‘Just so, friends. As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be impediments are not in fact impediments for one who engages in them.’

“Māvuso [V 0.0064] ariṭṭha, evaṃ avaca. Mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ [T 1.0108] abbhācikkhanaṃ (ka.). Na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso ariṭṭha, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā bahūpāyāsā (sī. syā.), ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā, bahudukkhā bahūpāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Maṃsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā…pe… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā…pe… aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā [P 2.0026] bhagavatā… asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā, bahudukkhā bahūpāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo”ti.

“Do not speak thus, friend Ariṭṭha. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus. In many ways, friend Ariṭṭha, the Blessed One has declared things that are impediments to be impediments. And they are indeed sufficient to be an impediment for one who engages in them. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to have little satisfaction, to have much suffering and much vexation; herein the danger is greater. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a skeleton, to have much suffering and much vexation; herein the danger is greater. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a piece of flesh… like a grass torch… like a pit of glowing embers… like a dream… like borrowed goods… like a fruit-bearing tree… like a butcher's block… like a spear and stake… like a snake’s head—to have much suffering and much vexation; herein the danger is greater.”

Evampi kho ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tehi bhikkhūhi vuccamāno tatheva taṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati – “evaṃbyā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti. Yato ca kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha [T 1.0109] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira te, ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti? “Evaṃbyā kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti.

Even so, when the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, was spoken to by those bhikkhus, he, just as before, forcefully and with wrong grasp, adhered to that evil view and declared: ‘Indeed, friends, this is how I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One: that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not sufficient to be an obstruction for one who engages in them.’ And when those bhikkhus were unable to make the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, desist from that evil view, they then approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this matter, had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assembled and questioned the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer: ‘Is it true, Ariṭṭha, as is said, that such an evil view has arisen in you—that you understand the Dhamma taught by me in such a way that those things declared by me to be obstructive are not sufficient to be an obstruction for one who engages in them?’ ‘Indeed, Venerable Sir, this is how I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One: that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not sufficient to be an obstruction for one who engages in them.’”

“Kassa [M 0.0070] nu kho nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi? Nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā? Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā mayā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Maṃsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā…pe… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā…pe… yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā [V 0.0065] mayā… sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Atha ca pana tvaṃ, moghapurisa, attanā duggahitena duggahitena diṭṭhigatena (syā.) amhe ceva abbhācikkhasi, attānañca khaṇasi[T 1.0110], bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavasi. Tañhi te, moghapurisa, bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karotu – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Evañca pana bhikkhave kātabbaṃ – paṭhamaṃ ariṭṭho bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Foolish man, for whom do you claim to understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way? Foolish man, have I not in many ways declared things that are impediments to be impediments? And they are indeed sufficient to be an impediment for one who engages in them. I have declared sensual pleasures to be of little satisfaction, to be full of suffering, full of vexation, and the danger in them is greater. I have declared sensual pleasures to be like a skeleton, full of suffering, full of vexation, and the danger in them is greater. I have declared sensual pleasures to be like a lump of flesh… like a grass torch… like a pit of glowing embers… like a dream… like borrowed goods… like fruit on a tree… like a butcher's block… like a spear and stake… like a snake’s head—full of suffering, full of vexation, and the danger in them is greater. Yet you, foolish man, by your wrong grasp, not only misrepresent us but also ruin yourself and produce much demerit. This, foolish man, will lead to your long-term harm and suffering. This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the unconfident, nor for the increase of confidence in the confident.” Having rebuked him… and given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha perform the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view—an act of non-communion with the Saṅgha. And this, bhikkhus, is how it should be done: First, the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha should be admonished. Having admonished him, he should be reminded. Having reminded him, he should be charged with the offense. Having charged him with the offense, a competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:”

66. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ [P 2.0027] uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyāti. So taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Esā ñatti.

66. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, has conceived such an evil view: ‘This is how I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One: that those things spoken of as obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to be an obstruction for one who engages in them.’ He does not relinquish that view. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha perform the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view, entailing non-communion with the Saṅgha. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā [M 0.0071] yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyāti. So taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na paṭinissajjati[T 1.0111]. Saṅgho ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Yassāyasmato khamati ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, has conceived such an evil view: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things spoken of as obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to be an obstruction for one who engages in them.’ He does not relinquish that view. The Saṅgha performs the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view, which is non-communion with the Saṅgha. Any venerable one who approves of the performance of the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view—which is non-communion with the Saṅgha—should remain silent. Any who does not approve should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyāti. So taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti – asambhogaṃ [V 0.0066] saṅghena. Yassāyasmato khamati ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa karaṇaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, has conceived such an evil view: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things spoken of as obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to be an obstruction for one who engages in them.’ He does not relinquish that view. The Saṅgha performs the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view, which is non-communion with the Saṅgha. Any venerable one who approves of the performance of the act of suspension against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view—which is non-communion with the Saṅgha—should remain silent. Any who does not approve should speak.”

“Kataṃ saṅghena ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

“The act of suspension has been performed by the Saṅgha against the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, for not relinquishing his evil view, which is non-communion with the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I record it.”

“Āvāsaparamparañca, bhikkhave, saṃsatha – ‘ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo, saṅghena pāpikāya gaddhabādhipubbo pāpikāya (sī. ka.) diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge[T 1.0112], ukkhepanīyakammakato – asambhogaṃ saṅghenā’”ti.

“And, bhikkhus, announce from residence to residence: ‘The bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, has been subjected to an act of suspension by the Saṅgha for not relinquishing his evil view, which is non-communion with the Saṅgha.’”

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelvefold Section on Unlawful Acts

67. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya [M 0.0072] diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

67. “Bhikkhus, endowed with three factors, an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is improperly settled. It is performed in one's absence, it is performed without questioning, and it is performed without an admission. Indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is improperly settled.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, asāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… asammukhā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0113] anāpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… acodetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… asāretvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ anāropetvā kataṃ hoti, adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave[V 0.0067], tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

“Bhikkhus, endowed with three other factors, an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is improperly settled. It is performed when there is no offense; it is performed for an offense not requiring confession; it is performed for an offense that has been confessed… It is performed without having censured; it is performed without having reminded; it is performed without having charged with an offense… It is performed not in the presence, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed without questioning, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed without an admission, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed when there is no offense, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed for an offense not requiring confession, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed for an offense that has been confessed, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed without having censured, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed without having reminded, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly… It is performed without having charged with an offense, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly. Indeed, bhikkhus, endowed with these three factors, an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view is an unlawful act, an act contrary to the Vinaya, and is improperly settled.”

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakamme

Concerning the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing an Evil View

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelvefold Section on Unlawful Acts is concluded.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Twelvefold Section on Lawful Acts

68. “Tīhi[T 1.0114], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

68. “Bhikkhus, an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view, when endowed with three factors, is a lawful act, an act according to the Vinaya, and is well-settled. It is performed in one's presence, it is performed after questioning, and it is performed upon admission. Indeed, bhikkhus, an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view, when endowed with these three factors, is a lawful act, an act according to the Vinaya, and is well-settled.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0073], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, sāretvā kataṃ hoti, āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti…pe… sammukhā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭipucchā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ [T 1.0115] hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… adesitāya āpattiyā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… codetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… sāretvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti…pe… āpattiṃ āropetvā kataṃ hoti, dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

Furthermore, monks, an act of suspension for not relinquishing a bad view, when endowed with another three factors, is a legitimate act, a Vinaya act, and is well-settled. It is done for an offense, it is done for an offense requiring confession, and it is done for an unconfessed offense... It is done after accusing, it is done after reminding, and it is done after imputing an offense... It is done face-to-face, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done after questioning, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done upon admission, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done for an offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done for an offense requiring confession, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done for an unconfessed offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done after accusing, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done after reminding, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha... It is done after imputing an offense, it is done in accordance with the Dhamma, and it is done by a united Saṅgha. Monks, indeed, an act of suspension for not relinquishing a bad view, when endowed with these three factors, is a legitimate act, a Vinaya act, and is well-settled.

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakamme

On the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing a Bad View.

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelve Legitimate Acts are Concluded.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ

The Chapter of Six on Wishing

69. pari. 323 “Tīhi[V 0.0068], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno[T 1.0116]; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

69. Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on a bhikkhu endowed with three factors for not relinquishing a bad view. He is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, verbose, and creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, commits many offenses, and his offenses are without limit; he lives in association with householders, in inappropriate association with householders. Monks, indeed, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors for not relinquishing a bad view.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0074], bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors for not relinquishing a bad view. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in conduct through transgression, and corrupt in view through extremism. Monks, indeed, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors for not relinquishing a bad view.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on a bhikkhu endowed with three other factors for not relinquishing a bad view. He speaks disparagingly of the Buddha, he speaks disparagingly of the Dhamma, and he speaks disparagingly of the Saṅgha. Monks, indeed, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on a bhikkhu endowed with these three factors for not relinquishing a bad view.

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imesaṃ [T 1.0117] kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on three bhikkhus for not relinquishing a bad view. One is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, verbose, and creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, commits many offenses, and his offenses are without limit; one lives in association with householders, in inappropriate association with householders. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on these three bhikkhus for not relinquishing a bad view.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave[V 0.0069], tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on another three bhikkhus for not relinquishing a bad view. One is corrupt in higher virtue; one is corrupt in conduct through transgression; one is corrupt in view through extremism. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on these three bhikkhus for not relinquishing a bad view.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati [M 0.0075] – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissage, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on another three bhikkhus for not relinquishing a bad view. One speaks disparagingly of the Buddha, one speaks disparagingly of the Dhamma, and one speaks disparagingly of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, if the Saṅgha wishes, it may carry out the act of suspension on these three bhikkhus for not relinquishing a bad view.

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissage ukkhepanīyakamme

On the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing a Bad View.

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter of Six on Wishing is concluded.

Tecattālīsavattaṃ

The Forty-Three Duties

70. “Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakatena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā – na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo [T 1.0118] na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā…pe… na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti.

70. “Monks, a monk against whom an act of suspension has been carried out for not relinquishing a wicked view should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct: He should not give higher ordination; he should not give dependence; he should not have a novice attend on him; he should not accept the authorization to instruct nuns; even if authorized, he should not instruct the nuns. The offense on account of which the Saṅgha has carried out the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view—that offense should not be committed, nor another of a similar nature, nor one that is more wicked than that. The act should not be disparaged; those who carried out the act should not be disparaged... He should not stop the Uposatha of a monk in good standing; he should not stop the Pavāraṇā; he should not make another subject to a formal injunction; he should not initiate a formal dispute; he should not ask for an opportunity to speak; he should not admonish another; he should not remind another of an offense; he should not associate with the monks.”

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakamme

Concerning the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view.

Tecattālīsavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The forty-three duties are concluded.

71. Atha kho saṅgho ariṭṭhassa bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ akāsi – asambhogaṃ saṅghena. So saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato vibbhami. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo saṅghena[V 0.0070], pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato vibbhamissatī”ti? Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

71. Then the Saṅgha performed the act of suspension against the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture killer, for not relinquishing his wicked view—exclusion from association with the Saṅgha. Suspended by the Saṅgha for not relinquishing his wicked view, he disrobed. The monks who were of few wishes… were critical, condemned, and voiced their displeasure: “How could the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture killer, disrobe after the Saṅgha performed the act of suspension against him for not relinquishing his wicked view?” Then those monks informed the Blessed One of this matter.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, ariṭṭho [T 1.0119] bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo [M 0.0076] saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato vibbhamatī”ti vibbhamīti (sī. ka.)? “Saccaṃ [P 2.0028] bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato vibbhamissati? Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetu.

Then the Blessed One, in connection with this cause, on this occasion, having convened the community of monks, questioned the monks: “Monks, is it true, as has been heard, that the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, having been subjected to the act of suspension by the Saṅgha for not relinquishing a wicked view, is disrobing?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “… How indeed, monks, could that foolish man, having been subjected to the act of suspension by the Saṅgha for not relinquishing a wicked view, disrobe? This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of the unconvinced… Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Well then, monks, let the Saṅgha revoke the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view.”

Nappaṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ

The Section of Forty-three Cases on What Should Not Be Revoked

72. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissage, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

72. “Monks, for a monk endowed with five factors, the act of suspension performed for not relinquishing a wicked view should not be revoked. He gives higher ordination, he gives dependence, he has a novice attend on him, he consents to the appointment as an admonisher of nuns, and though appointed, he admonishes the nuns. Indeed, monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension performed for not relinquishing a wicked view should not be revoked.”

pari. 420 “Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ…pe…[T 1.0120].

“Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should not be revoked. He commits the offense for which the act of suspension was performed by the Saṅgha on account of not relinquishing a wicked view, or he commits another similar offense, or one even more wicked than that; he disparages the formal act, he disparages those who performed the formal act. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should not be revoked...”

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, savacanīyaṃ karoti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, okāsaṃ kāreti, codeti, sāreti[V 0.0071], bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with eight factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should not be revoked. He suspends the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in good standing; he suspends the Pavāraṇā; he makes another subject to a formal injunction; he initiates a formal dispute; he makes another ask for an opportunity to speak; he admonishes another; he reminds another of an offense; he associates with the monks. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these eight factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should not be revoked.”

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakamme

Regarding the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing a Wicked View

Nappaṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Forty-Three Cases on What Should Not Be Revoked is completed.

Paṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ

The Section of Forty-Three Cases on What Should Be Revoked

73. “Pañcahi[M 0.0077], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na upasampādeti, na nissayaṃ deti, na sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo na ovadati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

73. “Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should be revoked. He does not give the higher ordination; he does not give dependence; he does not have a novice attend on him; he does not consent to the appointment to admonish nuns; even when appointed, he does not admonish the nuns. Indeed, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should be revoked.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ[T 1.0121], tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ; kammaṃ na garahati, kammike na garahati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ…pe….

Furthermore, monks, for a monk endowed with another five factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should be revoked. He does not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha has carried out the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view, nor another similar to it, nor one more wicked than that; he does not disparage the act, nor does he disparage those who carried out the act. Monks, for a monk endowed with these five factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should be revoked…and so on.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposathaṃ ṭhapeti, na pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, na savacanīyaṃ karoti, na anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapeti, na okāsaṃ kāreti, na codeti, na sāreti, na bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetabbaṃ”.

Monks, for a monk endowed with eight factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should be revoked. He does not suspend the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, he does not suspend the Pavāraṇā, he does not perform the act of making another open to admonition, he does not initiate a formal charge, he does not make another ask for leave, he does not admonish, he does not remind, he does not associate with the monks. Monks, for a monk endowed with these eight factors, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view should be revoked.

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakamme

Regarding the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing a Wicked View

Paṭippassambhetabbatecattālīsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Forty-three Cases on What Should Be Revoked is concluded.

74. “Evañca [V 0.0072] pana, bhikkhave, paṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Tena, bhikkhave, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakatena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyassa [M 0.0078] kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ [T 1.0122] yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

74. And, monks, it should be revoked in this way.
