That monk, who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view, should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and should say this: ‘Venerable sirs, I, having been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view, am conducting myself properly, I cast down my pride, I am practicing the conduct that leads to release, and I request the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so, having been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view, is conducting himself properly, casts down his pride, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should revoke the act of suspension for the monk named so-and-so for not relinquishing a wicked view. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge[T 1.0123], ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so, having been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view, is conducting himself properly, casts down his pride, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view. The Saṅgha revokes the act of suspension for the monk named so-and-so for not relinquishing a wicked view. To whichever venerable one the revocation of the act of suspension for the monk named so-and-so for not relinquishing a wicked view is agreeable, he should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghena, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambheti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhi, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For a second time, I speak on this matter... For a third time, I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so, upon whom the act of suspension was imposed by the Saṅgha for not relinquishing a wicked view, is conducting himself properly, he has cast down his pride, is practicing the conduct that leads to release, and he requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view. The Saṅgha revokes the act of suspension for the monk named so-and-so for not relinquishing a wicked view. To whichever venerable one the revocation of the act of suspension for the monk named so-and-so for not relinquishing a wicked view is agreeable, let him be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Paṭippassaddhaṃ [V 0.0073] saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge, ukkhepanīyakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The act of suspension imposed on the monk named so-and-so for not relinquishing a wicked view has been revoked by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I take it.

Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh Act of Suspension, for not relinquishing a wicked view, is concluded.

Kammakkhandhako paṭhamo.

The First Khandhaka on Formal Acts is concluded.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū satta.

In this Khandhaka, there are seven cases.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Paṇḍulohitakā [M 0.0079] bhikkhū, sayaṃ bhaṇḍanakārakā;

Tādise upasaṅkamma, ussahiṃsu ca bhaṇḍane.

The Paṇḍulohitaka monks, themselves instigators of quarrels, having approached those of a similar nature, also incited them to quarrel.

Anuppannāpi jāyanti anuppannāni jāyanti (sī. syā.), uppannānipi vaḍḍhare uppannāni pavaḍḍhare (sī.), uppannāpi pavaḍḍhanti (ka.);

Appicchā pesalā bhikkhū, ujjhāyanti padassato parīsato (syā.), parassato (sī.).

Quarrels not yet arisen arise, and those already arisen increase; the monks of few wishes, who are fond of virtue, were critical at the sight of it.

Saddhammaṭṭhitiko buddho, sayambhū aggapuggalo;

Āṇāpesi tajjanīyakammaṃ sāvatthiyaṃ jino.

The Buddha, establisher of the True Dhamma, the Self-become, the supreme person, the Conqueror, enjoined the act of censure in Sāvatthī.

Asammukhāppaṭipucchāppaṭiññāya [T 1.0124] katañca yaṃ;

Anāpatti adesane, desitāya katañca yaṃ.

And that which is done not in the presence of the monk, without questioning him, without his admission; and that which is done when there is no offense, when it is not an offense to be confessed, or after it has been confessed.

Acodetvā asāretvā, anāropetvā ca yaṃ kataṃ;

Asammukhā adhammena, vaggena cāpi vaggenāpi ca (sī. syā.) yaṃ kataṃ.

And that which is done without accusing, without reminding, without charging with an offense; and also that which is done not in the presence of the monk, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly.

Appaṭipucchā adhammena, puna vaggena vaggenāpi ca (sī. syā.) yaṃ kataṃ;

Appaṭiññāya adhammena, vaggena cāpi vaggenāpi ca (sī. syā.) yaṃ kataṃ.

And that which is done without questioning, unlawfully, and again by an incomplete assembly; and also that which is done without an admission, unlawfully, and by an incomplete assembly.

Anāpatti anāpattiyā (sī. syā.) adhammena, vaggena

When there is no offense, unlawfully, by an incomplete assembly,

Cāpi vaggenāpi ca (sī. syā.) yaṃ kataṃ.

And also any act that has been performed.

Adesanāgāminiyā, adhammavaggameva ca.

For an offense not requiring confession, and only unlawfully and by an incomplete assembly.

Desitāya [V 0.0074] adhammena, vaggenāpi tatheva ca;

Acodetvā [P 2.0029] adhammena, vaggenāpi tatheva ca.

And whatever act was performed after the teaching had been given, unlawfully and by a faction, likewise; and whatever act was performed without an accusation, unlawfully and by a faction, likewise.

Asāretvā adhammena, vaggenāpi tatheva ca;

Anāropetvā adhammena, vaggenāpi tatheva ca.

And whatever act was performed without reminding, unlawfully and by a faction, likewise; and whatever act was performed without establishing the offense, unlawfully and by a faction, likewise.

Kaṇhavāranayeneva, sukkavāraṃ vijāniyā;

Saṅgho ākaṅkhamāno ca yassa tajjaniyaṃ kare.

By the method of the dark section, one should also know the bright section. The Saṅgha should perform the act of censure for whichever monk it wishes.

Bhaṇḍanaṃ bālo saṃsaṭṭho, adhisīle ajjhācāre;

Atidiṭṭhivipannassa, saṅgho tajjaniyaṃ kare.

The Saṅgha should perform the act of censure for one who is quarrelsome, foolish, associates with laypeople, is corrupt in virtue, corrupt in conduct, or corrupt in sublime view.

Buddhadhammassa [T 1.0125][M 0.0080] saṅghassa, avaṇṇaṃ yo ca bhāsati;

Tiṇṇannampi ca bhikkhūnaṃ, saṅgho tajjaniyaṃ kare.

And for one who speaks dispraise of the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha; for these three kinds of monks, the Saṅgha should perform the act of censure.

Bhaṇḍanaṃ kārako eko, bālo saṃsagganissito;

Adhisīle ajjhācāre, tatheva atidiṭṭhiyā.

One is a maker of quarrels, is foolish, relies on association with laypeople; another is corrupt in virtue, corrupt in conduct, and likewise corrupt in sublime view.

Buddhadhammassa saṅghassa, avaṇṇaṃ yo ca bhāsati;

Tajjanīyakammakato, evaṃ sammānuvattanā.

And for one who speaks dispraise of the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha—for such a monk upon whom the act of censure has been performed, this is how he should conduct himself well.

Upasampadanissayā, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhanā;

Ovādasammatenāpi, na kare tajjanīkato.

A monk who has been censured should not give ordination or dependence, have a novice attend upon him, or, even if appointed, give exhortation.

Nāpajje tañca āpattiṃ, tādisañca tato paraṃ;

Kammañca kammike cāpi, na garahe tathāvidho.

Such a one should not commit that offense, nor a similar one, nor a worse one. And he should not disparage the formal act or the monks who performed it.

Uposathaṃ pavāraṇaṃ, pakatattassa naṭṭhape;

Savacaniṃ na savacaniyaṃ (sī. syā.) anuvādo, okāso codanena ca.

He should not suspend the Uposatha or Pavāraṇā of a monk in good standing. He should not make another subject to instruction, nor admonish, nor ask for leave to speak, nor make an accusation.

Sāraṇaṃ [V 0.0075] sampayogañca, na kareyya tathāvidho;

Upasampadanissayā, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhanā.

Such a one should not remind another of an offense, nor cause dissension. He should not give ordination or dependence, nor have a novice attend upon him.

Ovādasammatenāpi, pañcahaṅgehi pañcaaṅgo (ka.) na sammati;

Tañcāpajjati āpattiṃ, tādisañca tato paraṃ.

Even if appointed to give exhortation—by these five factors he is not pacified. He commits that same offense, a similar one, and a worse one.

Kammañca kammike cāpi, garahanto na sammati;

Uposathaṃ [T 1.0126] pavāraṇaṃ, savacanīyā ca novādo.

And by disparaging the formal act and the monks who performed it, he is not pacified. By suspending the Uposatha, suspending the Pavāraṇā, making another subject to instruction, and by admonishing, he is not pacified.

Okāso codanañceva, sāraṇā sampayojanā;

Imehaṭṭhaṅgehi yo yutto, tajjanānupasammati.

Asking for leave, making an accusation, reminding, and causing dissension: whoever is endowed with these eight factors is not pacified from the act of censure.

Kaṇhavāranayeneva, sukkavāraṃ vijāniyā;

Bālo āpattibahulo, saṃsaṭṭhopi ca seyyaso.

By the method of the dark section, one should also know the bright section. Seyyasaka was foolish, had many offenses, and also associated with laypeople.

Niyassakammaṃ sambuddho, āṇāpesi mahāmuni;

Kīṭāgirismiṃ dve bhikkhū, assajipunabbasukā.

The Perfectly Enlightened One, the Great Sage, enjoined the act of subordination. In Kīṭāgiri were the two monks, Assaji and Punabbasuka.

Anācārañca [M 0.0081] vividhaṃ, ācariṃsu asaññatā;

Pabbājanīyaṃ sambuddho, kammaṃ sāvatthiyaṃ jino;

Macchikāsaṇḍe sudhammo, cittassāvāsiko ahu.

Being unrestrained, they practiced various kinds of misconduct. The Victor, the Perfectly Enlightened One, enjoined the act of banishment in Sāvatthī. In Macchikāsaṇḍa, Sudhamma was the resident monk for the householder Citta.

Jātivādena khuṃseti, sudhammo cittupāsakaṃ;

Paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ, āṇāpesi tathāgato.

Sudhamma reviled Citta the lay follower with words concerning birth; the Tathāgata enjoined the act of reconciliation.

Kosambiyaṃ channaṃ bhikkhuṃ, nicchantāpattiṃ passituṃ;

Adassane [P 2.0030] ukkhipituṃ, āṇāpesi jinuttamo.

At Kosambī, the Supreme Victor enjoined the suspension of the monk Channa, who was unwilling to see an offense, on account of his not seeing it.

Channo taṃyeva āpattiṃ, paṭikātuṃ na icchati;

Ukkhepanāppaṭikamme, āṇāpesi vināyako.

Channa did not wish to make amends for that very offense; the Leader enjoined suspension for not making amends.

Pāpadiṭṭhi [V 0.0076] ariṭṭhassa, āsi aññāṇanissitā;

Diṭṭhiyāppaṭinissagge diṭṭhiappaṭinissagge (ka.), ukkhepaṃ jinabhāsitaṃ.

A wicked view based on ignorance arose for Ariṭṭha; for not relinquishing the view, suspension was spoken of by the Victor.

Niyassakammaṃ pabbajjaṃ pabbājaṃ (ka.), tatheva paṭisāraṇī;

Adassanāppaṭikamme[T 1.0127], anissagge ca diṭṭhiyā.

The act of subordination, banishment, and likewise reconciliation; as well as the acts for not seeing an offense, for not making amends, and for not relinquishing a view.

Davānācārūpaghāti, micchāājīvameva ca;

Pabbājanīyakammamhi, atirekapadā ime.

Playfulness, misconduct, destructiveness, and wrong livelihood—these are additional terms in the act of banishment.

Alābhāvaṇṇā dve pañca, dve pañcakāti nāmakā dve pañcakoti nāmako (ka.);

Paṭisāraṇīyakammamhi, atirekapadā ime.

The two pentads of non-gain and dispraise, and two others named 'pentad'—these are additional terms in the act of reconciliation.

Tajjanīyaṃ niyassañca, duve kammāpi sādisā kammesu sadisaṃ (ka.);

Pabbajjā pabbājā (ka.) paṭisārī ca, atthi padātirittatā.

Censure and subordination, both acts are similar; in banishment and reconciliation, there is an excess of terms.

Tayo ukkhepanā kammā, sadisā te vibhattito;

Tajjanīyanayenāpi, sesakammaṃ vijāniyāti.

The three acts of suspension are similar in their divisions; and by the method of censure, one should understand the remaining acts.

Kammakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on Formal Acts is concluded.

2. Pārivāsikakkhandhakaṃ

2. The Section on Probation

1. Pārivāsikavattaṃ

1. The Duties of One on Probation

75. Tena [T 1.0128][P 2.0031][M 0.0082][V 0.0077] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena pārivāsikā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma pārivāsikā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

75. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, monks undergoing probation consented to the following from monks in good standing: bowing down, rising up, saluting with joined palms, the act of paying respect, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, water for washing the feet, a footstool, a potsherd for rubbing the feet, the receiving of the bowl and robe, and the service of rubbing the back while bathing. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: 'How indeed can monks undergoing probation consent to the following from monks in good standing: bowing down, rising up, saluting with joined palms, the act of paying respect, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, water for washing the feet, a footstool, a potsherd for rubbing the feet, the receiving of the bowl and robe, and the service of rubbing the back while bathing?' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, pārivāsikā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, pārivāsikā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ [T 1.0129] pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ[V 0.0078], sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāro, seyyābhihāro, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having convened the assembly of monks, questioned the monks: “Is it true, monks, as is said, that monks on probation consent to the bowing, rising in salutation, raising of joined palms, respectful service, bringing of a seat, bringing of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, receiving of the bowl and robe, and scrubbing of the back while bathing, from monks in normal standing?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “It is not suitable... How indeed, monks, can monks on probation consent to the bowing, rising in salutation, raising of joined palms, respectful service, bringing of a seat, bringing of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, receiving of the bowl and robe, and scrubbing of the back while bathing, from monks in normal standing? This, monks, does not lead to the faith of the faithless...” Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a monk on probation should not consent to the bowing, rising in salutation, raising of joined palms, respectful service, bringing of a seat, bringing of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, receiving of the bowl and robe, and scrubbing of the back while bathing, from monks in normal standing. Whoever should consent to it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mithu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ.

I allow, monks, for monks on probation, among themselves, according to seniority: bowing, rising in salutation, raising of joined palms, respectful service, bringing of a seat, bringing of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, receiving of the bowl and robe, and scrubbing of the back while bathing.

“Anujānāmi[M 0.0083], bhikkhave, pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ – uposathaṃ, pavāraṇaṃ, vassikasāṭikaṃ, oṇojanaṃ, bhattaṃ. Tena hi, bhikkhave, pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā pārivāsikehi bhikkhūhi vattitabbaṃ[P 2.0032].

I allow, monks, for monks on probation, five things according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rainy-season cloth, the setting aside of a food portion, and the meal. Therefore, monks, I will lay down the duties for monks on probation, according to which monks on probation should conduct themselves.

76. “Pārivāsikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

76. Monks, a monk on probation should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

Na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena parivāso dinno hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā [T 1.0130] tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabbaṃ.

He should not give higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him, nor consent to the appointment as an exhorter of nuns; even if appointed, he should not exhort the nuns. The offense for which the Saṅgha has given him probation should not be committed, nor another of a similar nature, nor one more serious than that. The formal act should not be criticized, nor should the monks who performed the act be criticized. The Uposatha of a monk in normal standing should not be suspended, nor should the Pavāraṇā be suspended. A formal admonition should not be made, a charge should not be initiated, an opportunity to speak should not be caused to be requested, he should not accuse, he should not remind, nor should he engage in disputes with monks.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattassa bhikkhuno purato gantabbaṃ, na purato nisīditabbaṃ. Yo hoti saṅghassa āsanapariyanto seyyāpariyanto vihārapariyanto so tassa padātabbo. Tena ca so sāditabbo.

Monks, a monk on probation should not go in front of a monk in normal standing, nor sit in front of him. Whatever is the Saṅgha’s lowest seat, lowest resting place, or lowest lodging, that should be given to him. And he should be content with it.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā puresamaṇena vā pacchāsamaṇena vā kulāni upasaṅkamitabbāni, na āraññikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ samāditabbaṃ (ka.), na piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na ca tappaccayā piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo – mā maṃ jāniṃsūti.

Monks, a monk on probation should not approach families with a monk in normal standing, either as a forerunner or as a follower. The forest-dweller's ascetic practice should not be undertaken, nor the alms-food-eater's ascetic practice. And alms-food should not be caused to be brought on that account, thinking, 'May they not know me.'

“Pārivāsikena[V 0.0079], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā āgantukena ārocetabbaṃ, āgantukassa ārocetabbaṃ, uposathe ārocetabbaṃ, pavāraṇāya ārocetabbaṃ. Sace gilāno hoti, dūtenapi ārocetabbaṃ.

Monks, a monk on probation should, as an incoming monk, announce his status; he should announce it to an incoming monk; he should announce it on the Uposatha day; he should announce it on the Pavāraṇā day. If he is sick, he should announce it even by a messenger.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger.

“Na[M 0.0084], bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā[T 1.0131]. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger. Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks or a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger. Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger. Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks or a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger. Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger. Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks or a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in normal standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu [T 1.0132] bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena [V 0.0080] bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger. O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger. O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra [M 0.0085] pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena[P 2.0033], aññatra antarāyā.

O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger. O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger. O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra [T 1.0133] antarāyā.

O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger. O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger. O monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk of normal standing or in case of danger.

80. “Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

80. O monks, a monk on probation may go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo[V 0.0081], bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo[M 0.0086], bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā [T 1.0134] sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko anāvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

O monks, a monk on probation may go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know thus: ‘I am able to return this very day.’

81. “Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ. Pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ. Pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabbo. Na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkamantaṃ (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbapāṭho) caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

81. O monks, a monk on probation should not dwell with a monk of normal standing in a residence under one roof, nor in a non-residence under one roof, nor in a residence or a non-residence under one roof. Upon seeing a monk of normal standing, one should rise from one's seat. A monk of normal standing should be invited with a seat. One should not sit on the same seat with a monk of normal standing; when he is sitting on a low seat, one should not sit on a high seat; when he is sitting on the ground, one should not sit on a seat. One should not walk on the same walking path; when he is walking on a low walking path, one should not walk on a high walking path; when he is walking on the ground, one should not walk on a walking path.

82. “Na[V 0.0082], bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pārivāsikena vuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattacārikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne [T 1.0135] āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ[M 0.0087], na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

82. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation should not dwell in a dwelling under one roof together with a more senior bhikkhu who is undergoing probation, nor with a bhikkhu who deserves to be sent back to the beginning, nor with a bhikkhu who deserves mānatta, nor with a bhikkhu who is undertaking mānatta, nor with a bhikkhu who deserves rehabilitation. He should not dwell in a non-dwelling under one roof. He should not dwell in a dwelling or a non-dwelling under one roof. He should not sit on one seat. When another is sitting on a low seat, he should not sit on a high seat. When another is sitting on the ground, he should not sit on a seat. He should not walk on one walking path. When another is walking on a low walking path, he should not walk on a high walking path. When another is walking on the ground, he should not walk on a walking path.

mahāva. 393 “Pārivāsikacatuttho ce, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ dadeyya, mūlāya paṭikasseyya, mānattaṃ dadeyya, taṃvīso abbheyya, akammaṃ akammaṃ taṃ (syā.), na ca karaṇīya”nti.

Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu on probation is the fourth in a quorum that gives probation, sends a bhikkhu back to the beginning, or gives mānatta; or if he is one of twenty in a quorum that rehabilitates a bhikkhu, it is not a valid act, and it should not be done.

Catunnavutipārivāsikavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninety-four observances for a bhikkhu on probation are concluded.

83. Atha kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kati nu kho, bhante, pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā”ti? “Tayo kho, upāli, pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā[P 2.0034]. Sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā – ime kho, upāli, tayo pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā”ti.

83. Then the Venerable Upāli approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Upāli said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, how many interruptions of the nights are there for a bhikkhu undergoing probation?' 'There are three interruptions of the nights for a bhikkhu undergoing probation, Upāli: dwelling together, dwelling apart, and not announcing. These, Upāli, are the three interruptions of the nights for a bhikkhu undergoing probation.'

84. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito hoti. Na sakkonti pārivāsikā bhikkhū parivāsaṃ sodhetuṃ[T 1.0136]. Bhagavato te bhikkhū bhagavato (syā., evamuparipi) etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ nikkhipituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nikkhipitabbo. Tena pārivāsikena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘parivāsaṃ nikkhipāmī’ti. Nikkhitto hoti parivāso. ‘Vattaṃ nikkhipāmī’ti. Nikkhitto hoti parivāso.

84. At that time, a great community of bhikkhus had gathered in Sāvatthī. The bhikkhus undergoing probation were unable to purify their probation. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, bhikkhus, the setting aside of probation. And, bhikkhus, it should be set aside in this way: The bhikkhu undergoing probation should approach one bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, squat down, raise his joined palms, and say thus: "I set aside the probation." The probation is set aside. "I set aside the observance." The probation is set aside.'

85. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ pakkamiṃsu. Sakkonti pārivāsikā bhikkhū parivāsaṃ sodhetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ samādiyituṃ samādātuṃ (syā. kaṃ.). Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samādiyitabbo samāditabbo (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Tena pārivāsikena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā [M 0.0088] ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā [V 0.0083] añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘parivāsaṃ samādiyāmī’ti. Samādinno hoti parivāso. ‘Vattaṃ samādiyāmī’ti. Samādinno hoti parivāso”.

85. At that time, the bhikkhus in Sāvatthī had departed to various places. The bhikkhus undergoing probation were unable to purify their probation. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, bhikkhus, the undertaking of probation. And, bhikkhus, it should be undertaken in this way: The bhikkhu undergoing probation should approach one bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, squat down, raise his joined palms, and say thus: "I undertake the probation." The probation is undertaken. "I undertake the observance." The probation is undertaken.'

Pārivāsikavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Observance for a Bhikkhu on Probation is concluded.

2. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahavattaṃ

2. The Observance for One Deserving to be Sent Back to the Beginning

86. Tena [T 1.0137] kho pana samayena mūlāyapaṭikassanārahā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma mūlāyapaṭikassanārahā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

86. Now at that time, bhikkhus who deserved to be sent back to the beginning were accepting from bhikkhus in good standing: salutation, rising up, the gesture of homage, dutiful acts, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiper, the receiving of the bowl and robe, and the scrubbing of the back during bathing. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying: “How can bhikkhus who deserve to be sent back to the beginning accept from bhikkhus in good standing salutation, rising up… and the scrubbing of the back during bathing?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ! Netaṃ bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāro, seyyābhihāro, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahānaṃ [T 1.0138] bhikkhūnaṃ mithu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ – uposathaṃ[M 0.0089], pavāraṇaṃ, vassikasāṭikaṃ, oṇojanaṃ, bhattaṃ. Tena hi, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññāpessāmi yathā mūlāyapaṭikassanārahehi bhikkhūhi vattitabbaṃ.

Then, on that occasion, in connection with that matter, the Blessed One had the community of bhikkhus convened and questioned the bhikkhus: “Is it true, bhikkhus, that bhikkhus who deserve to be sent back to the beginning accept salutation, rising up… and back-scrubbing during bathing from bhikkhus in good standing?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “How indeed, bhikkhus, can bhikkhus who deserve to be sent back to the beginning accept salutation, rising up… and back-scrubbing during bathing from bhikkhus in good standing! This, bhikkhus, does not lead to the confidence of the unconvinced, nor to the increase of it in the convinced.” Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who deserves to be sent back to the beginning should not accept from bhikkhus in good standing: salutation, rising up, the gesture of homage, dutiful acts, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-wiper, the receiving of his bowl and robes, or back-scrubbing during bathing. Whoever should accept this, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, bhikkhus, for bhikkhus who deserve to be sent back to the beginning, among themselves and according to seniority: salutation, rising up… and back-scrubbing during bathing. I allow, bhikkhus, for bhikkhus who deserve to be sent back to the beginning, five things according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rains-cloth, the allotment of food, and meals. Therefore, bhikkhus, I will lay down the observance for bhikkhus who deserve to be sent back to the beginning, according to which they ought to conduct themselves.”

87. “Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena[V 0.0084], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

87. “Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

Na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena mūlāya paṭikassanāraho kato hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabbaṃ.

He should not give higher ordination, nor should he give dependence, nor should he have a novice attend on him, nor should he consent to the appointment as an instructor of nuns; and even if appointed, he should not instruct the nuns. The offense for which he was made by the Saṅgha to be one liable to be sent back to the beginning should not be committed, nor any other similar offense, nor one that is more wicked than that. The formal act should not be disparaged, nor the monks who performed it. The Uposatha of a monk in good standing should not be suspended, nor the Pavāraṇā. He should not make a formal statement, nor initiate an accusation, nor ask for leave, nor accuse, nor remind. He should not associate with the monks.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā pakatattassa bhikkhuno purato gantabbaṃ, na purato nisīditabbaṃ. Yo hoti saṅghassa āsanapariyanto seyyāpariyanto vihārapariyanto so tassa padātabbo. Tena ca so sāditabbo.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go in front of a monk in good standing, nor should he sit in front of him. Whatever is the last seat, the last bed, and the last dwelling of the Saṅgha, that should be given to him. And he should be content with it.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā puresamaṇena vā [T 1.0139] pacchāsamaṇena vā kulāni upasaṅkamitabbāni, na āraññikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na ca tappaccayā piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo – mā maṃ jāniṃsūti.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not approach families with a monk in good standing as his forerunner or follower. He should not undertake the forest-dweller's ascetic practice. He should not undertake the alms-food-eater's ascetic practice. And on that account, he should not have alms-food brought out, thinking, 'Let them not know me.'

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a dwelling with monks to a dwelling without monks, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a dwelling with monks to a non-dwelling without monks, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na[M 0.0090], bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a dwelling with monks to a dwelling without monks or to a non-dwelling without monks, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso [V 0.0085] gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a non-dwelling with monks to a dwelling without monks, nor to a non-dwelling without monks, nor to a dwelling or a non-dwelling without monks, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena[T 1.0140], aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a dwelling with monks or from a non-dwelling with monks to a dwelling without monks, nor to a non-dwelling without monks, nor to a dwelling or a non-dwelling without monks, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a dwelling with monks to a dwelling with monks, nor to a non-dwelling with monks, nor to a dwelling or a non-dwelling with monks, where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a non-dwelling with monks to a dwelling with monks, nor to a non-dwelling with monks, nor to a dwelling or a non-dwelling with monks, where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not go from a dwelling with monks or from a non-dwelling with monks to a dwelling with monks, nor to a non-dwelling with monks, nor to a dwelling or a non-dwelling with monks, where there are monks of different communion, except with a monk in good standing, except in case of danger.

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning may go from a dwelling with monks to a dwelling with monks, or to a non-dwelling with monks, or to a dwelling or a non-dwelling with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know: 'I am able to return this very day.'

“Gantabbo[M 0.0091], bhikkhave[T 1.0141], mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning may go from a non-dwelling with monks to a dwelling with monks, or to a non-dwelling with monks, or to a dwelling or a non-dwelling with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know: 'I am able to return this very day.'

“Gantabbo[V 0.0086], bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning may go from a dwelling with monks or from a non-dwelling with monks to a dwelling with monks, or to a non-dwelling with monks, or to a dwelling or a non-dwelling with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if he should know: 'I am able to return this very day.'

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabbo; na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ; na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame [P 2.0035] caṅkamitabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk liable to be sent back to the beginning should not dwell with a monk in good standing under one roof in a dwelling, nor under one roof in a non-dwelling, nor under one roof in a dwelling or a non-dwelling. Upon seeing a monk in good standing, he should rise from his seat. A monk in good standing should be invited with a seat. He should not sit on the same seat with a monk in good standing. He should not sit on a high seat when the other is sitting on a low seat. He should not sit on a seat when the other is sitting on the ground. He should not walk on the same walking path, nor walk on a high walking path when the other is walking on a low one, nor walk on a walking path when the other is walking on the ground.

“Na, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā pārivāsikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena vuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattacārikena bhikkhunā [T 1.0142] saddhiṃ…pe… abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ; na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

Monks, a monk deserving to be sent back to the beginning should not dwell under one roof with a monk undergoing probation... with a more senior monk deserving to be sent back to the beginning... with a monk deserving mānatta... with a monk observing mānatta... with a monk deserving rehabilitation. One should not dwell in a residence under one roof, one should not dwell in a non-residence under one roof, one should not dwell in a residence or a non-residence under one roof. One should not sit on one seat. When another is sitting on a low seat, one should not sit on a high seat; when another is sitting on the ground, one should not sit on a seat. One should not walk on one walking path. When another is walking on a low walking path, one should not walk on a high walking path; when another is walking on the ground, one should not walk on a walking path.

mahāva. 393 “Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahacatuttho ce, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ dadeyya, mūlāya paṭikasseyya, mānattaṃ dadeyya, taṃvīso abbheyya, akammaṃ, na ca karaṇīya”nti.

Monks, if a Saṅgha with a monk deserving to be sent back to the beginning as the fourth should give probation, should send back to the beginning, or should give mānatta; or if a Saṅgha of twenty with that monk should rehabilitate, it is not a valid act, and it should not be done.

Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the duties for one deserving to be sent back to the beginning is concluded.

3. Mānattārahavattaṃ

3. The Duties for One Deserving Mānatta

88. Tena [M 0.0092] kho pana samayena mānattārahā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā [V 0.0087] …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma mānattārahā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, mānattārahā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, mānattārahā [T 1.0143] bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mānattārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mithu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mānattārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ – uposathaṃ, pavāraṇaṃ, vassikasāṭikaṃ, oṇojanaṃ, bhattaṃ. Tena hi, bhikkhave, mānattārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññāpessāmi yathā mānattārahehi bhikkhūhi vattitabbaṃ.

88. At that time, monks deserving of mānatta consented to the following from monks in good standing: salutation, rising to greet them, raising the hands in reverence, proper service, the bringing of a seat, the bringing of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-scraper, the receiving of the bowl and robe, and scrubbing the back when bathing. Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can monks deserving of mānatta consent to the following from monks in good standing: salutation, rising to greet them, raising the hands in reverence, proper service, the bringing of a seat, the bringing of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-scraper, the receiving of the bowl and robe, and scrubbing the back when bathing?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, it is said, monks, that monks deserving of mānatta consent to the following from monks in good standing: salutation, rising to greet them… and scrubbing the back when bathing?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “...How indeed, monks, can monks deserving of mānatta consent to the following from monks in good standing: salutation… and scrubbing the back when bathing? Monks, this does not lead to the faith of the faithless…” After rebuking them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not consent to the following from monks in good standing: salutation, rising to greet them… and scrubbing the back when bathing. Whoever should consent, there is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, for monks deserving of mānatta, among themselves according to seniority: salutation, rising to greet them… and scrubbing the back when bathing. I allow, monks, for monks deserving of mānatta five things according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rains-cloth, the distribution of food, and meals. Therefore, monks, I will lay down the duties for monks deserving of mānatta, according to which monks deserving of mānatta should conduct themselves.

89. “Mānattārahena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

89. Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should conduct himself properly. In that regard, this is the proper conduct:

Na upasampādetabbaṃ…pe… (yathā mūlāya paṭikassanā, tathā vitthāretabbaṃ.) Na bhikkhūhi [T 1.0144] sampayojetabbaṃ.

He should not give higher ordination... (As it should be expanded for 'sending back to the beginning', so it should be expanded here.) He should not associate with monks in good standing.

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā pakatattassa bhikkhuno purato gantabbaṃ, na purato nisīditabbaṃ. Yo hoti saṅghassa āsanapariyanto seyyāpariyanto vihārapariyanto so tassa padātabbo. Tena ca so sāditabbo.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not go in front of a monk in good standing, nor sit in front of him. Whatever is the last seat, the last bed, and the last dwelling of the Saṅgha, that should be given to him. And he should be satisfied with it.

“Na[M 0.0093][V 0.0088], bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā puresamaṇena vā pacchāsamaṇena vā kulāni upasaṅkamitabbāni, na āraññikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na ca tappaccayā piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo – mā maṃ jāniṃsūti.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not approach families with a monk in good standing, having made him a forerunner or a follower. He should not undertake the ascetic practice of a forest-dweller, nor the ascetic practice of an alms-food-eater. And for that reason, he should not have alms-food brought out, thinking, ‘Let them not know me.’”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with a monk in good standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, manattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in good standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko [T 1.0145] āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks or to a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in good standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks... or to a non-residence without monks... or to a residence or a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in good standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, a monk deserving of mānatta should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks... or to a non-residence without monks... or to a residence or a non-residence without monks, except with a monk in good standing, or in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or a non-residence with bhikkhus where there are bhikkhus of a different communion, except with a bhikkhu in good standing, or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo [M 0.0094] …pe… sabhikkhuko [V 0.0089] āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of mānatta should not go from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or a non-residence with bhikkhus where there are bhikkhus of a different communion, except with a bhikkhu in good standing, or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū [T 1.0146] nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus or from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or a non-residence with bhikkhus where there are bhikkhus of a different communion, except with a bhikkhu in good standing, or in case of danger.”

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of mānatta may go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or a non-residence with bhikkhus where there are bhikkhus of the same communion, if he should know, ‘I am able to return today itself.’”

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of mānatta may go from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or a non-residence with bhikkhus where there are bhikkhus of the same communion, if he should know, ‘I am able to return today itself.’”

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of mānatta may go from a residence with bhikkhus or from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or a non-residence with bhikkhus where there are bhikkhus of the same communion, if he should know, ‘I am able to return today itself.’”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ. Pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ. Pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabbo. Na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na [T 1.0147] nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving mānatta should not live under the same roof in a residence with a bhikkhu in good standing, nor under the same roof in a non-residence, nor under the same roof in a residence or a non-residence. Upon seeing a bhikkhu in good standing, he should rise from his seat. A bhikkhu in good standing should be invited to take a seat. He should not sit on the same seat with a bhikkhu in good standing, nor on a higher seat when the bhikkhu in good standing is sitting on a lower seat, nor on a seat when the bhikkhu in good standing is sitting on the ground; he should not walk on the same walking path, nor on a higher walking path when the bhikkhu in good standing is walking on a lower one, nor on a walking path when the bhikkhu in good standing is walking on the ground.”

“Na[M 0.0095], bhikkhave, mānattārahena bhikkhunā pārivāsikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattārahena vuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattacārikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving mānatta should not live under the same roof in a residence with a bhikkhu undergoing probation… or with a bhikkhu deserving to be sent back to the beginning… or with a more senior bhikkhu deserving mānatta… or with a bhikkhu practicing mānatta… or with a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation, nor under the same roof in a non-residence, nor under the same roof in a residence or a non-residence; he should not sit on the same seat, nor on a higher seat when the other is sitting on a lower seat, nor on a seat when the other is sitting on the ground; he should not walk on the same walking path, nor on a higher walking path when the other is walking on a lower one, nor on a walking path when the other is walking on the ground.”

mahāva. 393 “Mānattārahacatuttho [V 0.0090] ce, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ dadeyya, mūlāya paṭikasseyya, mānattaṃ dadeyya, taṃvīso abbheyya, akammaṃ, na ca karaṇīya”nti.

“Bhikkhus, if a Saṅgha with a bhikkhu deserving mānatta as the fourth member should grant probation, send him back to the beginning, or grant mānatta; and if a Saṅgha of twenty including him should rehabilitate him, it is not a valid act, and it should not be done.”

Mānattārahavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the conduct for one deserving Mānatta is concluded.

4. Mānattacārikavattaṃ

4. The Conduct for one Practicing Mānatta

90. Tena kho pana samayena mānattacārikā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… [T 1.0148] te ujhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma mānattacārikā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

90. Now at that time, bhikkhus practicing mānatta consented to receiving from bhikkhus in good standing: salutation, rising up to greet, the añjali gesture, respectful service, the offering of a seat, the offering of a lodging, water for the feet, a footstool, a potsherd for rubbing the feet, the taking of the bowl and robes, and having their backs scrubbed while bathing. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How can bhikkhus practicing mānatta consent to receiving from bhikkhus in good standing: salutation, rising up to greet… and having their backs scrubbed while bathing?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, mānattacārikā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, mānattacārikā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having assembled the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, questioned the bhikkhus: “Is it true, bhikkhus, as is said, that bhikkhus practicing mānatta consent to receiving from bhikkhus in good standing: salutation, rising up to greet… and having their backs scrubbed while bathing?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them: “This is unsuitable… How, bhikkhus, can bhikkhus practicing mānatta consent to receiving from bhikkhus in good standing: salutation… and having their backs scrubbed while bathing? This, bhikkhus, does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident… Having rebuked them… and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:

“Na[M 0.0096], bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, āsanābhihāro, seyyābhihāro, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ, nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mānattacārikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mithu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mānattacārikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ – uposathaṃ, pavāraṇaṃ, vassikasāṭikaṃ, oṇojanaṃ, bhattaṃ. Tena hi, bhikkhave, mānattacārikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā mānattacārikehi bhikkhūhi vattitabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not consent to receiving from monks in good standing: salutation, rising up, the añjali gesture, proper service, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, water for the feet, a footstool, a foot-rubbing potsherd, the receiving of the bowl and robes, or having his back rubbed while bathing. Whoever should consent to these incurs an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Bhikkhus, that monks undergoing mānatta may mutually perform, according to seniority, salutation, rising up… and so forth… having their backs rubbed while bathing. I allow, Bhikkhus, five things for monks undergoing mānatta according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rains-cloth, the giving up of a portion of food, and a meal. Therefore, Bhikkhus, I will lay down the duties for monks undergoing mānatta, as to how monks undergoing mānatta should conduct themselves.”

91. “Mānattacārikena[T 1.0149][V 0.0091], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

91. “Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should conduct himself properly. Herein, this is the proper conduct:”

Na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā. Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena mānattaṃ dinnaṃ hoti sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā, tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā; kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā. Na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo, na okāso kāretabbo, na codetabbo, na sāretabbo, na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabbaṃ.

“He should not give the higher ordination, he should not give dependence, he should not have a novice attend on him, he should not consent to being appointed as an instructor of bhikkhunīs; even if appointed, he should not instruct bhikkhunīs. He should not commit the offense for which the Saṅgha has given him mānatta, nor another similar to it, nor one more serious than it; he should not criticize the formal act, nor the monks who performed it. He should not suspend the Uposatha of a monk in good standing, nor suspend his Pavāraṇā. He should not engage in admonition, he should not initiate a charge, he should not ask for an opportunity to speak, he should not admonish, he should not remind, nor should he associate with bhikkhus.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā pakatattassa bhikkhuno purato gantabbaṃ, na purato nisīditabbaṃ. Yo hoti saṅghassa āsanapariyanto seyyāpariyanto vihārapariyanto so tassa padātabbo. Tena ca so sāditabbo.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not walk in front of a monk in good standing, nor sit in front of him. Whatever is the last seat, the last bed, and the last dwelling of the Saṅgha, that should be given to him. And he should consent to it.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā puresamaṇena vā pacchāsamaṇena vā kulāni upasaṅkamitabbāni, na āraññikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ, na ca tappaccayā piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo – mā maṃ jāniṃsūti.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not approach families accompanied by a monk in good standing, either as a forerunner or as a follower. He should not undertake the wilderness-dweller’s practice, he should not undertake the alms-food-eater’s practice, nor should he have alms-food brought out on that account, thinking, ‘May they not know me.’”

“Mānattacārikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā āgantukena ārocetabbaṃ, āgantukassa ārocetabbaṃ, uposathe ārocetabbaṃ, pavāraṇāya ārocetabbaṃ[T 1.0150][M 0.0097], devasikaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Sace gilāno hoti, dūtenapi ārocetabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta, if he is a visitor, should announce it. He should announce it to a visitor. He should announce it on the Uposatha day. He should announce it on the Pavāraṇā day. He should announce it daily. If he is ill, he should announce it even by a messenger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence without bhikkhus, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a non-residence without bhikkhus, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na[V 0.0092], bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence without bhikkhus or a non-residence without bhikkhus, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence without bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence without bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence without bhikkhus or a non-residence without bhikkhus, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence without bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence without bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence without bhikkhus or a non-residence without bhikkhus, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus, where there are bhikkhus of a different communion, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na bhikkhave[T 1.0151], mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus, where there are bhikkhus of a different communion, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo…pe… sabhikkhuko [P 2.0036] āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo[M 0.0098], yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta should not go from a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus, where there are bhikkhus of a different communion, except with the Saṅgha or in case of danger.”

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.
