“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta may go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus, where there are bhikkhus of the same communion, if he knows, ‘I am able to arrive today itself.’”

“Gantabbo[V 0.0093], bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

“Bhikkhus, a monk undergoing mānatta may go from a non-residence with bhikkhus to a residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a non-residence with bhikkhus… and so forth… to a residence with bhikkhus or a non-residence with bhikkhus, where there are bhikkhus of the same communion, if he knows, ‘I am able to arrive today itself.’”

“Gantabbo, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

Bhikkhus, a monk observing mānatta is to go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks... (and so on)... to a non-residence with monks... (and so on)... to a residence or a non-residence where there are monks of the same communion, if he knows, ‘I am able to arrive today itself.’

“Na[T 1.0152], bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ. Pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ. Pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabbo. Na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a monk observing mānatta should not dwell in a residence under a single roof together with a monk in good standing, nor should he dwell in a non-residence under a single roof, nor should he dwell either in a residence or a non-residence under a single roof. Upon seeing a monk in good standing, he should rise from his seat. A monk in good standing should be invited with a seat. He should not sit on the same seat together with a monk in good standing; when that monk is sitting on a low seat, he should not sit on a high seat; when that monk is sitting on the ground, he should not sit on a seat. He should not walk on the same walking path; when that monk is walking on a low walking path, he should not walk on a high walking path; when that monk is walking on the ground, he should not walk on a walking path.

“Na, bhikkhave, mānattacārikena bhikkhunā pārivāsikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattacārikena vuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ[M 0.0099], na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a monk observing mānatta should not dwell in a residence under a single roof together with a monk undertaking probation... with a monk deserving to be sent back to the beginning... with a monk deserving mānatta... with a senior monk observing mānatta... with a monk deserving rehabilitation. He should not dwell in a residence under a single roof, nor in a non-residence under a single roof, nor either in a residence or a non-residence under a single roof; he should not sit on the same seat; when the other is sitting on a low seat, he should not sit on a high seat; when the other is sitting on the ground, he should not sit on a seat; he should not walk on the same walking path; when the other is walking on a low walking path, he should not walk on a high walking path; when the other is walking on the ground, he should not walk on a walking path.

mahāva. 393 “Mānattacārikacatuttho ce, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ dadeyya, mūlāya [T 1.0153] paṭikasseyya, mānattaṃ dadeyya, taṃvīso abbheyya, akammaṃ, na ca karaṇīya”nti.

Bhikkhus, if a Saṅgha with a monk observing mānatta as the fourth should grant probation, or should send a monk back to the beginning, or should grant mānatta; or if a Saṅgha of twenty including that monk should perform rehabilitation, it is not a valid act, and it should not be done.

92. Atha kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kati nu kho, bhante, mānattacārikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā”ti? “Cattāro kho[V 0.0094], upāli, mānattacārikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā. Sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā, ūne gaṇe caraṇaṃ caraṇanti (ka.) – ime kho, upāli, cattāro mānattacārikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā”ti.

92. Then the Venerable Upāli approached the Blessed One, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Venerable Upāli said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how many interruptions of nights are there for a monk observing mānatta?” “Upāli, there are four interruptions of nights for a monk observing mānatta: dwelling together with a monk in good standing, dwelling apart from the Saṅgha, not informing, and practicing in an incomplete group. These, Upāli, are the four interruptions of nights for a monk observing mānatta.”

93. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito hoti. Na sakkonti mānattacārikā bhikkhū mānattaṃ sodhetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mānattaṃ nikkhipituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nikkhipitabbaṃ. Tena mānattacārikena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘mānattaṃ nikkhipāmī’ti. Nikkhittaṃ hoti mānattaṃ. ‘Vattaṃ nikkhipāmī’ti. Nikkhittaṃ hoti mānatta”nti.

93. At that time, a large community of monks had gathered in Sāvatthī. The monks observing mānatta were unable to complete their mānatta. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow mānatta to be laid aside. And, bhikkhus, it should be laid aside thus: The monk observing mānatta should approach one monk, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit squatting, raise his joined palms, and say: ‘I lay aside the mānatta.’ The mānatta is thereby laid aside. He may also say: ‘I lay aside the duties.’ The mānatta is thereby laid aside.”

94. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ pakkamiṃsu[T 1.0154]. Sakkonti mānattacārikā bhikkhū mānattaṃ sodhetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mānattaṃ samādiyituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samādiyitabbaṃ. Tena mānattacārikena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā, evamassa vacanīyo – ‘mānattaṃ samādiyāmī’ti. Samādinnaṃ hoti mānattaṃ. ‘Vattaṃ samādiyāmī’ti. Samādinnaṃ hoti mānatta”nti.

94. At that time, the monks in Sāvatthī dispersed to various places. The monks observing mānatta were now able to purify their mānatta. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow mānatta to be undertaken. And, bhikkhus, it should be undertaken thus: That monk observing mānatta should approach one monk, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit squatting, raise his joined palms, and say: ‘I undertake the mānatta.’ The mānatta is thereby undertaken. He may also say: ‘I undertake the duties.’ The mānatta is thereby undertaken.”

Mānattacārikavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the duties of one observing mānatta is finished.

5. Abbhānārahavattaṃ

5. The Duties of One Deserving Rehabilitation

95. Tena [M 0.0100] kho pana samayena abbhānārahā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma abbhānārahā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

95. At that time, bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation accepted the homage of bhikkhus in good standing, their rising up for them... and the rubbing of their backs during bathing. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... complained, condemned, and criticized, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation accept the homage of bhikkhus in good standing, their rising up for them... and the rubbing of their backs during bathing?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, abbhānārahā bhikkhū sādiyanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammanti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho [V 0.0095] bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, abbhānārahā bhikkhū sādiyissanti pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ[T 1.0155]! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccupaṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, abbhānārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mithu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, abbhānārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ – uposathaṃ, pavāraṇaṃ, vassikasāṭikaṃ, oṇojanaṃ, bhattaṃ. Tena hi, bhikkhave, abbhānārahānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññāpessāmi yathā abbhānārahehi bhikkhūhi vattitabbaṃ.

Then the Blessed One, on this cause, on this occasion, having had the community of bhikkhus assemble, questioned the bhikkhus: “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus, that bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation consent to the homage of bhikkhus of restored standing, to their rising up for them... and to the rubbing of the back during bathing?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “...How indeed, bhikkhus, can bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation consent to the homage of bhikkhus of restored standing, to their rising up for them... and to the rubbing of the back during bathing! This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, the homage of bhikkhus of restored standing, their rising up for him... and the rubbing of the back during bathing should not be consented to by a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation. Whoever should consent, incurs an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, bhikkhus, for bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation, among themselves according to seniority, homage, rising up for one another... and the rubbing of the back during bathing. I allow, bhikkhus, five things for bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rains-bathing cloth, the allocated portion of food, and meals. Therefore, bhikkhus, I will lay down the duties for bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation, according to which bhikkhus deserving rehabilitation should conduct themselves.”

96. “Abbhānārahena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

96. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should conduct himself properly. Herein is the proper conduct:

Na upasampādetabbaṃ…pe… (yathā heṭṭhā, tathā vitthāretabbaṃ,) na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabbaṃ.

He should not give ordination… (as should be expanded upon as below,) he should not associate with bhikkhus.

“Na, bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā pakatattassa bhikkhuno purato gantabbaṃ, na purato nisīditabbaṃ. Yo hoti saṅghassa āsanapariyanto seyyāpariyanto vihārapariyanto so tassa padātabbo. Tena ca so sāditabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should not walk in front of a bhikkhu of restored standing, nor sit in front of him. Whatever is the Sangha’s last seat, last bed, or last dwelling, that should be given to him. And he should be content with it.

“Na[M 0.0101], bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā [T 1.0156] pakatattena bhikkhunā puresamaṇena vā pacchāsamaṇena vā kulāni upasaṅkamitabbāni; na āraññikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ; na piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ samādātabbaṃ; na ca tappaccayā piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo – mā maṃ jāniṃsūti.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should not visit families accompanied by a bhikkhu of restored standing, whether as a front-attendant or a rear-attendant. He should not undertake the wilderness-dweller’s ascetic practice. He should not undertake the alms-gatherer’s ascetic practice. And on account of that, he should not have almsfood brought out, thinking, ‘Let them not know me.’

“Na, bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a residence without bhikkhus, except with a bhikkhu of restored standing, except in case of danger.

“Na, bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra pakatattena, aññatra antarāyā…pe…. (Yathā heṭṭhā, tathā vitthāretabbā.)

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should not go from a residence with bhikkhus to a non-residence without bhikkhus, except with a bhikkhu of restored standing, except in case of danger… (As below, so it should be expanded.)

“Gantabbo[V 0.0096], bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā…pe… anāvāsā…pe… āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko [P 2.0037] āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation may go from a residence with bhikkhus… or from a non-residence… or from a residence or a non-residence, to a residence with bhikkhus… or to a non-residence with bhikkhus… or to a residence or non-residence where there are bhikkhus of the same communion, or to a place from which he knows he is able to return that same day.

“Na, bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabbo; na pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame [T 1.0157] caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should not dwell under the same roof in a monastery with a bhikkhu of restored standing, nor dwell under the same roof in a non-monastic residence, nor dwell under the same roof in a monastery or a non-monastic residence. Upon seeing a bhikkhu of restored standing, he should rise from his seat. A bhikkhu of restored standing should be invited with a seat. He should not sit on the same seat with a bhikkhu of restored standing. When the other is sitting on a low seat, he should not sit on a high seat. When the other is sitting on the ground, he should not sit on a seat. He should not walk on the same walking path. When the other is walking on a low walking path, he should not walk on a high walking path. When the other is walking on the ground, he should not walk on a walking path.

“Na, bhikkhave, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā pārivāsikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… mānattacārikena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ…pe… abbhānārahena vuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ; na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ; na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ; na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ[M 0.0102], na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation should not dwell under the same roof with a bhikkhu on probation… nor with a bhikkhu deserving to be sent back to the beginning… nor with a bhikkhu deserving mānatta… nor with a bhikkhu undergoing mānatta… nor with a more senior bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation. He should not dwell under the same roof in a monastery, nor dwell under the same roof in a non-monastic residence, nor dwell under the same roof in a monastery or a non-monastic residence. He should not sit on the same seat. When the other is sitting on a low seat, he should not sit on a high seat. When the other is sitting on the ground, he should not sit on a seat. He should not walk on the same walking path. When the other is walking on a low walking path, he should not walk on a high walking path. When the other is walking on the ground, he should not walk on a walking path.

mahāva. 393 “Abbhānārahacatuttho ce, bhikkhave, parivāsaṃ dadeyya, mūlāya paṭikasseyya, mānattaṃ dadeyya, taṃvīso abbheyya, akammaṃ, na ca karaṇīya”nti.

Bhikkhus, if a Saṅgha with a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation as its fourth member were to grant probation, or send back to the beginning, or grant mānatta, or if a Saṅgha of twenty including him were to grant rehabilitation, it is an invalid act and should not be done.

Abbhānārahavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The duties for one deserving rehabilitation are finished.

Pārivāsikakkhandhako dutiyo.

The second chapter, on probationers, is finished.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū pañca.

In this chapter, there are five topics.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Pārivāsikā [T 1.0158] sādenti, pakatattāna bhikkhunaṃ;

Abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjaliñca sāmīciyaṃ.

Probationers delight in homage, rising to greet, raising clasped hands, and proper respect from bhikkhus of restored standing.

Āsanaṃ [V 0.0097] seyyābhihāraṃ, pādo pīṭhaṃ kathalikaṃ;

Pattaṃ nahāne parikammaṃ, ujjhāyanti ca pesalā.

The bringing forward of a seat, the bringing forward of bedding, water for the feet, a footstool, a potsherd, taking the bowl, and service when bathing—the virtuous complain.

Dukkaṭaṃ sādiyantassa, mithu pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ punāpare (ka.);

Uposathaṃ pavāraṇaṃ, vassikoṇojabhojanaṃ.

For one who delights in it, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Five things are allowed among themselves according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rains-cloth, the allocated portion, and food.

Sammā ca vattanā tattha, pakatattassa gacchantaṃ;

Yo ca hoti pariyanto, pure pacchā tatheva ca na pure pacchāsamaṇena (sī. syā.).

And the proper conduct therein: not going before a bhikkhu of restored standing; accepting whatever is the lowest; and the same for having an attendant preceding or following.

Āraññapiṇḍanīhāro, āgantuke uposathe;

Pavāraṇāya dūtena, gantabbo ca sabhikkhuko.

The undertaking of the forest-dweller's practice and the alms-food-eater's practice, and the bringing forth of alms-food; announcing as a newcomer or to a newcomer, on the Uposatha day, on the Pavāraṇā day, and by a messenger. And one should go to a monastery where there are monks.

Ekacchanne [T 1.0159] ca vuṭṭhānaṃ, tatheva ca nimantaye;

Āsane nīce caṅkame, chamāyaṃ caṅkamena ca.

Dwelling under a single roof, and rising; likewise inviting; concerning a low seat and a walking path; on the ground and in a cloister for walking.

Vuḍḍhatarena akammaṃ, ratticchedā ca sodhanā;

Nikkhipanaṃ samādānaṃ, vattaṃva pārivāsike ratti vā pārivāsike (ka.), ñātabbaṃ pārivāsikā (sī. syā.).

With a more senior monk, it is an invalid act; the severance of nights and its purification; the laying down and the undertaking are like the duties for one on probation.

Mūlāya [M 0.0103] mānattārahā, tathā mānattacārikā;

Abbhānārahe nayo cāpi, sambhedaṃ nayato sambhedanayato (syā.) puna.

For one deserving to be sent back to the beginning, for one deserving mānatta, and likewise for one undergoing mānatta, and for one deserving rehabilitation, there is also a method. Again, by way of method, there is a distinction.

Pārivāsikesu tayo, catu mānattacārike;

Na samenti ratticchedesu ratticchede (itipi), ratticchedā (syā.), mānattesu ca devasi;

Dve kammā sadisā sesā, tayo kammā samāsamāti samā matāti (sī.).

For those on probation, there are three types of severance of nights; for one undergoing mānatta, there are four. They are not the same in the severances of nights. And in the mānatta penances, there is the daily announcing. Two formal acts are similar; the remaining three formal acts are exactly the same.

Pārivāsikakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter on Probation is finished.

3. Samuccayakkhandhakaṃ

3. The Chapter on Combination

1. Sukkavissaṭṭhi

1. Emission of Semen

97. Tena [T 1.0160][P 2.0038][M 0.0104][V 0.0098] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato te bhikkhū bhagavato (syā.) etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbaṃ –

97. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the venerable Udāyī had fallen into a single, unconcealed offense of intentional emission of semen. He told the monks: “Venerable sirs, I have fallen into a single, unconcealed offense of intentional emission of semen. Now how should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, monks, let the Sangha give the monk Udāyī a mānatta of six nights for the single, unconcealed offense of intentional emission of semen. And, monks, it should be given thus:

Appaṭicchannamānattaṃ

The Mānatta for an Unconcealed Offense

98. “Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Dutiyampi, sohaṃ dutiyampi (sī. ka.) bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā [T 1.0161] sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Tatiyampi sohaṃ tatiyampi (sī. ka.), bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī’ti. “Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

98. “Monks, that monk Udāyī should approach the Sangha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and should say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I have incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. Therefore, venerable sirs, I ask the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. Venerable sirs, I have incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. For the second time, venerable sirs, I ask the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. Venerable sirs, I have incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. For the third time, venerable sirs, I ask the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed.’ A competent and able monk should inform the Sangha:

99. “Suṇātu [V 0.0099] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā [M 0.0105] āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā [P 2.0039] appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

99. “Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk Udāyī has incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. He asks the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha may grant a six-night mānatta to the monk Udāyī for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa[T 1.0162]; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk Udāyī has incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. He asks the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. The Sangha grants the monk Udāyī a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. Any venerable one who approves of granting a six-night mānatta to the monk Udāyī for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed, should remain silent. Any who disapproves should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk Udāyī has incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. He asks the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. The Sangha grants the monk Udāyī a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. Any venerable one who approves of granting a six-night mānatta to the monk Udāyī for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed, should remain silent. Any who disapproves should speak.”

“Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a third time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk Udāyī has incurred one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. He asks the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. The Sangha grants the monk Udāyī a six-night mānatta for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed. Any venerable one who approves of granting a six-night mānatta to the monk Udāyī for one offense of intentional emission of semen, which was unconcealed, should remain silent. Any who disapproves should speak.”

“Dinnaṃ [V 0.0100] saṅghena udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti[T 1.0163].

A six-night mānatta has been granted by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu Udāyī for one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.

Appaṭicchannaabbhānaṃ

Rehabilitation for an Unconcealed Offense

100. So [M 0.0106] ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbhetu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, abbhetabbo –

100. He who had completed the mānatta informed the bhikkhus: “Friends, I committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. I then asked the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. I have completed the mānatta. How now should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha reinstate the bhikkhu Udāyī. And, bhikkhus, he should be reinstated in this way:

Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ bhante ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmi.

Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu Udāyī should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit down in the squatting position, raise his joined palms, and say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for that one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for that one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Venerable sirs, having completed the mānatta, I request rehabilitation from the Saṅgha.’

“Ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ [T 1.0164] saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmi.

‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for that one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for that one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Venerable sirs, having completed the mānatta, for a second time I request rehabilitation from the Saṅgha.’

“Ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmīti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho [P 2.0040] ñāpetabbo –

‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for that one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for that one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Venerable sirs, having completed the mānatta, for a third time I request rehabilitation from the Saṅgha.’ A competent and able bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

101. “Suṇātu [V 0.0101] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā [M 0.0107] sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. So ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya. Esā ñatti.

101. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu Udāyī for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Having completed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should rehabilitate the bhikkhu Udāyī. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya [T 1.0165] sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. So ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu Udāyī for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Having completed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha rehabilitates the bhikkhu Udāyī. Whichever venerable one approves of the rehabilitation of the bhikkhu Udāyī should be silent; whoever does not approve should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. So ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time, I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu Udāyī for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Having completed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha rehabilitates the bhikkhu Udāyī. Whichever venerable one approves of the rehabilitation of the bhikkhu Udāyī should be silent; whoever does not approve should speak.”

“Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. So ciṇṇamānatto [T 1.0166] saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a third time, I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī committed one offense: an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. The Saṅgha granted a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu Udāyī for this one offense of an intentional, unconcealed emission of semen. Having completed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha rehabilitates the bhikkhu Udāyī. Whichever venerable one approves of the rehabilitation of the bhikkhu Udāyī should be silent; whoever does not approve should speak.”

“Abbhito [M 0.0108][V 0.0102] saṅghena udāyī bhikkhu. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The monk Udāyī has been rehabilitated by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I bear this in mind.”

Ekāhappaṭicchannaparivāsaṃ

Probation for an Offense Concealed for One Day

102. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

102. At that time, the Venerable Udāyī had committed one offense: an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He informed the monks: “Friends, I have committed one offense: an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. How should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha grant the monk Udāyī a one-day probation for that one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. And, monks, it should be granted in this way:

“Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. “Byattena [T 1.0167] bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Monks, that monk Udāyī, having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having paid homage at the feet of the senior monks, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his joined palms, should speak thus: ‘Venerables, I have fallen into one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Venerables, I, that person, request from the Saṅgha a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

103. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno [P 2.0041] ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

103. Venerables, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has fallen into one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He requests from the Saṅgha a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. If the time is suitable for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the monk Udāyī a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ deti[M 0.0109]. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā [V 0.0103] ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerables, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has fallen into one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He requests from the Saṅgha a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha grants the monk Udāyī a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. To whichever venerable one the granting of a one-day probation to the monk Udāyī for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day, is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe…[T 1.0168].

For the second time, I speak on this matter… For the third time, I speak on this matter…

“Dinno saṅghena udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāso. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

A one-day probation has been granted by the Saṅgha to the monk Udāyī for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. This is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.

Ekāhappaṭicchannamānattaṃ

Mānatta for an Offense Concealed for One Day

104. So parivutthaparivāso bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbaṃ –

104. Having lived out his probation, he informed the monks: “Friends, I committed one offense: an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I then requested the Saṅgha for a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted me a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I have now lived out my probation. How should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha grant the monk Udāyī mānatta for six nights for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. And, monks, it should be granted thus:

“Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ [T 1.0169] ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbaṃ yācitabbo (sī. evamuparipi). Tatiyampi yācitabbaṃ yācitabbo (sī. evamuparipi). Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Monks, that monk Udāyī should approach the Saṅgha... and should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense: an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I then requested the Saṅgha for a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted me a one-day probation for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Venerable sirs, having lived out my probation, I now request the Saṅgha for mānatta for six nights for one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day.’ The request should be made a second time. The request should be made a third time. A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

105. “Suṇātu [M 0.0110] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ [P 2.0042] ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā [V 0.0104] ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

105. Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī has committed one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He requested the Saṅgha for one day of probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the bhikkhu Udāyī one day of probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed his probation, he requests the Saṅgha for mānatta for six nights for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the bhikkhu Udāyī mānatta for six nights for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā [T 1.0170] ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī has committed one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He requested the Saṅgha for one day of probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the bhikkhu Udāyī one day of probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed his probation, he requests the Saṅgha for mānatta for six nights for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha grants the bhikkhu Udāyī mānatta for six nights for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Whichever venerable one approves of the granting of mānatta for six nights to the bhikkhu Udāyī for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day, should remain silent. Whichever one does not approve should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe…[T 1.0171].

For a second time, I state this matter... For a third time, I state this matter...

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Mānatta for six nights has been granted by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu Udāyī for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Ekāhappaṭicchannaabbhānaṃ

Reinstatement for a One-Day Concealment

106. So ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ [M 0.0111] saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā [V 0.0105] ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbhetu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, abbhetabbo –

106. Having completed the mānatta, he informed the bhikkhus: “Friends, I committed one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I then requested the Saṅgha for a one-day probationary period on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted me a one-day probationary period on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed the probationary period, I then requested the Saṅgha for mānatta for six nights on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted me mānatta for six nights on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I have now completed the mānatta. How, then, should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha reinstate the bhikkhu Udāyī. And, bhikkhus, he should be reinstated in this way:

“Tena bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa [T 1.0172] vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbaṃ. Tatiyampi yācitabbaṃ. Byattena [T 1.0173] bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu Udāyī, having approached the Saṅgha... should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. On account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day, I requested the Saṅgha for one day of probation. The Saṅgha granted me one day of probation on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed the probation, on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day, I requested the Saṅgha for mānatta for six nights. The Saṅgha granted me mānatta for six nights on account of that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Venerable sirs, having completed the mānatta, I request the Saṅgha for reinstatement.’ It should be requested a second time. It should be requested a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

107. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno [P 2.0043] ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. So ciṇṇamānatto [M 0.0112] saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya. Esā ñatti.

107. Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Udāyī has committed one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He requested the Saṅgha for one day of probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the bhikkhu Udāyī one day of probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed his probation, he requested the Saṅgha for mānatta for six nights for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the bhikkhu Udāyī mānatta for six nights for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed the mānatta, he requests the Saṅgha for reinstatement. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should reinstate the bhikkhu Udāyī. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya [V 0.0106] chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya [T 1.0174] chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi. So ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has committed one offense—an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. He requested the Saṅgha for a one-day probationary period for that one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the monk Udāyī a one-day probationary period for that one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed the probationary period, he requested the Saṅgha for a six-night period of discipline for that one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the monk Udāyī a six-night period of discipline for that one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. Having completed the period of discipline, he asks the Saṅgha for reinstatement. The Saṅgha reinstates the monk Udāyī. Whichever venerable one approves of the reinstatement of the monk Udāyī should remain silent; whoever disapproves should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time, I speak on this matter… For a third time, I speak on this matter…

“Abbhito saṅghena udāyī bhikkhu. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The monk Udāyī has been reinstated by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Pañcāhappaṭicchannaparivāso

Probation for an Offense Concealed for Five Days

108. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ dvīhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… tīhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… [T 1.0175] catūhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

108. At that time, Venerable Udāyī had committed an offense—an intentional emission of semen, concealed for two days… concealed for three days… concealed for four days… concealed for five days. He informed the monks: “Friends, I have committed an offense—an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. How should I proceed?” They reported the matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha grant the monk Udāyī a five-day probation for that one offense of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. And, monks, it should be granted thus:

“Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ [M 0.0113] sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Monks, that monk Udāyī, having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having paid homage at the feet of the senior monks, having sat down squatting, and having raised his joined palms, should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I have fallen into one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. That I, venerable sirs, ask the Saṅgha for five days of probation for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days.’ He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

109. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyissa [T 1.0176][V 0.0107] bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

109. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has fallen into one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. He asks the Saṅgha for five days of probation for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the monk Udāyī five days of probation for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has fallen into one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. He asks the Saṅgha for five days of probation for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. The Saṅgha grants the monk Udāyī five days of probation for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. Whichever venerable one approves of the granting of five days of probation to the monk Udāyī for one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days, should be silent; whoever does not approve, should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

A second time I speak on this matter… A third time I speak on this matter…

“Dinno saṅghena udāyissa bhikkhuno [T 1.0177] ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāso. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

A five-day probation has been granted by the Saṅgha to the monk Udāyī for one offense—an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.

Pārivāsikamūlāyapaṭikassanā

Drawing Back to the Root for a Probationer

110. So parivasanto antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā [M 0.0114] sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikassatu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, mūlāya paṭikassitabbo –

110. While undergoing probation, he committed one intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. He informed the monks: 'Friends, I committed one intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. I requested from the Saṅgha a five-day probation for one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. The Saṅgha granted me a five-day probation for that one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. While undergoing probation, I committed one intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. How now should I proceed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha draw back the monk Udāyī to the root on account of the one, unconcealed, interim offense of an intentional emission of semen. And, monks, he should be drawn back to the root thus:'

“Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ[V 0.0108]. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā [T 1.0178] āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya [P 2.0044] paṭikassanaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā yācitabbo (sī. evamuparipi). Tatiyampi yācitabbā yācitabbo (sī. evamuparipi). Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Monks, that monk Udāyī should approach the Saṅgha and so on, and he should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I have committed one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. For that one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days, I requested the Saṅgha for a five-day probation. The Saṅgha granted me a five-day probation for that one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. While undergoing probation, in the interim, I committed one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. Venerable sirs, on account of that one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, that occurred in the interim, I request the Saṅgha for a drawing back to the beginning.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:”

111. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivasanto antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikasseyya. Esā ñatti.

111. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has committed one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. He requested the Saṅgha for a five-day probation for that one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. The Saṅgha granted the monk Udāyī a five-day probation for that one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. While undergoing probation, in the interim, he committed one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. He requests the Saṅgha for a drawing back to the beginning on account of the one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, that occurred in the interim. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should draw back the monk Udāyī to the beginning on account of the one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, that occurred in the interim. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0115] me, bhante[T 1.0179], saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yāci. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivasanto antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikassati. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī has committed one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. He requested the Saṅgha for a five-day probation on account of one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. The Saṅgha granted the monk Udāyī a five-day probation on account of one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. While he was on probation, in the interim, he committed one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. He requests the Saṅgha for a drawing back to the beginning on account of one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. The Saṅgha draws the monk Udāyī back to the beginning on account of one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. Whichever venerable one agrees with the drawing back to the beginning of the monk Udāyī on account of one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim, should remain silent. Whomever does not agree should speak.”

“Dutiyampi [V 0.0109] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe…[T 1.0180].

“A second time I state this matter… and so on…. A third time I state this matter… and so on….”

“Paṭikassito saṅghena udāyī bhikkhu antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanā mūlāya (syā.). Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The monk Udāyī has been drawn back to the beginning by the Saṅgha on account of one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I record it.”

Mānattārahamūlāyapaṭikassanā

Drawing Back to the Beginning of One Worthy of Mānatta

112. So parivutthaparivāso mānattāraho antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ [T 1.0181] pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ. Taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya [M 0.0116] sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikassi. Sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso mānattāraho antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikassatu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, mūlāya paṭikassitabbo –

112. Having completed his probation and being worthy of mānatta, he committed an offence in the interim: an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. He informed the monks: ‘Friends, I committed an offence: an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. I requested the Saṅgha for a five-day probation for one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. The Saṅgha granted me a five-day probation for one offence of an intentional emission of semen, concealed for five days. While undergoing probation, I committed an offence in the interim: an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. I requested the Saṅgha to draw me back to the beginning for one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. The Saṅgha drew me back to the beginning for one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. Having completed my probation and being worthy of mānatta, I committed an offence in the interim: an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. How then should I act?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha draw the monk Udāyī back to the beginning for one offence of an intentional emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. And, monks, he should be drawn back to the beginning in this way:’”

“Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… [T 1.0182] sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso mānattāraho antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ [P 2.0045] sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Monks, that monk Udāyī should approach the Saṅgha and... should say this: ‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days... Having completed that period of probation and being worthy of mānatta, in the interim I committed one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed. I ask the Saṅgha for relegation to the beginning on account of that one interim offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed.’ It should be requested a second time. It should be requested a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:”

113. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… [T 1.0183] so parivutthaparivāso mānattāraho antarā [V 0.0110] ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikasseyya. Esā ñatti.

113. ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī committed one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days… He, having completed his probation and being worthy of mānatta, in the interim committed one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha for relegation to the beginning on account of that one offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should relegate the monk Udāyī to the beginning on account of that one offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… so parivutthaparivāso mānattāraho antarā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ. So saṅghaṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati[T 1.0184]. Saṅgho udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāya paṭikassati. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā [M 0.0117] appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī committed one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days… Having completed his probation and being worthy of mānatta, he committed, in the interim, one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed. He requests the Saṅgha for relegation to the beginning on account of this one offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. The Saṅgha relegates the monk Udāyī to the beginning on account of this one offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. If any venerable one approves of the relegation of the monk Udāyī to the beginning on account of this one offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim, let him remain silent. If any does not approve, let him speak.’

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

‘For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…’

“Paṭikassito saṅghena udāyī bhikkhu antarā ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya mūlāyapaṭikassanā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘The monk Udāyī has been relegated to the beginning by the Saṅgha on account of this one offense of a deliberate emission of semen, unconcealed, committed in the interim. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.’

Tikāpattimānattaṃ

Mānatta for Three Offenses

114. So parivutthaparivāso bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… [T 1.0185] sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbaṃ –

114. Having completed the probationary period, he informed the monks: “Friends, I committed an offense—a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days… I have completed the probationary period. How should I now proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha grant the monk Udāyī a six-night mānatta for three offenses. And, monks, it should be granted in this way:”

“Tena, bhikkhave, udāyinā bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya [V 0.0111] pañcāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā pañcāhappaṭicchannāya pañcāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi…pe… [T 1.0186] sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbaṃ. Tatiyampi yācitabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Monks, that monk Udāyin, having approached the Saṅgha... should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I committed one offense: a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days. I, that one, requested from the Saṅgha a five-day probation on account of one offense of a deliberate emission of semen concealed for five days. The Saṅgha granted me a five-day probation on account of one offense of a deliberate emission of semen concealed for five days... I, that one, venerable sirs, having completed the probation, request from the Saṅgha the six-night mānatta on account of three offenses.’ It should be requested a second time. It should be requested a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable monk:”

115. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… [T 1.0187] so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

115. ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī committed one offense: a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days... He, having completed the probation, requests from the Saṅgha the six-night mānatta on account of three offenses. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the six-night mānatta on account of three offenses to the monk Udāyī. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ udāyī bhikkhu ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… [T 1.0188] so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ [M 0.0118] tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati. Saṅgho udāyissa bhikkhuno tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ [P 2.0046] chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati udāyissa bhikkhuno tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Udāyī committed one offense: a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for five days... He, having completed the probation, requests from the Saṅgha the six-night mānatta on account of three offenses. The Saṅgha grants the six-night mānatta on account of three offenses to the monk Udāyī. To whichever venerable one the granting of the six-night mānatta on account of three offenses to the monk Udāyī is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.’

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

‘For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…’

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena udāyissa bhikkhuno tissannaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.
