He should make the request a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:”

137. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji, ekā āpatti ekāhappaṭicchannā…pe… dasa āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyo tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyo tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

137. Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses: one offense concealed for one day… up to… ten offenses concealed for ten days. He requests from the Saṅgha a combined probation for those offenses, reckoned by the measure of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time. If the time is suitable for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha may grant a combined probation to the bhikkhu named so-and-so, reckoned by the measure of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [V 0.0129] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo [T 1.0222] āpajji – ekā āpatti ekāhappaṭicchannā…pe… dasa āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā [M 0.0137] āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyo tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyo tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyo tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses: one offense concealed for one day… up to… ten offenses concealed for ten days. He requests from the Saṅgha a combined probation for those offenses, reckoned by the measure of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time. The Saṅgha grants a combined probation to the bhikkhu named so-and-so, reckoned by the measure of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time. To whichever venerable one the granting of a combined probation to the bhikkhu named so-and-so, reckoned by the measure of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time, is approved, he should be silent. To whomever it is not approved, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time, I state this matter… up to… For a third time, I state this matter… up to…

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyo tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāso. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

A combined probation, reckoned by the measure of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time, has been granted by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus, I hold this.

Dvemāsaparivāso

Probation for two months.

138. Tena [P 2.0053] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpanno hoti dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya”nti. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa parivasantassa [T 1.0223] lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya”nti.

138. At that time, a certain bhikkhu had incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to him: “I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?” So he asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While he was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in him, and he thought: “I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months?”

So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ [M 0.0138] kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ [V 0.0130] dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ [T 1.0224] yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho tassa bhikkhuno itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

That bhikkhu informed the bhikkhus: “Friends, I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing the probation, a sense of shame arose in me. I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing the probation, a sense of shame arose in me, and it occurred to me: ‘What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months?’ How should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Well then, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha grant that bhikkhu a two-month probation for the other offense concealed for two months. And this is how it should be given:

“Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā, vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā, ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā, añjaliṃ paggahetvā, evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo[T 1.0225]. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ [M 0.0139] yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācāmīti.

“Then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined hands, and say thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. To me, this thought occurred: “I have indeed committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me: “I have indeed committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. To me, this thought occurred: ‘I have indeed committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me: ‘What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months?’ Therefore, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense concealed for two months.’”

“Dutiyampi [P 2.0054][V 0.0131] yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. “Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

139. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ [T 1.0226] saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. So saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

139. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, has incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to him: ‘Indeed, I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ So he asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While he was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in him: ‘Indeed, I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: “Indeed, I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha may grant the bhikkhu, named so-and-so, a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya [M 0.0140] dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ [T 1.0227] ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi [V 0.0132] āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. So saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, has incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to him: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ So he asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While he was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in him: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: “I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me a two-month probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense as well, concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for a two-month probation for the other offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants the bhikkhu, named so-and-so, a two-month probation for the other offense concealed for two months. To whichever venerable one the granting of a two-month probation to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for the other offense concealed for two months is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I speak of this matter... For a third time I speak of this matter...”

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāso. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tadupādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

“The Saṅgha has granted the bhikkhu named so-and-so two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should undergo probation for two months on account of that.”

Dve māsā parivasitabbavidhi

The Procedure for Undergoing Probation for Two Months

140. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti[T 1.0228]. So saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami [M 0.0141] – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. So saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tadupādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

140. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. It occurs to him thus: ‘I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for one offense concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for one offense concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, a sense of shame comes upon him: ‘I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. It occurred to me thus: “I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for one offense concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for one offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me two months’ probation for one offense concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame came upon me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well?’ He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should undergo probation for two months on account of that.”

141. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo[V 0.0133]; ekaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ekaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti. So saṅghaṃ yaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto [T 1.0229] itarampi āpattiṃ jānāti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ āpattiṃ jāniṃ, ekaṃ āpattiṃ na jāniṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ yaṃ āpattiṃ jāniṃ tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto itarampi āpattiṃ jānāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi [P 2.0055] āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tadupādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

141. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu falls into two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. He knows one offense, but does not know the other. He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the offense he knows, which was concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for that offense concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, he comes to know the other offense as well. It occurs to him thus: ‘I have fallen into two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. I knew one offense, but did not know the other. So I asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the offense I knew, which was concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me two months’ probation for that offense concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, I have come to know the other offense as well. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well?’ He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should undergo probation for two months on account of that.”

142. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ āpattiṃ sarati, ekaṃ āpattiṃ nassarati. So saṅghaṃ yaṃ āpattiṃ sarati tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya [M 0.0142] dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto itarampi āpattiṃ sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ āpattiṃ sariṃ, ekaṃ āpattiṃ nassariṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ yaṃ āpattiṃ sariṃ, tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ [T 1.0230] yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto itarampi āpattiṃ sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tadupādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

142. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. He remembers one offense, but does not remember the other. He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the offense he remembers, which was concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for that offense concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, he remembers the other offense as well. It occurs to him thus: ‘I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. I remembered one, but did not remember the other. So I asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the offense I remembered, which was concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me two months’ probation for that offense concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, I have remembered the other offense as well. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well?’ He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should undergo probation for two months on account of that.”

143. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekāya āpattiyā nibbematiko, ekāya āpattiyā vematiko. So saṅghaṃ yāya āpattiyā nibbematiko tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto itarissāpi āpattiyā nibbematiko hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā [V 0.0134] āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekāya āpattiyā nibbematiko, ekāya āpattiyā vematiko. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ yāya āpattiyā nibbematiko tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tassā āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto itarissāpi āpattiyā nibbematiko. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ [T 1.0231] saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho itarissāpi āpattiyā dvemāsappaṭicchannāya dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tadupādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

143. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. He is certain about one offense, but uncertain about the other. He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the offense about which he is certain, which was concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for that offense concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, he becomes certain about the other offense as well. It occurs to him thus: ‘I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months. I was certain about one, but uncertain about the other. So I asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the offense about which I was certain, which was concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me two months’ probation for that offense concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, I have become certain about the other offense as well. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months as well?’ He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for the other offense concealed for two months. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should undergo probation for two months on account of that offense.”

144. “Idha [M 0.0143] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekā āpatti jānappaṭicchannā, ekā āpatti ajānappaṭicchannā. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘kiṃ ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno? Kissāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti? Te evaṃ vadenti – ‘ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekā āpatti jānappaṭicchannā, ekā āpatti ajānappaṭicchannā. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tāyo ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno, tāsāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘yāyaṃ, āvuso[T 1.0232], āpatti jānappaṭicchannā, dhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ; dhammattā ruhati. Yā ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti ajānappaṭicchannā, adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ; adhammattā na ruhati. Ekissā, āvuso, āpattiyā bhikkhu mānattāraho’”ti.

144. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months—one offense was concealed knowingly, the other was concealed unknowingly. He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in the texts, a master of the Dhamma, a master of the Vinaya, a master of the Mātikā, wise, skilled, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. He says thus, ‘What offense has this bhikkhu committed, friends? For what is this bhikkhu undergoing probation?’ They reply thus: ‘This bhikkhu, friend, committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, both concealed for two months—one offense was concealed knowingly, the other was concealed unknowingly. He asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. These are the offenses this bhikkhu has committed, friend; for these he is undergoing probation.’ He then says, ‘Friends, the granting of probation for the offense that was concealed knowingly is lawful; it is valid because it is lawful. But as for the offense that was concealed unknowingly, friends, the granting of probation for that offense is unlawful; it is not valid because it is unlawful. For one offense, friends, the bhikkhu is deserving of penance.’”

145. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekā āpatti saramānappaṭicchannā, ekā āpatti assaramānappaṭicchannā. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī [V 0.0135] kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘ki ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno? Kissāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti? Te evaṃ vadenti – ‘ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekā āpatti saramānappaṭicchannā, ekā āpatti assaramānappaṭicchannā. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tāyo [M 0.0144] ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno; tāsāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘yāyaṃ, āvuso[T 1.0233], āpatti saramānappaṭicchannā dhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ; dhammattā ruhati. Yā ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti assaramānappaṭicchannā, adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ; adhammattā na ruhati. Ekissā, āvuso, āpattiyā bhikkhu mānattāraho’”ti.

145. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months: one offense was concealed while remembering, and one offense was concealed while not remembering. He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in the texts, a master of the Dhamma, a master of the Vinaya, a master of the Mātikā, wise, skilled, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. He asks, ‘Friends, what offense has this bhikkhu committed? For what is this bhikkhu undergoing probation?’ They reply, ‘Friend, this bhikkhu committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months: one offense was concealed while remembering, and one offense was concealed while not remembering. He asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him two months’ probation for those offenses concealed for two months. He has committed those offenses, friend; for those he is undergoing probation.’ He then says, ‘Friends, the granting of probation for the offense that was concealed while remembering is lawful; it is valid because it is lawful. But as for the offense that was concealed while not remembering, friends, the granting of probation for that offense is unlawful; it is not valid because it is unlawful. Friends, for one offense, the bhikkhu is deserving of penance.’”

146. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekā āpatti nibbematikappaṭicchannā, ekā āpatti vematikappaṭicchannā. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘kiṃ ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno? Kissāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti? Te evaṃ vadenti – ‘ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekā āpatti nibbematikappaṭicchannā, ekā āpatti vematikappaṭicchannā. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tāyo ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno; tāsāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘yāyaṃ[T 1.0234], āvuso, āpatti nibbematikappaṭicchannā, dhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ; dhammattā ruhati. Yā ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti vematikappaṭicchannā adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ; adhammattā na ruhati. Ekissā, āvuso, āpattiyā bhikkhu mānattāraho”ti.

146. Here, monks, a monk incurs two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months: one offense was concealed without uncertainty, and one offense was concealed with uncertainty. He asks the Saṅgha for two months’ probation on account of those offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months’ probation on account of those offenses concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, another monk arrives—learned, versed in the tradition, a master of the Dhamma, a master of the Vinaya, a master of the summaries, wise, accomplished, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. He says: ‘What offense has this monk incurred, friends? On account of what is this monk undergoing probation?’ They reply: ‘This monk, friend, incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months: one offense was concealed without uncertainty, and one offense was concealed with uncertainty. He asked the Saṅgha for two months’ probation on account of those offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him two months’ probation on account of those offenses concealed for two months. This monk incurred those offenses, friend; on account of them, this monk is undergoing probation.’ He says: ‘Friends, as for the offense that was concealed without uncertainty, the granting of probation on account of that offense is in accordance with the Dhamma; because it is in accordance with the Dhamma, it is valid. But indeed, friends, as for the offense that was concealed with uncertainty, the granting of probation on account of that offense is not in accordance with the Dhamma; because it is not in accordance with the Dhamma, it is not valid. Friends, on account of one offense, the monk is worthy of penance.’

147. Tena [P 2.0056] kho pana samayena aññattaro bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpanno hoti dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ [V 0.0136] yāceyya”nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ [M 0.0145] yāci. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – “ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ [T 1.0235] dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ itarampi māsaparivāsaṃ (syā. ka. evamuparipi) yāceyya”nti.

147. Now at that time a certain monk had incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to him: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ So he asked the Saṅgha for one month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him one month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While he was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in him: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: “I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for one month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for the other month's probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’

So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ kho, āvuso, dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho tassa bhikkhuno dvinnaṃ [T 1.0236] āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

He informed the monks: “Friends, I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for one month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. It occurred to me: ‘I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for one month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for the other month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months? How should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha grant that monk the other month of probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. And, monks, this is how it should be given:

“Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, bhante, dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo[M 0.0146]. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ [V 0.0137] ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ [T 1.0237] dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācāmīti. Dutiyampi [P 2.0057] yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should approach the Saṅgha... and he should say this: 'Venerable sirs, I have incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. It occurred to me: “I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me—I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. It occurred to me: ‘I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ So I asked the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months? Therefore, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months.' He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

148. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyyanti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ [M 0.0147] dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi [T 1.0238] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

148. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. It occurred to him: ‘I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ So he asked the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While he was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in him—he reflected: ‘I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. It occurred to me: “I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ He now asks the Saṅgha for the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the bhikkhu named so-and-so the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ [V 0.0138] yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dvinnaṃ [T 1.0239] āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsassa itarampi māsaparivāsassa (ka.), itarassapi māsaparivāsassa (syā.) dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. It occurred to him: ‘I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ So he asked the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While he was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in him—he reflected: ‘I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. It occurred to me: “I have indeed incurred two Saṅghādisesa offenses concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months?” So I asked the Saṅgha for one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month’s probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame arose in me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for the other month of probation as well for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants the bhikkhu named so-and-so the other month of probation as well for the two offenses concealed for two months. Whichever venerable one approves of granting the other month of probation for the two offenses concealed for two months to the bhikkhu named so-and-so should remain silent; whoever does not approve should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time, I state this matter… For a third time, I state this matter…

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāso itarampi māsaparivāso (ka.), itaropi māsaparivāso (syā.). Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The Saṅgha has granted the monk of such a name another month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. This is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.”

“Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā purimaṃ upādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

“Monks, that monk should undergo probation for two months, counting from the first.”

149. “Idha [M 0.0148] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami – ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Tassa me etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ [T 1.0240] saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ ekamāsaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ [V 0.0139] ekamāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tassa me parivasantassa lajjīdhammo okkami. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā purimaṃ upādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

149. “Furthermore, monks, in this teaching, a monk commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses which are concealed for two months. It occurs to him thus: ‘Indeed, I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses which were concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for one month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him one month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, a sense of shame descends upon him: ‘Indeed, I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses which were concealed for two months. It occurred to me thus: “Indeed, I have committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses which were concealed for two months. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for one month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months?” I then asked the Saṅgha for one month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me one month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. While I was undergoing probation, a sense of shame descended upon me. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for another month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for another month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him another month of probation on account of two offenses concealed for two months. Monks, that monk should undergo probation for two months, counting from the first.”

150. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ māsaṃ jānāti, ekaṃ māsaṃ na jānāti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ jānāti taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ jānāti taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto itarampi māsaṃ jānāti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ māsaṃ jāniṃ, ekaṃ māsaṃ na jāniṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ jāniṃ taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ [T 1.0241] māsaṃ jāniṃ taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto itarampi māsaṃ jānāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati[M 0.0149]. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā purimaṃ upādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

150. “Furthermore, monks, in this teaching, a monk commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses that have been concealed for two months; he is aware of one month, but he is not aware of the other month. He requests probation from the Saṅgha for the month of which he is aware, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him probation for the month of which he is aware, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, he becomes aware of the other month as well. It occurs to him: ‘I have indeed committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses that have been concealed for two months; I was aware of one month, but I was not aware of the other month. I requested probation from the Saṅgha for the month of which I was aware, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me probation for the month of which I was aware, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. While undergoing probation, I have become aware of the other month as well. What if I were to request probation from the Saṅgha for the other month as well, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months?’ He requests probation from the Saṅgha for the other month as well, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him probation for the other month as well, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. Monks, that monk should undergo probation for two months, counting from the first.”

151. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ māsaṃ sarati, ekaṃ māsaṃ nassarati. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ sarati taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ sarati taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto itarampi māsaṃ sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ māsaṃ sariṃ, ekaṃ māsaṃ nassariṃ. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ sariṃ taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ sariṃ taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto itarampi māsaṃ sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ [T 1.0242] āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa [V 0.0140] saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā purimaṃ upādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

151. “Furthermore, monks, in this teaching, a monk commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. He remembers one month, but does not remember the other month. He asks the Saṅgha for probation for the month he remembers, for the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him probation for the month he remembers, for the two offenses concealed for two months. While on probation, he remembers the other month. He thinks: ‘I committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. I remembered one month, but did not remember the other. I asked the Saṅgha for probation for the month I remembered, for the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me probation for the month I remembered, for the two offenses concealed for two months. While on probation, I remember the other month. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for probation for the other month as well, for the two offenses concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for probation for the other month, for the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him probation for the other month, for the two offenses concealed for two months. Monks, that monk should undergo probation for two months, counting from the first.”

152. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ māsaṃ nibbematiko, ekaṃ māsaṃ vematiko. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ nibbematiko taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ nibbematiko taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto itarampi māsaṃ nibbematiko hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; ekaṃ māsaṃ nibbematiko, ekaṃ māsaṃ vematiko[P 2.0058]. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ nibbematiko taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchānnānaṃ yaṃ māsaṃ nibbematiko taṃ māsaṃ parivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto itarampi māsaṃ nibbematiko. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ [M 0.0150] itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāceyya’nti. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ itarampi māsaṃ parivāsaṃ deti. Tena, bhikkhave[T 1.0243], bhikkhunā purimaṃ upādāya dve māsā parivasitabbā.

152. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months; for one month he is without doubt, and for one month he is in doubt. He asks the Saṅgha for probation for the month he is without doubt, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him probation for the month he is without doubt, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. While on probation, he becomes without doubt about the other month as well. It occurs to him thus: ‘I committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months; for one month I was without doubt, and for one month I was in doubt. I asked the Saṅgha for probation for the month I was without doubt, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted me probation for the month I was without doubt, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. While on probation, I have become without doubt about the other month as well. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for probation for the other month, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months?’ He asks the Saṅgha for probation for the other month, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him probation for the other month, on account of the two offenses concealed for two months. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should undergo probation for two months, based on the first.

153. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; eko māso jānappaṭicchanno, eko māso ajānappaṭicchanno. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘kiṃ ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno? Kissāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti? Te evaṃ vadenti – ‘ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo. Eko māso jānappaṭicchanno, eko māso ajānappaṭicchanno. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tāyo ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno tāsāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘yvāyaṃ, āvuso, māso jānappaṭicchanno dhammikaṃ tassa māsassa parivāsadānaṃ; dhammattā ruhati. Yo ca [V 0.0141] khvāyaṃ, āvuso, māso ajānappaṭicchanno adhammikaṃ tassa māsassa parivāsadānaṃ; adhammattā na ruhati. Ekassa, āvuso[T 1.0244], māsassa bhikkhu mānattāraho’ti.

153. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months; one month was knowingly concealed, one month was unknowingly concealed. He asks the Saṅgha for two months' probation for the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months' probation for the two offenses concealed for two months. While he is on probation, another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in the tradition, a master of the Dhamma, a master of the Vinaya, a master of the Mātikā, wise, experienced, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. He says thus: ‘Friends, what offense has this bhikkhu committed? For what is this bhikkhu undergoing probation?’ They say thus: ‘Friend, this bhikkhu committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months. One month was knowingly concealed, one month was unknowingly concealed. He asked the Saṅgha for two months' probation for the two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him two months' probation for the two offenses concealed for two months. Friend, this bhikkhu committed those offenses; for those, this bhikkhu is undergoing probation.’ He says thus: ‘Friends, for that month which was knowingly concealed, the granting of probation for that month is legitimate; because it is in accordance with the Dhamma, it is valid. But for that month which was unknowingly concealed, the granting of probation for that month is illegitimate; because it is not in accordance with the Dhamma, it is not valid. Friends, the bhikkhu is worthy of Mānatta for one month.’

154. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; eko māso saramānappaṭicchanno, eko māso assaramānappaṭicchanno. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo[M 0.0151]. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘kiṃ ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno? Kissāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti? Te evaṃ vadenti – ‘ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; eko māso saramānappaṭicchanno, eko māso assaramānappaṭicchanno. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tāyo ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno tāsāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘yvāyaṃ, āvuso, māso saramānappaṭicchanno dhammikaṃ tassa māsassa parivāsadānaṃ; dhammattā ruhati. Yo ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, māso assaramānappaṭicchanno adhammikaṃ tassa māsassa parivāsadānaṃ; adhammattā na ruhati. Ekassa, āvuso, māsassa bhikkhu mānattāraho’ti.

154. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months; one month concealed with remembrance, one month concealed without remembrance. He asks the Saṅgha for two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in the tradition, a master of the Dhamma, a master of the Vinaya, a master of the Mātikā, wise, experienced, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. He says: 'Friends, what offense has this bhikkhu committed? Why is this bhikkhu undergoing probation?' They reply: 'Friend, this bhikkhu committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months—one month concealed with remembrance, one month concealed without remembrance. He asked the Saṅgha for two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. These are the offenses he committed, and for these he is undergoing probation.' He says: 'Friends, for that month which was concealed with remembrance, the granting of probation for that month is legitimate; because it is in accordance with the Dhamma, it is valid. But for that month which was concealed without remembrance, the granting of probation for that month is illegitimate; because it is not in accordance with the Dhamma, it is not valid. Friends, for one month the bhikkhu is worthy of Mānatta.'

155. “Idha [T 1.0245] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; eko māso nibbematikappaṭicchanno, eko māso vematikappaṭicchanno. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ deti. Tassa parivasantassa añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘kiṃ ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno? Kissāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti? Te evaṃ vadenti – ‘ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dve saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji dvemāsappaṭicchannāyo; eko māso nibbematikappaṭicchanno, eko māso vematikappaṭicchanno. So saṅghaṃ dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ dvemāsappaṭicchannānaṃ dvemāsaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Tāyo ayaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āpanno tāsāyaṃ bhikkhu parivasatī’ti[V 0.0142]. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘yvāyaṃ, āvuso, māso nibbematikappaṭicchanno dhammikaṃ tassa māsassa parivāsadānaṃ; dhammattā ruhati. Yo ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, māso vematikappaṭicchanno adhammikaṃ tassa māsassa parivāsadānaṃ; adhammattā na ruhati. Ekassa, āvuso, māsassa bhikkhu mānattāraho”ti.

155. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months—one month concealed without doubt, one month concealed with doubt. He asks the Saṅgha for two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha grants him two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. While he is undergoing probation, another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in the tradition, a master of the Dhamma, a master of the Vinaya, a master of the Mātikā, wise, experienced, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. He asks: 'What offense has this bhikkhu committed, friends? For what is this bhikkhu undergoing probation?' They reply: 'Friend, this bhikkhu has committed two Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for two months—one month concealed without doubt, one month concealed with doubt. He asked the Saṅgha for two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. The Saṅgha granted him two months' probation for these two offenses concealed for two months. These are the offenses he has committed, and for these he is undergoing probation.' He then says: 'Friends, that month which was concealed without doubt—the granting of probation for that month is legitimate; it is valid because it is in accordance with the Dhamma. But as for that month which was concealed with doubt, the granting of probation for that month is illegitimate; it is invalid because it is not in accordance with the Dhamma. For one month, friends, the bhikkhu is worthy of Mānatta.'

Suddhantaparivāso

Probation until Purity

156. Tena [M 0.0152] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā [T 1.0246] āpattiyo āpanno hoti. So āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko. So bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ; āpattipariyantaṃ [P 2.0059] na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho tassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ detu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

156. At that time, a certain bhikkhu had committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He did not know the limit of the offenses, nor did he know the limit of the nights; he did not remember the limit of the offenses, nor did he remember the limit of the nights; he was uncertain about the limit of the offenses, and uncertain about the limit of the nights. He informed the bhikkhus, 'Friends, I have committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses. I do not know the limit of the offenses, nor do I know the limit of the nights; I do not remember the limit of the offenses, nor do I remember the limit of the nights; I am uncertain about the limit of the offenses, and uncertain about the limit of the nights. How should I proceed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha grant that bhikkhu Probation until Purity for those offenses. And thus, bhikkhus, it should be granted:

“Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ. Āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena [T 1.0247] bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, having approached the Saṅgha... should speak thus: 'Venerable sirs, I have committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses. I do not know the limit of the offenses, nor do I know the limit of the nights; I do not remember the limit of the offenses, nor do I remember the limit of the nights; I am uncertain about the limit of the offenses, and uncertain about the limit of the nights. That I, venerable sirs, request the Saṅgha for Probation until Purity for those offenses.' He should request a second time. He should request a third time. By a competent and capable bhikkhu, the Saṅgha should be informed:

157. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji. Āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

157. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He does not know the limit of the offenses, nor does he know the limit of the nights; he does not remember the limit of the offenses, nor does he remember the limit of the nights; he is uncertain about the limit of the offenses, and uncertain about the limit of the nights. That bhikkhu requests the Saṅgha for Probation until Purity for those offenses. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the bhikkhu named so-and-so Probation until Purity for those offenses. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji. Āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati[V 0.0143], rattipariyantaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ [M 0.0153] āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He does not know the limit of the offenses, nor does he know the limit of the nights; he does not remember the limit of the offenses, nor does he remember the limit of the nights; he is uncertain about the limit of the offenses, and uncertain about the limit of the nights. That bhikkhu requests the Saṅgha for Probation until Purity for those offenses. The Saṅgha gives the bhikkhu named so-and-so Probation until Purity for those offenses. To whichever venerable one the giving of Probation until Purity for those offenses to the bhikkhu named so-and-so is approved, he should be silent. To whom it is not approved, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time, I speak on this matter... For a third time, I speak on this matter...

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāso. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Probation until Purity for those offenses has been given by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. It is approved by the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus, by this silence, I record it.

158. “Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, suddhantaparivāso dātabbo; evaṃ [T 1.0248] parivāso dātabbo. Kathañca, bhikkhave, suddhantaparivāso dātabbo? Āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko – suddhantaparivāso dātabbo.

158. In this way, bhikkhus, Probation until Purity is to be given; thus probation is to be given. And how, bhikkhus, is Probation until Purity to be given? When one does not know the limit of the offenses, nor does one know the limit of the nights; when one does not remember the limit of the offenses, nor does one remember the limit of the nights; when one is uncertain about the limit of the offenses, and uncertain about the limit of the nights—Probation until Purity is to be given.

“Āpattipariyantaṃ jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ sarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante nibbematiko, rattipariyante vematiko – suddhantaparivāso dātabbo.

He knows the extent of the offenses but does not know the number of nights; he remembers the extent of the offenses but does not remember the number of nights; he is certain about the extent of the offenses but is uncertain about the number of nights—Probation until Purity should be granted.

“Āpattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ jānāti, ekaccaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ sarati, ekaccaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante ekacce vematiko, ekacce nibbematiko, rattipariyante vematiko – suddhantaparivāso dātabbo.

He knows some of the extent of the offenses but not others, and does not know the number of nights; he remembers some of the extent of the offenses but not others, and does not remember the number of nights; he is uncertain about some of the extent of the offenses but certain about others, and uncertain about the number of nights—probation for an indeterminate period should be granted.

“Āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ jānāti, ekaccaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ sarati, ekaccaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante ekacce vematiko, ekacce nibbematiko – suddhantaparivāso dātabbo.

He does not know the extent of the offenses, but knows some of the number of nights and not others; he does not remember the extent of the offenses, but remembers some of the number of nights and not others; he is uncertain about the extent of the offenses, but is uncertain about some of the number of nights and certain about others—probation for an indeterminate period should be granted.

“Āpattipariyantaṃ jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ jānāti, ekaccaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ [V 0.0144] sarati, rattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ sarati, ekaccaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante nibbematiko, rattipariyante ekacce vematiko, ekacce nibbematiko – suddhantaparivāso [P 2.0060] dātabbo.

He knows the extent of the offenses, and knows some of the number of nights but not others; he remembers the extent of the offenses, and remembers some of the number of nights but not others; he is certain about the extent of the offenses, but is uncertain about some of the number of nights and certain about others—probation for an indeterminate period should be granted.

“Āpattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ jānāti, ekaccaṃ na jānāti; rattipariyantaṃ [T 1.0249] ekaccaṃ jānāti, ekaccaṃ na jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ sarati, ekaccaṃ nassarati[M 0.0154]; rattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ sarati, ekaccaṃ nassarati; āpattipariyante ekacce vematiko, ekacce nibbematiko; rattipariyante ekacce vematiko, ekacce nibbematiko – suddhantaparivāso dātabbo. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, suddhantaparivāso dātabbo.

He knows some of the extent of the offenses but not others; he knows some of the number of nights but not others; he remembers some of the extent of the offenses but not others; he remembers some of the number of nights but not others; he is uncertain about some of the extent of the offenses but certain about others; he is uncertain about some of the number of nights but certain about others—probation for an indeterminate period should be granted. Thus, bhikkhus, probation for an indeterminate period should be granted.

159. “Kathañca, bhikkhave, parivāso dātabbo? Āpattipariyantaṃ jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ sarati, rattipariyantaṃ sarati; āpattipariyante nibbematiko, rattipariyante nibbematiko – parivāso dātabbo.

159. And how, bhikkhus, should probation be granted? He knows the extent of the offenses, he knows the number of nights; he remembers the extent of the offenses, he remembers the number of nights; he is without doubt about the extent of the offenses, he is without doubt about the number of nights—probation should be granted.

“Āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ sarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante nibbematiko – parivāso dātabbo.

He does not know the extent of the offenses, but he knows the number of nights; he does not remember the extent of the offenses, but he remembers the number of nights; he is doubtful about the extent of the offenses, but he is without doubt about the number of nights—probation should be granted.
