“Āpattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ jānāti, ekaccaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ jānāti; āpattipariyantaṃ ekaccaṃ sarati, ekaccaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ sarati; āpattipariyante ekacce vematiko, ekacce nibbematiko, rattipariyante nibbematiko – parivāso dātabbo. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, parivāso dātabbo.

He knows some of the extent of the offenses but does not know others, and he knows the number of nights; he remembers some of the extent of the offenses but does not remember others, and he remembers the number of nights; he is doubtful about some of the extent of the offenses but is without doubt about others, and is without doubt about the number of nights—probation should be granted. Thus, bhikkhus, probation should be granted.

Parivāso niṭṭhito.

The probation is finished.

3. Cattālīsakaṃ

3. The Fortieth

160. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu parivasanto vibbhami. So puna paccāgantvā bhikkhū upasampadaṃ yāci. Bhagavato [T 1.0250] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

160. At that time, a certain bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, disrobed. He then returned and requested higher ordination from the bhikkhus. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

“Idha [V 0.0145] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto vibbhamati. Vibbhantakassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna upasampajjati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation disrobes. For one who has disrobed, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he is ordained again, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto sāmaṇero hoti. Sāmaṇerassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna upasampajjati, tassa [M 0.0155] tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation becomes a novice. For a novice, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he is ordained again, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto ummattako hoti. Ummattakassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna anummattako hoti, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation becomes insane. For an insane bhikkhu, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he becomes sane again, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto khittacitto hoti. Khittacittassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na [P 2.0061] ruhati. So ce puna akhittacitto hoti, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo purivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation becomes of scattered mind. For a bhikkhu of scattered mind, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he again becomes of settled mind, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto vedanāṭṭo hoti. Vedanāṭṭassa[T 1.0251], bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna avedanāṭṭo hoti, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation becomes afflicted by pain. For a bhikkhu afflicted by pain, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he again is not afflicted by pain, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto, āpattiyā adassane, ukkhipiyyati ukkhipiyati (syā.), ukkhipīyati (ka.). Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati osāriyati (syā.), osārīyati (ka.), tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation is suspended for not seeing an offense. For a suspended bhikkhu, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he is reinstated again, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto, āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhipiyyati. Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation is suspended for not remedying an offense. For a suspended bhikkhu, bhikkhus, the probation does not take effect. If he is reinstated again, that very same previous granting of probation is his. The probation that was given was well-given, the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

“Idha [V 0.0146] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā, appaṭinissagge, ukkhipiyyati. Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation is suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view. For one who is suspended, bhikkhus, the probation does not count. If he is later reinstated, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone; the remainder must be undergone.

161. “Idha [M 0.0156] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho vibbhamati. Vibbhantakassa, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanā na ruhati. So ce puna [T 1.0252] upasampajjati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo.

161. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of being sent back to the beginning disrobes. For one who has disrobed, bhikkhus, the sending back to the beginning does not count. If he is reordained, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone. That bhikkhu must be sent back to the beginning.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe… khittacitto hoti…pe… vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiyyati…pe… āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhipiyyati…pe… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā, appaṭinissagge, ukkhipiyyati. Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, mūlāyapaṭikassanā na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of being sent back to the beginning becomes a novice… becomes insane… becomes deranged in mind… is afflicted by pain… is suspended for not acknowledging an offense… is suspended for not making amends for an offense… is suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view. For one who is suspended, bhikkhus, the sending back to the beginning does not count. If he is later reinstated, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone. That bhikkhu must be sent back to the beginning.

162. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattāraho vibbhamati. Vibbhantakassa, bhikkhave, mānattadānaṃ na ruhati. So ce puna upasampajjati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho. Tassa bhikkhuno mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

162. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of penance disrobes. For one who has disrobed, bhikkhus, the grant of penance does not count. If he is reordained, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone. That bhikkhu must be given the penance.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattāraho sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe… khittacitto hoti…pe… vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… āpattiyā adassane, ukkhipiyyati…pe… āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhipiyyati…pe… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā, appaṭinissagge[T 1.0253], ukkhipiyyati. Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, mānattadānaṃ na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho. Tassa bhikkhuno mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of penance becomes a novice... becomes insane... becomes deranged in mind... is afflicted by pain... is suspended for not acknowledging an offense... is suspended for not making amends for an offense... is suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view. For one who is suspended, bhikkhus, the grant of penance does not count. If he is later reinstated, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone. That bhikkhu must be given the penance.

163. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattaṃ caranto vibbhamati. Vibbhantakassa, bhikkhave[V 0.0147], mānattacariyā na ruhati. So ce puna upasampajjati tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho; yaṃ mānattaṃ dinnaṃ sudinnaṃ, yaṃ mānattaṃ ciṇṇaṃ suciṇṇaṃ, avasesaṃ caritabbaṃ.

163. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu while undertaking penance disrobes. For one who has disrobed, bhikkhus, the undertaking of penance does not count. If he is later reordained, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone; the penance that was given was well given, the penance that was undertaken was well undertaken; the remainder must be undertaken.

“Idha [M 0.0157] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattaṃ caranto sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe… khittacitto hoti…pe… vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… āpattiyā adassane, ukkhipiyyati…pe… āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhipiyyati…pe… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā, appaṭinissagge, ukkhipiyyati. Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, mānattacariyā na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo purivuttho suparivuttho; yaṃ mānattaṃ dinnaṃ sudinnaṃ, yaṃ mānattaṃ ciṇṇaṃ suciṇṇaṃ, avasesaṃ caritabbaṃ.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu while undertaking penance becomes a novice... becomes insane... becomes deranged in mind... is afflicted by pain... is suspended for not acknowledging an offense... is suspended for not making amends for an offense... is suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view. For one who is suspended, bhikkhus, the undertaking of penance does not count. If he is later reinstated, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone; the penance that was given was well given, the penance that was undertaken was well undertaken; the remainder must be undertaken.

164. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbhānāraho vibbhamati. Vibbhantakassa, bhikkhave, abbhānaṃ na ruhati. So ce puna upasampajjati[T 1.0254], tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho; yaṃ mānattaṃ dinnaṃ sudinnaṃ, yaṃ mānattaṃ ciṇṇaṃ suciṇṇaṃ. So bhikkhu abbhetabbo.

164. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of rehabilitation disrobes. For one who has disrobed, bhikkhus, rehabilitation does not count. If he is reordained, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone; the penance that was given was well given, the penance that was undertaken was well undertaken. That bhikkhu must be rehabilitated.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbhānāraho sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe…

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving of rehabilitation becomes a novice… becomes insane…

Khittacitto hoti…pe… vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… āpattiyā adassane, ukkhipiyyati…pe… āpattiyā appaṭikamme, ukkhipiyyati…pe… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā, appaṭinissagge, ukkhipiyyati. Ukkhittakassa, bhikkhave, abbhānaṃ [P 2.0062] na ruhati. So ce puna osāriyyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ. Yo parivāso dinno sudinno, yo parivuttho suparivuttho; yaṃ mānattaṃ dinnaṃ sudinnaṃ, yaṃ mānattaṃ ciṇṇaṃ suciṇṇaṃ. So bhikkhu abbhetabbo.

…becomes deranged in mind… is afflicted by pain… is suspended for not acknowledging an offense… is suspended for not making amends for an offense… is suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view. For one who is suspended, bhikkhus, rehabilitation does not count. If he is later reinstated, that previous grant of probation remains valid. The probation that was given was well given, the probation that was undergone was well undergone; the penance that was given was well given, the penance that was undertaken was well undertaken. That bhikkhu must be rehabilitated.

Cattālīsakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Section of Forty is concluded.

4. Chattiṃsakaṃ

4. 4. The Section of Thirty-Six

165. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā parimāṇāyo (sī. syā.) appaṭicchannāyo. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo.

165. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, falls into many Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are of a known number and are unconcealed. That bhikkhu must be sent back to the beginning.

“Idha [M 0.0158][V 0.0148] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, falls into many Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are of a known number and are concealed. That bhikkhu must be sent back to the beginning. And for him, a probation of aggregation with the previous offense must be given for the concealed offenses.

“Idha [T 1.0255] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, falls into many Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are of a known number, both concealed and unconcealed. That bhikkhu must be sent back to the beginning. And for him, a probation of aggregation with the previous offense must be given for the concealed offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati aparimāṇā aparimāṇāyo (sī. syā.) appaṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇā paṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi appaṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo…pe… [T 1.0256] parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu undergoing probation commits in the interim many Saṅghādisesa offenses of indeterminate number and unconcealed... of indeterminate number and concealed... of indeterminate number, both concealed and unconcealed... of both determinate and indeterminate number, and unconcealed... of both determinate and indeterminate number, and concealed... of both determinate and indeterminate number, and both concealed and unconcealed. That bhikkhu should be sent back to the beginning. A probation of concurrence with the first offense should be given to him for whichever of the offenses were concealed.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattāraho…pe… mānattaṃ caranto…pe… (yathāparivāsaṃ tathā vitthāretabbaṃ) abbhānāraho antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā appaṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo…pe… [T 1.0257] parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi…pe… aparimāṇā appaṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇā paṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi appaṭicchannāyo…pe… [T 1.0258] parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu deserving mānatta... or undergoing mānatta... or deserving rehabilitation, commits in the interim many Saṅghādisesa offenses of determinate number and unconcealed... of determinate number and concealed... of determinate number, both concealed and unconcealed... of indeterminate number and unconcealed... of indeterminate number and concealed... of indeterminate number, both concealed and unconcealed... of both determinate and indeterminate number, and unconcealed... of both determinate and indeterminate number, and concealed... of both determinate and indeterminate number, and both concealed and unconcealed. That bhikkhu should be sent back to the beginning. A probation of concurrence with the first offense should be given to him for whichever of the offenses were concealed.

Chattiṃsakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Section of Thirty-Six is completed.

5. Mānattasatakaṃ

5. The Hundred on Mānatta.

166. “Idha [M 0.0159][V 0.0149] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna so ce puna (ka.) upasampanno tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

166. Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses, disrobes without concealing them. Having been ordained again, he does not conceal those offenses. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā [P 2.0063] saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pacchimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses, disrobes without concealing them. Having been ordained again, he conceals those offenses. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for the later aggregate of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā paṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe [T 1.0259] yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses, disrobes after concealing them. Having been ordained again, he does not conceal those offenses. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for the earlier aggregate of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā paṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses, disrobes after concealing them. Having been ordained again, he conceals those offenses. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the earlier and the later aggregates of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

167. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

167. Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are concealed and offenses that are not concealed. Having disrobed and been ordained again, he does not conceal afterwards those offenses which he concealed previously; and those offenses which he did not conceal previously, he also does not conceal afterwards. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for the earlier aggregate of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are concealed and offenses that are not concealed. Having disrobed and been ordained again, he does not conceal afterwards those offenses which he concealed previously; he conceals afterwards those offenses which he did not conceal previously. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the earlier and the later aggregates of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha [T 1.0260][M 0.0160][V 0.0150] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are concealed and offenses that are not concealed. Having disrobed and been ordained again, he conceals afterwards those offenses which he concealed previously; he does not conceal afterwards those offenses which he did not conceal previously. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the earlier and the later aggregates of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Herein, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are concealed and offenses that are not concealed. Having disrobed and been ordained again, he conceals afterwards those offenses which he concealed previously; he also conceals afterwards those offenses which he did not conceal previously. To that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the earlier and the later aggregates of offenses according to how they were concealed, mānatta should be given.

168. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti. Yā āpattiyo na jānāti [P 2.0064] tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe [T 1.0261] ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

168. Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He knows some offenses; he does not know some offenses. The offenses he knows, he conceals; the offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later knows and does not conceal those offenses he previously knew and concealed; and later knows and does not conceal those offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for the former aggregate of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti. Yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti. Tassa[M 0.0161], bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He knows some offenses; he does not know some offenses. The offenses he knows, he conceals; the offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later knows and does not conceal those offenses he previously knew and concealed; and later knows and conceals those offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the former and the latter aggregates of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo [V 0.0151] chādeti. Yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe [T 1.0262] yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He knows some offenses; he does not know some offenses. The offenses he knows, he conceals; the offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later knows and conceals those offenses he previously knew and concealed; and later knows and does not conceal those offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the former and the latter aggregates of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He knows some offenses; he does not know some offenses. The offenses he knows, he conceals; the offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later knows and conceals those offenses he previously knew and concealed; and later knows and conceals those offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the former and the latter aggregates of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

169. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

169. Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He remembers some offenses; he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later remembers and does not conceal those offenses he previously remembered and concealed; and later remembers and does not conceal those offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for the former aggregate of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati[T 1.0263]. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā [M 0.0162] āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He remembers some offenses; he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later remembers and does not conceal those offenses he previously remembered and concealed; and later remembers and conceals those offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the former and the latter aggregates of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

“Idha [V 0.0152] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class. He remembers some offenses; he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. That bhikkhu, having disrobed and been ordained again, later remembers and conceals those offenses he previously remembered and concealed; and later remembers and does not conceal those offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal. To that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, after giving probation for both the former and the latter aggregates of offenses according to the duration of concealment, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo [T 1.0264] nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, here a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. He remembers some offenses; he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. That monk, having disrobed and been reordained—the offenses he formerly remembered and concealed, he later remembers and conceals; the offenses he formerly did not remember and did not conceal, he later remembers and conceals. For that monk, monks, having given probation for both the former and the later aggregate of offenses according to what was concealed, mānatta should be given.

170. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo [M 0.0163] pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

170. Furthermore, monks, here a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. Regarding some offenses, he is without doubt; regarding others, he is in doubt. The offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; the offenses about which he is in doubt, he does not conceal. That monk, having disrobed and been reordained—the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt. For that monk, monks, having given probation for the former aggregate of offenses according to what was concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi [T 1.0265] tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā [V 0.0153] nibbematiko chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, here a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. Regarding some offenses, he is without doubt; regarding others, he is in doubt. The offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; the offenses about which he is in doubt, he does not conceal. That monk, having disrobed and been reordained—the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later conceals while without doubt. For that monk, monks, having given probation for both the former and the later aggregate of offenses according to what was concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, here a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. Regarding some offenses, he is without doubt; regarding others, he is in doubt. The offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; the offenses about which he is in doubt, he does not conceal. That monk, having disrobed and been reordained—the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later conceals while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt. For that monk, monks, having given probation for both the former and the later aggregate of offenses according to what was concealed, mānatta should be given.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko [T 1.0266] chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, here a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses. Regarding some offenses, he is without doubt; regarding others, he is in doubt. The offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; the offenses about which he is in doubt, he does not conceal. That monk, having disrobed and been reordained—the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later conceals while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later conceals while without doubt. For that monk, monks, having given probation for both the former and the later aggregate of offenses according to what was concealed, mānatta should be given.

171. “Idha [M 0.0164] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe… khittacitto hoti…pe… (yathā heṭṭhā tathā vitthāretabbaṃ) vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi…pe… ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti…pe… ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā [P 2.0065] āpattiyo nassarati…pe… ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vedanāṭṭo hoti. So puna avedanāṭṭo hutvā yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi [V 0.0154] tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe [T 1.0267] vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimasmiñca pacchimasmiñca āpattikkhandhe yathāpaṭicchanne parivāsaṃ datvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

171. Furthermore, monks, here a monk, having committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses and not concealed them, becomes a novice… becomes insane… becomes of distracted mind… (it should be elaborated as below) becomes afflicted by pain… For him, there are offenses both concealed and unconcealed… he knows some offenses, he does not know some offenses… he remembers some offenses, he does not remember some offenses… regarding some offenses, he is without doubt; regarding others, he is in doubt. The offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; the offenses about which he is in doubt, he does not conceal. He becomes afflicted by pain. Then, having become unafflicted by pain again—the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt… the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later conceals while without doubt… the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later conceals while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later does not conceal while without doubt… the offenses he formerly concealed while without doubt, he later conceals while without doubt; and the offenses he formerly did not conceal while in doubt, he later conceals while without doubt. For that monk, monks, having given probation for both the former and the later aggregate of offenses according to what was concealed, mānatta should be given.

Mānattasataṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The hundredfold mānatta is concluded.

6. Samūlāyasamodhānaparivāsacatussataṃ

6. Four hundred cases of combined probation with relegation to the beginning.

172. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So [M 0.0165] puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo.

172. Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses without concealing them, and then disrobes. Having been reordained again, he does not conceal those offenses. That monk should be sent back to the beginning.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses without concealing them, and then disrobes. Having been reordained again, he conceals those offenses. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha [T 1.0268] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā paṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses, and having concealed them, he then disrobes. Having been reordained again, he does not conceal those offenses. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā paṭicchādetvā vibbhamati. So puna upasampanno tā āpattiyo chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses, and having concealed them, he then disrobes. Having been reordained again, he conceals those offenses. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

173. “Idha [V 0.0155] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo [P 2.0066] paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

173. Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are both concealed and not concealed. Having disrobed and been reordained, whichever offenses he previously concealed, he does not conceal afterward; and whichever offenses he previously did not conceal, he does not conceal afterward. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi [T 1.0269] appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti; yā [M 0.0166] āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are both concealed and not concealed. Having disrobed and been reordained, whichever offenses he previously concealed, he does not conceal afterward; and whichever offenses he previously did not conceal, he conceals afterward. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are both concealed and not concealed. Having disrobed and been reordained, whichever offenses he previously concealed, he conceals afterward; and whichever offenses he previously did not conceal, he does not conceal afterward. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa [T 1.0270] āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses. He has offenses that are both concealed and not concealed. Having disrobed and been reordained, whichever offenses he previously concealed, he conceals afterward; and whichever offenses he previously did not conceal, he conceals afterward. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

174. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo [V 0.0156] pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

174. Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses. Some offenses he knows, and some offenses he does not know. Whichever offenses he knows, he conceals; whichever offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been reordained, whichever offenses he previously knew and concealed, he afterward knows and does not conceal; and whichever offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal, he afterward knows and does not conceal. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo [M 0.0167] na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa [T 1.0271] āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation meanwhile commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses. Some offenses he knows, and some offenses he does not know. Whichever offenses he knows, he conceals; whichever offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been reordained, whichever offenses he previously knew and concealed, he afterward knows and does not conceal; and whichever offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal, he afterward knows and conceals. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. For whichever of his offenses were concealed, a combined probation should be given together with the earliest offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. He knows some offenses, and he does not know some offenses. The offenses he knows, he conceals; the offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses he previously knew and concealed, he later knows and conceals; the offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal, he later knows and does not conceal. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti. Yā āpattiyo jānāti tā āpattiyo chādeti, yā āpattiyo na jānāti tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe jānitvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe ajānitvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā jānitvā chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa [T 1.0272] āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. He knows some offenses, and he does not know some offenses. The offenses he knows, he conceals; the offenses he does not know, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses he previously knew and concealed, he later knows and conceals; the offenses he previously did not know and did not conceal, he later knows and conceals. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

175. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo [V 0.0157] sarati tā āpattiyo [M 0.0168] chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

175. Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. He remembers some offenses, and he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses he previously remembered and concealed, he later remembers and does not conceal; and the offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal, he later remembers and does not conceal. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo[T 1.0273]. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. He remembers some offenses, and he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses he previously remembered and concealed, he later remembers and does not conceal; and the offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal, he later remembers and conceals. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. He remembers some offenses, and he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses he previously remembered and concealed, he later remembers and conceals; the offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal, he later remembers and does not conceal. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati. Yā āpattiyo sarati tā āpattiyo chādeti; yā āpattiyo nassarati tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe saritvā chādesi [M 0.0169] tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe assaritvā nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā saritvā chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa [T 1.0274] āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. He remembers some offenses, and he does not remember some offenses. The offenses he remembers, he conceals; the offenses he does not remember, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses he previously remembered and concealed, he later remembers and conceals; the offenses he previously did not remember and did not conceal, he later remembers and conceals. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

176. “Idha [V 0.0158] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

176. Here, monks, a monk undergoing probation commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. Regarding some offenses he is without doubt, and regarding some offenses he has doubt. The offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; the offenses about which he has doubt, he does not conceal. Having disrobed and been ordained again, the offenses which he, being without doubt, previously concealed, he, being without doubt, later does not conceal; and the offenses which he, having doubt, previously did not conceal, he, being without doubt, later does not conceal. That monk should be sent back to the beginning. A combined probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, together with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo[T 1.0275]. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. Regarding some offenses he is without doubt; regarding other offenses he has doubt. He conceals those offenses about which he is without doubt; he does not conceal those offenses about which he has doubt. Having disrobed and been re-ordained, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later does not conceal while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt. That bhikkhu should be sent back to the beginning. A consolidated probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, combined with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo [M 0.0170] pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. Regarding some offenses he is without doubt; regarding other offenses he has doubt. He conceals those offenses about which he is without doubt; he does not conceal those offenses about which he has doubt. Having disrobed and been re-ordained, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later does not conceal while being without doubt. That bhikkhu should be sent back to the beginning. A consolidated probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, combined with the first offense.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vibbhamitvā so bhikkhu vibbhamitvā (ka.) puna upasampanno yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo [V 0.0159] pacchā nibbematiko chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo[T 1.0276]. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, commits several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim. Regarding some offenses he is without doubt; regarding other offenses he has doubt. He conceals those offenses about which he is without doubt; he does not conceal those offenses about which he has doubt. Having disrobed and been re-ordained, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt. That bhikkhu should be sent back to the beginning. A consolidated probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, combined with the first offense.

177. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe… khittacitto hoti…pe… vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi (yathā heṭṭhā vitthāritaṃ tathā vitthāretabbaṃ)…pe… ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti…pe… ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati…pe… ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vedanāṭṭo hoti. So puna avedanāṭṭo hutvā yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti[M 0.0171]; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti[T 1.0277]; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

177. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching a bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, having committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim without concealing them, becomes a novice… and so on… becomes insane… and so on… becomes one with a distracted mind… and so on… becomes afflicted by pain… and so on… For him there are offenses both concealed and unconcealed. (It should be elaborated as it was elaborated previously)… and so on… He knows some offenses but does not know others… and so on… He remembers some offenses but does not remember others… and so on… Regarding some offenses he is without doubt; regarding other offenses he has doubt. He conceals those offenses about which he is without doubt; he does not conceal those offenses about which he has doubt. He becomes afflicted by pain. Having become unafflicted by pain again, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later does not conceal while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later does not conceal while being without doubt… and so on… Or, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later does not conceal while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt… and so on… Or, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later does not conceal while being without doubt… and so on… Or, those offenses which he formerly concealed while being without doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt; and those offenses which he formerly did not conceal while having doubt, he later conceals while being without doubt. That bhikkhu should be sent back to the beginning. A consolidated probation should be given to him for whichever offenses were concealed, combined with the first offense.

178. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattāraho…pe… mānattaṃ caranto…pe… abbhānāraho antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā vibbhamati…pe… (mānattāraho ca mānattacārī ca abbhānāraho ca yathā parivāso vitthārito tathā vitthāretabbo).

178. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching a bhikkhu deserving of penance… and so on… while undertaking penance… and so on… deserving of reinstatement, having committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim without concealing them, disrobes… and so on… (The cases of one deserving of penance, one undertaking penance, and one deserving of reinstatement should be elaborated in the same way as the case of probation was elaborated).

179. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbhānāraho antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā appaṭicchādetvā sāmaṇero hoti…pe… ummattako hoti…pe… khittacitto hoti…pe… vedanāṭṭo hoti…pe… tassa honti āpattiyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi [V 0.0160] …pe… ekaccā āpattiyo jānāti, ekaccā āpattiyo na jānāti…pe… ekaccā āpattiyo sarati, ekaccā āpattiyo nassarati…pe… ekaccāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko, ekaccāsu [T 1.0278] āpattīsu vematiko. Yāsu āpattīsu nibbematiko tā āpattiyo chādeti; yāsu āpattīsu vematiko tā āpattiyo nacchādeti. So vedanāṭṭo hoti. So puna avedanāṭṭo hutvā yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi [M 0.0172] tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko nacchādeti…pe… yā āpattiyo pubbe nibbematiko chādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti; yā āpattiyo pubbe vematiko nacchādesi tā āpattiyo pacchā nibbematiko chādeti. So bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassitabbo. Yathāpaṭicchannānañcassa āpattīnaṃ [P 2.0067] purimāya āpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

179. Here, O monks, a monk worthy of rehabilitation, having in the interim fallen into many Saṅghādisesa offenses and not concealed them, becomes a novice...pe... becomes insane...pe... becomes one of distracted mind...pe... becomes one afflicted by pain...pe... He has offenses that are concealed and also not concealed...pe... he knows some offenses, he does not know some offenses...pe... he remembers some offenses, he does not remember some offenses...pe... regarding some offenses he is without doubt, regarding some offenses he has doubt. Those offenses about which he is without doubt, he conceals; those offenses about which he has doubt, he does not conceal. He becomes afflicted by pain. Then, having become free from that affliction, those offenses which he formerly, being without doubt, concealed, he later, being without doubt, does not conceal; those offenses which he formerly, being with doubt, did not conceal, he later, being without doubt, does not conceal...pe... those offenses which he formerly, being without doubt, concealed, he later, being without doubt, does not conceal; those offenses which he formerly, being with doubt, did not conceal, he later, being without doubt, conceals...pe... those offenses which he formerly, being without doubt, concealed, he later, being without doubt, conceals; those offenses which he formerly, being with doubt, did not conceal, he later, being without doubt, does not conceal...pe... those offenses which he formerly, being without doubt, concealed, he later, being without doubt, conceals; those offenses which he formerly, being with doubt, did not conceal, he later, being without doubt, conceals. That monk is to be sent back to the beginning. For his offenses, a probation of combination with the first offense is to be given, corresponding to the period of their concealment.

Samūlāyasamodhānaparivāsacatussataṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The four hundred cases of probation of combination with sending back to the beginning are concluded.

7. Parimāṇādivāraaṭṭhakaṃ

7. The Octad of Sections Beginning with Measure

180. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjitvā parimāṇā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… aparimāṇā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… ekanāmā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… [T 1.0279] nānānāmā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… sabhāgā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… visabhāgā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… vavatthitā appaṭicchādetvā…pe… sambhinnā appaṭicchādetvā vibbhamati…pe… (yathā heṭṭhā tathā vitthāretabbaṃ).

180. But here, monks, a monk, having incurred many Saṅghādisesa offenses of a limited number, without concealing them…pe… of an unlimited number, without concealing them…pe… of the same name, without concealing them…pe… of different names, without concealing them…pe… of a similar nature, without concealing them…pe… of a dissimilar nature, without concealing them…pe… determined, without concealing them…pe… mixed, without concealing them, disrobes…pe… (to be elaborated as below).

Parimāṇādivāraaṭṭhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eightfold section beginning with measure is concluded.

8. Dvebhikkhuvāraekādasakaṃ

8. The Section of Eleven on Two Monks

181. “Dve [V 0.0161] bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te saṅghādisese saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne yathāpaṭicchannānaṃ (sī.) cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

181. Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. They are of the view that it is a Saṅghādisesa offense. One conceals it, one does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation according to the concealed period, mānatta should be given to both.

“Dve [M 0.0173] bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te saṅghādisese vematikā honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. They are uncertain about the Saṅghādisesa offense. One conceals it, one does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation according to the concealed period, mānatta should be given to both.

“Dve bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te saṅghādisese missakadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. They are of the view that the Saṅghādisesa is a mixed offense. One conceals it, one does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation according to the concealed period, mānatta should be given to both.

“Dve bhikkhū missakaṃ āpannā honti. Te missake saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Two monks have incurred a mixed offense. They are of the view that the mixed offense is a Saṅghādisesa offense. One conceals it, one does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation according to the concealed period, mānatta should be given to both.

“Dve [T 1.0280] bhikkhū missakaṃ āpannā honti. Te missake missakadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Two monks have incurred a mixed offense. They are of the view that the mixed offense is a mixed offense. One conceals it, one does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation according to the concealed period, mānatta should be given to both.

“Dve bhikkhū suddhakaṃ āpannā honti. Te suddhake saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Ubhopi yathādhammaṃ kārāpetabbā.

Two monks have incurred a pure offense. They are of the view that the pure offense is a Saṅghādisesa. One conceals it, the other does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. Both should be proceeded against according to the Dhamma.

“Dve bhikkhū suddhakaṃ āpannā honti. Te suddhake suddhakadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Ubhopi yathādhammaṃ kārāpetabbā.

Two monks have incurred a pure offense. They are of the view that the pure offense is a pure offense. One conceals it, the other does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. Both should be proceeded against according to the Dhamma.

“Dve [V 0.0162] bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te saṅghādisese saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Ekassa hoti ārocessāmīti, ekassa hoti na ārocessāmīti. So paṭhamampi [P 2.0068] yāmaṃ chādeti, dutiyampi yāmaṃ chādeti, tatiyampi yāmaṃ chādeti – uṭṭhite aruṇe channā hoti āpatti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi [T 1.0281] mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. They are of the view that the Saṅghādisesa is a Saṅghādisesa. One thinks, ‘I will declare it,’ the other thinks, ‘I will not declare it.’ He conceals it during the first watch, conceals it during the second watch, and conceals it during the third watch. When dawn rises, the offense is concealed. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation corresponding to the period concealed, both should be given mānatta.

“Dve [M 0.0174] bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te saṅghādisese saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Te gacchanti ārocessāmāti. Ekassa antarāmagge makkhadhammo uppajjati na ārocessāmīti. So paṭhamampi yāmaṃ chādeti, dutiyampi yāmaṃ chādeti, tatiyampi yāmaṃ chādeti – uṭṭhite aruṇe channā hoti āpatti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. They are of the view that the Saṅghādisesa is a Saṅghādisesa. They go, thinking, ‘We will declare it.’ On the way, a disposition to dissemble arises in one: ‘I will not declare it.’ He conceals it during the first watch, he conceals it during the second watch, he conceals it during the third watch—when dawn rises, the offense is concealed. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation corresponding to the period concealed, both should be given mānatta.

“Dve bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te saṅghādisese saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Te ummattakā honti. Te pacchā anummattakā hutvā eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

“Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. They are of the view that the Saṅghādisesa is a Saṅghādisesa. They are insane. Later, having recovered their sanity, one conceals it, the other does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation corresponding to the period concealed, mānatta should be given to both.”

“Dve bhikkhū saṅghādisesaṃ āpannā honti. Te pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vadanti – ‘idāneva kho mayaṃ jānāma – ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī’ti. Te saṅghādisese saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko nacchādeti. Yo chādeti so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. Yathāpaṭicchanne cassa parivāsaṃ datvā ubhinnampi mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

“Two monks have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense. While the Pātimokkha is being recited, they say thus: ‘Only now, indeed, do we know that this rule, it seems, is transmitted in the Sutta, is included in the Sutta, and comes up for recitation every half-month.’ They are of the view that the Saṅghādisesa is a Saṅghādisesa. One conceals it, one does not conceal it. The one who conceals it should be made to confess a dukkaṭa offense. After giving him probation corresponding to the period concealed, mānatta should be given to both.”

Dvebhikkhuvāraekādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eleventh section on two monks is concluded.

9. Mūlāyaavisuddhinavakaṃ

9. The Ninefold Section on Impurity Concerning the Root

182. “Idha [T 1.0282] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ [V 0.0163] samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati [M 0.0175] dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; adhammena mānattaṃ deti, adhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

182. “Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses—some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of similar nature, some of dissimilar nature; some determined, some mixed. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses that are measurable and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha draws him back to the root for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is lawful, unalterable, and appropriate; they grant combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, but they grant mānatta contrary to the Dhamma and they rehabilitate contrary to the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi [P 2.0069] sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati.
