Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; adhammena mānattaṃ [T 1.0283] deti, adhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

“Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses—some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of a similar nature, some of a dissimilar nature; some determined, some mixed. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses that are measurable and concealed. He asks the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha draws him back to the root for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is lawful, unalterable, and appropriate; they grant combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, but they grant mānatta contrary to the Dhamma and they rehabilitate contrary to the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, adhammena mānattaṃ deti, adhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

“Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses—some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of a similar nature, some of a dissimilar nature; some determined, some mixed. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses that are measurable, both concealed and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha draws him back to the root for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is lawful, unalterable, and appropriate; they grant combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, but they grant mānatta contrary to the Dhamma and they rehabilitate contrary to the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati aparimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi [M 0.0176] …pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi appaṭicchannāyo[V 0.0164]. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati[T 1.0284]. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; adhammena mānattaṃ deti, adhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

“Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses—some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of similar nature, some of dissimilar nature; some determined, some mixed. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits in the interim multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: immeasurable, unconcealed... immeasurable, concealed... immeasurable, both concealed and unconcealed... both measurable and immeasurable, unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha draws him back to the root for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is lawful, unalterable, and appropriate; they grant combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, but they grant mānatta contrary to the Dhamma and they rehabilitate contrary to the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; adhammena [P 2.0070] mānattaṃ deti, adhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of similar nature, some of dissimilar nature; some determined, some of different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are both measurable and immeasurable, and concealed. He asks the Saṅgha to be sent back to the beginning for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is lawful, unalterable, and appropriate; it grants combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, grants penance contrary to the Dhamma, and rehabilitates contrary to the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi [T 1.0285] appaṭicchannāyopi. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena; dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; adhammena mānattaṃ deti; adhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of similar nature, some of dissimilar nature; some determined, some of different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are measurable and immeasurable, both concealed and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha to be sent back to the beginning for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is lawful, unalterable, and appropriate; it grants combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, grants penance contrary to the Dhamma, and rehabilitates contrary to the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.

Mūlāyaavisuddhinavakaṃ samūlāvisuddhinavakaṃ (ka.) niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninefold Section on Impurity Concerning the Root is finished.

10. Dutiyanavakaṃ idaṃ navakaṃ porāṇapotthakesu avisuddhivaseneva āgataṃ, vuccamānatatiyanavakena ca saṃsaṭṭhaṃ. taṃ paṭivisodhakehi asaṃsaṭṭhaṃ katvā visuṃ patiṭṭhāpitaṃ. sīhaḷasyāmapotthakesu pana taṃ visuddhivaseneva āgataṃ. taṃ panevaṃ veditabbaṃ –§10- mūlāyavisuddhinavaka (sī. syā.)§183. idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhu sambahulā saṃghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. so saṃghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati, tassa tassa saṃgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṃghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. so saṃghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, taṃ saṃgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. so bhikkhave bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (1-3)§idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhu sambahulā saṃghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. so saṃghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati, tassa saṃgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṃghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati aparimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. so saṃghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, taṃ saṃgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. so bhikkhave bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīti. (4-6)§idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhu sambahulā saṃghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjatī parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. so saṃghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati, tassa saṃgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṃghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi appaṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. so saṃghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, taṃ saṃgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. so bhikkhave bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (7-9)§mūlāya visuddhinavakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

10. The Second Ninefold Section

183. “Idha [M 0.0177] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto [V 0.0165] antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā appaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (1)

183. Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: some measurable, some immeasurable... some determined, some of different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are measurable and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha to be sent back to the beginning for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is unlawful, alterable, and inappropriate; it grants combined probation contrary to the Dhamma, grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitates in accordance with the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ [T 1.0286] āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena[M 0.0178], adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (2)

Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: some measurable, some immeasurable... some determined, some of different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are measurable and concealed. He asks the Saṅgha to be sent back to the beginning for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is unlawful, alterable, and inappropriate; it grants combined probation contrary to the Dhamma, grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitates in accordance with the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (3)

Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: some measurable, some immeasurable... some determined, some of different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are measurable, both concealed and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha to be sent back to the beginning for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is unlawful, alterable, and inappropriate; it grants combined probation contrary to the Dhamma, grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitates in accordance with the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi, ekanāmampi nānānāmampi, sabhāgampi visabhāgampi, vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti[M 0.0179]. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati aparimāṇā appaṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇā paṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi appaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ [V 0.0166] deti; dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (4-7)

Here, monks, a monk commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses: some measurable, some immeasurable; some of one name, some of various names; some of similar nature, some of dissimilar nature; some determined, some of different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits multiple Saṅghādisesa offenses in the interim that are: immeasurable and unconcealed... immeasurable and concealed... immeasurable, both concealed and unconcealed... both measurable and immeasurable, and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha to be sent back to the beginning for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is unlawful, alterable, and inappropriate; it grants combined probation contrary to the Dhamma, grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitates in accordance with the Dhamma. That monk, monks, is not purified from those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ [T 1.0288] mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (8)

Here, monks, a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses: of a determined period and of an undetermined period... recognized as having the same basis and distinct in its basis. He requests the Saṅgha for a consolidated probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him a consolidated probation for those offenses. While he is undergoing probation, in the interim, he commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses: of a determined period and of an undetermined period, which are concealed. He requests the Saṅgha for being sent back to the beginning for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the interim offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is unfit for the occasion; it unlawfully grants a consolidated probation, lawfully grants penance, and unlawfully rehabilitates him. Monks, that monk is not purified of those offenses.

“Idha [M 0.0180] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu avisuddho tāhi āpattīhi. (9)

Here, monks, a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses: of a determined period and of an undetermined period... recognized as having the same basis and distinct in its basis. He requests the Saṅgha for a consolidated probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him a consolidated probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, in the interim he commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses: of a determined period and of an undetermined period, concealed and unconcealed. He requests the Saṅgha for being sent back to the beginning for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the interim offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is unfit for the occasion; it unlawfully grants a consolidated probation, lawfully grants penance, and lawfully rehabilitates him. That monk, monks, is not purified of those offenses.

Dutiyanavakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Group of Nine is concluded.

11. Tatiyanavakaṃ

11. The Third Group of Nine

184. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa [T 1.0289] saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ [M 0.0181] samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ [V 0.0167] mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti[P 2.0071]. So parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo. So tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ. Taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo[T 1.0290]. Sohaṃ tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ purimāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāceyyaṃ dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ; dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhāna’nti. So saṅghaṃ purimāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ; dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhānaṃ. Taṃ saṅgho purimāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti; dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi ayaṃ paṭhamavāro sī syā. potthakesu paripuṇṇo dissati.

184. Here, monks, a monk commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses: of a determined period and of an undetermined period... recognized as having the same basis and distinct in its basis. He requests the Saṅgha for a consolidated probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him a consolidated probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, in the interim he commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined period which are unconcealed. He requests the Saṅgha for being sent back to the beginning for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the interim offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is unfit for the occasion, and it unlawfully grants a consolidated probation. Thinking he is undergoing probation, in the interim he commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined period which are unconcealed. While established in that state, he remembers the interim offenses related to the former offenses, and he remembers the interim offenses related to the latter offenses. It occurs to him: ‘I committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses: of a determined period and of an undetermined period... recognized as having the same basis and distinct in its basis. I requested the Saṅgha for a consolidated probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me a consolidated probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, in the interim I committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined period which were unconcealed. I requested the Saṅgha for being sent back to the beginning for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha sent me back to the beginning for the interim offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is unfit for the occasion, and it unlawfully granted me a consolidated probation. Thinking I was undergoing probation, in the interim I committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined period which were unconcealed. While established in this state, I remember the interim offenses related to the former offenses, and I remember the interim offenses related to the latter offenses. What if I were to request the Saṅgha for being sent back to the beginning for the interim offenses related to the former offenses and for the interim offenses related to the latter offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is fit for the occasion; and what if I were to request lawful consolidated probation, lawful penance, and lawful rehabilitation?’ He requests the Saṅgha for being sent back to the beginning for the interim offenses related to the former offenses and for the interim offenses related to the latter offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is fit for the occasion; he requests lawful consolidated probation, lawful penance, and lawful rehabilitation. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning for the interim offenses related to the former offenses and for the interim offenses related to the latter offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is fit for the occasion; it grants him lawful consolidated probation, grants him lawful penance, and lawfully rehabilitates him. Monks, that monk is purified of those offenses.

“Idha [M 0.0182] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati[T 1.0291]. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati, adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo. So tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimāāpattīnaṃ purimānaṃ āpattīnaṃ (ka.) antarāāpattiyo sarati, aparāāpattīnaṃ [V 0.0168] antarāāpattiyo sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ. Taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassi, adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇā paṭicchannāyo. Sohaṃ tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāceyyaṃ [T 1.0292] dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhāna’nti. So saṅghaṃ purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhānaṃ. Taṃ saṅgho purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena [M 0.0183] kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

Bhikkhus, here in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class, both measurable and immeasurable... both those determined by a common basis and those determined by a different basis. He asks the Saṅgha for consolidated probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him consolidated probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, in the interim, he commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class that are measurable and concealed. He asks the Saṅgha for a sending back to the beginning on account of the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning on account of the intervening offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, that is invalid, and that is not a proper case; it grants consolidated probation not in accordance with the Dhamma. Thinking, 'I am undergoing probation,' in the interim, he commits many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class that are measurable and concealed. Being established in that state, he remembers the intervening offenses of the earlier offenses, and he remembers the intervening offenses of the later offenses. It occurs to him thus: ‘I indeed committed many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class, both measurable and immeasurable... both those determined by a common basis and those determined by a different basis. I asked the Saṅgha for consolidated probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me consolidated probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, in the interim, I committed many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class that are measurable and concealed. I asked the Saṅgha for a sending back to the beginning on account of the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha sent me back to the beginning on account of the intervening offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, that is invalid, and that is not a proper case; it granted me consolidated probation not in accordance with the Dhamma. Thinking, “I am undergoing probation,” in the interim, I committed many offenses of the Saṅghādisesa class that are measurable and concealed. Being established in that state, I remember the intervening offenses of the earlier offenses, and I remember the intervening offenses of the later offenses. It would be good if I were to ask the Saṅgha for a sending back to the beginning on account of both the intervening offenses of the earlier offenses and the intervening offenses of the later offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, that is valid, and that is a proper case; and if I were to ask for consolidated probation in accordance with the Dhamma, for penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and for rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma.’ He asks the Saṅgha for a sending back to the beginning on account of both the intervening offenses of the earlier offenses and the intervening offenses of the later offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, that is valid, and that is a proper case; he asks for consolidated probation in accordance with the Dhamma, for penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and for rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma. The Saṅgha sends him back to the beginning on account of both the intervening offenses of the earlier offenses and the intervening offenses of the later offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, that is valid, and that is a proper case; it grants consolidated probation in accordance with the Dhamma, it grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and it rehabilitates him in accordance with the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is completely purified of those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ [T 1.0293] deti. So parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā [V 0.0169] saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ. Taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇā paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. Sohaṃ tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāceyyaṃ dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhāna’nti. So saṅghaṃ purimāpattīnaṃ antarā āpattīnañca, aparā āpattīnaṃ antarā āpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ [M 0.0184] yācati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhānaṃ. Taṃ saṅgho purimāpattīnaṃ antarā āpattīnañca, aparā āpattīnaṃ antarā āpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses—of a determined number and of an undetermined number... of a single type and of mixed types. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, he commits in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined number, both concealed and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for the interim offenses by means of a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is improper, and it grants combined probation unlawfully. Thinking, 'I am undergoing probation,' he commits in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined number, both concealed and unconcealed. Being in that state, he recalls the interim offenses among the former offenses, and he recalls the interim offenses among the later offenses. It occurs to him thus: 'I committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses—of a determined number and of an undetermined number... of a single type and of mixed types. I asked the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me combined probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, I committed in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined number, both concealed and unconcealed. I asked the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha relegated me to the root for the interim offenses by means of a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is improper, and it granted combined probation unlawfully. Thinking, 'I am undergoing probation,' I committed in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses of a determined number, both concealed and unconcealed. Being in that state, I recall the interim offenses among the former offenses, and I recall the interim offenses among the later offenses. What if I were to ask the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for the interim offenses among the former offenses and for the interim offenses among the later offenses, by means of a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is proper; and for combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, for penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and for rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma.' He asks the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for the interim offenses among the former offenses and for the interim offenses among the later offenses, by means of a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is proper; and for combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, for penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and for rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for the interim offenses among the former offenses and for the interim offenses among the later offenses, by means of a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is proper; it grants combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma; it grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma; and it rehabilitates him in accordance with the Dhamma. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is purified of those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati aparimāṇāyo appaṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyo…pe… aparimāṇāyo paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi…pe… parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi appaṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ [P 2.0072] yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasāmīti maññamāno…pe… taṃ saṅgho purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi imepi cattāro vārā sī. syā. potthakesu paripuṇṇā dissanti.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a definite number, some of an indefinite number... some of the same kind, some of different kinds. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, he commits in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses: of an indefinite number and unconcealed... of an indefinite number and concealed... of an indefinite number, both concealed and unconcealed... both of a definite and an indefinite number, and unconcealed. He asks the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for the interim offenses. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for the interim offenses by means of a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is improper, and it grants combined probation unlawfully. Thinking, 'I am undergoing probation,'... the Saṅgha relegates him to the root for the interim offenses among the former offenses and for the interim offenses among the later offenses, by means of a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is valid, and is proper; it grants combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitates him in accordance with the Dhamma. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is purified of those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ [V 0.0170] yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi [T 1.0294] aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā [M 0.0185] āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo. So tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ. Taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassi adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyo. Sohaṃ tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ purimā āpattīnaṃ antarā pattīnañca, aparāāpattīna [T 1.0295] antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāceyyaṃ dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhāna’nti. So saṅghaṃ purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhānaṃ. Taṃ saṅgho purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses—some definite, some indefinite... some of the same kind, some of different kinds. He asks the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, some definite, some indefinite, all concealed. He asks the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for these interim offenses. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for these interim offenses through an unlawful, invalid, and inappropriate formal act, and grants combined probation unlawfully. Thinking, 'I am on probation,' he commits in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, some definite, some indefinite, all concealed. While standing on that Saṅghādisesa ground, he recalls the interim offenses among the former offenses and the interim offenses among the later offenses. It occurs to him thus: 'I committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses—some definite, some indefinite... some of the same kind, some of different kinds. I asked the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, I committed in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, some definite, some indefinite, all concealed. I asked the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for these interim offenses. The Saṅgha relegated me to the root for these interim offenses through an unlawful, invalid, and inappropriate formal act, and granted combined probation unlawfully. Thinking, "I am on probation," I committed in the interim numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, some definite, some indefinite, all concealed. While standing on that Saṅghādisesa ground, I recall the interim offenses among the former offenses and the interim offenses among the later offenses. It would be good if I were to ask the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for both the interim offenses among the former offenses and the interim offenses among the later offenses through a lawful, unshakeable, and appropriate formal act; and for combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, for penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and for rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma.' He asks the Saṅgha for relegation to the root for both the interim offenses among the former offenses and the interim offenses among the later offenses through a lawful, unshakeable, and appropriate formal act; he asks for combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, for penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and for rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for both the interim offenses among the former offenses and the interim offenses among the later offenses through a lawful, unshakeable, and appropriate formal act, grants combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, grants penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitates him in accordance with the Dhamma. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is purified of those offenses.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. So saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati. Tassa saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ [M 0.0186] mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ [V 0.0171] yācati. Taṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti. So parivasāmīti maññamāno [T 1.0296] antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. So tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇampi aparimāṇampi…pe… vavatthitampi sambhinnampi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ. Tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. Sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ. Taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarāāpattīnaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi adhammikena kammena kuppena aṭṭhānārahena, adhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi. Sohaṃ parivasāmīti maññamāno antarā sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ parimāṇāyopi aparimāṇāyopi paṭicchannāyopi appaṭicchannāyopi. Sohaṃ tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ ṭhito purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattiyo sarāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghaṃ purimāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāceyyaṃ dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena [T 1.0297] samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhāna’nti. So saṅghaṃ purimā āpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, aparāāpattīnaṃ antarāāpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassanaṃ yācati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ, dhammena mānattaṃ, dhammena abbhānaṃ. Taṃ saṅgho purimā āpattīnaṃ antarā āpattīnañca, aparā āpattīnaṃ antarā āpattīnañca, mūlāya paṭikassati dhammikena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena, dhammena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, dhammena mānattaṃ deti, dhammena abbheti. So, bhikkhave, bhikkhu visuddho tāhi āpattīhi”.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu commits many Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a determined number, some of an undetermined number... offenses of the same kind and offenses of different kinds. He requests the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha grants him combined probation for those offenses. While on probation, he commits many further Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a determined number, some of an undetermined number, some concealed, some unconcealed. He requests the Saṅgha to relegate him to the root for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is inappropriate for the occasion, and grants him combined probation not in accordance with the Dhamma. Thinking, 'I am undergoing probation,' he commits many further Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a determined number, some of an undetermined number, some concealed, some unconcealed. While in that state, he remembers the intervening offenses among the former offenses, and he remembers the intervening offenses among the latter offenses. It occurs to him thus: ‘I committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a determined number, some of an undetermined number... offenses of the same kind and offenses of different kinds. I requested the Saṅgha for combined probation for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me combined probation for those offenses. While undergoing probation, I committed many further Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a determined number, some of an undetermined number, some concealed, some unconcealed. I requested the Saṅgha to relegate me to the root for the intervening offenses. The Saṅgha relegated me to the root for the intervening offenses by a formal act that is not in accordance with the Dhamma, is invalid, and is inappropriate for the occasion, and granted me combined probation not in accordance with the Dhamma. Thinking, "I am undergoing probation," I committed many further Saṅghādisesa offenses—some of a determined number, some of an undetermined number, some concealed, some unconcealed. While in that state, I remember the intervening offenses among the former offenses, and I remember the intervening offenses among the latter offenses. It would be good if I were to request the Saṅgha to relegate me to the root for the intervening offenses among the former offenses and for the intervening offenses among the latter offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is unshakeable, and is appropriate for the occasion; and to request combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma.’ He requests the Saṅgha to relegate him to the root for the intervening offenses among the former offenses and for the intervening offenses among the latter offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is unshakeable, and is appropriate for the occasion; and he requests combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and rehabilitation in accordance with the Dhamma. The Saṅgha relegates him to the root for the intervening offenses among the former offenses and for the intervening offenses among the latter offenses, by a formal act that is in accordance with the Dhamma, is unshakeable, and is appropriate for the occasion; it grants him combined probation in accordance with the Dhamma, it grants him penance in accordance with the Dhamma, and it rehabilitates him in accordance with the Dhamma. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is purified of those offenses.

Tatiyanavakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third section of nine is completed.

Samuccayakkhandhako tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Accumulations.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Appaṭicchannā [M 0.0187] ekāha-dvīha-tīha-catūha ca;

Pañcāhapakkhadasannaṃ, āpattimāha mahāmuni.

The Great Sage declared the offense: the unconcealed; and for one day, two, three, and four; for five days, a fortnight, and ten.

Suddhanto [V 0.0172] ca vibbhamanto, parimāṇamukhaṃ dve bhikkhū;

Tattha saññino dve yathā, vematikā tatheva ca.

Probation-until-purification, one who disrobes, the section beginning with 'measure,' and two bhikkhus; therein two are percipient, and likewise two are doubtful.

Missakadiṭṭhino [T 1.0298] dve ca, asuddhakekadiṭṭhino;

Dve ceva suddhadiṭṭhino.

And two who hold the view of it being mixed, two who view an impure offense as impure, and two who indeed hold the view of it being pure.

Tatheva ca eko chādeti, atha makkhamatena ca;

Ummattakadesanañca, mūlā aṭṭhārasa pannarasa (ka.) visuddhato.

Likewise, one conceals, and then with denigrating intent; the confession of one who is mad, sending back to the beginning, the eighteen cases, and from purity.

Ācariyānaṃ vibhajjapadānaṃ vibhajjavādīnaṃ (sī.), tambapaṇṇidīpapasādakānaṃ;

Mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ, vācanā saddhammaṭṭhitiyāti.

Of the teachers who expound the distinctions, who inspired faith in Tambapaṇṇidīpa, residents of the Mahāvihāra, their recitation is for the stability of the True Dhamma.

Samuccayakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter on Accumulations is concluded.

4. Samathakkhandhakaṃ

4. The Chapter on Settlement

1. Sammukhāvinayo

1. The Procedure in the Presence

185. Tena [T 1.0299][P 2.0073][M 0.0188][V 0.0173] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū asammukhībhūtānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karonti – tajjanīyampi, niyassampi, pabbājanīyampi, paṭisāraṇīyampi, ukkhepanīyampi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū asammukhībhūtānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karissanti – tajjanīyampi, niyassampi, pabbājanīyampi, paṭisāraṇīyampi, ukkhepanīyampī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū asammukhībhūtānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karonti – tajjanīyampi, niyassampi, pabbājanīyampi, paṭisāraṇīyampi, ukkhepanīyampī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ moghapurisānaṃ ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā asammukhībhūtānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karissanti – tajjanīyampi, niyassampi, pabbājanīyampi, paṭisāraṇīyampi, ukkhepanīyampi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – na, bhikkhave, asammukhībhūtānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – tajjanīyaṃ vā, niyassaṃ vā, pabbājanīyaṃ vā, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā, ukkhepanīyaṃ vā. Yo kareyya[T 1.0300], āpatti dukkaṭassa.

185. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six performed legal acts against monks who were not present: the act of censure, the act of subjection, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the act of suspension. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, censured, and spread it about, saying: “How can the monks of the group of six perform legal acts against monks who are not present: the act of censure, the act of subjection, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the act of suspension?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that the monks of the group of six perform legal acts against monks who are not present: the act of censure, the act of subjection, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the act of suspension?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “Monks, for those worthless men this is unsuitable, improper, unfitting, not befitting a recluse, not allowable, and should not be done. How can those worthless men, monks, perform legal acts against monks who are not present: the act of censure, the act of subjection, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the act of suspension? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a legal act should not be performed against monks who are not present—whether the act of censure, the act of subjection, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, or the act of suspension. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

186. “Adhammavādī puggalo adhammavādī sambahulā adhammavādī saṅgho. Dhammavādī puggalo dhammavādī sambahulā dhammavādī saṅgho.

186. A person who speaks what is not the Dhamma, many who speak what is not the Dhamma, a Saṅgha that speaks what is not the Dhamma. A person who speaks the Dhamma, many who speak the Dhamma, a Saṅgha that speaks the Dhamma.

Kaṇhapakkhanavakaṃ

The Section of Nine on the Dark Side

187. “Adhammavādī [V 0.0174] puggalo dhammavādiṃ puggalaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ [P 2.0074] rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

187. A person who proclaims what is not the Dhamma persuades a person who proclaims the Dhamma, makes him consider, makes him examine and re-examine, shows and repeatedly shows him: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī puggalo dhammavādī sambahule saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo[M 0.0189], idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

A person who proclaims what is not the Dhamma persuades many who proclaim the Dhamma, makes them consider, makes them examine and re-examine, shows and repeatedly shows them: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī puggalo dhammavādiṃ saṅghaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti (ka.). Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

A person who proclaims what is not the Dhamma persuades the Saṅgha that proclaims the Dhamma, makes it consider, makes it examine and re-examine, shows and repeatedly shows it: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī sambahulā dhammavādiṃ puggalaṃ saññāpenti nijjhāpenti pekkhenti anupekkhenti dassenti anudassenti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

Many who proclaim what is not the Dhamma persuade a person who proclaims the Dhamma, make him consider, make him examine and re-examine, show and repeatedly show him: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī [T 1.0301] sambahulā dhammavādī sambahule saññāpenti nijjhāpenti pekkhenti anupekkhenti dassenti anudassenti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

Many who proclaim what is not the Dhamma persuade many who proclaim the Dhamma, make them consider, make them examine and re-examine, show and repeatedly show them: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī sambahulā dhammavādiṃ saṅghaṃ saññāpenti nijjhāpenti pekkhenti anupekkhenti dassenti anudassenti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

Many who proclaim what is not the Dhamma persuade the Saṅgha that proclaims the Dhamma, make it consider, make it examine and re-examine, show and repeatedly show it: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī saṅgho dhammavādiṃ puggalaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti [V 0.0175] anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

The Saṅgha that proclaims what is not the Dhamma persuades a person who proclaims the Dhamma, makes him consider, makes him examine and re-examine, shows and repeatedly shows him: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī saṅgho dhammavādī sambahule saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

The Saṅgha that proclaims what is not the Dhamma persuades many who proclaim the Dhamma, makes them consider, makes them examine and re-examine, shows and repeatedly shows them: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

“Adhammavādī saṅgho dhammavādiṃ saṅghaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ [M 0.0190] satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, adhammena [T 1.0302] vūpasammati sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena.

The Saṅgha that proclaims what is not the Dhamma persuades the Saṅgha that proclaims the Dhamma, makes it consider, makes it examine and re-examine, shows and repeatedly shows it: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled unrighteously, by a counterfeit of the procedure-in-presence.

Kaṇhapakkhanavakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Nine on the Dark Side is concluded.

Sukkapakkhanavakaṃ

The Section of Nine on the Bright Side

188. “Dhammavādī puggalo adhammavādiṃ puggalaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

188. A person who speaks in accordance with the Dhamma convinces a person who speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma, makes him see, makes him examine, makes him examine accordingly, shows him, and shows him accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is thus settled, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the procedure in the presence.

“Dhammavādī puggalo adhammavādī sambahule saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

A person who speaks in accordance with the Dhamma convinces several persons who speak not in accordance with the Dhamma, makes them see, makes them examine, makes them examine accordingly, shows them, and shows them accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is thus settled, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the procedure in the presence.

“Dhammavādī puggalo adhammavādiṃ saṅghaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

A person who speaks in accordance with the Dhamma convinces a Saṅgha that speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma, makes it see, makes it examine, makes it examine accordingly, shows it, and shows it accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is thus settled, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the procedure in the presence.

“Dhammavādī sambahulā adhammavādiṃ puggalaṃ saññāpenti nijjhāpenti pekkhenti anupekkhenti dassenti anudassenti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi[V 0.0176], imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

Several persons who speak in accordance with the Dhamma convince a person who speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma, make him see, make him examine, make him examine accordingly, show him, and show him accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is thus settled, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the procedure in the presence.

“Dhammavādī sambahulā adhammavādī sambahule saññāpenti nijjhāpenti pekkhenti anupekkhenti dassenti [T 1.0303] anudassenti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

“Several speakers of Dhamma make several speakers of non-Dhamma understand, make them reflect, make them see, make them see accordingly, show them, and show them accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the settlement in the presence.”

“Dhammavādī sambahulā adhammavādiṃ saṅghaṃ saññāpenti nijjhāpenti pekkhenti anupekkhenti dassenti anudassenti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ[M 0.0191], imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

“Several speakers of Dhamma make a Saṅgha that speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma understand, make it reflect, make it see, make it see accordingly, show it, and show it accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the settlement in the presence.”

“Dhammavādī saṅgho adhammavādiṃ puggalaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

“A Saṅgha that speaks in accordance with the Dhamma makes a person who speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma understand, makes him reflect, makes him see, makes him see accordingly, shows him, and shows him accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the settlement in the presence.”

“Dhammavādī saṅgho adhammavādī sambahule saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethāti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayena.

“A Saṅgha that speaks in accordance with the Dhamma makes several persons who speak not in accordance with the Dhamma understand, makes them reflect, makes them see, makes them see accordingly, shows them, and shows them accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the settlement in the presence.”

“Dhammavādī saṅgho adhammavādiṃ saṅghaṃ saññāpeti nijjhāpeti pekkheti anupekkheti dasseti anudasseti – ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhāhi, imaṃ rocehīti. Evañcetaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, dhammena vūpasammati sammukhāvinayenā”ti.

“A Saṅgha that speaks in accordance with the Dhamma makes a Saṅgha that speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma understand, makes it reflect, makes it see, makes it see accordingly, shows it, and shows it accordingly: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Accept this, approve of this.’ If this legal issue is settled in this way, it is settled in accordance with the Dhamma, by the settlement in the presence.”

Sukkapakkhanavakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninefold section on the bright fortnight is finished.

2. Sativinayo

2. 2. The Verdict of Innocence

189. idaṃ vatthu pārā. 380 ādayo Tena [T 1.0304] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmatā dabbena mallaputtena jātiyā sattavassena arahattaṃ sacchikataṃ hoti[V 0.0177]. Yaṃ kiñci sāvakena pattabbaṃ sabbaṃ tena anuppattaṃ hoti. Natthi cassa kiñci uttari uttariṃ (sī.) karaṇīyaṃ, katassa vā paticayo. Atha kho āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “mayā kho jātiyā sattavassena arahattaṃ sacchikataṃ. Yaṃ kiñci sāvakena pattabbaṃ sabbaṃ mayā anuppattaṃ. Natthi ca me kiñci uttarikaraṇīyaṃ, katassa vā paticayo. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ saṅghassa veyyāvaccaṃ kareyya”nti?

189. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels' feeding ground. Now at that time, the Venerable Dabba the Mallian had realized arahantship at seven years of age. Whatever is to be attained by a disciple had all been attained by him. There was nothing further for him to do, nor anything to add to what had been done. Then, as the Venerable Dabba the Mallian was in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: “I realized arahantship at seven years of age. Whatever is to be attained by a disciple has all been attained by me. There is nothing further for me to do, nor anything to add to what has been done. What service, I wonder, should I perform for the Saṅgha?”

Atha [M 0.0192] kho āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghassa senāsanañca [P 2.0075] paññapeyyaṃ bhattāni ca uddiseyya”nti. Atha kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘mayā kho jātiyā sattavassena arahattaṃ sacchikataṃ. Yaṃ kiñci sāvakena pattabbaṃ, sabbaṃ mayā anuppattaṃ. Natthi ca me kiñci uttarikaraṇīyaṃ, katassa vā paticayo. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ saṅghassa veyyāvaccaṃ kareyya’nti[T 1.0305]? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṅghassa senāsanañca paññapeyyaṃ bhattāni ca uddiseyya’nti. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, saṅghassa senāsanañca paññāpetuṃ bhattāni ca uddisitu”nti. “Sādhu sādhu, dabba. Tena hi tvaṃ, dabba, saṅghassa senāsanañca paññapehi bhattāni ca uddisāhī”ti uddisāti (pārā. 380). “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ senāsanapaññāpakañca bhattuddesakañca sammannatu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ dabbo mallaputto yācitabbo dabbo yācitabbo (syā. ka.). Yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then this thought arose in the Venerable Dabba the Mallian: 'It would be good if I were to prepare the lodgings and assign the meals for the Saṅgha.' Then, in the evening, the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, having arisen from seclusion, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Dabba the Mallian said this to the Blessed One: 'Here, Venerable Sir, while I was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in my mind: ‘By me, arahantship was realized at seven years of age from birth. Whatever is to be attained by a disciple, all that has been attained by me. There is nothing further for me to do, nor is there an increasing of what has been done. What service, then, should I perform for the Saṅgha?’ To me, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred: ‘It would be good if I were to prepare the lodgings and assign the meals for the Saṅgha.’ I wish, Venerable Sir, to prepare the lodgings and assign the meals for the Saṅgha.' 'Good, good, Dabba. In that case, Dabba, you should prepare the lodgings and assign the meals for the Saṅgha.' 'Very well, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable Dabba the Mallian replied in assent to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha appoint Dabba the Mallian as the preparer of lodgings and the assigner of meals. And, monks, he should be appointed in this way. First, Dabba the Mallian should be requested. Having requested, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

190. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ senāsanapaññāpakañca bhattuddesakañca sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

190. “Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the Venerable Dabba the Mallian as the preparer of lodgings and the assigner of meals. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ senāsanapaññāpakañca bhattuddesakañca sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa senāsanapaññāpakassa ca bhattuddesakassa ca sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the Venerable Dabba the Mallian as the preparer of lodgings and the assigner of meals. If the appointment of the Venerable Dabba the Mallian as the preparer of lodgings and the assigner of meals is agreeable to the venerable ones, they should remain silent; whoever it is not agreeable to, they should speak.”

“Sammato [V 0.0178] saṅghena āyasmā dabbo mallaputto senāsanapaññāpako ca bhattuddesako ca. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti[T 1.0306].

“The Venerable Dabba the Mallian has been appointed by the Saṅgha as the preparer of lodgings and the assigner of meals. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.”

191. Sammato [M 0.0193] ca panāyasmā dabbo mallaputto sabhāgānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ekajjhaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti. Ye te bhikkhū suttantikā tesaṃ ekajjhaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti – te aññamaññaṃ suttantaṃ saṅgāyissantīti. Ye te bhikkhū vinayadharā tesaṃ ekajjhaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti – te aññamaññaṃ vinayaṃ vinicchinissantīti. Ye te bhikkhū dhammakathikā tesaṃ ekajjhaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti – te aññamaññaṃ dhammaṃ sākacchissantīti. Ye te bhikkhū jhāyino tesaṃ ekajjhaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti – te aññamaññaṃ na byābādhissantīti[P 2.0076]. Ye te bhikkhū tiracchānakathikā kāyadaḷhibahulā kāyadaḍḍhibahulā (sī.) viharanti tesampi ekajjhaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti – imāyapime āyasmanto ratiyā acchissantīti. Yepi te bhikkhū vikāle āgacchanti tesampi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā teneva ālokena senāsanaṃ paññapeti; apisu bhikkhū sañcicca vikāle āgacchanti – mayaṃ āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ passissāmāti.

191. Now, the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, having been appointed, prepared lodgings together for monks of similar dispositions. For those monks who were masters of the Suttas, he prepared lodgings together, thinking, ‘They will recite the Suttas to one another.’ For those monks who were masters of the Vinaya, he prepared lodgings together, thinking, ‘They will decide upon the Vinaya with one another.’ For those monks who were speakers on the Dhamma, he prepared lodgings together, thinking, ‘They will discuss the Dhamma with one another.’ For those monks who were meditators, he prepared lodgings together, thinking, ‘They will not disturb one another.’ For those monks who were accustomed to worldly talk and abounded in bodily training, he also prepared lodgings together, thinking, ‘These venerable ones will also dwell with this delight.’ And for those monks who arrived at the wrong time, having entered upon the fire-element, he would prepare lodgings by that very light. Indeed, some monks would intentionally come at the wrong time, thinking, ‘We shall see the miracle of psychic power of the Venerable Dabba the Mallian.’”

Te āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – “amhākaṃ, āvuso dabba, senāsanaṃ paññapehī”ti. Te āyasmā dabbo mallaputto evaṃ vadeti – “kattha āyasmantā icchanti kattha paññapemī”ti? Te sañcicca dūre apadisanti – “amhākaṃ, āvuso dabba, gijjhakūṭe pabbate senāsanaṃ [T 1.0307] paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, corapapāte senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhāyaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāre senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, gotamakakandarāyaṃ gomaṭakandarāyaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, tindukakandarāyaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, tapodakandarāyaṃ kapotakandarāyaṃ (ka.) senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, tapodārāme senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, jīvakambavane senāsanaṃ paññapehi. Amhākaṃ, āvuso, maddakucchimhi migadāye senāsanaṃ paññapehī”ti.

They approached the Venerable Dabba the Mallian and said, “Friend Dabba, prepare a lodging for us.” The Venerable Dabba the Mallian replied, “Where do the venerable ones wish? Where shall I prepare it?” Deliberately, they pointed to distant places: “Friend Dabba, prepare a lodging for us on Vulture Peak mountain. Friend, prepare a lodging for us at the Robbers' Cliff. Friend, prepare a lodging for us on the Black Rock on the slope of Isigili. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in the Seven-Leaf Cave on the slope of Vebhāra. Friend, prepare a lodging for us on the Snake's Hood slope in the Cool Wood. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in the Gotamaka ravine. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in the Tinduka ravine. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in the Tapoda ravine. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in the Tapoda Park. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in Jīvaka's Mango Grove. Friend, prepare a lodging for us in the Deer Park at Maddakucchi.”

Tesaṃ [M 0.0194] āyasmā dabbo mallaputto tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā aṅguliyā jalamānāya purato purato gacchati. Tepi teneva ālokena āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gacchanti. Tesaṃ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto evaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapeti – ayaṃ mañco, idaṃ pīṭhaṃ[V 0.0179], ayaṃ bhisi, idaṃ bibbohanaṃ bimbohanaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), idaṃ vaccaṭṭhānaṃ, idaṃ passāvaṭṭhānaṃ, idaṃ pānīyaṃ, idaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ, ayaṃ kattaradaṇḍo, idaṃ saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṃ, imaṃ kālaṃ pavisitabbaṃ[T 1.0308], imaṃ kālaṃ nikkhamitabbanti. Tesaṃ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto evaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapetvā punadeva veḷuvanaṃ paccāgacchati.

The Venerable Dabba the Mallian, having entered the meditative attainment of the fire element, went before them with his blazing finger. They too followed behind the Venerable Dabba the Mallian by that very light. The Venerable Dabba the Mallian prepared the lodging for them thus: “This is a bed, this is a stool, this is a mattress, this is a pillow, this is the toilet, this is the urinal, this is drinking water, this is water for use, this is a walking stick. This is the Sangha's agreement: ‘This is the time to enter; this is the time to depart.’” Having prepared the lodging for them in this way, the Venerable Dabba the Mallian returned once more to the Veḷuvana.

192. Tena kho pana samayena mettiyabhūmajakā mettiyabhummajakā (sī. syā. kaṃ.) bhikkhū navakā ceva honti appapuññā ca. Yāni saṅghassa lāmakāni senāsanāni tāni tesaṃ pāpuṇanti lāmakāni ca bhattāni. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe manussā icchanti [P 2.0077] therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhisaṅkhārikaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dātuṃ – sappimpi, telampi, uttaribhaṅgampi. Mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ pana bhikkhūnaṃ pākatikaṃ denti – yathārandhaṃ yathāraddhaṃ (syā.) kaṇājakaṃ bilaṅgadutiyaṃ. Te pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkantā there bhikkhū pucchanti – “tumhākaṃ, āvuso, bhattagge kiṃ ahosi, tumhākaṃ kiṃ ahosī”ti kiṃ nāhosi (syā. kaṃ.)? Ekacce therā evaṃ vadanti – “amhākaṃ, āvuso, sappi ahosi, telaṃ ahosi, uttaribhaṅgaṃ ahosī”ti. Mettiyabhūmajakā pana bhikkhū evaṃ vadanti – “amhākaṃ, āvuso, na kiñci ahosi – pākatikaṃ yathārandhaṃ kaṇājakaṃ bilaṅgadutiya”nti.

192. Now at that time, the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks were junior and of little merit. Whatever inferior lodgings of the Saṅgha there were, those they received, and inferior meals as well. At that time in Rājagaha, people wished to give the senior monks specially prepared almsfood—ghee, oil, and choice side-dishes.
