But to the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks, they gave ordinary food—as-it-is-cooked broken rice with sour gruel as the second dish. After the meal, having returned from the alms-round, they asked the senior monks, “Friends, what was there for you at the meal hall? What was there for you?” Some senior monks said thus: “Friends, for us there was ghee, there was oil, there were choice side-dishes.” But the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks said thus: “Friends, for us there was nothing special—just ordinary, as-it-is-cooked broken rice with sour gruel as the second dish.”

Tena kho pana samayena kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati saṅghassa catukkabhattaṃ deti niccabhattaṃ. So bhattagge saputtadāro upatiṭṭhitvā parivisati – aññe odanena pucchanti, aññe sūpena pucchanti, aññe telena pucchanti, aññe uttaribhaṅgena pucchanti. Tena kho pana samayena kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino bhattaṃ svātanāya mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ uddiṭṭhaṃ hoti. Atha [T 1.0309] kho kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati ārāmaṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. So yenāyasmā dabbo mallaputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ [M 0.0195] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho kalyāṇabhattikaṃ gahapatiṃ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati āyasmatā dabbena mallaputtena dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ etadavoca – “kassa, bhante, amhākaṃ ghare svātanāya bhattaṃ uddiṭṭha”nti? “Mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ kho, gahapati, bhikkhūnaṃ tumhākaṃ ghare svātanāya bhattaṃ uddiṭṭha”nti. Atha kho kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati anattamano ahosi. Kathañhi nāma pāpabhikkhū amhākaṃ ghare bhuñjissantīti gharaṃ gantvā dāsiṃ āṇāpesi – “ye, je, sve bhattikā āgacchanti te koṭṭhake āsanaṃ paññapetvā kaṇājakena bilaṅgadutiyena [V 0.0180] parivisā”ti. “Evaṃ ayyā”ti kho sā dāsī kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino paccassosi.

At that time, the householder Kalyāṇabhattika gave a perpetual meal for four to the Saṅgha. He, together with his wife and children, would attend and serve in the meal-hall; some would ask with rice, some with soup, some with oil, and some with side-dishes. Now at that time, the meal of the householder Kalyāṇabhattika for the next day was designated for the Mettiyabhūmajaka bhikkhus. Then the householder Kalyāṇabhattika went to the monastery on some business. He approached the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. To the householder Kalyāṇabhattika who was sitting to one side, the Venerable Dabba the Mallian instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened him with a Dhamma talk. Then the householder Kalyāṇabhattika, having been instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened by the Venerable Dabba the Mallian with a Dhamma talk, said to him, “Venerable sir, for whom is the meal at our house designated for tomorrow?” “Householder, the meal at your house for tomorrow is designated for the Mettiyabhūmajaka bhikkhus.” Then the householder Kalyāṇabhattika was displeased. Thinking, “How can these wicked bhikkhus eat at our house?” he went home and commanded a female servant: “Girl, for those who come for the meal tomorrow, prepare seats in the gateway and serve them broken rice with sour gruel as the second dish.” “Yes, master,” that female servant replied to the householder Kalyāṇabhattika.

Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū – hiyyo kho, āvuso, amhākaṃ kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino bhattaṃ uddiṭṭhaṃ; sve amhe kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati saputtadāro upatiṭṭhitvā parivisissati; aññe odanena pucchissanti, aññe sūpena pucchissanti, aññe [P 2.0078] telena pucchissanti, aññe uttaribhaṅgena pucchissantīti. Te teneva somanassena [T 1.0310] na cittarūpaṃ rattiyā supiṃsu. Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Addasā kho sā dāsī mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante; disvāna koṭṭhake āsanaṃ paññāpetvā mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca – “nisīdatha, bhante”ti. Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho na tāva bhattaṃ siddhaṃ bhavissati yathā mayaṃ koṭṭhake nisīdāpiyāmā”ti nisīdāpeyyāmāti (ka.). Atha kho sā dāsī kaṇājakena kāṇājakena (syā. kaṃ.) bilaṅgadutiyena upagañchi – bhuñjatha, bhanteti. “Mayaṃ kho, bhagini, niccabhattikā”ti. “Jānāmi ayyā niccabhattikāti. Api cāhaṃ hiyyova gahapatinā āṇattā – ‘ye, je, sve bhattikā āgacchanti, te koṭṭhake āsanaṃ paññāpetvā kaṇājakena bilaṅgadutiyena parivisā’ti. Bhuñjatha, bhante”ti. Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū – hiyyo kho, āvuso, kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati ārāmaṃ agamāsi dabbassa mallaputtassa [M 0.0196] santike. Nissaṃsayaṃ kho mayaṃ dabbena mallaputtena gahapatino antare paribhinnāti santike paribhinnāti (syā. kaṃ.). Te teneva domanassena na cittarūpaṃ bhuñjiṃsu. Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkantā ārāmaṃ gantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭisāmetvā bahārāmakoṭṭhake saṅghāṭipallatthikāya nisīdiṃsu tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā [T 1.0311] appaṭibhānā.

Then the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus thought: “Friends, just yesterday a meal was designated for us at the householder Kalyāṇabhattika’s. Tomorrow, the householder Kalyāṇabhattika, together with his son and wife, will attend upon us and serve us; some he will ask about rice, some about curry, some about oil, and some about side dishes.” With that very joy, they did not sleep as they wished that night. Then the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning and taken their bowls and robes, went to the residence of the householder Kalyāṇabhattika. The servant girl saw the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus coming from afar. Having seen them, she prepared a seat in the gateway and said to the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus: “Please sit, venerable sirs.” Then this thought occurred to the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus: “Surely the meal is not yet ready, as we are being made to sit in the gateway.” Then the servant girl approached with broken rice accompanied by sour gruel, saying: “Eat, venerable sirs.” “Sister, we are regular recipients of meals.” “I know that the masters are regular recipients of meals. But just yesterday I was instructed by the householder: ‘Girl, for those who come for the meal tomorrow, prepare a seat in the gateway and serve them broken rice accompanied by sour gruel.’ Please eat, venerable sirs.” Then the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus thought: “Friends, just yesterday the householder Kalyāṇabhattika went to the monastery to see Dabba the Mallian. Surely, Dabba the Mallian has sowed discord between us and the householder.” With that very displeasure, they did not eat as they wished. Then the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus, after the meal, having returned from their alms-round, went to the monastery, put away their bowls and robes, and sat down outside the monastery gateway with their outer robes tied as a supporting strap, silent, crestfallen, with drooping shoulders, with downcast faces, brooding, and unresponsive.

Atha kho mettiyā bhikkhunī yena mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca – “vandāmi ayyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū nālapiṃsu. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho mettiyā bhikkhunī mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca – “vandāmi ayyā”ti. Tatiyampi kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū nālapiṃsu. “Kyāhaṃ ayyānaṃ aparajjhāmi? Kissa maṃ ayyā nālapantī”ti? “Tathā hi pana tvaṃ, bhagini, amhe dabbena mallaputtena viheṭhiyamāne ajjhupekkhasī”ti? “Kyāhaṃ, ayyā, karomī”ti? “Sace kho tvaṃ, bhagini, iccheyyāsi, ajjeva bhagavā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ [V 0.0181] mallaputtaṃ nāsāpeyyā”ti. “Kyāhaṃ, ayyā, karomi? Kiṃ mayā sakkā kātu”nti? “Ehi tvaṃ, bhagini, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘idaṃ[P 2.0079], bhante, nacchannaṃ nappatirūpaṃ, yāyaṃ, bhante, disā abhayā anītikā anupaddavā sāyaṃ disā sabhayā saītikā saupaddavā; yato nivātaṃ tato savātaṃ tato pavātaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.); udakaṃ maññe ādittaṃ; ayyenamhi dabbena mallaputtena dūsitā’”ti. “Evaṃ ayyā”ti kho mettiyā bhikkhunī mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭissutvā paṭissuṇitvā (syā. kaṃ.) yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mettiyā sā mettiyā (syā. ka.) bhikkhunī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [T 1.0312] – “idaṃ, bhante, nacchannaṃ nappatirūpaṃ, yāyaṃ, bhante, disā abhayā anītikā anupaddavā sāyaṃ disā sabhayā saītikā saupaddavā; yato nivātaṃ tato savātaṃ; udakaṃ maññe ādittaṃ; ayyenamhi dabbena mallaputtena dūsitā”ti.

Then the bhikkhunī Mettiyā approached the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus. Having approached, she said to the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus: “I pay homage, venerable sirs.” When this was said, the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus did not speak. For a second time… For a third time, the bhikkhunī Mettiyā said to the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus: “I pay homage, venerable sirs.” For a third time, the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus did not speak. “In what have I offended the venerable sirs? Why do the venerable sirs not speak with me?” “It is because, sister, you looked on indifferently while we were being harassed by Dabba the Mallian.” “What am I to do, venerable sirs?” “Indeed, sister, if you wish, the Blessed One could have Venerable Dabba the Mallian expelled this very day.” “What am I to do, venerable sirs? What is it possible for me to do?” “Come, sister, approach the Blessed One, and having approached, say this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, this is unseemly and improper. Venerable sir, that direction which was safe, without affliction, and without calamity, that same direction is now unsafe, with affliction, and with calamity. Where it was sheltered from the wind, there it is now windy. The water, I think, is ablaze. I have been violated by the venerable Dabba the Mallian.’” “Very well, venerable sirs,” the bhikkhunī Mettiyā replied to the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus, and she approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, the bhikkhunī Mettiyā said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this is unseemly and improper. Venerable sir, that direction which was safe, without affliction, and without calamity, that same direction is now unsafe, with affliction, and with calamity. Where it was sheltered from the wind, there it is now windy. The water, I think, is ablaze. I have been violated by the venerable Dabba the Mallian.”

193. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ paṭipucchi – “sarasi tvaṃ, dabba, evarūpaṃ kattā [M 0.0197] yathāyaṃ bhikkhunī āhā”ti? “Yathā maṃ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ etadavoca – “sarasi tvaṃ, dabba, evarūpaṃ kattā yathāyaṃ bhikkhunī āhā”ti? “Yathā maṃ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ etadavoca – “sarasi tvaṃ, dabba, evarūpaṃ kattā yathāyaṃ bhikkhunī āhā”ti? “Yathā maṃ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti. “Na kho, dabba, dabbā evaṃ nibbeṭhenti. Sace tayā kataṃ katanti vadehi. Sace akataṃ akatanti vadehī”ti. “Yatohaṃ, bhante, jāto nābhijānāmi supinantenapi methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitā, pageva jāgaro”ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, mettiyaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nāsetha. Ime ca bhikkhū anuyuñjathā”ti. Idaṃ vatvā bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

193. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in connection with this matter, having had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assemble, questioned the Venerable Dabba the Mallian: “Dabba, do you remember having committed an act of such a nature as this bhikkhunī says?” “Venerable sir, it is as the Blessed One knows me.” A second time, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian: “Dabba, do you remember having committed an act of such a nature as this bhikkhunī says?” “Venerable sir, it is as the Blessed One knows me.” A third time, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian: “Dabba, do you remember having committed an act of such a nature as this bhikkhunī says?” “Venerable sir, it is as the Blessed One knows me.” “Dabba, the wise do not equivocate in this way. If it was done by you, say, ‘It was done.’ If it was not done, say, ‘It was not done.’” “Venerable sir, from the time I was born, I do not recall having engaged in the act of sexual intercourse even in a dream, let alone while awake.” Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, expel the bhikkhunī Mettiyā. And investigate these bhikkhus.” Having said this, the Blessed One, rising from his seat, entered the dwelling.

Atha kho te bhikkhū mettiyaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nāsesuṃ. Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “māvuso, mettiyaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nāsetha, na sā kiñci aparajjhati; amhehi sā ussāhitā kupitehi anattamanehi cāvanādhippāyehī”ti. “Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ [T 1.0313] mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsethā”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ [V 0.0182] …pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsentī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

Then those bhikkhus ruined the bhikkhunī Mettiyā. Then the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus said to those bhikkhus: “Friends, do not ruin the bhikkhunī Mettiyā; she has not committed any offense. She was incited by us, who were angry, displeased, and intended to cause his downfall.” “But friends, did you accuse the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a groundless corruption of virtue?” “Yes, friends.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a groundless corruption of virtue?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse Dabba the Mallian of a groundless corruption of virtue?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:

“Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa sativinayaṃ detu. Evañca [P 2.0080] pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo – “tena, bhikkhave, dabbena mallaputtena saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā, vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā, ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā, añjaliṃ paggahetvā, evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ime maṃ, bhante, mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Sohaṃ, bhante, sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo – ‘ime maṃ, bhante mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Sohaṃ [M 0.0198] sohaṃ bhante (ka.) sativepullappatto tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācāmī’ti. “Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha grant Dabba the Mallian, who has attained the fullness of mindfulness, the verdict of mindfulness. And it should be granted in this way: Bhikkhus, that Dabba the Mallian should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit down squatting, raise his joined palms, and he should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse me of a groundless corruption of virtue. I, venerable sirs, having attained the fullness of mindfulness, request the verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha.’ He should request it a second time. He should request it a third time: ‘Venerable sirs, these Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse me of a groundless corruption of virtue. I, venerable sirs, having attained the fullness of mindfulness, request the verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha for the third time.’ A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:”

194. Suṇātu [T 1.0314] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Āyasmā dabbo mallaputto sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa sativinayaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

194. “Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a baseless corruption of virtue. The Venerable Dabba the Mallian, having reached the fullness of mindfulness, requests the verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the verdict of mindfulness to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, who has reached the fullness of mindfulness. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Āyasmā dabbo mallaputto sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācati. Saṅgho āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa sativinayaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa sativinayassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a baseless corruption of virtue. The Venerable Dabba the Mallian, having reached the fullness of mindfulness, requests the verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha grants the verdict of mindfulness to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, who has reached the fullness of mindfulness. Whichever venerable one approves of the granting of the verdict of mindfulness to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, who has reached the fullness of mindfulness, should remain silent. Whichever one does not approve, should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ime mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Āyasmā dabbo mallaputto sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācati. Saṅgho āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa sativinayaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati āyasmato [V 0.0183] dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa sativinayassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“A second time I speak on this matter… and a third time I speak on this matter: Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. These Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus accuse the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a baseless corruption of virtue. The Venerable Dabba the Mallian, having reached the fullness of mindfulness, requests the verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha grants the verdict of mindfulness to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, who has reached the fullness of mindfulness. Whichever venerable one approves of the granting of the verdict of mindfulness to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, who has reached the fullness of mindfulness, should remain silent. Whichever one does not approve, should speak.”

“Dinno saṅghena āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa sativepullappattassa [T 1.0315] sativinayo. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The verdict of mindfulness has been granted by the Saṅgha to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian, who has reached the fullness of mindfulness. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.”

195. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, dhammikāni sativinayassa dānāni. Suddho hoti bhikkhu anāpattiko, anuvadanti ca naṃ, yācati ca, tassa saṅgho sativinayaṃ deti dhammena samaggena – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammikāni sativinayassa dānānī”ti.

195. “Bhikkhus, there are these five lawful grants of the verdict of mindfulness. A bhikkhu is pure and without offense; they accuse him, and he requests it; the Saṅgha grants him a verdict of mindfulness in accordance with the Dhamma and in concord. These, bhikkhus, are the five lawful grants of the verdict of mindfulness.”

3. Amūḷhavinayo

3. The Procedure for the Undeluded

196. Tena [M 0.0199] kho pana samayena gaggo bhikkhu ummattako hoti, cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Bhikkhū gaggaṃ bhikkhuṃ ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – “saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā”ti? So evaṃ vadeti – “ahaṃ kho, āvuso[P 2.0081], ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata”nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – “saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā”ti? Ye te bhikkhū appicchā..pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū gaggaṃ bhikkhuṃ ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codessanti – “saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti! So evaṃ vadeti [T 1.0316] – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – “saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā”ti? Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

196. At that time, the monk Gagga was insane, his mind deranged. Being insane and with his mind deranged, he had habitually engaged in much conduct unbefitting a monk, transgressing in speech and deed. The monks accused the monk Gagga of an offense habitually practiced while insane and with a deranged mind, saying: “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.” He said thus: “Friends, indeed I was insane, my mind deranged. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressed in speech and deed. I do not remember it. This was done by me while deluded.” Even when he spoke thus, they continued to accuse him, saying: “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.” Those monks who were of few desires… grumbled, criticized, and complained: ‘How indeed can monks accuse the monk Gagga of an offense habitually practiced while insane and with a deranged mind, saying: “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense!” And he says thus: “Friends, indeed I was insane, my mind deranged. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressed in speech and deed. I do not remember it. This was done by me while deluded.” And even when he speaks thus, they continue to accuse him, saying: “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense!”’ Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘Is it true, monks…?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’… Having rebuked them… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

“Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho gaggassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayaṃ detu. Evañca [V 0.0184] pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo – “tena, bhikkhave, gaggena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā, vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā, ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā, añjaliṃ paggahetvā, evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Maṃ bhikkhū ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi maṃ vuccamānā codenteva [M 0.0200] – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? Sohaṃ[T 1.0317], bhante, amūḷho saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Maṃ bhikkhū ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi maṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? Sohaṃ amūḷho sohaṃ bhante amūḷho (ka.) tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācāmī’ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha grant the verdict of past insanity to the monk Gagga, who is no longer deluded. And this is how it should be granted: Monks, the monk Gagga should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit in the squatting position, raise his joined palms, and say: ‘Venerable sirs, I was insane, with a deranged mind. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressed in speech and deed. The monks accuse me of an offense habitually practiced while insane and with a deranged mind, saying, “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.” I reply, “Friends, indeed I was insane, with a deranged mind. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressed in speech and deed. I do not remember it. This was done by me while deluded.” Even when I say this, they continue to accuse me, saying, “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.” Venerable sirs, I, being no longer deluded, request the Saṅgha for the verdict of past insanity.’ A second time he should make the request. A third time he should make the request: ‘Venerable sirs, I was insane, with a deranged mind. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressed in speech and deed. The monks accuse me of an offense habitually practiced while insane and with a deranged mind, saying, “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.” I reply, “Friends, indeed I was insane, with a deranged mind. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressed in speech and deed. I do not remember it. This was done by me while deluded.” Even when I say this, they continue to accuse me, saying, “Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.” Venerable sirs, I, being no longer deluded, for the third time request the Saṅgha for the verdict of past insanity.’ A competent and capable monk should then inform the Saṅgha:”

197. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ gaggo bhikkhu ummattako ahosi cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Bhikkhū gaggaṃ bhikkhuṃ ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ [T 1.0318] bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi, mūḷhena [P 2.0082] me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So amūḷho saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho gaggassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

197. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This monk Gagga was insane, his mind deranged. Being insane and with a deranged mind, he habitually practiced much conduct unbefitting a monk, transgressing in speech and deed. The monks charge the monk Gagga with an offense habitually practiced while he was insane and his mind was deranged, saying: ‘Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.’ He speaks thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I was insane, my mind deranged. By me, being insane and with a deranged mind, much conduct unbefitting a monk was habitually practiced, transgressing in speech and deed. I do not remember that; this was done by me while deluded.’ Even when spoken to thus, they continue to charge him: ‘Venerable one, remember that you have fallen into such an offense.’ He, being no longer deluded, requests the Saṅgha for the verdict of past insanity. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the verdict of past insanity to the monk Gagga, who is no longer deluded. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [V 0.0185] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ gaggo bhikkhu ummattako ahosi cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Bhikkhū gaggaṃ bhikkhuṃ ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ [M 0.0201] bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So amūḷho saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācati. Saṅgho gaggassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati gaggassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This monk Gagga was insane, his mind being deranged. While insane and with a deranged mind, he engaged in much unmonastic conduct, transgressing in speech and deed. The monks charge the monk Gagga with an offense committed while insane and with a deranged mind: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ He replies: ‘Indeed, friends, I was insane, my mind being deranged. While insane and with a deranged mind, I engaged in much unmonastic conduct, transgressing in speech and deed. I do not remember it; this was done by me in a state of delusion.’ Even when spoken to thus, they continue to charge him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ He, being no longer deluded, requests the Saṅgha for the Settlement of Non-Delusion. The Saṅgha grants the Settlement of Non-Delusion to the monk Gagga, who is no longer deluded. Let any venerable one who approves of granting the Settlement of Non-Delusion to the monk Gagga, who is no longer deluded, remain silent. Let any who does not approve, speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter... For a third time I state this matter...

“Dinno saṅghena gaggassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayo. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī[T 1.0319], evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The Settlement of Non-Delusion has been granted by the Saṅgha to the monk Gagga, who is no longer deluded. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand this.

198. “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, adhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānāni, tīṇi dhammikāni. Kammāni tīṇi adhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānāni?

198. Monks, there are these three unlawful grants of the Settlement of Non-Delusion, and three lawful ones. What are the three unlawful grants of the Settlement of Non-Delusion?

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So saramānova evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. Tassa saṅgho amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Adhammikaṃ amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ.

Here, monks, a monk has committed an offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of monks, or a single individual charges him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ Though remembering, he says: ‘Indeed, friends, I do not remember having committed such an offense.’ The Saṅgha grants him the Settlement of Non-Delusion. This is an unlawful granting of the Settlement of Non-Delusion.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So saramānova evaṃ vadeti – ‘sarāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, yathāsupinantenā’ti. Tassa saṅgho amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Adhammikaṃ amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, a monk here has committed an offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of monks, or a single individual charges him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ Though remembering, he says: ‘Friends, I remember it as if in a dream.’ The Saṅgha grants him the Settlement of Non-Delusion. This is an unlawful granting of the Settlement of Non-Delusion.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā [V 0.0186] vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So anummattako ummattakālayaṃ karoti – ‘ahampi kho evaṃ karomi. Tumhepi evaṃ karotha. Mayhampi etaṃ kappati. Tumhākampetaṃ kappatī’ti. Tassa saṅgho amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Adhammikaṃ amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ. Imāni tīṇi adhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānāni.

Furthermore, monks, a monk here has committed an offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of monks, or a single individual charges him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ Though not insane, he feigns insanity, saying: ‘I too do this. You too should do this. This is allowable for me, and this is allowable for you.’ The Saṅgha grants him the Settlement of Non-Delusion. This is an unlawful granting of the Settlement of Non-Delusion. These are the three unlawful grants of the Settlement of Non-Delusion.

199. “Katamāni [T 1.0320][M 0.0202] tīṇi dhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānāni?

199. What are the three lawful grants of the Settlement of Non-Delusion?

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ummattako hoti cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So assaramānova evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. Tassa saṅgho amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Dhammikaṃ amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ.

Here, monks, a monk is insane, his mind deranged. While insane and with a deranged mind, he has committed much that is unbefitting a monk, both in speech and in deed. The Saṅgha, or a number of monks, or a single individual charges him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ Not remembering, he says: ‘Friends, I do not remember having committed such an offense.’ The Saṅgha grants him the Settlement of Non-Delusion. This is a lawful granting of the Settlement of Non-Delusion.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ummattako hoti cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti[P 2.0083]? So assaramānova evaṃ vadeti – ‘sarāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, yathā supinantenā’ti. Tassa saṅgho amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Dhammikaṃ amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, a monk here is insane, his mind deranged. While insane and with a deranged mind, he has committed much that is unbefitting a monk, both in speech and in deed. The Saṅgha, or a number of monks, or a single individual charges him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ Not remembering, he says: ‘Friends, I remember it as if in a dream.’ The Saṅgha grants him the Settlement of Non-Delusion. This is a lawful granting of the Settlement of Non-Delusion.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ummattako hoti cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti? So ummattako ummattakālayaṃ karoti – ‘ahampi evaṃ [T 1.0321] karomi. Tumhepi evaṃ karotha. Mayhampi etaṃ kappati. Tumhākampetaṃ kappatī’ti. Tassa saṅgho amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Dhammikaṃ amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ. “Imāni tīṇi dhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānānī”ti.

Furthermore, monks, a monk here is insane, his mind deranged. While insane and with a deranged mind, he has committed much that is unbefitting a monk, both in speech and in deed. The Saṅgha, or a number of monks, or a single individual charges him: ‘Venerable one, remember having committed such an offense.’ Being insane, he acts like an insane person, saying: ‘I too will do this. You too should do this. This is allowable for me, and this is allowable for you.’ The Saṅgha grants him the Settlement of Non-Delusion. This is a lawful granting of the Settlement of Non-Delusion. These are the three lawful grants of the Settlement of Non-Delusion.

4. Paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ

4. The Procedure of Acknowledgment

200. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appaṭiññāya bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karonti [V 0.0187] – tajjanīyampi, niyassampi, pabbājanīyampi, paṭisāraṇīyampi, ukkhepanīyampi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appaṭiññāya bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karissanti – tajjanīyampi, niyassampi, pabbājanīyampi, paṭisāraṇīyampi, ukkhepanīyampī”ti! Atha kho [M 0.0203] te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, appaṭiññāya bhikkhūnaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – tajjanīyaṃ vā, niyassaṃ vā, pabbājanīyaṃ vā, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā, ukkhepanīyaṃ vā. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

200. At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six carried out formal acts on bhikkhus without their acknowledgment—an act of censure, an act of subjection, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, and an act of suspension. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... complained, murmured, and criticized: ‘How indeed can the bhikkhus of the group of six carry out formal acts on bhikkhus without their acknowledgment—an act of censure, an act of subjection, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, and an act of suspension?’ Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One... ‘Bhikkhus, is it true, as has been heard...?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’... Having rebuked them... having given a talk on the Dhamma, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Bhikkhus, a formal act should not be carried out on bhikkhus without their acknowledgment—whether it be an act of censure, an act of subjection, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension. Whoever does so, incurs an offense of wrong conduct.’

201. “Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, adhammikaṃ hoti paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ, evaṃ dhammikaṃ. Kathañca, bhikkhave, adhammikaṃ hoti paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ?

201. Thus, bhikkhus, the making of an acknowledgment is unlawful, and thus it is lawful. And how, bhikkhus, is the making of an acknowledgment unlawful?

“Bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘pārājikaṃ āyasmā ajjhāpanno’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno[T 1.0322], saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Taṃ saṅgho saṅghādisesena kāreti. Adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ.

A bhikkhu has incurred a pārājika offense. The Saṅgha, or many bhikkhus, or a single person accuses him: ‘Venerable one, you have incurred a pārājika offense.’ He says thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I have not incurred a pārājika offense; I have incurred a saṅghādisesa offense.’ The Saṅgha deals with him for a saṅghādisesa offense. This is an unlawful making of an acknowledgment.

“Bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘pārājikaṃ āyasmā ajjhāpanno’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno, thullaccayaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ…pe… pāṭidesanīyaṃ…pe… dukkaṭaṃ…pe… [T 1.0323] dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Taṃ saṅgho dubbhāsitena kāreti. Adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ.

A bhikkhu has incurred a pārājika offense. The Saṅgha, or many bhikkhus, or a single person accuses him: ‘Venerable one, you have incurred a pārājika offense.’ He says thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I have not incurred a pārājika offense; I have incurred a thullaccaya offense... a pācittiya offense... a pāṭidesanīya offense... a dukkaṭa offense... a dubbhāsita offense.’ The Saṅgha deals with him for a dubbhāsita offense. This is an unlawful making of an acknowledgment.

“Bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ…pe… thullaccayaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ…pe… pāṭidesanīyaṃ…pe… dukkaṭaṃ…pe… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘dubbhāsitaṃ āyasmā ajjhāpanno’ti[P 2.0084]? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Taṃ saṅgho pārājikena kāreti. Adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ.

A bhikkhu has incurred a saṅghādisesa offense... a thullaccaya offense... a pācittiya offense... a pāṭidesanīya offense... a dukkaṭa offense... a dubbhāsita offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of bhikkhus, or an individual bhikkhu accuses him, saying: ‘Venerable sir, you have incurred a dubbhāsita offense.’ He speaks thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I have not incurred a dubbhāsita offense; I have incurred a pārājika offense.’ The Saṅgha deals with him for a pārājika offense. This is an unlawful making of an acknowledgment.

“Bhikkhu dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo [V 0.0188] vā – ‘dubbhāsitaṃ āyasmā ajjhāpanno’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno, saṅghādisesaṃ…pe… thullaccayaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ…pe… pāṭidesanīyaṃ…pe… dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Taṃ saṅgho dukkaṭena kāreti. Adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. “Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, adhammikaṃ hoti paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ.

A bhikkhu has incurred a dubbhāsita offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of bhikkhus, or an individual bhikkhu accuses him, saying: ‘Venerable sir, you have incurred a dubbhāsita offense.’ He speaks thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I have not incurred a dubbhāsita offense; I have incurred a saṅghādisesa offense... a thullaccaya offense... a pācittiya offense... a pāṭidesanīya offense... a dukkaṭa offense.’ The Saṅgha deals with him for a dukkaṭa offense. This is an unlawful making of an acknowledgment. Thus, bhikkhus, the making of an acknowledgment is unlawful.

“Kathañca[M 0.0204], bhikkhave, dhammikaṃ hoti paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ? Bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘pārājikaṃ āyasmā ajjhāpanno’ti? So [T 1.0324] evaṃ vadeti – ‘āma, āvuso, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Taṃ saṅgho pārājikena kāreti. Dhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ.

And how, bhikkhus, is the making of an acknowledgment lawful? A bhikkhu has incurred a pārājika offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of bhikkhus, or an individual bhikkhu accuses him, saying: ‘Venerable sir, you have incurred a pārājika offense.’ He speaks thus: ‘Yes, friends, I have incurred a pārājika offense.’ The Saṅgha deals with him for a pārājika offense. This is a lawful making of an acknowledgment.

“Bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ…pe… thullaccayaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ…pe… pāṭidesanīyaṃ…pe… dukkaṭaṃ…pe… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Tamenaṃ codeti saṅgho vā, sambahulā vā, ekapuggalo vā – ‘dubbhāsitaṃ āyasmā ajjhāpanno’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘āma, āvuso, dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Taṃ saṅgho dubbhāsitena kāreti. Dhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dhammikaṃ hoti paṭiññātakaraṇa”nti.

A bhikkhu has incurred a saṅghādisesa offense... a thullaccaya offense... a pācittiya offense... a pāṭidesanīya offense... a dukkaṭa offense... a dubbhāsita offense. The Saṅgha, or a number of bhikkhus, or an individual bhikkhu accuses him, saying: ‘Venerable sir, you have incurred a dubbhāsita offense.’ He speaks thus: ‘Yes, friends, I have incurred a dubbhāsita offense.’ The Saṅgha deals with him for a dubbhāsita offense. This is a lawful making of an acknowledgment. Thus, bhikkhus, the making of an acknowledgment is lawful.

5. Yebhuyyasikā

5. By Majority

202. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti, na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ yebhuyyasikāya vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu salākaggāhāpako sammannitabbo – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, gahitāgahituñca jāneyya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

202. Now at that time, bhikkhus in the midst of the Saṅgha were quarreling, disputing, and arguing, wounding each other with verbal spears. They were unable to settle that legal issue. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Bhikkhus, I allow such a legal issue to be settled by a majority vote. A bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should be appointed as a taker of voting tickets: he should not follow a wrong course through desire, not follow a wrong course through hatred, not follow a wrong course through delusion, and not follow a wrong course through fear, and he should know what has been taken and what has not been taken. And, bhikkhus, he should be appointed in this way. First, a bhikkhu should be requested. Having been requested, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

203. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ salākaggāhāpakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā [T 1.0325] ñatti.

203. 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhu named so-and-so as the taker of voting tickets. This is the motion.'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ salākaggāhāpakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato [V 0.0189] khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno salākaggāhāpakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhu named so-and-so as the taker of voting tickets. If the appointment of the bhikkhu named so-and-so as the taker of voting tickets is agreeable to any venerable one, he should remain silent. He to whom it is not agreeable should speak.'

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu salākaggāhāpako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

'The bhikkhu named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as the taker of voting tickets. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.'

204. “Dasayime[P 2.0085][M 0.0205], bhikkhave, adhammikā salākaggāhā, dasa dhammikā dasa dhammikā salākaggāhā (ka.). Katame dasa adhammikā salākaggāhā? Oramattakañca adhikaraṇaṃ hoti, na ca gatigataṃ hoti, na ca saritasāritaṃ hoti, jānāti adhammavādī bahutarāti, appeva nāma adhammavādī bahutarā assūti, jānāti saṅgho bhijjissatīti, appeva nāma saṅgho bhijjeyyāti, adhammena gaṇhanti, vaggā gaṇhanti, na ca yathādiṭṭhiyā gaṇhanti – ime dasa adhammikā salākaggāhā.

204. “Monks, there are these ten unrighteous takings of voting tickets, and ten righteous ones. What are the ten unrighteous takings of voting tickets? The legal issue is minor; it has not been thoroughly investigated; it has not been thoroughly reviewed; one knows that the speakers of non-Dhamma are in the majority; one knows, ‘Perhaps the speakers of non-Dhamma will be in the majority;’ one knows that the Saṅgha will split; one knows, ‘Perhaps the Saṅgha will split;’ they take the tickets unrighteously; they take them as a faction; and they do not take them in accordance with their own view—these are the ten unrighteous takings of voting tickets.”

“Katame dasa dhammikā salākaggāhā? Na ca oramattakaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti, gatigatañca hoti, saritasāritañca hoti, jānāti dhammavādī bahutarāti, appeva nāma dhammavādī bahutarā assūti, jānāti saṅgho na bhijjissatīti, appeva nāma saṅgho na bhijjeyyāti, dhammena gaṇhanti, samaggā gaṇhanti, yathādiṭṭhiyā ca gaṇhanti – ime dasa dhammikā salākaggāhā”ti.

“What are the ten righteous takings of voting tickets? The legal issue is not a minor matter; it has been thoroughly investigated; it has been thoroughly reviewed; one knows that those who speak according to the Dhamma are in the majority; one knows, ‘It may be that those who speak according to the Dhamma will be in the majority;’ one knows that the Saṅgha will not be split; one knows, ‘It may be that the Saṅgha will not be split;’ they take the voting tickets in accordance with the Dhamma; they take them in unity; and they take them in accordance with their view—these are the ten righteous takings of voting tickets.”

6. Tassapāpiyasikā

6. The Procedure for Corruptness

205. Tena kho pana samayena upavāḷo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā [T 1.0326] anuyuñjiyamāno avajānitvā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā avajānāti, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, sampajānamusā bhāsati. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma upavāḷo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjiyamāno avajānitvā paṭijānissati, paṭijānitvā avajānissati, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissati, sampajānamusā bhāsissatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho upavāḷassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ karotu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ [V 0.0190] upavāḷo bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo, āpattiṃ āropetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

205. Now at that time, the monk Upavāḷa, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha about an offense, having denied it, confesses; having confessed, he denies; he evades the issue, and he knowingly speaks falsely. Those monks who were of few wishes… and so on… criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying: “How can the monk Upavāḷa, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha about an offense, having denied it, confess; having confessed, deny; evade the issue, and knowingly speak falsely?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… and so on… “Is it true, monks…?”… and so on… “It is true, Blessed One.”… and so on… Having rebuked him… and so on… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “In that case, monks, let the Saṅgha carry out the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure against the monk Upavāḷa. And it should be done in this way, monks. First, the monk Upavāḷa should be accused; having been accused, he should be reminded; having been reminded, he should be charged with the offense. Having charged him with the offense, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

206. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ upavāḷo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjiyamāno avajānitvā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā avajānāti, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, sampajānamusā ‘bhāsati. Yadi [M 0.0206] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho upavāḷassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya. Esā ñatti.

206. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Upavāḷa, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha about an offense, having denied it, confesses; having confessed, he denies; he evades the issue, and he knowingly speaks falsely. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should carry out the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure against the monk Upavāḷa. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ upavāḷo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjiyamāno avajānitvā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā [T 1.0327] avajānāti, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, sampajānamusā bhāsati. Saṅgho upavāḷassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati upavāḷassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammassa karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk Upavāḷa, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha about an offense, having denied it, confesses; having confessed, he denies; he evades the issue, and he knowingly speaks falsely. The Saṅgha carries out the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure against the monk Upavāḷa. To whichever venerable one the carrying out of the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure against the monk Upavāḷa is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I state this matter… and so on… For a third time I state this matter… and so on…”

“Kataṃ saṅghena upavāḷassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The Tassapāpiyasikā procedure has been carried out by the Saṅgha against the monk Upavāḷa. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.”

207. “Pañcimāni[P 2.0086], bhikkhave, dhammikāni tassapāpiyasikākammassa karaṇāni. Asuci ca hoti, alajjī ca, sānuvādo ca, tassa saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ karoti dhammena, samaggena – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammikāni tassapāpiyasikākammassa karaṇāni.

207. “Monks, there are these five lawful grounds for carrying out the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure. He is impure, shameless, and subject to accusation; for him, the Saṅgha carries out the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure lawfully and in concord. Indeed, monks, these are the five lawful grounds for carrying out the Tassapāpiyasikā procedure.”

Adhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Chapter of Twelve on Unlawful Procedures

208. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca. Asammukhā kataṃ hoti, appaṭipucchākataṃ hoti, appaṭiññāya kataṃ hoti…pe… adhammena kataṃ hoti, vaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti, avinayakammañca, duvūpasantañca.

208. “Monks, a Tassapāpiyasikā procedure endowed with three factors is an unlawful procedure, a non-disciplinary procedure, and is improperly settled. It is carried out in the absence of the monk, it is carried out without questioning him, and it is carried out without his admission… and so on… It is carried out unlawfully, and it is carried out by a faction. Indeed, monks, endowed with these three factors, a Tassapāpiyasikā procedure is an unlawful procedure, a non-disciplinary procedure, and is improperly settled.”

Dhammakammadvādasakaṃ

The Chapter of Twelve on Lawful Procedures

209. “Tīhi[V 0.0191], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca. Sammukhā kataṃ hoti, paṭipucchākataṃ hoti, paṭiññāya kataṃ hoti…pe… [T 1.0328] dhammena kataṃ hoti, samaggena kataṃ hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgataṃ tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ dhammakammañca hoti, vinayakammañca, suvūpasantañca.

209. “Monks, a Tassapāpiyasikā procedure endowed with three factors is a lawful procedure, a disciplinary procedure, and is well-settled. It is carried out in his presence, after questioning him, and with his admission… and so on… It is carried out lawfully, and it is carried out by a united Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, endowed with these three factors, a Tassapāpiyasikā procedure is a lawful procedure, a disciplinary procedure, and is well-settled.”

Ākaṅkhamānachakkaṃ

The Chapter of Six on Optional Procedures

210. “Tīhi[M 0.0207], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya. Bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya.

210. “Monks, the Saṅgha, if it so wishes, may carry out a Tassapāpiyasikā procedure against a monk endowed with three factors. He is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, commits many offenses, and his offenses are boundless; he lives associating with householders through unsuitable connections with them. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it so wishes, may carry out a Tassapāpiyasikā procedure against a monk endowed with these three factors.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno [T 1.0329] saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out a tassapāpiyasikākamma on a bhikkhu possessed of three other factors. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in higher conduct, and corrupt in higher view. Indeed, monks, by these factors... and so on.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave…pe… buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya.

Furthermore, monks... and so on... he speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out a tassapāpiyasikākamma on a bhikkhu possessed of these three factors.

“Tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya. Eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako; eko bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno; eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya.

Monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out the tassapāpiyasikākamma for three monks. One is quarrelsome... and so on... and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha; one is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and is without limit to his offenses; one dwells associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders. Indeed, monks, for these three monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out the tassapāpiyasikākamma.

“Aparesampi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya. Eko adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, eko ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, eko atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Furthermore, monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out the tassapāpiyasikākamma for another three monks. One is corrupt in higher virtue; one is corrupt in higher conduct; one is corrupt in higher view. Indeed, monks, for these three monks... and so on.

“Aparesampi[V 0.0192], bhikkhave…pe… eko buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, eko saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ [T 1.0330] kareyya.

Furthermore, monks... and so on... one speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, one speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, one speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha. Indeed, monks, for these three monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out the tassapāpiyasikākamma.

Aṭṭhārasavattaṃ

The Eighteen Duties

211. “Tassapāpiyasikākammakatena[M 0.0208], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

211. Monks, a monk on whom a tassapāpiyasikākamma has been carried out should conduct himself properly. Herein is the proper conduct:

Na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā…pe… na bhikkhūhi sampayojetabba”nti. Atha kho saṅgho upavāḷassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ akāsi.

He should not give higher ordination; he should not give dependence; he should not have a novice attend on him; he should not accept the authorization to instruct nuns; even if authorized, he should not instruct nuns... and so on... he should not be associated with monks. Then, indeed, the Saṅgha carried out the tassapāpiyasikākamma for the monk Upavāḷa.

7. Tiṇavatthārakaṃ

7. The Covering with Grass

212. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “amhākaṃ kho bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya kakkhaḷatāya vāḷatāya (syā. kaṃ.) bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Kathaṃ nu kho [P 2.0087] amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

212. Now at that time, for monks who were dwelling quarrelsome, contentious, and fallen into disputes, much that was unbecoming of a recluse—spoken and transgressed by body—had been habitually practiced. Then this thought occurred to those monks: 'Indeed, for us who are dwelling quarrelsome, contentious, and fallen into disputes, much that is unbecoming of a recluse—spoken and transgressed by body—has been habitually practiced. If we were to make one another answer for these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would lead to harshness, fierceness, and schism. How then should we proceed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ[T 1.0331]. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ tatra ce bhikkhave bhikkhūnaṃ (syā.) evaṃ hoti – ‘amhākaṃ kho bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ; sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyyā’ti, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tiṇavatthārakena vūpasametuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, vūpasametabbaṃ. Sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbaṃ, sannipatitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Here, monks, for monks who are dwelling quarrelsome, contentious, and fallen into disputes, much that is unbecoming of a recluse—spoken and transgressed by body—is habitually practiced. If, in that case, this thought occurs to the monks: ‘Indeed, for us who are dwelling quarrelsome, contentious, and fallen into disputes, much that is unbecoming of a recluse—spoken and transgressed by body—has been habitually practiced; if we were to make one another answer for these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would lead to harshness, fierceness, and schism,’ I allow, monks, such a legal issue to be settled by the procedure of covering with grass. And it should be settled in this way, monks. All should assemble together in one place. Having assembled, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0193] me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ [M 0.0209] adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tiṇavatthārakena vūpasameyya, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyutta”nti. “Ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena sako pakkho ñāpetabbo –

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. While we were living quarrelsome, contentious, and in dispute, much conduct unbecoming of a recluse, both spoken and physically committed, has been transgressed. If we were to deal with one another regarding these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would lead to harshness, fierceness, and schism. If the Saṅgha deems it the proper time, the Saṅgha should settle this legal issue by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside grave offenses and setting aside offenses connected with householders.” A competent and capable monk of one faction should inform his own faction:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya [T 1.0332] vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, āyasmantānañceva atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyutta”nti.

“Venerable sirs, may you hear me. While we were living quarrelsome, contentious, and in dispute, much conduct unbecoming of a recluse, both spoken and physically committed, has been transgressed. If we were to deal with one another regarding these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would lead to harshness, fierceness, and schism. If the venerable sirs deem it the proper time, I would confess—for the benefit of the venerable sirs and for my own benefit—whatever offense there is of the venerable sirs and whatever offense there is of my own, in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside grave offenses and setting aside offenses connected with householders.”

“Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena sako pakkho ñāpetabbo –

Then, a competent and capable monk of the other faction should inform his own faction:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, āyasmantānañceva atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyutta”nti.

May the venerable ones hear me. While we were living, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is unbecoming of a monk has been transgressed, both spoken and acted upon. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it is possible that this legal issue might lead to harshness, roughness, and schism. If the time is right for the venerable ones, I would confess—for the benefit of the venerable ones and for my own benefit—both the offenses of the venerable ones and my own offenses in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders.

213. “Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

213. Then, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk from the other faction:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadi [V 0.0194] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva [T 1.0333] imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya, attano ca [M 0.0210] atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. While we were living, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is unbecoming of a monk has been transgressed, both spoken and acted upon. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it is possible that this legal issue might lead to harshness, roughness, and schism. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would confess—for the benefit of these venerable ones and for my own benefit—both the offenses of these venerable ones and my own offenses in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena desemi, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati amhākaṃ imāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena desanā, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. While we were living, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is unbecoming of a monk has been transgressed, both spoken and acted upon. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it is possible that this legal issue might lead to harshness, roughness, and schism. For the benefit of these venerable ones and for my own benefit, I confess in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass both the offenses of these venerable ones and my own offenses, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders. To whichever venerable one the confession of these our offenses in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass—setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders—is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Desitā amhākaṃ imā āpattiyo saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā [P 2.0088] gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

These our offenses have been confessed in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold it.

214. “Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

214. Then, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk from the other faction:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ [T 1.0334] kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. While we were living, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is unbecoming of a monk has been transgressed, both spoken and acted upon. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it is possible that this legal issue might lead to harshness, roughness, and schism. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would confess—for the benefit of these venerable ones and for my own benefit—both the offenses of these venerable ones and my own offenses in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ [M 0.0211][V 0.0195] atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena desemi, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati amhākaṃ imāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena desanā, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. While we were living, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is unbecoming of a monk has been transgressed, both spoken and acted upon. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it is possible that this legal issue might lead to harshness, roughness, and schism. For the benefit of these venerable ones and for my own benefit, I confess in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass both the offenses of these venerable ones and my own offenses, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders. To whichever venerable one the confession of these our offenses in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass—setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders—is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Desitā amhākaṃ imā āpattiyo saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

These our offenses have been confessed in the midst of the Saṅgha by the procedure of covering with grass, setting aside a grave offense and setting aside an offense connected with householders. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold it.

“Evañca pana, bhikkhave, te bhikkhū tāhi āpattīhi vuṭṭhitā honti, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, ṭhapetvā diṭṭhāvikammaṃ[T 1.0335], ṭhapetvā ye na tattha hontī”ti.

And thus, monks, those monks are cleared of those offenses, setting aside a grave offense, setting aside an offense connected with householders, setting aside the act of making a wrong view known, and setting aside those who are not present there.

8. Adhikaraṇaṃ

8. Legal Issue

215. Tena kho pana samayena (bhikkhūpi bhikkhūhi vivadanti,) ( ) natthi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) bhikkhūpi bhikkhunīhi vivadanti, bhikkhuniyopi bhikkhūhi vivadanti, channopi bhikkhu bhikkhunīnaṃ anupakhajja bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vivadati, bhikkhunīnaṃ pakkhaṃ gāheti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma channo bhikkhu bhikkhunīnaṃ anupakhajja bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vivadissati, bhikkhunīnaṃ pakkhaṃ gāhessatīti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

215. Now at that time, monks disputed with monks, monks disputed with nuns, and nuns disputed with monks. The monk Channa, intruding among the nuns, disputed with the monks, taking the nuns’ side. Those monks who were of few wishes…pe… complained and criticized him: “How can the monk Channa, intruding among the nuns, dispute with the monks, taking the nuns’ side?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One…pe… “Is it true, monks…pe…?” “It is true, Blessed One.” …pe… Having rebuked him…pe… the Blessed One gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks:

pari. 275 “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇāni – vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kiccādhikaraṇañca (ka.).

“Monks, there are these four legal questions: a legal question concerning disputes, a legal question concerning accusations, a legal question concerning offenses, and a legal question concerning procedures.

“Tattha katamaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ pari. 314? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ (ka.) vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā, vinayoti vā avinayoti vā, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā appaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āpattīti vā anāpattīti vā[M 0.0212], lahukā āpattīti vā garukā āpattīti vā, sāvasesā āpattīti vā anavasesā āpattīti vā, duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā? Yaṃ tattha [T 1.0336] bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho [V 0.0196] vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhagaṃ – idaṃ vuccati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ.

“Among these, what is a legal question concerning disputes? Here, monks, monks dispute: ‘This is the Dhamma’ or ‘This is not the Dhamma;’ ‘This is the Vinaya’ or ‘This is not the Vinaya;’ ‘This was spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata’ or ‘This was not spoken and not uttered by the Tathāgata;’ ‘This was practiced by the Tathāgata’ or ‘This was not practiced by the Tathāgata;’ ‘This was laid down by the Tathāgata’ or ‘This was not laid down by the Tathāgata;’ ‘This is an offense’ or ‘This is not an offense;’ ‘This is a light offense’ or ‘This is a grave offense;’ ‘This is an offense with a remainder’ or ‘This is an offense without a remainder;’ ‘This is a gross offense’ or ‘This is not a gross offense.’ Whatever wrangling, quarreling, contention, disputation, difference of opinion, misstatement, vexatious speech, or strife arises in this matter—this is called a legal question concerning disputes.

“Tattha katamaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ? pari. 315 Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ anuvadanti sīlavipattiyā vā ācāravipattiyā vā diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ.

“Among these, what is a legal question concerning accusation? Here, monks, monks accuse a monk of corruption of virtue, or corruption of conduct, or corruption of view, or corruption of livelihood. Whatever therein is an accusation, a charge, a statement, a report, a persistent assertion, an insistence, or the giving of support—this is called a legal question concerning accusation.

“Tattha katamaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ? Pañcapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, sattapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ[P 2.0089].

“Among these, what is a legal question concerning offenses? The five aggregates of offenses are a legal question concerning offenses; the seven aggregates of offenses are a legal question concerning offenses. This is called a legal question concerning offenses.

“Tattha katamaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ? pari. 317 Yā saṅghassa kiccayatā, karaṇīyatā, apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

“Among these, what is a legal question concerning duties? Whatever is a duty for the Sangha, an obligation, an act of declaration, a motion-only act, a motion-and-one-announcement act, or a motion-and-three-announcements act—this is called a legal question concerning duties.

216. “Vivādādhikaraṇassa kiṃ mūlaṃ? Cha vivādamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ. Tīṇipi akusalamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ, tīṇipi kusalamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ. pari. 272; a. ni. 2.35-36; ma. ni. 3.44 Katamāni cha vivādamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso[T 1.0337], saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi…pe… saṅghepi…pe… sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe vivādaṃ janeti. Yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa [M 0.0213] āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti.

216. “What is the root of a legal question concerning disputes? Six roots of disputes are the root of a legal question concerning disputes. The three unwholesome roots are the root of a legal question concerning disputes, and the three wholesome roots are the root of a legal question concerning disputes. What are the six roots of disputes that are the root of a legal question concerning disputes? Here, monks, a monk is angry and bears grudges.
