A monk who is angry and bears grudges dwells disrespectfully and irreverently toward the Teacher, disrespectfully and irreverently toward the Dhamma, disrespectfully and irreverently toward the Sangha, and does not fulfill the training. A monk who dwells disrespectfully and irreverently toward the Teacher, disrespectfully and irreverently toward the Dhamma, disrespectfully and irreverently toward the Sangha, and does not fulfill the training, gives rise to disputes in the Sangha. That dispute is for the harm and unhappiness of many people, for the disadvantage, harm, and suffering of gods and humans. If, monks, you see such a root of dispute either internally or externally, you should strive for the abandoning of that evil root of dispute. If, monks, you do not see such a root of dispute either internally or externally, you should practice for the non-arising of that evil root of dispute in the future. Thus there is the abandoning of this evil root of dispute. Thus there is the non-arising of this evil root of dispute in the future.”

pari.272 “Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti paḷāsī…pe… issukī hoti maccharī[V 0.0197], saṭho hoti māyāvī, pāpiccho hoti micchādiṭṭhī, sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī [T 1.0338] duppaṭinissaggī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi…pe… saṅghepi…pe… sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe vivādaṃ janeti. Yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti. Imāni cha vivādamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is denigrating and domineering… he is envious and stingy, deceitful and scheming, has evil desires and wrong views, and is one who clings to his own views, stubbornly adhering to them and unwilling to relinquish them. A bhikkhu who clings to his own views, stubbornly adhering to them and unwilling to relinquish them, dwells without reverence and deference for the Teacher, without reverence and deference for the Dhamma, without reverence and deference for the Saṅgha, and does not fulfill the training. A bhikkhu who dwells without reverence and deference for the Teacher, without reverence and deference for the Dhamma… for the Saṅgha… and does not fulfill the training, generates a dispute in the Saṅgha. Such a dispute is for the harm of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the detriment of many people, and for the harm and suffering of gods and humans. If, bhikkhus, you should perceive such a root of dispute within yourselves or externally, you should strive to abandon that evil root of dispute. If, bhikkhus, you should not perceive such a root of dispute within yourselves or externally, you should practice for the non-occurrence of that evil root of dispute in the future. Thus there is the abandoning of this evil root of dispute. Thus there is the non-occurrence of this evil root of dispute in the future. These six roots of dispute are the roots of a legal issue concerning disputes.”

“Katamāni tīṇi akusalamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū luddhacittā vivadanti, duṭṭhacittā vivadanti, mūḷhacittā vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā, vinayoti vā avinayoti vā, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti [T 1.0339] vā, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā appaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āpattīti vā anāpattīti vā, lahukā āpattīti vā garukā āpattīti vā, sāvasesā āpattīti vā anavasesā āpattīti vā, duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Imāni tīṇi akusalamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

“What are the three unwholesome roots that are the root of a legal issue concerning disputes? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute with greedy minds, with hateful minds, and with deluded minds, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma,’ or ‘This is not the Dhamma’; ‘This is the Vinaya,’ or ‘This is not the Vinaya’; ‘This was spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata,’ or ‘This was not spoken and not uttered by the Tathāgata’; ‘This was practiced by the Tathāgata,’ or ‘This was not practiced by the Tathāgata’; ‘This was laid down by the Tathāgata,’ or ‘This was not laid down by the Tathāgata’; ‘This is an offense,’ or ‘This is not an offense’; ‘This is a light offense,’ or ‘This is a grave offense’; ‘This is an offense with a remainder,’ or ‘This is an offense without a remainder’; ‘This is a gross offense,’ or ‘This is not a gross offense.’ These three unwholesome roots are the root of a legal issue concerning disputes.”

“Katamāni [M 0.0214] tīṇi kusalamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aluddhacittā vivadanti, aduṭṭhacittā vivadanti, amūḷhacittā vivadanti [P 2.0090] – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā…pe… duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Imāni tīṇi kusalamūlāni vivādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

“What are the three wholesome roots that are the root of a legal issue concerning disputes? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute with minds free from greed, free from hatred, and free from delusion, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma,’ or ‘This is not the Dhamma’… ‘This is a gross offense,’ or ‘This is not a gross offense.’ These three wholesome roots are the root of a legal issue concerning disputes.”

217. pari. 272 “Anuvādādhikaraṇassa kiṃ mūlaṃ? Cha anuvādamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ. Tīṇipi akusalamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ, tīṇipi kusalamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa [V 0.0198] mūlaṃ, kāyopi anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ, vācāpi anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ. “Katamāni cha anuvādamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati [T 1.0340] appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi…pe… saṅghepi…pe… sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe anuvādaṃ janeti. Yo hoti anuvādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, anuvādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, anuvādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha. Evametassa pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti.

217. “What is the root of an accusation-issue? Six roots of accusation are the root of an accusation-issue. The three unwholesome roots are also the root of an accusation-issue, the three wholesome roots are also the root of an accusation-issue, the body is also the root of an accusation-issue, and speech is also the root of an accusation-issue. What are the six roots of accusation that are the root of an accusation-issue? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is irascible and resentful. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who is irascible and resentful, dwells disrespectful and unsubmissive towards the Teacher, dwells disrespectful and unsubmissive towards the Dhamma, dwells disrespectful and unsubmissive towards the Saṅgha, and does not fulfill the training completely. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who dwells disrespectful and unsubmissive towards the Teacher, towards the Dhamma, towards the Saṅgha, and does not fulfill the training completely, gives rise to an accusation in the Saṅgha. That accusation is for the harm of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the disadvantage of many people, and for the harm and suffering of devas and humans. If, bhikkhus, you perceive such a root of accusation internally or externally, you should strive for the abandoning of that evil root of accusation. If, bhikkhus, you do not perceive such a root of accusation internally or externally, you should practice for the non-arising in the future of that evil root of accusation. Thus there is the abandoning of this evil root of accusation. Thus there is the non-arising in the future of this evil root of accusation.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti paḷāsī…pe… issukī hoti maccharī, saṭho hoti māyāvī, pāpiccho hoti micchādiṭṭhī, sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattharipi agāravo [T 1.0341] viharati appatisso[M 0.0215], dhammepi…pe… saṅghepi…pe… sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe anuvādaṃ janeti. Yo hoti anuvādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, anuvādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha. Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, anuvādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa āyattiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha. Evametassa pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa anuvādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti. Imāni cha anuvādamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is denigrating and spiteful… He is envious and stingy, fraudulent and deceitful, has evil wishes and wrong view, is attached to his own views, obstinate, and difficult to relinquish them. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who is attached to his own views, obstinate, and difficult to relinquish them, dwells disrespectful and undeferential towards the Teacher, dwells disrespectful and undeferential towards the Dhamma, dwells disrespectful and undeferential towards the Saṅgha, and does not fulfill the training. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who dwells disrespectful and undeferential towards the Teacher, towards the Dhamma, towards the Saṅgha, and does not fulfill the training, gives rise to an accusation in the Saṅgha. That accusation is for the detriment of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the disadvantage of many people, and for the detriment and suffering of devas and humans. If, bhikkhus, you perceive such a root of accusation internally or externally, you should strive for the abandoning of that evil root of accusation. If, bhikkhus, you do not perceive such a root of accusation internally or externally, you should practice for the non-arising in the future of that evil root of accusation. Thus there is the abandoning of that evil root of accusation. Thus there is the non-arising in the future of that evil root of accusation. These six roots of accusation are the root of an accusation-issue.

“Katamāni [V 0.0199] tīṇi akusalamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ luddhacittā anuvadanti, duṭṭhacittā anuvadanti, mūḷhacittā anuvadanti – sīlavipattiyā vā, ācāravipattiyā vā, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā, ājīvavipattiyā vā. Imāni tīṇi akusalamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

What are the three unwholesome roots that are the root of an accusation-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus accuse a bhikkhu with a greedy mind; they accuse him with a hateful mind; they accuse him with a deluded mind—on account of a lapse in virtue, or a lapse in conduct, or a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. These three unwholesome roots are the root of an accusation-issue.

“Katamāni tīṇi kusalamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ aluddhacittā anuvadanti, aduṭṭhacittā anuvadanti, amūḷhacittā anuvadanti – sīlavipattiyā vā, ācaravipattiyā [T 1.0342] vā, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā, ājīvavipattiyā vā. Imāni tīṇi kusalamūlāni anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

What are the three wholesome roots that are the root of an accusation-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus accuse a bhikkhu with minds free from greed, with minds free from hatred, with minds free from delusion—on account of a lapse in virtue, or a lapse in conduct, or a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. These three wholesome roots are the root of an accusation-issue.

“Katamo kāyo katamo ca kāyo (syā. kaṃ.) anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idhekacco dubbaṇṇo hoti, duddassiko, okoṭimako, bahvābādho, kāṇo vā, kuṇī vā, khañjo vā, pakkhahato vā, yena naṃ anuvadanti. Ayaṃ kāyo anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

What is the body that is the root of an accusation-issue? Here, someone is ill-favored, unsightly, dwarfish, or very sickly; or they are blind, or have a crippled hand, or are lame, or are paralyzed on one side, on account of which they are accused. This body is the root of an accusation-issue.

“Katamā vācā anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ? Idhekacco dubbaco hoti, mammano, eḷagalavāco, yāya naṃ anuvadanti. Ayaṃ vācā anuvādādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

What is the speech that is the root of an accusation-issue? Here, someone is difficult to admonish, a stammerer, and has slurred speech, on account of which they are accused. This speech is the root of an accusation-issue.

218. “Āpattādhikaraṇassa kiṃ mūlaṃ? Cha āpattisamuṭṭhānā āpattādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ. Atthāpatti kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato, na [M 0.0216] cittato. Atthāpatti vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato, na cittato. Atthāpatti kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato. Atthāpatti kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Atthāpatti vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato. Atthāpatti kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti. Ime cha āpattisamuṭṭhānā āpattādhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ.

218. What is the root of an offense-issue? The six origins of offenses are the root of an offense-issue. There is an offense that arises from the body, not from speech, not from the mind. There is an offense that arises from speech, not from the body, not from the mind. There is an offense that arises from the body and from speech, not from the mind. There is an offense that arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech. There is an offense that arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body. There is an offense that arises from the body, from speech, and from the mind. These six origins of offenses are the root of an offense-issue.

219. “Kiccādhikaraṇassa kiṃ mūlaṃ? Kiccādhikaraṇassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ – saṅgho.

219. What is the root of a procedural issue? A procedural issue has one root: the Saṅgha.

220. “Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [T 1.0343][P 2.0091] kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, abyākataṃ. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ. Tattha katamaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū kusalacittā vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā…pe… duṭṭhullā āpattīti [V 0.0200] vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhagaṃ – idaṃ vuccati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ.

220. A dispute-issue is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate. A dispute-issue may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be indeterminate. What, then, is a wholesome dispute-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute with wholesome minds, saying: ‘This is Dhamma’ or ‘This is not Dhamma’… ‘This is a grave offense’ or ‘This is not a grave offense.’ Whatever wrangling, quarreling, contention, disputation, diverse statements, contrary statements, speech for the sake of mental distress, or strife there is—this is called a wholesome dispute-issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū akusalacittā vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā…pe… duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhagaṃ – idaṃ vuccati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ.

What, then, is an unwholesome dispute-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute with unwholesome minds, saying: ‘This is Dhamma’ or ‘This is not Dhamma’… ‘This is a grave offense’ or ‘This is not a grave offense.’ Whatever wrangling, quarreling, contention, disputation, diverse statements, contrary statements, speech for the sake of mental distress, or strife there is—this is called an unwholesome dispute-issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū abyākatacittā vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā…pe… duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhagaṃ – idaṃ vuccati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ.

What, then, is an indeterminate dispute-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute with indeterminate minds, saying: ‘This is Dhamma’ or ‘This is not Dhamma’… ‘This is a grave offense’ or ‘This is not a grave offense.’ Whatever wrangling, quarreling, contention, disputation, diverse statements, contrary statements, speech for the sake of mental distress, or strife there is—this is called an indeterminate dispute-issue.

221. “Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ [T 1.0344] kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, abyākataṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ. Tattha katamaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ kusalacittā anuvadanti – sīlavipattiyā vā, ācāravipattiyā vā, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā, ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā [M 0.0217] anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ.

221. Is an accusation-issue wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate? An accusation-issue may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be indeterminate. Among these, which accusation-issue is wholesome? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus accuse a bhikkhu with wholesome minds—on account of a lapse in virtue, a lapse in conduct, a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. Whatever accusation, accusing, reproaching, denouncing, insistence, exertion, or giving support there is—this is called a wholesome accusation-issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ akusalacittā anuvadanti – sīlavipattiyā vā, ācāravipattiyā vā, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā, ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ.

Among these, which accusation-issue is unwholesome? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus accuse a bhikkhu with unwholesome minds—on account of a lapse in virtue, a lapse in conduct, a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. Whatever accusation, accusing, reproaching, denouncing, insistence, exertion, or giving support there is—this is called an unwholesome accusation-issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ abyākatacittā anuvadanti – sīlavipattiyā vā, ācāravipattiyā vā, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā, ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ.

Among these, which accusation-issue is indeterminate? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus accuse a bhikkhu with indeterminate minds—on account of a lapse in virtue, a lapse in conduct, a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. Whatever accusation, accusing, reproaching, denouncing, insistence, exertion, or giving support there is—this is called an indeterminate accusation-issue.

222. “Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ [V 0.0201] kusalaṃ idaṃ padaṃ kesuci natthi, akusalaṃ, abyākataṃ? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ; natthi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ. Tattha [T 1.0345] katamaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ? Yaṃ jānanto sañjānanto cecca abhivitaritvā vītikkamo – idaṃ vuccati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ.

222. Is an offense-issue wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate? An offense-issue may be unwholesome or may be indeterminate; there is no wholesome offense-issue. Among these two, which offense-issue is unwholesome? A transgression committed knowingly, with full awareness, intentionally, and deliberately—this is called an unwholesome offense-issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ? Yaṃ ajānanto asañjānanto acecca anabhivitaritvā vītikkamo – idaṃ vuccati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ.

Among these two, which offense-issue is indeterminate? A transgression committed unknowingly, without full awareness, unintentionally, and not deliberately—this is called an indeterminate offense-issue.

223. “Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, abyākataṃ? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ. Tattha katamaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ? Yaṃ saṅgho kusalacitto kammaṃ karoti – apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kusalaṃ.

223. Is a duty-issue wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate? A duty-issue may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be indeterminate. Among these, which duty-issue is wholesome? When the Saṅgha, with a wholesome mind, performs a formal act—an act by taking consent, an act by motion, an act with a motion and one announcement, or an act with a motion and three announcements—this is called a wholesome duty-issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ [P 2.0092] akusalaṃ? Yaṃ saṅgho akusalacitto kammaṃ karoti – apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kiccādhikaraṇaṃ akusalaṃ.

Among these, which duty-issue is unwholesome? When the Saṅgha, with an unwholesome mind, performs a formal act—an act by taking consent, an act by motion, an act with a motion and one announcement, or an act with a motion and three announcements—this is called an unwholesome duty-issue.

“Tattha [M 0.0218] katamaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ? Yaṃ saṅgho abyākatacitto kammaṃ karoti – apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kiccādhikaraṇaṃ abyākataṃ.

Among these, which duty-issue is indeterminate? When the Saṅgha, with an indeterminate mind, performs a formal act—an act by taking consent, an act by motion, an act with a motion and one announcement, or an act with a motion and three announcements—this is called an indeterminate duty-issue.

224. pari. 355 “Vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo, adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca. Siyā vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no [T 1.0346] vivādo, siyā adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca.

224. Is a dispute a dispute-issue? Is a dispute not an issue? Is an issue not a dispute? Is it both an issue and a dispute? There may be a dispute that is a dispute-issue; there may be a dispute that is not an issue; there may be an issue that is not a dispute; and there may be that which is both an issue and a dispute.

“Tattha katamo vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā…pe… duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhagaṃ – ayaṃ vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these four, which dispute is a dispute-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma,’ or ‘This is not the Dhamma;’ … ‘This is a grave offense,’ or ‘This is not a grave offense.’ Whatever quarreling, strife, contention, dispute, speaking variously, speaking otherwise, speech for the sake of vexation, or brawling there is in that context—this dispute is a dispute-issue.

“Tattha [V 0.0202] katamo vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ? Mātāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi mātarā vivadati, pitāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi pitarā vivadati, bhātāpi bhātarā vivadati, bhātāpi bhaginiyā vivadati, bhaginīpi bhātarā vivadati, sahāyopi sahāyena vivadati – ayaṃ vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these four, which dispute is not an issue? A mother disputes with her son, and a son disputes with his mother; a father disputes with his son, and a son disputes with his father; a brother disputes with a brother; a brother disputes with a sister, and a sister disputes with a brother; a friend disputes with a friend—this dispute is not an issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo.

Among these four, which issue is not a dispute? An accusation-issue, an offense-issue, and a duty-issue—these issues are not a dispute.

“Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca.

Among these four, what is both an issue and a dispute? A dispute-issue is both an issue and a dispute.

225. pari. 356 “Anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo, adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca. Siyā anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo, siyā adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca.

225. Is an accusation an accusation-issue? Is an accusation not an issue? Is an issue not an accusation? Is it both an issue and an accusation? There may be an accusation that is an accusation-issue; there may be an accusation that is not an issue; there may be an issue that is not an accusation; and there may be that which is both an issue and an accusation.

“Tattha katamo anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ anuvadanti – sīlavipattiyā vā, ācāravipattiyā vā[T 1.0347], diṭṭhivipattiyā vā, ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā [M 0.0219] anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ – ayaṃ anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which accusation is an accusation-issue? Here, bhikkhus, bhikkhus accuse a bhikkhu on account of a lapse in virtue, a lapse in conduct, a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. Whatever accusation, accusing, reproaching, denouncing, insistence, exertion, or giving support there is—this accusation is an accusation-issue.

“Tattha katamo anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ? Mātāpi puttaṃ anuvadati, puttopi mātaraṃ anuvadati, pitāpi puttaṃ anuvadati, puttopi pitaraṃ anuvadati, bhātāpi bhātaraṃ anuvadati, bhātāpi bhaginiṃ anuvadati, bhaginīpi bhātaraṃ anuvadati, sahāyopi sahāyaṃ anuvadati – ayaṃ anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which accusation is not an issue? A mother accuses her son, and a son accuses his mother; a father accuses his son, and a son accuses his father; a brother accuses his brother; a brother accuses his sister, and a sister accuses her brother; a friend accuses a friend—this accusation is not an issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo.

Among these, which legal issue is not an accusation? A legal issue concerning offenses, a legal issue concerning duties, and a legal issue concerning disputes—this legal issue is not an accusation.

“Tattha [V 0.0203] katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca.

Among these, which is both a legal issue and an accusation? A legal issue concerning an accusation is both a legal issue and an accusation.

226. pari. 357 “Āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti, adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca. Siyā āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti, siyā adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca. “Tattha katamaṃ [P 2.0093] āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ? Pañcapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, sattapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ – ayaṃ āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

226. Is an offense a legal issue concerning an offense? Is an offense not a legal issue? Is a legal issue not an offense? Is it both a legal issue and an offense? In some cases, an offense is a legal issue concerning an offense. In some cases, an offense is not a legal issue. In some cases, a legal issue is not an offense. In some cases, it is both a legal issue and an offense. Among these, which offense is a legal issue concerning an offense? The five groups of offenses are a legal issue concerning an offense, and the seven groups of offenses are a legal issue concerning an offense—this offense is a legal issue concerning an offense.

“Tattha katamaṃ āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ? Sotāpatti samāpatti – ayaṃ āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ[T 1.0348].

Among these, which offense is not a legal issue? The attainment of stream-entry—this attainment is not a legal issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti.

Among these, which legal issue is not an offense? A legal issue concerning duties, a legal issue concerning disputes, and a legal issue concerning accusations—this legal issue is not an offense.

“Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca.

Among these, which is both a legal issue and an offense? A legal issue concerning an offense is both a legal issue and an offense.

227. pari. 358 “Kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ, adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca. Siyā kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca.

227. Is a duty a legal issue concerning duties? Is a duty not a legal issue? Is a legal issue not a duty? Is it both a legal issue and a duty? In some cases, a duty is a legal issue concerning duties; in some cases, a duty is not a legal issue; in some cases, a legal issue is not a duty; in some cases, it is both a legal issue and a duty.

“Tattha [M 0.0220] katamaṃ kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ? Yā saṅghassa kiccayatā, karaṇīyatā, apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ – idaṃ kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which duty is a legal issue concerning duties? Whatever is the Saṅgha's state of having a duty, its state of having something to be done, an act of announcement, an act of motion, an act with a motion and one announcement, and an act with a motion and three announcements—this duty is a legal issue concerning duties.

“Tattha katamaṃ kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ? Ācariyakiccaṃ, upajjhāyakiccaṃ, samānupajjhāyakiccaṃ, samānācariyakiccaṃ – idaṃ kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which duty is not a legal issue? The duty of a teacher, the duty of a preceptor, the duty of one with the same preceptor, and the duty of one with the same teacher—this duty is not a legal issue.

“Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ.

Among these, which legal issue is not a duty? A legal issue concerning a dispute, a legal issue concerning an accusation, and a legal issue concerning an offense—this legal issue is not a duty.

“Tattha [V 0.0204] katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca.

Among these, which is both a legal issue and a duty? A legal issue concerning duties is both a legal issue and a duty.

9. Adhikaraṇavūpasamanasamatho

9. The Settlements for Appeasing Legal Issues

Sammukhāvinayo

Verdict in the Presence of

228. pari. 292-293, 307 ādayo “Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ dvīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca, yebhuyyasikāya ca. Siyā vivādādhikaraṇaṃ ekaṃ samathaṃ anāgamma yebhuyyasikaṃ, ekena samathena sameyya – sammukhāvinayenāti? Siyātissa vacanīyaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha [T 1.0349] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā, vinayoti vā avinayoti vā, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āpattīti vā anāpattīti vā, lahukā āpattīti vā garukā āpattīti vā, sāvasesā āpattīti vā anavasesā āpattīti vā, duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā.

228. “By how many settlements is a legal issue concerning a dispute settled? A legal issue concerning a dispute is settled by two settlements: by the procedure in the presence of and by the procedure of the majority. Could a legal issue concerning a dispute be settled by one settlement—the procedure in the presence of—without resorting to the procedure of the majority?” “It could be,” it should be said. “How so? Here, Bhikkhus, bhikkhus dispute: ‘This is Dhamma’ or ‘This is not Dhamma’; ‘This is Vinaya’ or ‘This is not Vinaya’; ‘This was spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata’ or ‘This was not spoken and not uttered by the Tathāgata’; ‘This was practiced by the Tathāgata’ or ‘This was not practiced by the Tathāgata’; ‘This was prescribed by the Tathāgata’ or ‘This was not prescribed by the Tathāgata’; ‘This is an offense’ or ‘This is not an offense’; ‘This is a light offense’ or ‘This is a serious offense’; ‘This is an offense with a remainder’ or ‘This is an offense without a remainder’; ‘This is a gross offense’ or ‘This is not a gross offense.’”

“Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha saṅghasammukhatā? Yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – ayaṃ tattha saṅghasammukhatā. Kā ca [M 0.0221] tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā[P 2.0094]? Yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati – ayaṃ tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca vivadati, yena ca vivadati, ubho atthapaccatthikā sammukhībhūtā honti – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako [T 1.0350] ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

“If, Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus are able to settle that legal issue, this, Bhikkhus, is called a settled legal issue. By what is it settled? By the procedure in the presence of. And what is there in the procedure in the presence of? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individuals. And what, in this case, is the presence of the Saṅgha? However many bhikkhus are eligible for the act have come, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those who are present do not object—this, in this case, is the presence of the Saṅgha. And what, in this case, is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya? By whatever Dhamma, by whatever Vinaya, by whatever Teacher's instruction that legal issue is settled—this, in this case, is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya. And what, in this case, is the presence of the individuals? The one who disputes and the one with whom he disputes, both adversaries, are present face-to-face—this, in this case, is the presence of the individuals. If, Bhikkhus, the agent reopens a legal issue thus settled, there is an offense of expiation for reopening it; if the one who gave consent complains, there is an offense of expiation for complaining.”

229. “Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ āvāse vūpasametuṃ, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi, yasmiṃ āvāse sambahulā bahutarā (sī. syā.) bhikkhū, so āvāso gantabbo. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchantā antarāmagge sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena[V 0.0205]. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha saṅghasammukhatā? Yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – ayaṃ tattha saṅghasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā? Yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati – ayaṃ tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca vivadati, yena ca vivadati, ubho atthapaccatthikā sammukhībhūtā honti – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

229. Bhikkhus, if those bhikkhus are unable to settle that legal question in that residence, then, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus should go to a residence where there are many bhikkhus. If, bhikkhus, while going to that residence, those bhikkhus are able to settle that legal question on the way, this legal question, bhikkhus, is said to be settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of being in the presence. And what is there in the procedure of being in the presence? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the persons. And what, in this case, is the presence of the Saṅgha? However many bhikkhus are fit for the formal act have come, the consent of those worthy of giving consent has been brought, and those who are present do not object—this is the presence of the Saṅgha in this case. And what, in this case, is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya? By whichever Dhamma, whichever Vinaya, whichever teaching of the Teacher that legal question is settled—this is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya in this case. And what, in this case, is the presence of the persons? Both the one who disputes and the one with whom one disputes, both parties to the dispute, are present—this is the presence of the persons in this case. Bhikkhus, if a legal question has been settled in this way and the one who carried out the settlement reopens it, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening; if the one who gave consent complains, there is a pācittiya offense for complaining.

230. “Te [T 1.0351] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū taṃ āvāsaṃ āgacchantā antarāmagge na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi, taṃ āvāsaṃ gantvā āvāsikā bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – ‘idaṃ kho, āvuso, adhikaraṇaṃ evaṃ jātaṃ, evaṃ samuppannaṃ; sādhāyasmantā imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamentu dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena, yathayidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ suvūpasantaṃ assā’ti.

230. Bhikkhus, if those bhikkhus, while coming to that residence, are unable to settle that legal question on the way, then, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus, having gone to that residence, should speak to the resident bhikkhus thus: ‘Friends, this legal question has arisen thus, has originated thus. Venerable sirs, please settle this legal question according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s teaching, so that this legal question may be well-settled.’

“Sace[M 0.0222], bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū vuḍḍhatarā honti, āgantukā bhikkhū navakatarā, tehi, bhikkhave, āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi āgantukā bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – ‘iṅgha tumhe, āyasmanto, muhuttaṃ ekamantaṃ hotha, yāva mayaṃ mantemā’ti. Sace pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū navakatarā honti, āgantukā bhikkhū vuḍḍhatarā, tehi, bhikkhave, āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi āgantukā bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – ‘tena hi tumhe, āyasmanto, muhuttaṃ idheva tāva hotha, yāva mayaṃ mantemā’ti.

If, bhikkhus, the resident bhikkhus are more senior and the visiting bhikkhus are more junior, then, bhikkhus, those resident bhikkhus should speak to the visiting bhikkhus thus: ‘Come, Venerables, be aside for a moment while we deliberate.’ But if, bhikkhus, the resident bhikkhus are more junior and the visiting bhikkhus are more senior, then, bhikkhus, those resident bhikkhus should speak to the visiting bhikkhus thus: ‘Well then, Venerables, be right here for a moment while we deliberate.’

“Sace pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mantayamānānaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘na mayaṃ sakkoma imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanenā’ti, na taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi sampaṭicchitabbaṃ. Sace pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mantayamānānaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘sakkoma mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanenā’ti, tehi, bhikkhave, āvāsikehi [T 1.0352] bhikkhūhi āgantukā bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – ‘sace tumhe, āyasmanto, amhākaṃ [P 2.0095] imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ yathājātaṃ yathāsamuppannaṃ ārocessatha, yathā ca mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessāma dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena tathā suvūpasantaṃ [V 0.0206] bhavissati. Evaṃ mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ sampaṭicchissāma. No ce tumhe, āyasmanto, amhākaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ yathājātaṃ yathāsamuppannaṃ ārocessatha, yathā ca mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessāma dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena tathā na suvūpasantaṃ bhavissati, na mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ sampaṭicchissāmā’ti. Evaṃ supariggahitaṃ kho, bhikkhave, katvā āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ.

But if, bhikkhus, while the resident bhikkhus are deliberating, it occurs to them thus: ‘We are not able to settle this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s teaching,’ that legal issue should not be accepted by the resident bhikkhus. But if, bhikkhus, while the resident bhikkhus are deliberating, it occurs to them thus: ‘We are able to settle this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s teaching,’ then, bhikkhus, those resident bhikkhus should speak to the visiting bhikkhus thus: ‘If you, Venerables, report this legal issue to us as it arose and as it came about, it will be well-settled in the way that we settle it according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s teaching. In that case, we will accept this legal issue. But if you, Venerables, do not report this legal issue to us as it arose and as it came about, it will not be well-settled in the way that we would settle it according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s teaching. In that case, we will not accept this legal issue.’ Indeed, bhikkhus, having thus made it a well-grasped matter, that legal issue should be accepted by the resident bhikkhus.

“Tehi, bhikkhave, āgantukehi bhikkhūhi āvāsikā bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – ‘yathājātaṃ yathāsamuppannaṃ mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ āyasmantānaṃ ārocessāma. Sace āyasmantā sakkonti ettakena vā ettakena vā antarena imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena tathā suvūpasantaṃ bhavissati. Evaṃ mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ āyasmantānaṃ niyyādessāma. No ce āyasmantā sakkonti ettakena vā ettakena vā antarena imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena tathā na suvūpasantaṃ bhavissati, na mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ āyasmantānaṃ niyyādessāma[M 0.0223]. Mayameva [T 1.0353] imassa adhikaraṇassa sāmino bhavissāmā’ti. Evaṃ supariggahitaṃ kho, bhikkhave, katvā āgantukehi bhikkhūhi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ niyyādetabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, those visiting bhikkhus should speak to the resident bhikkhus thus: ‘We will inform the venerable ones of this legal issue just as it has arisen, just as it has come to be. If the venerable ones are able to settle this legal issue by this or that means, in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher's teaching, in that way it will be well-settled. In that case, we will hand over this legal issue to the venerable ones. But if the venerable ones are not able to settle this legal issue by this or that means, in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher's teaching, in that way it will not be well-settled, and we will not hand over this legal issue to the venerable ones. We ourselves will be the owners of this legal issue.’ Indeed, bhikkhus, having thus made it a well-grasped matter, the visiting bhikkhus should hand over that legal issue to the resident bhikkhus.

“Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

Bhikkhus, if those bhikkhus are able to settle that legal issue, this legal issue, bhikkhus, is said to be settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of settling in the presence of. And what constitutes 'presence' therein? There is the presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individual... Bhikkhus, if a legal issue has been settled in this way and the one who effected the settlement reopens it, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening. If the one who gave consent complains, there is a pācittiya offense for complaining.

Ubbāhikāyavūpasamanaṃ

Settling by Ad Hoc Arbitration

231. “Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anantāni anaggāni (sī.) ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa na cetassa (ka.) bhāsitassa attho viññāyati, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ubbāhikāya vūpasametuṃ. “Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo – sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu; bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpassa dhammā bahussutā honti, [V 0.0207] dhātā dhatā (sī. syā.) vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā [T 1.0354] diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā; ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso[P 2.0096]; vinaye kho pana ṭhito cheko (ka.) hoti asaṃhīro; paṭibalo hoti ubho atthapaccatthike assāsetuṃ saññāpetuṃ nijjhāpetuṃ pekkhetuṃ pasādetuṃ; adhikaraṇasamuppādavūpasamanakusalo hoti; adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti; adhikaraṇasamudayaṃ jānāti; adhikaraṇanirodhaṃ jānāti; adhikaraṇanirodhagāminipaṭipadaṃ jānāti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ ubbāhikāya sammannituṃ. Evañca [M 0.0224] pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

231. “Bhikkhus, if, while those bhikkhus are settling that legal issue, endless discussions arise and the meaning of even a single statement is not understood, I allow, bhikkhus, such a legal issue to be settled by ad hoc arbitration. A bhikkhu endowed with ten qualities should be appointed for ad hoc arbitration: He is virtuous, restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, and he trains himself by undertaking the training rules. He is learned, a preserver of the teachings, a storehouse of the teachings. Those teachings which are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure spiritual life—teachings such as these he has learned much, retained, practiced verbally, examined mentally, and penetrated well by view. Moreover, both Pātimokkhas are thoroughly learned by him in detail, well analyzed, well mastered, well determined in terms of the rules and their detailed analysis. He is firm in the discipline and not prone to wavering. He is capable of reassuring, convincing, persuading, making them see reason, and pleasing both sides. He is skilled in the arising and settling of legal issues. He knows what a legal issue is. He knows the origin of a legal issue. He knows the cessation of a legal issue. He knows the way leading to the cessation of a legal issue. I allow, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities to be appointed for ad hoc arbitration. And this is how, bhikkhus, he should be appointed. First, a bhikkhu should be invited. Having been invited, a competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

232. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anantāni ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa bhāsitassa attho viññāyati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmañca itthannāmañca bhikkhuṃ sammanneyya ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Esā ñatti.

232. ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. While this legal issue of ours is being settled, endless discussions arise, and the meaning of a single statement is not understood. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhu named so-and-so and the bhikkhu named so-and-so to settle this legal issue by ad hoc arbitration. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anantāni ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa bhāsitassa attho viññāyati. Saṅgho itthannāmañca itthannāmañca bhikkhuṃ sammannati ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ [T 1.0355] vūpasametuṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa ca itthannāmassa ca bhikkhuno sammuti ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. While this legal issue of ours is being settled, endless discussions arise, and the meaning of a single statement is not understood. The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhu named so-and-so and the bhikkhu named so-and-so to settle this legal issue by ad hoc arbitration. If any venerable one approves of the appointment of the bhikkhu named so-and-so and the bhikkhu named so-and-so to settle this legal issue by ad hoc arbitration, he should be silent. He who does not approve should speak.’

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo ca itthannāmo ca bhikkhu ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘The bhikkhu named so-and-so and the bhikkhu named so-and-so have been appointed by the Saṅgha to settle this legal issue by ad hoc arbitration. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I take note of this.’”

“Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ubbāhikāya vūpasametuṃ, idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if those bhikkhus are able to settle that legal issue by ad hoc arbitration, this, bhikkhus, is called a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of settling in the presence of. And what is there in that procedure of settling in the presence of? The presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, the presence of the individuals… Bhikkhus, if the one who effected the settlement reopens a legal issue thus settled, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening it.”

233. “Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne tatrāssa bhikkhu dhammakathiko, tassa neva suttaṃ āgataṃ hoti, no suttavibhaṅgo, so atthaṃ asallakkhento [V 0.0208] byañjanacchāyāya atthaṃ paṭibāhati, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

233. “Bhikkhus, if, while that legal issue is being settled by those bhikkhus, there is a bhikkhu who is a speaker on the Dhamma, but he is not conversant with the Pātimokkha, nor with the Suttavibhaṅga, and, not discerning the meaning, he rejects the meaning by the shadow of the phrasing, then a competent and capable bhikkhu should inform those bhikkhus:”

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dhammakathiko. Imassa neva suttaṃ āgataṃ hoti, no suttavibhaṅgo. So atthaṃ asallakkhento byañjanacchāyāya atthaṃ paṭibāhati. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ[M 0.0225], itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ [P 2.0097] vuṭṭhāpetvā avasesā imaṃ [T 1.0356] adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyāmāti.

“‘Venerable sirs, listen to my words. This bhikkhu of such-and-such a name is a speaker of the Dhamma. The Pātimokkha is not known to him by heart, nor the Suttavibhaṅga. Not discerning the meaning, he obstructs the meaning by the shadow of the letter. If it seems the proper time to the venerable sirs, having made the bhikkhu of such-and-such a name rise from his seat, we, the remaining ones, should settle this legal issue.’”

“Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if those bhikkhus, having made that bhikkhu rise from his seat, are able to settle that legal issue, this, bhikkhus, is called a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of settling in the presence of. And what is there in that procedure of settling in the presence of? There is the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, the presence of the individual... Bhikkhus, if the one who effected the settlement reopens a legal issue thus settled, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening.”

“Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne tatrāssa bhikkhu dhammakathiko, tassa suttañhi kho āgataṃ hoti, no suttavibhaṅgo, so atthaṃ asallakkhento byañjanacchāyāya atthaṃ paṭibāhati, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

“Bhikkhus, if, while that legal issue is being decided by those bhikkhus, there is a bhikkhu who is a speaker of the Dhamma, and for him only the Pātimokkha is known by heart, but not the Suttavibhaṅga, and not discerning the meaning, he obstructs the meaning by the shadow of the letter, then a competent and capable bhikkhu should inform those bhikkhus:”

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dhammakathiko. Imassa suttañhi kho āgataṃ hoti, no suttavibhaṅgo. So atthaṃ asallakkhento byañjanacchāyāya atthaṃ paṭibāhati. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā avasesā imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyāmāti.

“May the venerable ones listen to me. This monk of such-and-such a name is a speaker of the Dhamma. Only the Pātimokkha is known to him by heart, but not the Suttavibhaṅga. Not discerning the meaning, he obstructs the meaning by the shadow of the letter. If it seems the proper time to the venerable ones, having made the monk of such-and-such a name rise from his seat, we, the remaining ones, should settle this legal issue.”

“Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ, idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

“If, monks, those monks, having made that monk rise, are able to settle that legal issue, this is called, monks, a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure in the presence. And what is there in that procedure in the presence? The presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, the presence of the individuals… If, monks, a member of the assembly that performed the act reopens a legal issue thus settled, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening it.”

Yebhuyyasikāvinayo

The Procedure of the Majority

234. “Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ubbāhikāya [T 1.0357] vūpasametuṃ, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ saṅghassa niyyādetabbaṃ – ‘na mayaṃ na ca mayaṃ (ka.), bhante, sakkoma [V 0.0209] imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ubbāhikāya vūpasametuṃ, saṅghova imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametū’ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ yebhuyyasikāya vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu salākaggāhāpako sammannitabbo – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na [M 0.0226] dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, gahitāgahitañca jāneyya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

234. “If, monks, those monks are unable to settle that legal issue by the ubbāhikā procedure, then, monks, those monks should refer that legal issue to the Sangha: ‘Venerable sirs, we are unable to settle this legal issue by the ubbāhikā procedure; let the Sangha itself settle this legal issue.’ I allow, monks, such a legal issue to be settled by a majority vote. A monk endowed with five factors should be appointed as a ballot distributor: one who would not go the wrong way through desire, would not go the wrong way through ill will, would not go the wrong way through delusion, would not go the wrong way through fear, and who would know what has been taken and what has not been taken… And thus, monks, he should be appointed. First, a monk should be requested. Having requested, the Sangha should be informed by a clever and competent monk:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ salākaggāhāpakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as the ballot distributor. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ salākaggāhāpakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno salākaggāhāpakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as the ballot distributor. Let the venerable one who approves of the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as the ballot distributor remain silent. Let the one who does not approve speak.”

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu salākaggāhāpako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Sangha as the ballot distributor. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

“Tena salākaggāhāpakena bhikkhunā salākā gāhetabbā. Yathā bahutarā bhikkhū dhammavādino vadanti tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, yebhuyyasikāya ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha saṅghasammukhatā? Yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – ayaṃ tattha saṅghasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā? Yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati – ayaṃ tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā[T 1.0358]. Kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca vivadati, yena ca vivadati, ubho atthapaccatthikā sammukhībhūtā honti – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā. Kā ca tattha yebhuyyasikāya? Yā yebhuyyasikākammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – ayaṃ tattha yebhuyyasikāya. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

“That monk appointed as the ballot distributor should have the ballots taken. The legal issue should be settled according to how the majority of monks who speak in accordance with the Dhamma declare. This, monks, is called a settled legal issue. By what is it settled? By the procedure in the presence and by the procedure of the majority. And what, in this case, is the procedure in the presence? The presence of the Sangha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individuals. And what, herein, is the presence of the Sangha? However many monks are competent for the formal act have come, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present do not object—this, herein, is the presence of the Sangha. And what, herein, is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya? By whichever Dhamma, whichever Vinaya, whichever teaching of the Teacher that legal issue is settled—this, herein, is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya. And what, herein, is the presence of the individuals? Both the one who disputes and the one with whom one disputes, both litigants, are present—this, herein, is the presence of the individuals. And what, herein, is the procedure by majority? Whatever is the carrying out, the performance, the undertaking, the acceptance, the consent, and the non-objection regarding the formal act by majority—this, herein, is the procedure by majority. Monks, if a member of the assembly that performed the act reopens a legal issue that has been settled in this way, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening it. If the one who gave consent complains, there is a pācittiya offense for complaining.”

Tividhasalākaggāho

The Threefold Distribution of Ballots

235. Tena [P 2.0098][M 0.0227][V 0.0210] kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā evaṃ jātaṃ evaṃ samuppannaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti. Atha kho te bhikkhū – asantuṭṭhā sāvatthiyā saṅghassa adhikaraṇavūpasamanena – assosuṃ kho amukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā therā viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā paṇḍitā viyattā medhāvino lajjino kukkuccakā sikkhākāmā. Te ce therā imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena, evamidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ suvūpasantaṃ assāti. Atha kho te bhikkhū taṃ āvāsaṃ gantvā te there etadavocuṃ – “idaṃ, bhante, adhikaraṇaṃ evaṃ jātaṃ, evaṃ samuppannaṃ. Sādhu, bhante, therā imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamentu dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena, yathayidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ suvūpasantaṃ assā”ti. Atha kho te therā – yathā sāvatthiyā saṅghena adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamitaṃ tathā suvūpasantanti yathā suvūpasantaṃ (sī. syā.) – tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamesuṃ[T 1.0359].

235. At that time, a legal issue had arisen in this way, had come about in this way in Sāvatthī. Then those monks—dissatisfied with the settlement of the legal issue by the Sangha in Sāvatthī—heard: ‘In a certain monastery, it is said, many elder monks are dwelling who are learned, versed in the transmitted texts, upholders of the Dhamma, upholders of the Vinaya, upholders of the Mātikās, wise, clever, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training. If those elders were to settle this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, then this legal issue would be well-settled.’ Then those monks went to that monastery and said this to those elders: ‘Venerable sirs, this legal issue has arisen in this way, has come about in this way. It would be good, venerable sirs, if the elders would settle this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, so that this legal issue might be well-settled.’ Then those elders, considering, ‘As the legal issue was settled by the Sangha in Sāvatthī, so it is well-settled,’ settled that legal issue in that same way.

Atha kho te bhikkhū – asantuṭṭhā sāvatthiyā saṅghassa adhikaraṇavūpasamanena, asantuṭṭhā sambahulānaṃ therānaṃ adhikaraṇavūpasamanena – assosuṃ kho amukasmiṃ kira āvāse tayo therā viharanti…pe… dve therā viharanti…pe… eko thero viharati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. So ce thero imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyya dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena, evamidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ suvūpasantaṃ assāti. Atha kho te bhikkhū taṃ āvāsaṃ gantvā taṃ theraṃ etadavocuṃ – “idaṃ, bhante, adhikaraṇaṃ evaṃ jātaṃ, evaṃ samuppannaṃ. Sādhu, bhante, thero imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametu dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena, yathayidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ suvūpasantaṃ assā”ti. Atha kho so thero – yathā sāvatthiyā saṅghena adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamitaṃ, yathā sambahulehi therehi adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamitaṃ, yathā tīhi therehi adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamitaṃ, yathā dvīhi therehi adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamitaṃ, tathā suvūpasantanti – tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamesi.

Then those monks—dissatisfied with the settlement of the legal question by the Saṅgha in Sāvatthī, dissatisfied with the settlement by many elder monks—heard that in a certain monastery three elder monks were dwelling… two elder monks were dwelling… one elder monk was dwelling: learned, a master of the tradition, an expert on the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the outlines; wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and eager for the training. 'If that elder monk were to settle this legal question in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, then this legal question would be well-settled.' Then those monks went to that monastery and said to that elder monk, 'Venerable sir, this legal question has arisen in this way, has originated in this way. Please, venerable sir, settle this legal question in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, so that this legal question may be well-settled.' Then that elder monk, reflecting, 'It is well-settled in the same manner as the Saṅgha in Sāvatthī settled the legal question, as many elder monks settled it, as three elder monks settled it, and as two elder monks settled it,' settled that legal question in that very manner.

Atha [M 0.0228] kho te bhikkhū asantuṭṭhā sāvatthiyā saṅghassa adhikaraṇavūpasamanena, asantuṭṭhā sambahulānaṃ therānaṃ adhikaraṇavūpasamanena, asantuṭṭhā tiṇṇaṃ therānaṃ adhikaraṇavūpasamanena, asantuṭṭhā dvinnaṃ therānaṃ adhikaraṇavūpasamanena, asantuṭṭhā ekassa therassa adhikaraṇavūpasamanena, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… [T 1.0360] “nihatametaṃ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ santaṃ vūpasantaṃ suvūpasantaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ saññattiyā tayo salākaggāhe – gūḷhakaṃ, sakaṇṇajappakaṃ, vivaṭakaṃ.

Then those monks, being dissatisfied with the Saṅgha’s settlement of the legal question in Sāvatthī, dissatisfied with the settlement of the legal question by many senior monks, dissatisfied with the settlement of the legal question by three senior monks, dissatisfied with the settlement of the legal question by two senior monks, and dissatisfied with the settlement of the legal question by one senior monk, went to the Blessed One. Having approached, they reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Monks, this legal question is settled, calmed, pacified, and well-pacified. I allow, monks, for the purpose of convincing those monks, three ways of taking voting tickets: the secret, the whispering-in-the-ear, and the open.'

“Kathañca[V 0.0211], bhikkhave, gūḷhako salākaggāho hoti? Tena salākaggāhāpakena bhikkhunā [P 2.0099] salākāyo vaṇṇāvaṇṇāyo katvā ekameko bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā, ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā. Yaṃ icchasi taṃ gaṇhāhī’ti. Gahite vattabbo – ‘mā ca kassaci dassehī’ti. Sace jānāti – adhammavādī bahutarāti, duggahoti, paccukkaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Sace jānāti – dhammavādī bahutarāti, suggahoti, sāvetabbaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, gūḷhako salākaggāho hoti.

“And how, monks, is the secret taking of voting tickets? That monk who is the distributor of voting tickets, having made the voting tickets of various kinds, should approach each monk and speak to him thus: ‘This is the voting ticket for one who holds this view; this is the voting ticket for one who holds that view. Take the one that you wish.’ When it has been taken, he should be told: ‘Do not show it to anyone.’ If he knows, ‘Those not in accordance with the Dhamma are more numerous,’ it is badly taken and should be withdrawn. If he knows, ‘Those in accordance with the Dhamma are more numerous,’ it is well taken and should be announced. In this way, monks, is the secret taking of voting tickets.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, sakaṇṇajappako salākaggāho hoti? Tena salākaggāhāpakena bhikkhunā ekamekassa bhikkhuno upakaṇṇake ārocetabbaṃ – ‘ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā, ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā. Yaṃ icchasi taṃ gaṇhāhī’ti. Gahite vattabbo – ‘mā ca kassaci ārocehī’ti. Sace jānāti – adhammavādī bahutarāti, duggahoti, paccukkaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Sace jānāti – dhammavādī bahutarāti, suggahoti, sāvetabbaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sakaṇṇajappako salākaggāho hoti.

“And how, monks, is the whispering-in-the-ear taking of voting tickets? That monk who is the distributor of voting tickets should announce in the ear of each monk: ‘This is the voting ticket for one who holds this view; this is the voting ticket for one who holds that view. Take the one that you wish.’ When it has been taken, he should be told: ‘Do not announce this to anyone.’ If he knows, ‘Those not in accordance with the Dhamma are more numerous,’ it is badly taken and should be withdrawn. If he knows, ‘Those in accordance with the Dhamma are more numerous,’ it is well taken and should be announced. In this way, monks, is the whispering-in-the-ear taking of voting tickets.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, vivaṭako salākaggāho hoti? Sace jānāti – dhammavādī bahutarāti, vissaṭṭheneva vivaṭena gāhetabbo[T 1.0361]. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, vivaṭako salākaggāho hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo salākaggāhā”ti.

“And how, monks, is there an open taking of the ballot? If one knows, ‘Those who speak according to the Dhamma are in the majority,’ the ballot should be taken openly and unconcealedly. In this way, monks, there is an open taking of the ballot. These, monks, are the three ways of taking the ballot.”

Sativinayo

The Verdict of Mindfulness

236. pari. 292-293, 307 ādayo “Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0229] katihi samathehi sammati? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ catūhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca, sativinayena ca, amūḷhavinayena ca, tassapāpiyasikāya ca. Siyā anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ dve samathe anāgamma – amūḷhavinayañca, tassapāpiyasikañca; dvīhi samathehi sammeyya – sammukhāvinayena ca, sativinayena cāti? Siyātissa vacanīyaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Tassa kho, bhikkhave tassa kho taṃ bhikkhave (syā. ka.), bhikkhuno sativepullappattassa sativinayo dātabbo. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

236. “By how many means of settlement is a dispute concerning accusation resolved? A dispute concerning accusation is resolved by four means of settlement: by settlement in the presence, by the verdict of mindfulness, by the verdict of past insanity, and by the procedure for a monk’s further bad conduct. Could a dispute concerning accusation be settled without resorting to two means of settlement—the verdict of past insanity and the procedure for a monk’s further bad conduct—and instead be settled by two means of settlement: by settlement in the presence and by the verdict of mindfulness? It could be so. How so? Here, monks, monks accuse a monk of a groundless breach of morality. For that monk, monks, who has attained fullness of mindfulness, a verdict of mindfulness should be granted. And how, monks, should it be granted—

“Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅga karitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘maṃ, bhante, bhikkhū amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. Sohaṃ, bhante[V 0.0212], sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattenaṃ bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Monks, that monk should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder… and should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, monks are accusing me of a groundless breach of morality. I, venerable sirs, having attained fullness of mindfulness, request a verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. A competent, capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Bhikkhū itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. So sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācati[P 2.0100]. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sativepullappattassa [T 1.0362] sativinayaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

“‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. Monks are accusing the monk named so-and-so of a groundless breach of morality. He, having attained fullness of mindfulness, requests a verdict of mindfulness from the Saṅgha. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant a verdict of mindfulness to the monk named so-and-so, who has attained fullness of mindfulness. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Bhikkhū itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsenti. So sativepullappatto saṅghaṃ sativinayaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sativepullappattassa sativinayaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sativepullappattassa sativinayassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The monks are accusing the monk named so-and-so of a groundless corruption of virtue. He, having attained fullness of mindfulness, requests the Saṅgha for a verdict of mindfulness. The Saṅgha grants a verdict of mindfulness to the monk named so-and-so, who has attained fullness of mindfulness. If it is agreeable to any venerable one to grant a verdict of mindfulness to the monk named so-and-so, who has attained fullness of mindfulness, let him be silent. If it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter… and so on… For a third time I state this matter… and so on…

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sativepullappattassa sativinayo. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The verdict of mindfulness has been granted by the Saṅgha to the monk named so-and-so, who has attained fullness of mindfulness. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

“Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca sativinayena ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā[M 0.0230], vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca anuvadati, yañca anuvadati, ubho sammukhībhūtā honti – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā. Kiñca tattha sativinayasmiṃ? Yā sativinayassa kammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – idaṃ tattha sativinayasmiṃ. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

This, monks, is called a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of being in the presence and by the verdict of mindfulness. And what, in that case, is the procedure of being in the presence? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individual… and so on… And what, in that case, is the presence of the individual? Both the one who accuses and the one who is accused are present—this, in that case, is the presence of the individual. And what, in that case, is the verdict of mindfulness? The doing, the performing, the undertaking, the full undertaking, the acceptance, and the non-rejection of the formal act for the verdict of mindfulness—this, in that case, is the verdict of mindfulness. If, monks, after a legal issue has been thus settled, the one who performed the act reopens it, there is a pācittiya offense for reopening it. If the one who gave his consent complains, there is a pācittiya offense for complaining.

Amūḷhavinayo

The Verdict of Lucidity

237. “Siyā anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ dve samathe anāgamma – sativinayañca, tassapāpiyasikañca; dvīhi samathehi sammeyya – sammukhāvinayena ca, amūḷhavinayena [T 1.0363] cāti? Siyātissa vacanīyaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ummattako hoti cittavipariyāsakato[V 0.0213]. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Taṃ bhikkhū ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. “Tassa kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayo dātabbo. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo –

237. “Could a legal issue concerning accusation be settled without resorting to two settlements—the settlement by a verdict of mindfulness and the settlement by a verdict for specific depravity—and be settled by two settlements: by the settlement of a verdict in the presence and by the settlement of a verdict for one who is no longer confused? It could be. It should be said thus. How so? Here, monks, a monk is insane, his mind deranged. Being insane and his mind deranged, many un-monk-like acts, transgressed in speech and action, have been committed by him. The monks accuse him of an offense committed while he was insane and his mind was deranged, saying, ‘Venerable sir, remember having committed such an offense.’ He says thus: ‘Friends, I was indeed insane, my mind was deranged. Being insane and my mind being deranged, many un-monk-like acts, transgressed in speech and action, were committed by me. I do not remember that. This was done by me while confused.’ Even when he says this, they continue to accuse him, saying, ‘Venerable sir, remember having committed such an offense.’ Monks, for that monk who is no longer confused, the verdict for one who is no longer confused should be given. And, monks, it should be given thus:”

“Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Maṃ bhikkhū ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti[T 1.0364]. Evampi maṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā [M 0.0231] evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. ‘Sohaṃ, bhante, amūḷho saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Then, monks, that monk should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder… and should speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I was insane, of deranged mind. By me, being insane and of deranged mind, much conduct unbecoming of a recluse, both spoken and acted upon, was habitually practiced. The monks charge me with an offense for what was habitually practiced while I was insane and of deranged mind, saying: “May the venerable one remember having fallen into an offense of such a kind.” I say this to them: “Indeed, friends, I was insane, of deranged mind. By me, being insane and of deranged mind, much conduct unbecoming of a recluse, both spoken and acted upon, was habitually practiced. I do not remember it. This was done by me while deluded.” Even when I say this, they still charge me, saying: “May the venerable one remember having fallen into an offense of such a kind.” Venerable sirs, I, being undeluded, ask the Saṅgha for the legal procedure for one who is not deluded.’ A second time it should be asked. A third time it should be asked. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu ummattako ahosi cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Taṃ bhikkhū ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. So amūḷho saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.
