“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk of such-and-such a name was insane, mentally deranged. By him, being insane and mentally deranged, much that is unbecoming of a recluse, both spoken and transgressed, was habitually practiced. The monks charge him with an offense habitually practiced while insane and mentally deranged, saying: ‘May the venerable one remember having committed an offense of such a nature.’ He speaks thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I was insane, mentally deranged. By me, being insane and mentally deranged, much that is unbecoming of a recluse, both spoken and transgressed, was habitually practiced. I do not remember that. This was done by me while deluded.’ Even when he is spoken to thus, they continue to charge him, saying: ‘May the venerable one remember having committed an offense of such a nature.’ He, being undeluded, requests the Saṅgha for the legal procedure for one who is undeluded. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the legal procedure for one who is undeluded to the monk of such-and-such a name, who is undeluded. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [V 0.0214] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu ummattako ahosi cittavipariyāsakato. Tena ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Taṃ bhikkhū ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena ajjhāciṇṇena āpattiyā codenti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti[T 1.0365]. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummattako ahosiṃ cittavipariyāsakato. Tena me ummattakena cittavipariyāsakatena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Evampi naṃ vuccamānā codenteva – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. So amūḷho saṅghaṃ amūḷhavinayaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so was insane, having become mentally deranged. Being insane and mentally deranged, he habitually practiced much that was unbecoming of a monk, both in speech and in deed. The bhikkhus charge him with an offense on account of this habitual practice while he was insane and mentally deranged, saying: ‘May the venerable one recall having committed such an offense.’ He says thus: ‘Indeed, friends, I was insane, mentally deranged. Being insane and mentally deranged, I habitually practiced much that was unbecoming of a monk, both in speech and in deed. I do not remember that. This was done by me while I was confused.’ Even when he speaks thus, they continue to charge him: ‘May the venerable one recall having committed such an offense.’ He, no longer being confused, requests from the Saṅgha the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused. The Saṅgha grants the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused to the bhikkhu named so-and-so, who is no longer confused. To whichever venerable one the granting of the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused to the bhikkhu named so-and-so is agreeable, let them remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, let them speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

A second time, I state this matter… and so on… A third time, I state this matter… and so on…

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayo. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The legal procedure for one who is no longer confused has been granted by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so, who is no longer confused. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I take note of this.

“Idaṃ [M 0.0232] vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, amūḷhavinayena ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… kiñca tattha amūḷhavinayasmiṃ[P 2.0101]? Yā amūḷhavinayassa kammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – idaṃ tattha amūḷhavinayasmiṃ. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

Bhikkhus, this legal issue is said to be settled. By what is it settled? By the legal procedure of being in the presence and by the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused. And what, therein, constitutes the legal procedure of being in the presence? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individual… and so on… And what, therein, constitutes the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused? The acting, the carrying out, the undertaking, the full undertaking, the consenting, and the non-rejection of the formal act for one who is no longer confused—this, therein, constitutes the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused. Bhikkhus, if the one who carried out the procedure reopens a legal issue that has been settled in this way, it is an offense of expiation for reopening. If one who gave consent complains, it is an offense of expiation for complaining.

Tassapāpiyasikāvinayo

The Legal Procedure for One of a More Evil Nature

238. “Siyā anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ dve samathe anāgamma – sativinayañca, amūḷhavinayañca[T 1.0366]; dvīhi samathehi sammeyya – sammukhāvinayena ca, tassapāpiyasikāya cāti? Siyātissa vacanīyaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ saṅghamajjhe garukāya āpattiyā codeti – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. Tamenaṃ so nibbeṭhentaṃ [V 0.0215] ativeṭheti – ‘iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi, yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā. Sarāmi ca kho ahaṃ, āvuso, evarūpiṃ appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. Tamenaṃ so nibbeṭhentaṃ ativeṭheti – ‘iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi, yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. So evaṃ vadeti – ‘imañhi nāmāhaṃ, āvuso, appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā apuṭṭho paṭijānissāmi. Kiṃ panāhaṃ evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā, puṭṭho na paṭijānissāmī’ti? So evaṃ vadeti – ‘imañhi nāma tvaṃ, āvuso, appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā apuṭṭho na paṭijānissasi. Kiṃ pana tvaṃ evarūpiṃ [T 1.0367] garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā, apuṭṭho paṭijānissasi? Iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi, yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. So evaṃ vadesi – ‘sarāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, evarūpiṃ [M 0.0233] garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā. Davā me etaṃ vuttaṃ, ravā me etaṃ vuttaṃ – nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā, pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. Tassa kho, bhikkhave tassa kho taṃ bhikkhave (ka.) tassa khvataṃ bhikkhave (syā.), bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

238. Could a legal issue concerning accusation be settled without resorting to two legal procedures—the legal procedure of mindfulness and the legal procedure for one who is no longer confused—and instead be settled by two legal procedures: the legal procedure of being in the presence and the legal procedure for one of a more evil nature? It could be, this should be said. How so? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu accuses another bhikkhu in the midst of the Saṅgha of a grave offense: ‘May the venerable one recall having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika.’ He says thus: ‘I do not recall, friend, having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika.’ While he is trying to extricate himself, the accuser presses him further: ‘Come now, venerable one, ascertain well if you recall having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika.’ He says thus: ‘I do not recall, friend, having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika. But I do recall, friend, having committed a minor offense of such a kind.’ While he is trying to extricate himself, the accuser presses him further: ‘Come now, venerable one, ascertain well if you recall having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika.’ He says thus: ‘Friend, I would confess this minor offense by name even when unasked. How then, having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika, would I not confess when asked?’ The accuser says thus: ‘Friend, you would not confess this minor offense by name when unasked. How then, having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika, would you confess when unasked? Come now, venerable one, ascertain well if you recall having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika.’ He then says: ‘I do recall, friend, having committed such a grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika. It was said by me in jest, it was said by me in error. I do not recall having committed that grave offense, a pārājika or one bordering on a pārājika.’ For that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, the formal act for one of a more evil nature should be carried out. And, bhikkhus, it should be carried out thus: A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe garukāya āpattiyā anuyuñjiyamāno avajānitvā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā avajānāti, aññenāññaṃ paṭicarati, sampajānamusā bhāsati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ kareyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha concerning a grave offense, denies and then confesses; he confesses and then denies; he evades one matter with another; he speaks a deliberate falsehood. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha carry out the formal act for one of a more evil nature for the bhikkhu named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe garukāya āpattiyā anuyuñjiyamāno avajānitvā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā avajānāti, aññenāññaṃ paṭicarati, sampajānamusā bhāsati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ [T 1.0368] karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammassa karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha concerning a grave offense, having denied, confesses; having confessed, denies; he evades one matter with another; he speaks a deliberate falsehood. The Saṅgha carries out the tassapāpiyasikā act for the bhikkhu named so-and-so. Whichever venerable one approves of carrying out the tassapāpiyasikā act for the bhikkhu named so-and-so, he should be silent. Whomever does not approve, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter… and so on… for a third time I state this matter… and so on.

“Kataṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The tassapāpiyasikā act has been carried out by the Saṅgha for the bhikkhu named so-and-so. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I take it.

“Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ [P 2.0102] vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, tassapāpiyasikāya ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā…pe… kā ca tattha tassapāpiyasikāya? Yā tassapāpiyasikākammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – ayaṃ tattha tassapāpiyasikāya. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ kārako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

Bhikkhus, this is called a legal issue that is settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of acting in the presence and by the tassapāpiyasikā procedure. And what therein is the procedure of acting in the presence? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya… and so on… And what therein is the tassapāpiyasikā procedure? Whatever is the doing, performing, approaching, undertaking, acceptance, and non-rejection of the tassapāpiyasikā act—this therein is the tassapāpiyasikā procedure. Bhikkhus, if the bhikkhu who effected the settlement of a legal issue thus settled re-opens it, there is a pācittiya offense for re-opening. If the bhikkhu who gave consent complains, there is a pācittiya offense for complaining.

Paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ

Acting on an Admission

239. pari. 295, 306, 308 ādayo “Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca, paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, tiṇavatthārakena [M 0.0234] ca. Siyā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ ekaṃ samathaṃ anāgamma – tiṇavatthārakaṃ, dvīhi samathehi sammeyya – sammukhāvinayena ca, paṭiññātakaraṇena cāti? Siyātissa vacanīyaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lahukaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ [T 1.0369] paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno; taṃ paṭidesemī’ti. Tena vattabbo – ‘passasī’ti? ‘Āma passāmī’ti. ‘Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī’ti.

239. By how many settlement procedures is a legal issue concerning offenses settled? A legal issue concerning offenses is settled by three settlement procedures: by the procedure of acting in the presence, by acting on an admission, and by covering over with grass. Could a legal issue concerning offenses be settled without one settlement procedure—covering over with grass—and be settled by two settlement procedures: by the procedure of acting in the presence and by acting on an admission? It could be, it should be said. How so? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has committed a minor offense. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should approach one bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit down squatting, raise his joined hands, and say this: ‘Friend, I have committed such-and-such an offense; I confess it.’ He should be asked: ‘Do you see it?’ ‘Yes, I see it.’ ‘In the future, you should restrain yourself.’

“Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca deseti, yassa ca deseti, ubho sammukhībhūtā honti – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā. Kiñca tattha paṭiññātakaraṇasmiṃ? Yā paṭiññātakaraṇassa kammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – idaṃ tattha paṭiññātakaraṇasmiṃ. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ paṭiggāhako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sambahule bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ [V 0.0217] bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno; taṃ paṭidesemī’ti. Byattena bhikkhunā [P 2.0103] paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

Bhikkhus, this is called a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of acting in the presence and by acting on an admission. And what, in that case, is acting in the presence? The presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the person… and so on… And what, in that case, is the presence of the person? Both the one who confesses and the one to whom he confesses are present—this is the presence of the person in that case. And what, in that case, is acting on an admission? Whatever is the doing, performing, approaching, undertaking, acceptance, and non-rejection of the act of acting on an admission—this is acting on an admission in that case. Bhikkhus, if the receiver re-opens a legal issue settled in this way, there is a pācittiya offense for re-opening it. If one should obtain this, it is good. If one should not obtain it, then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, having approached many bhikkhus, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having paid homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his joined palms, should speak thus: ‘Venerable Sirs, I have committed such-and-such an offense; I confess it.’ A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform those bhikkhus:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu āpattiṃ sarati, vivarati, uttāniṃ karoti deseti. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇheyyanti. Tena vattabbo – ‘passasī’ti? ‘Āma [T 1.0370] passāmī’ti. ‘Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī’ti.

May the Venerable Sirs listen to me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, remembers an offense, reveals it, makes it plain, and confesses it. If the time is suitable for the Venerable Sirs, I would receive the confession of the offense of the bhikkhu named so-and-so. The confessor should be asked: ‘Do you see it?’ ‘Yes, I see it.’ ‘In the future, you should restrain yourself.’

“Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca deseti, yassa ca deseti, ubho sammukhībhūtā honti [M 0.0235] – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā. Kiñca tattha paṭiññātakaraṇasmiṃ? Yā paṭiññātakaraṇassa kammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – idaṃ tattha paṭiññātakaraṇasmiṃ. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ paṭiggāhako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno; taṃ paṭidesemī’ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Bhikkhus, this is called a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure of acting in the presence and by acting on an admission. And what is the procedure of acting in the presence in this case? The presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, the presence of the person… and so on… And what is the presence of the person in this case? Both the one who confesses and the one to whom he confesses are present—this is the presence of the person in this case. And what is acting on an admission in this case? Whatever is the doing, performing, approaching, undertaking, acceptance, and non-rejection of the act of acting on an admission—this is acting on an admission in this case. Bhikkhus, if a legal issue settled in this way is re-opened by the receiver, there is a pācittiya offense for re-opening it. If this is achieved, it is good. If not, then that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and say: ‘Venerable sirs, I have committed such-and-such an offense; I confess it.’ A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu āpattiṃ sarati, vivarati, uttāniṃ karoti, deseti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇheyyanti. Tena vattabbo – ‘passasī’ti? ‘Āma passāmī’ti. ‘Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī’ti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This bhikkhu named so-and-so remembers, reveals, makes plain, and confesses an offense. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, I would receive the offense of the bhikkhu named so-and-so.” He should be told: “Do you see?” When it is said, “Yes, I see,” he should be told: “In the future, you should restrain yourself.”

“Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, paṭiññātakaraṇena ca[T 1.0371]. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā…pe… evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ paṭiggāhako [V 0.0218] ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, this is called a legal issue that has been settled. By what is it settled? By the procedure in the presence and by the procedure of acting on an admission. And what, in that procedure in the presence, is presence? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, the presence of the individual... Bhikkhus, if a legal issue thus settled is re-opened by the bhikkhu who received the confession, it is a pācittiya offense for re-opening; if the one who gave consent criticizes, it is a pācittiya offense for criticizing.”

Tiṇavatthārakaṃ

Covering Over as with Grass

240. “Siyā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ ekaṃ samathaṃ anāgamma – paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ, dvīhi samathehi sammeyya – sammukhāvinayena ca, tiṇavatthārakena cāti? Siyātissa vacanīyaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘amhākaṃ kho bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyyā’ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tiṇavatthārakena vūpasametuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, vūpasametabbaṃ. Sabbeheva [M 0.0236] ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbaṃ, sannipatitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

240. “Could a legal issue concerning an offense be settled without resorting to one procedure for settling—the procedure of acting on an admission—but be settled by two procedures: by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over as with grass?” “It could be,” should be said. In what way? Here, bhikkhus, while bhikkhus are living having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is not befitting a recluse is transgressed, spoken and done. In that case, if it occurs to those bhikkhus thus: ‘For us, while living having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much that is not befitting a recluse has been transgressed, spoken and done. If we were to deal with each other regarding these offenses, that legal issue might lead to harshness, severity, and schism.’ Bhikkhus, I allow such a legal issue to be settled by the covering over as with grass. And, bhikkhus, it should be settled in this way. All should assemble together in one place. Having assembled, a competent, capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya[T 1.0372]. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tiṇavatthārakena vūpasameyya, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttanti. “Ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena sako pakkho ñāpetabbo –

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my word. While we were dwelling, having given rise to quarrels, strife, and disputes, much conduct unseemly for a recluse has been transgressed, both spoken and enacted. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would conduce to harshness, roughness, and schism. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should settle this legal issue by the covering with grass, setting aside a grave offense and that which is connected with householders.” A competent and capable bhikkhu from one faction should inform his own faction:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, āyasmantānañceva atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttanti.

“Venerable ones, may you hear my word. While we were dwelling, having given rise to quarrels, strife, and disputes, much conduct unseemly for a recluse has been transgressed, both spoken and enacted. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would conduce to harshness, roughness, and schism. If the time is right for the venerable ones, I would confess in the midst of the Saṅgha by the covering with grass—for the benefit of the venerable ones and for my own benefit—both the offenses of the venerable ones and my own offenses, setting aside a grave offense and that which is connected with householders.”

241. “Athāparesaṃ [V 0.0219] ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena sako pakkho ñāpetabbo –

241. Then, a competent and capable bhikkhu from the other faction should inform his own faction:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, āyasmantānañceva atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttanti.

“Venerable ones, may you hear my word. While we were dwelling, having given rise to quarrels, strife, and disputes, much conduct unseemly for a recluse has been transgressed, both spoken and enacted. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would conduce to harshness, roughness, and schism. If the time is right for the venerable ones, I would confess in the midst of the Saṅgha by the covering with grass—for the benefit of the venerable ones and for my own benefit—both the offenses of the venerable ones and my own offenses, setting aside a grave offense and that which is connected with householders.”

242. “Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ [T 1.0373] bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

242. Then, a competent and capable bhikkhu from the other faction should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu [M 0.0237] me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my word. While we were dwelling, having given rise to quarrels, strife, and disputes, much conduct unseemly for a recluse has been transgressed, both spoken and enacted. If we were to deal with one another for these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would conduce to harshness, roughness, and schism. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, I would confess in the midst of the Saṅgha by the covering with grass—for the benefit of these venerable sirs and for my own benefit—both the offenses of these venerable sirs and my own offenses, setting aside a grave offense and that which is connected with householders. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya. Ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti, yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya, attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena desemi, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati amhākaṃ imāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena desanā, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. While we were dwelling, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, much un-monk-like conduct was transgressed, spoken and acted upon. If we were to deal with one another concerning these offenses, it might be that this legal issue would lead to harshness, coarseness, and division. For the benefit of these venerable ones and for my own benefit, I confess these offenses—whatever offense of these venerable ones and whatever offense of my own—in the midst of the Saṅgha by the method of covering with grass, setting aside grave offenses and setting aside offenses connected with laypeople. If the confession of these our offenses in the midst of the Saṅgha by the method of covering with grass—setting aside grave offenses and setting aside offenses connected with laypeople—is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Desitā [V 0.0220] amhākaṃ imā āpattiyo saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena[T 1.0374], ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ, ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

These our offenses have been confessed in the midst of the Saṅgha by the method of covering with grass, setting aside grave offenses and setting aside offenses connected with laypeople. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.

“Athāparesaṃ…pe… evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Then for the others... and so on... Thus I hold this.

“Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Kena vūpasantaṃ? Sammukhāvinayena ca, tiṇavatthārakena ca. Kiñca tattha sammukhāvinayasmiṃ? Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā.

Monks, this is called a settled legal issue. By what is it settled? By the procedure-in-the-presence and by the covering with grass. And what therein constitutes the procedure-in-the-presence? The presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the person.

“Kā ca tattha saṅghasammukhatā? Yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – ayaṃ tattha saṅghasammukhatā.

And what therein is the presence of the Saṅgha? As many monks as are fit for the formal act have come, the consent of those worthy of giving consent has been brought, and those who are present do not object—this therein is the presence of the Saṅgha.

“Kā [M 0.0238] ca tattha dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā? Yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati – ayaṃ tattha dhammasammukhatā[P 2.0104], vinayasammukhatā.

And what therein is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya? By whatever Dhamma, by whatever Vinaya, by whatever teaching of the Teacher that legal issue is settled—this therein is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya.

“Kā ca tattha puggalasammukhatā? Yo ca deseti, yassa ca deseti, ubho sammukhībhūtā honti – ayaṃ tattha puggalasammukhatā.

And what, among these, is the presence of the individual? The monk who confesses and the one to whom he confesses, both are present face-to-face. This, among these, is the presence of the individual.

“Kiñca tattha tiṇavatthārakasmiṃ? Yā tiṇavatthārakassa kammassa kiriyā karaṇaṃ upagamanaṃ ajjhupagamanaṃ adhivāsanā appaṭikkosanā – idaṃ tattha tiṇavatthārakasmiṃ. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ ce, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇaṃ paṭiggāhako ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ; chandadāyako khīyati, khīyanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

And what, in this case, is the procedure of covering with grass? Whatever is the acting, the doing, the approaching, the undertaking, the acceptance, the non-rejection of the formal act of covering with grass—this, in this case, is the procedure of covering with grass. If, monks, a legal issue thus settled is re-opened by one who accepted it, there is a pācittiya offense for re-opening. If the one who gave consent complains, there is a pācittiya offense for complaining.

pari. 295, 307, 308 “Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ ekena samathena sammati – sammukhāvinayenā”ti.

By how many settlements is a legal issue concerning duties settled? A legal issue concerning duties is settled by one settlement: by the procedure-in-the-presence.

Samathakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth Chapter on Settlements is finished.

5. Khuddakavatthukkhandhakaṃ

5. The Chapter on Minor Matters

Khuddakavatthūni

Minor Matters

243. Tena [T 2.0001][P 2.0105][M 0.0239][V 0.0221] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nahāyamānā rukkhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsenti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā nahāyamānā rukkhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsessanti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi, seyyathāpi mallamuṭṭhikā gāmamoddavā”ti gāmapoddavā (sī.), gāmapūtavā (syā.)! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nahāyamānā rukkhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsenti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave[T 2.0002], tesaṃ moghapurisānaṃ ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā nahāyamānā rukkhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsessanti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi? Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, nahāyamānena bhikkhunā rukkhe kāyo ugghaṃsetabbo. Yo ugghaṃseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

243. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, while bathing, rubbed their bodies against a tree—their thighs, arms, chests, and backs. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: 'How indeed can the Sakyan ascetics, while bathing, rub their bodies against a tree—their thighs, arms, chests, and backs—just like wrestlers and village dandies!' The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, had the Saṅgha of monks assembled and questioned the monks: 'Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six monks, while bathing, rub their bodies against a tree—their thighs, arms, chests, and backs?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: 'This is unsuitable, monks, for those foolish men, inappropriate, unbecoming, not the conduct of an ascetic, improper, and not to be done. How indeed, monks, can those foolish men, while bathing, rub their bodies against a tree—their thighs, arms, chests, and backs? This, monks, is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident… Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, a monk who is bathing should not rub his body against a tree. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nahāyamānā thambhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsenti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā nahāyamānā thambhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsessanti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi, seyyathāpi mallamuṭṭhikā gāmamoddavā”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ [V 0.0222] khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, nahāyamānena bhikkhunā thambhe kāyo ugghaṃsetabbo. Yo ugghaṃseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks, while bathing, rubbed their bodies against a pillar—their thighs, their arms, their chests, and their backs. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the Sakyan ascetics, while bathing, rub their bodies against a pillar—their thighs, their arms, their chests, and their backs—just like wrestlers and village dandies!” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a monk who is bathing should not rub his body against a pillar. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena [M 0.0240] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nahāyamānā kuṭṭe kuḍḍe (sī. syā.) kāyaṃ ugghaṃsenti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā [T 2.0003] nahāyamānā kuṭṭe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsessanti, ūrumpi bāhumpi urampi piṭṭhimpi, seyyathāpi mallamuṭṭhikā gāmamoddavā”ti…pe… “na, bhikkhave, nahāyamānena bhikkhunā kuṭṭe kāyo ugghaṃsetabbo. Yo ugghaṃseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six, while bathing, rubbed their bodies against a wall—their thighs, their arms, their chests, and their backs. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, while bathing, rub their bodies against a wall—their thighs, their arms, their chests, and their backs—just like wrestlers and villagers who are fond of adornments!”… “Monks, a monk while bathing should not rub his body against a wall. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū aṭṭāne aṭṭhāne (sī. syā.) nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti[P 2.0106]! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, aṭṭāne nahāyitabbaṃ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six bathed at a rubbing post. People complained, criticized, and spread it about… “just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, one should not bathe at a rubbing post. Whoever should bathe there, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū gandhabbahatthakena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “na, bhikkhave, gandhabbahatthakena nahāyitabbaṃ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks bathed with a wooden hand. People complained, criticized, and spread it about... 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Monks, one should not bathe with a wooden hand. Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kuruvindakasuttiyā nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti [V 0.0223] khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi [T 2.0004] gihī kāmabhoginoti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, kuruvindakasuttiyā nahāyitabbaṃ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks bathed with a ball of ruby-dust powder. People complained, criticized, and spread it about... 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one should not bathe with a ball of ruby-dust powder. Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū viggayha parikammaṃ kārāpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, viggayha parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks had their bodies scrubbed by rubbing against each other. People complained, criticized, and spread it about... 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one should not have one's body scrubbed by rubbing against another. Whoever should have it done commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena [M 0.0241] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mallakena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, mallakena nahāyitabbaṃ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks bathed with a serrated scrubbing bowl. People complained, criticized, and spread it about... 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one should not bathe with a serrated scrubbing bowl. Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

244. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno kacchurogābādho hoti. Na tassa vinā mallakena phāsu hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa akatamallaka”nti.

244. At that time, a certain monk had a disease of severe scabies. He was not comfortable without a scrubbing bowl. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, for one who is sick, I allow a plain scrubbing bowl.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu jarādubbalo nahāyamāno na sakkoti attano kāyaṃ ugghaṃsetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [T 2.0005] ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ukkāsika”nti.

At that time, a certain monk, being weak due to old age, was unable to scrub his own body while bathing. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a twisted bathing cloth.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū piṭṭhiparikammaṃ kātuṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puthupāṇika”nti.

At that time, the monks were scrupulous about performing a back rubbing. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O monks, rubbing with the heel of the hand.'

245. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vallikaṃ dhārenti…pe… pāmaṅgaṃ dhārenti…pe… kaṇṭhasuttakaṃ dhārenti…pe… kaṭisuttakaṃ dhārenti…pe… ovaṭṭikaṃ dhārenti…pe… kāyuraṃ dhārenti…pe… hatthābharaṇaṃ dhārenti…pe… aṅgulimuddikaṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vallikaṃ dhārenti…pe… pāmaṅgaṃ dhārenti, kaṇṭhasuttakaṃ dhārenti, kaṭisuttakaṃ dhārenti, ovaṭṭikaṃ dhārenti, kāyuraṃ dhārenti, hatthābharaṇaṃ dhārenti, aṅgulimuddikaṃ dhārentī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, vallikā dhāretabbā…pe… na pāmaṅgo dhāretabbo… na kaṇṭhasuttakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ… na [V 0.0224] kaṭisuttakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ… na ovaṭṭikaṃ dhāretabbaṃ… na kāyuraṃ dhāretabbaṃ… na hatthābharaṇaṃ dhāretabbaṃ… na aṅgulimuddikā [T 2.0006] dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

245. At that time, the group-of-six monks wore ear-ornaments... they wore head ornaments... they wore neck-thread ornaments... they wore waist-threads... they wore bracelets... they wore anklets... they wore hand-ornaments... they wore finger-rings. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Is it true, it is said, O monks, that the group-of-six monks wear ear-ornaments... wear head ornaments, wear neck-thread ornaments, wear waist-threads, wear bracelets, wear anklets, wear hand-ornaments, and wear finger-rings?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' ... Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'O monks, an ear-ornament is not to be worn... a head ornament is not to be worn... a neck-thread ornament is not to be worn... a waist-thread is not to be worn... a bracelet is not to be worn... an anklet is not to be worn... a hand-ornament is not to be worn... a finger-ring is not to be worn. Whoever should wear one, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

246. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā [P 2.0107] bhikkhū dīghe kese dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, dīghā kesā [M 0.0242] dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dumāsikaṃ vā duvaṅgulaṃ vā”ti.

246. At that time, the group-of-six monks kept their hair long. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'O monks, long hair is not to be kept. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, O monks, hair of two months' growth or of two finger-breadths.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kocchena kese osaṇṭhenti osaṇhenti (sī. syā.) …pe… phaṇakena kese osaṇṭhenti, hatthaphaṇakena kese osaṇṭhenti, sitthatelakena kese osaṇṭhenti, udakatelakena kese osaṇṭhenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, kocchena kesā osaṇṭhetabbā…pe… na sitthatelakena kesā osaṇṭhetabbā… na udakatelakena kesā osaṇṭhetabbā. Yo osaṇṭheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were combing their hair with a boar's bristle brush... with a comb, with the hand as a comb, with beeswax oil, and with oil mixed with water. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, hair is not to be combed with a boar's bristle brush... hair is not to be combed with beeswax oil... hair is not to be combed with oil mixed with water. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

247. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ādāsepi udakapattepi mukhanimittaṃ olokenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ādāse vā udakapatte vā mukhanimittaṃ oloketabbaṃ. Yo olokeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

247. At that time, the monks of the group of six were looking at the reflection of their faces in mirrors and in water bowls. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the reflection of the face is not to be looked at in a mirror or in a water bowl. Whoever should look commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena [T 2.0007] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno mukhe vaṇo hoti. So bhikkhū pucchi – “kīdiso me, āvuso, vaṇo”ti? Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “ediso te, āvuso vaṇo”ti. So na saddahati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā ādāse vā udakapatte vā mukhanimittaṃ oloketu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk had a sore on his face. He asked the monks, 'Friends, what kind of sore do I have?' The monks replied, 'Friend, you have a sore of such a kind.' He did not believe them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, on account of illness, I allow looking at the reflection of the face in a mirror or in a water bowl.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mukhaṃ ālimpanti…pe… mukhaṃ ummaddenti, mukhaṃ cuṇṇenti, manosilikāya mukhaṃ lañchenti, aṅgarāgaṃ karonti, mukharāgaṃ karonti, aṅgarāgamukharāgaṃ karonti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, mukhaṃ ālimpitabbaṃ…pe… na mukhaṃ ummadditabbaṃ, na mukhaṃ cuṇṇetabbaṃ, na manosilikāya mukhaṃ lañchetabbaṃ, na aṅgarāgo kātabbo, na mukharāgo kātabbo[V 0.0225], na aṅgarāgamukharāgo kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were anointing their faces... massaging their faces, powdering their faces, making marks on their faces with red arsenic, applying coloring to their limbs, applying coloring to their lips, and applying both coloring to their limbs and coloring to their lips. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the face should not be anointed... the face should not be massaged, the face should not be powdered, marks should not be made on the face with red arsenic, coloring of the limbs should not be done, coloring of the lips should not be done, and both coloring of the limbs and coloring of the lips should not be done. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena [M 0.0243] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno cakkhurogābādho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā mukhaṃ ālimpitu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk was afflicted with an eye disease. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the face to be anointed on account of illness.'

248. Tena [T 2.0008] kho pana samayena rājagahe giraggasamajjo samajjā (abhidhānaganthesu) hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū giraggasamajjaṃ dassanāya agamaṃsu. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā naccampi gītampi vāditampi dassanāya [P 2.0108] gacchissanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, naccaṃ vā gītaṃ vā vāditaṃ vā dassanāya gantabbaṃ. Yo gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

248. At that time, there was a mountain-top festival in Rājagaha. The monks of the group of six went to see the mountain-top festival. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'How indeed can Sakyan recluses go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music, just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one should not go to see dancing, singing, or instrumental music. Whoever should go, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

249. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṃ gāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yatheva yathā ca (ka.) mayaṃ gāyāma, evamevime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṃ gāyantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṃ gāyissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṃ gāyantassa. Attanāpi tasmiṃ sare sārajjati, parepi tasmiṃ sare sārajjanti, gahapatikāpi ujjhāyanti, sarakuttimpi nikāmayamānassa [T 2.0009] samādhissa bhaṅgo hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjati – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṃ gāyantassa. Na, bhikkhave, āyatakena gītassarena dhammo gāyitabbo. Yo gāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

249. At that time, the monks of the group of six were singing the Dhamma with drawn-out musical tones. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'Just as we sing, so too do these Sakyan recluses sing the Dhamma with drawn-out musical tones!' The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'How could the monks of the group of six sing the Dhamma with drawn-out musical tones?' Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One. 'Is it true, monks, that…?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' … Having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, there are these five drawbacks for one who sings the Dhamma with drawn-out musical tones. One becomes attached to that sound oneself; others also become attached to that sound; householders complain; for one desiring to embellish the voice, there is a break in concentration; and later generations imitate what they have seen. These, monks, are the five drawbacks for one who sings the Dhamma with drawn-out musical tones. Monks, the Dhamma should not be sung with drawn-out musical tones. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sarabhaññe kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sarabhañña”nti.

At that time, the monks were scrupulous about chanting with intonation. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow chanting with intonation.'

“Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bāhiralomiṃ bāhiyalomiṃ (ka.) uṇṇiṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti [V 0.0226] khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti[M 0.0244]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bāhiyalomi uṇṇi dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six wore a woolen garment with the fleece on the outside. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a woolen garment with the fleece on the outside should not be worn. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

250. Tena kho pana samayena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa ārāme ambā phalino honti. Raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena anuññātaṃ hoti – “yathāsukhaṃ ayyā ambaṃ paribhuñjantū”ti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū taruṇaññeva ambaṃ pātāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsu. Rañño ca māgadhassa [P 2.0109] seniyassa bimbisārassa ambena attho hoti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro manusse āṇāpesi – “gacchatha, bhaṇe, ārāmaṃ gantvā ambaṃ āharathā”ti[T 2.0010]. “Evaṃ devā”ti kho te manussā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paṭissutvā ārāmaṃ gantvā ārāmapālaṃ etadavocuṃ – “devassa, bhaṇe, ambena attho, ambaṃ dethā”ti. “Natthāyyā ambaṃ. Taruṇaññeva ambaṃ pātāpetvā bhikkhū paribhuñjiṃsū”ti. Atha kho te manussā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Suparibhuttaṃ, bhaṇe, ayyehi ambaṃ, api ca bhagavatā mattā vaṇṇitā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na mattaṃ jānitvā rañño ambaṃ paribhuñjissantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ambaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

250. Now at that time, in the park of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, the mango trees were bearing fruit. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had given permission, saying: “May the venerable sirs partake of the mangoes as they please.” The group-of-six monks had unripe mangoes knocked down and partook of them. Now King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had need of mangoes. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha commanded his men: “Go, sirs, go to the park and bring mangoes.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” those men replied to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, and having gone to the park, they said this to the park-keeper: “Sir, the king has need of mangoes; give us mangoes.” “Sirs, there are no mangoes. The monks had unripe mangoes knocked down and partook of them.” Then those men reported this matter to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. He said: “Sirs, the mangoes have been well partaken of by the venerable sirs; however, the Blessed One has praised moderation.” The people complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying: “How indeed could the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, not knowing moderation, partake of the king’s mangoes?” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and disparaging. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, mangoes are not to be partaken of. Whoever should partake of them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti. Sūpe ambapesikāyo pakkhittā honti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nappaṭiggaṇhanti. “Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ambapesika”nti.

At that time, a certain association was providing a meal for the Sangha. Mango slices had been put into the curry. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept it. “Accept it, monks, and partake of it. Monks, I allow mango slices.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti. Te na pariyāpuṇiṃsu ambapesikaṃ kātuṃ, bhattagge sakaleheva ambehi denti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nappaṭiggaṇhanti. “Paṭiggaṇhatha[T 2.0011], bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṃ paribhuñjituṃ – aggiparicitaṃ[M 0.0245], satthaparicitaṃ, nakhaparicitaṃ, abījaṃ, nibbattabījaññeva nibbaṭṭabījaṃ (sī. syā.) pañcamaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṃ paribhuñjitu”nti.

At that time, a certain association had a meal for the Sangha. They were not able to prepare mango slices, so they gave whole mangoes in the dining hall. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept them. “Accept them, monks, and consume them. Monks, I allow the consumption of fruit by five means suitable for recluses: that which has been treated with fire, that which has been marked with a knife, that which has been marked with a fingernail, that which has immature seeds, and fifth, that from which the seed has been removed. Monks, I allow the consumption of fruit by these five means suitable for recluses.”

251. Tena [V 0.0227] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅkato hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na hi nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phari. Sace hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phareyya, na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅkareyya. Katamāni cattāri ahirājakulāni? Virūpakkhaṃ ahirājakulaṃ, erāpathaṃ ahirājakulaṃ, chabyāputtaṃ ahirājakulaṃ, kaṇhāgotamaṃ ahirājakulaṃ[P 2.0110]. Na hi nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phari. Sace hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phareyya, na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅkareyya. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena pharituṃ, attaguttiyā attarakkhāya attaparittaṃ kātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ –

251. Now at that time a certain monk, bitten by a snake, had died. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Surely, monks, that monk did not pervade these four royal families of snakes with a mind of loving-kindness. For if, monks, that monk had pervaded these four royal families of snakes with a mind of loving-kindness, that monk would not have died from being bitten by a snake. What are the four royal families of snakes? The royal family of snakes Virūpakkha, the royal family of snakes Erāpatha, the royal family of snakes Chabyāputta, and the royal family of snakes Kaṇhāgotama. Surely, monks, that monk did not pervade these four royal families of snakes with a mind of loving-kindness. For if, monks, that monk had pervaded these four royal families of snakes with a mind of loving-kindness, that monk would not have died from being bitten by a snake. Monks, I allow you to pervade these four royal families of snakes with a mind of loving-kindness, for your own security, for your own protection, and to make a protective charm for yourselves. And, monks, it should be done in this way:

jā. 1.2.105-106; a. ni. 4.67 idaṃ vatthu āgataṃ “Virūpakkhehi me mettaṃ, mettaṃ erāpathehi me;

Chabyāputtehi me mettaṃ, mettaṃ kaṇhāgotamakehi ca.

“My loving-kindness is with the Virūpakkhas, with the Erāpathas is my loving-kindness; my loving-kindness is with the Chabyāputtas, and with the Kaṇhāgotamakas.”

“Apādakehi [T 2.0012] me mettaṃ, mettaṃ dvipādakehi me;

Catuppadehi me mettaṃ, mettaṃ bahuppadehi me.

“My loving-kindness is with the footless, with the two-footed is my loving-kindness; my loving-kindness is with the four-footed, with the many-footed is my loving-kindness.”

“Mā maṃ apādako hiṃsi, mā maṃ hiṃsi dvipādako;

Mā maṃ catuppado hiṃsi, mā maṃ hiṃsi bahuppado.

“May a footless being not harm me, may a two-footed being not harm me; may a four-footed being not harm me, may a many-footed being not harm me.”

“Sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā, sabbe bhūtā ca kevalā;

Sabbe bhadrāni passantu, mā kiñci pāpamāgamā.

“May all beings, all living things, all creatures without exception, may they all see good things; may no evil come to any being whatsoever.”

“Appamāṇo buddho, appamāṇo dhammo,

Appamāṇo saṅgho, pamāṇavantāni sarīsapāni siriṃsapāni (sī. syā.).

“Immeasurable is the Buddha, immeasurable is the Dhamma, immeasurable is the Sangha. Measurable are creeping things:

“Ahi vicchikā satapadī, uṇṇanābhi sarabū mūsikā;

Katā me rakkhā kataṃ me parittaṃ, paṭikkamantu bhūtāni.

snakes, scorpions, centipedes, spiders, lizards, and mice. Protection has been made by me, a safeguard has been made by me. May the beings depart.”

“Sohaṃ [V 0.0228] namo bhagavato, namo sattannaṃ sammāsambuddhāna”nti.

“I pay homage to the Blessed One, I pay homage to the seven Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones.”

Tena [M 0.0246] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu anabhiratiyā pīḷito attano aṅgajātaṃ chindi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Aññamhi so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso chetabbamhi, aññaṃ chindi. Na, bhikkhave, attano aṅgajātaṃ chetabbaṃ. Yo chindeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

Now at that time, a certain monk, being afflicted by discontent, cut off his own sexual organ. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, that worthless man, when another thing should have been cut off, cut off something else. Monks, one's own sexual organ is not to be cut off. Whoever should cut it off, commits a grave offense.”

252. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa mahagghassa candanassa candanasārassa (sī. syā.) candanagaṇṭhi uppannā hoti. Atha kho rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa [T 2.0013] etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāya candanagaṇṭhiyā pattaṃ lekhāpeyyaṃ. Lekhañca me paribhogaṃ bhavissati, pattañca dānaṃ dassāmī”ti. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhi tāya candanagaṇṭhiyā pattaṃ lekhāpetvā sikkāya uḍḍitvā vāhitvā (sī.) veḷagge ālaggetvā veḷuparamparāya bandhitvā vāhitvā (syā.) evamāha – “yo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā arahā ceva iddhimā ca dinnaṃyeva pattaṃ oharatū”ti. Atha kho pūraṇo [P 2.0111] kassapo yena rājagahako seṭṭhi tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājagahakaṃ seṭṭhiṃ etadavoca – “ahañhi, gahapati, arahā ceva iddhimā ca, dehi me patta”nti. “Sace, bhante, āyasmā arahā ceva iddhimā ca dinnaṃyeva pattaṃ oharatū”ti. Atha kho makkhali gosālo… ajito kesakambalo… pakudho kaccāyano… sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto sañjayo bellaṭṭhiputto (sī.) … nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto nāthaputto (sī.) yena rājagahako seṭṭhi tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājagahakaṃ seṭṭhiṃ etadavoca – “ahañhi, gahapati, arahā ceva iddhimā ca, dehi me patta”nti. “Sace, bhante, āyasmā arahā ceva iddhimā ca, dinnaṃyeva pattaṃ oharatū”ti.

252. At that time, a very valuable block of sandalwood had come into the possession of the merchant of Rājagaha. Then this thought occurred to the merchant of Rājagaha: “Indeed, I should have a bowl turned from this block of sandalwood. The shavings will be for my use, and I will also give the bowl as a gift.” Then the merchant of Rājagaha, having had a bowl turned from that block of sandalwood, placed it in a carrying net, hung it on the tip of a bamboo, and fastened it up high with a succession of bamboos, saying: “Whatever ascetic or brahmin is both an Arahant and possesses psychic power, let him bring down the bowl that has already been given.” Then Pūraṇa Kassapa approached the merchant of Rājagaha and said to him: “I, householder, am indeed both an Arahant and possess psychic power. Give me the bowl.” “If, venerable sir, you are both an Arahant and possess psychic power, then bring down the bowl that has already been given.” Then Makkhali Gosāla… Ajita Kesakambala… Pakudha Kaccāyana… Sañcaya Belaṭṭhaputta… Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta approached the merchant of Rājagaha and said to him: “I, householder, am indeed both an Arahant and possess psychic power. Give me the bowl.” “If, venerable sir, you are both an Arahant and possess psychic power, then bring down the bowl that has already been given.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā [T 2.0014] ca piṇḍolabhāradvājo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “āyasmā kho mahāmoggallāno arahā ceva iddhimā ca. Gacchāvuso, moggallāna, etaṃ pattaṃ ohara. Tuyheso patto”ti. “Āyasmā kho bhāradvājo arahā ceva iddhimā ca. Gacchāvuso, bhāradvāja, etaṃ pattaṃ ohara. Tuyheso patto”ti. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā taṃ pattaṃ gahetvā tikkhattuṃ rājagahaṃ anupariyāyi.

At that time, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, having dressed in the morning and taken their bowls and robes, entered Rājagaha for alms-food. Then the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: “Indeed, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna is both an Arahant and possesses psychic power. Go, friend Moggallāna, bring down this bowl. This is your bowl.” “Indeed, the Venerable Bhāradvāja is both an Arahant and possesses psychic power. Go, friend Bhāradvāja, bring down this bowl. This is your bowl.” Then the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, having risen up into the air, took that bowl and circled Rājagaha three times.

Tena [M 0.0247] kho pana samayena rājagahako seṭṭhi saputtadāro sake nivesane ṭhito hoti pañjaliko [V 0.0229] namassamāno – idheva, bhante, ayyo bhāradvājo amhākaṃ nivesane patiṭṭhātūti. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa nivesane patiṭṭhāsi. Atha [T 2.0015] kho rājagahako seṭṭhi āyasmato piṇḍolabhāradvājassa hatthato pattaṃ gahetvā mahagghassa khādanīyassa pūretvā āyasmato piṇḍolabhāradvājassa adāsi. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo taṃ pattaṃ gahetvā ārāmaṃ agamāsi. Assosuṃ kho manussā – ayyena kira piṇḍolabhāradvājena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohāritoti. Te ca manussā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā āyasmantaṃ piṇḍolabhāradvājaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhiṃsu.

At that time, the merchant of Rājagaha, together with his wife and children, was standing in his own residence with hands reverently joined, paying homage, saying: “Venerable sir, may the noble Bhāradvāja alight right here in our residence.” Then the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja alighted in the residence of the merchant of Rājagaha. Then the merchant of Rājagaha took the bowl from the hand of the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, filled it with valuable edibles, and offered it to the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja. Then the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, having taken that bowl, went to the monastery. The people heard: “It is said that the bowl of the merchant of Rājagaha was brought down by the noble Piṇḍolabhāradvāja.” And those people, with loud and great shouts, followed the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja from behind.

Assesi kho bhagavā uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ; sutvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, ānanda, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo”ti? “Āyasmatā, bhante, piṇḍolabhāradvājena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohārito. Assosuṃ kho, bhante, manussā – ayyena kira piṇḍolabhāradvājena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohāritoti. Te ca, bhante, manussā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā āyasmantaṃ piṇḍolabhāradvājaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā. So eso, bhante, bhagavā uccāsaddo mahāsaddo”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṃ [P 2.0112] piṇḍolabhāradvājaṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tayā, bhāradvāja, rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohārito”ti? “Saccaṃ [T 2.0016] bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhāradvāja, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, bhāradvāja, chavassa dārupattassa kāraṇā gihīnaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassessasi! Seyyathāpi, bhāradvāja, mātugāmo chavassa māsakarūpassa kāraṇā kopinaṃ dasseti, evameva kho tayā, bhāradvāja, chavassa dārupattassa kāraṇā gihīnaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassitaṃ. Netaṃ, bhāradvāja, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, gihīnaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetabbaṃ. Yo dasseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bhindathetaṃ, bhikkhave, dārupattaṃ sakalikaṃ sakalikaṃ katvā[M 0.0248], bhikkhūnaṃ añjanupapisanaṃ detha. Na ca, bhikkhave, dārupatto dhāretabbo. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

The Blessed One heard a loud and great noise. Having heard it, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “What, Ānanda, is that loud and great noise?” “Venerable sir, the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja has brought down the bowl belonging to the merchant of Rājagaha. People heard, venerable sir, that the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja had brought down the bowl belonging to the merchant of Rājagaha. Those people, venerable sir, are making a loud and great noise, following the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja from behind. That, venerable sir, is the loud and great noise.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, had the Sangha of monks assembled and questioned the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja: “Is it true, it is said, Bhāradvāja, that you brought down the bowl belonging to the merchant of Rājagaha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “It is improper, Bhāradvāja, unsuitable, unbecoming, unworthy of an ascetic, not allowable, not to be done. How could you, Bhāradvāja, for the sake of a worthless wooden bowl, display a superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power to householders! Just as, Bhāradvāja, a woman might expose her private parts for the sake of a worthless copper coin, so too, Bhāradvāja, you have displayed a superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power to householders for the sake of a worthless wooden bowl. This, Bhāradvāja, does not lead to faith in those without it… Having rebuked him… he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks: “Monks, one should not display a superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power to householders. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong conduct. Break this wooden bowl, monks, into small pieces, and give them to the monks for grinding ointment. And monks, a wooden bowl should not be kept. Whoever keeps one commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace patte dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, sovaṇṇamayo patto dhāretabbo…pe… na rūpiyamayo [V 0.0230] patto dhāretabbo… na maṇimayo patto dhāretabbo… na veḷuriyamayo patto dhāretabbo… na phalikamayo patto dhāretabbo… na kaṃsamayo patto dhāretabbo… na [T 2.0017] kācamayo patto dhāretabbo… na tipumayo patto dhāretabbo… na sīsamayo patto dhāretabbo… na tambalohamayo patto dhāretabbo. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve patte – ayopattaṃ, mattikāpatta”nti.

At that time the monks of the group of six used various kinds of bowls—golden and silver. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a golden bowl should not be used, a silver bowl should not be used, a jeweled bowl should not be used, a beryl bowl should not be used, a crystal bowl should not be used, a bronze bowl should not be used, a glass bowl should not be used, a tin bowl should not be used, a lead bowl should not be used, nor should a copper bowl be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, two bowls: an iron bowl and a clay bowl.”

253. Tena kho pana samayena pattamūlaṃ ghaṃsiyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattamaṇḍala”nti.

253. At that time, the base of a bowl was being worn away. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, a bowl-ring.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhāretabbāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve pattamaṇḍalāni – tipumayaṃ, sīsamaya”nti. Bahalāni maṇḍalāni na acchupiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, likhitu”nti. Valī calī (ka.) honti[P 2.0113]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, makaradantakaṃ chinditu”nti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six used various kinds of bowl-rings—golden and silver. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of bowl-rings should not be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, two bowl-rings: one of tin and one of lead.” The thick rings could not be handled properly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, for them to be scraped.” Ridges formed. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, for the ‘makara-tooth’ to be cut off.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū citrāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhārenti rūpakākiṇṇāni bhittikammakatāni. Tāni rathikāyapi dassentā āhiṇḍanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [T 2.0018] ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, citrāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhāretabbāni rūpakākiṇṇāni bhittikammakatāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pakatimaṇḍala”nti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six used ornate bowl-rings, filled with figures and decorated with mural-like work. They wandered about, displaying them even on the main road. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, ornate bowl-rings, filled with figures and decorated with mural-like work, are not to be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, a plain bowl-ring.”

254. Tena [M 0.0249] kho pana samayena bhikkhū sodakaṃ pattaṃ paṭisāmenti. Patto dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, sodako patto paṭisāmetabbo. Yo paṭisāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, otāpetvā pattaṃ paṭisāmetu”nti.

254. At that time, monks were putting away a bowl with water in it. The bowl was spoiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bowl with water in it is not to be put away. Whoever should put one away, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to put away a bowl after drying it in the sun.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sodakaṃ saudakaṃ (ka.) pattaṃ otāpenti. Patto duggandho hoti. Bhagavato [V 0.0231] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, sodako patto otāpetabbo. Yo otāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vodakaṃ katvā otāpetvā pattaṃ paṭisāmetu”nti.

At that time, monks were drying a bowl with water in it in the sun. The bowl became foul-smelling. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bowl with water in it is not to be dried in the sun. Whoever should dry one, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to put away a bowl after making it waterless and drying it in the sun.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū uṇhe pattaṃ nidahanti. Pattassa vaṇṇo dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Yo nidaheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetvā pattaṃ paṭisāmetu”nti.

At that time, monks were placing a bowl in the sun. The bowl’s color was spoiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bowl is not to be placed in the sun. Whoever should place one there, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to put away a bowl after drying it briefly in the sun.”

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā pattā ajjhokāse anādhārā nikkhittā honti. Vātamaṇḍalikāya āvaṭṭetvā pattā bhijjiṃsu[T 2.0019]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattādhāraka”nti.

At that time, many bowls were placed in an open space without support. Having been tumbled by a whirlwind, the bowls broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, a bowl-support.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū miḍḍhante pattaṃ nikkhipanti. Paripatitvā parivaṭṭitvā (syā.) patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, miḍḍhante patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were placing their bowls at the edge of an inner wall. The bowl fell and broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bowl is not to be placed at the edge of an inner wall. Whoever should place one there commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū paribhaṇḍante pattaṃ nikkhipanti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, paribhaṇḍante patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were placing their bowls at the edge of an outer wall. The bowl fell and broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bowl is not to be placed at the edge of an outer wall. Whoever should place one there commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chamāya pattaṃ nikkujjanti. Oṭṭho ghaṃsiyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthāraka”nti. Tiṇasanthārako upacikāhi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, coḷaka”nti. Coḷakaṃ upacikāhi khajjati. Bhagavato [P 2.0114] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattamāḷaka”nti. Pattamāḷako paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [M 0.0250] ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattakuṇḍolika”nti. Pattakuṇḍolikāya patto ghaṃsiyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattathavika”nti[T 2.0020]. Aṃsabaddhako na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṃsabaddhakaṃ bandhanasuttaka”nti.

At that time, monks were placing their bowls upside down on the ground. The rim was getting worn. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a grass mat.” The grass mat was eaten by termites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a piece of cloth.” The piece of cloth was eaten by termites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a bowl-stand.” The bowl-stand fell over, and the bowl broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a bowl-pot.” The bowl was getting worn by the bowl-pot. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a bowl-bag.” There was no shoulder strap.
