They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a shoulder strap and a tying cord.”

Tena [V 0.0232] kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhittikhilepi nāgadantakepi pattaṃ laggenti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, patto laggetabbo. Yo laggeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were hanging their bowls on wall-pegs and on elephant-tusk pegs. The bowl fell and broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bowl is not to be hung. Whoever should hang one commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañce pattaṃ nikkhipanti, satisammosā nisīdantā ottharitvā pattaṃ bhindenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, mañce patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus were placing their bowls on a couch; sitting down unmindfully, they crushed and broke the bowls. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a bowl is not to be placed on a couch. Whoever should place it there, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū pīṭhe pattaṃ nikkhipanti, satisammosā nisīdantā ottharitvā pattaṃ bhindenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, pīṭhe patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus were placing their bowls on stools; sitting down unmindfully, they crushed and broke them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a bowl is not to be placed on a stool. Whoever should place it there, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū aṅke pattaṃ nikkhipanti, satisammosā uṭṭhahanti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, aṅke patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus were placing their bowls on their laps, and being unmindful, they would get up. The bowl would fall and break. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a bowl is not to be placed on the lap. Whoever should place it there, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chatte pattaṃ nikkhipanti. Vātamaṇḍalikāya chattaṃ ukkhipiyati paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato [T 2.0021] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, chatte patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus placed their bowls on sunshades. A whirlwind lifted the sunshade, and the bowl fell and broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a bowl is not to be placed on a sunshade. Whoever should place it there, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

255. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū pattahatthā kavāṭaṃ paṇāmenti. Kavāṭo āvaṭṭitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, pattahatthena kavāṭaṃ paṇāmetabbaṃ kavāṭo paṇāmetabbo (ka.). Yo paṇāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

255. At that time, bhikkhus, with bowls in hand, were pushing a door-leaf. The door-leaf swung around, and the bowl broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a door-leaf is not to be pushed by one with a bowl in hand. Whoever should push it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena [M 0.0251] kho pana samayena bhikkhū tumbakaṭāhe piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, tumbakaṭāhe piṇḍāya caritabbaṃ. Yo careyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus were going about for alms with gourd-bowls. People complained, grumbled, and disparaged them, saying: 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to go about for alms with a gourd-bowl. Whoever should go about, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ghaṭikaṭāhe [P 2.0115] ghaṭikaṭāhena (syā.) piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [V 0.0233] vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ghaṭikaṭāhe piṇḍāya caritabbaṃ. Yo careyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus were going for alms with earthenware bowls. People complained, grumbled, and disparaged them, saying: 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to go for alms with an earthenware bowl. Whoever should go about, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sabbapaṃsukūliko hoti. So chavasīsassa pattaṃ dhāreti. Aññatarā itthī passitvā [T 2.0022] bhītā vissaramakāsi – “abhuṃ me pisāco vatāya”nti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā chavasīsassa pattaṃ dhāressanti, seyyathāpi pisācillikā”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, chavasīsassa patto dhāretabbo. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, sabbapaṃsukūlikena bhavitabbaṃ. Yo bhaveyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhu was one who used only requisites from refuse heaps. He carried a bowl made from a skull. A certain woman saw him and, frightened, cried out, 'Woe is me! This is truly a goblin!' People complained, grumbled, and disparaged them, saying, 'How indeed can these Sakyan ascetics carry a bowl made from a skull, just like goblins?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a bowl made from a skull is not to be carried. Whoever should carry one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, bhikkhus, one is not to be one who uses only requisites from refuse heaps. Whoever should be so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū calakānipi aṭṭhikānipi ucchiṭṭhodakampi pattena nīharanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yasmiṃ yevime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bhuñjanti sova nesaṃ paṭiggaho”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na bhikkhave, calakāni vā aṭṭhikāni vā ucchiṭṭhodakaṃ vā pattena nīharitabbaṃ. Yo nīhareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭiggaha”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus were removing food scraps, bones, and rinsing water with their bowls. People complained, grumbled, and disparaged them, saying, 'The very bowl in which these Sakyan ascetics eat is their spittoon!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, food scraps, bones, or rinsing water are not to be removed with the bowl. Whoever should remove them, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, bhikkhus, a spittoon.'

256. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū hatthena vipphāḷetvā cīvaraṃ sibbenti. Cīvaraṃ vilomikaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, satthakaṃ namataka”nti.

256. At that time, bhikkhus were sewing robes, bunching them up with their hands. The robe became uneven. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, bhikkhus, a small knife and a coarse cloth for wrapping it.'

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa daṇḍasatthakaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, daṇḍasatthaka”nti[T 2.0023].

At that time, a small knife with a handle had arisen for the Sangha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, bhikkhus, a small knife with a handle.'

Tena [M 0.0252] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace satthakadaṇḍe dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā satthakadaṇḍā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ dantamayaṃ visāṇamayaṃ naḷamayaṃ veḷumayaṃ kaṭṭhamayaṃ jatumayaṃ phalamayaṃ lohamayaṃ saṅkhanābhimaya”nti.

At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six carried various kinds of small knife handles, some made of gold and some of silver. People complained, grumbled, and disparaged them, saying: 'Like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, various kinds of small knife handles are not to be carried. Whoever should carry one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, bhikkhus, a handle made of bone, made of ivory, made of horn, made of reed, made of bamboo, made of wood, made of lac, made of fruit, made of metal, or made of conch-shell navel.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kukkuṭapattenapi veḷupesikāyapi cīvaraṃ sibbenti. Cīvaraṃ [V 0.0234] dussibbitaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sūci”nti. Sūciyo kaṇṇakitāyo honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave[P 2.0116], sūcināḷika”nti. Sūcināḷikāyapi kaṇṇakitāyo honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kiṇṇena pūretu”nti. Kiṇṇepi kaṇṇakitāyo honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattuyā pūretu”nti. Sattuyāpi kaṇṇakitāyo honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saritaka”nti. Saritakepi kaṇṇakitāyo honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, madhusitthakena sāretu”nti. Saritakaṃ paribhijjati. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saritakasipāṭika”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus were sewing robes with a chicken feather and with a bamboo sliver. The robe was badly sewn. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow a needle.' The needles became rusty. … 'Bhikkhus, I allow a needle case.' In the needle case too, they became rusty. … 'Bhikkhus, I allow it to be filled with yeast.' In the yeast too, they became rusty. … 'Bhikkhus, I allow it to be filled with flour mixed with turmeric.' In the flour mixed with turmeric too, they became rusty. … 'Bhikkhus, I allow stone powder.' In the stone powder too, they became rusty. … 'Bhikkhus, I allow it to be smeared with beeswax.' The stone powder was damaged. 'Bhikkhus, I allow a bag for the stone powder.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū tattha tattha khilaṃ nikkhaṇitvā sambandhitvā [T 2.0024] cīvaraṃ sibbenti. Cīvaraṃ vikaṇṇaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ kathinarajjuṃ kaṭhinaṃ kaṭhinarajjuṃ (sī. syā.) tattha tattha obandhitvā cīvaraṃ sibbetu”nti. Visame kathinaṃ pattharanti. Kathinaṃ paribhijjati…pe… “na, bhikkhave, visame kathinaṃ pattharitabbaṃ. Yo patthareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus, having driven in stakes here and there and having tied the robe to them, were sewing the robe. The robe became uneven at the corners. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a kaṭhina-frame and a kaṭhina-frame rope in order to sew the robe, having fastened it here and there.” They spread the kaṭhina-frame on uneven ground. The kaṭhina-frame broke. … “Bhikkhus, a kaṭhina-frame is not to be spread on uneven ground. Whoever should spread it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Chamāya kathinaṃ pattharanti. Kathinaṃ paṃsukitaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthāraka”nti. Kathinassa anto jīrati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anuvātaṃ paribhaṇḍaṃ āropetu”nti. Kathinaṃ nappahoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, daṇḍakathinaṃ bidalakaṃ salākaṃ vinandhanarajjuṃ vinandhanasuttaṃ vinandhitvā cīvaraṃ sibbetu”nti. Suttantarikāyo visamā honti…pe… “anujānāmi[M 0.0253], bhikkhave, kaḷimbhaka”nti. Suttā vaṅkā honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, moghasuttaka”nti.

They spread out the kaṭhina-frame on the ground. The kaṭhina-frame became dusty... 'I allow, O monks, a grass mat.' The inside of the kaṭhina-frame wore out... 'I allow, O monks, to attach a lengthwise border and a widthwise border.' The kaṭhina-frame was not sufficient... 'I allow, O monks, a small kaṭhina-frame with a handle, a folding one, a bamboo slip, a binding cord, and a binding thread, and having bound it, to sew the robe.' The spaces between the stitches were uneven... 'I allow, O monks, a measuring guide.' The lines of stitches were crooked... 'I allow, O monks, a marking thread.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū adhotehi pādehi kathinaṃ akkamanti. Kathinaṃ dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, adhotehi pādehi kathinaṃ akkamitabbaṃ. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were stepping on the kaṭhina-frame with unwashed feet. The kaṭhina-frame was damaged. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'O monks, the kaṭhina-frame should not be stepped on with unwashed feet. Should any monk step on it, he incurs an offense of wrongdoing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū allehi pādehi kathinaṃ akkamanti. Kathinaṃ dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na[T 2.0025], bhikkhave, allehi pādehi kathinaṃ akkamitabbaṃ. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were stepping on the kaṭhina-frame with wet feet. The kaṭhina-frame was damaged. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'O monks, the kaṭhina-frame should not be stepped on with wet feet. Should any monk step on it, he incurs an offense of wrongdoing.'

Tena [V 0.0235] kho pana samayena bhikkhū saupāhanā kathinaṃ akkamanti. Kathinaṃ dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, saupāhanena kathinaṃ akkamitabbaṃ. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks, wearing footwear, were stepping on the kaṭhina-frame. The kaṭhina-frame was damaged. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'O monks, the kaṭhina-frame should not be stepped on by one wearing footwear. Should any monk step on it, he incurs an offense of wrongdoing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū cīvaraṃ sibbantā aṅguliyā paṭiggaṇhanti. Aṅguliyo dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭiggaha”nti.

At that time, monks, while sewing a robe, would push the needle with a finger. Their fingers became sore. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O monks, a finger-stall.'

257. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace paṭiggahe dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā [P 2.0117] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā paṭiggahā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ…pe… saṅkhanābhimaya”nti.

257. At that time, the group-of-six monks were using various finger-stalls made of gold and silver. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: 'Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, various finger-stalls are not to be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrongdoing. I allow, monks, those made of bone... of conch-shell nacre.'

Tena kho pana samayena sūciyopi satthakāpi paṭiggahāpi nassanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āvesanavitthaka”nti. Āvesanavitthake samākulā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭiggahathavika”nti. Aṃsabaddhako na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṃsabaddhakaṃ bandhanasuttaka”nti.

At that time, needles, small knives, and finger-stalls were getting lost. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a pouch for implements.' Things became jumbled in the pouch. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a bag for the finger-stall.' There was no shoulder-strap. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a shoulder-strap and a tying string.'

Tena [T 2.0026] kho pana samayena bhikkhū abbhokāse cīvaraṃ sibbantā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinasālaṃ kathinamaṇḍapa”nti. Kathinasālā nīcavatthukā [M 0.0254] hoti, udakena otthariyyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Kathinasālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ogumbetvā (sī. syā.) ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajjuka”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus sewing robes in the open air were exhausted by both cold and heat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O bhikkhus, a kaṭhina hall and a kaṭhina pavilion.' The kaṭhina hall had a low foundation and was flooded with water. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O bhikkhus, that it be made with a high foundation.' The foundation collapsed... 'I allow, O bhikkhus, to build three kinds of foundations: a brick foundation, a stone foundation, and a wood foundation.' Those climbing were wearied... 'I allow, O bhikkhus, three kinds of staircases: a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.' Those climbing fell... 'I allow, O bhikkhus, a handrail.' Chaff fell in the kaṭhina hall... 'I allow, O bhikkhus, having swept it clean, to plaster it inside and out, and to apply white coloring, black coloring, a finish of red ochre, garland-work, creeper-work, makara-tooth carvings, the five-stripes pattern, a robe-bamboo, and a robe-rope.'

Tena [V 0.0236] kho pana samayena bhikkhū cīvaraṃ sibbetvā tattheva kathinaṃ ujjhitvā pakkamanti, undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ saṅgharitu”nti. Kathinaṃ paribhijjati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, goghaṃsikāya kathinaṃ saṅgharitu”nti. Kathinaṃ viniveṭhiyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bandhanarajju”nti[T 2.0027].

At that time, bhikkhus, having sewn the robe, would abandon the kaṭhina frame right there and depart; it was then eaten by rats and termites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O bhikkhus, to fold up the kaṭhina frame.' The kaṭhina frame broke... 'I allow, O bhikkhus, to fold up the kaṭhina frame using a roller-pole.' The kaṭhina frame came unrolled... 'I allow, O bhikkhus, a binding rope.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kuṭṭepi thambhepi kathinaṃ ussāpetvā pakkamanti. Paripatitvā kathinaṃ bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhittikhile vā nāgadante vā laggetu”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus would depart after propping the kaṭhina frame against a wall or a pillar. Having fallen over, the kaṭhina frame would break. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O bhikkhus, to hang it on a wall-peg or on an elephant's-tusk bracket.'

258. Atha kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Tena kho pana samayena [P 2.0118] bhikkhū sūcikampi satthakampi bhesajjampi pattena ādāya gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhesajjatthavika”nti. Aṃsabaddhako na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṃsabaddhakaṃ bandhanasuttaka”nti.

258. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha for as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Vesālī. At that time, monks were traveling carrying a needle, a small knife, and medicine in their bowls. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow a medicine bag.' There was no shoulder strap... He said, 'Monks, I allow a shoulder strap and a tying string.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu upāhanāyo kāyabandhanena bandhitvā gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Aññataro upāsako taṃ bhikkhuṃ abhivādento upāhanāyo sīsena ghaṭṭeti. So bhikkhu maṅku ahosi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upāhanatthavika”nti. Aṃsabaddhako na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṃsabaddhakaṃ bandhanasuttaka”nti.

At that time, a certain monk, having tied his sandals with a waistband, entered a village for alms-food. A certain lay follower, while paying homage to that monk, struck the sandals with his head. That monk became displeased. Then that monk, having gone to the monastery, reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow a sandal bag.' There was no shoulder strap... He said, 'Monks, I allow a shoulder strap and a tying string.'

Tena [M 0.0255] kho pana samayena antarāmagge udakaṃ akappiyaṃ hoti. Parissāvanaṃ na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi[T 2.0028], bhikkhave, parissāvana”nti. Coḷakaṃ nappahoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaṭacchuparissāvana”nti. Coḷakaṃ nappahoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhammakaraṇa”nti dhammakaraṇaṃ (sī. syā.), dhamakaraṇaṃ (ka.).

At that time, water along the road was unsuitable. There was no water strainer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow a water strainer.' A piece of cloth was not sufficient... He said, 'Monks, I allow a tripod strainer.' A piece of cloth was not sufficient... They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow a `dhammakaraṇa` water strainer.'

259. Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Eko bhikkhu anācāraṃ ācarati. Dutiyo bhikkhu taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “mā, āvuso, evarūpaṃ akāsi. Netaṃ kappatī”ti. So tasmiṃ upanandhi. Atha kho so bhikkhu pipāsāya [V 0.0237] pīḷito upanaddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “dehi me, āvuso, parissāvanaṃ, pānīyaṃ pivissāmī”ti. Upanaddho bhikkhu na adāsi. So bhikkhu pipāsāya pīḷito kālamakāsi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, parissāvanaṃ yāciyamāno na adāsī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu parissāvanaṃ yāciyamāno na dassatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, parissāvanaṃ yāciyamāno na adāsī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ [T 2.0029] akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, parissāvanaṃ yāciyamāno na dassasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa[P 2.0119], appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na bhikkhave, addhānamaggappaṭipannena bhikkhunā parissāvanaṃ yāciyamānena na dātabbaṃ. Yo na dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, aparissāvanakena addhāno paṭipajjitabbo. Yo paṭipajjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sace na hoti parissāvanaṃ vā dhammakaraṇo vā, saṅghāṭikaṇṇopi adhiṭṭhātabbo – iminā parissāvetvā pivissāmī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ[M 0.0256]. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṃ karonti. Parissāvanaṃ na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, daṇḍaparissāvana”nti. Daṇḍaparissāvanaṃ na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ottharaka”nti.

259. At that time, two monks were traveling on a long journey in the Kosala country. One monk engaged in improper conduct. The second monk said to him, “Venerable sir, do not do such a thing. This is not allowable.” That monk bore a grudge against him. Then the second monk, being afflicted by thirst, said to the monk who bore a grudge, “Venerable sir, give me the water-strainer; I shall drink water.” The monk who bore a grudge did not give it. The other monk, being afflicted by thirst, passed away. Then the monk who had borne the grudge went to the monastery and informed the monks of this matter. “Venerable sir, when you were asked for the water-strainer, did you not give it?” “It is so, venerable sirs.” Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could a monk, when asked for a water-strainer, not give it!” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having had the community of monks assembled, questioned that monk: “Is it true, it is said, monk, that when asked for the water-strainer, you did not give it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked him: “Worthless man, this is unsuitable, not in accordance, unbecoming, not the conduct of a recluse, not allowable, and not to be done. How indeed could you, worthless man, when asked for a water-strainer, not give it? This, worthless man, does not lead to the confidence of the unconverted…” Having rebuked him and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, by a monk traveling on a long journey, a water-strainer, when asked for, is to be given. Whoever should not give it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, monks, a long journey is not to be undertaken by one without a water-strainer. Whoever should undertake it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. If there is no water-strainer or a water filter, even the corner of the outer robe is to be determined thus: ‘Having strained with this, I shall drink.’” Then the Blessed One, wandering on tour in due course, arrived at Vesālī. There, indeed, the Blessed One was staying in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof. At that time, the monks were doing new work. The water-strainers were not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a stick-strainer.” The stick-strainers were not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a dipping strainer.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū makasehi ubbāḷhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, makasakuṭika”nti.

At that time, the monks were oppressed by mosquitoes. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Monks, I allow a mosquito net.”

260. Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyaṃ paṇītānaṃ bhattānaṃ bhattapaṭipāṭi aṭṭhitā hoti. Bhikkhū paṇītāni bhojanāni bhuñjitvā abhisannakāyā [T 2.0030] honti bahvābādhā bavhābādhā (sī.). Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco vesāliṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Addasā kho jīvako komārabhacco bhikkhū abhisannakāye bahvābādhe. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jīvako komārabhacco [V 0.0238] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “etarahi, bhante, bhikkhū abhisannakāyā bahvābādhā. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ caṅkamañca jantāgharañca anujānātu. Evaṃ bhikkhū appābādhā bhavissantī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, caṅkamañca jantāgharañcā”ti.

260. Now at that time in Vesālī, an established order of excellent food was being provided. The monks, having eaten the excellent foods, became bilious and were afflicted with many ailments. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca went to Vesālī on some business. Jīvaka Komārabhacca saw that the monks were bilious and afflicted with many ailments. Having seen this, he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Jīvaka Komārabhacca said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, at present the monks are bilious and afflicted with many ailments. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would allow the monks a walking path and a steam-bath house. Thus the monks will have fewer ailments.' Then the Blessed One instructed, incited, roused, and gladdened Jīvaka Komārabhacca with a Dhamma talk. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca, having been instructed, incited, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow a walking path and a steam-bath house.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū [P 2.0120] visame caṅkame caṅkamanti. Pādā dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, samaṃ kātu”nti. Caṅkamo nīcavatthuko hoti. Udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo [T 2.0031] paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti.

At that time, monks were walking on an uneven walking path. Their feet hurt. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'I allow, monks, that it be made level.' The walking path was low-lying. It was covered by water... 'I allow, monks, that it be made high-lying.' The embankment collapsed... 'I allow, monks, to build three kinds of embankments—a brick embankment, a stone embankment, and a wooden embankment.' Those ascending were weary... 'I allow, monks, three kinds of staircases—a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.' Those ascending fell... 'I allow, monks, a handrail.'

Tena [M 0.0257] kho pana samayena bhikkhū caṅkame caṅkamantā paripatanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, caṅkamanavedika”nti.

At that time, monks, while walking on the walking path, fell down. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'I allow, monks, a railing for the walking path.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajjhokāse caṅkamantā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, caṅkamanasāla”nti. Caṅkamanasālāyaṃ tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti. Jantāgharaṃ nīcavatthukaṃ hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti[T 2.0032]. Jantāgharassa kavāṭaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ pīṭhasaṃghāṭaṃ (ka.) udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsakaṃ aggaḷavaṭṭikaṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭikaṃ tāḷacchiddaṃ āviñchanachiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti[V 0.0239]. Jantāgharassa kuṭṭapādo jīrati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, maṇḍalikaṃ kātu”nti. Jantāgharassa dhūmanettaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhūmanetta”nti.

At that time, monks walking in the open air were weary from both cold and heat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a hall for the walking path.' In the hall for the walking path, grass dust fell... 'I allow, monks, after shaking it down, to plaster it inside and out—to apply whitewash, black coloring, red ochre finishing, garland work, creeper work, makara-tooth patterns, five-stripes patterns, a robe-pole, and a robe-line.' The steam-bath house was low-lying and was flooded with water... 'I allow, monks, to make it high-lying.' The embankment collapsed... 'I allow, monks, to build three types of embankments—a brick embankment, a stone embankment, and a wooden embankment.' Those ascending were weary... 'I allow, monks, three types of staircases—a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.' Those ascending fell... 'I allow, monks, a handrail.' The steam-bath house had no door... 'I allow, monks, a door-leaf, a door-frame, a lower pivot socket, an upper pivot socket, a bolt-post, a monkey-head bolt, a pin, a latch, a keyhole, a hole for a pull-cord, and a pull-cord.' The base of the wall of the steam-bath house deteriorated... 'I allow, monks, to make a circular buttress.' The steam-bath house had no chimney... 'I allow, monks, a chimney.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū khuddake jantāghare majjhe aggiṭṭhānaṃ karonti. Upacāro na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khuddake jantāghare ekamantaṃ aggiṭṭhānaṃ kātuṃ, mahallake majjhe”ti. Jantāghare aggi mukhaṃ ḍahati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mukhamattika”nti. Hatthe mattikaṃ tementi…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mattikādoṇika”nti. Mattikā duggandhā hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vāsetu”nti. Jantāghare aggi kāyaṃ ḍahati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaṃ atiharitu”nti. Pātiyāpi pattenapi udakaṃ atiharanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaṭṭhānaṃ, udakasarāvaka”nti. Jantāgharaṃ tiṇacchadanaṃ na sedeti tiṇacchādanena chādeti (ka.) …pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātu”nti. Jantāgharaṃ [M 0.0258] cikkhallaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santharituṃ tayo santhare – iṭṭhakāsantharaṃ, silāsantharaṃ[T 2.0033], dārusanthara”nti. Cikkhallaṃyeva hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhovitu”nti. Udakaṃ santiṭṭhati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamana”nti.

At that time, the monks were making the fireplace in the middle of a small steam-bath house. There was no room to move around. They reported the matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, in a small steam-bath house, to make the fireplace to one side; in a large one, in the middle.' The fire in the steam-bath house burns the face... 'I allow, monks, facial clay.' They moisten clay in their hands... 'I allow, monks, a clay trough.' The clay becomes foul-smelling... 'I allow, monks, to scent it.' The fire in the steam-bath house burns the body... 'I allow, monks, to bring in water.' They bring in water in bowls and almsbowls... 'I allow, monks, a place for water and a water scoop.' A steam-bath house with a thatched roof does not hold in the steam... 'I allow, monks, after shaking it down, to plaster it inside and out.' The steam-bath house becomes muddy... 'I allow, monks, to lay three kinds of flooring—brick flooring, stone flooring, and wooden flooring.' It remains muddy... 'I allow, monks, to wash it.' The water stagnates... 'I allow, monks, a drain for the water.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū jantāghare chamāya [P 2.0121] nisīdanti, gattāni kaṇḍūvanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, jantāgharapīṭha”nti. Tena kho pana samayena jantāgharaṃ aparikkhittaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo pākāre – iṭṭhakāpākāraṃ, silāpākāraṃ, dārupākāra”nti. Koṭṭhako na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koṭṭhaka”nti. Koṭṭhako nīcavatthuko hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Koṭṭhakassa kavāṭaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsakaṃ aggaḷavaṭṭiṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭikaṃ tāḷacchiddaṃ āviñchanachiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti. Koṭṭhake tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ [T 2.0034][V 0.0240] kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikanti. Pariveṇaṃ cikkhallaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, marumbaṃ upakiritu”nti. Na pariyāpuṇanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, padarasilaṃ nikkhipitu”nti. Udakaṃ santiṭṭhati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamana”nti.

At that time, monks were sitting on the bare ground in the hot-air bath, and their bodies were itching. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, a bench for the hot-air bath.” At that time, the hot-air bath was unenclosed… “I allow, monks, to enclose it with three kinds of walls—a brick wall, a stone wall, and a wooden wall.” There was no gatehouse… “I allow, monks, a gatehouse.” The gatehouse had a low foundation and was flooded with water… “I allow, monks, to make a high foundation.” The retaining wall collapsed… “I allow, monks, to build with three kinds of retaining walls—a brick retaining wall, a stone retaining wall, and a wooden retaining wall.” Those ascending struggled… “I allow, monks, three kinds of stairways—a brick stairway, a stone stairway, and a wooden stairway.” Those ascending fell… “I allow, monks, a handrail.” The gatehouse had no door… “I allow, monks, a door leaf, a door frame, a door-socket, an upper staple, a bolt-post, a bolt-head, a pin, a latch, a keyhole, a pull-cord hole, and a pull-cord.” Grass-dust fell in the gatehouse… “I allow, monks, after brushing it down, to have it plastered inside and out and finished with whitewash, black paint, red ochre work, garland designs, creeper designs, sea-monster tooth designs, and five-stripe designs.” The surrounding area was muddy… “I allow, monks, to scatter gravel.” It was not sufficient… “I allow, monks, to lay a flagstone.” The water stagnated… “I allow, monks, a drain for the water.”

261. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū naggā naggaṃ abhivādenti…pe… naggā naggaṃ abhivādāpenti, naggā naggassa parikammaṃ karonti, naggā naggassa parikammaṃ kārāpenti, naggā naggassa denti, naggā paṭiggaṇhanti, naggā khādanti, naggā bhuñjanti, naggā sāyanti, naggā pivanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, naggena idaṃ padaṃ katthaci natthi naggo abhivādetabbo…pe… na naggena abhivādetabbaṃ… na naggena idaṃ padaṃ katthaci natthi naggo abhivādāpetabbo… na naggena abhivādāpetabbaṃ… na naggena naggassa parikammaṃ [M 0.0259] kātabbaṃ… na naggena naggassa parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ… na naggena naggassa dātabbaṃ… na naggena paṭiggahetabbaṃ… na naggena khāditabbaṃ… na naggena bhuñjitabbaṃ… na [T 2.0035] naggena sāyitabbaṃ… na naggena pātabbaṃ. Yo piveyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

261. At that time, naked monks paid homage to another naked monk… they caused homage to be paid to another naked monk, they performed the service of back-scrubbing for another naked monk, they caused the service of back-scrubbing to be performed for another naked monk, they gave to another naked monk, and while naked they received, ate hard food, ate soft food, licked, and drank. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a naked monk should not pay homage to another naked monk… homage should not be paid by a naked monk… a naked monk should not cause another naked monk to be paid homage to… homage should not be caused to be paid by a naked monk… the service of back-scrubbing should not be performed by a naked monk for another naked monk… the service of back-scrubbing should not be caused to be performed by a naked monk for another naked monk… a naked monk should not give to another naked monk; a naked monk should not receive; a naked monk should not eat hard food; a naked monk should not eat soft food; a naked monk should not lick; a naked monk should not drink. Whosoever should drink while naked commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū jantāghare chamāya cīvaraṃ nikkhipanti. Cīvaraṃ paṃsukitaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti. Deve vassante cīvaraṃ ovassati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave[P 2.0122], jantāgharasāla”nti. Jantāgharasālā nīcavatthukā hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ…pe… ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Jantāgharasālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ…pe… cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti.

At that time, monks were placing their robes on the ground in the steam-bath house. The robes became smeared with dust. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a robe-pole and a robe-cord.' When it rained, the robes got wet... 'I allow, monks, a hall for the steam-bath house.' The hall for the steam-bath house had a low foundation and was flooded with water... 'I allow, monks, to make it with a high foundation.' The retaining wall collapsed... 'I allow, monks, to build it up...' Those climbing up became weary... those climbing up fell down... 'I allow, monks, a handrail.' Grass-dust fell in the hall for the steam-bath house... 'I allow, monks, after brushing it down, to plaster it inside and out... a robe-pole and a robe-cord.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū jantāgharepi udakepi parikammaṃ kātuṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso paṭicchādiyo – jantāgharapaṭicchādiṃ, udakapaṭicchādiṃ, vatthapaṭicchādi”nti.

At that time, the monks were scrupulous about scrubbing themselves in the steam-bath house and in the water. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, three kinds of coverings: the covering of a steam-bath house, the covering of water, and the covering of a cloth.'

Tena kho pana samayena jantāghare udakaṃ na hoti. Bhagavato [T 2.0036] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi[V 0.0241], bhikkhave, udapāna”nti. Udapānassa kūlaṃ lujjati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Udapāno nīcavatthuko hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti.

At that time, there was no water in the steam-bath house. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a well.' The bank of the well collapsed… 'I allow, monks, to build three kinds of linings: a brick lining, a stone lining, and a wooden lining.' The well had a low base and was flooded by water… 'I allow, monks, to make a high base.' The lining collapsed… Those climbing up struggled… Those climbing up fell down… 'I allow, monks, a handrail.'

262. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū vallikāyapi kāyabandhanenapi udakaṃ vāhenti vāhanti (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakavāhanarajju”nti. Hatthā dukkhā honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tulaṃ karakaṭakaṃ cakkavaṭṭaka”nti. Bhājanā bahū bhijjanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo vārake – lohavārakaṃ, dāruvārakaṃ, cammakkhaṇḍa”nti.

262. At that time, monks were drawing water with vines and waistbands. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, a water-drawing rope.' Their hands became sore… 'I allow, monks, a water-drawing balance, a pulley, and a water-wheel.' Many vessels were broken… 'I allow, monks, three kinds of buckets: a metal bucket, a wooden bucket, and a leather bucket.'

Tena [M 0.0260] kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajjhokāse udakaṃ vāhentā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udapānasāla”nti. Udapānasālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti. Udapāno apāruto hoti, tiṇacuṇṇehipi [T 2.0037] paṃsukehipi okiriyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhāna”nti. Udakabhājanaṃ na saṃvijjati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakadoṇiṃ udakakaṭāha”nti.

At that time, monks drawing water in the open were afflicted by both cold and heat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, a well-house.” In the well-house, grass-dust would fall… “I allow, monks, after brushing it off, to have it plastered inside and out, to apply white color, black color, a finish with red ochre, garland-work, creeper-work, makara-tooth carvings, a five-band design, a robe-rail, and a robe-line.” The well was without a cover; it was strewn with grass-dust and dust from the soil… “I allow, monks, a cover.” There was no water vessel… “I allow, monks, a water trough and a water cauldron.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ārāme tahaṃ tahaṃ nahāyanti. Ārāmo cikkhallo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, candanika”nti. Candanikā pākaṭā hoti. Bhikkhū hiriyanti nahāyituṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo pākāre – iṭṭhakāpākāraṃ, silāpākāraṃ, dārupākāra”nti. Candanikā cikkhallā hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santharituṃ tayo santhare – iṭṭhakāsantharaṃ, silāsantharaṃ, dārusanthara”nti. Udakaṃ santiṭṭhati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamana”nti.

At that time, monks were bathing here and there in the monastery. The monastery became muddy. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, plank flooring.” The plank flooring was exposed. The monks were shy to bathe… “I allow, monks, to enclose it with three kinds of enclosures: a brick enclosure, a stone enclosure, and a wooden enclosure.” The plank flooring became muddy… “I allow, monks, to lay three kinds of flooring: brick flooring, stone flooring, and wooden flooring.” The water was stagnating… “I allow, monks, a water drain.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ gattāni sītigatāni honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakapuñchaniṃ coḷakenapi paccuddharitu”nti.

At that time, the monks' bodies were afflicted by cold. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, monks, a water-wiping cloth, and to wipe oneself even with a coarse cloth.”

263. Tena [V 0.0242] kho pana samayena [P 2.0123] aññataro upāsako saṅghassa atthāya pokkharaṇiṃ kāretukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pokkharaṇi”nti. Pokkharaṇiyā kūlaṃ [T 2.0038] lujjati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Pokkharaṇiyā udakaṃ purāṇaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakamātikaṃ udakaniddhamana”nti.

263. At that time, a certain lay follower wished to have a pond constructed for the Sangha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'I allow, monks, a pond.' The bank of the pond crumbled… 'I allow, monks, to build three kinds of retaining walls: a brick retaining wall, a stone retaining wall, and a wooden retaining wall.' Those ascending became weary… 'I allow, monks, three kinds of stairs: brick stairs, stone stairs, and wooden stairs.' Those ascending fell… 'I allow, monks, a handrail.' The water in the pond became stale… 'I allow, monks, a water inlet and a water outlet.'

Tena [M 0.0261] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu saṅghassa atthāya nillekhaṃ jantāgharaṃ kattukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nillekhaṃ jantāghara”nti.

At that time, a certain monk wished to build an undecorated steam-bath house for the Sangha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'I allow, monks, an undecorated steam-bath house.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū cātumāsaṃ nisīdanena vippavasanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “na, bhikkhave, cātumāsaṃ nisīdanena vippavasitabbaṃ. Yo vippavaseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six dwelt apart from their sitting cloth for four months. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Monks, one should not dwell apart from the sitting cloth for four months. Whichever monk should dwell apart from it, there is an offense of wrong conduct.'

264. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pupphābhikiṇṇesu sayanesu sayanti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, pupphābhikiṇṇesu sayanesu sayitabbaṃ. Yo sayeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti[T 2.0039].

264. At that time, the group-of-six monks were sleeping on beds strewn with flowers. People wandering on monastery rounds saw them and complained, criticized, and denounced them: 'Just like householders enjoying sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one should not sleep on beds strewn with flowers. Whoever should do so, there is an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena manussā gandhampi mālampi ādāya ārāmaṃ āgacchanti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gandhaṃ gahetvā kavāṭe pañcaṅgulikaṃ dātuṃ, pupphaṃ gahetvā vihāre ekamantaṃ nikkhipitu”nti.

At that time, people came to the monastery bringing perfumes and garlands. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept them. They reported the matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, that you take the perfume and apply a five-finger mark on the door panel, and that you take the flowers and place them in a suitable place in the monastery.'

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa namatakaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, namataka”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “namatakaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ nu kho udāhu vikappetabba”nti…pe… “na, bhikkhave, namatakaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, na vikappetabba”nti.

At that time, a felt rug had arisen for the Sangha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a felt rug.' Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'Should a felt rug be determined, or should it be shared?'... 'Monks, a felt rug is not to be determined, nor is it to be shared.'

Tena [V 0.0243] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū āsittakūpadhāne bhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “na, bhikkhave, āsittakūpadhāne bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo bhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti[P 2.0124].

At that time, the group-of-six monks were eating from a cast metal food container. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Monks, one should not eat from a cast metal food container. Whoever should eat from one commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. So bhuñjamāno na sakkoti hatthena pattaṃ sandhāretuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, maḷorika”nti.

At that time, a certain monk was ill. While eating, he was unable to hold his bowl steady with his hand. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a bowl-stand.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ekabhājanepi bhuñjanti…pe… [T 2.0040] ekathālakepi pivanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti [M 0.0262] khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ekabhājane bhuñjitabbaṃ…pe… na ekathālake pātabbaṃ… na ekamañce tuvaṭṭitabbaṃ… na ekattharaṇā na ekattharaṇe tuvaṭṭitabbaṃ… na ekapāvuraṇā na ekapāvuraṇe tuvaṭṭitabbaṃ… na ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā na ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe (syā.) tuvaṭṭitabbaṃ. Yo tuvaṭṭeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were eating from a single bowl... drinking from a single dish, lying down together on a single bed, lying down together on a single spread, lying down together under a single covering, and lying down together on a single spread and under a single covering. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one should not eat from a single bowl... one should not drink from a single dish... one should not lie down together on a single bed... one should not lie down together on a single spread... one should not lie down together under a single covering... one should not lie down together on a single spread and under a single covering. Whoever should lie down thus commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

265. Tena kho pana samayena vaḍḍho licchavī mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sahāyo hoti. Atha kho vaḍḍho licchavī yena mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca – “vandāmi ayyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū nālapiṃsu. Dutiyampi kho vaḍḍho licchavī mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca – “vandāmi ayyā”ti. Dutiyampi kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū nālapiṃsu. Tatiyampi kho vaḍḍho licchavī mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca – “vandāmi ayyā”ti. Tatiyampi kho mettiyabhūmajakā [T 2.0041] bhikkhū nālapiṃsu. “Kyāhaṃ ayyānaṃ aparajjhāmi, kissa maṃ ayyā nālapantī”ti? “Tathā hi pana tvaṃ, āvuso vaḍḍha, amhe dabbena mallaputtena viheṭhiyamāne ajjhupekkhasī”ti. “Kyāhaṃ ayyā karomī”ti? “Sace kho tvaṃ, āvuso vaḍḍha, iccheyyāsi, ajjeva bhagavā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ nāsāpeyyā”ti. “Kyāhaṃ ayyā karomi, kiṃ mayā sakkā kātu”nti? “Ehi tvaṃ, āvuso vaḍḍha, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘idaṃ, bhante, nacchannaṃ nappatirūpaṃ. Yāyaṃ, bhante, disā abhayā anītikā anupaddavā sāyaṃ disā sabhayā saītikā saupaddavā; yato nivātaṃ tato savātaṃ[V 0.0244]; udakaṃ maññe ādittaṃ; ayyena me dabbena mallaputtena pajāpati dūsitā’”ti. “Evaṃ ayyā”ti kho vaḍḍho licchavī mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vaḍḍho licchavī [P 2.0125] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ, bhante, nacchannaṃ nappatirūpaṃ. Yāyaṃ, bhante, disā abhayā anītikā anupaddavā sāyaṃ disā sabhayā saītikā saupaddavā; yato nivātaṃ tato savātaṃ; udakaṃ maññe ādittaṃ; ayyena me dabbena mallaputtena pajāpati dūsitā”ti.

265. Now at that time, the Licchavi Vaḍḍha was a friend of the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks. Then Vaḍḍha the Licchavi approached the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks, and having approached, he said to them: 'Venerable sirs, I pay homage.' When this was said, the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks did not speak. A second time, Vaḍḍha the Licchavi said to the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks: 'Venerable sirs, I pay homage.' A second time, the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks did not speak. A third time, Vaḍḍha the Licchavi said to the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks: 'Venerable sirs, I pay homage.' A third time, the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks did not speak. 'In what way have I wronged the venerable sirs? Why do the venerable sirs not speak with me?' 'It is because, friend Vaḍḍha, you look on with indifference while we are being harassed by Dabba the Mallian.' 'What can I do, venerable sirs?' 'Friend Vaḍḍha, if you so wished, the Blessed One could have the Venerable Dabba the Mallian expelled this very day.' 'What can I do, venerable sirs? What is it in my power to do?' 'Come, friend Vaḍḍha, approach the Blessed One and, having approached, say this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, this is not seemly, it is not proper. Venerable Sir, the direction that was without danger, without affliction, and without calamity is now with danger, with affliction, and with calamity. Where it was sheltered from the wind, it is now windy. The water, I think, is ablaze. My wife has been violated by the Venerable Dabba the Mallian.”' 'Very well, venerable sirs,' Vaḍḍha the Licchavi replied, having assented to the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks. He then approached the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Vaḍḍha the Licchavi said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, this is not seemly, it is not proper. Venerable Sir, the direction that was without danger, without affliction, and without calamity is now with danger, with affliction, and with calamity. Where it was sheltered from the wind, it is now windy. The water, I think, is ablaze. My wife has been violated by the Venerable Dabba the Mallian.'

Atha [M 0.0263] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ paṭipucchi – “sarasi [T 2.0042] tvaṃ, dabba, evarūpaṃ kattā yathāyaṃ vaḍḍho āhā”ti? “Yathā maṃ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ etadavoca – “sarasi tvaṃ, dabba, evarūpaṃ kattā yathāyaṃ vaḍḍho āhā”ti? “Yathā maṃ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti. “Na kho, dabba, dabbā evaṃ nibbeṭhenti. Sace tayā kataṃ, katanti vadehi; sace akataṃ, akatanti vadehī”ti. “Yato ahaṃ, bhante, jāto nābhijānāmi supinantenapi methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitā, pageva jāgaro”ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ nikkujjatu, asambhogaṃ saṅghena karotu.

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having convened the community of bhikkhus, questioned the Venerable Dabba the Mallian: 'Dabba, do you remember having done such a thing as this Vaḍḍha has stated?' 'Venerable sir, as the Blessed One knows me.' For a second time... for a third time the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Dabba the Mallian: 'Dabba, do you remember having done such a thing as this Vaḍḍha has stated?' 'Venerable sir, as the Blessed One knows me.' 'Dabba, the wise do not answer in this way. If it was done by you, say, "It was done"; if it was not done, say, "It was not done."' 'Venerable sir, from when I was born, I do not recall having engaged in the act of sexual intercourse even in a dream, how much more so when awake.' Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha overturn the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi; let the Saṅgha place him in non-communion.'

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa patto nikkujjitabbo – bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya anāvāsāya (syā.) parisakkati, bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati, bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti, buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa pattaṃ nikkujjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nikkujjitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā [T 2.0043] paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Bhikkhus, the bowl should be overturned for a lay follower who is endowed with eight factors: he strives for the non-gain of bhikkhus, he strives for the detriment of bhikkhus, he strives for the non-residence of bhikkhus, he abuses and reviles bhikkhus, he divides bhikkhus from bhikkhus, he speaks dispraise of the Buddha, he speaks dispraise of the Dhamma, he speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha. Bhikkhus, I allow the overturning of the bowl for a lay follower endowed with these eight factors. And, bhikkhus, it should be overturned in this way: the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

266. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Vaḍḍho licchavī āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ nikkujjeyya, asambhogaṃ saṅghena kareyya. Esā ñatti.

266. “Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. Vaḍḍha the Licchavi accuses the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a baseless corruption of virtue. If it seems fit to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should overturn the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and place him in non-communion. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Vaḍḍho licchavī āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti. Saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ nikkujjati, asambhogaṃ saṅghena karoti[V 0.0245]. Yassāyasmato khamati vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattassa nikkujjanā, asambhogaṃ saṅghena karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. Vaḍḍha the Licchavi accuses the Venerable Dabba the Mallian of a baseless corruption of virtue. The Saṅgha overturns the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and places him in non-communion. Whoever agrees with the overturning of the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and his being placed in non-communion by the Saṅgha, let him remain silent; whoever disagrees, let him speak.”

“Nikkujjito saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto, asambhogo saṅghena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi has been overturned by the Saṅgha, and he has been placed in non-communion by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Atha [M 0.0264] kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā vaḍḍhaṃ licchaviṃ etadavoca – “saṅghena te, āvuso vaḍḍha, patto nikkujjito. Asambhogosi saṅghenā”ti. Atha [P 2.0126] kho vaḍḍho licchavī – saṅghena kira me patto nikkujjito, asambhogomhi kira saṅghenāti – tattheva mucchito papato. Atha kho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa [T 2.0044] mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā vaḍḍhaṃ licchaviṃ etadavocuṃ – “alaṃ, āvuso vaḍḍha, mā soci, mā paridevi. Mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ pasādessāma bhikkhusaṅghañcā”ti.

Then, in the forenoon, the Venerable Ānanda, having dressed, and taken his bowl and robe, approached the dwelling of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi. Having approached, he said this to Vaḍḍha the Licchavi: “Friend Vaḍḍha, the Saṅgha has overturned your bowl. You are not in communion with the Saṅgha.” Then Vaḍḍha the Licchavi—thinking, “It seems the Saṅgha has overturned my bowl! It seems I am not in communion with the Saṅgha!”—fainted and fell down right there. Then the friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi said this to him: “Enough, friend Vaḍḍha, do not grieve, do not lament. We will appease the Blessed One and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.”

Atha kho vaḍḍho licchavī saputtadāro samittāmacco sañātisālohito allavattho allakeso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yohaṃ ayyaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsesiṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti. “Taggha tvaṃ, āvuso vaḍḍha, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsesi. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, āvuso vaḍḍha, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuḍḍhihesā, āvuso vaḍḍha, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti, āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ ukkujjatu, sambhogaṃ saṅghena karotu.

Then Vaḍḍha the Licchavi, together with his son and wife, his friends and ministers, and his relatives and kinsmen, with wet clothes and wet hair, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he fell with his head at the Blessed One’s feet and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, a transgression has overcome me, foolish, deluded, and unskillful as I am, in that I groundlessly accused the venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a corruption of virtue. Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept my transgression as a transgression for the sake of future restraint.” “Indeed, friend Vaḍḍha, a transgression has overcome you, foolish, deluded, and unskillful as you are, in that you groundlessly accused Dabba Mallaputta of a corruption of virtue. And since you, friend Vaḍḍha, having seen your transgression as a transgression, make amends according to the Dhamma, we accept it from you. For this is growth in the Noble One's Discipline, friend Vaḍḍha: that one sees one's transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, and undertakes future restraint.” Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha turn Vaḍḍha the Licchavi’s bowl upright and have communion with him.

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa patto ukkujjitabbo – na bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, na bhikkhūnaṃ [T 2.0045] anatthāya parisakkati, na bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, na bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati, na bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti, na buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, na dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, na saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Anujānāmi[V 0.0246], bhikkhave, imehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa pattaṃ ukkujjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ukkujjitabbo. Tena, bhikkhave, vaḍḍhena licchavinā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘saṅghena me, bhante, patto [M 0.0265] nikkujjito, asambhogomhi saṅghena. Sohaṃ, bhante, sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, saṅghaṃ pattukkujjanaṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho [P 2.0127] ñāpetabbo –

“Bhikkhus, the bowl of a lay follower endowed with eight factors should be turned upright: he does not strive for the non-gain of bhikkhus, he does not strive for the harm of bhikkhus, he does not strive for the non-residence of bhikkhus, he does not abuse or revile bhikkhus, he does not cause division between bhikkhus, he does not speak in dispraise of the Buddha, he does not speak in dispraise of the Dhamma, he does not speak in dispraise of the Saṅgha. I allow, bhikkhus, the turning upright of the bowl for a lay follower endowed with these eight factors. And it should be turned upright in this way, bhikkhus. That Vaḍḍha the Licchavi, bhikkhus, should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhus, sit on his haunches, raise his joined hands, and should say this: ‘Venerable Sirs, the Saṅgha has overturned my bowl; I am not in communion with the Saṅgha. I, Venerable Sirs, am conducting myself properly, I cast off my pride, I am practicing for my rehabilitation. I ask the Saṅgha to turn my bowl upright.’ He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:”

267. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto nikkujjito, asambhogo saṅghena. So sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, saṅghaṃ pattukkujjanaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ ukkujjeyya, sambhogaṃ saṅghena kareyya. Esā ñatti.

267. “Venerable Sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha has overturned the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi; he is not in communion with the Saṅgha. He is conducting himself properly, he casts off his pride, he is practicing for his rehabilitation, and he asks the Saṅgha to turn his bowl upright. If the Saṅgha is ready, the Saṅgha should turn Vaḍḍha the Licchavi's bowl upright and should have communion with him. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto nikkujjito, asambhogo saṅghena. So sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati[T 2.0046], saṅghaṃ pattukkujjanaṃ yācati. Saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ ukkujjati, sambhogaṃ saṅghena karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattassa ukkujjanā, sambhogaṃ saṅghena karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha has overturned the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi; he is not in communion with the Saṅgha. He is conducting himself properly, he casts off his pride, he is practicing for his rehabilitation, and he asks the Saṅgha to turn his bowl upright. The Saṅgha turns Vaḍḍha the Licchavi’s bowl upright and has communion with him. If the turning upright of the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and having communion with him is agreeable to the venerable ones, they should remain silent. Whoever does not agree should speak.

“Ukkujjito saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto, sambhogo saṅghena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The Saṅgha has turned upright the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi; communion has been established with him by the Saṅgha. This is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I take it.”

268. Atha kho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bhaggā tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bhaggā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire suṃsumāragire (sī. syā.), saṃsumāragire (ka.) bhesakaḷāvane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bodhissa rājakumārassa kokanado kokanudo (ka.) nāma pāsādo acirakārito hoti, anajjhāvuttho samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtena. Atha kho bodhi rājakumāro sañjikāputtaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, samma sañcikāputta, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama, upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vanda; appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘bodhi, bhante, rājakumāro bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ [M 0.0266] lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ [V 0.0247] pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘adhivāsetu kira, bhante[T 2.0047], bhagavā bodhissa rājakumārassa svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’”ti. “Evaṃ bho”ti kho sañcikāputto māṇavo bodhissa rājakumārassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sañcikāputto māṇavo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bodhi kho rājakumāro bhoto gotamassa pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati. Evañca vadeti – ‘adhivāsetu kira bhavaṃ gotamo bodhissa rājakumārassa svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho sañcikāputto māṇavo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bodhi rājakumāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā [P 2.0128] bodhiṃ rājakumāraṃ etadavoca – “avocumha kho mayaṃ bhoto vacanena taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ – ‘bodhi kho rājakumāro bhoto gotamassa pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati. Evañca vadeti – adhivāsetu kira bhavaṃ gotamo bodhissa rājakumārassa svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’ti. Adhivutthañca pana samaṇena gotamenā”ti.

268. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Vesālī as long as he pleased, set out on a journey towards the Bhaggas. Traveling in stages, he arrived at the Bhaggas. There the Blessed One stayed among the Bhaggas at Susumāragira in the Bhesakaḷā Forest, a deer park. At that time, Prince Bodhi had recently built a palace named Kokanada, which had not yet been occupied by any ascetic, brahmin, or any human being. Then Prince Bodhi addressed the young man Sañjikāputta: 'Come, my dear Sañjikāputta, go to the Blessed One, approach him, and in my name venerate his feet with your head. Inquire about his freedom from illness and affliction, his lightness, strength, and comfortable abiding. Say this: "Venerable sir, Prince Bodhi venerates the Blessed One’s feet with his head and inquires about his freedom from illness and affliction, his lightness, strength, and comfortable abiding." And say this: "Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to tomorrow’s meal from Prince Bodhi together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus."' 'Yes, sir,' replied the young man Sañjikāputta to Prince Bodhi. He then went to the Blessed One, approached him, exchanged courteous and memorable greetings, and sat down at one side. Seated at one side, the young man Sañjikāputta said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, Prince Bodhi venerates venerable Gotama’s feet with his head and inquires about his freedom from illness and affliction, his lightness, strength, and comfortable abiding. And he says this: "May the venerable Gotama consent to tomorrow’s meal from Prince Bodhi together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus."' The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the young man Sañjikāputta, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, went to Prince Bodhi, and said: 'We have spoken in your name to that venerable Gotama, saying: "Venerable Gotama, Prince Bodhi venerates venerable Gotama’s feet with his head and inquires about his freedom from illness and affliction, his lightness, strength, and comfortable abiding. And he says this: May the venerable Gotama consent to tomorrow’s meal from Prince Bodhi together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus." And it has been consented to by the ascetic Gotama.'

Atha kho bodhi rājakumāro tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ [T 2.0048] khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā, kokanadañca pāsādaṃ odātehi dussehi santharāpetvā yāva pacchimasopānakaḷevarā, sañcikāputtaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, samma sañcikāputta, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocehi – ‘kālo, bhante niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’”nti. “Evaṃ bho”ti kho sañcikāputto māṇavo bodhissa rājakumārassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocesi – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti.

Then Prince Bodhi, after that night had passed, had fine hard and soft foods prepared, and had the Kokanada Palace spread with white cloths up to the last step of the staircase. He addressed the young man Sañjikāputta: “Come, my dear Sañjikāputta, go to the Blessed One, and upon arrival, announce the time to the Blessed One: ‘It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.’” “Yes, sir,” the young man Sañjikāputta replied to Prince Bodhi. He then went to the Blessed One and, upon arrival, announced the time: “It is time, venerable Gotama, the meal is ready.”

Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena bodhissa rājakumārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena bodhi rājakumāro bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito hoti, bhagavantaṃ āgamayamāno. Addasā kho bodhi rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ dūratova [M 0.0267] āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna tato paccuggantvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā purekkhatvā yena kokanado pāsādo tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho bhagavā pacchimasopānakaḷevaraṃ nissāya aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho bodhi rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “akkamatu, bhante, bhagavā dussāni, akkamatu sugato dussāni, yaṃ mama assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte [V 0.0248] bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho bodhi rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “akkamatu, bhante, bhagavā dussāni, akkamatu [T 2.0049] sugato dussāni, yaṃ mama assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ apalokesi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bodhiṃ rājakumāraṃ etadavoca – “saṃharantu, rājakumāra, dussāni. Na bhagavā celapaṭikaṃ celapattikaṃ (sī.) akkamissati pacchimaṃ janataṃ tathāgato anukampatī”ti.

Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having put on his lower robe and taken his bowl and outer robe, approached the dwelling of Prince Bodhi. At that time, Prince Bodhi was standing at the outer gateway, awaiting the Blessed One. Prince Bodhi saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he went forth to meet him, paid homage to him, and escorting him, approached the Kokanada Palace. Then the Blessed One stood by the last step of the staircase. Then Prince Bodhi said to the Blessed One, “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One step on the cloths, may the Sugata step on the cloths, that it may be for my welfare and happiness for a long time.” When this was said, the Blessed One remained silent. A second time… A third time, Prince Bodhi said to the Blessed One, “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One step on the cloths, may the Sugata step on the cloths, that it may be for my welfare and happiness for a long time.” Then the Blessed One looked toward Venerable Ānanda. Then Venerable Ānanda said to Prince Bodhi, “Prince, have the cloths removed. The Blessed One will not step on a cloth spread out. The Tathāgata has compassion for the future generation.”

Atha kho bodhi rājakumāro dussāni saṃharāpetvā uparikokanade pāsāde āsanaṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā kokanadaṃ pāsādaṃ abhiruhitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho bodhi rājakumāro buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ, ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho bodhiṃ rājakumāraṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā [P 2.0129] samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, celapaṭikā akkamitabbā. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Then Prince Bodhi had the cloths removed and a seat prepared in the upper Kokanada Palace. Then the Blessed One ascended the Kokanada Palace and sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of bhikkhus. Then Prince Bodhi, with his own hands, served and satisfied the community of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with excellent edible and staple foods. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Prince Bodhi sat down at a suitable place. The Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened Prince Bodhi, who was sitting at a suitable place, with a Dhamma talk, then rose from his seat and departed. Then, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, a cloth spread out is not to be stepped on. Whoever should step on it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā itthī apagatagabbhā bhikkhū nimantetvā dussaṃ paññapetvā etadavoca – “akkamatha, bhante[T 2.0050], dussa”nti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na akkamanti. “Akkamatha, bhante, dussaṃ maṅgalatthāyā”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na akkamiṃsu. Atha kho sā itthī ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā maṅgalatthāya yāciyamānā celappaṭikaṃ na akkamissantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassā itthiyā ujjhāyantiyā khiyyantiyā vipācentiyā. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ [M 0.0268] ārocesuṃ. “Gihī, bhikkhave, maṅgalikā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gihīnaṃ maṅgalatthāya yāciyamānena celappaṭikaṃ akkamitu”nti.

Now at that time, a certain woman who had miscarried invited the bhikkhus, had a cloth spread out, and said this: 'Venerable sirs, please step on the cloth.' The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not step on it. 'Venerable sirs, please step on the cloth for the sake of a blessing,' she said. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not step on it. Then that woman complained, disparaged, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the noble ones, being requested for the sake of a blessing, will not step on the cloth spread out?' The bhikkhus heard that woman complaining, disparaging, and spreading it about. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, householders are fond of blessings. I allow, bhikkhus, stepping on a cloth spread out when requested by householders for the sake of a blessing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dhotapādakaṃ akkamituṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhotapādakaṃ akkamitu”nti.

Now at that time, the bhikkhus were scrupulous about stepping on a foot-mat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow stepping on a foot-mat.'

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is finished.

269. Atha [V 0.0249] kho bhagavā bhaggesu yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā ghaṭakañca katakañca sammajjaniñca ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā ghaṭakañca katakañca sammajjaniñca, yaṃ [T 2.0051] mama assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā ghaṭakañca sammajjaniñca. Na bhagavā katakaṃ paṭiggahesi. Atha kho bhagavā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

269. Then the Blessed One, having stayed among the Bhaggas as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Sāvatthī. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One stayed in Sāvatthī, at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then Visākhā, Migāra's mother, took a water pot, a foot scraper, and a broom, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Visākhā, Migāra's mother, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept from me the water pot, the foot scraper, and the broom, for my long-term welfare and happiness.” The Blessed One accepted the water pot and the broom but did not accept the foot scraper. Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened Visākhā, Migāra's mother, with a talk on the Dhamma. Then Visākhā, Migāra's mother, having been instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from her seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed.

Atha kho [P 2.0130] bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ghaṭakañca sammajjaniñca. Na, bhikkhave, katakaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso pādaghaṃsaniyo – sakkharaṃ, kathalaṃ, samuddapheṇaka”nti.
