Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, a water pot and a broom. Bhikkhus, a foot scraper is not to be used. Whoever should use one commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, bhikkhus, three kinds of foot-rubbers: gravel, a potsherd, and sea-foam.”

Atha kho visākhā migāramātā vidhūpanañca tālavaṇṭañca tālavaṇḍañca (ka.) ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā vidhūpanañca tālavaṇṭañca, yaṃ mama assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā vidhūpanañca tālavaṇṭañca.

Then Visākhā, Migāra's mother, taking a square fan and a palm-leaf fan, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Having sat down to one side, Visākhā, Migāra's mother, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept from me the square fan and the palm-leaf fan, for my long-term welfare and happiness.” The Blessed One accepted the square fan and the palm-leaf fan.

Atha [M 0.0269] kho bhagavā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi…pe… padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ [T 2.0052] kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vidhūpanañca tālavaṇṭañcā”ti.

Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, with a Dhamma talk... After circumambulating him to the right, she departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow a square fan and a palm-leaf fan.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa makasabījanī uppannā hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, makasabījani”nti. Cāmaribījanī uppannā hoti. Bhagavato [V 0.0250] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, cāmaribījanī dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso bījaniyo – vākamayaṃ, usīramayaṃ, morapiñchamaya”nti.

At that time, a mosquito-whisk had arisen for the Saṅgha. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow a mosquito-whisk.” A chowrie-whisk had arisen. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, a chowrie-whisk is not to be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, I allow three kinds of whisks: one made of bark-fibre, one made of usīra-grass, and one made of peacock feathers.”

270. Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa chattaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, chatta”nti.

270. At that time, an umbrella had arisen for the Saṅgha. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow an umbrella.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū chattappaggahitā chattaṃ paggahetvā (ka.) āhiṇḍanti. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako sambahulehi ājīvakasāvakehi saddhiṃ uyyānaṃ agamāsi. Addasāsuṃ kho te ājīvakasāvakā chabbaggiye bhikkhū dūratova chattappaggahite āgacchante. Disvāna taṃ upāsakaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ete kho, ayyā ayyo (ka.), tumhākaṃ bhadantā chattappaggahitā āgacchanti, seyyathāpi gaṇakamahāmattā”ti. “Nāyyā ete bhikkhū, paribbājakā”ti. ‘Bhikkhū na bhikkhū’ti abbhutaṃ akaṃsu. Atha kho so upāsako upagate sañjānitvā ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā chattappaggahitā [T 2.0053][P 2.0131] āhiṇḍissantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa upāsakassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, chattaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhus of the group-of-six wandered about holding up umbrellas. On that occasion, a certain lay follower went to a park with several Ājīvaka disciples. From a distance, those Ājīvaka disciples saw the bhikkhus of the group-of-six approaching while holding up umbrellas. Having seen them, they said to that lay follower: “Sir, these venerables of yours are coming holding up umbrellas, just like great ministers leading an army.” “Sirs, these are not bhikkhus; they are wanderers.” They made a bet, saying, “They are bhikkhus,” “They are not bhikkhus.” Then, when they had approached, that lay follower recognized them and complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the venerables wander about holding up umbrellas?” The bhikkhus heard that lay follower complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those bhikkhus informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus…?” … “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked them… having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, an umbrella is not to be carried. Whoever should carry one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Tassa bhikkhuno vinā chattaṃ na phāsu hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa chattaṃ dhāretu”nti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhu was sick. It was not comfortable for that bhikkhu without an umbrella. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow a sick bhikkhu to carry an umbrella.”

Tena [M 0.0270] kho pana samayena bhikkhū – gilānasseva bhagavatā chattaṃ anuññātaṃ no agilānassāti – ārāme ārāmūpacāre chattaṃ dhāretuṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, agilānenapi ārāme ārāmūpacāre chattaṃ dhāretu”nti.

At that time the bhikkhus were scrupulous about carrying an umbrella in the monastery or its vicinity, thinking, “The Blessed One has allowed an umbrella only for the sick, not for the healthy.” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow even a healthy bhikkhu to carry an umbrella in the monastery or its vicinity.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sikkāya pattaṃ uṭṭitvā daṇḍe ālaggitvā vikāle aññatarena gāmadvārena atikkamati. Manussā – ‘esayyo coro gacchati, asissa vijjotalatī’ti anupatitvā [T 2.0054] gahetvā sañjānitvā muñciṃsu. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā [V 0.0251] bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, daṇḍasikkaṃ dhāresī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu daṇḍasikkaṃ dhāressasī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, daṇḍasikkā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhu, having placed his bowl in a sling and hung it on a staff, was passing through a certain village gate at an improper time. People, saying, “This fellow is a thief going by; his sword is flashing,” pursued him, seized him, and upon recognizing him, released him. Then that bhikkhu went to the monastery and informed the bhikkhus of this matter. “But, friend, do you carry a sling hung on a staff?” “Yes, friends.” Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… criticized, scorned, and disparaged him, saying, “How indeed can a bhikkhu carry a sling hung on a staff?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked him… and after giving a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, a sling hung on a staff is not to be carried. Whoever should carry one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti, na sakkoti vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tena gilānena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, gilāno; na sakkomi vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ daṇḍasammutiṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho [P 2.0132] ñāpetabbo –

At that time, a certain bhikkhu was sick; he could not walk about without a staff. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow that a sick bhikkhu be given permission for a staff. And, bhikkhus, it should be given in this way. That sick bhikkhu should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and say this: ‘Venerable sirs, I am sick; I cannot walk about without a staff. Therefore, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for permission for a staff.’ It should be requested a second time. It should be requested a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu gilāno, na sakkoti [T 2.0055] vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ. So saṅghaṃ daṇḍasammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, is sick and cannot go about without a staff. He asks the Saṅgha for permission for a staff. If it seems fit to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the bhikkhu named so-and-so permission for a staff. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu gilāno, na sakkoti vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ. So saṅghaṃ daṇḍasammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho [M 0.0271] itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasammutiṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasammutiyā dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, is sick and is not able to go about without a staff. He asks the Saṅgha for permission for a staff. The Saṅgha gives permission for a staff to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. Whichever venerable one approves of giving permission for a staff to the bhikkhu named so-and-so should remain silent; whoever does not approve should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Permission for a staff has been given by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.”

271. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti, na sakkoti vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa bhikkhuno sikkāsammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tena gilānena bhikkhunā [V 0.0252] saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, gilāno; na sakkomi vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ sikkāsammutiṃ yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

271. At that time, a certain bhikkhu was sick and was not able to carry his bowl without a sling. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow that a sick bhikkhu be given permission for a sling. And thus, bhikkhus, it should be given. That sick bhikkhu should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I am sick; I am not able to carry my bowl without a sling. Therefore, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for permission for a sling.’ He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:”

“Suṇātu [T 2.0056] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu gilāno, na sakkoti vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. So saṅghaṃ sikkāsammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sikkāsammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, is sick; he is not able to carry his bowl without a sling. He asks the Saṅgha for authorization for a sling. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give authorization for a sling to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu gilāno, na sakkoti vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. So saṅghaṃ sikkāsammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sikkāsammutiṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sikkāsammutiyā dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, is sick; he cannot carry his bowl without a sling. He asks the Saṅgha for authorization for a sling. The Saṅgha gives the bhikkhu named so-and-so authorization for a sling. Whichever venerable one approves of giving the bhikkhu named so-and-so authorization for a sling should remain silent; whoever does not approve should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sikkāsammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Authorization for a sling has been given by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

272. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti, na sakkoti vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ, na sakkoti vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasikkāsammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā[M 0.0272]. Tena gilānena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, gilāno; na sakkomi vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ; na sakkomi vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ daṇḍasikkāsammutiṃ [T 2.0057] yācāmī’ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

272. At that time, a certain bhikkhu was sick; he could not walk about without a staff, nor could he carry his bowl without a sling. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow that a sick bhikkhu be given authorization for a staff and a sling. And thus, bhikkhus, it should be given. That sick bhikkhu should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and say: ‘Venerable sirs, I am sick; I cannot walk about without a staff, nor can I carry my bowl without a sling. Therefore, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for authorization for a staff and a sling.’ He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhu should then inform the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu gilāno, na sakkoti vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ, na sakkoti vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. So saṅghaṃ daṇḍasikkāsammutiṃ [V 0.0253] yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasikkāsammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, is sick; he cannot walk about without a staff, nor can he carry his bowl without a sling. He asks the Saṅgha for authorization for a staff and a sling. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the bhikkhu named so-and-so authorization for a staff and a sling. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu gilāno na sakkoti vinā daṇḍena āhiṇḍituṃ, na sakkoti vinā sikkāya pattaṃ pariharituṃ. So saṅghaṃ daṇḍasikkāsammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasikkāsammutiṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasikkāsammutiyā dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, is sick; he cannot walk about without a staff, nor can he carry his bowl without a sling. He asks the Saṅgha for authorization for a staff and a sling. The Saṅgha gives the bhikkhu named so-and-so authorization for a staff and a sling. Whichever venerable one approves of giving the bhikkhu named so-and-so authorization for a staff and a sling should remain silent; whoever does not approve should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno daṇḍasikkāsammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Authorization for a staff and a sling has been given by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

273. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu romanthako romaṭṭhako (ka.) hoti. So romanthitvā romanthitvā ajjhoharati. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “vikālāyaṃ kathaṃ hi nāma vikālāyaṃ(ka.) bhikkhu bhojanaṃ bhuñjatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Eso, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aciraṃgoyoniyā [T 2.0058] cuto. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, romanthakassa romanthanaṃ. Na ca, bhikkhave, bahimukhadvāraṃ nīharitvā ajjhoharitabbaṃ. Yo ajjhohareyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

273. At that time, a certain bhikkhu was a ruminator. He would ruminate again and again and then swallow it. The bhikkhus complained, grumbled, and criticized: “This bhikkhu eats food at the wrong time.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, this bhikkhu has not long ago passed away from the bovine species. I allow, bhikkhus, a ruminator to ruminate. But, bhikkhus, having brought it out of the mouth, it should not be swallowed. Whoever should swallow it is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma.”

Tena [M 0.0273] kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti. Bhattagge bahusitthāni pakiriyiṃsu vippakirīyiṃsu (sī.), parikiriṃsu (syā.). Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā odane diyyamāne na sakkaccaṃ paṭiggahessanti, ekamekaṃ sitthaṃ kammasatena niṭṭhāyatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū [P 2.0133] tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ diyyamānaṃ patati, taṃ sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjituṃ. Pariccattaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, dāyakehī”ti.

At that time, a certain group was offering a meal to the Saṅgha. In the dining hall, many grains of cooked rice were scattered about. People complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can these Sakyan ascetics not carefully accept the rice when it is being given? Each single grain of cooked rice is brought to completion by a hundred acts of labor!” The bhikkhus heard these people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, to pick up and consume what falls while being given. That, bhikkhus, has been relinquished by the donors.”

274. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu dīghehi nakhehi piṇḍāya carati. Aññatarā itthī passitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “ehi, bhante, methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevā”ti. “Alaṃ, bhagini, netaṃ kappatī”ti. “Sace kho tvaṃ, bhante, nappaṭisevissasi, idānāhaṃ attano nakhehi gattāni vilikhitvā kuppaṃ karissāmi – ayaṃ maṃ bhikkhu vippakarotī”ti. “Pajānāhi [V 0.0254] tvaṃ, bhaginī”ti. Atha kho sā itthī [T 2.0059] attano nakhehi gattāni vilikhitvā kuppaṃ akāsi – ayaṃ maṃ bhikkhu vippakarotīti. Manussā upadhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ aggahesuṃ. Addasāsuṃ kho te manussā tassā itthiyā nakhe chavimpi lohitampi. Disvāna – imissāyeva itthiyā idaṃ kammaṃ, akārako bhikkhūti – taṃ bhikkhuṃ muñciṃsu. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, dīghe nakhe dhāresī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu dīghe nakhe dhāressasī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, dīghā nakhā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

274. At that time, a certain monk with long nails was walking for alms. A certain woman saw that monk and said to him: “Come, venerable sir, let us engage in sexual intercourse.” “Enough, sister, that is not allowable.” “If you, venerable sir, do not comply, then I will scratch my body with my own nails and make a commotion—‘This monk has violated me!’” “You know what you are doing, sister.” Then that woman scratched her body with her own nails and made a commotion—‘This monk has violated me!’ People came running and seized that monk. They saw skin and blood on the woman’s nails. Having seen this, and thinking, “This is the deed of this very woman; the monk is not the doer,” they released that monk. Then that monk went to the monastery and informed the monks of the matter. “Friend, do you keep long nails?” “Yes, friends.” Those monks who were modest… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How can a monk keep long nails?” Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, long nails should not be kept. Whoever keeps them incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū nakhenapi nakhaṃ chindanti, mukhenapi nakhaṃ chindanti, kuṭṭepi ghaṃsanti. Aṅguliyo dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nakhacchedana”nti. Salohitaṃ nakhaṃ chindanti. Aṅguliyo dukkhā honti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, maṃsappamāṇena nakhaṃ chinditu”nti.

At that time, monks were cutting nails with their nails, biting nails with their mouths, and rubbing them against walls. Their fingers and toes became painful. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, a nail-cutter.” They cut their nails until they bled. Their fingers and toes became painful… “I allow, monks, to cut the nails to the measure of the flesh.”

Tena [M 0.0274] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vīsatimaṭṭhaṃ vīsatimaṭṭaṃ (sī.) kārāpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na[T 2.0060], bhikkhave, vīsatimaṭṭhaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, malamattaṃ apakaḍḍhitu”nti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were having their twenty nails polished. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the twenty nails should not be polished. Whoever should have it done, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, the removal of just the dirt.”

275. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ kesā dīghā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Ussahanti pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ kese oropetu”nti? “Ussahanti bhagavā”ti[P 2.0134]. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā…pe… bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khuraṃ khurasilaṃ khurasipāṭikaṃ namatakaṃ sabbaṃ khurabhaṇḍa”nti.

275. At that time, the monks’ hair was long. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, are the monks able to cut one another’s hair?” “They are able, Blessed One.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having convened the Sangha of monks, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, a razor, a razor-sharpening stone, a razor case, a wrapping cloth, and all razor equipment.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū massuṃ kappāpenti…pe… massuṃ vaḍḍhāpenti… golomikaṃ kārāpenti… caturassakaṃ kārāpenti… parimukhaṃ kārāpenti… aḍḍhadukaṃ aḍḍhurakaṃ (sī.), aḍḍharukaṃ (syā.) kārāpenti… dāṭhikaṃ ṭhapenti… sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave[V 0.0255], massu kappāpetabbaṃ…pe… na massu vaḍḍhāpetabbaṃ… na golomikaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ… na caturassakaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ… na parimukhaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ… na aḍḍhadukaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ… na dāṭhikā ṭhapetabbā… na sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpetabbaṃ. Yo saṃharāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six had their beards trimmed... let their beards grow... had a goat-beard style made... had a square style made... had their chest-hair shaved... had a pattern of chest-hair left... kept side-whiskers... had hair shaved in a private area. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a beard should not be trimmed... a beard should not be grown... a goat-beard style should not be made... a square style should not be made... chest-hair should not be shaved... a pattern of chest-hair should not be left... side-whiskers should not be kept... hair in a private area should not be shaved. Whoever should have it shaved commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno sambādhe vaṇo hoti. Bhesajjaṃ na santiṭṭhati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 2.0061]. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpetu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk had a wound in a private area. Medicine would not stay on it. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, on account of illness, to have hair shaved in a private area.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kattarikāya kese chedāpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, kattarikāya kesā chedāpetabbā. Yo chedāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were having their hair cut with scissors. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, hair is not to be cut with scissors. Whichever monk should have it cut, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena [M 0.0275] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno sīse vaṇo hoti, na sakkoti khurena kese oropetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā kattarikāya kese chedāpetu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk had a wound on his head and was not able to have his hair removed with a razor. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, on account of illness, to have the hair cut with scissors.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dīghāni nāsikālomāni dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi pisācillikāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, dīghaṃ nāsikālomaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were keeping long nose hairs. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like goblins!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, long nose hair is not to be kept. Whichever monk should keep it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sakkharikāyapi madhusitthakenapi nāsikālomaṃ gāhāpenti. Nāsikā dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṇḍāsa”nti.

At that time, monks were having their nose hair removed with a pebble and with beeswax. Their noses became sore. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, tweezers.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū palitaṃ gāhāpenti[T 2.0062]. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, palitaṃ gāhāpetabbaṃ. Yo gāhāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were having their grey hair removed. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, grey hair is not to be removed. Whichever monk should have it removed, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

276. Tena [V 0.0256] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno kaṇṇagūthakehi kaṇṇā thakitā honti[P 2.0135]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaṇṇamalaharaṇi”nti.

276. At that time, a certain monk’s ears were blocked with earwax. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an ear-cleaner.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacā kaṇṇamalaharaṇiyo dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā kaṇṇamalaharaṇiyo dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ dantamayaṃ visāṇamayaṃ naḷamayaṃ veḷumayaṃ kaṭṭhamayaṃ jatumayaṃ phalamayaṃ lohamayaṃ saṅkhanābhimaya”nti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were using various kinds of ear-cleaners made of gold and silver. People complained, grumbled, and criticized them, saying: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of ear-cleaners are not to be used. Whoever should use one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, those made of bone, ivory, horn, reed, bamboo, wood, lac, fruit, metal, or the center of a conch shell.”

277. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bahuṃ lohabhaṇḍaṃ kaṃsabhaṇḍaṃ sannicayaṃ karonti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bahuṃ lohabhaṇḍaṃ kaṃsabhaṇḍaṃ sannicayaṃ karissanti[T 2.0063], seyyathāpi [M 0.0276] kaṃsapattharikā”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bahuṃ lohabhaṇḍaṃ kaṃsabhaṇḍaṃ sannicayo kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

277. At that time, the monks of the group of six were accumulating a great quantity of ironware and bronze ware. People wandering on a tour of the monasteries saw this and complained, grumbled, and criticized them, saying: “How indeed can the Sakyan ascetics accumulate a great quantity of ironware and bronze ware, just like bronze merchants!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a great accumulation of ironware and bronze ware is not to be made. Whoever should do so incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū añjanimpi añjanisalākampi kaṇṇamalaharaṇimpi bandhanamattampi kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, añjaniṃ añjanisalākaṃ kaṇṇamalaharaṇiṃ bandhanamatta”nti.

At that time, monks were scrupulous about even an eye-ointment pot, an eye-ointment applicator, an ear-cleaner, or a mere binding. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an eye-ointment pot, an eye-ointment applicator, an ear-cleaner, and a mere binding.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghāṭipallatthikāya nisīdanti. Saṅghāṭiyā pattā lujjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, saṅghāṭipallatthikāya nisīditabbaṃ. Yo nisīdeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were sitting using the outer robe as a binding for the cross-legged posture. The hems of the outer robes were becoming frayed. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one should not sit using the outer robe as a binding for the cross-legged posture. Whoever should sit so incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Tassa vinā āyogena āyogā (sī. syā.) na phāsu hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āyoga”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho āyogo kātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tantakaṃ vemaṃ kavaṭaṃ vemakaṃ vaṭṭaṃ (sī.), vemakaṃ vaṭaṃ (syā.) salākaṃ sabbaṃ tantabhaṇḍaka”nti.

At that time, a certain monk was sick. He was not comfortable without a supporting strap. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a supporting strap.” Then this thought arose in the monks: “How, indeed, should a supporting strap be made?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a loom, a shuttle, a board, a rod, and all the equipment of a weaver.”

278. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu akāyabandhano gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tassa rathikāya antaravāsako pabhassittha. Manussā ukkuṭṭhimakaṃsu[T 2.0064]. So bhikkhu maṅku [V 0.0257] ahosi[P 2.0136]. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, akāyabandhanena gāmo pavisitabbo. Yo paviseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kāyabandhana”nti.

278. At that time, a certain monk entered a village for alms without a waistband. On the main road, his lower robe fell down. People made a commotion. That monk was embarrassed. Then that monk went to the monastery and told this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a village should not be entered without a waistband. Whoever should enter, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow a waistband.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacāni kāyabandhanāni dhārenti – kalābukaṃ, deḍḍubhakaṃ, murajaṃ, maddavīṇaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacāni kāyabandhanāni dhāretabbāni – kalābukaṃ, deḍḍubhakaṃ, murajaṃ, maddavīṇaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve kāyabandhanāni – paṭṭikaṃ, sūkarantaka”nti. Kāyabandhanassa dasā [M 0.0277] jīranti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, murajaṃ maddavīṇa”nti. Kāyabandhanassa anto jīrati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sobhaṇaṃ guṇaka”nti. Kāyabandhanassa pavananto jīrati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vidha”nti vīthanti (sī. syā.).

At that time, the group-of-six monks were wearing various kinds of waistbands: a waistband of many strands, one shaped like a water-snake’s head, one shaped like a drum, and one shaped like a round chisel handle. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “Just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of waistbands should not be worn: a waistband of many strands, one shaped like a water-snake’s head, one shaped like a drum, and one shaped like a round chisel handle. Whoever wears one commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow two kinds of waistbands: a flat band and one shaped like a pig’s intestine.” The fringes of the waistband wore out… “Monks, I allow the drum-shaped and the round-chisel-handle-shaped for the fringes.” The edge of the waistband wore out… “Monks, I allow hemming and cord-like stitching.” The loop-end of the waistband wore out… “Monks, I allow a clasp.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace vidhe dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [T 2.0065] vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā vidhā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ…pe… saṅkhanābhimayaṃ suttamaya”nti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six wore various kinds of clasps: made of gold, made of silver. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying, “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of clasps should not be worn. Whoever should wear one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow one made of bone... of conch-shell, and of thread.”

279. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando lahukā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Vātamaṇḍalikāya saṅghāṭiyo ukkhipiyiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā ānando ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gaṇṭhikaṃ pāsaka”nti.

279. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having put on light outer robes, entered the village for alms. A gust of wind lifted up his outer robes. Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the monastery and informed the monks about this matter. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a button and a loop.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacā gaṇṭhikāyo dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā gaṇṭhikā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ dantamayaṃ visāṇamayaṃ naḷamayaṃ veḷumayaṃ kaṭṭhamayaṃ jatumayaṃ phalamayaṃ lohamayaṃ saṅkhanābhimayaṃ suttamaya”nti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six wore various kinds of buttons: made of gold, made of silver. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying, “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of buttons should not be worn. Whoever should wear one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow buttons made of bone, of ivory, of horn, of reed, of bamboo, of wood, of lac, of fruit, of metal, of conch-shell, and of thread.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gaṇṭhikampi pāsakampi cīvare [T 2.0066] appenti. Cīvaraṃ jīrati[V 0.0258]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gaṇṭhikaphalakaṃ pāsakaphalaka”nti. Gaṇṭhikaphalakampi [P 2.0137] pāsakaphalakampi ante appenti. Koṭṭo koṇo (sī. syā.) vivariyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gaṇṭhikaphalakaṃ ante appetuṃ; pāsakaphalakaṃ sattaṅgulaṃ vā aṭṭhaṅgulaṃ vā ogāhetvā appetu”nti.

At that time, monks were attaching both the fastener and the clasp to their robes. The robe wore out. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a fastener-plate and a clasp-plate.” They attached both the fastener-plate and the clasp-plate at the edge. The hem opened up. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow the fastener-plate to be attached at the edge, and the clasp-plate to be attached after setting it back by seven or eight finger-breadths.”

280. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū gihinivatthaṃ nivāsenti – hatthisoṇḍakaṃ, macchavāḷakaṃ, catukaṇṇakaṃ, tālavaṇṭakaṃ, satavalikaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti [M 0.0278] khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, gihinivatthaṃ nivāsetabbaṃ – hatthisoṇḍakaṃ, macchavāḷakaṃ, catukaṇṇakaṃ, tālavaṇṭakaṃ, satavalikaṃ. Yo nivāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

280. At that time, the monks of the group-of-six wore their lower robes in the manner of laypeople: with a part hanging down like an elephant's trunk, like a fish's tail, with four corners hanging down, like a palm-leaf fan, and with many pleats. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “Just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the lower robe should not be worn in the manner of laypeople: with a part hanging down like an elephant's trunk, like a fish's tail, with four corners hanging down, like a palm-leaf fan, and with many pleats. Whatever monk should wear it thus, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū gihipārutaṃ pārupanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, gihipārutaṃ pārupitabbaṃ. Yo pārupeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group-of-six draped their upper robes in the manner of laypeople. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “Just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the upper robe should not be draped in the manner of laypeople. Whatever monk should drape it thus, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṃvelliyaṃ nivāsenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi [T 2.0067] rañño muṇḍavaṭṭīti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, saṃvelliyaṃ nivāsetabbaṃ. Yo nivāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks of the group-of-six wore their lower robes tucked up. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “Just like the king's porters!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the lower robe should not be worn tucked up. Whatever monk should wear it thus, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

281. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ubhatokājaṃ haranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi rañño muṇḍavaṭṭīti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ubhatokājaṃ haritabbaṃ. Yo hareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekatokājaṃ antarākājaṃ sīsabhāraṃ khandhabhāraṃ kaṭibhāraṃ olambaka”nti.

281. At that time, the monks of the group-of-six carried things using a carrying-pole with loads on both ends. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “Just like the king's porters!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a carrying-pole with loads on both ends should not be used. Whatever monk should carry things thus, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow a carrying-pole with a load on one end, a load in the middle of a pole, a load carried on the head, a load carried on the shoulder, a load carried on the hip, and a load carried hanging down.”

282. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dantakaṭṭhaṃ na khādanti. Mukhaṃ duggandhaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

282. At that time, the monks did not chew tooth-sticks. Their mouths became foul-smelling. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

“Pañcime[V 0.0259], bhikkhave, ādīnavā dantakaṭṭhassa akhādane. Acakkhussaṃ, mukhaṃ duggandhaṃ hoti, rasaharaṇiyo na visujjhanti, pittaṃ semhaṃ bhattaṃ pariyonandhati, bhattamassa nacchādeti – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā dantakaṭṭhassa akhādane.

“Monks, there are these five drawbacks in not using a tooth-stick. One’s eyesight is impaired, the mouth becomes foul-smelling, the taste buds are not cleansed, bile and phlegm envelop the food, and one does not delight in the food. These, monks, are the five drawbacks in not using a tooth-stick.”

“Pañcime, bhikkhave, ānisaṃsā dantakaṭṭhassa khādane. Cakkhussaṃ, mukhaṃ na duggandhaṃ hoti, rasaharaṇiyo visujjhanti, pittaṃ semhaṃ bhattaṃ na pariyonandhati, bhattamassa chādeti [P 2.0138] – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṃsā dantakaṭṭhassa khādane. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dantakaṭṭha”nti.

“Monks, there are these five benefits in using a tooth-stick. It is good for the eyesight, the mouth does not become foul-smelling, the taste buds are cleansed, bile and phlegm do not envelop the food, and one delights in the food. These, monks, are the five benefits in using a tooth-stick. Monks, I allow a tooth-stick.”

Tena [T 2.0068] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dīghāni dantakaṭṭhāni khādanti, teheva sāmaṇeraṃ ākoṭenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na[M 0.0279], bhikkhave, dīghaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ khāditabbaṃ. Yo khādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgulaparamaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ, na ca tena sāmaṇero ākoṭetabbo. Yo ākoṭeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were using long tooth-sticks, and with those very ones they would strike a novice. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a long tooth-stick should not be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow a tooth-stick of at most eight fingerbreadths in length, and a novice should not be struck with it. Whoever should strike one, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno atimaṭāhakaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādantassa kaṇṭhe vilaggaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, atimaṭāhakaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ khāditabbaṃ. Yo khādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, caturaṅgulapacchimaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ pacchimaṃ (ka.) dantakaṭṭha”nti.

At that time, a certain monk, while using a very short tooth-stick, got it stuck in his throat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a very short tooth-stick should not be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow a tooth-stick that is at least four fingerbreadths long.”

283. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dāyaṃ ālimpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi davaḍāhakāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, dāyo ālimpitabbo. Yo ālimpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

283. At that time, the group-of-six monks were setting fire to a woodland. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying, “Just like those who set fire to the forest!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a woodland should not be set on fire. Whoever should set it on fire, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena vihārā tiṇagahanā honti, davaḍāhe ḍayhamāne vihārā ḍayhanti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyanti paṭaggiṃ [T 2.0069] dātuṃ, parittaṃ kātuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, davaḍāhe ḍayhamāne paṭaggiṃ dātuṃ, parittaṃ kātu”nti.

At that time, the monasteries were overgrown with grass. When a forest fire was burning, the monasteries were burned. The monks were scrupulous about setting a counter-fire and making a protective barrier. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you, when a forest fire is burning, to set a counter-fire and to make a protective barrier.”

284. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū rukkhaṃ abhiruhanti, rukkhā rukkhaṃ saṅkamanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi makkaṭāti. Bhagavato [V 0.0260] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, rukkho abhiruhitabbo. Yo abhiruheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

284. At that time, the group-of-six monks were climbing trees and crossing from tree to tree. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “Just like monkeys!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a tree is not to be climbed. Whichever monk should climb one, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchantassa antarāmagge hatthī pariyuṭṭhāti. Atha kho so bhikkhu rukkhamūlaṃ upadhāvitvā kukkuccāyanto rukkhaṃ na abhiruhi. So hatthī aññena agamāsi. Atha kho so bhikkhu sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati karaṇīye porisaṃ rukkhaṃ abhiruhituṃ āpadāsu yāvadattha”nti.

At that time, as a certain monk was going to Sāvatthī in the country of the Kosalans, he was pursued by an elephant on the way. Then that monk, having run up to the foot of a tree, being scrupulous, did not climb the tree. That elephant went another way. Then that monk, having gone to Sāvatthī, told this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit you to climb a tree to the height of a man when there is a reason, and in times of danger, to climb as high as is needed.'

285. Tena [P 2.0139][M 0.0280] kho pana samayena yameḷakekuṭā nāma yameḷutekulā nāma (sī.), meṭṭhakokuṭṭhā nāma (syā.) bhikkhū dve bhātikā honti brāhmaṇajātikā kalyāṇavācā kalyāṇavākkaraṇā. Te yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho [T 2.0070] te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “etarahi, bhante, bhikkhū nānānāmā nānāgottā nānājaccā nānākulā pabbajitā. Te sakāya niruttiyā buddhavacanaṃ dūsenti. Handa mayaṃ, bhante, buddhavacanaṃ chandaso āropemā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, evaṃ vakkhatha – ‘handa mayaṃ, bhante, buddhavacanaṃ chandaso āropemā’ti. Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, buddhavacanaṃ chandaso āropetabbaṃ. Yo āropeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sakāya niruttiyā buddhavacanaṃ pariyāpuṇitu”nti.

285. Now at that time, in the village of Yameḷaka, there were two brothers named Kuṭa, monks of the brahmin caste, who had pleasant speech and a fine voice. They approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, at present, monks of various names, various clans, various castes, and from various families have gone forth. They corrupt the Buddha’s words with their own dialects. Come, venerable sir, let us render the Buddha’s words into Sanskrit.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can you, foolish men, say this: ‘Come, venerable sir, let us render the Buddha’s words into Sanskrit’? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…” Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, the Buddha’s words are not to be rendered into Sanskrit. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I permit, monks, that the Buddha’s words be learned in one’s own dialect.”

286. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū lokāyataṃ pariyāpuṇanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Api nu kho, bhikkhave, lokāyate sāradassāvī imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyā”ti? “Nohetaṃ bhante”. “Imasmiṃ vā pana dhammavinaye sāradassāvī lokāyataṃ pariyāpuṇeyyā”ti? “Nohetaṃ bhante”. “Na, bhikkhave, lokāyataṃ pariyāpuṇitabbaṃ. Yo pariyāpuṇeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

286. At that time the group-of-six monks were learning Lokāyata. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them: “Just like householders indulging in sensual pleasures!” The monks heard these people complaining, criticizing, and disparaging. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, could one who finds essence in Lokāyata attain growth, increase, and abundance in this Dhamma-Vinaya?” “No, venerable sir.” “Or could one who finds essence in this Dhamma-Vinaya learn Lokāyata?” “No, venerable sir.” “Monks, Lokāyata should not be learned. Whoever learns it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena [T 2.0071] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū lokāyataṃ vācenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [V 0.0261] vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, lokāyataṃ vācetabbaṃ. Yo vāceyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching Lokāyata. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, Lokāyata is not to be taught. Whoever should teach it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

287. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti[M 0.0281]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, tiracchānavijjā pariyāpuṇitabbā. Yo pariyāpuṇeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

287. At that time, the group-of-six monks were learning worldly arts. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, worldly arts are not to be learned. Whoever should learn them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tiracchānavijjaṃ vācenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, tiracchānavijjā vācetabbā. Yo vāceyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching worldly arts. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, worldly arts are not to be taught. Whoever should teach them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

288. Tena kho pana [P 2.0140] samayena bhagavā mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṃ desento khipi. Bhikkhū – ‘jīvatu, bhante, bhagavā; jīvatu sugato’ti – uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ akaṃsu. Tena saddena dhammakathā antarā ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “api nu kho, bhikkhave, khipite ‘jīvā’ti vutto vutte (ka.) tappaccayā jīveyya vā [T 2.0072] mareyya vā”ti? “Nohetaṃ bhante”. “Na, bhikkhave, khipite ‘jīvā’ti vattabbo. Yo vadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

288. At that time, the Blessed One was teaching the Dhamma surrounded by a large assembly when he sneezed. The monks—saying, “May the Blessed One live, venerable sir! May the Well-farer live!”—made a loud noise, a great noise. Because of that noise, the Dhamma talk was interrupted. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, when someone has sneezed and is told ‘Live!’, does that cause them to live or to die?” “That is not so, venerable sir.” “Monks, when one has sneezed, ‘Live!’ is not to be said. Whoever should say so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhikkhūnaṃ khipite ‘jīvatha bhante’ti vadanti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nālapanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā ‘jīvatha bhante’ti vuccamānā nālapissantī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Gihī, bhikkhave, maṅgalikā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gihīnaṃ ‘jīvatha bhante’ti vuccamānena ‘ciraṃ jīvā’ti vattu”nti.

At that time, people would say to the monks when they sneezed, “Live long, venerable sirs!” The monks, being scrupulous, did not respond. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them: “How can these Sakyan ascetics not respond when told, ‘Live long, venerable sirs’!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, householders are fond of auspicious words. I permit, monks, that when householders say, ‘Live long, venerable sirs,’ you may respond, ‘May you live long.’”

289. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṃ desento nisinno hoti. Aññatarena bhikkhunā lasuṇaṃ khāyitaṃ hoti. So – mā bhikkhū byābādhiṃsūti – ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Addasā kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekamantaṃ nisinno”ti[V 0.0262]? “Etena, bhante, bhikkhunā lasuṇaṃ khāyitaṃ. So – mā bhikkhū byābādhiṃsūti – ekamantaṃ nisinno”ti. “Api nu kho, bhikkhave bhikkhave bhikkhunā (syā.), taṃ khāditabbaṃ, yaṃ khāditvā evarūpāya dhammakathāya paribāhiyo assā”ti? “Nohetaṃ bhante”. “Na, bhikkhave, lasuṇaṃ khāditabbaṃ. Yo khādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

289. At that time, the Blessed One was seated, teaching the Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly. A certain monk had eaten garlic. Thinking, “Lest the monks be disturbed,” he sat to one side. The Blessed One saw that monk seated to one side. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: “Why, monks, is that monk sitting to one side?” “Venerable sir, this monk has eaten garlic. Thinking, ‘Lest the monks be disturbed,’ he is sitting to one side.” “Monks, should that be eaten, which, having been eaten, would cause one to be excluded from such a Dhamma talk?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.” “Monks, garlic should not be eaten. Whoever should eat it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena [T 2.0073][M 0.0282] kho pana samayena āyasmato sāriputtassa udaravātābādho hoti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “pubbe te, āvuso sāriputta, udaravātābādho kena phāsu hotī”ti? “Lasuṇena me, āvuso”ti atha kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca “pubbe kho me āvuso moggallāna udaravātābādho lasuṇena phāsu hotī”ti (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā lasuṇaṃ khāditu”nti.

At that time, the Venerable Sāriputta had an illness of wind in the stomach. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna went to where the Venerable Sāriputta was. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, previously, by what was your illness of wind in the stomach relieved?” “By garlic, friend.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow garlic to be eaten on account of illness.”

290. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ārāme tahaṃ tahaṃ passāvaṃ karonti. Ārāmo dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekamantaṃ passāvaṃ kātu”nti[P 2.0141]. Ārāmo duggandho hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, passāvakumbhi”nti. Dukkhaṃ nisinnā passāvaṃ karonti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, passāvapāduka”nti. Passāvapādukā pākaṭā honti. Bhikkhū hiriyanti passāvaṃ kātuṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo pākāre – iṭṭhakāpākāraṃ, silāpākāraṃ, dārupākāra”nti. Passāvakumbhī apārutā duggandhā hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhāna”nti.

290. At that time, monks were urinating here and there in the monastery. The monastery became defiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow urinating in a secluded place.” The monastery became foul-smelling… “Monks, I allow a urinal pot.” They were uncomfortable sitting while urinating… “Monks, I allow a urinal foot-stand.” The urinal foot-stands were conspicuous. The monks were ashamed to urinate… “Monks, I allow enclosing it with three kinds of walls—a brick wall, a stone wall, and a wooden wall.” The urinal pot, being uncovered, became foul-smelling… “Monks, I allow a lid.”

291. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ārāme tahaṃ tahaṃ vaccaṃ karonti. Ārāmo dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi[T 2.0074], bhikkhave, ekamantaṃ vaccaṃ kātu”nti. Ārāmo duggandho hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaccakūpa”nti. Vaccakūpassa kūlaṃ lujjati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Vaccakūpo nīcavatthuko hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Ante nisinnā vaccaṃ karontā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santharitvā majjhe chiddaṃ katvā vaccaṃ kātu”nti[V 0.0263]. Dukkhaṃ nisinnā vaccaṃ karonti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaccapāduka”nti. Bahiddhā passāvaṃ [M 0.0283] karonti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, passāvadoṇika”nti. Avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, avalekhanakaṭṭha”nti. Avalekhanapiṭharo na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, avalekhanapiṭhara”nti. Vaccakūpo apāruto duggandho hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhāna”nti. Ajjhokāse vaccaṃ karontā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti…pe… [T 2.0075] “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaccakuṭi”nti. Vaccakuṭiyā kavāṭaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsakaṃ aggaḷavaṭṭiṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭikaṃ tāḷacchiddaṃ āviñchanacchiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti. Vaccakuṭiyā tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti.

291. At that time, monks were relieving themselves here and there in the monastery. The monastery became defiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you to relieve yourselves in a secluded place.” The monastery became foul-smelling… “Monks, I allow a latrine pit.” The bank of the latrine pit collapsed… “Monks, I allow you to build three kinds of linings: a brick lining, a stone lining, and a wood lining.” The latrine pit was low-lying and would get flooded with water… “Monks, I allow it to be made elevated.” The lining collapsed… “Monks, I allow you to build three kinds of linings: a brick lining, a stone lining, and a wood lining.” Those climbing up were weary… “Monks, I allow three kinds of staircases: a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wood staircase.” Those climbing up would fall… “Monks, I allow a handrail.” Those sitting at the edge while relieving themselves would fall… “Monks, I allow you to relieve yourselves after spreading something out and making a hole in the middle.” They relieved themselves while sitting with difficulty… “Monks, I allow a latrine foot-board.” They were urinating outside… “Monks, I allow a urinal.” There was no wiping stick… “Monks, I allow a wiping stick.” There was no basket for wiping sticks… “Monks, I allow a basket for wiping sticks.” The latrine pit, being uncovered, became foul-smelling… “Monks, I allow a cover.” Those relieving themselves in the open were afflicted by both cold and heat… “Monks, I allow a latrine hut.” The latrine hut had no door… “Monks, I allow a door-leaf, a doorpost, a pivot socket, a lintel socket, a bolt-post, a clasp, a pin and socket, a keyhole, a hole for a pull-cord, and a pull-cord.” Grass and dust would fall into the latrine hut… “Monks, I allow that, after brushing it down, it be plastered inside and out, and that you make whitewash, black coloring, red-ochre work, garland patterns, creeper patterns, makara-tooth patterns, five-panel patterns, a robe-pole, and a robe-line.”

292. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu jarādubbalo vaccaṃ katvā vuṭṭhahanto [P 2.0142] paripatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, olambaka”nti. Vaccakuṭi aparikkhittā hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo pākāre – iṭṭhakāpākāraṃ, silāpākāraṃ, dārupākāra”nti. Koṭṭhako na hoti…pe… (“anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koṭṭhaka”nti. Koṭṭhakassa kavāṭaṃ na [T 2.0076] hoti) (anujānāmi bhikkhave koṭṭhakanti. koṭṭhako nīcavatthuko hoti…pe… anujānāmi bhikkhave uccavatthukaṃ kātunti. cayo paripatati…pe… anujānāmi bhikkhave cinituṃ tayo caye iṭṭhakācayaṃ silācayaṃ dārucayanti. ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… anujānāmi bhikkhave tayo sopāne iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ silāsopānaṃ dārusopānanti. ārohantā paripatanti…pe… anujānāmi bhikkhave ālambanabāhanti. koṭṭhakassa kavāṭaṃ na hoti.) (syā. kaṃ.) …pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsakaṃ aggaḷavaṭṭiṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭikaṃ tāḷacchiddaṃ āviñchanacchiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti. Koṭṭhake tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭika”nti. Pariveṇaṃ cikkhallaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, marumbaṃ pakiritu”nti. Na pariyāpuṇanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, padarasilaṃ paṭṭasilaṃ (ka.) nikkhipitu”nti. Udakaṃ santiṭṭhati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamana”nti. Ācamanakumbhī na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācamanakumbhi”nti. Ācamanasarāvako [M 0.0284] na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācamanasarāvaka”nti. Dukkhaṃ nisinnā ācamenti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācamanapāduka”nti. Ācamanapādukā pākaṭā honti, bhikkhū hiriyanti ācametuṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo pākāre [V 0.0264] – iṭṭhakāpākāraṃ, silāpākāraṃ, dārupākāra”nti. Ācamanakumbhī apārutā hoti, tiṇacuṇṇehipi paṃsukehipi okiriyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhāna”nti.

292. At that time, a certain elderly and weak monk, having relieved himself, fell down while getting up. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, a handrail.” The latrine hut was not enclosed… “I allow, monks, to enclose it with three types of walls—a brick wall, a stone wall, or a wooden wall.” There was no porch… (“I allow, monks, a porch.” The porch had no door…) “I allow, monks, a door, a doorjamb, a pivot socket, an upper staple, a post for the bolt, a monkey-head hasp, a pin, a bolt, a keyhole, a hole for a pull-string, and a pull-string.” Grass dust fell in the porch… “I allow, monks, having swept it down, to have it plastered inside and out with whitewash, black coloring, red-ochre work, garland-work, creeper-work, sea-monster tooth patterns, and five-panel patterns.” The enclosure was muddy… “I allow, monks, to scatter gravel.” It was insufficient… “I allow, monks, to place a flagstone.” Water stagnated… “I allow, monks, a drain.” There was no water-pot for washing… “I allow, monks, a water-pot for washing.” There was no water dipper for washing… “I allow, monks, a water dipper for washing.” They washed while sitting with difficulty… “I allow, monks, a footrest for washing.” The footrest for washing was exposed, and the monks were ashamed to wash… “I allow, monks, to enclose it with three types of walls—a brick wall, a stone wall, or a wooden wall.” The water-pot for washing was uncovered, and was strewn with grass and dust… “I allow, monks, a cover.”

293. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācaranti – mālāvacchaṃ ropentipi ropāpentipi, siñcantipi siñcāpentipi, ocinantipi ocināpentipi, ganthentipi ganthāpentipi, ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ karontipi [T 2.0077] kārāpentipi, mañjarikaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, vidhūtikaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, āveḷaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, uracchadaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi. Te kulitthīnaṃ kuladhītānaṃ kulakumārīnaṃ kulasuṇhānaṃ kuladāsīnaṃ ekatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, mañjarikaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, vidhūtikaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, vaṭaṃsakaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, āveḷaṃ harantipi harāpentipi, uracchadaṃ harantipi harāpentipi. Te kulitthīhi kuladhītāhi kulakumārīhi kulasuṇhāhi kuladāsīhi saddhiṃ ekabhājanepi bhuñjanti, ekathālakepi pivanti, ekāsanepi nisīdanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, vikālepi bhuñjanti, majjampi pivanti, mālāgandhavilepanampi dhārenti, naccantipi, gāyantipi, vādentipi, lāsentipi; naccantiyāpi naccanti, naccantiyāpi gāyanti, naccantiyāpi vādenti, naccantiyāpi lāsenti…pe… lāsentiyāpi naccanti, lāsentiyāpi gāyanti, lāsentiyāpi vādenti, lāsentiyāpi lāsenti; aṭṭhapadepi kīḷanti, dasapadepi kīḷanti, ākāsepi kīḷanti, parihārapathepi kīḷanti, santikāyapi kīḷanti, khalikāyapi kīḷanti, ghaṭikāyapi kīḷanti, salākahatthenapi kīḷanti, akkhenapi kīḷanti, paṅgacīrenapi kīḷanti, vaṅkakenapi kīḷanti, mokkhacikāyapi kīḷanti, ciṅgulakenapi kīḷanti, pattāḷhakenapi kīḷanti, rathakenapi kīḷanti, dhanukenapi kīḷanti[T 2.0078], akkharikāyapi kīḷanti, manesikāyapi kīḷanti, yathāvajjenapi kīḷanti; hatthismimpi sikkhanti, assasmimpi sikkhanti, rathasmimpi sikkhanti, dhanusmimpi [M 0.0285] sikkhanti; tharusmimpi sikkhanti; hatthissapi purato dhāvanti, assassapi purato dhāvanti, rathassapi purato dhāvantipi ādhāvantipi; usseḷentipi, apphoṭentipi, nibbujjhantipi, muṭṭhīhipi yujjhanti; raṅgamajjhepi saṅghāṭiṃ pattharitvā naccakiṃ evaṃ vadanti – “idha, bhagini, naccassū”ti; nalāṭikampi denti; vividhampi anācāraṃ ācaranti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “na, bhikkhave, vividhaṃ anācāraṃ ācaritabbaṃ. Yo ācareyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

293. At that time, the monks of the group of six engaged in such improper conduct—they planted flower plants themselves or had them planted, watered them or had them watered, picked flowers themselves or had them picked, strung garlands themselves or had them strung, made single-stalk garlands themselves or had them made, made double-stalk garlands themselves or had them made, made bouquets themselves or had them made, made flower bracelets themselves or had them made, made flower head-dresses themselves or had them made, made ear-pendants of flowers themselves or had them made, and made chest-garlands of flowers themselves or had them made. For the sake of women of good families, daughters of good families, young women of good families, daughters-in-law of good families, and female servants of good families, they carried single-stalk garlands themselves or had them carried, carried double-stalk garlands themselves or had them carried, carried bouquets themselves or had them carried, carried flower bracelets themselves or had them carried, carried flower head-dresses themselves or had them carried, carried ear-pendants of flowers themselves or had them carried, and carried chest-garlands of flowers themselves or had them carried. With these women, they ate from the same bowl, drank from the same cup, sat on the same seat, lay on the same bed, lay on the same sheet, lay under the same cloak, and lay on the same sheet and under the same cloak. They also ate at the wrong time, drank intoxicants, and wore garlands, perfumes, and ointments. They danced, sang, played musical instruments, and made playful gestures. They danced along with a dancing woman, sang along with a dancing woman, played musical instruments along with a dancing woman, and made playful gestures along with a dancing woman… and so on… they danced along with a woman making playful gestures, sang along with a woman making playful gestures, played musical instruments along with a woman making playful gestures, and made playful gestures along with a woman making playful gestures. They played on an eight-square board, played on a ten-square board, played a game of imagining figures in the air, played a game of moving through a diagram without touching the lines, played with marbles, played dice on a board, played tip-cat, played a game of marking with a painted hand or stick, played with dice, played by blowing on a pipe made of palm leaves, played with a toy plough, did somersaults, played with a pinwheel made of palm leaves, played with toy leaf-measures, played with a toy chariot, played with a toy bow, played a game of guessing letters, played a game of guessing thoughts, and played by mimicking the afflicted. They trained in elephantry, horsemanship, charioteering, archery, and swordsmanship. They ran in front of an elephant, ran in front of a horse, and ran in front of and towards a chariot. They shouted challenges, slapped their arms, wrestled, and fought with their fists. In the middle of an arena, they would spread out their double-layered robe and say to a dancing girl, ‘Sister, dance here on this robe of mine!’ They also gave a snap on the forehead. They engaged in various kinds of improper conduct. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘Monks, various kinds of improper conduct should not be engaged in. Whoever should engage in it should be dealt with according to the Dhamma.’”

Tena [V 0.0265] kho pana samayena āyasmante uruvelakassape pabbajite saṅghassa bahuṃ lohabhaṇḍaṃ dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā lohabhaṇḍaṃ anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññātaṃ; kiṃ dārubhaṇḍaṃ anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññātaṃ; kiṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññāta”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā paharaṇiṃ sabbaṃ lohabhaṇḍaṃ, ṭhapetvā āsandiṃ pallaṅkaṃ [P 2.0143] dārupattaṃ dārupādukaṃ sabbaṃ dārubhaṇḍaṃ, ṭhapetvā katakañca kumbhakārikañca sabbaṃ mattikābhaṇḍa”nti.

At that time, after the Venerable Uruvelakassapa had gone forth, the Saṅgha acquired a large amount of metal goods, wooden goods, and earthenware. Then the monks thought, “What metal goods has the Blessed One allowed, and what has he not allowed? What wooden goods has he allowed, and what has he not allowed? What earthenware has he allowed, and what has he not allowed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow all metal goods except weapons. I allow all wooden goods except a long-legged couch, a couch with animal figures on its feet, a wooden bowl, and wooden footwear. I allow all earthenware except a spiky foot-scrubber and a clay hut.”

Khuddakavatthukkhandhako pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on Minor Matters.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this:

Rukkhe [T 2.0079] thambhe ca kuṭṭe ca, aṭṭāne gandhasuttiyā;

Vigayha mallako kacchu, jarā ca puthupāṇikā.

On a tree, a pillar, and a wall; a rubbing-post; with scented powder; grappling; a scraper; scabies; an old monk; and rubbing with the heel of the hand.

Vallikāpi ca pāmaṅgo, kaṇṭhasuttaṃ na dhāraye;

Kaṭi ovaṭṭi kāyuraṃ, hatthābharaṇamuddikā.

An earring and a shoulder-sash; a necklace should not be worn. A waistband, a bracelet, an anklet, an armlet, and a finger-ring.

Dīghe kocche phaṇe hatthe, sitthā udakatelake;

Ādāsudapattavaṇā, ālepommaddacuṇṇanā.

Long hair, a brush, a comb, a hand-comb; pomade and oil mixed with water; a mirror, a water bowl, looking at one's reflection due to a wound; anointing, massaging, and using fine powder.

Lañchenti aṅgarāgañca, mukharāgaṃ tadūbhayaṃ;

Cakkhurogaṃ giraggañca, āyataṃ sarabāhiraṃ.

Making marks, coloring the nails, coloring the face, and doing both; eye disease and a mountain-top festival; a long-drawn-out song and wearing a cloak with the fleece turned outwards.

Ambapesisakalehi, ahicchindi ca candanaṃ;

Uccāvacā pattamūlā, suvaṇṇo bahalā valī.

With mango slices and whole mangoes; a snake-bitten one, one who has castrated himself, and a sandalwood bowl; various bowls, a worn bowl-base; a golden, a thick, and a shaky bowl-stand.

Citrā [M 0.0286] dussati duggandho, uṇhe bhijjiṃsu miḍḍhiyā;

Paribhaṇḍaṃ tiṇaṃ coḷaṃ, mālaṃ kuṇḍolikāya ca.

A decorated bowl-stand, a spoiled bowl, a bad-smelling one; in the sun, they broke, on an inner ledge; on an outer ledge, grass, a cloth, a rack, and in a wide-mouthed pot.

Thavikā [V 0.0266] aṃsabaddhañca, tathā bandhanasuttakā;

Khile mañce ca pīṭhe ca, aṅke chatte paṇāmanā.

A bag and a shoulder strap, and likewise a binding string; on a peg, a couch, and a stool; in the lap, under a parasol, and pushing.

Tumbaghaṭichavasīsaṃ, calakāni paṭiggaho;

Vipphālidaṇḍasovaṇṇaṃ, patte pesi ca nāḷikā.

A gourd, a pot, a skull; food wrappers, a spittoon; squeezing, a knife handle, a golden one; mending with a feather, a sliver, and a needle-case.

Kiṇṇasattu saritañca, madhusitthaṃ sipāṭikaṃ;

Vikaṇṇaṃ bandhivisamaṃ, chamājirapahoti ca.

Ferment, flour, and stone powder; beeswax, a powder-pouch; an uneven edge, binding, an uneven place; the ground, decay, and not being enough.

Kaḷimbhaṃ [T 2.0080] moghasuttañca, adhotallaṃ upāhanā;

Aṅgule paṭiggahañca, vitthakaṃ thavikabaddhakā.

A strip of palm-leaf, a marking thread, unwashed or wet feet, sandals; a finger, a hand-protector, a bag, and a bag-strap fastener.

Ajjhokāse nīcavatthu, cayo cāpi vihaññare;

Paripati tiṇacuṇṇaṃ, ullittaavalittakaṃ.

In the open air, a low foundation, and a mound, they are troubled; grass dust falls, and plastering inside and out.

Setaṃ kāḷakavaṇṇañca, parikammañca gerukaṃ;

Mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ, makaradantakapāṭikaṃ.

White color, black color, and finishing work with red ochre; floral work, creeper work, the makara-tooth pattern, and decorative stripes.

Cīvaravaṃsaṃ rajjuñca, anuññāsi vināyako;

Ujjhitvā pakkamanti ca, kathinaṃ paribhijjati.

A bamboo and a rope for robes, the Guide allowed; having abandoned, they depart, and the Kathina is broken.

Viniveṭhiyati kuṭṭepi, pattenādāya gacchare;

Thavikā bandhasuttañca, bandhitvā ca upāhanā.

It is unwound against a wall; taking things in a bowl, they go; a medicine bag, a binding thread, and tying up sandals.

Upāhanatthavikañca, aṃsabaddhañca suttakaṃ;

Udakākappiyaṃ magge, parissāvanacoḷakaṃ.

Unallowable water on the road, and a water-straining cloth.

Dhammakaraṇaṃ dve bhikkhū, vesāliṃ agamā muni;

Daṇḍaṃ ottharakaṃ tattha, anuññāsi parissāvanaṃ.

A dhammakaraṇa water strainer, two monks; the Sage went to Vesālī; there he allowed a water strainer stretched on poles.

Makasehi [V 0.0267] paṇītena, bahvābādhā ca jīvako;

Caṅkamanajantāgharaṃ[P 2.0144], visame nīcavatthuko.

By gnats, with excellent food, many illnesses, and Jīvaka; a walking path, a steam-bath house, on uneven ground, and a low foundation.

Tayo [T 2.0081] caye vihaññanti, sopānālambavedikaṃ;

Ajjhokāse tiṇacuṇṇaṃ, ullittaavalittakaṃ.

Three layers, they are troubled, a staircase with a handrail and a railing; in the open air, grass dust, and plastering inside and out.

Setakaṃ [M 0.0287] kāḷavaṇṇañca, parikammañca gerukaṃ;

Mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ, makaradantakapāṭikaṃ.

White color, black color, and finishing work with red ochre; floral work, creeper work, the makara-tooth pattern, and decorative stripes.

Vaṃsaṃ cīvararajjuñca, uccañca vatthukaṃ kare;

Cayo sopānabāhañca, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ.

A bamboo and a rope for robes, one should make a high foundation; a mound, a staircase handrail, a door leaf, and a door frame.

Udukkhaluttarapāsakaṃ, vaṭṭiñca kapisīsakaṃ;

Sūcighaṭitāḷacchiddaṃ, āviñchanañca rajjukaṃ.

A lower socket and an upper ring, a bolt-post and a monkey-head bracket; a small bolt, a large bolt, a keyhole, a pulling-hole, and a pulling-rope.

Maṇḍalaṃ dhūmanettañca, majjhe ca mukhamattikā;

Doṇi duggandhā dahati, udakaṭṭhānaṃ sarāvakaṃ.

A circular enclosure, a smoke-vent, and in the middle, clay for the surface; a trough, a foul smell, it burns; a water receptacle, and a water cup.

Na sedeti ca cikkhallaṃ, dhovi niddhamanaṃ kare;

Pīṭhañca koṭṭhake kammaṃ, marumbā silā niddhamanaṃ.

It should be roofed, and there is mud; one should make a drain for washing. A bench, work in the gateway; gravel, stone, and a drain.

Naggā chamāya vassante, paṭicchādī tayo tahiṃ;

Udapānaṃ lujjati nīcaṃ, valliyā kāyabandhane.

Naked on the ground in the rain; there are three coverings there. A well with a low foundation crumbles; by a creeper and by a waistband.

Tulaṃ kaṭakaṭaṃ cakkaṃ, bahū bhijjanti bhājanā;

Lohadārucammakhaṇḍaṃ, sālātiṇāpidhāni ca.

A well-sweep, a windlass, a pulley-wheel; many pots are broken. Pieces of bronze, wood, and leather; a hall by the well, grass, and a cover.

Doṇicandani pākāraṃ, cikkhallaṃ niddhamanena ca;

Sītigataṃ pokkharaṇiṃ, purāṇañca nillekhaṇaṃ.

A trough, a wooden floor, a surrounding wall, and muddiness; a pond made cool by a drainpipe, and an old, unadorned steam-bath house.

Cātumāsaṃ [V 0.0268] sayanti ca, namatakañca gandhapupphaṃ (syā.) nadhiṭṭhahe;

Āsittakaṃ [T 2.0082] maḷorikaṃ, bhuñjantekaṃ tuvaṭṭeyyuṃ.

They sleep for four months, and one should not determine upon a felt rug; a copper or silver lid, a spear-handle bowl-stand; they eat from a single vessel; they sleep on a single couch.

Vaḍḍho bodhi na akkami, ghaṭaṃ katakasammajjani;

Sakkharaṃ kathalañceva, pheṇakaṃ pādaghaṃsanī.

Vaḍḍha the Licchavi; Prince Bodhi did not step on it; a bathing pot, a spiky foot-rubbing potsherd, a broom; a potsherd with gravel, sea-foam, a foot-rubber.

Vidhūpanaṃ tālavaṇṭaṃ, makasañcāpi cāmarī;

Chattaṃ vinā ca ārāme, tayo sikkāya sammuti.

A square fan, a palm-leaf fan, a fly-whisk, and a chowrie whisk; an umbrella. Without an umbrella in the monastery, and with a carrying sling: there are three conventions.

Romasitthā nakhā dīghā, chindantaṅgulikā dukkhā;

Salohitaṃ pamāṇañca, vīsati dīghakesatā.

A ruminating monk; dropping a ball of rice; long nails; they cut, and the fingers are in pain; with blood, the standard of cutting level with the flesh; adorning the twenty fingers and toes; having long hair.

Khuraṃ silaṃ sipāṭikaṃ, namatakaṃ khurabhaṇḍakaṃ;

Massuṃ kappenti vaḍḍhenti, golomicaturassakaṃ.

A razor, a whetstone, a razor-wrapper, a felt rug, a razor kit; they trim the beard, they let it grow; making a goat's beard, making a square beard.

Parimukhaṃ [M 0.0288] aḍḍhadukañca, dāṭhisambādhasaṃhare;

Ābādhā kattarivaṇo, dīghaṃ sakkharikāya ca.

Shaving the chest hair, making patterns in it; keeping sideburns, shaving hair in a confined place; due to sickness, cutting with scissors; due to a wound; long nose hair, and removing it with a pebble.

Palitaṃ thakitaṃ uccā, lohabhaṇḍañjanī saha;

Pallatthikañca āyogo, vaṭaṃ salākabandhanaṃ.

Plucking grey hair; it is closed with a lid; high-quality metal goods, together with an eyeliner container; sitting with a cloth binding the knees and back, a yoga-strap; a disc, a waistband with sticks.

Kalābukaṃ deḍḍubhakaṃ, murajaṃ maddavīṇakaṃ;

Paṭṭikā sūkarantañca, dasā murajaveṇikā;

Anto sobhaṃ guṇakañca, pavanantopi jīrati.

A waistband of many cords, a water-snake-shaped waistband, a muraja-drum-shaped waistband, a chisel-handle-shaped waistband; a flat waistband, and a pig's-intestine-shaped waistband; the fringes are shaped like a muraja drum or a chisel handle; hemming the end, a braided pattern; and even the edge of the robe wears out.

Gaṇṭhikā uccāvacañca, phalakantepi ogāhe;

Gihivatthaṃ hatthisoṇḍaṃ, macchakaṃ catukaṇṇakaṃ.
