A knot of various kinds; attaching the button-loop loosely at the edge; wearing the robe like a layman: the elephant's trunk style, the fish-tail style, the four-cornered style.

Tālavaṇṭaṃ satavali, gihipārutapārupaṃ;

Saṃvelli [T 2.0083] ubhatokājaṃ, dantakaṭṭhaṃ ākoṭane.

The palm-leaf fan style, the hundred-folds style; covering oneself as laypeople do; tucking up the robe; carrying a yoke with loads on both sides; a tooth-stick; striking.

Kaṇṭhe [V 0.0269] vilaggaṃ dāyañca, paṭaggi rukkhahatthinā;

Yameḷe lokāyatakaṃ, pariyāpuṇiṃsu vācayuṃ.

Getting stuck in the throat; setting a forest fire, giving a firebrand in welcome; climbing a tree, being chased by an elephant; in the village of Yameḷa, they learned and taught the Lokāyata treatise.

Tiracchānakathā [P 2.0145] vijjā, khipi maṅgalaṃ khādi ca;

Vātābādho dussati ca, duggandho dukkhapādukā.

The art of animal talk, sneezing, desiring auspicious signs, and eating; wind disease, being corrupt, a bad smell, difficulty, and footwear.

Hiriyanti pāruduggandho, tahaṃ tahaṃ karonti ca;

Duggandho kūpaṃ lujjanti, uccavatthu cayena ca.

Being ashamed; being uncovered and having a bad smell; defecating here and there; a bad smell; the pits being destroyed; a high foundation and a foundation.

Sopānālambanabāhā ante, dukkhañca pādukā;

Bahiddhā doṇi kaṭṭhañca, piṭharo ca apāruto.

Stairs, a handrail, and being at the end; difficulty and footwear; urinating outside, a urinal trough, a stick, and an uncovered basket.

Vaccakuṭiṃ kavāṭañca, piṭṭhasaṅghāṭameva ca;

Udukkhaluttarapāso, vaṭṭiñca kapisīsakaṃ.

A latrine hut, a door leaf, and a door frame; the lower pivot-hole and the upper pivot-ring; a bolt-post, and a 'monkey's hand' latch.

Sūcighaṭitāḷacchiddaṃ, āviñchanacchiddameva ca;

Rajju ullittāvalittaṃ, setavaṇṇañca kāḷakaṃ.

A small bolt, a large bolt, a keyhole, and a hole for pulling; a rope; plastering inside and out; white color and black color.

Mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ, makaraṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ;

Cīvaravaṃsaṃ rajjuñca, jarādubbalapākāraṃ.

Floral work, creeper work, the makara-tooth pattern, and the five-fold design; a bamboo and rope for robes, and a wall for the old and weak.

Koṭṭhake cāpi tatheva, marumbaṃ padarasilā;

Santiṭṭhati niddhamanaṃ, kumbhiñcāpi sarāvakaṃ.

In the gateway, likewise; gravel and a stone slab; stagnation of water, a drain, a water pot, and a small cup.

Dukkhaṃ [M 0.0289] hiri apidhānaṃ, anācārañca ācaruṃ;

Lohabhaṇḍaṃ [T 2.0084] anuññāsi, ṭhapayitvā paharaṇiṃ.

Difficulty, shame, and lack of a covering; they practiced improper conduct. He allowed metal goods, having set aside weapons.

Ṭhapayitvā sandipallaṅkaṃ, dārupattañca pādukaṃ;

Sabbaṃ dārumayaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ, anuññāsi mahāmuni.

Having set aside a long-legged couch (āsandi), a couch with animal figures (pallaṅka), a wooden bowl, and wooden footwear, the Great Sage allowed all goods made of wood.

Katakaṃ [V 0.0270] kumbhakārañca, ṭhapayitvā tathāgato;

Sabbampi mattikābhaṇḍaṃ, anuññāsi anukampako.

Having set aside a potsherd for rubbing the feet and an earthen hut made by a potter, the compassionate Tathāgata allowed all earthenware goods.

Yassa vatthussa niddeso, purimena yadi samaṃ;

Tampi saṃkhittaṃ uddāne, nayato taṃ vijāniyā.

If the detailed explanation of any matter is the same as a preceding one, that matter is also summarized in the summary verse; one should understand it by that method.

Evaṃ dasasatā vatthū, vinaye khuddakavatthuke;

Saddhammaṭṭhitiko ceva, pesalānañcanuggaho.

Thus there are one hundred and ten matters in this Vinaya section on Minor Matters, for the stability of the good Dhamma and for the support of those with lovely virtue.

Susikkhito vinayadharo, hitacitto supesalo;

Padīpakaraṇo dhīro, pūjāraho bahussutoti.

A master of the Vinaya who is well-trained, has a mind set on welfare, possesses very lovely virtue, creates the lamp of wisdom, is wise and steadfast, and is deeply learned, is worthy of honor: thus it should be known.

Khuddakavatthukkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Khandhaka on Minor Matters is concluded.

6. Senāsanakkhandhakaṃ

6. The Khandhaka on Lodgings

1. Paṭhamabhāṇavāro

1. The First Recitation Section

Vihārānujānanaṃ

The Allowance of a Dwelling

294. Tena [T 2.0085][P 2.0146][M 0.0290][V 0.0271] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ apaññattaṃ hoti. Te ca bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ viharanti – araññe, rukkhamūle, pabbate, kandarāyaṃ, giriguhāyaṃ, susāne, vanapatthe, ajjhokāse, palālapuñje. Te kālasseva tato tato upanikkhamanti – araññā rukkhamūlā pabbatā kandarā giriguhā susānā vanapatthā ajjhokāsā palālapuñjā, pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena, ālokitena vilokitena, samiñjitena pasāritena, okkhittacakkhū, iriyāpathasampannā. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahako seṭṭhī seṭṭhi (ka.) kālasseva uyyānaṃ agamāsi. Addasā kho rājagahako seṭṭhī te bhikkhū kālasseva tato tato upanikkhamante – araññā rukkhamūlā pabbatā kandarā giriguhā susānā vanapatthā ajjhokāsā palālapuñjā, pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena, ālokitena vilokitena, samiñjitena pasāritena, okkhittacakkhū, iriyāpathasampanne. Disvānassa cittaṃ pasīdi. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “sacāhaṃ, bhante, vihāre kārāpeyyaṃ, vaseyyātha me vihāresū”ti? “Na kho, gahapati, bhagavatā vihārā [T 2.0086] anuññātā”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, bhagavantaṃ paṭipucchitvā mama āroceyyāthā”ti. “Evaṃ gahapatī”ti kho te bhikkhū rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “rājagahako, bhante, seṭṭhī vihāre kārāpetukāmo. Kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, amhehi bhante (sī. ka.) paṭipajjitabba”nti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne [V 0.0272] etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca leṇāni pañca senāsanāni (syā.) – vihāraṃ, aḍḍhayogaṃ, pāsādaṃ, hammiyaṃ, guha”nti.

294. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Veḷuvana, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. Now at that time, a lodging for the monks had not yet been prescribed by the Blessed One. And those monks dwelt here and there: in a forest, at the foot of a tree, on a mountain, in a ravine, in a mountain cave, in a charnel ground, in a forest grove, in the open air, or on a heap of straw. Early in the morning, they would emerge from those various places—from a forest, from the foot of a tree, from a mountain, from a ravine, from a mountain cave, from a charnel ground, from a forest grove, from the open air, or from a heap of straw—inspiring confidence in their going forward and going back, in their looking ahead and looking aside, in their bending and stretching, with downcast eyes and endowed with perfect deportment. Now at that time, the merchant of Rājagaha went to the park early in the morning. The merchant of Rājagaha saw those monks emerging early in the morning from those various places—from a forest, from the foot of a tree, from a mountain, from a ravine, from a mountain cave, from a charnel ground, from a forest grove, from the open air, or from a heap of straw—inspiring confidence in their going forward and going back, in their looking ahead and looking aside, in their bending and stretching, with downcast eyes and endowed with perfect deportment. Having seen them, his mind was gladdened. Then the merchant of Rājagaha approached those monks, and having approached, he said this to those monks: “Venerable sirs, if I were to have dwellings built, would you dwell in my dwellings?” “Householder, dwellings have not been allowed by the Blessed One.” “In that case, venerable sirs, having asked the Blessed One, you should inform me.” “So be it, householder,” those monks replied to the merchant of Rājagaha. Then they approached the Blessed One, and having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the merchant of Rājagaha wishes to have dwellings built. How then should we proceed?” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow five kinds of lodgings: a dwelling, a gabled house, a long-house, a storied building, and a cave.”

Atha [M 0.0291] kho te [P 2.0147] bhikkhū yena rājagahako seṭṭhī tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā rājagahakaṃ seṭṭhiṃ etadavocuṃ – “anuññātā kho, gahapati, bhagavatā vihārā; yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī ekāheneva saṭṭhivihāre patiṭṭhāpesi. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī te saṭṭhivihāre pariyosāpetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha [T 2.0087] kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then those monks approached the merchant of Rājagaha. Having approached, they said to the merchant of Rājagaha: “Householder, dwellings have been permitted by the Blessed One; now is the time for that which you see fit.” Then the merchant of Rājagaha had sixty dwellings established in a single day. Then the merchant of Rājagaha, having had the sixty dwellings completed, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the merchant of Rājagaha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to a meal from me tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the merchant of Rājagaha, having understood the Blessed One's consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed.

Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ, ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ete me, bhante, saṭṭhivihārā puññatthikena saggatthikena kārāpitā. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu vihāresu paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, gahapati, te saṭṭhivihāre āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa patiṭṭhāpehī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavato paṭissutvā te saṭṭhivihāre āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa patiṭṭhāpesi.

Then, when that night had passed, the merchant of Rājagaha had excellent hard and soft foods prepared and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and went to the residence of the merchant of Rājagaha. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then the merchant of Rājagaha, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft foods until they refused more. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, the merchant sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the merchant of Rājagaha said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have had these sixty dwellings built, desiring merit, desiring heaven. How, venerable sir, should I act in regard to these dwellings?” “In that case, householder, you should establish these sixty dwellings for the Saṅgha of the four directions, both those who have arrived and those who are yet to come.” “So be it, venerable sir,” the merchant of Rājagaha assented to the Blessed One, and he established those sixty dwellings for the Saṅgha of the four directions, both those who have arrived and those who are yet to come.

295. Atha kho bhagavā rājagahakaṃ seṭṭhiṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

295. Then the Blessed One expressed his appreciation to the merchant of Rājagaha with these verses:

“Sītaṃ uṇhaṃ paṭihanti paṭihanati (ka.), tato vāḷamigāni ca;

Sarīsape ca makase, sisire cāpi vuṭṭhiyo.

“It wards off cold and heat, and then wild beasts, and creeping things and mosquitoes, and also the chilling winds and the rains.

“Tato [T 2.0088][M 0.0292][V 0.0273] vātātapo ghore, sañjāto vātātape ghore, sañjāte (ka. saddanīti) paṭihaññati;

Leṇatthañca sukhatthañca, jhāyituñca vipassituṃ.

Furthermore, fierce wind and heat that have arisen are warded off; for the purpose of seclusion and for comfort, for meditating and for practicing insight.

“Vihāradānaṃ saṅghassa, aggaṃ buddhena buddhehi (syā.) vaṇṇitaṃ;

Tasmā hi paṇḍito, poso sampassaṃ atthamattano.

The gift of a dwelling to the Saṅgha is praised by the Buddha as supreme; therefore, a wise person, seeing his own welfare—

“Vihāre kāraye ramme, vāsayettha bahussute;

Tesaṃ [P 2.0148] annañca pānañca, vatthasenāsanāni ca;

Dadeyya ujubhūtesu, vippasannena cetasā.

should have delightful dwellings built and let the learned reside therein. To them, who are upright, one should give food, drink, clothing, and lodgings with a serene mind.

“Te tassa dhammaṃ desenti, sabbadukkhāpanūdanaṃ;

Yaṃ so dhammaṃ idhaññāya, parinibbāti anāsavo”ti.

They teach him the Dhamma that dispels all suffering; having understood that Dhamma here, he, free from taints, attains Parinibbāna.”

Atha kho bhagavā rājagahakaṃ seṭṭhiṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to the merchant of Rājagaha with these verses, rose from his seat and departed.

296. Assosuṃ kho manussā – “bhagavatā kira vihārā anuññātā”ti sakkaccaṃ te sakkaccaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) vihāre kārāpenti. Te vihārā akavāṭakā honti; ahīpi vicchikāpi satapadiyopi pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭa”nti. Bhittichiddaṃ karitvā valliyāpi rajjuyāpi kavāṭaṃ bandhanti. Undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjanti. Khayitabandhanāni kavāṭāni patanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsaka”nti[T 2.0089]. Kavāṭā na phusīyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āviñchanacchiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti. Kavāṭā na thakiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aggaḷavaṭṭiṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭika”nti.

296. People heard, “It is said that dwellings have been allowed by the Blessed One,” so they carefully had dwellings built. Those dwellings were without doors; snakes, scorpions, and centipedes entered. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a door.” They made a hole in the wall and tied the door with creepers or ropes. They were gnawed by rats and termites. The doors, with their fastenings gnawed, fell. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a door-frame, a lower pivot-hole, and an upper pivot-ring.” The doors did not fit. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a hole for pulling and a rope for pulling.” The doors could not be closed. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a bolt-post, a staple, a pin, and a latch.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū na sakkonti kavāṭaṃ apāpurituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tāḷacchiddaṃ. Tīṇi tāḷāni – lohatāḷaṃ, kaṭṭhatāḷaṃ, visāṇatāḷa”nti. Yehi yepi (sī. syā.) te ugghāṭetvā pavisanti visāṇatāḷaṃ, yehi te ugghāṭetvā pavisantīti (ka.), vihārā aguttā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yantakaṃ sūcika”nti.

At that time, the monks were not able to open the door. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a keyhole. I allow three kinds of keys: a metal key, a wooden key, and a horn key.” With these they could open the door and enter. The dwellings were unguarded. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a lock and a key.”

Tena [M 0.0293][V 0.0274] kho pana samayena vihārā tiṇacchadanā honti; sītakāle sītā, uṇhakāle uṇhā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātu”nti.

At that time, the dwellings had thatched roofs; they were cold in the cold season and hot in the hot season. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow you to cover them over and to plaster them inside and out.”

Tena kho pana samayena vihārā avātapānakā honti acakkhussā duggandhā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tīṇi vātapānāni – vedikāvātapānaṃ, jālavātapānaṃ, salākavātapāna”nti. Vātapānantarikāya kāḷakāpi vagguliyopi pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vātapānacakkalika”nti. Cakkalikantarikāyapi kāḷakāpi vagguliyopi pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vātapānakavāṭakaṃ vātapānabhisika”nti.

At that time, the dwellings had no ventilation openings; they were unclear to the eye and foul-smelling. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow three types of windows: a window with a railing, a window with a lattice, and a window with bars.” Through the gaps in the windows, squirrels and bats entered. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a cloth covering for the window.” Through the gaps in the cloth covering, squirrels and bats also entered. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a window shutter and a window bolster.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chamāyaṃ sayanti. Gattānipi [T 2.0090] cīvarānipi paṃsukitāni honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthāraka”nti. Tiṇasanthārako undūrehipi [P 2.0149] upacikāhipi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, miḍḍhi”nti mīḍhanti (sī.), miḍhinti (syā.). Miḍḍhiyā gattāni dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bidalamañcaka”nti.

At that time, the monks were sleeping on the ground. Their bodies and robes became soiled with dust. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a grass mat.” The grass mat was eaten by rats and termites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow plastering with clay.” Because of the clay plaster, their bodies were uncomfortable. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a bedstead woven with split bamboo.”

Mañcapīṭhādianujānanaṃ

The Allowance of Beds, Seats, and so forth

297. Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko masārako mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, masārakaṃ mañca”nti. Masārakaṃ pīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, masārakaṃ pīṭha”nti.

297. At that time, a bedstead from a charnel ground with legs fitted into sockets had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a bedstead with legs fitted into sockets.” A stool with legs fitted into sockets had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool with legs fitted into sockets.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko bundikābaddho mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bundikābaddhaṃ mañca”nti. Bundikābaddhaṃ pīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bundikābaddhaṃ pīṭha”nti.

At that time, a bedstead from a charnel ground with legs fixed into the frame had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a bedstead with legs fixed into the frame.” A stool with legs fixed into the frame had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool with legs fixed into the frame.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko kuḷīrapādako mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[M 0.0294], kuḷīrapādakaṃ [V 0.0275] mañca”nti. Kuḷīrapādakaṃ pīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[T 2.0091], kuḷīrapādakaṃ pīṭha”nti.

At that time, a bedstead from a charnel ground with legs like a crab's claw had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a bedstead with legs like a crab's claw.” A stool with legs like a crab's claw had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool with legs like a crab's claw.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko āhaccapādako mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ orācesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āhaccapādakaṃ mañca”nti. Āhaccapādakaṃ pīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āhaccapādakaṃ pīṭha”nti.

At that time, a bedstead from a charnel ground with inserted legs had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a bedstead with inserted legs.” A stool with inserted legs had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool with inserted legs.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa āsandiko uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āsandika”nti. Uccako āsandiko uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccakampi āsandika”nti. Sattaṅgo uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattaṅga”nti. Uccako sattaṅgo uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccakampi sattaṅga”nti. Bhaddapīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhaddapīṭha”nti. Pīṭhikā uppannā hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pīṭhika”nti. Eḷakapādakaṃ pīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, eḷakapādakaṃ pīṭha”nti. Āmalakavaṭṭikaṃ āmalakavaṇṭikaṃ (syā.) pīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āmalakavaṭṭikaṃ pīṭha”nti. Phalakaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, phalaka”nti. Kocchaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koccha”nti. Palālapīṭhaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 2.0092]. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, palālapīṭha”nti.

At that time, a square stool had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a square stool.” A high square stool had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow even a high square stool.” A couch with seven parts had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a couch with seven parts.” A high couch with seven parts had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow even a high couch with seven parts.” A wicker seat had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a wicker seat.” A stool of coarse cloth had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool of coarse cloth.” A stool with legs curved like a goat's had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool with legs curved like a goat's.” A stool with many legs turned like amalaka fruits had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a stool with many legs turned like amalaka fruits.” A leaning-board had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a leaning-board.” A rush mat had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a rush mat.” A straw seat had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a straw seat.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ucce mañce sayanti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ucce mañce sayitabbaṃ. Yo sayeyya, āpatti [P 2.0150] dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were sleeping on high bedsteads. People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, one should not sleep on a high bedstead. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena [M 0.0295] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu nīce mañce sayanto ahinā daṭṭho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mañcapaṭipādaka”nti.

At that time, a certain monk, while sleeping on a low bedstead, was bitten by a snake. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow supports for a bedstead.”

Tena [V 0.0276] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ucce mañcapaṭipādake dhārenti, saha mañcapaṭipādakehi pavedhenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, uccā mañcapaṭipādakā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgulaparamaṃ mañcapaṭipādaka”nti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were using high supports for their bedsteads and were rocking on them. People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, high supports for a bedstead should not be used. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Monks, a support for a bedstead of at most eight finger-breadths.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa suttaṃ uppannaṃ hoti[T 2.0093]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, suttaṃ mañcaṃ veṭhetu”nti vetunti (sī.). Aṅgāni bahusuttaṃ pariyādiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṅge vijjhitvā aṭṭhapadakaṃ veṭhetu”nti. Coḷakaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cimilikaṃ kātu”nti. Tūlikā uppannā hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vijaṭetvā bibbohanaṃ bimbohanaṃ (sī. syā. bimba + ohanaṃ) kātuṃ. Tīṇi tūlāni – rukkhatūlaṃ, latātūlaṃ, poṭakitūla”nti.

At that time, thread had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow thread for wrapping a bedstead.” The parts of the bedstead used up much thread. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow you to pierce the frame and wrap it in a woven pattern.” A coarse cloth had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow you to make a floor-covering.” A stuffed mattress had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow you to tease it out and make a pillow. There are three kinds of stuffing: tree-cotton, creeper-cotton, and grass-down.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū addhakāyikāni aḍḍhakāyikāni (ka.) bibbohanāni dhārenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, aḍḍhakāyikāni bibbohanāni dhāretabbāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīsappamāṇaṃ bibbohanaṃ kātu”nti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were using pillows half the length of the body. People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, pillows half the length of the body should not be used. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Monks, you to make a pillow the size of the head.”

Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe giraggasamajjo hoti. Manussā mahāmattānaṃ atthāya bhisiyo paṭiyādenti – uṇṇabhisiṃ, coḷabhisiṃ, vākabhisiṃ, tiṇabhisiṃ, paṇṇabhisiṃ. Te vītivatte samajje chaviṃ uppāṭetvā haranti. Addasāsuṃ kho bhikkhū samajjaṭṭhāne bahuṃ uṇṇampi coḷakampi vākampi tiṇampi paṇṇampi chaṭṭitaṃ. Disvāna [T 2.0094] bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[M 0.0296]. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca bhisiyo – uṇṇabhisiṃ, coḷabhisiṃ, vākabhisiṃ, tiṇabhisiṃ, paṇṇabhisi”nti.

At that time, there was a mountain-top festival in Rājagaha. People prepared bolsters for the great ministers—wool bolsters, coarse cloth bolsters, bark-fibre bolsters, grass bolsters, and leaf bolsters. When the festival was over, they stripped off the coverings and took them away. The bhikkhus saw a large amount of discarded wool, coarse cloth, bark-fibre, grass, and leaves at the festival grounds. Having seen this, they reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, five kinds of bolsters: wool bolsters, coarse cloth bolsters, bark-fibre bolsters, grass bolsters, and leaf bolsters.”

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa senāsanaparikkhārikaṃ dussaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhisiṃ onandhitu”nti onaddhituṃ (syā.).

At that time, cloth for monastery furnishings had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, to cover a bolster.”

Tena [V 0.0277] kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañcabhisiṃ pīṭhe santharanti, pīṭhabhisiṃ mañce santharanti. Bhisiyo paribhijjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, onaddhamañcaṃ onaddhamañcaṃ (ka.) evamuparipi onaddhapīṭha”nti. Ullokaṃ akaritvā [P 2.0151] santharanti, heṭṭhato nipatanti nipaṭanti (ka.), nipphaṭanti (sī.), nippāṭenti (syā.) …pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ullokaṃ karitvā santharitvā bhisiṃ onandhitu”nti. Chaviṃ uppāṭetvā haranti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, phositu”nti. Harantiyeva…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattikamma”nti. Harantiyeva…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, hatthabhattikamma”nti. Harantiyeva…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, hatthabhatti”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus were spreading bed-bolsters on stools and stool-bolsters on beds. The bolsters were being damaged. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, a covered bed and a covered stool.” They spread them without making a base-cloth, and they fell from below… “I allow, bhikkhus, to make a base-cloth, spread it, and then cover the bolster.” They stripped off the covering and took it away… “I allow, bhikkhus, to sprinkle it with dye.” They still took them away… “I allow, bhikkhus, pattern-work.” They still took them away… “I allow, bhikkhus, hand pattern-work.” They still took them away… “I allow, bhikkhus, a five-finger pattern.”

Setavaṇṇādianujānanaṃ

The Allowance Concerning White Color and so on

298. Tena kho pana samayena titthiyānaṃ seyyāyo setavaṇṇā honti, kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi, gerukaparikammakatā bhitti. Bahū manussā seyyāpekkhakā gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vihāre setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikamma”nti[T 2.0095].

298. At that time, the lodgings of the sectarians were white, the floor was blackened, and the walls were finished with red ochre. Many people went, wishing to see the lodgings. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow white color, black color, and a finish with red ochre in a monastery.”

Tena kho pana samayena pharusāya bhittiyā setavaṇṇo na nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, thusapiṇḍaṃ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā setavaṇṇaṃ nipātetu”nti. Setavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṇhamattikaṃ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā setavaṇṇaṃ nipātetu”nti. Setavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ikkāsaṃ piṭṭhamadda”nti.

At that time, white color would not adhere to a rough wall. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow one to apply a lump of earth mixed with husk, rub it with a trowel, and then apply the white color.” The white color would not bind... “Bhikkhus, I allow one to apply fine earth, rub it with a trowel, and then apply the white color.” The white color would not bind... “Bhikkhus, I allow tree gum and that which is kneaded with rice-water starch.”

Tena kho pana samayena pharusāya bhittiyā gerukā na nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, thusapiṇḍaṃ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā gerukaṃ nipātetu”nti. Gerukā anibandhanīyā hoti [M 0.0297] …pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kuṇḍakamattikaṃ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā gerukaṃ nipātetu”nti. Gerukā anibandhanīyā hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāsapakuṭṭaṃ sitthatelaka”nti. Accussannaṃ hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, coḷakena paccuddharitu”nti.

At that time, red ochre would not adhere to a rough wall. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow one to apply a lump of earth mixed with husk, rub it with a trowel, and then apply the red ochre.” The red ochre would not bind... “Bhikkhus, I allow one to apply earth mixed with broken rice powder, rub it with a trowel, and then apply the red ochre.” The red ochre would not bind... “Bhikkhus, I allow mustard cake and beeswax oil.” It was excessive... “Bhikkhus, I allow one to wipe it with a coarse cloth.”

Tena kho pana samayena pharusāya bhūmiyā kāḷavaṇṇo na nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, thusapiṇḍaṃ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā kāḷavaṇṇaṃ nipātetu”nti. Kāḷavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti…pe… [T 2.0096] “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gaṇḍumattikaṃ [V 0.0278] datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā kāḷavaṇṇaṃ nipātetu”nti. Kāḷavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ikkāsaṃ kasāva”nti.

At that time, black color would not adhere to a rough floor. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow one to apply a lump of earth mixed with husk, rub it with a trowel, and then apply the black color.” The black color would not bind... “Bhikkhus, I allow one to apply earth from earthworm castings, rub it with a trowel, and then apply the black color.” The black color would not bind... “Bhikkhus, I allow tree gum and astringent liquid.”

Paṭibhānacittapaṭikkhepaṃ

Rejection of Representational Paintings

299. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vihāre paṭibhānacittaṃ kārāpenti – itthirūpakaṃ purisarūpakaṃ. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī [P 2.0152] kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, paṭibhānacittaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ – itthirūpakaṃ purisarūpakaṃ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭika”nti.

299. At that time the bhikkhus of the group of six were having imaginative paintings made in the monastery: figures of women and figures of men. People wandering on a tour of the monastery saw them and complained, criticized, and denounced them, saying, “Just like householders enjoying sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, imaginative paintings should not be made: figures of women or figures of men. Whoever has them made commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow garland work, creeper work, makara-tooth designs, and five-colored patterns.”

Iṭṭhakācayādianujānanaṃ

Allowance for Brick Foundations and so on

300. Tena kho pana samayena vihārā nīcavatthukā honti, udakena otthariyyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti.

300. At that time, the monasteries had low foundations and were flooded with water. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow making high foundations.” The foundation collapses… “Bhikkhus, I allow building three kinds of foundations: a brick foundation, a stone foundation, and a wooden foundation.” Those climbing up are troubled… “Bhikkhus, I allow three kinds of staircases: a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.” Those climbing up fall down… “Bhikkhus, I allow a handrail.”

Tena kho pana samayena vihārā āḷakamandā honti[T 2.0097]. Bhikkhū hiriyanti nipajjituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tirokaraṇi”nti. Tirokaraṇiṃ ukkhipitvā olokenti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave[M 0.0298], aḍḍhakuṭṭaka”nti. Aḍḍhakuṭṭakā uparito olokenti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo gabbhe – sivikāgabbhaṃ, nāḷikāgabbhaṃ, hammiyagabbha”nti.

At that time the monasteries were wide open. The bhikkhus were embarrassed to lie down. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a curtain.” They lifted the curtain and looked… “Bhikkhus, I allow a half-wall.” They looked over the half-wall… “Bhikkhus, I allow three kinds of inner chambers: a square chamber, a long chamber, and an upper chamber.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū khuddake vihāre majjhe gabbhaṃ karonti. Upacāro na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khuddake vihāre ekamantaṃ gabbhaṃ kātuṃ, mahallake majjhe”ti.

At that time the monks were making an inner chamber in the middle of small monasteries. There was no surrounding space. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow making an inner chamber to one side in small monasteries, and in the middle in large ones.”

Tena kho pana samayena vihārassa kuṭṭapādo jīrati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi[V 0.0279], bhikkhave, kulaṅkapādaka”nti kuḷuṅkapādakanti (sī.). Vihārassa kuṭṭo ovassati…pe…“anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parittāṇakiṭikaṃ uddasudha”nti uddhāsudhanti (syā.).

At that time, the wall foundation of a dwelling was decaying. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a buttress.” The wall of the dwelling was being soaked by rain… “Monks, I allow a protective screen and plaster made of earth mixed with cow-dung ash.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno tiṇacchadanā ahi khandhe patati. So bhīto vissaramakāsi. Bhikkhū upadhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, vissaramakāsī”ti? Atha kho so bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vitāna”nti.

At that time, a snake fell from a thatched roof onto a certain monk’s shoulder. Frightened, he cried out. The monks rushed over and said to that monk, “Why did you cry out, friend?” Then that monk told the monks this matter. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a ceiling-cloth.”

Tena [T 2.0098] kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañcapādepi pīṭhapādepi thavikāyo laggenti. Undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhittikhilaṃ nāgadantaka”nti.

At that time, the monks were hanging bags on the legs of beds and on the legs of benches. They were being eaten by rats and termites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a wall-peg and an elephant’s-tusk bracket.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañcepi pīṭhepi cīvaraṃ nikkhipanti. Cīvaraṃ paribhijjiti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vihāre cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti[P 2.0153].

At that time, monks were placing robes on beds and on benches. The robes were getting damaged. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a robe-pole and a robe-cord in the dwelling.”

Tena kho pana samayena vihārā anāḷindakā honti appaṭissaraṇā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āḷindaṃ paghanaṃ pakuṭṭaṃ pakuḍḍaṃ (sī.) osāraka”nti. Āḷindā pākaṭā honti. Bhikkhū hiriyanti nipajjituṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṃsaraṇakiṭikaṃ ugghāṭanakiṭika”nti.

At that time, the dwellings had no verandas and were unprotected. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a veranda, a porch, a narrow passage, and an antechamber.” The verandas were exposed. The monks were embarrassed to lie down… “Monks, I allow a sliding screen and a hinged shutter.”

Upaṭṭhānasālāanujānanaṃ

The Allowance of an Assembly Hall

301. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajjhokāse bhattavissaggaṃ karontā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upaṭṭhānasāla”nti. Upaṭṭhānasālā nīcavatthukā hoti[M 0.0299], udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… [T 2.0099] “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Upaṭṭhānasālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā [V 0.0280] ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti.

301. At that time, the monks, while partaking of their meal in the open, were troubled by both cold and heat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, O monks, an attendance hall.' The attendance hall had a low foundation and was flooded by water… 'I allow, O monks, to make it with a high foundation.' The foundation collapsed… 'I allow, O monks, to construct three types of foundations—a brick foundation, a stone foundation, and a wooden foundation.' Those climbing up were struggling… 'I allow, O monks, three types of staircases—a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.' Those climbing up were falling… 'I allow, O monks, a handrail.' Grass dust fell in the attendance hall… 'I allow, O monks, after covering it over, to plaster it inside and out, and to make whitewashing, black coloring, red-ochre work, garland designs, creeper designs, a makara-tooth pattern, a five-panel pattern, a robe rack, and a robe cord.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajjhokāse chamāya cīvaraṃ pattharanti. Cīvaraṃ paṃsukitaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ajjhokāse cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti. Pānīyaṃ otappati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pānīyasālaṃ pānīyamaṇḍapa”nti. Pānīyasālā nīcavatthukā hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Pānīyasālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti. Pānīyabhājanaṃ na saṃvijjati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pānīyasaṅkhaṃ pānīyasarāvaka”nti.

At that time, the monks spread their robes on the bare ground in the open. The robes became soiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, O monks, a robe rack and a robe cord in the open.” The drinking water became warm… “I allow, O monks, a water hall and a water pavilion.” The water hall had a low foundation and was flooded by water… “I allow, O monks, to make it with a high foundation.” The foundation collapsed… “I allow, O monks, to construct three types of foundations—a brick foundation, a stone foundation, and a wooden foundation.” Those climbing up struggled… “I allow, O monks, three types of staircases—a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.” Those climbing up fell… “I allow, O monks, a handrail.” Grass dust fell into the water hall… “I allow, O monks, after covering it over, to plaster it inside and out, and to make whitewashing, black coloring, red-ochre work, garland designs, creeper designs, the makara-tooth pattern, the five-panel pattern, a robe rack, and a robe cord.” There were no drinking water vessels… “I allow, O monks, a drinking conch and a water bowl.”

Pākārādianujānanaṃ

The Allowance for Walls, etc.

302. Tena [T 2.0100] kho pana samayena vihārā aparikkhittā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo pākāre – iṭṭhakāpākāraṃ, silāpākāraṃ, dārupākāra”nti. Koṭṭhako na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koṭṭhaka”nti. Koṭṭhako nīcavatthuko hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Koṭṭhakassa kavāṭaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsakaṃ aggaḷavaṭṭiṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭikaṃ tāḷacchiddaṃ [M 0.0300] āviñchanacchiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti. Koṭṭhake tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭika”nti.

302. At that time the monasteries were unenclosed. They informed the Blessed One about this matter. 'I allow, monks, enclosing with three kinds of walls: a brick wall, a stone wall, and a wooden wall.' There was no gatehouse… 'I allow, monks, a gatehouse.' The gatehouse had a low foundation and was flooded by water… 'I allow, monks, to make the foundation high.' The gatehouse had no door… 'I allow, monks, a door, a door-post, a lower pivot, an upper pivot, a bolt-holder, a latch, a pin, a hasp, a keyhole, a pull-hole, and a pull-rope.' Grass-dust fell into the gatehouse… 'I allow, monks, after brushing it down, to plaster it inside and out and to create designs: whitewashing, black coloring, red-ochre work, garland work, creeper work, a makara-tooth pattern, and a five-panel pattern.'

Tena kho pana samayena pariveṇaṃ cikkhallaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, marumbaṃ upakiritu”nti. Na pariyāpuṇanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave[P 2.0154][V 0.0281], padarasilaṃ nikkhipitu”nti. Udakaṃ santiṭṭhati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamana”nti.

At that time the monastery grounds were muddy. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, gravel to be scattered.' It was not sufficient… 'I allow, monks, a stone pavement to be laid down.' Water pooled… 'I allow, monks, a drain.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū pariveṇe tahaṃ tahaṃ aggiṭṭhānaṃ karonti. Pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekamantaṃ aggisālaṃ kātu”nti[T 2.0101]. Aggisālā nīcavatthukā hoti, udakena otthariyyati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṃ kātu”nti. Cayo paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṃ tayo caye – iṭṭhakācayaṃ, silācayaṃ, dārucaya”nti. Ārohantā vihaññanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne – iṭṭhakāsopānaṃ, silāsopānaṃ, dārusopāna”nti. Ārohantā paripatanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāha”nti. Aggisālāya kavāṭaṃ na hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṃ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ udukkhalikaṃ uttarapāsakaṃ aggaḷavaṭṭiṃ kapisīsakaṃ sūcikaṃ ghaṭikaṃ tāḷacchiddaṃ āviñchanacchiddaṃ āviñchanarajju”nti. Aggisālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajju”nti.

At that time, the monks were making fireplaces here and there in the monastery compound. The monastery compound became littered. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, to make a fire-hall in a suitable place.' The fire-hall had a low foundation and was flooded by water… 'I allow, monks, to make it with a high foundation.' The embankment collapsed… 'I allow, monks, to construct three kinds of embankments: a brick embankment, a stone embankment, and a wooden embankment.' Those climbing up became weary… 'I allow, monks, three kinds of staircases: a brick staircase, a stone staircase, and a wooden staircase.' Those climbing up fell… 'I allow, monks, a handrail.' The fire-hall had no door… 'I allow, monks, a door-leaf, a door-post, a lower pivot socket, an upper pivot ring, a slot for the bolt, a monkey-head staple, a pin, a latch, a keyhole, a hole for a pull-cord, and a pull-cord.' Grass dust fell in the fire-hall… 'I allow, monks, after covering it over, to plaster it inside and out, and to make whitewashing, black coloring, red-ochre work, garland designs, creeper designs, a makara-tooth pattern, a five-panel pattern, a robe-bamboo, and a robe-cord.'

Ārāmaparikkhepaanujānanaṃ

Permission for a Monastery Enclosure

303. Tena kho pana samayena ārāmo aparikkhitto hoti. Ajakāpi pasukāpi uparope viheṭhenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṃ tayo vāṭe – veḷuvāṭaṃ, kaṇḍakavāṭaṃ vaṭe veḷuvaṭaṃ kaṇḍakavaṭaṃ (syā.), parikha”nti. Koṭṭhako na hoti. Tatheva ajakāpi pasukāpi uparope viheṭhenti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koṭṭhakaṃ apesiṃ yamakakavāṭaṃ toraṇaṃ paligha”nti. Koṭṭhake tiṇacuṇṇaṃ paripatati…pe… “anujānāmi[M 0.0301], bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṃ kātuṃ – setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ [T 2.0102] latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭika”nti. Ārāmo cikkhallo hoti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, marumbaṃ upakiritu”nti. Na pariyāpuṇanti…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, padarasilaṃ nikkhipitu”nti. Udakaṃ santiṭṭhati…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamana”nti.

303. At that time, the monastery was unenclosed. Goats and cattle harassed the trees planted nearby. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow enclosing with three kinds of enclosures: a bamboo fence, a thorny fence, and a moat.” There was no gatehouse. Just as before, goats and cattle harassed the trees planted nearby… “Monks, I allow a gatehouse, a bolt, a double door, an archway, and a crossbar.” Grass dust fell in the gatehouse… “Monks, I allow it to be covered and plastered inside and out, and to be finished with whitewashing, blackening, red-ochre work, garland designs, creeper designs, makara-tooth designs, and five-panel designs.” The monastery was muddy… “Monks, I allow the spreading of gravel.” It was not enough… “Monks, I allow the laying of flagstones.” Water collected… “Monks, I allow a drain for the water.”

Tena kho pana samayena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro saṅghassa atthāya sudhāmattikālepanaṃ pāsādaṃ kāretukāmo hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā [V 0.0282] chadanaṃ anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññāta”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca chadanāni – iṭṭhakāchadanaṃ, silāchadanaṃ, sudhāchadanaṃ, tiṇacchadanaṃ, paṇṇacchadana”nti.

At that time, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha wished to have a mansion plastered with mortar and clay built for the Saṅgha. Then the monks thought, “What kind of roofing has the Blessed One allowed, and what has he not allowed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow five kinds of roofing: brick roofing, stone roofing, plaster roofing, grass roofing, and leaf roofing.”

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is Concluded.

2. Dutiyabhāṇavāro

2. The Second Recitation Section

Anāthapiṇḍikavatthu

The Account of Anāthapiṇḍika

304. Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa bhaginipatiko hoti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati rājagahaṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahakena seṭṭhinā svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito hoti. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī dāse ca kammakāre kammakare (sī. syā.) ca āṇāpesi – “tena hi, bhaṇe, kālasseva uṭṭhāya yāguyo pacatha, bhattāni pacatha, sūpāni sampādetha, uttaribhaṅgāni sampādethā”ti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa etadahosi – “pubbe khvāyaṃ [T 2.0103] gahapati mayi āgate sabbakiccāni nikkhipitvā mamaññeva saddhiṃ paṭisammodati. Sodānāyaṃ vikkhittarūpo dāse ca kammakāre ca āṇāpesi – ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, kālasseva uṭṭhāya yāguyo pacatha, bhattāni pacatha, sūpāni sampādetha, uttaribhaṅgāni [P 2.0155] sampādethā’ti. Kiṃ nu kho imassa gahapatissa āvāho vā bhavissati, vivāho vā bhavissati, mahāyañño vā paccupaṭṭhito[M 0.0302], rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ balakāyenā”ti?

304. Now at that time, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was the brother-in-law of the wealthy merchant of Rājagaha. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went to Rājagaha on some business or other. Now at that time, the wealthy merchant of Rājagaha had invited the Saṅgha headed by the Buddha for the next day's meal. Then the wealthy merchant of Rājagaha ordered his slaves and workers: “Well then, good sirs, rise early in the morning and prepare the rice gruel, prepare the meals, prepare the soups, and prepare the side dishes.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika thought: “Previously, when I arrived, this householder would set aside all his work and greet me personally. But now he seems distracted and orders his slaves and workers: ‘Well then, good sirs, rise early in the morning and prepare the rice gruel, prepare the meals, prepare the soups, and prepare the side dishes.’ Could it be that for this householder there will be a wedding for giving a daughter away, or a wedding for taking a daughter-in-law? Or is a great sacrifice imminent? Or has King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha been invited for tomorrow along with his army?”

Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī dāse ca kammakāre ca āṇāpetvā yena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā anāthapiṇḍikena gahapatinā saddhiṃ paṭisammoditvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rājagahakaṃ seṭṭhiṃ anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati etadavoca – “pubbe kho tvaṃ, gahapati, mayi āgate sabbakiccāni nikkhipitvā mamaññeva saddhiṃ paṭisammodasi. Sodāni tvaṃ vikkhittarūpo dāse ca kammakāre ca āṇāpesi – ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, kālasseva uṭṭhāya yāguyo pacatha, bhattāni pacatha, sūpāni sampādetha, uttaribhaṅgāni sampādethā’ti. Kiṃ nu kho te, gahapati, āvāho vā bhavissati, vivāho vā bhavissati, mahāyañño vā paccupaṭṭhito, rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ [V 0.0283] balakāyenā”ti? “Na me, gahapati, āvāho [T 2.0104] vā bhavissati, nāpi vivāho vā bhavissati, nāpi rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ balakāyena; api ca me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito; svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito”ti. “Buddhoti tvaṃ, gahapati, vadesī”ti? “Buddho tyāhaṃ, gahapati, vadāmī”ti. “Buddhoti tvaṃ, gahapati, vadesī”ti? “Buddho tyāhaṃ, gahapati, vadāmī”ti. “Buddhoti tvaṃ, gahapati, vadesī”ti? “Buddho tyāhaṃ, gahapati, vadāmī”ti. “Ghosopi kho eso, gahapati, dullabho lokasmiṃ yadidaṃ – buddho buddhoti. Sakkā nu kho, gahapati, imaṃ kālaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti? “Akālo kho, gahapati, imaṃ kālaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Svedāni tvaṃ kālena taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissasi arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati – svedānāhaṃ kālena taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāmi arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhanti – buddhagatāya satiyā nipajjitvā rattiyā sudaṃ tikkhattuṃ vuṭṭhāsi pabhātaṃ maññamāno.

Then the merchant of Rājagaha, having instructed his slaves and workers, approached the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the householder Anāthapiṇḍika and sat down to one side. The householder Anāthapiṇḍika said this to the merchant of Rājagaha who was sitting to one side: “Previously, householder, when I arrived, you would set aside all your duties and exchange courteous greetings with me alone. But now you seem distracted, instructing your slaves and workers: ‘Well then, sirs, rising very early, cook the gruel, cook the rice, prepare the curries, and prepare the side dishes.’ What is it, householder? Will there be a wedding where you give away a daughter, or a wedding where you take a daughter-in-law? Or is a great sacrifice at hand? Or has King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha been invited for tomorrow along with his army?” “Neither will there be a wedding where I give away a daughter, householder, nor a wedding where I take a daughter-in-law, nor has King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha been invited for tomorrow along with his army. But a great sacrifice is at hand for me; for tomorrow, the Saṅgha headed by the Buddha has been invited.” “Do you say ‘Buddha,’ householder?” “I say ‘Buddha,’ householder.” “Do you say ‘Buddha,’ householder?” “I say ‘Buddha,’ householder.” “Do you say ‘Buddha,’ householder?” “I say ‘Buddha,’ householder.” “Even this sound, householder, is rare in the world—that is, ‘Buddha, Buddha.’ Is it possible now, householder, to approach to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One?” “This is not the right time, householder, to approach to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Tomorrow, at the proper time, you will approach to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, thinking, “Tomorrow, at the proper time, I will approach to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One,” lay down with his mindfulness directed toward the Buddha. During the night, he rose three times, thinking it was dawn.

305. saṃ. ni. 1.242 Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena sivakadvāraṃ sīvadvāraṃ (sī.), sītavanadvāraṃ (syā.) tenupasaṅkami. Amanussā dvāraṃ vivariṃsu. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa [M 0.0303] nagaramhā nikkhantassa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro [T 2.0105] pāturahosi, bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso [P 2.0156] udapādi; tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Atha kho sivako sīvako (sī. syā.) yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi –

305. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Sivaka Gate. Non-human beings opened the gate. Then, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, as he was leaving the city, the light disappeared and darkness appeared. Fear, stiffness, and horripilation arose, and from that very spot, he wished to turn back. Then the yakkha Sivaka, having become invisible, made a sound be heard:

“Sataṃ hatthī sataṃ assā, sataṃ assatarīrathā;

Sataṃ kaññāsahassāni, āmukkamaṇikuṇḍalā;

Ekassa padavītihārassa, kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ soḷasinti (sī. ka.).

One hundred thousand elephants, one hundred thousand horses, one hundred thousand chariots drawn by she-mules, and one hundred thousand maidens adorned with jeweled earrings, are not worth the sixteenth part of a single footstep.

“Abhikkama gahapati abhikkama gahapati;

Abhikkantaṃ te seyyo no paṭikkanta”nti.

“Go forward, householder! Go forward, householder! For you, going forward is better; retreating is not.”

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi, āloko pāturahosi. Yaṃ ahosi bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso so paṭippassambhi. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho…pe… anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ [V 0.0284] lomahaṃso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Tatiyampi kho sivako yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi –

Then, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the darkness disappeared and the light appeared. The fear, stiffness, and horripilation that had arisen subsided. For a second time… For a third time, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the light disappeared and darkness appeared. Fear, stiffness, and horripilation arose, and from that very spot, he wished to turn back. For the third time, the yakkha Sivaka, having become invisible, made a sound be heard:

“Sataṃ hatthī sataṃ assā, sataṃ assatarīrathā;

Sataṃ kaññāsahassāni, āmukkamaṇikuṇḍalā;

Ekassa padavītihārassa, kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ.

One hundred thousand elephants, one hundred thousand horses, one hundred thousand chariots drawn by she-mules, and one hundred thousand maidens adorned with jeweled earrings, are not worth the sixteenth part of a single footstep.

“Abhikkama gahapati abhikkama gahapati,

Abhikkantaṃ te seyyo no paṭikkanta”nti.

“Go forward, householder! Go forward, householder! For you, going forward is better; retreating is not.”

Tatiyampi kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi[T 2.0106], āloko pāturahosi, yaṃ ahosi bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso, so paṭippassambhi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena sītavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya ajjhokāse caṅkamati. Addasā kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna caṅkamā orohitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ [M 0.0304] etadavoca – “ehi sudattā”ti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati – nāmena maṃ bhagavā ālapatīti – haṭṭho udaggo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kacci, bhante, bhagavā sukhaṃ sayitthā”ti?

For the third time, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the darkness disappeared and light appeared. The fear, stiffness, and horripilation that had arisen subsided. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Sītavana. At that time, the Blessed One had risen in the early dawn and was walking in the open. The Blessed One saw the householder Anāthapiṇḍika coming from afar. Having seen him, he descended from the walking path and sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Come, Sudatta.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, joyful and elated that the Blessed One was addressing him by name, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One’s feet and said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, did the Blessed One sleep well?”

saṃ. ni. 1.242 “Sabbadā ve sukhaṃ seti, brāhmaṇo parinibbuto;

Yo na limpati kāmesu, sītibhūto nirūpadhi.

“Always, indeed, does the brāhmaṇa who is fully extinguished sleep in peace; he who is not stained by sensual pleasures, having become cooled, is without attachments.

“Sabbā āsattiyo chetvā, vineyya hadaye daraṃ;

Upasanto sukhaṃ seti, santiṃ pappuyya cetasā”ti cetasoti (sī. syā.).

Having cut off all attachments, having dispelled distress in the heart, the peaceful one sleeps in peace, having attained tranquility with the mind.”

Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ ānupubbikathaṃ (sī.) kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā [T 2.0107] bhagavā aññāsi anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ kallacittaṃ muducittaṃ vinīvaraṇacittaṃ udaggacittaṃ pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi [V 0.0285] – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ [P 2.0157] apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ bhante, abhikkantaṃ bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ. Adhivāsetu ca me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.

Then the Blessed One gave the householder Anāthapiṇḍika a sequential discourse, that is to say: a discourse on giving, a discourse on virtue, a discourse on heaven; he explained the danger, inferiority, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that the householder Anāthapiṇḍika’s mind was receptive, soft, free from hindrances, uplifted, and clear, he then revealed that Dhamma teaching which is the special instruction of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free of black stains, would properly absorb dye, even so, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, right in that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose: “Whatever is of the nature to arise, all that is of the nature to cease.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over doubt, was without perplexity, attained to confidence, and was not reliant on another in the Teacher’s dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One. I, venerable sir, go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One regard me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts. And may the Blessed One, venerable sir, consent to my meal for tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by silence.

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Assosi [T 2.0108] kho [M 0.0305] rājagahako seṭṭhī – “anāthapiṇḍikena kira gahapatinā svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito”ti.

Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, having known the Blessed One’s acceptance, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed. The merchant of Rājagaha heard: “It is said that the householder Anāthapiṇḍika has invited the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow.”

306. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “tayā kira, gahapati, svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito. Tvañcāsi āgantuko. Demi te, gahapati, veyyāyikaṃ yena tvaṃ buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa bhattaṃ kareyyāsī”ti. “Alaṃ, gahapati atthi me veyyāyikaṃ yenāhaṃ buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa bhattaṃ karissāmī”ti.

306. Then the merchant of Rājagaha said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Householder, it is said that you have invited the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow. And you are a visitor. Householder, let me provide you with the means so that you may offer a meal to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head.” “Enough, householder; I have the means by which I shall offer a meal to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head.”

Assosi kho rājagahako negamo – “anāthapiṇḍikena kira gahapatinā svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito”ti. Atha kho rājagahako negamo anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “tayā kira, gahapati, svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito. Tvañcāsi āgantuko. Demi te, gahapati, veyyāyikaṃ yena tvaṃ buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa bhattaṃ kareyyāsī”ti. “Alaṃ ayya; atthi me veyyāyikaṃ yenāhaṃ buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa bhattaṃ karissāmī”ti.

The town-merchant of Rājagaha heard: “It is said that the householder Anāthapiṇḍika has invited the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow.” Then the town-merchant of Rājagaha said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Householder, it is said that you have invited the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow. And you are a visitor. Householder, let me provide you with the means so that you may offer a meal to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head.” “Enough, sir; I have the means by which I shall offer a meal to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head.”

Assosi kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro – “anāthapiṇḍikena kira gahapatinā svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito”ti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro anāthapiṇḍikaṃ [V 0.0286] gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “tayā kira, gahapati, svātanāya buddhappamukho saṅgho nimantito. Tvañcāsi āgantuko. Demi te, gahapati, veyyāyikaṃ yena tvaṃ buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa bhattaṃ kareyyāsī”ti. “Alaṃ [T 2.0109] deva; atthi me veyyāyikaṃ yenāhaṃ buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa bhattaṃ karissāmī”ti.

King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha heard: “It is said that the householder Anāthapiṇḍika has invited the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow.” Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Householder, it is said that you have invited the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow. And you are a visitor. Householder, let me provide you with the means so that you may offer a meal to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head.” “Enough, Your Majesty; I have the means by which I shall offer a meal to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head.”

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati tassā rattiyā accayena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā [P 2.0158] bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ, ekamantaṃ nisīdi[M 0.0306]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ vassāvāsaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. “Suññāgāre kho, gahapati, tathāgatā abhiramantī”ti. “Aññātaṃ bhagavā, aññātaṃ sugatā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then, when the night had passed, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had excellent hard and soft food prepared in the residence of the merchant of Rājagaha and had the time announced to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable sir, it is time; the meal is ready.” Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and outer robe, and went to the residence of the merchant of Rājagaha. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Anāthapiṇḍika sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to my invitation to spend the rains-residence in Sāvatthī together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” “Householder, Tathāgatas delight in secluded dwellings.” “It is understood, Blessed One; it is understood, Sugata.” Then the Blessed One, having instructed, roused, encouraged, and gladdened the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat and departed.

307. Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bahumitto hoti bahusahāyo ādeyyavāco. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati rājagahe taṃ karaṇīyaṃ tīretvā yena sāvatthi tena pakkāmi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati antarāmagge manusse āṇāpesi – “ārāme[T 2.0110], ayyā, karotha, vihāre patiṭṭhāpetha, dānāni paṭṭhapetha. Buddho loke uppanno. So ca mayā bhagavā nimantito iminā maggena āgacchissatī”ti. Atha kho te manussā anāthapiṇḍikena gahapatinā uyyojitā ārāme akaṃsu, vihāre patiṭṭhāpesuṃ, dānāni paṭṭhapesuṃ.

307. Now at that time, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had many friends and companions, and his word was heeded. Then, after concluding that business in Rājagaha, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika departed for Sāvatthī. Then, along the way, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika commanded the people: “Sirs, make parks, establish monasteries, and prepare alms-givings. A Buddha has arisen in the world. And that Blessed One has been invited by me; he will be coming by this road.” Then those people, being urged on by the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, made parks, established monasteries, and prepared alms-givings.

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati sāvatthiṃ gantvā samantā sāvatthiṃ anuvilokesi – “kattha nu kho bhagavā vihareyya? Yaṃ assa gāmato neva atidūre na accāsanne, gamanāgamanasampannaṃ, atthikānaṃ atthikānaṃ manussānaṃ abhikkamanīyaṃ, divā appākiṇṇaṃ, rattiṃ appasaddaṃ, appanigghosaṃ, vijanavātaṃ, manussarāhasseyyakaṃ, paṭisallānasāruppa”nti.

Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, having gone to Sāvatthī, looked all around Sāvatthī, thinking: “In what place, indeed, might the Blessed One dwell? A place that is neither too far from the village nor too near, convenient for coming and going, accessible to those who wish to visit, uncrowded by day, quiet at night, with little noise, free from the presence of people, secluded from people, and suitable for retreat.”

Addasā [V 0.0287] kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati jetassa kumārassa rājakumārassa (sī. syā. kaṃ.) uyyānaṃ – gāmato neva atidūre na accāsanne, gamanāgamanasampannaṃ, atthikānaṃ atthikānaṃ manussānaṃ abhikkamanīyaṃ, divā appākiṇṇaṃ, rattiṃ appasaddaṃ, appanigghosaṃ, vijanavātaṃ, manussarāhasseyyakaṃ, paṭisallānasāruppaṃ. Disvāna yena jeto kumāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā jetaṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “dehi me, ayyaputta, uyyānaṃ ārāmaṃ kātu”nti ketuṃ (vajīrabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ). “Adeyyo, gahapati, ārāmo api koṭisantharenā”ti. “Gahito, ayyaputta, ārāmo”ti. “Na, gahapati, gahito ārāmo”ti. Gahito na gahitoti vohārike mahāmatte pucchiṃsu. Mahāmattā evamāhaṃsu [M 0.0307] – “yato tayā[P 2.0159], ayyaputta, aggho kato, gahito ārāmo”ti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko [T 2.0111] gahapati sakaṭehi hiraññaṃ nibbāhāpetvā jetavanaṃ koṭisantharaṃ santharāpesi. Sakiṃ nīhaṭaṃ hiraññaṃ thokassa okāsassa koṭṭhakasāmantā nappahoti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati manusse āṇāpesi – “gacchatha, bhaṇe, hiraññaṃ āharatha; imaṃ okāsaṃ santharissāmā”ti.

Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika saw Prince Jeta’s park—it was neither too far from the village nor too near, convenient for coming and going, accessible to those who wish to visit, uncrowded by day, quiet at night, with little noise, free from the presence of people, secluded from people, and suitable for retreat. Having seen it, he approached Prince Jeta and said, “Young lord, give me the park to make a monastery.” “Householder, the park is not to be given, except by paving it with coins.” “The park is bought, young lord.” “No, householder, the park is not bought.” They consulted the legal officials as to whether it was bought or not bought. The legal officials said, “Young lord, since you have set a price, the park is bought.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had gold brought by carts and had Jeta’s Grove paved with a layer of coins. The gold brought at one time did not suffice for a small area near the gatehouse. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika ordered his men, “Go, sirs, bring more gold; we will cover this area.”

Atha kho jetassa kumārassa etadahosi – “na kho idaṃ orakaṃ bhavissati, yathāyaṃ gahapati tāva bahuṃ hiraññaṃ pariccajatī”ti. Anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, gahapati; mā taṃ okāsaṃ santharāpesi. Dehi me etaṃ okāsaṃ. Mametaṃ dānaṃ bhavissatī”ti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati – ayaṃ kho jeto kumāro abhiññāto ñātamanusso; mahatthiko kho pana evarūpānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pasādoti – taṃ okāsaṃ jetassa kumārassa pādāsi adāsi (syā.). Atha kho jeto kumāro tasmiṃ okāse koṭṭhakaṃ māpesi.

Then this thought occurred to Prince Jeta: “This will surely be no trifling matter, in that this householder is giving up so much gold.” He said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Enough, householder; do not have that space covered. Give me this space. It will be my donation.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, thinking, “This Prince Jeta is well-known, a famous person; indeed, the confidence of such famous people in this Dhamma and Discipline is of great benefit,” gave that space to Prince Jeta. Then Prince Jeta had a gatehouse built in that space.

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati jetavane vihāre kārāpesi, pariveṇāni kārāpesi, koṭṭhake kārāpesi, upaṭṭhānasālāyo kārāpesi, aggisālāyo kārāpesi, kappiyakuṭiyo kārāpesi, vaccakuṭiyo kārāpesi, caṅkame kārāpesi, caṅkamanasālāyo kārāpesi, udapāne kārāpesi, udapānasālāyo kārāpesi, jantāghare kārāpesi, jantāgharasālāyo kārāpesi, pokkharaṇiyo kārāpesi, maṇḍape [T 2.0112] kārāpesi.

Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had built in Jeta’s Grove: dwellings, surrounding cells, gatehouses, attendance halls, fire halls, storerooms for allowable things, latrines, walkways, halls adjoining the walkways, wells, well-pavilions, steam-bath houses, halls for the steam-baths, ponds, and pavilions.

Navakammadānaṃ

The Assignment of New Construction

308. Atha kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena manussā sakkaccaṃ navakammaṃ [V 0.0288] karonti. Yepi bhikkhū navakammaṃ adhiṭṭhenti tepi sakkaccaṃ upaṭṭhenti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena[M 0.0308]. Atha kho aññatarassa daliddassa tunnavāyassa etadahosi – “na kho idaṃ orakaṃ bhavissati, yathayime manussā sakkaccaṃ navakammaṃ karonti; yaṃnūnāhampi navakammaṃ kareyya”nti. Atha kho so daliddo tunnavāyo sāmaṃ cikkhallaṃ madditvā iṭṭhakāyo cinitvā kuṭṭaṃ uṭṭhāpesi. Tena akusalakena citā vaṅkā bhitti paripati. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho so daliddo tunnavāyo sāmaṃ cikkhallaṃ madditvā iṭṭhakāyo cinitvā kuṭṭaṃ uṭṭhāpesi. Tena akusalakena citā vaṅkā bhitti paripati. Atha kho so daliddo tunnavāyo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “ye imesaṃ samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ [P 2.0160] denti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ, te ime ovadanti anusāsanti, tesañca navakammaṃ adhiṭṭhenti. Ahaṃ [T 2.0113] panamhi daliddo. Na maṃ koci ovadati vā anusāsati vā navakammaṃ vā adhiṭṭhetī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa daliddassa tunnavāyassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, navakammaṃ dātuṃ. Navakammiko, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ussukkaṃ āpajjissati – ‘kinti nu kho vihāro khippaṃ pariyosānaṃ gaccheyyā’ti; khaṇḍaṃ phullaṃ paṭisaṅkharissati. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

308. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha for as long as he was pleased, set out on a journey toward Vesālī. Traveling in stages, he eventually arrived at Vesālī. There the Blessed One stayed in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the Hall with the Peaked Roof. At that time, people were earnestly engaged in new construction. The monks who were in charge of the new construction were also diligently provided with robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal supplies as requisites for the sick. Then a certain poor tailor thought: 'This is surely no inferior matter, how these people are earnestly engaged in new construction. Why should I not also undertake new construction?' So that poor tailor himself kneaded clay, laid bricks, and built a wall. But due to his lack of skill, the wall he built was crooked and collapsed. A second time... a third time, that poor tailor himself kneaded clay, laid bricks, and built a wall. But due to his lack of skill, the wall he built was crooked and collapsed. Then that poor tailor complained, grumbled, and protested: 'Those who give robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal supplies as requisites for the sick to these ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, are advised and instructed by them, and they oversee their new construction. But I am poor. No one advises or instructs me, nor oversees my new construction.' The monks heard that poor tailor complaining, grumbling, and protesting. Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One, on this occasion, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow the assigning of new construction work.
