A monk in charge of new construction, monks, should be diligent, thinking, “How might the dwelling be quickly completed?” He should repair what is broken or damaged. And monks, it should be given in this way: First, a monk should be requested. Having been requested, a competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:'

309. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa gahapatino vihāraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno navakammaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

309. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If the time is right for the Sangha, the Sangha should assign the new construction work for the monastery of the householder named so-and-so to the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmassa gahapatino vihāraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno navakammaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa gahapatino vihāraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno navakammassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha assigns the new construction work for the monastery of the householder named so-and-so to the monk named so-and-so. If any venerable one approves of the assigning of the new construction work for the monastery of the householder named so-and-so to the monk named so-and-so, he should remain silent. If anyone does not approve, he should speak.

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa gahapatino vihāro itthannāmassa bhikkhuno navakammaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The new construction work for the monastery of the householder named so-and-so has been assigned by the Sangha to the monk named so-and-so. The Sangha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I record it.

Aggāsanādianujānanaṃ

The Allowing of the Foremost Seat and So Forth

310. Atha [M 0.0309] kho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi[V 0.0289]. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [T 2.0114] antevāsikā bhikkhū buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa purato purato gantvā vihāre pariggaṇhanti, seyyāyo pariggaṇhanti – idaṃ amhākaṃ upajjhāyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ bhavissatī”ti.

310. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Vesālī for as long as he was pleased, set out on a journey toward Sāvatthī. Now at that time, the resident pupils of the group-of-six monks, going on ahead of the Sangha with the Buddha at its head, were taking possession of the monasteries and lodgings, saying: ‘This will be for our preceptors, this will be for our teachers, and this will be for us.’”

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā vihāresu pariggahitesu, seyyāsu pariggahitāsu, seyyaṃ alabhamāno aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya ukkāsi. Āyasmāpi sāriputto ukkāsi. “Ko etthā”ti? “Ahaṃ, bhagavā, sāriputto”ti. “Kissa tvaṃ, sāriputtaṃ, idha nisinno”ti? Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyānaṃ [P 2.0161] bhikkhūnaṃ antevāsikā bhikkhū buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa purato purato gantvā vihāre pariggaṇhanti, seyyāyo pariggaṇhanti – idaṃ amhākaṃ upajjhāyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ bhavissatī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa purato purato gantvā vihāre pariggahessanti, seyyāyo pariggahessanti – idaṃ amhākaṃ upajjhāyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ bhavissatīti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ [T 2.0115] vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “ko, bhikkhave, arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti?

Then the Venerable Sāriputta, following behind the Sangha with the Buddha at its head, since the monasteries and lodgings had been taken, was unable to find a lodging and sat down at the foot of a certain tree. Then the Blessed One, having risen at dawn, cleared his throat. The Venerable Sāriputta also cleared his throat. 'Who is there?' 'It is I, Blessed One, Sāriputta.' 'Sāriputta, why are you sitting here?' Then the Venerable Sāriputta informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this context, had the community of monks assembled and questioned the monks: 'Monks, is it true that the resident pupils of the group-of-six monks go on ahead of the Sangha with the Buddha at its head and take possession of the monasteries and lodgings, saying: “This will be for our preceptors, this will be for our teachers, and this will be for us”?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How, monks, could those foolish men go on ahead of the Sangha with the Buddha at its head and take possession of the monasteries and lodgings, saying: “This will be for our preceptors, this will be for our teachers, and this will be for us”? This, monks, is not for inspiring faith in the faithless…' Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, who is worthy of the foremost seat, the foremost water, and the foremost almsfood?'

Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, khattiyakulā pabbajito so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, brāhmaṇakulā pabbajito so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, gahapatikulā pabbajito so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce [M 0.0310] bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, suttantiko so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, vinayadharo so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ [V 0.0290] aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, dhammakathiko so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, dutiyassa jhānassa lābhī so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, tatiyassa jhānassa lābhī so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, catutthassa jhānassa lābhī so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, sotāpanno so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, sakadāgāmī…pe… yo, bhagavā, anāgāmī…pe… yo, bhagavā[T 2.0116], arahā so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, tevijjo so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti. Ekacce bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “yo, bhagavā, chaḷabhiñño so arahati aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa”nti.

Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has gone forth from a noble family deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has gone forth from a brahmin family deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has gone forth from a householder’s family deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who is a master of the discourses deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who is a master of the discipline deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who is a preacher of the Dhamma deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has attained the first jhāna deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has attained the second jhāna deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has attained the third jhāna deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one who has attained the fourth jhāna deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, a stream-enterer deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, a once-returner… a non-returner… an arahant deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one with the three knowledges deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.” Some monks said: “Venerable sir, one with the six super-knowledges deserves the best seat, the best water, and the best alms-food.”

311. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, himavantapadese himavantapasse (sī. syā.) mahānigrodho ahosi. Taṃ tayo sahāyā upanissāya vihariṃsu – tittiro ca, makkaṭo ca, hatthināgo ca. Te aññamaññaṃ agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā viharanti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, tesaṃ sahāyānaṃ etadahosi – ‘aho nūna mayaṃ jāneyyāma yaṃ amhākaṃ jātiyā mahantataraṃ taṃ mayaṃ sakkareyyāma garuṃ kareyyāma māneyyāma pūjeyyāma, tassa ca mayaṃ ovāde tiṭṭheyyāmā’ti.

311. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, once upon a time, in the Himalayan region, there was a great banyan tree. Three friends lived in dependence on it: a partridge, a monkey, and an elephant. They lived without respect for one another, without deference, and without a common way of life. Then, monks, this thought occurred to those friends: “It would be good if we were to find out which of us is the eldest by birth. We would honor him, respect him, esteem him, and venerate him, and we would abide by his instruction.”'

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, tittiro ca makkaṭo ca hatthināgaṃ pucchiṃsu – ‘tvaṃ, samma, kiṃ porāṇaṃ sarasī’ti? ‘Yadāhaṃ, sammā, poto homi, imaṃ nigrodhaṃ antarā [M 0.0311] satthīnaṃ antarāsatthikaṃ (sī.) karitvā atikkamāmi, aggaṅkurakaṃ me udaraṃ chupati. Imāhaṃ, sammā, porāṇaṃ sarāmī’ti.

Then, monks, the partridge and the monkey asked the elephant: 'Friend, what ancient thing do you remember?' 'When I was young, friends, I could step over this banyan tree, having placed it between my thighs, and its topmost shoot would touch my belly. This, friends, is the ancient thing I remember.'

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, tittiro ca hatthināgo ca makkaṭaṃ pucchiṃsu – ‘tvaṃ, samma, kiṃ porāṇaṃ sarasī’ti? ‘Yadāhaṃ, sammā, chāpo homi, chamāyaṃ nisīditvā imassa nigrodhassa aggaṅkurakaṃ khādāmi. Imāhaṃ, sammā, porāṇaṃ sarāmī’ti.

Then, monks, the partridge and the elephant asked the monkey: 'Friend, what ancient thing do you remember?' 'When I was young, friends, I would sit on the ground and eat the topmost shoot of this banyan tree. This, friends, is the ancient thing I remember.'

“Atha [T 2.0117] kho, bhikkhave, makkaṭo ca hatthināgo ca tittiraṃ pucchiṃsu – ‘tvaṃ, samma, kiṃ porāṇaṃ sarasī’ti? ‘Amukasmiṃ, sammā, okāse mahānigrodho ahosi. Tato ahaṃ phalaṃ bhakkhitvā imasmiṃ okāse vaccaṃ akāsiṃ; tassāyaṃ nigrodho jāto. Tadāhaṃ, sammā, jātiyā mahantataro’ti[P 2.0162].

Then, monks, the monkey and the elephant asked the partridge: ‘Friend, what ancient thing do you remember?’ ‘Friends, in a certain place, there was a great banyan tree. Having eaten a fruit from it, I passed excrement in this spot; from that, this banyan tree grew. Therefore, friends, I am the eldest by birth.’

“Atha [V 0.0291] kho, bhikkhave, makkaṭo ca hatthināgo ca tittiraṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘tvaṃ, samma, amhākaṃ jātiyā mahantataro. Taṃ mayaṃ sakkarissāma garuṃ karissāma mānessāma pūjessāma, tuyhañca mayaṃ ovāde patiṭṭhissāmā’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, tittiro makkaṭañca hatthināgañca pañcasu sīlesu samādapesi, attanā ca pañcasu sīlesu samādāya vattati. Te aññamaññaṃ sagāravā sappatissā sabhāgavuttikā viharitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjiṃsu. Evaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, tittiriyaṃ nāma brahmacariyaṃ ahosi.

“Then, monks, the monkey and the elephant said to the partridge: ‘Friend, you are greater than us by birth. We will honor, respect, esteem, and revere you, and we will abide by your instruction.’ Then, monks, the partridge established the monkey and the elephant in the five precepts, and he himself lived observing the five precepts. Living with mutual respect, deference, and a common way of life, after the breakup of the body, upon death, they were reborn in a good destination, the heavenly world. Thus, monks, that was the holy life called 'Tittiriya'.”

jā. 1.1.37 “Ye vuḍḍhamapacāyanti, narā dhammassa kovidā;

Diṭṭhe dhamme ca pāsaṃsā, samparāye ca suggatī”ti.

“Those people who respect the elderly, wise in the Dhamma, are praised in this very life, and have a good destination in the next.”

“Te hi nāma, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā aññamaññaṃ sagāravā sappatissā sabhāgavuttikā viharissanti. Idha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sobhetha yaṃ tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṃ agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā vihareyyātha? Netaṃ, bhikkhave[T 2.0118], appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ, añjalikammaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ, aggāsanaṃ, aggodakaṃ, aggapiṇḍaṃ. Na ca, bhikkhave, saṅghikaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

“Monks, even those beings who are animals live with mutual respect, deference, and a common way of life. How then, monks, could it be fitting for you, who have gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, to live without mutual respect, deference, and a common way of life? This, monks, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident… Having rebuked them… he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks: ‘I allow, monks, according to seniority: paying homage, rising, saluting with joined palms, proper etiquette, the first seat, the first water, and the first alms-food. And, monks, what belongs to the Saṅgha should not be withheld according to seniority. Whoever should withhold it commits an offense of wrong-doing.’”

Avandiyādipuggalā

Persons Not to Be Venerated, Etc.

312. “Dasayime[M 0.0312], bhikkhave, avandiyā – pure upasampannena pacchā upasampanno avandiyo, anupasampanno avandiyo, nānāsaṃvāsako vuḍḍhataro adhammavādī avandiyo, mātugāmo avandiyo, paṇḍako avandiyo, pārivāsiko avandiyo, mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho avandiyo, mānattāraho avandiyo, mānattacāriko avandiyo, abbhānāraho avandiyo. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa avandiyā.

312. Bhikkhus, these ten are persons not to be venerated: a bhikkhu ordained later is not to be venerated by a bhikkhu ordained earlier; an unordained person is not to be venerated; a senior bhikkhu of a different communion who speaks contrary to the Dhamma is not to be venerated; a woman is not to be venerated; a eunuch is not to be venerated; a bhikkhu undergoing probation is not to be venerated; a bhikkhu liable to be sent back to the beginning is not to be venerated; a bhikkhu deserving of penance is not to be venerated; a bhikkhu undergoing penance is not to be venerated; a bhikkhu deserving of rehabilitation is not to be venerated. These, Bhikkhus, are the ten persons not to be venerated.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, vandiyā – pacchā upasampannena pure upasampanno vandiyo, nānāsaṃvāsako vuḍḍhataro dhammavādī vandiyo, sadevake bhikkhave loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vandiyo. Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo vandiyā”ti.

Bhikkhus, these three are persons to be venerated: a bhikkhu ordained earlier is to be venerated by a bhikkhu ordained later; a senior bhikkhu of a different communion who speaks in accordance with the Dhamma is to be venerated; in the world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is to be venerated. These, Bhikkhus, are the three persons to be venerated.

Āsanappaṭibāhanapaṭikkhepaṃ

The Rejection of Prohibiting Seats

313. Tena [V 0.0292] kho pana samayena manussā saṅghaṃ uddissa maṇḍape paṭiyādenti, santhare paṭiyādenti, okāse paṭiyādenti. Chabbaggiyānaṃ [P 2.0163] bhikkhūnaṃ antevāsikā bhikkhū – ‘saṅghikaññeva bhagavatā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ anuññātaṃ[T 2.0119], no uddissakata’nti buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa purato purato gantvā maṇḍapepi pariggaṇhanti, santharepi pariggaṇhanti, okāsepi pariggaṇhanti – idaṃ amhākaṃ upajjhāyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ bhavissatīti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā maṇḍapesu pariggahitesu, santharesu pariggahitesu, okāsesu pariggahitesu, okāsaṃ alabhamāno aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya ukkāsi. Āyasmāpi sāriputto ukkāsi. “Ko etthā”ti? “Ahaṃ, bhagavā, sāriputto”ti. “Kissa tvaṃ, sāriputta, idha nisinno”ti? Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ antevāsikā bhikkhū – ‘saṅghikaññeva bhagavatā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ anuññātaṃ, no uddissakata’nti buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa purato purato gantvā [M 0.0313] maṇḍape pariggaṇhanti, santhare pariggaṇhanti, okāse pariggaṇhanti – idaṃ amhākaṃ upajjhāyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ bhavissati, idaṃ amhākaṃ bhavissatī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, uddissakatampi yathāvuḍḍhaṃ paṭibāhetabbaṃ. Yo [T 2.0120] paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

313. At that time, people were preparing pavilions, floor-coverings, and spaces in dedication to the Sangha. The resident-pupil bhikkhus of the group-of-six bhikkhus—saying, “The Blessed One has only permitted what belongs to the Sangha according to seniority, not what is specifically dedicated”—went ahead of the Sangha headed by the Buddha and took possession of the pavilions, the floor-coverings, and the spaces, saying, “This will be for our preceptors, this will be for our teachers, this will be for us.” Then, the Venerable Sāriputta, following behind the Sangha headed by the Buddha, found that the pavilions, floor-coverings, and spaces had been taken. Unable to find a space, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree. Then, at the time of dawn, the Blessed One rose and coughed. The Venerable Sāriputta also coughed. “Who is there?” “It is I, Blessed One, Sāriputta.” “Sāriputta, why are you sitting here?” Then the Venerable Sāriputta related this matter to the Blessed One. Then, on that occasion, in that matter, the Blessed One convened the Sangha of bhikkhus and questioned the bhikkhus: “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the resident-pupil bhikkhus of the group-of-six bhikkhus—saying, ‘The Blessed One has only permitted what belongs to the Sangha according to seniority, not what is specifically dedicated’—went ahead of the Sangha headed by the Buddha and took possession of the pavilions, the floor-coverings, and the spaces, saying, ‘This will be for our preceptors, this will be for our teachers, this will be for us’?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … After rebuking them … having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, even what is specifically dedicated should not be prohibited according to seniority. Whoever should prohibit it, incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

Gihivikataanujānanaṃ

Permission Regarding Articles Belonging to Householders

314. Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhattagge antaraghare uccāsayanamahāsayanāni paññapenti, seyyathidaṃ – āsandiṃ, pallaṅkaṃ, gonakaṃ, cittakaṃ, paṭikaṃ, paṭalikaṃ, tūlikaṃ, vikatikaṃ, uddalomiṃ, ekantalomiṃ, kaṭṭissaṃ, koseyyaṃ koseyyaṃ kambalaṃ (sī. syā.), kuttakaṃ, hatthattharaṃ, assattharaṃ, rathattharaṃ, ajinapaveṇiṃ, kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇaṃ, sauttaracchadaṃ, ubhatolohitakūpadhānaṃ. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nābhinisīdanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā tīṇi – āsandiṃ, pallaṅkaṃ, tūlikaṃ – gihivikataṃ gihivikaṭaṃ (sī. ka.), avasesaṃ gihivikaṭaṃ (syā.) abhinisīdituṃ, natveva abhinipajjitu”nti.

314. At that time, people were arranging high and great seats in dining halls within houses, that is to say: a long-legged chair, a divan with animal figures on its feet, a large carpet with long fleece, a variegated woolen coverlet, a white woolen coverlet, a woolen coverlet thick with flowers, a mattress filled with cotton, a woolen coverlet embroidered with figures such as lions and tigers, a woolen coverlet with fleece on both sides, a woolen coverlet with fleece on one side, a coverlet woven with silk threads and sewn with gems, a silk coverlet, a large woolen carpet sufficient for sixteen dancers, an elephant-saddle rug, a horse-saddle rug, a chariot-rug, a rug made by sewing together panther skins, a superior coverlet made of the hide of the kadalī antelope, a seat with a red canopy above, and a seat with red pillows at both ends. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not sit down upon them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, setting aside three things—a long-legged chair, a divan, and a mattress filled with cotton—I allow you to sit down upon an article belonging to a householder, but not to lie down upon it.”

Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhattagge antaraghare tūlonaddhaṃ mañcampi pīṭhampi paññapenti[V 0.0293]. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nābhinisīdanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gihivikataṃ abhinisīdituṃ, natveva abhinipajjitu”nti.

At that time, people were arranging cotton-upholstered couches and chairs in dining halls within houses. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not sit down upon them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow you to sit down upon an article belonging to a householder, but not to lie down upon it.”

Jetavanavihārānumodanā

The Appreciation for the Dedication of the Jetavana Monastery

315. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati [P 2.0164] jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavantaṃ [T 2.0121] etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ [M 0.0314] abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ, ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathāhaṃ, bhante, jetavane paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, gahapati, jetavanaṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa patiṭṭhapehī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavato paṭissutvā jetavanaṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa patiṭṭhāpesi.

315. Then the Blessed One, wandering on tour by stages, arrived at Sāvatthī. There in Sāvatthī the Blessed One dwelt in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Blessed One, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept tomorrow’s meal from me together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and departed. Then, when the night had passed, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had exquisite food, both hard and soft, prepared and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe, and went to the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika personally served and satisfied the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with exquisite food, both hard and soft, until they indicated they were satisfied. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Anāthapiṇḍika sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how should I act in Jeta’s Grove?” “Well then, householder, establish Jeta’s Grove for the Saṅgha of the four quarters, both present and future.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the householder Anāthapiṇḍika replied to the Blessed One, and he established Jeta’s Grove for the Saṅgha of the four quarters, both present and future.

Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

Then the Blessed One expressed his appreciation to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with these verses:

“Sītaṃ uṇhaṃ paṭihanti, tato vāḷamigāni ca;

Sarīsape [T 2.0122] ca makase, sisire cāpi vuṭṭhiyo.

“It wards off cold and heat, and also wild beasts, reptiles, and mosquitoes, as well as the cold season and the rains.

“Tato vātātapo ghoro, sañjāto paṭihaññati;

Leṇatthañca sukhatthañca, jhāyituñca vipassituṃ.

Furthermore, the fierce, arisen wind and heat are dispelled; it is for the purpose of shelter and for comfort, for meditation and for insight.

“Vihāradānaṃ [V 0.0294] saṅghassa, aggaṃ buddhena vaṇṇitaṃ;

Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano.

The gift of a monastery to the Saṅgha is praised by the Buddha as supreme; therefore indeed, a wise person, seeing their own welfare,

“Vihāre kāraye ramme, vāsayettha bahussute;

Tesaṃ annañca pānañca, vatthasenāsanāni ca;

Dadeyya ujubhūtesu, vippasannena cetasā.

should have delightful monasteries built, and cause the very learned to dwell therein. To them—to the upright—one should give food and drink, clothing, and lodgings, with a specially serene mind.

“Te tassa dhammaṃ desenti, sabbadukkhāpanūdanaṃ;

Yaṃ so dhammaṃ idhaññāya, parinibbāti anāsavo”ti.

They teach him the Dhamma that dispels all suffering. Having understood that Dhamma here, he, being without taints, attains Parinibbāna.”

Atha [P 2.0165] kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with these verses, rose from his seat and departed.

Āsanappaṭibāhanādi

Denying a Seat, etc.

316. Tena [M 0.0315] kho pana samayena aññatarassa ājīvakasāvakassa mahāmattassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti. Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto pacchā āgantvā vippakatabhojanaṃ ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpesi. Bhattaggaṃ kolāhalaṃ ahosi. Atha kho so mahāmatto ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā pacchā āgantvā vippakatabhojanaṃ ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Bhattaggaṃ kolāhalaṃ ahosi. Nanu nāma labbhā aññatrāpi nisinnena yāvadatthaṃ [T 2.0123] bhuñjitu”nti? Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa mahāmattassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto pacchā āgantvā vippakatabhojanaṃ ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpessati! Bhattaggaṃ kolāhalaṃ ahosī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, pacchā āgantvā vippakatabhojanaṃ ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpesi, bhattaggaṃ kolāhalaṃ ahosī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, pacchā āgantvā vippakatabhojanaṃ ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpessasi? Bhattaggaṃ kolāhalaṃ ahosi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, vippakatabhojano bhojano ānantariko (syā.) bhikkhu vuṭṭhāpetabbo. Yo vuṭṭhāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sace vuṭṭhāpeti, pavārito ca hoti, ‘gaccha udakaṃ āharā’ti vattabbo. Evañcetaṃ [V 0.0295] labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, sādhukaṃ sitthāni gilitvā vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, kenaci pariyāyena vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno āsanaṃ paṭibāhitabbanti vadāmi. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti”.

316. Now at that time, a certain high official, a disciple of an Ājīvaka, had a meal for the Saṅgha. The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having arrived late, made a bhikkhu who was next to him and whose meal was unfinished get up. There was an uproar in the dining hall. Then that high official complained, grumbled, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the Sakyan ascetics, having arrived late, make a bhikkhu who is next to them and whose meal is unfinished get up? There was an uproar in the dining hall. Is it not indeed possible for those sitting even elsewhere to eat as much as they wish?” The bhikkhus heard that high official complaining, grumbling, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… complained, grumbled, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having arrived late, make a bhikkhu who was next to him and whose meal was unfinished get up? There was an uproar in the dining hall!” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Is it true, Upananda, that having arrived late, you made a bhikkhu who was next to you and whose meal was unfinished get up, and there was an uproar in the dining hall?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how indeed could you, having arrived late, make a bhikkhu who was next to you and whose meal was unfinished get up? There was an uproar in the dining hall. This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu whose meal is unfinished should not be made to get up. Whoever should make one get up, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one makes him get up, and he has been invited to eat more, he should be told, ‘Go, bring water.’ If one should obtain it thus, this is skillful. If one should not obtain it, having carefully swallowed the morsels, the seat should be given to the more senior bhikkhu. However, bhikkhus, I do not say that in any way a more senior bhikkhu’s seat should be denied. Whoever should deny it, there is an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena [T 2.0124] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū gilāne bhikkhū vuṭṭhāpenti. Gilānā evaṃ vadenti – “na mayaṃ, āvuso, sakkoma vuṭṭhātuṃ, gilānāmhā”ti. “Mayaṃ āyasmante vuṭṭhāpessāmā”ti pariggahetvā vuṭṭhāpetvā ṭhitake muñcanti. Gilānā mucchitā papatanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[M 0.0316]. “Na, bhikkhave, gilāno vuṭṭhāpetabbo. Yo vuṭṭhāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six were making sick bhikkhus get up. The sick bhikkhus said: “Friends, we are not able to get up; we are sick.” Saying, “We will make you venerables get up,” they took hold of them, made them get up, and then released them while they were standing. The sick bhikkhus, having fainted, fell down. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Bhikkhus, a sick bhikkhu is not to be made to get up. Whoever should make one get up, there is an offense of wrong conduct for that bhikkhu.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [P 2.0166] ‘gilānā mayamhā avuṭṭhāpanīyā’ti varaseyyāyo palibuddhenti palibundhanti (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa patirūpaṃ seyyaṃ dātu”nti.

At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six, claiming, “We are sick and are not to be made to get up,” occupied the excellent lodgings. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Bhikkhus, I allow a suitable lodging to be given to a sick bhikkhu.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū lesakappena senāsanaṃ paṭibāhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, lesakappena senāsanaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six were obstructing a lodging on a slight pretext. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‐Bhikkhus, a lodging is not to be obstructed on a slight pretext. Whoever should obstruct one incurs an offense of wrong conduct.‑

pāci. 122 Tena kho pana samayena sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū aññataraṃ paccantimaṃ mahāvihāraṃ paṭisaṅkharonti – ‘idha mayaṃ vassaṃ vasissāmā’ti. Addasaṃsu addasāsuṃ (ka.) kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū vihāraṃ aññataraṃ vihāraṃ (ka.) paṭisaṅkharonte. Disvāna evamāhaṃsu – “ime, āvuso, sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū vihāraṃ paṭisaṅkharonti. Handa ne vuṭṭhāpessāmā”ti. Ekacce [T 2.0125] evamāhaṃsu – “āgamethāvuso, yāva paṭisaṅkharonti, paṭisaṅkhate vuṭṭhāpessāmā”ti. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “uṭṭhethāvuso, amhākaṃ vihāro pāpuṇātī”ti. “Nanu, āvuso, paṭikacceva ācikkhitabbaṃ? Mayañcaññaṃ paṭisaṅkhareyyāmā”ti. “Nanu, āvuso, saṅghiko vihāro”ti? “Āmāvuso, saṅghiko vihāro”ti. “Uṭṭhethāvuso, amhākaṃ vihāro pāpuṇātī”ti. “Mahallako, āvuso, vihāro; tumhepi vasatha, mayampi vasissāmā”ti. “Uṭṭhethāvuso, amhākaṃ vihāro pāpuṇātī”ti kupitā anattamanā gīvāyaṃ gahetvā nikkaḍḍhanti. Te nikkaḍḍhiyamānā rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā [V 0.0296] anattamanā amhe saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhantī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā bhikkhū saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, tumhe bhikkhave, kupitā anattamanā saṅghikā vihārā bhikkhū nikkaḍḍhathā”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, kupitena [T 2.0126][M 0.0317] anattamanena bhikkhu saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhitabbo. Yo nikkaḍḍheyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, senāsanaṃ gāhetu”nti.

At that time the bhikkhus of the group of seventeen were repairing a certain remote great monastery, thinking, ‐We will spend the rains retreat here.‑ The bhikkhus of the group of six saw the bhikkhus of the group of seventeen repairing the monastery. Having seen them, they said: ‐Friends, these bhikkhus of the group of seventeen are repairing the monastery. Come, let us evict them.‑ Some said: ‐Wait, friends, until they finish repairing it; we will evict them when they have finished.‑ Then the bhikkhus of the group of six said to the bhikkhus of the group of seventeen: ‐Get up, friends, the monastery falls to us.‑ ‐But, friends, shouldn't you have told us beforehand? We would have repaired another one.‑ ‐Isn't this monastery owned by the Sangha, friends?‑ ‐Yes, friends, it is owned by the Sangha.‑ ‐Get up, friends, the monastery falls to us.‑ ‐The monastery is large, friends; you stay, and we will stay too.‑ ‐Get up, friends, the monastery falls to us,‑ they said, and being angry and displeased, they grabbed them by the neck and dragged them out. As they were being dragged out, they cried. The bhikkhus asked: ‐Why are you crying, friends?‑ ‐Friends, these bhikkhus of the group of six, angry and displeased, are dragging us out of the Sangha's monastery.‑ Those bhikkhus who were modest… complained, grumbled, and criticized: ‐How could the bhikkhus of the group of six, angry and displeased, drag bhikkhus out of the Sangha's monastery!‑ Then those bhikkhus reported the matter to the Blessed One… ‐Is it true, bhikkhus, that you, angry and displeased, dragged bhikkhus out of the Sangha's monastery?‑ ‐It is true, Blessed One.‑… Having rebuked them… after delivering a Dhamma talk, he addressed the bhikkhus: ‐Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not to be dragged out of a monastery belonging to the Sangha by one who is angry and displeased. Whoever does so should be dealt with according to the rule. Bhikkhus, I permit the assigning of lodgings.‑

Senāsanaggāhāpakasammuti

Appointment of a Lodgings Allocator

317. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – ‘kena nu kho senāsanaṃ gāhetabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ [P 2.0167]…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannituṃ – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, gahitāgahitañca jāneyya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo –

317. Then this thought arose in the bhikkhus: ‘By whom, indeed, should lodgings be allocated?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One... ‘Bhikkhus, I allow a bhikkhu endowed with five factors to be appointed as a lodgings allocator: one who would not go the wrong way through desire, would not go the wrong way through aversion, would not go the wrong way through delusion, and would not go the wrong way through fear, and who would know what has been taken and what has not been taken. And, bhikkhus, he should be appointed thus:

“Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

First, a bhikkhu should be requested. Having requested, a clever and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhu named so-and-so as a lodgings allocator. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno senāsanaggāhāpakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhu named so-and-so as a lodgings allocator. To whichever venerable one the appointment of the bhikkhu named so-and-so as a lodgings allocator is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu senāsanaggāhāpako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti[T 2.0127].

“The bhikkhu named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as a lodgings allocator. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

318. Atha kho senāsanaggāhāpakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho senāsanaṃ gāhetabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ bhikkhū gaṇetuṃ[V 0.0297], bhikkhū gaṇetvā seyyā gaṇetuṃ, seyyā gaṇetvā seyyaggena gāhetu”nti. Seyyaggena gāhentā seyyā ussārayiṃsu…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vihāraggena gāhetu”nti. Vihāraggena gāhentā vihārā ussārayiṃsu…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pariveṇaggena gāhetu”nti. Pariveṇaggena gāhentā pariveṇā ussārayiṃsu…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anubhāgampi dātuṃ. Gahite anubhāge añño bhikkhu āgacchati, na akāmā dātabbo”ti.

318. Then this thought arose in the bhikkhus who were lodgings allocators: ‘How, indeed, should lodgings be allocated?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow you first to count the bhikkhus; having counted the bhikkhus, to count the sleeping places; having counted the sleeping places, to allocate by portion of sleeping places.’ When they allocated by portion of sleeping places, there was a surplus of sleeping places... ‘Bhikkhus, I allow you to allocate by portion of dwellings.’ When they allocated by portion of dwellings, there was a surplus of dwellings... ‘Bhikkhus, I allow you to allocate by portion of compounds.’ When they allocated by portion of compounds, there was a surplus of compounds... ‘Bhikkhus, I also allow a subsequent portion to be given. When a subsequent portion has been taken, if another bhikkhu arrives, it should not be given against one's will.’”

Tena [M 0.0318] kho pana samayena bhikkhū nissīme ṭhitassa senāsanaṃ gāhenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, nissīme ṭhitassa senāsanaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. Yo gāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks assigned lodgings to a monk staying outside the precinct boundary. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, lodgings should not be assigned to a monk staying outside the precinct boundary. Whoever should assign them, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū senāsanaṃ gahetvā sabbakālaṃ paṭibāhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, senāsanaṃ gahetvā sabbakālaṃ paṭibāhetabbaṃ. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassānaṃ temāsaṃ [T 2.0128] paṭibāhituṃ, utukālaṃ pana na paṭibāhitu”nti.

At that time, monks, having taken possession of lodgings, were turning others away at all times. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, having taken possession of lodgings, you should not turn others away at all times. Whoever should turn others away, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to turn others away for the three months of the rains, but not during the other seasons.”

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho senāsanaggāhā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tayo me, bhikkhave, senāsanaggāhā – purimako, pacchimako, antarāmuttako. Aparajjugatāya āsāḷhiyā purimako gāhetabbo. Māsagatāya āsāḷhiyā pacchimako gāhetabbo. Aparajjugatāya pavāraṇāya āyatiṃ vassāvāsatthāya antarāmuttako gāhetabbo. Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo senāsanaggāhā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: “How many kinds of lodging allocations are there?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, there are these three kinds of lodging allocations: the early, the late, and the intermediate. The early allocation is to be made on the day after the Āsāḷhī full moon. The late allocation is to be made one month after the Āsāḷhī full moon. The intermediate allocation is to be made on the day after the Pavāraṇā for the purpose of a future rains-residence. These, monks, are the three kinds of lodging allocations.”

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is finished.

3. Tatiyabhāṇavāro

3. The Third Recitation Section

319. Tena [P 2.0168] kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sāvatthiyaṃ senāsanaṃ gahetvā aññataraṃ gāmakāvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tatthapi senāsanaṃ aggahesi. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhaṇḍanakārako kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Sacāyaṃ idha vassaṃ vasissati, sabbeva mayaṃ na phāsu bhavissāma. Handa naṃ pucchāmā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ [V 0.0298] upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “nanu tayā, āvuso upananda, sāvatthiyaṃ senāsanaṃ gahita”nti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso upananda, eko dve paṭibāhasī”ti? “Idhadānāhaṃ āvuso, muñcāmi; tattha gaṇhāmī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti [T 2.0129] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto [M 0.0319] eko dve paṭibāhessatī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, eko dve paṭibāhasī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, eko dve paṭibāhissasi? Tattha tayā, moghapurisa, gahitaṃ idha muttaṃ, idha tayā gahitaṃ tatra muttaṃ. Evaṃ kho tvaṃ, moghapurisa, ubhayattha paribāhiro. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, ekena dve paṭibāhetabbā. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

319. At that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having taken up a lodging in Sāvatthī, went to a certain village monastery. There too, he took up a lodging. Then this thought occurred to those monks: 'Friends, this Venerable Upananda the Sakyan is quarrelsome, disputatious, contentious, verbose, and a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha. If he spends the rains-residence here, none of us will be at ease. Come, let us question him.' Then those monks said this to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan: 'Friend Upananda, did you not take up a lodging in Sāvatthī?' 'Yes, friends.' 'Why then, friend Upananda, do you, being one person, reserve two lodgings?' 'Friends, I now relinquish the one here and will take the one there.' Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, being one person, reserve two lodgings?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, Upananda, as is said, that you, being one person, reserve two lodgings?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… 'How indeed, foolish man, could you, being one person, reserve two lodgings? Foolish man, when you took the one there, the one here was relinquished; when you took the one here, the one there was relinquished. Thus, foolish man, you are excluded from both. This, foolish man, does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident…' Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, two lodgings should not be reserved by one person. Whoever should reserve them commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

320. pāci. 438 Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ anekapariyāyena vinayakathaṃ katheti, vinayassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, vinayapariyattiyā vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, ādissa ādissa āyasmato upālissa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavā kho anekapariyāyena vinayakathaṃ katheti, vinayassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, vinayapariyattiyā vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, ādissa ādissa āyasmato upālissa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmato upālissa santike vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇāmā”ti. Tedha te ca (syā. ka.) bahū bhikkhū therā ca navā ca majjhimā ca āyasmato upālissa [T 2.0130] santike vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇanti. Āyasmā upāli ṭhitakova uddisati therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ gāravena. Therāpi bhikkhū ṭhitakāva uddisāpenti dhammagāravena. Tattha therā ceva bhikkhū kilamanti, āyasmā ca upāli kilamati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, navakena bhikkhunā [P 2.0169] uddisantena samake vā āsane nisīdituṃ, uccatare vā dhammagāravena; therena bhikkhunā uddisāpentena samake vā āsane nisīdituṃ, nīcatare vā dhammagāravenā”ti.

320. At that time, the Blessed One spoke to the monks in many ways on the Vinaya, spoke of the virtue of the Vinaya, spoke of the virtue of learning the Vinaya, and specifically mentioning, spoke of the virtue of the Venerable Upāli. This thought occurred to the monks: 'The Blessed One speaks on the Vinaya in many ways, speaks of the virtue of the Vinaya, speaks of the virtue of learning the Vinaya, and specifically mentioning, speaks of the virtue of the Venerable Upāli. Come now, friends, let us learn the Vinaya in the presence of the Venerable Upāli.' Then many monks—elders, newly ordained, and those of middle standing—learned the Vinaya in the presence of the Venerable Upāli. The Venerable Upāli, out of respect for the elder monks, taught while standing. The elder monks, too, out of respect for the Dhamma, had him teach while they were standing. Thereby, both the elder monks and the Venerable Upāli became fatigued. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a junior monk who is teaching to sit on a seat of equal height, or, out of respect for the Dhamma, on a higher one; and an elder monk who is being taught to sit on a seat of equal height, or, out of respect for the Dhamma, on a lower one.'

Tena kho pana samayena bahū bhikkhū āyasmato upālissa santike ṭhitakā uddesaṃ paṭimānentā kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, samānāsanikehi saha nisīditu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kittāvatā nu kho samānāsaniko hotī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tivassantarena saha nisīditu”nti.

At that time, many monks, standing in the presence of the Venerable Upāli while awaiting the recitation, became fatigued. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to sit together with those entitled to an equal seat.' Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'By what measure, indeed, is one entitled to an equal seat?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to sit together with those within three years of seniority.'

Tena [M 0.0320][V 0.0299] kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū samānāsanikā mañce ekamañce (syā.) nisīditvā mañcaṃ bhindiṃsu, pīṭhe ekapīṭhe (syā.) nisīditvā pīṭhaṃ bhindiṃsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tivaggassa [T 2.0131] mañcaṃ, tivaggassa pīṭha”nti. Tivaggopi mañce nisīditvā mañcaṃ bhindi, pīṭhe nisīditvā pīṭhaṃ bhindi…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, duvaggassa mañcaṃ, duvaggassa pīṭha”nti.

At that time, many monks of equal seating sat on a couch and broke the couch; they sat on a stool and broke the stool. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a couch for a group of three and a stool for a group of three.' Even a group of three, having sat on a couch, broke the couch; having sat on a stool, they broke the stool... 'Monks, I allow a couch for a group of two and a stool for a group of two.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū asamānāsanikehi saha dīghāsane nisīdituṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā paṇḍakaṃ, mātugāmaṃ, ubhatobyañjanakaṃ, asamānāsanikehi saha dīghāsane nisīditu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kittakaṃ pacchimaṃ nu kho dīghāsanaṃ hotī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pahoti, ettakaṃ pacchimaṃ dīghāsana”nti.

At that time, monks were scrupulous about sitting on a long seat together with those with whom it is not permissible to share a seat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, setting aside a paṇḍaka, a woman, and a person of both sexes, I allow you to sit on a long seat together with those with whom it is not permissible to share a seat.' Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'What, indeed, is the minimum for a long seat?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow as the minimum for a long seat that which is sufficient for three.'

Tena kho pana samayena visākhā migāramātā saṅghassa atthāya sāḷindaṃ pāsādaṃ kārāpetukāmā hoti hatthinakhakaṃ. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā pāsādaparibhogo anuññāto kiṃ ananuññāto”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ pāsādaparibhoga”nti.

At that time, Visākhā Migāramātā wished to have a mansion with a portico of the 'elephant-faced' type built for the benefit of the Saṅgha. Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'Has the use of a mansion been allowed by the Blessed One, or has it not been allowed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow every use of a mansion.'

Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa ayyikā kālaṅkatā hoti. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya saṅghassa bahuṃ akappiyabhaṇḍaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, seyyathidaṃ – āsandi, pallaṅko, gonako[T 2.0132], cittako, paṭikā, paṭalikā, tūlikā, vikatikā, uddalomī, ekantalomī, kaṭṭissaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kuttakaṃ, hatthattharaṃ, assattharaṃ, rathattharaṃ, ajinappaveṇi, kadalimigappavarapaccattharaṇaṃ, sauttaracchadaṃ, ubhatolohitakūpadhānaṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āsandiyā pāde chinditvā [P 2.0170] paribhuñjituṃ, pallaṅkassa vāḷe bhinditvā paribhuñjituṃ, tūlikaṃ vijaṭetvā bibbohanaṃ kātuṃ, avasesaṃ bhūmattharaṇaṃ summattharaṇaṃ (sī. syā.) kātu”nti.

At that time, the grandmother of King Pasenadi of Kosala had passed away. On the occasion of her death, much unsuitable property had arisen for the Saṅgha, namely: a long-legged chair, a couch with animal figures on its feet, a large rug with long fleece, a woolen coverlet with intricate stitching, a white woolen coverlet, a woolen coverlet with a thick floral design, a cotton-filled mattress, a woolen coverlet with figures of lions and tigers, a woolen coverlet with fleece on both sides, a woolen coverlet with fleece on one side, a silk coverlet embroidered with gems and gold thread, a silk spread interwoven with gold thread, a woolen rug large enough for sixteen dancing girls, an elephant saddle-blanket, a horse saddle-blanket, a chariot-rug, a spread made by sewing together pieces of black antelope skin, a choice coverlet made from the hide of the kadali deer, a couch with a red canopy above, and a couch with red pillows at both ends. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to use the long-legged chair after cutting off its legs, to use the couch after breaking off its animal figures, to make a pillow after unravelling the cotton-filled mattress, and to make the remaining coverlets into floor-coverings.'

Avissajjiyavatthu

The Section on Things Not to Be Relinquished

321. Tena [M 0.0321] kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā avidūre aññatarasmiṃ gāmakāvāse āvāsikā bhikkhū upaddutā honti āgantukagamikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapentā. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “etarahi kho mayaṃ, āvuso, upaddutā āgantukagamikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapentā. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ ekassa dema. Tassa [V 0.0300] santakaṃ paribhuñjissāmā”ti. Te sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ ekassa adaṃsu. Āgantukā bhikkhū te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “amhākaṃ, āvuso, senāsanaṃ paññāpethā”ti. “Natthāvuso, saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ; sabbaṃ amhehi ekassa dinna”nti. “Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ vissajjethā”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ vissajjessantī”ti vissajjissantīti (ka.)! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ [T 2.0133] ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ vissajjentī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ vissajjessanti? Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

321. At that time, in a certain small village monastery near Sāvatthī, the resident monks were troubled by having to prepare lodgings for visiting and traveling monks. Then those monks thought: 'Friends, we are now troubled by having to prepare lodgings for visiting and traveling monks. Come, friends, let us give all the communal lodgings to one monk. We will use what belongs to him.' They gave all the communal lodgings to one monk. Visiting monks said to those monks: 'Friends, prepare lodgings for us.' 'There are no communal lodgings, friends; we have given them all to one monk.' 'But friends, did you relinquish the communal lodgings?' 'Yes, friends.' Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, condemned, and complained: 'How can these monks relinquish communal lodgings?' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, monks, that monks are relinquishing communal lodgings?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How can these foolish men relinquish communal lodgings? This will not inspire confidence in those without it…' Having rebuked them… he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks:

“Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, avissajjiyāni, na vissajjetabbāni na vissajjitabbāni (ka.), saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vissajjitānipi avissajjitāni honti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa. Katamāni pañca? Ārāmo, ārāmavatthu – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ avissajjiyaṃ, na vissajjetabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vissajjitampi avissajjitaṃ hoti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

“Monks, there are these five things that are not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if relinquished, they remain un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes them, commits a thullaccaya offense. What are the five? A park and the park grounds—this is the first thing that is not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if relinquished, it remains un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes it, commits a thullaccaya offense.

“Vihāro, vihāravatthu – idaṃ dutiyaṃ avissajjiyaṃ, na vissajjetabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggallena vā. Vissajjitampi avissajjitaṃ hoti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

A monastery and a monastery site—this is the second thing that is not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if relinquished, it remains un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes it, commits a thullaccaya offense.

“Mañco, pīṭhaṃ, bhisi, bibbohanaṃ – idaṃ tatiyaṃ avissajjiyaṃ, na vissajjetabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vissajjitampi avissajjitaṃ hoti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

A couch, a chair, a mattress, and a pillow—this is the third thing that is not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if relinquished, it remains un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes it, commits a thullaccaya offense.

“Lohakumbhī[M 0.0322], lohabhāṇakaṃ, lohavārako, lohakaṭāhaṃ, vāsi, parasu pharasu (sī. syā. ka.), kuṭhārī kudhārī (ka.), kudālo, nikhādanaṃ – idaṃ catutthaṃ avissajjiyaṃ, na vissajjetabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vissajjitampi avissajjitaṃ hoti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

A copper pot, a large copper vessel, a copper bucket, a copper cauldron, an adze, an axe, a hatchet, a spade, and a chisel—this is the fourth thing that is not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if relinquished, it remains un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes it, commits a thullaccaya offense.

“Valli, veḷu, muñjaṃ, pabbajaṃ [T 2.0134] babbajaṃ (sī.), tiṇaṃ, mattikā, dārubhaṇḍaṃ, mattikābhaṇḍaṃ – idaṃ pañcamaṃ [V 0.0301] avissajjiyaṃ, na vissajjetabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vissajjitampi avissajjitaṃ hoti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca avissajjiyāni, na vissajjetabbāni, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vissajjitānipi avissajjitāni honti. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

Creepers, bamboo, muñja grass, pabbaja grass, grass, clay, wooden articles, and clay articles—this is the fifth thing that is not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if relinquished, it remains un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes it, commits a thullaccaya offense. Monks, these are the five things that are not to be relinquished, not to be given away, whether by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. Even if they are relinquished, they remain un-relinquished. Whoever relinquishes them, commits a thullaccaya offense.”

Avebhaṅgiyavatthu

The Section on Indivisible Things

322. Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā [P 2.0171] yena kīṭāgiri tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sāriputtamoggallānehi ca. Assosuṃ kho assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū – “bhagavā kira kīṭāgiriṃ āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sāriputtamoggallānehi ca”. “Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ bhājema. Pāpicchā sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā; na mayaṃ tesaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapessāmā”ti, te sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ bhājesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena kīṭāgiri tadavasari. Atha kho bhagavā sambahule bhikkhū āmantesi – “gacchatha tumhe, bhikkhave; assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadetha – ‘bhagavā, āvuso, āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sāriputtamoggallānehi ca. Bhagavato ca, āvuso, senāsanaṃ paññapetha, bhikkhusaṅghassa ca, sāriputtamoggallānānañcā’”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā yena assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “bhagavā, āvuso, āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sāriputtamoggallānehi ca[T 2.0135]. Bhagavato ca, āvuso, senāsanaṃ [M 0.0323] paññapetha, bhikkhusaṅghassa ca, sāriputtamoggallānānañcā”ti. “Natthāvuso, saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ. Sabbaṃ amhehi bhājitaṃ. Svāgataṃ, āvuso, bhagavato. Yasmiṃ vihāre bhagavā icchissati tasmiṃ vihāre vasissati. Pāpicchā sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā. Na mayaṃ tesaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapessāmā”ti. “Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ bhājitthā”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ bhājessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma [V 0.0302] te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ bhājessanti? Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

322. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Sāvatthī for as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Kīṭāgiri together with a great Saṅgha of about five hundred bhikkhus, and with Sāriputta and Moggallāna. The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, is coming to Kīṭāgiri together with a great Saṅgha of about five hundred bhikkhus, and with Sāriputta and Moggallāna.” They said: “Come now, friends, let us divide all the lodgings belonging to the Saṅgha. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of evil wishes, they have fallen under the power of evil wishes; we will not prepare lodgings for them.” So they divided all the lodgings belonging to the Saṅgha. Then the Blessed One, journeying by stages, arrived at Kīṭāgiri. There the Blessed One addressed a number of bhikkhus: “Go, bhikkhus; approach the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu and say this: ‘Friends, the Blessed One is coming together with a great Saṅgha of about five hundred bhikkhus, and with Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Prepare lodgings, friends, for the Blessed One, for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, and for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.’” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. They approached the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu and said this to them: “Friends, the Blessed One is coming together with a great Saṅgha of about five hundred bhikkhus, and with Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Prepare lodgings, friends, for the Blessed One, for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, and for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.” They replied: “There are no lodgings belonging to the Saṅgha, friends. We have divided them all. Welcome to the Blessed One, friends. The Blessed One may dwell in whichever dwelling he wishes. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of evil wishes, they have fallen under the power of evil wishes; we will not prepare lodgings for them.” “But friends, have you divided the lodgings belonging to the Saṅgha?” “Yes, friends.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... murmured, complained, and criticized: “How indeed could the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu divide the lodgings belonging to the Saṅgha?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One... “Is it true, bhikkhus...?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, bhikkhus, could those foolish men divide the lodgings belonging to the Saṅgha? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:

“Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, avebhaṅgiyāni avebhaṅgikāni (ka.), na vibhajitabbāni, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena [T 2.0136] vā. Vibhattānipi avibhattāni honti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa. Katamāni pañca? Ārāmo, ārāmavatthu – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ, na vibhajitabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vibhattampi avibhattaṃ hoti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

“Bhikkhus, there are these five indivisible things, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, they are considered undivided. Whoever should divide them incurs an offense of grave misconduct. What are the five? A park, the site of a park—this is the first indivisible thing, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, it is considered undivided. Whoever should divide it incurs an offense of grave misconduct.

“Vihāro, vihāravatthu – idaṃ dutiyaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ, na vibhajitabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vibhattampi avibhattaṃ hoti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

“A dwelling, the site of a dwelling—this is the second indivisible thing, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, it is considered undivided. Whoever should divide it incurs an offense of grave misconduct.

“Mañco, pīṭhaṃ, bhisi, bibbohanaṃ – idaṃ tatiyaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ, na vibhajitabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vibhattampi avibhattaṃ hoti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

“A couch, a chair, a mattress, a pillow—this is the third indivisible thing, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, it is considered undivided. Whoever should divide it incurs an offense of grave misconduct.

“Lohakumbhī, lohabhāṇakaṃ, lohavārako, lohakaṭāhaṃ, vāsī, parasu, kuṭhārī, kudālo, nikhādanaṃ – idaṃ catutthaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ, na vibhajitabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vibhattampi avibhattaṃ hoti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa.

“A metal pot, a metal basin, a metal bucket, a metal cauldron, an adze, an axe, a hatchet, a spade, a chisel—this is the fourth indivisible thing, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, it is considered undivided. Whoever should divide it incurs an offense of grave misconduct.

“Vallī, veḷu, muñjaṃ, pabbajaṃ, tiṇaṃ, mattikā, dārubhaṇḍaṃ, mattikābhaṇḍaṃ – idaṃ pañcamaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ, na vibhajitabbaṃ, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vibhattampi [M 0.0324] avibhattaṃ hoti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca avebhaṅgiyāni, na vibhajitabbāni, saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā. Vibhattānipi avibhattāni honti. Yo vibhajeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

“Creepers, bamboo, muñja grass, pabbaja grass, grass, clay, wooden articles, earthenware—this is the fifth indivisible thing, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, it is considered undivided. Whoever should divide it incurs an offense of grave misconduct. These then, Bhikkhus, are the five indivisible things, not to be divided by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if divided, they are considered undivided. Whoever should divide them incurs an offense of grave misconduct.”

Navakammadānakathā

The Discourse on Assigning New Work

323. Atha [T 2.0137][P 2.0172] kho bhagavā kīṭāgirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena āḷavī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena āḷavī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye. Tena kho pana samayena āḷavakā āḷavikā (syā. ka.) bhikkhū evarūpāni navakammāni [V 0.0303] denti – piṇḍanikkhepanamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; kuṭṭalepanamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; dvāraṭṭhapanamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; aggaḷavaṭṭikaraṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; ālokasandhikaraṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; setavaṇṇakaraṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; kāḷavaṇṇakaraṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; gerukaparikammakaraṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; chādanamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; bandhanamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; bhaṇḍikāṭṭhapanamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; khaṇḍaphullapaṭisaṅkharaṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; paribhaṇḍakaraṇamattenapi navakammaṃ denti; vīsativassikampi navakammaṃ denti; tiṃsavassikampi navakammaṃ denti; yāvajīvikampi navakammaṃ denti; dhūmakālikampi pariyositaṃ vihāraṃ navakammaṃ denti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āḷavakā bhikkhū evarūpāni navakammāni dassanti – piṇḍanikkhepanamattenapi navakammaṃ dassanti; kuṭṭalepanamattenapi… dvāraṭṭhapanamattenapi [T 2.0138]… aggaḷavaṭṭikaraṇamattenapi… ālokasandhikaraṇamattenapi… setavaṇṇakaraṇamattenapi… kāḷavaṇṇakaraṇamattenapi… gerukaparikammakaraṇamattenapi… chādenamattenapi… bandhanamattenapi… bhaṇḍikāḷapanamattenapi… khaṇḍaphullapaṭisaṅkharaṇamattenapi… paribhaṇḍakaraṇamattenapi… visativassikampi… tiṃsavassikampi… yāvajīvikampi… dhūmakālikampi pariyositaṃ vihāraṃ navakammaṃ dassantī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… “saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, piṇḍanikkhepanamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ; na kuṭṭalepanamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na [M 0.0325] dvāraṭṭhapanamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na aggaḷavaṭṭikaraṇamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na ālokasandhikaraṇamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na setavaṇṇakaraṇamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na kāḷavaṇṇakaraṇamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na gerukaparikammakaraṇamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na chādenamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na bandhanamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na bhaṇḍikāḷapanamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na khaṇḍaphullapaṭisaṅkharaṇamattena navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na paribhaṇḍakaraṇamattena [T 2.0139] navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na visativassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na tiṃsavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na yāvajīvikaṃ navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na dhūmakālikampi pariyositaṃ vihāraṃ navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, akataṃ vā vippakataṃ vā navakammaṃ dātuṃ, khuddake vihāre kammaṃ oloketvā chappañcavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātuṃ, aḍḍhayoge kammaṃ oloketvā sattaṭṭhavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātuṃ, mahallake vihāre pāsāde vā kammaṃ oloketvā dasadvādasavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātu”nti.

323. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Kīṭāgiri as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Āḷavī. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Āḷavī. There the Blessed One stayed at the Aggāḷava Shrine in Āḷavī. At that time, the monks of Āḷavī were assigning new work for such reasons as these: they would assign new work for merely placing a lump of plaster or clay; for merely plastering a wall; for merely setting up a door; for merely making a bolt-post; for merely making a window opening; for merely applying a white color; for merely applying a black color; for merely finishing with red ochre; for merely roofing; for merely binding; for merely setting up a rack; for merely repairing what is broken and decaying; for merely applying a protective coating. They would assign new work for twenty years, for thirty years, and for a lifetime. They would assign new work to a completed dwelling for as long as the smoke rises. Those monks who were of few wants… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the monks of Āḷavī assign new work for such reasons as these? They assign new work for merely placing a lump of plaster or clay; for merely plastering a wall; for merely setting up a door; for merely making a bolt-post; for merely making a window opening; for merely applying a white color; for merely applying a black color; for merely finishing with red ochre; for merely roofing; for merely binding; for merely setting up a rack; for merely repairing what is broken and decaying; for merely applying a protective coating. They assign new work for twenty years, for thirty years, for a lifetime, and they assign new work to a completed dwelling for as long as the smoke rises!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks…?” “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, new work is not to be assigned for merely placing a lump of plaster or clay; not for merely plastering a wall; not for merely setting up a door; not for merely making a bolt-post; not for merely making a window opening; not for merely applying a white color; not for merely applying a black color; not for merely finishing with red ochre; not for merely roofing; not for merely binding; not for merely setting up a rack; not for merely repairing what is broken and decaying; not for merely applying a protective coating. New work is not to be assigned for twenty years; not for thirty years; not for a lifetime. New work is not to be assigned to a completed dwelling for as long as the smoke rises. Whoever should assign it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, that new work be assigned for what is unbuilt or unfinished. For a small dwelling, after inspecting the work, I allow new work to be assigned for five or six years. For a lean-to dwelling, after inspecting the work, I allow new work to be assigned for seven or eight years. For a large dwelling or a multi-storied building, after inspecting the work, I allow new work to be assigned for ten or twelve years.”

Tena [V 0.0304] kho pana samayena bhikkhū sabbe vihāre navakammaṃ denti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, sabbe vihāre navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks were assigning new work for all the dwellings. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, new work should not be assigned for all the dwellings. Whoever should assign it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ekassa dve denti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ekassa dve dātabbā. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks were assigning two dwellings to one monk. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, two dwellings should not be assigned to one. Whoever should assign them, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṃ gahetvā aññaṃ vāsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, navakammaṃ [P 2.0173] gahetvā añño vāsetabbo. Yo vāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks, having undertaken new work, were causing another monk to reside there. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, having undertaken new work, another should not be caused to reside there. Whoever should cause another to reside there, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṃ gahetvā saṅghikaṃ [T 2.0140] paṭibāhenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, navakammaṃ gahetvā saṅghikaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṃ varaseyyaṃ gahetu”nti.

At that time, the monks, having undertaken new work, were obstructing a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, having undertaken new work, a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha should not be obstructed. Whoever should obstruct it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to take one excellent lodging.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū nissīme ṭhitassa navakammaṃ denti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, nissīme ṭhitassa navakammaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the monks were assigning new work to a monk standing outside the boundary. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, new work should not be assigned to one standing outside the boundary. Whoever should assign it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena [M 0.0326] kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṃ gahetvā sabbakālaṃ paṭibāhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, navakammaṃ gahetvā sabbakālaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassānaṃ temāsaṃ paṭibāhituṃ, utukālaṃ pana na paṭibāhitu”nti.

At that time, monks who had undertaken new work were refusing entry at all times. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, having undertaken new work, entry should not be refused at all times. Whoever should refuse entry commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to refuse entry for the three months of the rainy season, but I do not allow it during the other seasons.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṃ gahetvā pakkamantipi, vibbhamantipi, kālampi karonti; sāmaṇerāpi paṭijānanti; sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakāpi paṭijānanti; antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakāpi paṭijānanti; ummattakāpi paṭijānanti; khittacittāpi paṭijānanti; vedanāṭṭāpi paṭijānanti; āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakāpi paṭijānanti; āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakāpi paṭijānanti; pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakāpi paṭijānanti; paṇḍakāpi paṭijānanti; theyyasaṃvāsakāpi paṭijānanti; titthiyapakkantakāpi [V 0.0305]

Now at that time, monks, having undertaken new work, would also depart, also disrobe, or also die. They would also claim to be novices; they would also claim to be those who have renounced the training; they would also claim to be those who have committed an ultimate offense; they would also claim to be insane; they would also claim to have distracted minds; they would also claim to be afflicted by pain; they would also claim to be suspended for not seeing an offense; they would also claim to be suspended for not making amends for an offense; they would also claim to be suspended for not relinquishing a wicked view; they would also claim to be pandakas; they would also claim to be those in communion by theft; they would also claim to be those who have gone over to another sect.

Paṭijānanti; tiracchānagatāpi paṭijānanti; mātughātakāpi paṭijānanti; pitughātakāpi paṭijānanti[T 2.0141]; arahantaghātakāpi paṭijānanti; bhikkhunidūsakāpi paṭijānanti; saṅghabhedakāpi paṭijānanti; lohituppādakāpi paṭijānanti; ubhatobyañjanakāpi paṭijānanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

They would also claim to be animals; they would also claim to be matricides; they would also claim to be patricides; they would also claim to be killers of Arahants; they would also claim to be violators of bhikkhunis; they would also claim to be schismatics; they would also claim to be those who have shed the Buddha's blood; they would also claim to be ubhatobyanjanakas. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu navakammaṃ gahetvā pakkamati – mā saṅghassa hāyīti aññassa dātabbaṃ.

“Here, monks, if a monk undertakes new work and then departs—thinking, ‘Lest the Sangha suffer loss’—it should be given to another.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu navakammaṃ gahetvā vibbhamati…pe… kālaṅkaroti, sāmaṇero paṭijānāti, sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti, antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti, ummattako paṭijānāti, khittacitto paṭijānāti, vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti, āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti, paṇḍako paṭijānāti, theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti, titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti, tiracchānagato paṭijānāti, mātughātako paṭijānāti, pitughātako paṭijānāti, arahantaghātako paṭijānāti, bhikkhunīdūsako paṭijānāti, saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti, lohituppādako paṭijānāti, ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti – mā saṅghassa hāyīti aññassa dātabbaṃ.

“Here, monks, if a monk, having undertaken new work, disrobes… or dies, or declares himself a novice… or declares himself an ubhatobyañjanaka—thinking, ‘Lest the Sangha suffer loss’—it should be given to another.

“Idha [M 0.0327] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu navakammaṃ gahetvā vippakate pakkamati – mā saṅghassa hāyīti aññassa dātabbaṃ.

“Here, monks, if a monk, having undertaken new work, departs while it is unfinished—thinking, ‘Lest the Sangha suffer loss’—it should be given to another.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu navakammaṃ gahetvā vippakate vibbhamati…pe… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti – mā saṅghassa hāyīti [T 2.0142] aññassa dātabbaṃ.

“Here, monks, if a monk, having undertaken new work, disrobes while it is unfinished… or declares himself an ubhatobyañjanaka—thinking, ‘Lest the Sangha suffer loss’—it should be given to another.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu navakammaṃ gahetvā pariyosite pakkamati – tassevetaṃ.

“Here, monks, if a monk, having undertaken new work, departs when it is finished—it belongs to that very monk.
