I will lead the community of bhikkhus.’ ‘Devadatta, I would not hand over the community of bhikkhus even to Sāriputta and Moggallāna, so how could I hand it over to you, a vile spittle-swallower!’ Then Devadatta, thinking, ‘In this assembly that includes the king, the Blessed One disparages me by calling me a spittle-swallower, while he extols only Sāriputta and Moggallāna,’ became angry and displeased. Having paid homage to the Blessed One and circumambulating him, he departed. This was the first animosity of Devadatta toward the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho devadattassa rājagahe pakāsanīyaṃ kammaṃ karotu – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Well then, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha perform the act of proclamation concerning Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, on account of that the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha should not be regarded; on account of that, only Devadatta should be regarded.’ And this, bhikkhus, is how it should be done. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

337. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho devadattassa rājagahe pakāsanīyaṃ kammaṃ kareyya – “pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena [M 0.0348] vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Esā ñatti.

337. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the act of proclamation concerning Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, on account of that the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha should not be regarded; on account of that, only Devadatta should be regarded.’ This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho devadattassa rājagahe [T 2.0174] pakāsanīyaṃ kammaṃ karoti – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Yassāyasmato khamati devadattassa rājagahe pakāsanīyaṃ kammassa karaṇaṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati, yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti – so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha performs the act of proclamation concerning Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, on account of that the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha should not be regarded; on account of that, only Devadatta should be regarded.’ To whichever venerable one the performance of the act of proclamation concerning Devadatta in Rājagaha is agreeable—‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, on account of that the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha should not be regarded; on account of that, only Devadatta should be regarded’—he should remain silent. He to whom it is not agreeable should speak.

“Kataṃ saṅghena devadattassa rājagahe pakāsanīyaṃ kammaṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The Sangha has performed the act of proclamation concerning Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‐Previously, Devadatta's nature was one thing; now his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby.‑ This is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.‑

338. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “tena hi tvaṃ, sāriputta, devadattaṃ [V 0.0327] rājagahe pakāsehī”ti. “Pubbe mayā, bhante, devadattassa rājagahe vaṇṇo bhāsito – ‘mahiddhiko godhiputto, mahānubhāvo godhiputto’ti. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsemī”ti? “Nanu tayā, sāriputta, bhūtoyeva devadattassa rājagahe vaṇṇo bhāsito – ‘mahiddhiko godhiputto, mahānubhāvo godhiputto’” ti? “Evaṃ [T 2.0175] bhante”ti. “Evameva kho tvaṃ, sāriputta, bhūtaṃyeva devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsehī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato paccassosi.

338. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “In that case, Sāriputta, you are to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha.” “Venerable sir, I have previously spoken in praise of Devadatta in Rājagaha, saying: ‘Godhiputta is of great psychic power, Godhiputta is of great might.’ How, venerable sir, am I to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha?” “Sāriputta, was it not indeed the truth that you spoke in praise of Devadatta in Rājagaha, saying: ‘Godhiputta is of great psychic power, Godhiputta is of great might’?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “In that very same way, Sāriputta, you are to proclaim what is true about Devadatta in Rājagaha.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Sāriputta replied in assent to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho sāriputtaṃ sammannatu devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsetuṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ sāriputto [M 0.0349] yācitabbo. Yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Sangha appoint Sāriputta to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby.’ And, bhikkhus, the appointment is to be made in this way. First, Sāriputta is to be requested. After he has been requested, the Sangha is to be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ sammanneyya [P 2.0190] devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsetuṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should authorize the Venerable Sāriputta to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby.’ This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ sammannati devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsetuṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati, yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Yassāyasmato khamati, āyasmato sāriputtassa sammuti [T 2.0176] devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsetuṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati, yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti – so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha authorizes the Venerable Sāriputta to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby.’ Whoever of the venerable ones approves of the authorization of the Venerable Sāriputta to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha—‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby’—should remain silent. Whoever does not approve should speak.

“Sammato saṅghena āyasmā sāriputto devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsetuṃ – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo’ti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The Venerable Sāriputta has been authorized by the Sangha to proclaim Devadatta in Rājagaha: ‘Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby.’ This is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.”

Sammato [V 0.0328] ca āyasmā sāriputto sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ rājagahaṃ pavisitvā devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsesi – “pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo”ti. Tattha ye te manussā assaddhā appasannā dubbuddhino, te evamāhaṃsu – “usūyakā ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā devadattassa lābhasakkāraṃ usūyantī”ti. Ye pana te manussā saddhā pasannā paṇḍitā byattā buddhimanto, te evamāhaṃsu – “na kho idaṃ orakaṃ bhavissati yathā bhagavā devadattaṃ rājagahe pakāsāpetī”ti.

Venerable Sāriputta, having been authorized, entered Rājagaha together with many bhikkhus and proclaimed Devadatta in Rājagaha: “Previously, Devadatta’s nature was one thing; now, his nature is another. Whatever Devadatta may do by body or speech, neither the Buddha, the Dhamma, nor the Sangha is to be regarded thereby; only Devadatta is to be regarded thereby.” There, those people who were without faith, without confidence, and without wisdom said: “These ascetics, sons of the Sakyans, are envious; they envy Devadatta’s gain and honor.” But those people who had faith, were confident, wise, and intelligent said: “This will surely not be an insignificant matter, since the Blessed One has caused a proclamation to be made concerning Devadatta in Rājagaha.”

Ajātasattukumāravatthu

The Story of Prince Ajātasattu

339. Atha [T 2.0177][M 0.0350] kho devadatto yena ajātasattu kumāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā ajātasattuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “pubbe kho, kumāra, manussā dīghāyukā, etarahi appāyukā. Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ tvaṃ kumārova samāno kālaṃ kareyyāsi. Tena hi tvaṃ, kumāra, pitaraṃ hantvā rājā hohi. Ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ hantvā buddho bhavissāmī”ti.

339. Then Devadatta approached Prince Ajātasattu and said to him: “Prince, indeed, in the past people were long-lived, but now they are short-lived. It is possible that you, while still a prince, might die. Therefore, prince, kill your father and become king. I will kill the Blessed One and become a Buddha.”

Atha kho ajātasattu kumāro – ayyo kho devadatto mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo, jāneyyāsi ayyo devadattoti – ūruyā potthanikaṃ bandhitvā divā divassa divā divasassa (ka.) bhīto ubbiggo ussaṅkī utrasto sahasā antepuraṃ pāvisi. Addasāsuṃ kho antepure upacārakā mahāmattā ajātasattuṃ kumāraṃ divā divassa bhītaṃ ubbiggaṃ ussaṅkiṃ utrastaṃ sahasā antepuraṃ pavisantaṃ; disvāna aggahesuṃ. Te vicinantā ūruyā potthanikaṃ baddhaṃ bandhaṃ (ka.) disvāna ajātasattuṃ kumāraṃ etadavocuṃ – “kiṃ tvaṃ, kumāra, kattukāmosī”ti? “Pitaramhi hantukāmo”ti. “Kenāsi ussāhito”ti? “Ayyena devadattenā”ti. Ekacce mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – “kumāro ca hantabbo, devadatto ca, sabbe ca bhikkhū hantabbā”ti. Ekacce mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – “na bhikkhū hantabbā. Na bhikkhū kiñci aparajjhanti. Kumāro ca hantabbo, devadatto cā”ti. Ekacce mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – “na kumāro ca hantabbo, na devadatto. Na bhikkhū [T 2.0178] hantabbā. Rañño ārocetabbaṃ. Yathā rājā vakkhati tathā karissāmā”ti.

Then Prince Ajātasattu—thinking, 'Indeed, the venerable Devadatta is of great psychic power and great majesty; the venerable Devadatta would know'—tied a butcher's knife to his thigh and, in the middle of the day, being afraid, alarmed, apprehensive, and trembling with fear, hastily entered the inner palace. The attendant high officials in the inner palace saw Prince Ajātasattu hastily entering the inner palace in the middle of the day, being afraid, alarmed, apprehensive, and trembling with fear. Having seen him, they seized him. While searching, they saw the butcher's knife tied to his thigh and said to Prince Ajātasattu, 'What do you intend to do, prince?' 'I wish to kill my father,' he replied. 'By whom were you incited?' 'By the venerable Devadatta,' he said. Some high officials were of this opinion: 'The prince should be killed, Devadatta should be killed, and all the monks should be killed.' Some high officials were of this opinion: 'The monks should not be killed. The monks have done no wrong. The prince should be killed, and Devadatta too.' Some high officials were of this opinion: 'Neither the prince nor Devadatta should be killed. The monks should not be killed. The king should be informed. We will act as the king directs.'

Atha kho te mahāmattā ajātasattuṃ kumāraṃ ādāya yena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[P 2.0191], upasaṅkamitvā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0329]. “Kathaṃ, bhaṇe, mahāmattehi mati katā”ti? “Ekacce, deva, mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – ‘kumāro ca hantabbo, devadatto ca, sabbe ca bhikkhū hantabbā’ti. Ekacce mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – ‘na bhikkhū hantabbā. Na bhikkhū kiñci aparajjhanti. Kumāro ca hantabbo, devadatto cā’ti. Ekacce mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – ‘na kumāro ca hantabbo, na devadatto. Na bhikkhū hantabbā. Rañño [M 0.0351] ārocetabbaṃ. Yathā rājā vakkhati tathā karissāmā’”ti. “Kiṃ, bhaṇe, karissati buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā? Nanu bhagavatā paṭikacceva devadatto rājagahe pakāsāpito – ‘pubbe devadattassa aññā pakati ahosi, idāni aññā pakati. Yaṃ devadatto kareyya kāyena vācāya, na tena buddho vā dhammo vā saṅgho vā daṭṭhabbo, devadattova tena daṭṭhabbo”ti? Tattha ye te mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – ‘kumāro ca hantabbo devadatto ca; sabbe ca bhikkhū hantabbā’ti; te aṭṭhāne akāsi. Ye te mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – ‘na bhikkhū hantabbā; na bhikkhū kiñci aparajjhanti; kumāro ca hantabbo devadatto cā’ti; te nīce ṭhāne ṭhapesi. Ye [T 2.0179] te mahāmattā evaṃ matiṃ akaṃsu – ‘na kumāro ca hantabbo, na devadatto; na bhikkhū hantabbā; rañño ārocetabbaṃ; yathā rājā vakkhati tathā karissāmā’ti; te ucce ṭhāne ṭhapesi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro ajātasattuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “kissa maṃ tvaṃ, kumāra, hantukāmosī”ti? “Rajjenāmhi, deva, atthiko”ti. “Sace kho tvaṃ, kumāra, rajjena atthiko, etaṃ te rajja”nti ajātasattussa kumārassa rajjaṃ niyyādesi.

Then those high officials took Prince Ajātasattu and approached King Bimbisāra of Magadha. Having approached, they informed King Bimbisāra of Magadha of this matter. 'How, sirs, have the high officials decided?' 'Sire, some high officials formed this opinion: “The prince should be killed, Devadatta too, and all the monks should be killed.” Some high officials formed this opinion: “The monks should not be killed. The monks have done no wrong. The prince should be killed, and Devadatta too.” Some high officials formed this opinion: “The prince should not be killed, nor Devadatta. The monks should not be killed. The king should be informed. We will act as the king says.”' 'What, sirs, will the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Sangha do? Has not the Blessed One already declared in Rājagaha concerning Devadatta: “Formerly, Devadatta's nature was different; now his nature is different. For whatever Devadatta might do by body or speech, the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Sangha should not be regarded on account of it; only Devadatta should be regarded on account of it”?' Thereupon, those high officials who had formed the opinion, ‘The prince should be killed, Devadatta too; and all the monks should be killed,’ he dismissed from their posts. Those high officials who had formed the opinion, ‘The monks should not be killed; the monks have done no wrong; the prince should be killed, and Devadatta too,’ he placed in lower positions. Those high officials who had formed the opinion, ‘The prince should not be killed, nor Devadatta; the monks should not be killed; the king should be informed; we will act as the king says,’ he placed in higher positions. Then King Bimbisāra of Magadha said to Prince Ajātasattu, 'Why, prince, do you wish to kill me?' 'Sire, I desire the kingdom.' 'If you, prince, desire the kingdom, this kingdom is yours.' And he handed over the kingdom to Prince Ajātasattu.

Abhimārapesanaṃ

The Sending of Men to Kill

340. Atha kho devadatto yena ajātasattu kumāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā ajātasattuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “purise, mahārāja, āṇāpehi, ye samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ jīvitā voropessantī”ti. Atha kho ajātasattu kumāro manusse āṇāpesi – “yathā, bhaṇe, ayyo devadatto āha tathā kareyyāthā”ti. Atha kho devadatto ekaṃ purisaṃ āṇāpesi – “gacchāvuso, amukasmiṃ okāse samaṇo gotamo viharati. Taṃ jīvitā voropetvā iminā maggena āgacchā”ti. Tasmiṃ magge dve purise ṭhapesi – “yo iminā maggena eko puriso āgacchati, taṃ jīvitā voropetvā iminā maggena āgacchathā”ti. Tasmiṃ magge cattāro purise ṭhapesi – “ye iminā maggena [T 2.0180] dve purisā āgacchanti, te jīvitā voropetvā iminā maggena āgacchathā”ti. Tasmiṃ magge aṭṭha purise ṭhapesi – “ye iminā maggena cattāro purisā āgacchanti, te jīvitā [P 2.0192] voropetvā iminā maggena [M 0.0352] āgacchathā”ti. Tasmiṃ magge soḷasa [V 0.0330] purise ṭhapesi – “ye iminā maggena aṭṭha purisā āgacchanti, te jīvitā voropetvā āgacchathā”ti.

340. Then Devadatta approached Prince Ajātasattu and said to him, “Great King, command men to deprive the ascetic Gotama of life.” Then Prince Ajātasattu commanded the men, “Sirs, do as the venerable Devadatta says.” Then Devadatta commanded one man, “Go, friend. The ascetic Gotama is dwelling in such-and-such a place. Deprive him of life and come back by this path.” On that path, he stationed two men: “The one man who comes by this path, deprive him of life and come back by this path.” On that path, he stationed four men: “The two men who come by this path, deprive them of life and come back by this path.” On that path, he stationed eight men: “The four men who come by this path, deprive them of life and come back by this path.” On that path, he stationed sixteen men: “The eight men who come by this path, deprive them of life and come back.”

Atha kho so eko puriso asicammaṃ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṃ sannayhitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato avidūre bhīto ubbiggo ussaṅkī utrasto patthaddhena kāyena aṭṭhāsi. Addasā kho bhagavā taṃ purisaṃ bhītaṃ ubbiggaṃ ussaṅkiṃ utrastaṃ patthaddhena kāyena ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – “ehāvuso, mā bhāyī”ti. Atha kho so puriso asicammaṃ ekamantaṃ karitvā dhanukalāpaṃ nikkhipitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yohaṃ duṭṭhacitto vadhakacitto idhūpasaṅkanto. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti. “Taggha tvaṃ, āvuso, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ duṭṭhacitto vadhakacitto idhūpasaṅkanto. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, āvuso[T 2.0181], accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuḍḍhi hesā, āvuso, ariyassa vinaye – yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti, āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī”ti.

Then that one man, taking up his sword and shield and slinging on his bow and quiver, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he stood not far from the Blessed One—frightened, alarmed, apprehensive, and terrified, with his body rigid. The Blessed One saw that man standing there, frightened, alarmed, apprehensive, and terrified, with his body rigid. Seeing him, the Blessed One said this: “Come, friend, do not be afraid.” Then that man, setting his sword and shield to one side and putting down his bow and quiver, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, a transgression has overcome me, in that I, being foolish, deluded, and unskillful, approached this place with a mind of ill will, a murderous mind. May the Blessed One accept my transgression as a transgression for the sake of future restraint.” “Indeed, friend, a transgression has overcome you, in that you, being foolish, deluded, and unskillful, approached this place with a mind of ill will, a murderous mind. But since you, friend, having seen your transgression as a transgression, make amends according to the Dhamma, we accept it from you. For this is growth in the Noble One's discipline, friend: that one sees a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, and undertakes future restraint.”

Atha kho bhagavā tassa purisassa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā taṃ bhagavā aññāsi kallacittaṃ, muducittaṃ, vinīvaraṇacittaṃ, udaggacittaṃ, pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaheyya, evameva tassa purisassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Atha kho so puriso diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa [M 0.0353] vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ [P 2.0193] gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ [T 2.0182] gata”nti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca [V 0.0331] – “mā kho tvaṃ, āvuso, iminā maggena gaccha, iminā maggena gacchāhī”ti aññena maggena uyyojesi.

Then the Blessed One gave that man a gradual discourse; that is, a talk on generosity, a talk on virtue, and a talk on heaven. He explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that the man's mind was ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he then revealed that Dhamma teaching which is the special province of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free of stains, would properly absorb dye, so too, right there in that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in that man: “Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.” Then that man—having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, and penetrated the Dhamma; having crossed over doubt, become free from perplexity, and gained assurance; being independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching—said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! It is as if one were to set upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms. In the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” Then the Blessed One said this to that man: “Do not go by this path, friend; go by this path,” and sent him off by another path.

Atha kho te dve purisā – kiṃ nu kho so eko puriso cirena āgacchatīti – paṭipathaṃ gacchantā addasaṃsu bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tesaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi…pe… aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… upāsake no bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gate”ti. Atha kho bhagavā te purise etadavoca – “mā kho tumhe, āvuso, iminā maggena gacchittha, iminā maggena gacchathā”ti aññena maggena uyyojesi.

Then those two men, thinking, “Why is that one man taking so long to come?” went to meet him on the path and saw the Blessed One seated at the foot of a certain tree. Seeing him, they approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One gave them a gradual discourse... and they, being independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! ... May the Blessed One remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” Then the Blessed One said this to those men: “Do not go by this path, friends; go by this path,” and sent them off by another path.

Atha kho te cattāro purisā…pe… atha kho te aṭṭha purisā…pe… atha kho te soḷasa purisā – kiṃ nu kho te aṭṭha purisā cirena āgacchantīti – paṭipathaṃ gacchantā addasāsuṃ bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tesaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ…pe… aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… [T 2.0183] upāsake no bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gate”ti. Atha kho bhagavā te purise etadavoca – “mā kho tumhe, āvuso, iminā maggena gacchittha, iminā maggena gacchathā”ti aññena maggena uyyojesi.

Then those four men... Then those eight men... Then those sixteen men, thinking, “Why are those eight men taking so long to come?” went to meet them on the path and saw the Blessed One seated at the foot of a certain tree. Seeing him, they approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One gave them a gradual discourse; that is, a talk on generosity... and they, being independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! ... May the Blessed One remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” Then the Blessed One said this to those men: “Do not go by this path, friends; go by this path,” and sent them off by another path.

Atha kho so eko puriso yena devadatto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā devadattaṃ etadavoca – “nāhaṃ, bhante, sakkomi taṃ bhagavantaṃ jīvitā voropetuṃ; mahiddhiko so bhagavā, mahānubhāvo”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso; mā tvaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ jīvitā voropesi. Ahameva samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ jīvitā voropessāmī”ti.

Then that one man approached Devadatta and said this to him: “Venerable sir, I am unable to deprive that Blessed One of life; that Blessed One is of great psychic power and great might.” “Enough, friend. Do not deprive the ascetic Gotama of life. I myself will deprive the ascetic Gotama of life.”

Lohituppādakakammaṃ

The Deed of Shedding a Buddha's Blood

341. Tena [M 0.0354] kho pana samayena bhagavā gijjhakūṭassa pabbatassa chāyāyaṃ caṅkamati. Atha kho devadatto gijjhakūṭaṃ pabbataṃ āruhitvā mahatiṃ silaṃ pavijjhi – imāya samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ jīvitā voropessāmīti. Dve pabbatakūṭā samāgantvā taṃ silaṃ sampaṭicchiṃsu. Tato papatikā uppatitvā bhagavato pāde ruhiraṃ uppādesi. Atha kho bhagavā uddhaṃ ulloketvā devadattaṃ [V 0.0332] etadavoca – “bahuṃ tayā, moghapurisa, apuññaṃ pasutaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ duṭṭhacitto vadhakacitto tathāgatassa ruhiraṃ uppādesī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “idaṃ, bhikkhave, devadattena paṭhamaṃ ānantariyaṃ kammaṃ upacitaṃ, yaṃ duṭṭhacittena vadhakacittena tathāgatassa ruhiraṃ uppādita”nti.

341. Now at that time the Blessed One was pacing up and down in the shade of the Vulture Peak mountain. Then Devadatta climbed the Vulture Peak mountain and rolled down a great rock, thinking: 'With this I shall deprive the recluse Gotama of life.' But two mountain peaks came together and caught that rock. Then a splinter flew off and caused blood to arise on the Blessed One’s foot. Then the Blessed One looked up and said to Devadatta: 'Much demerit has been generated by you, worthless man, in that with a mind of ill will and a murderous mind you have caused the Tathāgata’s blood to arise.' Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'This, bhikkhus, is the first deed with immediate result accumulated by Devadatta, in that with a mind of ill will and a murderous mind, the Tathāgata’s blood was caused to arise.'

Assosuṃ [P 2.0194] kho bhikkhū – “devadattena kira bhagavato vadho payutto”ti. Te ca bhikkhū bhagavato vihārassa parito parito caṅkamanti uccāsaddā mahāsaddā sajjhāyaṃ [T 2.0184] karontā, bhagavato rakkhāvaraṇaguttiyā. Assosi kho bhagavā uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ sajjhāyasaddaṃ. Sutvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, ānanda, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo sajjhāyasaddo”ti? “Assosuṃ kho, bhante, bhikkhū – ‘devadattena kira bhagavato vadho payutto’ti. Te ca tedha (sī.), bhante, bhikkhū bhagavato vihārassa parito parito caṅkamanti uccāsaddā mahāsaddā sajjhāyaṃ karontā, bhagavato rakkhāvaraṇaguttiyā. So eso, bhagavā, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo sajjhāyasaddo”ti. “Tena hānanda, mama vacanena te bhikkhū āmantehi – satthā āyasmante āmantetī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “satthā āyasmante āmantetī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca –

The bhikkhus heard: “It is said that Devadatta has made an attempt on the Blessed One’s life.” Those bhikkhus then were pacing up and down all around the Blessed One’s dwelling, with loud voices and great voices, making recitation for the protection, guarding, and security of the Blessed One. The Blessed One heard the loud sound, the great sound, the sound of recitation. Having heard it, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “What, Ānanda, is that loud sound, that great sound, that sound of recitation?” “Venerable sir, the bhikkhus heard: ‘It is said that Devadatta has made an attempt on the Blessed One’s life.’ Those bhikkhus, venerable sir, are pacing up and down all around the Blessed One’s dwelling, with loud voices and great voices, making recitation for the protection, guarding, and security of the Blessed One. That, Blessed One, is this loud sound, this great sound, this sound of recitation.” “Well then, Ānanda, in my name, summon those bhikkhus, saying: ‘The Teacher summons the venerable ones.’” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. He then approached those bhikkhus and said to them: “The Teacher summons the venerable ones.” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. They then approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. When they were seated to one side, the Blessed One said this to them:

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ[M 0.0355], bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ parūpakkamena tathāgataṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Anupakkamena, bhikkhave, tathāgatā parinibbāyanti.

“It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen, that a Tathāgata could be deprived of life by the assault of another. Tathāgatas, bhikkhus, attain final Nibbāna without assault.”

cūḷava. 334; a. ni. 5.100 “Pañcime, bhikkhave, satthāro santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame pañca? “Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco satthā aparisuddhasīlo samāno ‘parisuddhasīlomhī’ti paṭijānāti [T 2.0185] ‘parisuddhaṃ me sīlaṃ pariyodātaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭha’nti ca. Tamenaṃ sāvakā evaṃ jānanti – ‘ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ satthā aparisuddhasīlo samāno ‘parisuddhasīlomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṃ me sīlaṃ pariyodātaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭha’nti ca. Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṃ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṃ. Yaṃ kho panassa amanāpaṃ, kathaṃ naṃ mayaṃ tena samudācareyyāma? Sammannati kho pana cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena – yaṃ tumo karissati, tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti[V 0.0333]. Evarūpaṃ kho, bhikkhave, satthāraṃ sāvakā sīlato rakkhanti; evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi sīlato rakkhaṃ paccāsīsati.

“Bhikkhus, these five teachers are found existing in the world. Which five? Here, bhikkhus, a certain teacher, being impure in moral conduct, claims: ‘I am pure in moral conduct,’ and ‘My moral conduct is pure, bright, and unblemished.’ His disciples know him thus: ‘This venerable teacher, being impure in moral conduct, claims: “I am pure in moral conduct,” and “My moral conduct is pure, bright, and unblemished.” If we were to inform householders, it would not be pleasing to him. And that which is displeasing to him, how could we address him with that? He is honored with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick—whatever he does, he himself will be known by that.’ Such a teacher, bhikkhus, is protected by his disciples in regard to moral conduct; and such a teacher expects protection from his disciples in regard to moral conduct.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, idhekacco satthā aparisuddhaājīvo samāno…pe… aparisuddhadhammadesano samāno…pe… aparisuddhaveyyākaraṇo samāno…pe… [T 2.0186] aparisuddhañāṇadassano samāno ‘parisuddhañāṇadassanomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṃ me ñāṇadassanaṃ pariyodātaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭha’nti ca. Tamenaṃ sāvakā evaṃ jānanti – ‘ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ satthā aparisuddhañāṇadassano samāno ‘parisuddhañāṇadassanomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṃ me ñāṇadassanaṃ pariyodātaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭha’nti ca. Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṃ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṃ. Yaṃ kho panassa amanāpaṃ, kathaṃ na mayaṃ tena samudācareyyāma? Sammannati kho pana cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena – yaṃ tumo karissati, tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti. Evarūpaṃ kho, bhikkhave, satthāraṃ sāvakā ñāṇadassanato rakkhanti; evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi ñāṇadassanato rakkhaṃ paccāsīsati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca satthāro santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. “Ahaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, parisuddhasīlo samāno ‘parisuddhasīlomhī’ti paṭijānāmi ‘parisuddhaṃ me sīlaṃ pariyodātaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭha’nti ca. Na ca maṃ sāvakā sīlato rakkhanti; na cāhaṃ sāvakehi sīlato rakkhaṃ paccāsīsāmi. Ahaṃ kho pana [M 0.0356] bhikkhave parisuddhājīvo samāno…pe… [T 2.0187] parisuddhadhammadesano samāno…pe… parisuddhaveyyākaraṇo samāno…pe… parisuddhañāṇadassano samāno “parisuddhañāṇadassanomhī”ti paṭijānāmi “parisuddhaṃ me ñāṇadassanaṃ pariyodātaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭha”nti ca, na ca maṃ sāvakā ñāṇadassanato rakkhanti, na cāhaṃ sāvakehi ñāṇadassanato rakkhaṃ paccāsīsāmi. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ parūpakkamena tathāgataṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Anupakkamena, bhikkhave, tathāgatā parinibbāyanti. Gacchatha tumhe, bhikkhave, yathāvihāraṃ. Arakkhiyā, bhikkhave, tathāgatā”ti.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, here some teacher, being impure in livelihood… being impure in teaching the Dhamma… being impure in exposition… being impure in knowledge and vision, claims: ‘I am pure in knowledge and vision,’ and declares: ‘My knowledge and vision is pure, bright, and unblemished.’ His disciples know him thus: ‘This venerable teacher, while being impure in knowledge and vision, claims: “I am pure in knowledge and vision,” and declares: “My knowledge and vision is pure, bright, and unblemished.” If we were to inform householders about this, it would not be pleasing to him. And how could we address him in a manner that is displeasing to him? He is honored with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites; whatever he does, he will be known for it.’ Such a teacher, bhikkhus, is protected by his disciples with regard to knowledge and vision; and such a teacher expects protection from his disciples with regard to knowledge and vision. These, bhikkhus, are the five teachers who are found existing in the world. “But I, bhikkhus, being pure in moral conduct, claim: ‘I am pure in moral conduct,’ and declare: ‘My moral conduct is pure, bright, and unblemished.’ My disciples do not protect me with regard to moral conduct, nor do I expect protection from my disciples with regard to moral conduct. I, bhikkhus, being pure in livelihood… pure in teaching the Dhamma… pure in exposition… pure in knowledge and vision, claim: ‘I am pure in knowledge and vision,’ and declare: ‘My knowledge and vision is pure, bright, and unblemished.’ My disciples do not protect me with regard to knowledge and vision, nor do I expect protection from my disciples with regard to knowledge and vision. “It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen, that a Tathāgata could be deprived of life by the assault of another. Tathāgatas, bhikkhus, attain final Nibbāna without any assault. Go, bhikkhus, to your dwellings. Tathāgatas, bhikkhus, need no protection.”

Nāḷāgiripesanaṃ

The Sending of Nāḷāgiri

342. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe nāḷāgiri nāma hatthī caṇḍo hoti, manussaghātako. Atha kho devadatto rājagahaṃ pavisitvā hatthisālaṃ gantvā hatthibhaṇḍe etadavoca – “mayaṃ kho, bhaṇe, rājañātakā nāma paṭibalā nīcaṭṭhāniyaṃ uccaṭṭhāne ṭhapetuṃ, bhattampi vetanampi vaḍḍhāpetuṃ. Tena hi, bhaṇe, yadā samaṇo gotamo imaṃ racchaṃ paṭipanno hoti, tadā imaṃ nāḷāgiriṃ hatthiṃ muñcetvā imaṃ racchaṃ paṭipādethā”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho te [V 0.0334] hatthibhaṇḍā devadattassa paccassosuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sambahulehi [P 2.0195] bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ racchaṃ paṭipajji. Addasāsuṃ kho te hatthibhaṇḍā bhagavantaṃ taṃ racchaṃ paṭipannaṃ. Disvāna nāḷāgiriṃ hatthiṃ muñcitvā taṃ racchaṃ paṭipādesuṃ. Addasā kho nāḷāgiri hatthī bhagavantaṃ dūratova [T 2.0188] āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna soṇḍaṃ ussāpetvā pahaṭṭhakaṇṇavālo yena bhagavā tena abhidhāvi. Addasāsuṃ kho te bhikkhū nāḷāgiriṃ hatthiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bhante, nāḷāgiri hatthī caṇḍo manussaghātako imaṃ racchaṃ paṭipanno. Paṭikkamatu, bhante, bhagavā; paṭikkamatu sugato”ti. “Āgacchatha, bhikkhave, mā bhāyittha. Aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ parūpakkamena tathāgataṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Anupakkamena, bhikkhave, tathāgatā parinibbāyantī”ti. Dutiyampi kho te bhikkhū…pe… tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bhante, nāḷāgiri hatthī caṇḍo manussaghātako imaṃ racchaṃ paṭipanno. Paṭikkamatu, bhante, bhagavā; paṭikkamatu sugato”ti. “Āgacchatha, bhikkhave, mā bhāyittha. Aṭṭhānametaṃ[M 0.0357], bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ parūpakkamena tathāgataṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Anupakkamena, bhikkhave, tathāgatā parinibbāyantī”ti.

342. At that time, in Rājagaha, there was a fierce elephant named Nāḷāgiri, a killer of men. Then Devadatta entered Rājagaha, went to the elephant stable, and said to the elephant keepers: “Friends, we are known as relatives of the king, capable of elevating the low to high positions and increasing food and wages. Therefore, friends, when the ascetic Gotama walks along this street, release this elephant Nāḷāgiri and drive him down this street.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied the elephant keepers to Devadatta. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Rājagaha for alms with a large group of bhikkhus. Then the Blessed One proceeded along that street. The elephant keepers saw the Blessed One walking along the street. Seeing him, they released the elephant Nāḷāgiri and drove him down the street. The elephant Nāḷāgiri saw the Blessed One approaching from afar. Seeing him, he raised his trunk, with ears and tail erect, and charged toward the Blessed One. The bhikkhus saw the elephant Nāḷāgiri approaching from afar. Seeing him, they said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this elephant Nāḷāgiri is fierce and a killer of men; he is coming down this street. Retreat, venerable sir! Retreat, Sugata!” “Come, bhikkhus, do not fear. It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen, that a Tathāgata could be deprived of life by the assault of another. Tathāgatas, bhikkhus, attain final Nibbāna without any assault.” For a second time the bhikkhus… For a third time the bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this elephant Nāḷāgiri is fierce and a killer of men; he is coming down this street. Retreat, venerable sir! Retreat, Sugata!” “Come, bhikkhus, do not fear. It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen, that a Tathāgata could be deprived of life by the assault of another. Tathāgatas, bhikkhus, attain final Nibbāna without any assault.”

Tena kho pana samayena manussā pāsādesupi hammiyesupi chadanesupi āruḷhā acchanti. Tattha ye te manussā assaddhā appasannā dubbuddhino, te evamāhaṃsu – “abhirūpo vata, bho abhirūpo vata bho gotamo (syā. kaṃ.), mahāsamaṇo nāgena viheṭhīyissatī”ti. Ye pana te manussā [T 2.0189] saddhā pasannā paṇḍitā byattā buddhimanto, te evamāhaṃsu – “nacirassaṃ vata, bho, nāgo nāgena saṅgāmessatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā nāḷāgiriṃ hatthiṃ mettena cittena phari. Atha kho nāḷāgiri hatthī bhagavato bhagavatā (sī.) mettena cittena phuṭṭho phuṭo (ka.) soṇḍaṃ oropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato purato aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena hatthena nāḷāgirissa hatthissa kumbhaṃ parāmasanto nāḷāgiriṃ hatthiṃ imāhi gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

At that time, people had ascended and were on long palaces, on pinnacled mansions, and on rooftops. Among them, those people who were without faith, without devotion, and without wisdom, spoke thus: 'Indeed, friends, the very handsome great ascetic will be harmed by the elephant.' But those people who had faith, were devoted, wise, discerning, and intelligent, spoke thus: 'Indeed, friends, soon the elephant will contend with the Nāga.' Then the Blessed One suffused the elephant Nāḷāgiri with a mind of loving-kindness. Then the elephant Nāḷāgiri, having been touched by the Blessed One's mind of loving-kindness, lowered its trunk and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, it stood before the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, stroking the head of the elephant Nāḷāgiri with his right hand, admonished the elephant Nāḷāgiri with these verses:

“Mā kuñjara nāgamāsado, dukkhañhi kuñjara nāgamāsado;

Na hi nāgahatassa kuñjara sugati, hoti ito paraṃ yato.

“O elephant, do not assail the Nāga; for to assail the Nāga is indeed suffering, O elephant. For one who has killed a Nāga, O elephant, there is indeed no good destination when going from here to the next world.

“Mā ca mado mā ca pamādo, na hi pamattā sugatiṃ vajanti te;

Tvaññeva tathā karissasi, yena tvaṃ sugatiṃ gamissasī”ti.

“Let there be no intoxication and no heedlessness, for the heedless indeed do not go to a good destination. You yourself must act in such a way by which you will go to a good destination.”

Atha [V 0.0335] kho nāḷāgiri hatthī soṇḍāya bhagavato pādapaṃsūni gahetvā uparimuddhani ākiritvā paṭikuṭiyova paṭikuṭito paṭisakki (sī. syā.) osakki, yāva bhagavantaṃ addakkhi. Atha kho nāḷāgiri hatthī hatthisālaṃ gantvā sake ṭhāne aṭṭhāsi. Tathā danto ca pana nāḷāgiri [P 2.0196] hatthī ahosi. Tena [T 2.0190] kho pana samayena manussā imaṃ gāthaṃ gāyanti –

Then the elephant Nāḷāgiri, taking the dust from the Blessed One's feet with its trunk and sprinkling it upon its head, retreated backwards for as long as it could see the Blessed One. Then the elephant Nāḷāgiri, having gone to the elephant stable, stood in its own place. Thus the elephant Nāḷāgiri was tamed. At that time, the people sang this verse:

ma. ni. 2.352; theragā. 878 “Daṇḍeneke damayanti, aṅkusehi kasāhi ca;

Adaṇḍena asatthena, nāgo danto mahesinā”ti.

“Some tame with a staff, with goads, and with whips; but without a staff, without a weapon, the elephant was tamed by the great sage.”

Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yāva pāpo ayaṃ devadatto, alakkhiko, yatra hi nāma samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃmahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vadhāya parakkamissatī”ti. Devadattassa lābhasakkāro parihāyi. Bhagavato ca lābhasakkāro abhivaḍḍhi.

People criticized, condemned, and disparaged him, saying: “How very wicked is this Devadatta, how disgraceful, that he would strive to kill the ascetic Gotama, who is of such great psychic power and of such great might!” Devadatta's gain and honor declined, while the Blessed One's gain and honor increased.

Pañcavatthuyācanakathā

The Account of the Request for Five Points

343. pāci. 209 Tena [M 0.0358] kho pana samayena devadatto parihīnalābhasakkāro sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjati. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Kassa sampannaṃ na manāpaṃ, kassa sāduṃ na ruccatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma devadatto sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjissatī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, devadatta, sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjasī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ kulesu tikabhojanaṃ paññapessāmi tayo atthavase paṭicca – dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalāna niggahāya[T 2.0191]; pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, mā pāpicchā pakkhaṃ nissāya saṅghaṃ bhindeyyunti; kulānuddayāya kulānudayatāya (sī. syā.) ca. Gaṇabhojane yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

343. At that time, Devadatta, his gain and honor having declined, ate with his retinue after repeatedly soliciting from the families of supporters. People criticized, condemned, and disparaged them, saying: “How indeed can these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, eat after repeatedly soliciting from families! To whom is well-prepared food not pleasing? Who does not like what is delicious?” The monks heard those people criticizing, condemning, and disparaging them. Those monks who were of few desires [...] criticized, condemned, and disparaged him, saying: “How indeed can Devadatta eat with his retinue after repeatedly soliciting from families!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. [...] “Is it true, it is said, Devadatta, that you eat with your retinue after repeatedly soliciting from families?” “It is true, Blessed One.” [...] Having rebuked him [...] and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Therefore, monks, I will lay down a rule for the monks concerning a meal for three among families, on account of three reasons: for the restraint of immoral persons; for the comfortable living of virtuous monks; so that those with evil desires, relying on a faction, may not split the Sangha; and also out of compassion for the families. In the matter of a group meal, it should be carried out according to the rule.”

pārā. 409 Atha kho devadatto yena kokāliko kaṭamodakatissako kaṭamorakatissako (sī. syā.) khaṇḍadeviyā putto samuddadatto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā kokālikaṃ kaṭamodakatissakaṃ khaṇḍadeviyā puttaṃ samuddadattaṃ etadavoca – “etha, mayaṃ, āvuso, samaṇassa gotamassa saṅghabhedaṃ karissāma cakkabheda”nti. Evaṃ [V 0.0336] vutte kokāliko devadattaṃ etadavoca – “samaṇo kho, āvuso, gotamo mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo. Kathaṃ mayaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa saṅghabhedaṃ karissāma cakkabheda”nti? “Etha, mayaṃ, āvuso, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañca vatthūni yācissāma – ‘bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa [P 2.0197] dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādī. Imāni, bhante, pañca vatthūni anekapariyāyena appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā sallekhāya dhutatāya pāsādikatāya apacayāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattanti. Sādhu, bhante, bhikkhū yāvajīvaṃ āraññikā assu; yo gāmantaṃ [M 0.0359] osareyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ piṇḍapātikā assu; yo nimantanaṃ sādiyeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ paṃsukūlikā [T 2.0192] assu; yo gahapaticīvaraṃ sādiyeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ rukkhamūlikā assu; yo channaṃ upagaccheyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ macchamaṃsaṃ na khādeyyuṃ; yo macchamaṃsaṃ khādeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyyā’ti. Imāni pañca vatthūni samaṇo gotamo nānujānissati. Te mayaṃ imehi pañcahi vatthūhi janaṃ saññāpessāmā”ti. “Sakkā kho, āvuso, imehi pañcahi vatthūhi samaṇassa gotamassa saṅghabhedo kātuṃ cakkabhedo. Lūkhappasannā hi, āvuso, manussā”ti.

Then Devadatta approached Kokālika, Kaṭamodakatissaka, and Samuddadatta the son of Khaṇḍadeviyā. Having approached, he said to Kokālika, Kaṭamodakatissaka, and Samuddadatta the son of Khaṇḍadeviyā: “Come, sirs, let us create a schism in the Sangha of the ascetic Gotama and a breaking of the wheel.” When this was said, Kokālika said to Devadatta: “Sir, the ascetic Gotama is of great psychic power and great majesty. How can we create a schism in his Sangha and a breaking of the wheel?” “Come, sirs, let us approach the ascetic Gotama and request five points: ‘Venerable sir, the Blessed One in many ways praises fewness of wishes, contentment, self-effacement, ascetic practices, graciousness, non-accumulation, and energetic striving. These five points, venerable sir, in many ways conduce to fewness of wishes, contentment, self-effacement, ascetic practices, graciousness, non-accumulation, and energetic striving. It would be good, venerable sir, if the monks were to be lifelong forest-dwellers; whoever should go to the vicinity of a village, an offense should befall him. If they were to be lifelong alms-food eaters; whoever should accept an invitation, an offense should befall him. If they were to be lifelong rag-robe wearers; whoever should accept a householder’s robe, an offense should befall him. If they were to be lifelong tree-root dwellers; whoever should go under a roof, an offense should befall him. For life, they should not eat fish and meat; whoever should eat fish and meat, an offense should befall him.’ The ascetic Gotama will not grant these five points. Then we shall persuade the people with these five points.” “It is possible, sir, to create a schism in the Sangha of the ascetic Gotama and a breaking of the wheel with these five points. For people, sir, are devoted to austerity.”

Atha kho devadatto sapariso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho devadatto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādī. Imāni, bhante, pañca vatthūni anekapariyāyena appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā sallekhāya dhutatāya pāsādikatāya apacayāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattanti. Sādhu, bhante, bhikkhū yāvajīvaṃ āraññikā assu; yo gāmantaṃ osareyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ piṇḍapātikā assu; yo nimantanaṃ sādiyeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ paṃsukūlikā assu; yo gahapaticīvaraṃ [T 2.0193] sādiyeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ rukkhamūlikā assu; yo channaṃ upagaccheyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya. Yāvajīvaṃ macchamaṃsaṃ na khādeyyuṃ; yo macchamaṃsaṃ khādeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyyā”ti. “Alaṃ, devadatta. Yo icchati, āraññiko hotu; yo icchati, gāmante viharatu. Yo icchati, piṇḍapātiko hotu; yo icchati, nimantanaṃ sādiyatu. Yo icchati, paṃsukūliko hotu; yo icchati, gahapaticīvaraṃ sādiyatu. Aṭṭhamāse kho mayā, devadatta, rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ anuññātaṃ; tikoṭiparisuddhaṃ macchamaṃsaṃ – adiṭṭhaṃ, assutaṃ, aparisaṅkita”nti. Atha kho devadatto – na bhagavā [V 0.0337] imāni pañca vatthūni anujānātīti – haṭṭho udaggo sapariso uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then Devadatta, together with his retinue, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Devadatta said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, the Blessed One has, in many ways, spoken in praise of fewness of wishes, of contentment, of effacement, of shaking off defilements, of graciousness, of non-accumulation, and of the arousing of energy. Venerable sir, these five points conduce in many ways to fewness of wishes, to contentment, to effacement, to shaking off defilements, to graciousness, to non-accumulation, and to the arousing of energy. It would be good, venerable sir, if the monks were to be forest-dwellers for life; should one resort to the vicinity of a village, may an offense befall him. May they be eaters of alms-food for life; should one consent to an invitation, may an offense befall him. May they be wearers of rag-robes for life; should one consent to a householder's robe, may an offense befall him. May they be dwellers at the foot of a tree for life; should one approach a roofed dwelling, may an offense befall him. May they not eat fish and meat for life; should one eat fish and meat, may an offense befall him.' 'Enough, Devadatta. Whoever wishes, let him be a forest-dweller; whoever wishes, let him dwell in the vicinity of a village. Whoever wishes, let him be an eater of alms-food; whoever wishes, let him consent to an invitation. Whoever wishes, let him be a wearer of rag-robes; whoever wishes, let him consent to a householder's robe. For eight months, Devadatta, the dwelling at the foot of a tree has been allowed by me. And I have allowed fish and meat that is pure in three respects: not seen, not heard, and not suspected.' Then Devadatta, thinking, 'The Blessed One does not allow these five points,' joyful and elated, together with his retinue, rose from his seat, and having paid homage to the Blessed One and circumambulated him to the right, he departed.

Atha kho devadatto sapariso rājagahaṃ pavisitvā pañcahi vatthūhi janaṃ saññāpesi – “mayaṃ, āvuso, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañca vatthūni [M 0.0360] yācimhā – ‘bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa…pe… vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādī. Imāni, bhante, pañca vatthūni anekapariyāyena appicchatāya…pe… vīriyārambhāya saṃvattanti. Sādhu, bhante, bhikkhū yāvajīvaṃ āraññikā assu; yo gāmantaṃ osareyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya…pe… yāvajīvaṃ macchamaṃsaṃ na khādeyyuṃ; yo macchamaṃsaṃ khādeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyyā’ti. Imāni pañca vatthūni samaṇo gotamo nānujānāti. Te mayaṃ imehi pañcahi vatthūhi [T 2.0194] samādāya vattāmā”ti.

Then Devadatta, together with his retinue, entered Rājagaha and proclaimed these five points to the people: 'Friends, we approached the ascetic Gotama and requested five points: "Venerable sir, the Blessed One in many ways is one who speaks in praise of one with few wishes... of one with energetic striving. These five points, venerable sir, in many ways conduce to fewness of wishes... to energetic striving. It would be good, venerable sir, if the monks were forest-dwellers for life; should any monk resort to the vicinity of a village, may an offense befall him... they should not eat fish and meat for life; should any monk eat fish and meat, may an offense befall him." The ascetic Gotama does not permit these five points. We, for our part, having undertaken these five points, live in accordance with them.'

Tattha ye te manussā assaddhā appasannā dubbuddhino, te evamāhaṃsu – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dhutā sallekhavuttino. Samaṇo pana gotamo bāhulliko bāhullāya cetetī”ti. Ye pana te manussā saddhā [P 2.0198] pasannā paṇḍitā byattā buddhimanto, te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma devadatto bhagavato saṅghabhedāya parakkamissati cakkabhedāyā”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma devadatto saṅghabhedāya parakkamissati cakkabhedāyā”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, devadatta, saṅghabhedāya parakkamasi cakkabhedāyā”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. “Alaṃ, devadatta. Mā te rucci saṅghabhedo. Garuko kho, devadatta, saṅghabhedo. Yo kho, devadatta, samaggaṃ saṅghaṃ bhindati, kappaṭṭhikaṃ kappaṭṭhitikaṃ (syā.) kibbisaṃ pasavati, kappaṃ nirayamhi paccati. Yo ca kho, devadatta, bhinnaṃ saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ karoti, brahmaṃ puññaṃ pasavati, kappaṃ saggamhi modati. Alaṃ, devadatta. Mā te rucci saṅghabhedo. Garuko kho, devadatta, saṅghabhedo”ti.

There, those people who were faithless, displeased, and unwise said this: "These Sakyan ascetics are austere and self-effacing in conduct. But the ascetic Gotama is indulgent and strives for indulgence." However, those people who were faithful, devout, wise, discerning, and intelligent complained, criticized, and spread reproach: "How could Devadatta strive to split the Sangha and break the wheel?" The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading reproach. Those monks who were of few desires... also complained, criticized, and spread reproach: "How could Devadatta strive to split the Sangha and break the wheel?" Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One... "Is it true, Devadatta, that you are striving to split the Sangha and break the wheel?" "It is true, Blessed One." "Enough, Devadatta. Do not let splitting the Sangha appeal to you. Grave is the splitting of the Sangha, Devadatta. Whoever splits a united Sangha generates evil that lasts for an eon; he is cooked in hell for an eon. But whoever unites a divided Sangha generates sublime merit; he rejoices in heaven for an eon. Enough, Devadatta. Do not let splitting the Sangha appeal to you. Grave is the splitting of the Sangha, Devadatta."

udā. 48 Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasā kho devadatto āyasmantaṃ [T 2.0195] ānandaṃ rājagahe piṇḍāya carantaṃ. Disvāna yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “ajjataggedānāhaṃ[V 0.0338], āvuso ānanda, aññatreva bhagavatā, aññatreva bhikkhusaṅghā, uposathaṃ karissāmi saṅghakammaṃ karissāmī”ti.

Then, in the morning, Venerable Ānanda, having dressed, took his bowl and robe and entered Rājagaha for alms. Devadatta saw Venerable Ānanda walking for alms in Rājagaha. Having seen him, he approached Venerable Ānanda and said: "From today onward, friend Ānanda, I will perform the Uposatha and Saṅgha acts separately from the Blessed One and separately from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus."

Atha [M 0.0361] kho āyasmā ānando rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idhāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Addasā kho maṃ, bhante, devadatto rājagahe piṇḍāya carantaṃ. Disvāna yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘ajjataggedānāhaṃ, āvuso ānanda, aññatreva bhagavatā, aññatreva bhikkhusaṅghā, uposathaṃ karissāmi saṅghakammaṃ karissāmī’ti. Ajjatagge, bhante, devadatto saṅghaṃ bhindissatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having wandered for alms in Rājagaha and returned from his alms-round after the meal, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, this morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I entered Rājagaha for alms. Venerable Sir, Devadatta saw me wandering for alms in Rājagaha. Having seen me, he approached where I was. Having approached, he said this to me: ‘Friend Ānanda, from today onwards, I, apart from the Blessed One, apart from the community of monks, will perform the Uposatha and will perform acts of the Saṅgha.’ Venerable Sir, from today onwards, Devadatta will split the Saṅgha.' Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

udā. 48 “Sukaraṃ sādhunā sādhuṃ, sādhuṃ pāpena dukkaraṃ;

Pāpaṃ pāpena sukaraṃ, pāpamariyehi dukkara”nti.

A good deed is easy for the good; a good deed is difficult for the wicked. An evil deed is easy for the wicked; an evil deed is difficult for the noble.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is finished.

3. Tatiyabhāṇavāro

3. The Third Recitation Section

Saṅghabhedakathā

The Discourse on Schism in the Saṅgha

344. Atha [P 2.0199] kho devadatto tadahuposathe uṭṭhāyāsanā salākaṃ gāhesi – “mayaṃ, āvuso, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañca vatthūni yācimhā [T 2.0196] – ‘bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa…pe… vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādī. Imāni, bhante, pañca vatthūni anekapariyāyena appicchatāya…pe… vīriyārambhāya saṃvattanti. Sādhu, bhante, bhikkhū yāvajīvaṃ āraññikā assu; yo gāmantaṃ osareyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya…pe… yāvajīvaṃ macchamaṃsaṃ na khādeyyuṃ; yo macchamaṃsaṃ khādeyya, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyyā’ti. Imāni pañca vatthūni samaṇo gotamo nānujānāti. Te mayaṃ imehi pañcahi vatthūhi samādāya vattāma. Yassāyasmato imāni pañca vatthūni khamanti, so salākaṃ gaṇhātū”ti.

344. Then, on that Uposatha day, Devadatta, having risen from his seat, had the voting-tickets taken up, saying: 'Friends, we approached the ascetic Gotama and requested five points: ‘Venerable Sir, the Blessed One in many ways speaks in praise of one with few wishes… of one who has aroused energy. Venerable Sir, these five points in many ways conduce to fewness of wishes… to the arousing of energy. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the monks were to be forest-dwellers for life; whoever should descend to the vicinity of a village, a fault would befall him… for life they should not eat fish and meat; whoever should eat fish and meat, a fault would befall him.’ The ascetic Gotama does not permit these five points. We, having undertaken them, will live in accordance with these five points. To whichever venerable one these five points are agreeable, let him take a voting-ticket.'

Tena kho pana samayena vesālikā vajjiputtakā pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni navakā ceva [V 0.0339] honti appakataññuno ca. Te – ‘ayaṃ dhammo[M 0.0362], ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsana’nti – salākaṃ gaṇhiṃsu. Atha kho devadatto saṅghaṃ bhinditvā pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni ādāya yena gayāsīsaṃ tena pakkāmi. Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “devadatto, bhante, saṅghaṃ bhinditvā pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni ādāya yena gayāsīsaṃ tena pakkanto”ti. “Na hi nāma tumhākaṃ, sāriputtā, tesu [T 2.0197] navakesu bhikkhūsu kāruññampi bhavissati? Gacchatha tumhe, sāriputtā, purā te bhikkhū anayabyasanaṃ āpajjantī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho sāriputtamoggallānā bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena gayāsīsaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu.

At that time, there were five hundred Vajjian monks from Vesālī who were newly ordained and unskilled in the discipline. They took the voting-tickets, saying, 'This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher's Dispensation.' Then Devadatta, having created a schism in the Saṅgha, took the five hundred monks and departed for Gayāsīsa. Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, Devadatta, having created a schism in the Saṅgha, has taken the five hundred monks and departed for Gayāsīsa.' 'Sāriputtas, will you indeed have no compassion for those newly ordained monks? Go, Sāriputtas, before those monks meet with ruin and disaster.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' Sāriputta and Moggallāna replied to the Blessed One, and having risen from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping their right side towards him, and approached Gayāsīsa.

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bhagavato avidūre rodamāno ṭhito hoti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, bhikkhu, rodasī”ti? “Yepi te, bhante, bhagavato aggasāvakā sāriputtamoggallānā tepi devadattassa santike gacchanti devadattassa dhammaṃ rocentā”ti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhu, anavakāso, yaṃ sāriputtamoggallānā devadattassa dhammaṃ roceyyuṃ, api ca te gatā bhikkhūnaṃ saññattiyā”ti bhikkhusaññattiyāti (sī. syā.), bhikkhū saññattiyā (ka.).

At that time, a certain monk was standing not far from the Blessed One, weeping. Then the Blessed One said to that monk: 'Why are you weeping, monk?' 'Venerable Sir, even the Blessed One's chief disciples, Sāriputta and Moggallāna, are going to Devadatta, approving of Devadatta's teaching.' 'Monk, it is impossible, it cannot be that Sāriputta and Moggallāna would approve of Devadatta's teaching. Rather, they have gone for the purpose of instructing those monks.'

345. Tena kho pana samayena devadatto mahatiyā parisāya parivutto dhammaṃ desento nisinno hoti. Addasā kho devadatto sāriputtamoggallāne dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “passatha, bhikkhave, yāva svākkhāto mayā dhammo, yepi te samaṇassa gotamassa aggasāvakā sāriputtamoggallānā tepi mama santike āgacchanti. Mama dhammaṃ rocentā”ti. Evaṃ vutte kokāliko devadattaṃ etadavoca – “mā, āvuso devadatta, sāriputtamoggallāne vissasi[T 2.0198]. Pāpicchā sāriputtamoggallānā[P 2.0200], pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso. Svāgataṃ tesaṃ yato me dhammaṃ rocentī”ti.

345. Now at that time, Devadatta, surrounded by a large assembly, was seated teaching the Dhamma. Devadatta saw Sāriputta and Moggallāna coming from afar. Having seen them, he addressed the monks: “Behold, monks, how well-proclaimed the Dhamma is by me, that even Sāriputta and Moggallāna, the chief disciples of the ascetic Gotama, come to my presence, approving of my Dhamma.” When this was said, Kokālika said this to Devadatta: “Friend Devadatta, do not trust Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil desires; they have come under the sway of evil desires.” “Enough, friend. Welcome to them, since they approve of my Dhamma.”

Atha kho devadatto āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ upaḍḍhāsanena nimantesi – “ehāvuso sāriputta, idha nisīdāhī”ti. “Alaṃ āvuso”ti kho āyasmā [M 0.0363] sāriputto aññataraṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Āyasmāpi kho mahāmoggallāno aññataraṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Atha kho devadatto bahudeva rattiṃ bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ ajjhesi – “vigatathinamiddho [V 0.0340] kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhusaṅgho. Paṭibhātu taṃ, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammī kathā, piṭṭhi me āgilāyati, tamahaṃ āyamissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto devadattassa paccassosi. Atha kho devadatto catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvā dakkhiṇena passena seyyaṃ kappesi. Tassa kilamantassa muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa muhuttakeneva niddā okkami.

Then Devadatta invited the Venerable Sāriputta with half a seat, saying, “Come, friend Sāriputta, sit here.” “Enough, friend,” said the Venerable Sāriputta, and taking another seat, he sat down to one side. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna also took another seat and sat down to one side. Then Devadatta, for a great part of the night, having instructed, established, roused, and gladdened the monks with a Dhamma talk, requested the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, the community of monks is free from sloth and torpor. Let a Dhamma talk for the monks occur to you. My back is aching; I will stretch it.” “Very well, friend,” the Venerable Sāriputta consented to Devadatta. Then Devadatta, spreading his four-fold outer robe, lay down on his right side. As he was weary, of lapsed mindfulness, and without clear comprehension, sleep overcame him in just a moment.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsaniyā bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya ovadi anusāsi. Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno iddhipāṭihāriyānusāsaniyā bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya ovadi anusāsi. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āyasmatā sāriputtena ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsaniyā āyasmatā ca mahāmoggallānena iddhipāṭihāriyānusāsaniyā [T 2.0199] ovadiyamānānaṃ anusāsiyamānānaṃ virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta instructed and admonished the monks with a Dhamma talk, with the instruction that is the miracle of mind-reading. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna instructed and admonished the monks with a Dhamma talk, with the instruction that is the miracle of psychic power. Then, as those monks were being instructed and admonished with a Dhamma talk by the Venerable Sāriputta with the instruction that is the miracle of mind-reading, and by the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna with the instruction that is the miracle of psychic power, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in them: ‘Whatever is of a nature to arise, all that is of a nature to cease.’

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “gacchāma mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato santike. Yo tassa bhagavato dhammaṃ rocesi so āgacchatū”ti. Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā tāni pañcabhikkhusatāni ādāya yena veḷuvanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho kokāliko devadattaṃ uṭṭhāpesi – “uṭṭhehi, āvuso devadatta, nītā te bhikkhū sāriputtamoggallānehi. Nanu tvaṃ, āvuso devadatta, mayā vutto – ‘mā, āvuso devadatta, sāriputtamoggallāne vissāsi. Pāpicchā sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā’”ti? Atha kho devadattassa tattheva uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ mukhato uggañchi.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the monks: ‘Let us go, friends, to the Blessed One. Whoever approves of the Dhamma of that Blessed One, let him come.’ Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna, taking those five hundred monks, approached the Veḷuvana. Then Kokālika roused Devadatta: ‘Get up, friend Devadatta, your monks have been led away by Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Were you not told by me, friend Devadatta: “Friend Devadatta, do not trust Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of evil desires; they have fallen under the sway of evil desires”?’ Then, right there, hot blood gushed from Devadatta’s mouth.

Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdisuṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto [P 2.0201] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante[M 0.0364], bhedakānuvattakā bhikkhū puna upasampajjeyyu”nti. “Alaṃ, sāriputta. Mā te rucci bhedakānuvattakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ puna upasampadā. Tena hi tvaṃ, sāriputta, bhedakānuvattake bhikkhū thullaccayaṃ desāpehi. Kathaṃ pana te, sāriputta, devadatto paṭipajjī”ti? “Yatheva, bhante, bhagavā bahudeva rattiṃ bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā maṃ ajjhesati – ‘vigatathinamiddho kho[T 2.0200], sāriputta, bhikkhusaṅgho; paṭibhātu taṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammī kathā, piṭṭhi me āgilāyati, tamahaṃ āyamissāmī’ti, evameva kho, bhante, devadatto paṭipajjī”ti.

Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the monks who are followers of the schismatic were to be ordained again.” “Enough, Sāriputta. Do not approve of the re-ordination of the monks who are followers of the schismatic. Therefore, Sāriputta, you should have the monks who are followers of the schismatic confess a grave offense. But how, Sāriputta, did Devadatta behave towards you?” “Just as, Venerable sir, the Blessed One, after spending much of the night instructing, establishing, rousing, and gladdening the monks with a Dhamma talk, addresses me, saying: ‘Sāriputta, the community of monks is free from sloth and torpor. Let a Dhamma talk occur to you, Sāriputta. My back is aching; I will stretch it.’ In the very same way, Venerable sir, did Devadatta behave.”

346. Atha [V 0.0341] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, araññāyatane mahāsarasī. Taṃ nāgā upanissāya vihariṃsu. Te taṃ sarasiṃ ogāhetvā, soṇḍāya bhisamuḷālaṃ abbuhitvā, suvikkhālitaṃ vikkhāletvā, akaddamaṃ saṅkhāditvā, ajjhoharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ vaṇṇāya ceva hoti, balāya ca. Na ca tatonidānaṃ maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti, maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Tesaṃyeva kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānāgānaṃ anusikkhamānā taruṇā bhiṅkacchāpā. Te taṃ sarasiṃ ogāhetvā, soṇḍāya bhisamuḷālaṃ abbuhitvā, na suvikkhālitaṃ vikkhāletvā, sakaddamaṃ saṅkhāditvā, ajjhoharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ neva vaṇṇāya hoti, na balāya. Tatonidānañca maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti, maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, devadatto mamānukrubbaṃ mamānukubbaṃ (sī. syā.) kapaṇo marissatīti.

346. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, in the past, there was a great lake in a forest region. Elephants lived relying on it. They would enter that lake, pull up lotus roots and stalks with their trunks, wash them thoroughly, chew them free of mud, and swallow them. That was for both their complexion and their strength. And from that cause, they did not meet with death or suffering amounting to death. But, monks, there were young elephant calves who imitated those great elephants. They would enter that lake, pull up lotus roots and stalks with their trunks, not wash them thoroughly, chew them with the mud, and swallow them. That was for neither their complexion nor their strength. And from that cause, they met with death or suffering amounting to death. In the very same way, monks, Devadatta, imitating me, will die wretchedly.”

“Mahāvarāhassa mahiṃ vikrubbato vikubbato (sī. syā.), bhisaṃ ghasānassa ghasamānassa (ka.) nadīsu jaggato;

Bhiṅkova [T 2.0201] paṅkaṃ abhibhakkhayitvā, mamānukrubbaṃ kapaṇo marissatī”ti.

“Imitating the great tusker that tears up the earth, eats lotus stalks, and roams in the rivers, a young elephant, having eaten mud, perishes; just so, the wretched one, imitating me, will die.”

347. a. ni. 8.16 “Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu dūteyyaṃ gantumarahati. Katamehi aṭṭhahi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā ca hoti, sāvetā ca, uggahetā ca, dhāretā ca, viññātā ca, viññāpetā ca, kusalo ca sahitāsahitassa, no ca kalahakārako – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu dūteyyaṃ gantumarahati.

347. “Monks, a monk endowed with eight qualities is fit to go on a mission. With which eight? Here, monks, a monk is one who listens and makes others listen, learns and retains, understands and makes others understand, is skilled in what is beneficial and unbeneficial, and is not a quarrel-maker. Monks, a monk endowed with these eight qualities is fit to go on a mission.”

a. ni. 8.16 “Aṭṭhahi[M 0.0365], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato sāriputto dūteyyaṃ gantumarahati. Katamehi aṭṭhahi? Idha, bhikkhave, sāriputto sotā ca hoti, sāvetā ca, uggahetā ca, dhāretā ca, viññātā ca, viññāpetā ca, kusalo ca sahitāsahitassa, no ca kalahakārako – imehi [P 2.0202] kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato sāriputto dūteyyaṃ gantumarahatīti.

Bhikkhus, Sāriputta, being endowed with eight qualities, is fit to go on a mission. With which eight? Here, bhikkhus, Sāriputta is one who listens and makes others listen, learns and retains, understands and makes others understand, is skilled in what is beneficial and unbeneficial, and is not a quarrel-maker. Bhikkhus, Sāriputta, being endowed with these eight qualities, is fit to go on a mission.

a. ni. 8.16 “Yo ve na byathati byādhati (sī. syā.) patvā, parisaṃ uggavādiniṃ;

Na ca hāpeti vacanaṃ, na ca chādeti sāsanaṃ.

Indeed, one who is not agitated upon approaching an assembly that speaks harshly, and neither diminishes the word nor conceals the message.

“Asandiddho ca akkhāti akkhātā (ka.), pucchito ca na kuppati;

Sa ve tādisako bhikkhu, dūteyyaṃ gantumarahatī”ti.

He speaks without hesitation, and when questioned, does not become angry; such a bhikkhu is indeed fit to go on a mission.

348. a. ni. 8.7 “Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko [V 0.0342] nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi aṭṭhahi[T 2.0202]? Lābhena, bhikkhave, abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho; alābhena, bhikkhave…pe… yasena, bhikkhave…pe… ayasena, bhikkhave…pe… sakkārena, bhikkhave…pe… asakkārena, bhikkhave…pe… pāpicchatāya, bhikkhave…pe… pāpamittatāya bhikkhave, abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho – imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi asaddhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

348. Bhikkhus, Devadatta, being overwhelmed and his mind completely seized by eight qualities of the unrighteous, is destined for the states of woe, destined for hell, to remain for the aeon, incurable. By which eight? Bhikkhus, Devadatta, being overwhelmed and his mind completely seized by gain, is destined for the states of woe, destined for hell, to remain for the aeon, incurable; by loss of gain, bhikkhus…; by fame, bhikkhus…; by lack of fame, bhikkhus…; by honor, bhikkhus…; by lack of honor, bhikkhus…; by evil desire, bhikkhus…; by evil friendship, bhikkhus, being overwhelmed and his mind completely seized, Devadatta is destined for the states of woe, destined for hell, to remain for the aeon, incurable. Indeed, bhikkhus, Devadatta, being overwhelmed and his mind completely seized by these eight qualities of the unrighteous, is destined for the states of woe, destined for hell, to remain for the aeon, incurable.

349. “Sādhu, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ lābhaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya, uppannaṃ alābhaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ yasaṃ… uppannaṃ ayasaṃ… uppannaṃ sakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ asakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ pāpicchataṃ… uppannaṃ pāpamittataṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ lābhaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya, uppannaṃ alābhaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ yasaṃ… uppannaṃ ayasaṃ… uppannaṃ sakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ asakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ pāpicchataṃ… uppannaṃ pāpamittataṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya? Yaṃ hissa, bhikkhave, uppannaṃ lābhaṃ anabhibhuyya viharato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, uppannaṃ lābhaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya [M 0.0366] viharato evaṃsate āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Yaṃ hissa, bhikkhave, uppannaṃ alābhaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ yasaṃ… uppannaṃ ayasaṃ… uppannaṃ sakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ asakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ pāpicchataṃ… uppannaṃ [T 2.0203] pāpamittataṃ anabhibhuyya viharato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, uppannaṃ pāpamittataṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya viharato evaṃsate āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, atthavasaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ lābhaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya, uppannaṃ alābhaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ yasaṃ… uppannaṃ ayasaṃ… uppannaṃ sakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ asakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ pāpicchataṃ… uppannaṃ pāpamittataṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, uppannaṃ lābhaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya viharissāma, uppannaṃ alābhaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ yasaṃ… uppannaṃ ayasaṃ… uppannaṃ sakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ asakkāraṃ… uppannaṃ pāpicchataṃ… uppannaṃ pāpamittataṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya viharissāmāti; evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbanti.

349. It is good, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu to dwell repeatedly overcoming any gain that has arisen, any loss that has arisen… any fame… any disrepute… any honor… any dishonor… any evil desire… any evil friendship that has arisen. And for what reason, bhikkhus, should a bhikkhu dwell repeatedly overcoming these things? For one who dwells without overcoming an arisen gain, bhikkhus, taints, distress, and anguish might arise. But for one who dwells repeatedly overcoming an arisen gain, those taints, distress, and anguish do not arise. For one who dwells without overcoming an arisen loss… or an arisen evil friendship, taints, distress, and anguish might arise.
