But for one who dwells repeatedly overcoming an arisen evil friendship, those taints, distress, and anguish do not arise. This, bhikkhus, is the reason on account of which one should dwell repeatedly overcoming an arisen gain… an arisen evil friendship. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will dwell repeatedly overcoming any gain that has arisen… we will dwell repeatedly overcoming any evil friendship that has arisen.’ This, bhikkhus, is how you should train.

350. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehi [P 2.0203] abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi tīhi? Pāpicchatā, pāpamittatā, oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṃ āpādi – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi asaddhammehi [V 0.0343] abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekicchoti.

350. Bhikkhus, Devadatta, overcome and with his mind completely seized by three qualities of the unrighteous, is destined for the states of woe, for hell, to remain for an aeon, incurable. What are the three? Evil desire, evil friendship, and having come to a stop midway after achieving only a minor distinction. Bhikkhus, Devadatta, overcome and with his mind completely seized by these three qualities of the unrighteous, is destined for the states of woe, for hell, to remain for an aeon, incurable.

“Mā jātu koci lokasmiṃ, pāpiccho udapajjatha;

Tadamināpi [T 2.0204] jānātha, pāpicchānaṃ yathāgati.

May no one in the world with evil desires ever arise. By this, too, you should know the destination of those with evil desires.

“Paṇḍitoti samaññāto, bhāvitattoti sammato;

Jalaṃva yasasā aṭṭhā, devadattoti me sutaṃ.

‘Known as “wise,” considered as “one with a developed mind,” he stood blazing with fame’—thus have I heard of Devadatta.

“So pamādaṃ anuciṇṇo, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ;

Avīcinirayaṃ patto, catudvāraṃ bhayānakaṃ.

He, having repeatedly practiced negligence and having assailed the Tathāgata, has reached the Avīci hell, dreadful with its four gates.

“Aduṭṭhassa hi yo dubbhe, pāpakammaṃ akrubbato;

Tameva pāpaṃ phusati, duṭṭhacittaṃ anādaraṃ.

Whoever harms one who is not corrupt, one who does no evil deed, that evil befalls that very one who is disrespectful and has a corrupt mind.

“Samuddaṃ visakumbhena, yo maññeyya padūsituṃ padussituṃ (ka.);

Na so tena padūseyya, bhesmā hi udadhī mahā.

Whoever might think to pollute the ocean with a pot of poison—he would not pollute it with that, for the great ocean is indeed formidable.

“Evameva [M 0.0367] tathāgataṃ, yo vādenupahiṃsati;

Samaggataṃ sammāgataṃ (sī.), samagataṃ (syā.) santacittaṃ, vādo tamhi na rūhati.

In the same way, whoever harms the Tathāgata—who has reached harmony and has a peaceful mind—with argumentative speech, that speech does not take root in him.

“Tādisaṃ mittaṃ krubbetha kubbetha (sī. syā.), tañca sevetha paṇḍito;

Yassa maggānugo bhikkhu, khayaṃ dukkhassa pāpuṇe”ti.

One should make such a one a friend, and a wise person should associate with him; a bhikkhu who follows his path may attain the destruction of suffering.

Upālipañhā

The Questions of Upāli

351. Atha kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “saṅgharāji saṅgharājīti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgharāji hoti, no ca saṅghabhedo? Kittāvatā ca pana saṅgharāji ceva hoti [T 2.0205] saṅghabhedo cā”ti?

351. Then the Venerable Upāli approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Upāli said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, it is said, ‘a crack in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha.’ To what extent, Venerable Sir, is there a crack in the Saṅgha, but not a schism in the Saṅgha? And to what extent is there both a crack in the Saṅgha and a schism in the Saṅgha?”

“Ekato[V 0.0344], upāli, eko hoti, ekato dve, catuttho anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti, no ca saṅghabhedo. Ekato, upāli, dve honti, ekato dve, pañcamo anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti, no ca saṅghabhedo. Ekato, upāli, dve honti, ekato tayo, chaṭṭho anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti, no ca saṅghabhedo[P 2.0204]. Ekato, upāli, tayo honti, ekato tayo, sattamo anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti, no ca saṅghabhedo. Ekato, upāli, tayo honti, ekato cattāro, aṭṭhamo anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti, no ca saṅghabhedo. Ekato, upāli, cattāro honti, ekato cattāro, navamo anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti[T 2.0206]. Evaṃ [M 0.0368] kho, upāli, saṅgharāji ceva hoti saṅghabhedo ca. Navannaṃ vā, upāli, atirekanavannaṃ vā saṅgharāji ceva hoti saṅghabhedo ca. Na kho, upāli, bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ bhindati, api ca bhedāya parakkamati, na sikkhamānā saṅghaṃ bhindati…pe… na sāmaṇero saṅghaṃ bhindati, na sāmaṇerī saṅghaṃ bhindati, na upāsako saṅghaṃ bhindati, na upāsikā saṅghaṃ bhindati, api ca bhedāya parakkamati. Bhikkhu kho, upāli, pakatatto, samānasaṃvāsako, samānasīmāyaṃ ṭhito, saṅghaṃ bhindatī”ti.

“Upāli, on one side there is one, on the other side there are two; a fourth announces and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction; accept this, approve of this.’ Even in this way, Upāli, there is discord in the Sangha, but not a schism in the Sangha. Upāli, on one side there are two, on the other side there are two; a fifth announces and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction; accept this, approve of this.’ Even in this way, Upāli, there is discord in the Sangha, but not a schism in the Sangha. Upāli, on one side there are two, on the other side there are three; a sixth announces and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction; accept this, approve of this.’ Even in this way, Upāli, there is discord in the Sangha, but not a schism in the Sangha. Upāli, on one side there are three, on the other side there are three; a seventh announces and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction; accept this, approve of this.’ Even in this way, Upāli, there is discord in the Sangha, but not a schism in the Sangha. Upāli, on one side there are three, on the other side there are four; an eighth announces and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction; accept this, approve of this.’ Even in this way, Upāli, there is discord in the Sangha, but not a schism in the Sangha. Upāli, on one side there are four, on the other side there are four; a ninth announces and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction; accept this, approve of this.’ In this way, Upāli, there is both discord in the Sangha and a schism in the Sangha. With nine, Upāli, or more than nine, there is both discord in the Sangha and a schism in the Sangha. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhunī does not split the Sangha, but she may strive for a split. A probationary nun does not split the Sangha… a male novice does not split the Sangha, a female novice does not split the Sangha, a male lay follower does not split the Sangha, a female lay follower does not split the Sangha, but they may strive for a split. Indeed, Upāli, it is a bhikkhu who is in a normal state, sharing the same communion, residing within the same boundary, who splits the Sangha.”

352. a. ni. 10.37 “Saṅghabhedo saṅghabhedoti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgho bhinno hotī”ti?

352. “‘A schism of the Sangha, a schism of the Sangha,’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Sangha split?”

“Idhupāli, bhikkhū adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpenti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāpattiṃ āpattīti dīpenti, āpattiṃ anāpattīti [V 0.0345] dīpenti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpenti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpenti, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā [T 2.0207] āpattīti dīpenti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpenti, duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhulā āpattīti dīpenti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpenti. Te imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi apakassanti, avapakassanti, āveniṃ āveṇi (sī.), āveṇikaṃ (syā.) uposathaṃ karonti, āveniṃ pavāraṇaṃ karonti, āveniṃ saṅghakammaṃ karonti. Ettāvatā kho, upāli, saṅgho bhinno hotī”ti.

“Here, Upāli, monks explain what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma; they explain what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, and the Vinaya as not the Vinaya; they explain what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; they explain what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as not practiced by the Tathāgata; they explain what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as not laid down by the Tathāgata; they explain a non-offense as an offense, and an offense as a non-offense; they explain a light offense as a grave offense, and a grave offense as a light offense; they explain an offense with a remainder as an offense without a remainder, and an offense without a remainder as an offense with a remainder; they explain a gross offense as a non-gross offense, and a non-gross offense as a gross offense. By these eighteen grounds, they draw away, they drag down, they perform the Uposatha separately, they perform the Pavāraṇā separately, they perform acts of the Sangha separately. To this extent, Upāli, the Sangha is split.”

353. a. ni. 10.37 “Saṅghasāmaggī saṅghasāmaggīti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgho samaggo hotī”ti? “Idhupāli, bhikkhū adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti, vinayaṃ vinayoti [M 0.0369] dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpenti, āpattiṃ āpattīti dīpenti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpenti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpenti, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpenti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpenti[T 2.0208], duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpenti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpenti. Te imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi na apakassanti, na avapakassanti, na āveniṃ uposathaṃ karonti, na āveniṃ pavāraṇaṃ karonti, na āveniṃ saṅghakammaṃ karonti. Ettāvatā kho, upāli, saṅgho samaggo hotī”ti.

353. “‘Concord of the Sangha, concord of the Sangha,’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Sangha in concord?” “Here, Upāli, monks declare what is not-Dhamma as ‘not-Dhamma,’ and what is Dhamma as ‘Dhamma’; they declare what is not-Vinaya as ‘not-Vinaya,’ and what is Vinaya as ‘Vinaya’; they declare what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as ‘not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata,’ and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as ‘spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata’; they declare what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as ‘not practiced by the Tathāgata,’ and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as ‘practiced by the Tathāgata’; they declare what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as ‘not laid down by the Tathāgata,’ and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as ‘laid down by the Tathāgata’; they declare a non-offense as ‘a non-offense,’ and an offense as ‘an offense’; they declare a light offense as ‘a light offense,’ and a grave offense as ‘a grave offense’; they declare an offense with a remainder as ‘an offense with a remainder,’ and an offense without a remainder as ‘an offense without a remainder’; they declare a gross offense as ‘a gross offense,’ and a non-gross offense as ‘a non-gross offense.’ On these eighteen grounds, they do not draw away, they do not drag down; they do not perform the Uposatha separately, they do not perform the Pavāraṇā separately, and they do not perform a formal act of the Sangha separately. To this extent, Upāli, the Sangha is in concord.”

354. “Samaggaṃ pana, bhante, saṅghaṃ bhinditvā kiṃ so pasavatī”ti? “Samaggaṃ kho, upāli, saṅghaṃ bhinditvā kappaṭṭhikaṃ kibbisaṃ pasavati, kappaṃ nirayamhi paccatī”ti.

354. “Venerable sir, what does one produce by splitting a concordant Saṅgha?” “Upāli, by splitting a concordant Saṅgha, one produces evil that lasts for an aeon; one is cooked in hell for an aeon.”

itivu. 18; a. ni. 10.39 “Āpāyiko [P 2.0205] nerayiko, kappaṭṭho saṅghabhedako;

Vaggarato adhammaṭṭho, yogakkhemā padhaṃsati;

Saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ bhinditvā, kappaṃ nirayamhi paccatī”ti.

“Destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon is the Saṅgha-divider; delighting in factions, established in what is not the Dhamma, one falls away from security from bondage. Having split the concordant Saṅgha, one is cooked in hell for an aeon.”

“Bhinnaṃ [V 0.0346] pana, bhante, saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ katvā kiṃ so pasavatī”ti? “Bhinnaṃ kho, upāli, saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ katvā brahmaṃ puññaṃ pasavati, kappaṃ saggamhi modatī”ti.

“Venerable Sir, what does one generate by making a split Saṅgha harmonious?” “Indeed, Upāli, by making a split Saṅgha harmonious, one generates sublime merit and rejoices in heaven for an aeon.”

ittivu. 18; a. ni. 10.40 “Sukhā saṅghassa sāmaggī, samaggānañca anuggaho;

Samaggarato dhammaṭṭho, yogakkhemā na dhaṃsati;

Saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ katvāna, kappaṃ saggamhi modatī”ti.

“Happiness is the harmony of the Saṅgha, and the support of those who are harmonious. Delighting in harmony, established in the Dhamma, one does not fall away from the security from bondage. Having made the Saṅgha harmonious, one rejoices in heaven for an aeon.”

355. pari. 459 “Siyā nu kho, bhante, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho”ti? “Siyā, upāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho”ti.

355. “Venerable Sir, could it be that a Saṅgha-splitter is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable?” “It could be, Upāli. A Saṅgha-splitter is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable.”

pari. 459 “Siyā [M 0.0370] siyā nu kho (syā. kaṃ.) pana, bhante, saṅghabhedako [T 2.0209] na āpāyiko, na nerayiko, na kappaṭṭho, na atekiccho”ti? “Siyā, upāli, saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko, na nerayiko, na kappaṭṭho, na atekiccho”ti.

“Venerable Sir, could it be that a Saṅgha-splitter is not destined for the plane of misery, not destined for hell, not remaining for an aeon, and not incurable?” “It could be, Upāli, that a Saṅgha-splitter is not destined for the plane of misery, not destined for hell, not remaining for an aeon, and not incurable.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho”ti? “Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti. Tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhi, bhede adhammadiṭṭhi, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho, upāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho.

“Venerable Sir, which Saṅgha-splitter is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable?” “Here, Upāli, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma. Regarding that matter, he holds the view that it is not the Dhamma; regarding the schism, he holds the view that it is not the Dhamma. Having established his view, having established his preference, having established his inclination, and having established his disposition, he makes an announcement and causes voting tickets to be taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Take this, approve of this.’ Indeed, Upāli, this Saṅgha-splitter is also destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti. Tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhi, bhede dhammadiṭṭhi, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho, upāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma. Regarding that matter, he holds the view that it is not the Dhamma; but regarding the schism, he holds the view that it is the Dhamma. Having established his view, having established his preference, having established his inclination, and having established his disposition, he makes an announcement and causes voting tickets to be taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Take this, approve of this.’ Indeed, Upāli, this Saṅgha-splitter is also destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti. Tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhi, bhede vematiko, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ [V 0.0347] rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho, upāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma. Regarding that matter, he holds the view that it is not the Dhamma; regarding the schism, he is doubtful. Having established his view, having established his preference, having established his inclination, and having established his disposition, he makes an announcement and causes a voting ticket to be taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Take this, approve of this.’ Indeed, Upāli, this Saṅgha-splitter is also destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti. Tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi, bhede [T 2.0210] adhammadiṭṭhi…pe… (tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi bhede dhammadiṭṭhi) ( ) syāmapotthake natthi, vimativinodanīṭīkāya sameti. Tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi bhede vematiko. Tasmiṃ vematiko bhede adhammadiṭṭhi. Tasmiṃ vematiko bhede dhammadiṭṭhi. Tasmiṃ vematiko bhede vematiko vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho, upāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma. Regarding that matter, he holds the view that it is the Dhamma; regarding the schism, he holds the view that it is not the Dhamma… (Regarding that matter, he holds the view that it is the Dhamma; regarding the schism, he holds the view that it is the Dhamma.) Regarding that matter, he holds the view that it is the Dhamma; regarding the schism, he is doubtful. Regarding that matter, he is doubtful; regarding the schism, he holds the view that it is not the Dhamma. Regarding that matter, he is doubtful; regarding the schism, he holds the view that it is the Dhamma. Regarding that matter, he is doubtful; regarding the schism, he is doubtful. Having established his view, having established his preference, having established his inclination, and having established his disposition, he makes an announcement and causes a voting ticket to be taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s teaching. Take this, approve of this.’ Indeed, Upāli, this Saṅgha-splitter is also destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for an aeon, and incurable.”

“Puna [M 0.0371] caparaṃ, upāli, bhikkhu dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti…pe… avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti… vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti… abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti… bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti… anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti… āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti… apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti… paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti… anāpattiṃ āpattīti dīpeti… āpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti… lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti… garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti… sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpeti… anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti… aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti… tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhi, bhede adhammadiṭṭhi…pe… tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhi, bhede dhammadiṭṭhi [T 2.0211]… tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhi, bhede vematiko… tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi, bhede adhammadiṭṭhi… (tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi, bhede dhammadiṭṭhi) ( ) syāmapotthake natthi … tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi, bhede vematiko… tasmiṃ vematiko, bhede adhammadiṭṭhi… tasmiṃ vematiko, bhede dhammadiṭṭhi… tasmiṃ vematiko, bhede vematiko, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho, upāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko, nerayiko, kappaṭṭho, atekiccho”ti.

‐Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is Dhamma to be non-Dhamma… declares what is non-Vinaya to be Vinaya; declares what is Vinaya to be non-Vinaya; declares what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata to be spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; declares what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata to be not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; declares what was not habitually practiced by the Tathāgata to be habitually practiced by the Tathāgata; declares what was habitually practiced by the Tathāgata to be not habitually practiced by the Tathāgata; declares what was not laid down by the Tathāgata to be laid down by the Tathāgata; declares what was laid down by the Tathāgata to be not laid down by the Tathāgata; declares a non-offense to be an offense; declares an offense to be a non-offense; declares a light offense to be a grave offense; declares a grave offense to be a light offense; declares an offense with residue to be an offense without residue; declares an offense without residue to be an offense with residue; declares a gross offense to be a non-gross offense; declares a non-gross offense to be a gross offense. Regarding that, he has the view of non-Dhamma; in the schism, he has the view of non-Dhamma… Regarding that, he has the view of non-Dhamma; in the schism, he has the view of Dhamma… Regarding that, he has the view of non-Dhamma; in the schism, he is doubtful… Regarding that, he has the view of Dhamma; in the schism, he has the view of non-Dhamma… Regarding that, he has the view of Dhamma; in the schism, he has the view of Dhamma… Regarding that, he has the view of Dhamma; in the schism, he is doubtful… Regarding that, he is doubtful; in the schism, he has the view of non-Dhamma… Regarding that, he is doubtful; in the schism, he has the view of Dhamma… Regarding that, he is doubtful; in the schism, he is doubtful. Misrepresenting his view, misrepresenting his approval, misrepresenting his preference, misrepresenting his intention, he makes an announcement and has voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher's instruction; take this, approve of this.’ Indeed, Upāli, this Sangha-splitter is bound for the states of woe, bound for hell, destined to remain for an eon, and incurable.‑

“Katamo pana, bhante, saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko, na nerayiko, na kappaṭṭho[P 2.0206], na atekiccho”ti? “Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti. Tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi, bhede dhammadiṭṭhi[V 0.0348], avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, avinidhāya khantiṃ, avinidhāya ruciṃ, avinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho, upāli, saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko, na nerayiko, na kappaṭṭho, na atekiccho.

“Venerable sir, what kind of Sangha-splitter is not bound for the states of woe, not bound for hell, not destined to remain for an eon, and not incurable?” “Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu explains non-Dhamma as Dhamma. Regarding that, he has the view that it is Dhamma, and in the schism, he has the view that it is Dhamma. Without being established in his view, without being established in his approval, without being established in his preference, without being established in his disposition, he makes an announcement and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Take this, approve of this.’ This Sangha-splitter, Upāli, is also not bound for the states of woe, not bound for hell, not destined to remain for an eon, and not incurable.

“Puna [M 0.0372] caparaṃ, upāli, bhikkhu dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhi, bhede dhammadiṭṭhi, avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, avinidhāya khantiṃ, avinidhāya ruciṃ, avinidhāya bhāvaṃ, anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti – ‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo, idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti. Ayampi kho[T 2.0212], upāli, saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko, na nerayiko, na kappaṭṭho, na atekiccho”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu explains Dhamma as non-Dhamma… he explains a gross offense as a non-gross offense. Regarding that, he has the view that it is Dhamma, and in the schism, he has the view that it is Dhamma. Without being established in his view, without being established in his approval, without being established in his preference, without being established in his disposition, he makes an announcement and has the voting tickets taken, saying: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction. Take this, approve of this.’ This Sangha-splitter, Upāli, is also not bound for the states of woe, not bound for hell, not destined to remain for an eon, and not incurable.”

Tatiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The third recitation section is concluded.

Saṅghabhedakakkhandhako sattamo.

The seventh, the Chapter on Schism in the Sangha, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Anupiye abhiññātā, sukhumālo na icchati;

Kasā vapā abhi ninne, niddhā lāve ca ubbahe.

At Anupiya, the well-known ones; the delicate one does not wish for it. Ploughing, sowing, irrigating, weeding, reaping, and carrying.

Puñjamaddapalālañca, bhusaophuṇanīhare;

Āyatimpi na khīyanti, pitaro ca pitāmahā.

Heaping, threshing, straw, and chaff, winnowing, and carrying away; in the future it is not exhausted, for fathers and grandfathers.

Bhaddiyo anuruddho ca, ānando bhagu kimilo;

Sakyamāno ca kosambiṃ, parihāyi kakudhena ca.

Bhaddiya and Anuruddha, Ānanda, Bhagu, Kimila; the pride of the Sakyans, and at Kosambī; the decline, and with Kakudha.

Pakāsesi pituno ca, purise silaṃ nāḷāgiriṃ;

Tikapañcagaruko kho, bhindi thullaccayena ca;

Tayo aṭṭha puna tīṇi, rāji bhedā siyā nu khoti.

He revealed, and his father; the men, and Nāḷāgiri; the triad, the five points, the grave offense; the split by a grave offense; three, eight, and again three; the scratch, the schism, and ‘Could it be?’

Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter on Schism in the Sangha is concluded.

8. Vattakkhandhakaṃ

8. The Section on Duties

1. Āgantukavattakathā

1. The Discourse on the Observances for Incoming Bhikkhus

356. Tena [T 2.0213][P 2.0207][M 0.0373][V 0.0349] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āgantukā bhikkhū saupāhanāpi ārāmaṃ pavisanti, chattapaggahitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisanti, oguṇṭhitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisanti, sīsepi cīvaraṃ karitvā ārāmaṃ pavisanti, pānīyenapi pāde dhovanti, vuḍḍhatarepi āvāsike bhikkhū na abhivādenti, napi senāsanaṃ pucchanti. Aññataropi āgantuko bhikkhu anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vihāraṃ ghaṭikaṃ ugghāṭetvā kavāṭaṃ paṇāmetvā sahasā pāvisi. Tassa uparipiṭṭhito uparipiṭṭhato (?) ahi khandhe papati. So bhīto vissaramakāsi. Bhikkhū upadhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, vissaramakāsī”ti? Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āgantukā bhikkhū saupāhanāpi ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, chattapaggahitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, oguṇṭhitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, sīsepi cīvaraṃ karitvā ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, pānīyenapi pāde dhovissanti, vuḍḍhatarepi āvāsike bhikkhū na abhivādessanti, napi senāsanaṃ pucchissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ [T 2.0214] kira, bhikkhave, “āgantukā bhikkhū saupāhanāpi ārāmaṃ pavisanti, chattapaggahitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisanti, oguṇṭhitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisanti, sīsepi cīvaraṃ karitvā ārāmaṃ pavisanti, pānīyenipi pāde dhovanti, vuḍḍhatarepi āvāsike bhikkhū na abhivādenti, napi senāsanaṃ pucchantīti. Saccaṃ bhagavāti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma bhikkhave āgantukā bhikkhū saupāhanāpi ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, chattapaggahitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, oguṇṭhitāpi ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, sīsepi cīvaraṃ karitvā ārāmaṃ pavisissanti, pānīyenapi pāde dhovissanti, vuḍḍhatarepi āvāsike [V 0.0350] bhikkhū na abhivādessanti, napi senāsanaṃ pucchissanti, netaṃ bhikkhave appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

356. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, visiting monks entered the monastery wearing sandals, entered the monastery holding up umbrellas, entered the monastery with their heads covered, entered the monastery with a robe placed on their heads, washed their feet with drinking water, did not pay respect to the senior resident monks, and did not ask about lodging. A certain visiting monk unfastened the bolt of an unoccupied dwelling, pushed open the door, and entered abruptly. A snake fell from above the door-frame onto his shoulder. Terrified, he screamed. The monks rushed over and said to him, “Why did you scream, friend?” Then that monk related the matter to the monks. Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, expressed displeasure, and spoke disparagingly, “How indeed can visiting monks enter the monastery wearing sandals, enter holding up umbrellas, enter with their heads covered, enter with a robe placed on their heads, wash their feet with drinking water, not pay respect to the senior resident monks, and not ask about lodging?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that visiting monks enter the monastery wearing sandals, enter holding up umbrellas, enter with their heads covered, enter with a robe placed on their heads, wash their feet with drinking water, do not pay respect to the senior resident monks, and do not ask about lodging?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can visiting monks enter the monastery wearing sandals, enter holding up umbrellas, enter with their heads covered, enter with a robe placed on their heads, wash their feet with drinking water, not pay respect to the senior resident monks, and not ask about lodging? Monks, this is not for the confidence of the unconfident…” Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

357. “Tena [M 0.0374] hi, bhikkhave, āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā āgantukehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Āgantukena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ‘idāni ārāmaṃ pavisissāmī’ti upāhanā omuñcitvā [P 2.0208] nīcaṃ katvā papphoṭetvā gahetvā chattaṃ apanāmetvā sīsaṃ vivaritvā sīse cīvaraṃ vivaritvā cīvaraṃ (ka.) khandhe katvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena ārāmo pavisitabbo. Ārāmaṃ pavisantena sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘kattha [T 2.0215] āvāsikā bhikkhū paṭikkamantī’ti? Yattha āvāsikā bhikkhū paṭikkamanti – upaṭṭhānasālāya vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā – tattha gantvā ekamantaṃ patto nikkhipitabbo; ekamantaṃ cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; patirūpaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā nisīditabbaṃ; pānīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ – ‘katamaṃ pānīyaṃ, katamaṃ paribhojanīya’nti? Sace pānīyena attho hoti, pānīyaṃ gahetvā pātabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyena attho hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ gahetvā pādā dhovitabbā. Pāde dhovantena ekena hatthena udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ, ekena hatthena pādā dhovitabbā. Teneva udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ yena hatthena udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ (syā.) na teneva hatthena pādā dhovitabbā. Upāhanapuñchanacoḷakaṃ pucchitvā upāhanā puñchitabbā. Upāhanā puñchantena paṭhamaṃ sukkhena coḷakena puñchitabbā, pacchā allena. Upāhanāpuñchanacoḷakaṃ dhovitvā pīḷetvā (syā.) ekamantaṃ vissajjetabbaṃ.

357. “Well then, monks, I will lay down the duties for visiting monks, so that visiting monks may conduct themselves properly. A visiting monk, monks, having thought, ‘Now I will enter the monastery,’ should take off his sandals, lower them, shake them out, and carry them. He should lower his umbrella, uncover his head, place the robe from his head onto his shoulder, and enter the monastery carefully and without haste. Upon entering the monastery, he should note where the resident monks are staying—whether in the assembly hall, a pavilion, or at the foot of a tree. He should go there, place his bowl in a suitable place, place his robe in a suitable place, take a suitable seat, and sit down. He should ask for drinking water and water for use, inquiring, ‘Which is drinking water, and which is water for use?’ If he needs drinking water, he should take it and drink. If he needs water for use, he should take it and wash his feet. While washing his feet, he should pour water with one hand and wash his feet with the other. He should ask for a cloth to wipe his sandals and then wipe them. When wiping his sandals, he should first wipe them with a dry cloth and then with a damp one. After washing the sandal-wiping cloth, he should spread it out in a suitable place.”

“Sace āvāsiko bhikkhu vuḍḍho hoti, abhivādetabbo. Sace navako hoti, abhivādāpetabbo. Senāsanaṃ pucchitabbaṃ – ‘katamaṃ me senāsanaṃ pāpuṇātī’ti? Ajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā pucchitabbaṃ, gocaro pucchitabbo, agocaro pucchitabbo, sekkhasammatāni sekhasammatāni (ka.) kulāni pucchitabbāni[T 2.0216], vaccaṭṭhānaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, passāvaṭṭhānaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, pānīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, kattaradaṇḍo pucchitabbo, saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṃ pucchitabbaṃ – ‘kaṃ kālaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, kaṃ kālaṃ nikkhamitabba’nti? Sace vihāro anajjhāvuṭṭho hoti, kavāṭaṃ ākoṭetvā muhuttaṃ āgametvā ghaṭikaṃ ugghāṭetvā kavāṭaṃ paṇāmetvā bahi ṭhitena nilloketabbo.

“If the resident monk is senior, he should be paid respect to. If he is junior, he should receive respect. The lodging should be asked about: ‘Which lodging is assigned to me?’ It should be asked whether it is occupied or unoccupied. The alms-resort should be asked about; the non-alms-resort should be asked about. Families designated for trainees should be asked about. The place for defecation should be asked about; the place for urination should be asked about. Drinking water should be asked about; water for use should be asked about. The staff should be asked about. The Saṅgha's convention should be asked about: ‘At what time should one enter, at what time should one leave?’ If the dwelling is unoccupied, one should knock on the door, wait a moment, lift the bolt, push open the door, and look inside while standing outside.”

“Sace [M 0.0375] vihāro uklāpo hoti, mañce vā mañco āropito hoti, pīṭhe vā pīṭhaṃ āropitaṃ hoti, senāsanaṃ upari puñjīkataṃ puñjakitaṃ (ka.) hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. mahāva. 66-67 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ) Vihāraṃ sodhentena [V 0.0351] paṭhamaṃ bhūmattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ [P 2.0209] nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā [T 2.0217] pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti ūhaññīti (sī. syā.). Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

“If the dwelling is littered, if a bed is placed upon a bed, if a bench is placed upon a bench, if the lodging is piled high, if one is capable, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first the floor covering should be taken out and set aside; the bed legs should be taken out and set aside; the mattress and pillow should be taken out and set aside; the sitting cloth and underlay should be taken out and set aside; the bed should be lowered carefully, without scraping it or knocking it against the door panel and doorpost, taken out, and set aside; the bench should be lowered carefully, without scraping it or knocking it against the door panel and doorpost, taken out, and set aside; the spittoon should be taken out and set aside; the leaning board should be taken out and set aside. If there is a cobweb in the dwelling, it should first be removed from the ceiling, and the corners of the window openings should be wiped. If a wall prepared with red ochre is moldy, a cloth should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If a floor prepared with black coloring is moldy, a cloth should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is unprepared, it should be sprinkled with water and swept, bearing in mind, ‘May the dwelling not be afflicted by dust.’ The sweepings should be collected and discarded in a suitable place.”

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne yathāpaññattaṃ (sī. syā.), yathābhāgaṃ (ka.) paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne yathābhāgaṃ (syā. ka.) ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāṭhāne yathābhāgaṃ (syā. ka.) paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāṭhāne yathābhāgaṃ (syā. ka.) paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathābhāgaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathābhāgaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathābhāgaṃ ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathābhāgaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena [M 0.0376] ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā [T 2.0218] patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

“The floor covering should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and spread in its usual place. The bed legs should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in their usual place. The bed, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be lowered and brought back carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door-leaf and door-post, and spread in its usual place. The chair, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be lowered and brought back carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door-leaf and door-post, and spread in its usual place. The mattress and pillow should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and spread in their proper arrangement. The sitting cloth and underlay should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and spread in their proper arrangement. The spittoon should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its proper place. The leaning board should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its proper place. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, having taken it with one hand and felt under the bed or under the chair with the other, the bowl should be put down. And the bowl should not be placed on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, having taken it with one hand and wiped the robe-pole or the robe-line with the other, making a fold on the near side with the end on the far side, the robe should be put away.”

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā[V 0.0352]. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

“If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.”

“Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ [P 2.0210] hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ yathā āgantukehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabba”nti.

“If the monastic precinct is dirty, the monastic precinct should be swept. If the gateway is dirty, the gateway should be swept. If the service hall is dirty, the service hall should be swept. If the fire-room is dirty, the fire-room should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing jar, water should be poured into the rinsing jar. This, bhikkhus, is the duty for visiting bhikkhus, which should be properly practiced by visiting bhikkhus.”

2. Āvāsikavattakathā

2. The Discourse on the Duties of Resident Bhikkhus

358. Tena [T 2.0219] kho pana samayena āvāsikā bhikkhū āgantuke bhikkhū disvā neva āsanaṃ paññapenti, na pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipanti, na paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhanti, na pānīyena pucchanti na pānīyena pucchanti, na paribhojanīyena pucchanti (syā. kaṃ.), na vuḍḍhatarepi āgantuke bhikkhū abhivādenti, na senāsanaṃ paññapenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āvāsikā bhikkhū āgantuke bhikkhū disvā neva āsanaṃ paññapessanti, na pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipissanti, na [M 0.0377] paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahissanti, na pānīyena pucchissanti, vuḍḍhatarepi āgantuke bhikkhū na abhivādessanti, na senāsanaṃ paññapessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kiraṃ, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

358. At that time, the resident bhikkhus, upon seeing visiting bhikkhus, neither prepared seats, nor placed nearby water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet, nor went out to meet them and receive their bowl and robe, nor inquired with an offer of drinking water, nor paid homage even to the more senior visiting bhikkhus, nor prepared their lodging. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How is it that the resident bhikkhus, upon seeing visiting bhikkhus, will neither prepare seats, nor place nearby water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet, nor go out to meet them and receive their bowl and robe, nor inquire with an offer of drinking water, nor pay homage even to the more senior visiting bhikkhus, nor prepare their lodging?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, bhikkhus…?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:

359. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Āvāsikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā āgantukaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuḍḍhataraṃ disvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ[T 2.0220], paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, pānīyena pucchitabbo pānīyena pucchitabbo, paribhojanīyena pucchitabbo (syā.). Sace ussahati, upāhanā puñchitabbā. Upāhanā puñchantena paṭhamaṃ sukkhena coḷakena puñchitabbā, pacchā allena. Upāhanāpuñchanacoḷakaṃ dhovitvā dhovitvā pīḷetvā (syā.) ekamantaṃ vissajjetabbaṃ.

359. “Therefore, bhikkhus, I will lay down the duties for resident bhikkhus, according to which resident bhikkhus should conduct themselves. A resident bhikkhu, bhikkhus, upon seeing a visiting bhikkhu who is more senior, should prepare a seat; water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby; having gone out to meet him, his bowl and robe should be received; he should be asked about drinking water. If he is able, the sandals should be wiped. When wiping the sandals, they should first be wiped with a dry cloth, and afterwards with a wet one. The cloth for wiping the sandals should be washed and spread out in a suitable place.”

“Āgantuko [V 0.0353] bhikkhu vuḍḍhataro abhivādetabbo. Senāsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ – ‘etaṃ te senāsanaṃ pāpuṇātī’ti. Ajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā ācikkhitabbaṃ. Gocaro ācikkhitabbo. Agocaro ācikkhitabbo. Sekkhasammatāni kulāni ācikkhitabbāni. Vaccaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Passāvaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Pānīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Paribhojanīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Kattaradaṇḍo ācikkhitabbo. Saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘imaṃ kālaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, imaṃ kālaṃ nikkhamitabba’nti[P 2.0211].

“A visiting bhikkhu who is senior should be venerated. A lodging should be prepared, saying, ‘This lodging is for you.’ He should be told whether it has been previously inhabited or not. The alms-resort should be pointed out. What is not an alms-resort should be pointed out. Families designated as being ‘in training’ should be pointed out. The latrine should be pointed out. The place for urination should be pointed out. Drinking water should be pointed out. Water for use should be pointed out. The walking stick should be pointed out. The Saṅgha’s established agreement should be pointed out: ‘One should enter at this time; one should depart at this time.’”

“Sace navako hoti, nisinnakeneva ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘atra pattaṃ nikkhipāhi, atra cīvaraṃ nikkhipāhi, idaṃ āsanaṃ nisīdāhī’ti. Pānīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Paribhojanīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Upāhanāpuñchanacoḷakaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Āgantuko bhikkhu navako abhivādāpetabbo. Senāsanaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘etaṃ [T 2.0221] te senāsanaṃ pāpuṇātī’ti. Ajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā ācikkhitabbaṃ. Gocaro ācikkhitabbo. Agocaro ācikkhitabbo. Sekkhasammatāni kulāni ācikkhitabbāni. Vaccaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Passāvaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Pānīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Paribhojanīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Kattaradaṇḍo ācikkhitabbo. Saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘imaṃ kālaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, imaṃ kālaṃ nikkhamitabba’nti. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave[M 0.0378], āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ yathā āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabba”nti.

“If he is a junior, he should be instructed while one is seated: ‘Place your bowl here, place your robe here, sit on this seat.’ Drinking water should be pointed out. Water for use should be pointed out. The cloth for wiping sandals should be pointed out. The visiting junior bhikkhu should be made to venerate. The lodging should be pointed out, saying, ‘This lodging is for you.’ He should be told whether it has been previously inhabited or not. The alms-resort should be pointed out. What is not an alms-resort should be pointed out. Families designated as being ‘in training’ should be pointed out. The latrine should be pointed out. The place for urination should be pointed out. Drinking water should be pointed out. Water for use should be pointed out. The walking stick should be pointed out. The Saṅgha’s established agreement should be pointed out: ‘One should enter at this time; one should depart at this time.’ This, bhikkhus, is the duty for resident bhikkhus, which should be properly observed by them.”

3. Gamikavattakathā

3. The Discourse on the Duties for Traveling Bhikkhus

360. Tena kho pana samayena gamikā bhikkhū dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ appaṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ vivaritvā senāsanaṃ anāpucchā pakkamanti. Dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ nassati. Senāsanaṃ aguttaṃ hoti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma gamikā bhikkhū dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ appaṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ vivaritvā senāsanaṃ anāpucchā pakkamissanti! Dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ nassati. Senāsanaṃ aguttaṃ hotī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

360. Now at that time, traveling bhikkhus departed without putting away the wooden articles and earthenware articles, having opened the doors and windows, and without asking leave for the lodging. The wooden articles and earthenware articles were ruined. The lodging was unprotected. Those bhikkhus who were of few wants…pe… complained, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can traveling bhikkhus depart without putting away the wooden articles and earthenware articles, having opened the doors and windows, and without asking leave for the lodging! The wooden articles and earthenware articles are ruined. The lodging is unprotected!” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One…pe… “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus…?” “It is true, Blessed One.” …pe… Having rebuked them…pe… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:

361. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, gamikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā gamikehi [T 2.0222] bhikkhūhi [V 0.0354] sammā vattitabbaṃ. Gamikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā senāsanaṃ āpucchā pakkamitabbaṃ āpucchitabbaṃ (syā.). Sace bhikkhu na hoti, sāmaṇero āpucchitabbo. Sace sāmaṇero na hoti, ārāmiko āpucchitabbo. Sace ārāmiko na hoti, upāsako āpucchitabbo. Sace na hoti bhikkhu vā sāmaṇero vā ārāmiko vā upāsako vā, catūsu pāsāṇesu mañcaṃ paññapetvā mañce mañcaṃ āropetvā pīṭhe pīṭhaṃ āropetvā senāsanaṃ upari puñjaṃ karitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace vihāro ovassati, sace ussahati, chādetabbo, ussukaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – ‘kinti nu kho vihāro chādiyethā’ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, yo deso anovassako hoti, tattha catūsu pāsāṇesu mañcaṃ paññapetvā mañce mañcaṃ āropetvā pīṭhe pīṭhaṃ āropetvā senāsanaṃ upari puñjaṃ karitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace sabbo vihāro ovassati, sace ussahati, senāsanaṃ [T 2.0223] gāmaṃ atiharitabbaṃ, ussukaṃ vā kātabbaṃ [P 2.0212][M 0.0379] – ‘kinti nu kho senāsanaṃ gāmaṃ atihariyethā’ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, ajjhokāse catūsu pāsāṇesu mañcaṃ paññapetvā mañce mañcaṃ āropetvā pīṭhe pīṭhaṃ āropetvā senāsanaṃ upari puñjaṃ karitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā tiṇena vā paṇṇena vā paṭicchādetvā pakkamitabbaṃ – appeva nāma aṅgānipi seseyyunti. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, gamikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ yathā gamikehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabba”nti.

361. “Well then, bhikkhus, I shall lay down the observance for traveling bhikkhus, according to which traveling bhikkhus should properly conduct themselves. A traveling bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should put away the wooden and earthenware articles, close the doors and windows, and depart after asking leave for the lodging. If there is no bhikkhu, a novice should be asked for leave. If there is no novice, a monastery attendant should be asked for leave. If there is no monastery attendant, a lay follower should be asked for leave. If there is no bhikkhu, novice, monastery attendant, or lay follower, he should set up a bed on four stones, place a bed upon a bed, place a bench upon a bench, make a pile of the lodging’s furnishings on top, put away the wooden and earthenware articles, close the doors and windows, and then depart. If the monastery is leaking, and if he is able, it should be roofed, or an effort should be made: ‘How, indeed, might the monastery be roofed?’ If he should obtain this, it is good. If he should not obtain it, in a place that is not rained upon, he should set up a bed on four stones, place a bed upon a bed, place a bench upon a bench, make a pile of the lodging’s furnishings on top, put away the wooden and earthenware articles, close the doors and windows, and then depart. If the entire monastery is leaking, and if he is able, the lodging’s furnishings should be carried to the village, or an effort should be made: ‘How, indeed, might the lodging’s furnishings be carried to the village?’ If he should obtain this, it is good. If he should not obtain it, in an open space, he should set up a bed on four stones, place a bed upon a bed, place a bench upon a bench, make a pile of the lodging’s furnishings on top, put away the wooden and earthenware articles, cover them with grass or leaves, and then depart, thinking: ‘May the component parts at least remain.’ This, bhikkhus, is the observance for traveling bhikkhus, according to which traveling bhikkhus should properly conduct themselves.”

4. Anumodanavattakathā

4. The Discourse on the Observance of Giving Thanks

362. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhattagge na anumodanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bhattagge na anumodissantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattagge anumoditu”nti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho bhattagge anumoditabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā bhattagge anumoditu”nti.

362. Now at that time, monks were not giving a blessing in the refectory. People complained, disparaged, and criticized, saying: “How is it that the Sakyan ascetics do not give a blessing in the refectory?” The monks heard those people complaining, disparaging, and criticizing. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then, on this occasion, in this connection, the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow giving a blessing in the refectory.” Then this thought occurred to those monks: “By whom, indeed, should the blessing be given in the refectory?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then, on this occasion, in this connection, the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow the senior monk to give the blessing in the refectory.”

Tena [V 0.0355] kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti[T 2.0224]. Āyasmā sāriputto saṅghatthero hoti. Bhikkhū – ‘bhagavatā anuññātaṃ therena bhikkhunā bhattagge anumoditu’nti – āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ ekakaṃ ohāya pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto te manusse paṭisammoditvā pacchā ekako agamāsi. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ dūratova ekakaṃ āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “kacci, sāriputta, bhattaṃ iddhaṃ ahosī”ti? “Iddhaṃ kho, bhante, bhattaṃ ahosi; apica maṃ bhikkhū ekakaṃ ohāya pakkantā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattagge catūhi pañcahi therānutherehi bhikkhūhi āgametu”nti.

Now at that time, a certain group was offering a meal to the Sangha. The Venerable Sāriputta was the senior monk of the Sangha. The monks, considering, “The Blessed One has allowed the senior monk to give a blessing in the refectory,” left the Venerable Sāriputta behind alone and departed. Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having spoken words of appreciation to those people, went alone afterwards. The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta coming alone from afar. Having seen him, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Sāriputta, I hope the meal was abundant?” “Venerable sir, the meal was indeed abundant; however, the monks left me behind alone and departed.” Then, on this occasion, in this connection, the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow four or five senior and junior monks to wait in the refectory.”

Tena [M 0.0380] kho pana samayena aññataro thero bhattagge vaccito āgamesi. So vaccaṃ sandhāretuṃ asakkonto mucchito papati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati karaṇīye ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchitvā gantu”nti.

Now at that time, a certain elder monk in the refectory, being afflicted by the need to defecate, waited. Unable to hold in his feces, he fainted and fell. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow that if there is a need, one may go after asking leave of a nearby monk.”

5. Bhattaggavattakathā

5. Discourse on the Conduct in the Refectory

363. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā [P 2.0213] bhattaggaṃ gacchanti, vokkammapi therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ purato purato gacchanti, therepi bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīdanti[T 2.0225], navepi bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhanti, saṅghāṭimpi ottharitvā antaraghare nisīdanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā bhattaggaṃ gacchissanti, vokkammapi therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ purato purato gacchissanti, therepi bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīdissanti, navepi bhikkhū āsanenapi paṭibāhissanti, saṅghāṭimpi ottharitvā antaraghare nisīdissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā bhattaggaṃ gacchanti, vokkammapi therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ purato purato gacchanti, therepi bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīdanti, navepi bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhanti, saṅghāṭimpi ottharitvā antaraghare nisīdantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

363. At that time, the monks of the group of six went to the refectory improperly dressed and robed, and lacking in proper deportment. They walked ahead of the elder monks, bypassing them. They sat down encroaching upon the elder monks and denied seats to the junior monks. They also sat on their outer robes, having spread them out in the village. The monks who were of few wishes… complained, disparaged, and criticized, saying: “How can the monks of the group of six go to the refectory improperly dressed and robed, and lacking in proper deportment? How can they walk ahead of the elder monks, bypassing them? How can they sit down encroaching upon the elder monks and deny seats to the junior monks? How can they also sit on their outer robes, having spread them out in the village?” Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the monks of the group of six go to the refectory improperly dressed and robed, and lacking in proper deportment; that they walk ahead of the elder monks, bypassing them; that they sit down encroaching upon the elder monks and deny seats to the junior monks; and that they also sit on their outer robes, having spread them out in the village?” “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

364. “Tena [V 0.0356] hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ bhattaggavattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā bhikkhūhi bhattagge sammā vattitabbaṃ. Sace ārāme kālo ārocito hoti, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena gāmo pavisitabbo.

364. “Well then, monks, I shall lay down for the monks the code of conduct for the refectory, so that they may conduct themselves properly in the refectory. If the time has been announced in the monastery, one should enter the village properly and without haste, having covered the three circles, having worn the lower robe evenly all around, having tied the waistband, having put on the outer robes as a double layer, having fastened the clasp, and having washed and taken the bowl.

“Na vokkamma therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ purato purato gantabbaṃ. Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare [T 2.0226] gantabbaṃ. Susaṃvutena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Appasaddena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ[M 0.0381]. Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na khambhakatena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ.

“One should not walk in front of elder monks, having bypassed them. One should go within the village well-covered. One should go within the village well-restrained. One should go within the village with eyes cast down. One should not go within the village with robes hitched up. One should not go within the village laughing loudly. One should go within the village with little sound. One should not go within the village swaying the body. One should not go within the village swinging the arms. One should not go within the village shaking the head. One should not go within the village with arms akimbo. One should not go within the village with the head covered. One should not go within the village walking on tiptoe.”

“Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Susaṃvutena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ na ujjagghikāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ, appasaddena antaraghare nisīditabba. Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na khambhakatena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na pallatthikāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Na saṅghāṭiṃ ottharitvā antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ.

One should sit within the village well-covered. One should sit within the village well-restrained. One should sit within the village with eyes cast down. One should not sit within the village with robes hitched up. One should not sit within the village laughing loudly. One should sit within the village with little sound. One should not sit within the village swaying the body. One should not sit within the village swinging the arms. One should not sit within the village shaking the head. One should not sit within the village with arms akimbo. One should not sit within the village with the head covered. One should not sit within the village with knees bound. One should not sit encroaching upon elder monks. Junior monks should not be obstructed from a seat. One should not sit within the village pressing down upon the outer robe.

“Udake diyyamāne ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā udakaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena patto dhovitabbo. Sace udakappaṭiggāhako hoti, nīcaṃ katvā udakappaṭiggahe udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ – mā udakappaṭiggāhako udakena osiñci osiñciyyī (ka.), mā [T 2.0227] sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu osiñciyyiṃsu (ka.), mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcīti. Sace udakappaṭiggāhako [P 2.0214] na hoti, nīcaṃ katvā chamāya udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ – mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcīti.

When water is being given, the water should be received by taking the bowl with both hands. Holding it low, the bowl should be washed well and without scraping it. If there is a water receptacle, holding it low, the water should be poured into the water receptacle, reflecting: 'Let the water receptacle not be splashed with water, let the nearby monks not be splashed with water, let the outer robe not be splashed with water.' If there is no water receptacle, holding it low, the water should be poured onto the ground, reflecting: 'Let the nearby monks not be splashed with water, let the outer robe not be splashed with water.'

“Odane diyyamāne ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā odano paṭiggahetabbo, sūpassa okāso kātabbo. Sace hoti sappi vā telaṃ vā uttaribhaṅgaṃ vā, therena vattabbo – ‘sabbesaṃ [V 0.0357] samakaṃ sampādehī’ti. Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Pattasaññinā piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Samasūpako piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Samatittiko piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo.

When rice is being given, the rice should be received by taking the bowl with both hands; space for the curry should be made. If there is ghee, or oil, or relish, it should be said by the elder monk: 'Make it sufficient equally for all.' Almsfood should be received respectfully. Almsfood should be received with mindfulness of the bowl. Almsfood should be received with an equal amount of curry. Almsfood should be received level with the rim.

“Na tāva therena bhuñjitabbaṃ yāva na sabbesaṃ odano sampatto hoti. Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Pattasaññinā piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Sapadānaṃ piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Samasūpako piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo[M 0.0382]. Na thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍipāto bhuñjitabbo. Na sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vā odanena paṭicchādetabbaṃ bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāya. Na sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilānena attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na ujjhānasaññinā paresaṃ patto oloketabbo. Nātimahanto kabaḷo kātabbo. Parimaṇḍalo ālopo kātabbo. Na [T 2.0228] anāhaṭe kabaḷe mukhadvāraṃ vivaritabbaṃ. Na bhuñjamānena sabbo hattho mukhe pakkhipitabbo. Na sakabaḷena mukhena byāharitabbaṃ. Na piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na avagaṇḍakārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na hatthaniddhunakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na sitthāvakārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na jivhānicchārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na capucapukārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na surusurukārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na hatthanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na pattanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Na oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The elder should not eat until the rice has been served to all. The almsfood should be eaten respectfully. The almsfood should be eaten mindfully of the bowl. The almsfood should be eaten in sequence. The almsfood should be eaten with an equal amount of curry. The almsfood should not be eaten by pressing it down from the top of the heap. Neither curry nor relish should be covered with rice on account of desiring more. Neither curry nor rice should be eaten by one who is not sick, having requested it for one's own sake. The bowl of others should not be looked at with a mind to find fault. A very large morsel should not be made. A round morsel should be made. The mouth should not be opened before the morsel is brought to it. While eating, the whole hand should not be put into the mouth. One should not speak with a mouthful of food. One should not eat by tossing the morsel. One should not eat by biting off morsels. One should not eat by stuffing the cheeks. One should not eat by shaking the hand. One should not eat by scattering grains of rice. One should not eat by sticking out the tongue. One should not eat by making smacking sounds. One should not eat by making slurping sounds. One should not eat by licking the hand. One should not eat by licking the bowl. One should not eat by licking the lips.

“Na sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālako paṭiggahetabbo. Na tāva therena udakaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ yāva na sabbeva bhuttāvino honti. Udake diyyamāne ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā udakaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena patto dhovitabbo. Sace udakappaṭiggāhako hoti, nīcaṃ katvā udakappaṭiggahe udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ – mā udakappaṭiggāhako udakena osiñci, mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcīti. Sace udakappaṭiggāhako na hoti, nīcaṃ katvā chamāya udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ – mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcīti. Na sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

A water vessel should not be received with a hand soiled by food. The elder monk should not receive water until all have finished eating. When water is being given, the water should be received by taking the bowl with both hands. Holding it low, the bowl should be washed well and without scraping it. If there is a water receptacle, holding it low, water should be poured into the water receptacle, reflecting: 'Let the water receptacle not be splashed with water, let the nearby monks not be splashed with water, let the outer robe not be splashed with water.' If there is no water receptacle, holding it low, water should be poured onto the ground, reflecting: 'Let the nearby monks not be splashed with water, let the outer robe not be splashed with water.' Bowl-washing water containing rice grains should not be discarded within the village.

“Nivattantena navakehi bhikkhūhi paṭhamataraṃ nivattitabbaṃ. Pacchā therehi [P 2.0215] suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Susaṃvutena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkhittakāya [T 2.0229] antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Appasaddena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ[V 0.0358]. Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na khambhakatena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ bhattaggavattaṃ yathā bhikkhūhi bhattagge sammā vattitabba”nti.

When returning, the junior monks should return first; the elders should return afterward. One should go within the village well-covered. One should go within the village with restraint. One should go within the village with eyes downcast. One should not go within the village with one's robe hitched up. One should not go within the village laughing loudly. One should go within the village with little sound. One should not go within the village swaying the body. One should not go within the village swinging the arms. One should not go within the village shaking the head. One should not go within the village with arms akimbo. One should not go within the village with the head covered. One should not go within the village walking on tiptoe. This, monks, is the proper conduct for monks in the refectory, which monks should rightly follow.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is Concluded.

6. Piṇḍacārikavattakathā

6. The Discourse on the Conduct for the Alms-Round

365. Tena [M 0.0383] kho pana samayena piṇḍacārikā bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya caranti, asallakkhetvāpi nivesanaṃ pavisanti, asallakkhetvāpi nikkhamanti, atisahasāpi pavisanti, atisahasāpi nikkhamanti, atidūrepi tiṭṭhanti, accāsannepi tiṭṭhanti, aticirampi tiṭṭhanti, atilahumpi nivattanti. Aññataropi piṇḍacāriko bhikkhu asallakkhetvā nivesanaṃ pāvisi. So ca dvāraṃ maññamāno aññataraṃ ovarakaṃ pāvisi. Tasmimpi ovarake itthī naggā uttānā nipannā hoti. Addasā kho so bhikkhu taṃ itthiṃ naggaṃ uttānaṃ nipannaṃ. Disvāna – “nayidaṃ dvāraṃ, ovarakaṃ ida”nti [T 2.0230] tamhā ovarakā nikkhami. Addasā kho tassā itthiyā sāmiko taṃ itthiṃ naggaṃ uttānaṃ nipannaṃ. Disvāna – “iminā me bhikkhunā pajāpatī dūsitā”ti taṃ bhikkhuṃ gahetvā ākoṭesi. Atha kho sā itthī tena saddena paṭibujjhitvā taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, ayya, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ ākoṭesī”ti? “Imināsi tvaṃ bhikkhunā dūsitā”ti? “Nāhaṃ, ayya, iminā bhikkhunā dūsitā; akārako so bhikkhū”ti taṃ bhikkhuṃ muñcāpesi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma piṇḍacārikā bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya carissanti, asallakkhetvāpi nivesanaṃ pavisissanti, asallakkhetvāpi nikkhamissanti, atisahasāpi pavisissanti, atisahasāpi nikkhamissanti, atidūrepi tiṭṭhissanti, accāsannepi tiṭṭhissanti, aticirampi tiṭṭhissanti, atilahumpi nivattissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

365. At that time, monks going for alms were improperly dressed, improperly robed, and not endowed with proper deportment as they went about for alms. They entered dwellings without paying attention, left without paying attention, entered too hastily, left too hastily, stood too far away, stood too close, stood too long, and turned back too quickly. A certain monk going for alms entered a dwelling without paying attention. Thinking it was a door, he entered a private room. In that private room, a woman was lying naked on her back. The monk saw that woman lying naked on her back. Upon seeing her, he thought, 'This is not the door; this is a private room,' and he departed from that private room. The woman’s husband saw her lying naked on her back. Thinking, 'My wife has been defiled by this monk,' he seized that monk and beat him. Then that woman, awakened by the sound, said to the man, 'Sir, why are you beating this monk?' 'You have been defiled by this monk!' 'Sir, I have not been defiled by this monk; that monk is incapable of such an act,' she said, and had the monk released. Then that monk went to the monastery and reported this matter to the monks. Those monks who were of few desires… criticized, complained, and spread it about: 'How can monks going for alms be so improperly dressed, improperly robed, and not endowed with proper deportment? How can they enter and leave dwellings without paying attention, too hastily, stand too far or too close, too long, or turn back too quickly?' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. … 'Is it true, monks…?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' … Having rebuked them… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

366. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, piṇḍacārikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññāpessāmi yathā piṇḍacārikehi [V 0.0359] bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Piṇḍacārikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā – ‘idāni gāmaṃ pavisissāmī’ti timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ [T 2.0231] bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena gāmo pavisitabbo.

366. Therefore, monks, I will lay down the conduct for monks who go on alms round, according to which monks who go on alms round should conduct themselves. Monks, a monk going on alms round, thinking, 'Now I will enter the village,' having covered the three circles, having worn the lower robe evenly all around, having tied the waistband, having put on the outer robes making them double-layered, having fastened the knot, and having washed and taken his bowl, should enter the village carefully and unhurriedly.

“Suppaṭicchannena [M 0.0384] antaraghare gantabbaṃ[P 2.0216]. Susaṃvutena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Appasaddena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na khambhakatena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ.

One should go among the houses well-covered. One should go among the houses well-restrained. One should go among the houses with eyes cast down. One should not go among the houses with robes hitched up. One should not go among the houses laughing loudly. One should go among the houses with little sound. One should not go among the houses swaying the body. One should not go among the houses swaying the head. One should not go among the houses with hands on hips. One should not go among the houses with the head covered. One should not go among the houses walking on one's heels.

“Nivesanaṃ pavisantena sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘iminā pavisissāmi, iminā nikkhamissāmī’ti. Nātisahasā pavisitabbaṃ. Nātisahasā nikkhamitabbaṃ. Nātidūre ṭhātabbaṃ. Nāccāsanne ṭhātabbaṃ. Nāticiraṃ ṭhātabbaṃ. Nātilahuṃ nivattitabbaṃ. Ṭhitakena sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘bhikkhaṃ dātukāmā vā adātukāmā vā’ti. Sace kammaṃ vā nikkhipati, āsanā vā vuṭṭhāti, kaṭacchuṃ vā parāmasati, bhājanaṃ vā parāmasati, ṭhapeti ṭhāpeti (ka.) vā – dātukāmassāti dātukāmiyāti (syā.), dātukāmā viyāti (sī.) ṭhātabbaṃ. Bhikkhāya diyyamānāya vāmena hatthena saṅghāṭiṃ uccāretvā dakkhiṇena hatthena pattaṃ paṇāmetvā ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā bhikkhā paṭiggahetabbā. Na ca bhikkhādāyikāya mukhaṃ [T 2.0232] ulloketabbaṃ oloketabbaṃ (syā.). Sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘sūpaṃ dātukāmā vā adātukāmā vā’ti. Sace kaṭacchuṃ vā parāmasati, bhājanaṃ vā parāmasati, ṭhapeti vā – dātukāmassāti ṭhātabbaṃ. Bhikkhāya dinnāya saṅghāṭiyā pattaṃ paṭicchādetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena nivattitabbaṃ.

When entering a dwelling, one should take note: ‘I will enter by this way, I will exit by this way.’ One should not enter too hastily. One should not exit too hastily. One should not stand too far away. One should not stand too close. One should not stand for too long. One should not turn back too quickly. While standing, one should observe: ‘Do they wish to give alms or not?’ If they put down their work, or rise from their seat, or handle a ladle, or handle a dish, or set something down, one should stand, considering that they may wish to give. When alms are being given, one should lift the outer robe with the left hand, extend the bowl with the right hand, and receive the alms, taking the bowl with both hands. And one should not look up at the face of the female almsgiver.
