One should observe: ‘Do they wish to give curry or not?’ If they handle a ladle, or handle a dish, or set something down, one should stand, considering that they may wish to give. After alms have been given, one should cover the bowl with the outer robe and depart carefully, without hurrying.

“Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Susaṃvutena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Appasaddena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na khambhakatena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, tena āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ [V 0.0360] pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, avakkārapāti dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpetabbā, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso, sace ākaṅkhati, bhuñjitabbaṃ[M 0.0385]. No ce ākaṅkhati, appaharite vā chaḍḍetabbaṃ, appāṇake vā udake opilāpetabbaṃ. Tena āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ, avakkārapāti dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbā, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ[T 2.0233], bhattaggaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ tena upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, na ca tappaccayā vācā bhinditabbā. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, piṇḍacārikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ yathā piṇḍacārikehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabba”nti.

One should enter inhabited areas well-covered. One should enter inhabited areas well-restrained. One should enter inhabited areas with eyes cast down. One should not enter inhabited areas with robes hitched up. One should not enter inhabited areas laughing loudly. One should enter inhabited areas quietly. One should not enter inhabited areas swaying the body. One should not enter inhabited areas swinging the arms. One should not enter inhabited areas shaking the head. One should not enter inhabited areas with arms akimbo. One should not enter inhabited areas with the head covered. One should not enter inhabited areas walking on the heels. The monk who returns first from the alms-round in the village should prepare the seats, set out water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet, wash and set out the bowl for first portions, and set out drinking water and water for use. The monk who returns last from the alms-round in the village, if there are leftovers and if he wishes, may eat. If he does not wish, he should discard them in a place with little greenery or pour them into water that is free of living beings. He should put away the seats, put away the water for washing the feet, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet, wash and put away the bowl for first portions, and put away the drinking water and water for use. He should sweep the refectory. Whoever sees a water pot for drinking, for use, or for the toilet that is empty or vacant should set it up. If it is too heavy for him, he should summon another by a gesture of the hand and, linking hands, they should set it up; but he should not break his silence on that account. This, monks, is the code of conduct for monks who go on alms-round, which should be properly observed by monks who go on alms-round.

7. Āraññikavattakathā

7. The Discourse on the Observances of Forest Dwellers

367. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū araññe viharanti. Te neva pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, na paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti[P 2.0217], na aggiṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, na araṇisahitaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, na nakkhattapadāni jānanti, na disābhāgaṃ jānanti. Corā tattha gantvā te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “atthi, bhante, pānīya”nti? “Natthāvuso”ti. “Atthi, bhante, paribhojanīya”nti? “Natthāvuso”ti. “Atthi, bhante, aggī”ti? “Natthāvuso”ti. “Atthi, bhante, araṇisahita”nti? “Natthāvuso”ti. ( ) (atthi bhante nakkhattapadānīti, na jānāma āvusoti, atthi bhante disābhāganti, na jānāma āvusoti.) sī. vimatiṭīkāya pana sameti “Kenajja, bhante, yutta”nti? “Na kho mayaṃ, āvuso, jānāmā”ti. “Katamāyaṃ, bhante, disā”ti? “Na kho mayaṃ, āvuso, jānāmā”ti. Atha kho te corā – ‘nevimesaṃ pānīyaṃ atthi, na paribhojanīyaṃ atthi, na aggi atthi, na araṇisahitaṃ atthi, na nakkhattapadāni jānanti, na disābhāgaṃ jānanti; corā ime, nayime bhikkhū’ti – ākoṭetvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha [T 2.0234] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

367. At that time, many monks were dwelling in the forest. They did not keep drinking water available, nor water for use, nor fire, nor a fire-drill; they did not know the portions of the constellations, nor the portions of the directions. Thieves went there and asked those monks, “Is there drinking water, venerable sirs?” “There is not, friends.” “Is there water for use, venerable sirs?” “There is not, friends.” “Is there fire, venerable sirs?” “There is not, friends.” “Is there a fire-drill, venerable sirs?” “There is not, friends.” “With which constellation is today conjoined, venerable sirs?” “We do not know, friends.” “Which direction is this, venerable sirs?” “We do not know, friends.” Then those thieves thought, ‘These ones have no drinking water, no water for use, no fire, no fire-drill; they do not know the portions of the constellations or the portions of the directions. These are thieves, not monks.’ So they beat them and departed. Then those monks informed the other monks about this matter. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks:

368. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, āraññikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā āraññikehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Āraññikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā kālasseva uṭṭhāya pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipitvā aṃse ālaggetvā [M 0.0386] cīvaraṃ khandhe karitvā upāhanā ārohitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā senāsanā otaritabbaṃ [V 0.0361] – idāni gāmaṃ pavisissāmīti. Upāhanā omuñcitvā nīcaṃ katvā papphoṭetvā thavikāya pakkhipitvā aṃse ālaggetvā timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena gāmo pavisitabbo. Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbaṃ…pe… na khambhakatena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ.

368. “Well then, monks, I will lay down a practice for forest-dwelling monks, how forest-dwelling monks should properly conduct themselves. A forest-dwelling monk, monks, should rise early, place his bowl in a bag, hang it over his shoulder, place his robe on his shoulder, put on his sandals, put away his wooden and clay utensils, close the door and window, and descend from his dwelling, thinking, ‘Now I will enter the village.’ He should take off his sandals, place them low, shake them out, put them in the bag, and hang it over his shoulder. Covering the three circles, wearing the lower robe evenly all around, fastening the belt, putting on the folded outer robes, and fastening the knot, he should wash and take his bowl, and enter the village carefully and unhurriedly. He should go among the houses well-covered… He should not go among the houses with hands on hips. He should not go among the houses with his head covered. He should not go among the houses walking on the heels.

“Nivesanaṃ pavisantena sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘iminā pavisissāmi, iminā nikkhamissāmī’ti. Nātisahasā pavisitabbaṃ. Nātisahasā nikkhamitabbaṃ. Nātidūre ṭhātabbaṃ. Nāccāsanne ṭhātabbaṃ. Nāticiraṃ ṭhātabbaṃ. Nātilahuṃ nivattitabbaṃ. Ṭhitakena sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘bhikkhaṃ dātukāmā vā adātukāmā vā’ti. Sace kammaṃ vā nikkhipati, āsanā vā vuṭṭhāti, kaṭacchuṃ vā parāmasati, bhājanaṃ vā parāmasati, ṭhapeti vā – dātukāmassāti ṭhātabbaṃ. Bhikkhāya diyyamānāya vāmena hatthena [T 2.0235] saṅghāṭiṃ uccāretvā dakkhiṇena hatthena pattaṃ paṇāmetvā ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā bhikkhā paṭiggahetabbā. Na ca bhikkhādāyikāya mukhaṃ ulloketabbaṃ. Sallakkhetabbaṃ – ‘sūpaṃ dātukāmā vā adātukāmā vā’ti. Sace kaṭacchu vā parāmasati, bhājanaṃ vā parāmasati, ṭhapeti vā – dātukāmassāti ṭhātabbaṃ. Bhikkhāya dinnāya saṅghāṭiyā pattaṃ paṭicchādetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena nivattitabbaṃ.

When entering a dwelling, it should be noted: ‘I will enter by this way; I will exit by this way.’ One should not enter too hastily. One should not exit too hastily. One should not stand too far away. One should not stand too close. One should not stand for too long. One should not turn back too quickly. While standing, it should be discerned: ‘Are they willing to give almsfood or not?’ If they put down their work, or rise from their seat, or touch a ladle, or handle a vessel, or set it down, one should stand, thinking, ‘She may be willing to give.’ When almsfood is being given, having lifted the outer robe with the left hand and extended the bowl with the right hand, the almsfood should be received by accepting the bowl with both hands. And the face of the female alms-giver should not be looked up at. It should be discerned: ‘Are they willing to give curry or not?’ If they touch a ladle, or handle a vessel, or set it down, one should stand, thinking, ‘She may be willing to give.’ After the almsfood has been given, one should cover the bowl with the outer robe and depart properly, without haste.

“Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbaṃ…pe… na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Gāmato nikkhamitvā pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipitvā aṃse ālaggetvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitvā sīse karitvā upāhanā ārohitvā gantabbaṃ.

One should go within the village well-covered… one should not go within the village in a squatting posture. After leaving the village, having placed the bowl in its bag and hung it over the shoulder, having folded the robe and placed it on the head, and having put on sandals, one should go.

“Āraññikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, aggi upaṭṭhāpetabbo, araṇisahitaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, kattaradaṇḍo upaṭṭhāpetabbo, nakkhattapadāni uggahetabbāni – sakalāni vā ekadesāni vā, disākusalena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, āraññikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ yathā āraññikehi bhikkhūhi sammā vattitabba”nti.

Monks, a forest-dwelling monk should keep drinking water available, keep water for use available, keep a fire available, keep a fire-drill set available, and keep a walking stick available. The positions of the constellations—either all or in part—should be learned, and he should be skilled in directions. This, monks, is the duty for forest-dwelling monks, according to which forest-dwelling monks should conduct themselves properly.

8. Senāsanavattakathā

8. The Discourse on the Duties Concerning Lodgings

369. Tena [M 0.0387][V 0.0362] kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū ajjhokāse cīvarakammaṃ [P 2.0218] karonti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū paṭivāte aṅgaṇe paṅgaṇe (sī. syā.) senāsanaṃ papphoṭesuṃ. Bhikkhū rajena okiriṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… [T 2.0236] te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū paṭivāte aṅgaṇe senāsanaṃ papphoṭessanti! Bhikkhū rajena okiriṃsū”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū paṭivāte aṅgaṇe senāsanaṃ papphoṭenti, bhikkhū rajena okiriṃsū”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

369. Now at that time, many monks were doing robe-work in the open air. The monks of the group of six shook out bedding in an open space upwind. The other monks were covered with dust. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the monks of the group of six shake out bedding in an open space upwind! The monks were covered with dust.” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that the monks of the group of six shake out bedding in an open space upwind, and that the other monks were covered with dust?” “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

370. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanavattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā bhikkhūhi senāsane sammā vattitabbaṃ. Yasmiṃ vihāre viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. mahāva. 66, 67; cūḷava. 357 Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhummattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace [T 2.0237] vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā pariphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

370. In that case, monks, I will lay down the duties concerning lodgings for monks, according to which monks should conduct themselves properly in a lodging. If the monastery in which one is residing is dirty, it should be cleaned, if one is able. When cleaning the monastery, first the bowl and robes should be taken out and placed to one side; the sitting-cloth and ground-sheet should be taken out and placed to one side; the mattress and pillow should be taken out and placed to one side; the bed should be lowered and taken out carefully, without scraping it on the ground or bumping it against the door-frame, and placed to one side; the stool should be lowered and taken out carefully, without scraping it on the ground or bumping it against the door-frame, and placed to one side; the supports for the bed should be taken out and placed to one side; the spittoon should be taken out and placed to one side; the leaning-board should be taken out and placed to one side; the floor covering should be taken out, after noting how it was laid, and placed to one side. If there are cobwebs in the monastery, they should first be removed, starting from the ceiling; the corners of the window openings should be wiped. If a wall finished with red ochre has become mildewed, a cloth should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If a floor finished in black has become mildewed, a cloth should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is unfinished, it should be sprinkled repeatedly with water and swept, with the thought, ‘Let the monastery not be sullied by dust.’ The sweepings should be collected and discarded to one side.

“Na [M 0.0388] bhikkhusāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ. Na vihārasāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ. Na pānīyasāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ. Na paribhojanīyasāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ. Na paṭivāte aṅgaṇe senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ. Adhovāte senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ.

Bedding should not be shaken out in the vicinity of a monk. Bedding should not be shaken out in the vicinity of a monastery. Bedding should not be shaken out in the vicinity of drinking water. Bedding should not be shaken out in the vicinity of water for use. Bedding should not be shaken out in an open space upwind. Bedding should be shaken out downwind.

“Bhummattharaṇaṃ [V 0.0363] ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā ekamantaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā [P 2.0219] atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā [T 2.0238] atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako ekamantaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajju vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The floor covering should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The bed legs should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in their usual place. The bed should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken, and having lowered it, it should be brought back carefully without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door panel or door frame, and laid out as it was before. The stool should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken, and having lowered it, it should be brought back carefully without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door panel or door frame, and laid out as it was before. The mattress and pillow should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The sitting cloth and bedding cover should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The spittoon should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The leaning-board should be taken to a suitable place, aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, having taken the bowl with one hand, one should feel with the other hand underneath the bed or underneath the stool, and the bowl should be put down. And the bowl should not be placed on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, having taken the robe with one hand, one should wipe the robe-pole or robe-line with the other hand, and having placed the end on the far side and made the fold on the near side, the robe should be put away.

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace [M 0.0389] pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā [T 2.0239] uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the monastery precinct is dirty, the monastery precinct should be swept. If the gatehouse is dirty, the gatehouse should be swept. If the service hall is dirty, the service hall should be swept. If the fire hall is dirty, the fire hall should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

“Sace vuḍḍhena saddhiṃ ekavihāre viharati, na vuḍḍhaṃ anāpucchā uddeso dātabbo, na paripucchā dātabbā, na sajjhāyo kātabbo, na dhammo bhāsitabbo, na padīpo kātabbo, na padīpo [V 0.0364] vijjhāpetabbo, na vātapānā vivaritabbā, na vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace [P 2.0220] vuḍḍhena saddhiṃ ekacaṅkame caṅkamati, yena vuḍḍho tena parivattitabbaṃ, na ca vuḍḍho saṅghāṭikaṇṇena ghaṭṭetabbo. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanavattaṃ yathā bhikkhūhi senāsane sammā vattitabba”nti.

If one dwells in the same dwelling with an elder, one should not give a lesson without asking the elder, nor ask questions, nor engage in recitation, nor speak the Dhamma, nor light a lamp, nor extinguish a lamp, nor open the windows, nor close the windows. If one walks on the same walking path with an elder, one should turn towards the elder, and one should not brush against the elder with the corner of one’s outer robe. This, monks, is the conduct for monks regarding lodgings, by which monks should conduct themselves properly in lodgings.

9. Jantāgharavattakathā

9. The Discourse on the Conduct for the Sweat-Bath

371. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jantāghare therehi bhikkhūhi nivāriyamānā anādariyaṃ paṭicca pahūtaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ āropetvā aggiṃ datvā dvāraṃ thaketvā dvāre nisīdanti. Bhikkhū therā ca bhikkhū (syā. kaṃ.) uṇhābhitattā dvāraṃ alabhamānā mucchitā papatanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [T 2.0240] nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jantāghare therehi bhikkhūhi nivāriyamānā anādariyaṃ paṭicca pahūtaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ āropetvā aggiṃ datvā dvāraṃ thaketvā dvāre nisīdissanti! Bhikkhū uṇhābhitattā dvāraṃ alabhamānā mucchitā papatantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jantāghare therehi bhikkhūhi nivāriyamānā anādariyaṃ paṭicca pahūtaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ āropetvā aggiṃ datvā dvāraṃ thaketvā dvāre nisīdanti; bhikkhū uṇhābhitattā dvāraṃ alabhamānā mucchitā papatantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na[M 0.0390], bhikkhave, jantāghare therena bhikkhunā nivāriyamānena anādariyaṃ paṭicca pahūtaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ āropetvā aggi dātabbo. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na, bhikkhave, dvāraṃ thaketvā dvāre nisīditabbaṃ. Yo nisīdeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

371. At that time the monks of the group of six, while in a hot-house and being forbidden by the elder monks, out of disrespect piled up a great deal of firewood, lit a fire, blocked the door, and sat at the door. The monks, overcome by the heat and unable to find the door, fainted and collapsed. Those monks who were of few wishes…pe… criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the monks of the group of six, while in a hot-house and being forbidden by the elder monks, out of disrespect pile up a great deal of firewood, light a fire, block the door, and sit at the door! The monks, overcome by the heat and unable to find the door, are fainting and collapsing!” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One…pe… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that the monks of the group of six, while in a hot-house and being forbidden by the elder monks, out of disrespect piled up a great deal of firewood, lit a fire, blocked the door, and sat at the door; and that the monks, overcome by the heat and unable to find the door, fainted and collapsed?” “It is true, Blessed One.”…pe… Having rebuked them…pe… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, in a hot-house, when being forbidden by an elder monk, one should not, out of disrespect, pile up a great deal of firewood and light a fire. Whoever should do so, incurs an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, one should not block the door and sit at the door. Whoever should do so, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

372. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ jantāgharavattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā bhikkhūhi jantāghare sammā vattitabbaṃ. Yo paṭhamaṃ jantāgharaṃ gacchati, sace chārikā ussannā hoti, chārikā chaḍḍetabbā. Sace jantāgharaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, jantāgharaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace paribhaṇḍaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, paribhaṇḍaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo[T 2.0241]. Sace jantāgharasālā uklāpā hoti, jantāgharasālā sammajjitabbā.

372. “Therefore, monks, I will lay down the observance for the steam-bath for monks, according to which monks should properly conduct themselves in the steam-bath. Whichever monk goes to the steam-bath first, if the ashes are abundant, the ashes should be discarded. If the steam-bath has rubbish, the steam-bath should be swept. If the equipment has rubbish, the equipment should be swept. If the surrounding area has rubbish, the surrounding area should be swept. If the gateway has rubbish, the gateway should be swept. If the steam-bath hall has rubbish, the steam-bath hall should be swept.”

“Cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, udakadoṇikāya udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ [V 0.0365] pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāghare therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ. Sace ussahati, udakepi therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Na therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ puratopi nahāyitabbaṃ, na [P 2.0221] uparitopi nahāyitabbaṃ. Nahātena uttarantena otarantānaṃ maggo dātabbo. Yo pacchā jantāgharā nikkhamati, sace jantāgharaṃ cikkhallaṃ hoti, dhovitabbaṃ. Mattikādoṇikaṃ dhovitvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ paṭisāmetvā aggiṃ vijjhāpetvā dvāraṃ thaketvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ jantāgharavattaṃ yathā bhikkhūhi jantāghare sammā vattitabba”nti.

“Bathing powder should be gathered, fine clay should be moistened, and water should be poured into the water trough. When entering the steam-bath, one should smear the face with fine clay, cover oneself in front and in back, and then enter the steam-bath. One should not sit down encroaching upon the senior monks. Junior monks should not be prevented from taking a seat. If one is able, service for the senior monks, such as tending the fire, should be done in the steam-bath. When leaving the steam-bath, one should take the steam-bath stool, cover oneself in front and in back, and then leave the steam-bath. If one is able, service for the senior monks, such as scrubbing their backs, should also be done at the bathing place. One should not bathe in front of the senior monks, nor should one bathe upstream from them. One who has bathed and is coming up from the water should give way to those who are going down. Whoever leaves the steam-bath last, if the steam-bath is muddy, it should be washed. Having washed the clay trough, put away the steam-bath stool, extinguished the fire, and closed the door, one should depart. This, O monks, is the observance for monks in the steam-bath, according to which monks should properly conduct themselves in the steam-bath.”

10. Vaccakuṭivattakathā

10. Discourse on the Observances for the Latrine

373. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu brāhmaṇajātiko vaccaṃ katvā na icchati ācametuṃ – ko imaṃ vasalaṃ duggandhaṃ [T 2.0242] āmasissatīti [M 0.0391] ācamissatīti (ka.). Tassa vaccamagge kimi saṇṭhāti. Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, vaccaṃ katvā na ācamesī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu vaccaṃ katvā na ācamessatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, vaccaṃ katvā na ācamesī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, vaccaṃ katvā sati udake nācametabbaṃ. Yo nācameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

373. At that time, a certain monk of brahmin birth, after defecating, did not wish to wash, thinking: “Who would touch this vile, foul-smelling thing?” Worms then arose in his anal passage. Then that monk informed the monks of this matter. “Friend, did you not wash after defecating?” “Yes, friend.” Those monks who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could a monk, after defecating, not wash?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monk, as has been heard, that you did not wash after defecating?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked him… having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks: “Monks, after defecating, when water is available, one must not fail to wash. Whoever should not wash, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū vaccakuṭiyā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vaccaṃ karonti. Navakā bhikkhū paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā vaccitā āgamenti. Te vaccaṃ sandhārentā mucchitā papatanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… “na, bhikkhave, vaccakuṭiyā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vacco kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āgatapaṭipāṭiyā vaccaṃ kātu”nti.

At that time, monks would defecate in the latrine according to seniority. Junior monks, having arrived first, had to wait while being pressed by the need to defecate. While holding in their feces, they would faint and fall down. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, as has been heard…?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … “Monks, in the latrine, defecation should not be done according to seniority. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, defecation in the order of arrival.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atisahasāpi vaccakuṭiṃ pavisanti, ubbhajitvāpi [V 0.0366] ubbhujjitvāpi (sī.), ubbhujitvā (syā.) pavisanti, nitthunantāpi vaccaṃ karonti[T 2.0243], dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādantāpi vaccaṃ karonti, bahiddhāpi vaccadoṇikāya vaccaṃ karonti, bahiddhāpi passāvadoṇikāya passāvaṃ karonti, passāvadoṇikāyapi kheḷaṃ karonti, pharusenapi kaṭṭhena avalekhanti, avalekhanakaṭṭhampi vaccakūpamhi pātenti, atisahasāpi nikkhamanti, ubbhajitvāpi nikkhamanti, capucapukārakampi ācamenti, ācamanasarāvakepi udakaṃ sesenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti [P 2.0222] – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atisahasāpi vaccakuṭiṃ pavisissanti, ubbhajitvāpi pavisissanti, nitthunantāpi vaccaṃ karissanti, dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādantāpi vaccaṃ karissanti, bahiddhāpi vaccadoṇikāya vaccaṃ karissanti, bahiddhāpi passāvadoṇikāya passāvaṃ karissanti, passāvadoṇikāyapi kheḷaṃ karissanti, pharusenapi kaṭṭhena avalekhissanti, avalekhanakaṭṭhampi vaccakūpamhi pātessanti, atisahasāpi nikkhamissanti, ubbhajitvāpi nikkhamissanti, capucapukārakampi ācamessanti, ācamanasarāvakepi udakaṃ sesessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ [M 0.0392] ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

At that time, the monks of the group of six entered the latrine too hastily, entered while lifting their robes, defecated while grunting, defecated while chewing tooth-cleaning sticks, defecated outside the latrine trough, urinated outside the urinal trough, spat into the urinal trough, wiped with rough sticks, dropped the wiping stick into the latrine pit, exited too hastily, exited while lifting their robes, made smacking sounds while rinsing, and left water in the rinsing bowl. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained and criticized them: “How can the monks of the group of six enter the latrine too hastily, enter while lifting their robes, defecate while grunting, defecate while chewing tooth-cleaning sticks, defecate outside the latrine trough, urinate outside the urinal trough, spit into the urinal trough, wipe with rough sticks, drop the wiping stick into the latrine pit, exit too hastily, exit while lifting their robes, make smacking sounds while rinsing, and leave water in the rinsing bowl?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, as has been heard…?” “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks:

374. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ vaccakuṭivattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā bhikkhūhi vaccakuṭiyā sammā vattitabbaṃ. Yo [T 2.0244] vaccakuṭiṃ gacchati tena bahi ṭhitena bahi ṭhitena (sī. ka.) ukkāsitabbaṃ. Anto nisinnenapi ukkāsitabbaṃ. Cīvaravaṃse vā cīvararajjuyā vā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena vaccakuṭī pavisitabbā. Nātisahasā pavisitabbā. Na ubbhajitvā pavisitabbā. Vaccapādukāya ṭhitena ubbhajitabbaṃ. Na nitthunantena vacco kātabbo. Na dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādantena vacco kātabbo. Na bahiddhā vaccadoṇikāya vacco kātabbo. Na bahiddhā passāvadoṇikāya passāvo kātabbo. Na passāvadoṇikāya kheḷo kātabbo. Na pharusena kaṭṭhena avalekhitabbaṃ. Na avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ vaccakūpamhi pātetabbaṃ. Vaccapādukāya ṭhitena paṭicchādetabbaṃ. Nātisahasā nikkhamitabbaṃ. Na ubbhajitvā nikkhamitabbaṃ. Ācamanapādukāya ṭhitena ubbhajitabbaṃ. Na capucapukārakaṃ ācametabbaṃ. Na ācamanasarāvake udakaṃ sesetabbaṃ. Ācamanapādukāya ṭhitena paṭicchādetabbaṃ.

374. “Well then, monks, I shall lay down the observance for monks regarding the latrine, as to how monks should properly conduct themselves in the latrine. One who goes to the latrine should clear their throat while standing outside. One who is sitting inside should also clear their throat. After placing the robe on the robe-rack or robe-cord, one should enter the latrine carefully, without hurrying. One should not enter too hastily. One should not enter while lifting one’s lower robe. One should lift one’s lower robe while standing on the latrine sandals. One should not defecate while grunting. One should not defecate while chewing a tooth-stick. One should not defecate outside the latrine trough. One should not urinate outside the urinal trough. One should not spit into the urinal trough. One should not scrape with a rough stick. The scraping stick should not be thrown into the latrine pit. While standing on the latrine sandals, one should cover it. One should not exit too hastily. One should not exit while lifting one’s lower robe. One should lift one’s lower robe while standing on the rinsing sandals. One should not make smacking sounds while rinsing. Water should not be left in the rinsing vessel. While standing on the rinsing sandals, one should cover oneself.”

“Sace vaccakuṭi uhatā ūhatā (sī. syā.) hoti, dhovitabbā. Sace avalekhanapidharo pūro hoti, avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace paribhaṇḍaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, paribhaṇḍaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ[V 0.0367]. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ[T 2.0245]. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ vaccakuṭivattaṃ yathā bhikkhūhi vaccakuṭiyā sammā vattitabba”nti.

“If the latrine is soiled with excrement, it should be washed. If the scraping-stick container is full, the scraping sticks should be discarded. If the latrine has rubbish, the latrine should be swept. If the anteroom has rubbish, the anteroom should be swept. If the enclosure has rubbish, the enclosure should be swept. If the gateway has rubbish, the gateway should be swept. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot. This, monks, is the observance for monks regarding the latrine, according to which monks should conduct themselves properly in the latrine.”

11. Upajjhāyavattakathā

11. The Discourse on the Observances toward a Preceptor

375. Tena kho pana samayena saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti vigarahi buddho [M 0.0393] bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu [P 2.0223] na sammā vattissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

375. At that time, resident disciples were not conducting themselves properly toward their preceptors. Those monks who were of few wishes... criticized, disparaged, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could resident disciples not conduct themselves properly toward their preceptors!' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Is it true, monks, as is said, that resident disciples are not conducting themselves properly toward their preceptors?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, monks, could resident disciples not conduct themselves properly toward their preceptors! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced...' Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

376. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikānaṃ upajjhāyesu vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā saddhivihārikehi upajjhāyesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. mahāva. 66 Saddhivihārikena, bhikkhave, upajjhāyamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

376. “Well then, monks, I shall lay down the observance for resident disciples toward their preceptors, according to which resident disciples should conduct themselves properly toward their preceptors. A resident disciple, monks, should conduct himself properly toward his preceptor. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

“Kālasseva uṭṭhāya upāhanā omuñcitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Upajjhāyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti[T 2.0246], so deso sammajjitabbo.

“Having risen early, having taken off his sandals, and having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, a tooth-stick should be given, water for the face should be given, and a seat should be prepared. If there is gruel, having washed the bowl, the gruel should be offered. When he has drunk the gruel, water should be given, the bowl should be received, and holding it low, it should be carefully washed without scraping it and then put away. When the preceptor has risen, the seat should be cleared away. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.”

“Sace upajjhāyo gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto sodako saudako (ka.) dātabbo. Sace upajjhāyo pacchāsamaṇaṃ ākaṅkhati, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā upajjhāyassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ. Nātidūre gantabbaṃ, nāccāsanne gantabbaṃ[V 0.0368], pattapariyāpannaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbā. Upajjhāyo āpattisāmantā bhaṇamāno nivāretabbo.

“If the preceptor wishes to enter the village, the lower robe should be given, and the previously worn lower robe should be received. The waistband should be given. The outer robes, having been folded, should be given. The bowl, having been washed and containing water, should be given. If the preceptor desires an accompanying monk, one should become the preceptor's accompanying monk by covering the three circles, wearing the lower robe evenly all around, tying the waistband, folding and putting on the outer robes, fastening the clasp, and washing and taking the bowl. One should not walk too far away, nor too close. One should be ready to receive the alms placed in the bowl. While the preceptor is speaking, one should not interrupt his speech. If the preceptor is speaking on a matter bordering on an offense, he should be stopped.”

“Nivattantena paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

“When returning, one should arrive first and prepare a seat. Water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. Having gone out to meet him, one should receive his bowl and robes. The fresh lower robe should be given, and the worn lower robe should be received. If a robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the sun. The robe should be folded. When folding the robe, one should offset the edge by four finger-widths, thinking, ‘May the crease not be in the middle.’ The waistband should be placed inside the fold.”

“Sace [M 0.0394] piṇḍapāto hoti, upajjhāyo ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto [T 2.0247] upanāmetabbo. Upajjhāyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo. Na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ [P 2.0224] nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Upajjhāyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If there is almsfood and the preceptor wishes to eat, water should be given and the almsfood presented. The preceptor should be asked about drinking water. After he has eaten, water should be given, the bowl received, and having lowered it, it should be washed well without scraping it. Having made it free of water, it should be warmed in the sun for a moment. The bowl should not be left in the sun for a long time. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, one should take the bowl with one hand, feel under the bed or under the stool with the other hand, and then put the bowl down. The bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, one should take the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-pole or robe-rope with the other hand, and put the robe away with its edge on the far side and its fold on the near side. When the preceptor has arisen, the seat should be put away; the water for the feet, the footstool, and the foot-scraper should be stored away. If that place is strewn with rubbish, it should be swept.

“Sace upajjhāyo nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

If the preceptor wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If there is a need for cold water, cold water should be prepared. If there is a need for hot water, hot water should be prepared.

“Sace upajjhāyo jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya upajjhāyassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā [T 2.0248] jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare upajjhāyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā [V 0.0369] nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the preceptor wishes to enter the steam-room, bath powder should be mixed with water and clay should be moistened. Taking the steam-room stool, one should go behind the preceptor, give the steam-room stool, receive the robe, and place it in a suitable place. The bath powder should be given; the clay should be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam-room. When entering the steam-room, one should smear one's face with clay, cover oneself in front and in back, and enter. One should not sit down crowding the elder bhikkhus. Junior bhikkhus should not be obstructed from their seats. In the steam-room, service should be done for the preceptor. When leaving the steam-room, taking the steam-room stool and covering oneself in front and in back, one should exit from the steam-room.

“Udakepi upajjhāyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā upajjhāyassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ. Upajjhāyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Sace uddisāpetukāmo hoti, uddisitabbo. Sace paripucchitukāmo hoti, paripucchitabbo.

In the water also, service should be done for the preceptor. Having bathed, one should come out first, make one's own body dry, put on the lower robe, and wipe the water from the preceptor's body. The lower robe should be given; the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam-room stool, one should arrive first and prepare a seat. Water for the feet, a footstool, and a foot-scraper should be placed nearby. The preceptor should be asked about drinking water. If he wishes to have the Pāli recited, it should be recited. If he wishes to be questioned on the commentary, he should be questioned.

“Yasmiṃ [M 0.0395] vihāre upajjhāyo viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena[P 2.0225], asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; apassenaphalakaṃ [T 2.0249] nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā pariphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

In the dwelling where the preceptor resides, if that dwelling is untidy, and if one is able, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first take out the bowl and robe and set them aside in a suitable place. Take out the sitting mat and its covering and set them aside in a suitable place. Take out the mattress and bolster and set them aside in a suitable place. Lower the bed carefully, without scraping it or knocking it against the doorposts, and take it out to set aside in a suitable place. Lower the stool carefully, without scraping it or knocking it against the doorposts, and take it out to set aside in a suitable place. Take out the bed legs and set them aside in a suitable place. Take out the spittoon and set it aside in a suitable place. Take out the leaning-board and set it aside in a suitable place. Note how the floor covering is laid out, then take it out and set it aside in a suitable place. If the dwelling has cobwebs, first remove them from the ceiling, and wipe the corners of the windows and pillars. If the walls that have been prepared with red ochre are moldy, moisten a cloth, wring it out, and wipe them. If the floor that has been prepared with a black color is moldy, moisten a cloth, wring it out, and wipe it. If the floor is unprepared, sprinkle it with water and sweep it—so that the dwelling is not afflicted by dust. Gather the rubbish and discard it in a suitable place.

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ [V 0.0370] otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako otāpetvā [T 2.0250] pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto [M 0.0396] nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The ground covering should be sunned, cleaned, shaken, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The bed legs should be sunned, wiped, brought back, and placed in their usual place. The bed should be sunned, cleaned, shaken, and having lowered it, it should be brought back carefully without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door panel and frame, and laid out as it was before. The chair should be sunned, cleaned, shaken, and having lowered it, it should be brought back carefully without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door panel and frame, and laid out as it was before. The mattress and bolster should be sunned, cleaned, shaken, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The sitting cloth should be sunned, cleaned, shaken, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The spittoon should be sunned, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The leaning-board should be sunned, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The bowl and robes should be put down. When putting down the bowl, having taken the bowl with one hand, one should feel under the bed or under the chair with the other hand, and then the bowl should be put down. And the bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting down the robe, having taken the robe with one hand, one should wipe the robe-pole or the robe-rope with the other hand, and having made a fold on the near side with the end on the far side, the robe should be put down.

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā [P 2.0226] sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ [T 2.0251] upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the precinct is dirty, the precinct should be swept. If the gatehouse is dirty, the gatehouse should be swept. If the assembly hall is dirty, the assembly hall should be swept. If the fire hall is dirty, the fire hall should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

“Sace upajjhāyassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, saddhivihārikena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyo garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace upajjhāyo mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho hoti, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace upajjhāyo mānattāraho hoti, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace [V 0.0371] upajjhāyo abbhānāraho hoti, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho [M 0.0397] saṅgho upajjhāyaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho upajjhāyassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ [T 2.0252] vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyo sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If discontent has arisen for the preceptor, he should be taken elsewhere by the co-resident disciple, or he should be caused to be taken elsewhere, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse has arisen for the preceptor, it should be dispelled by the co-resident disciple, or it should be caused to be dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view has arisen for the preceptor, he should be dissuaded from it by the co-resident disciple, or he should be caused to be dissuaded from it, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If the preceptor has committed a grave offense and is deserving of probation, an effort should be made by the co-resident disciple: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant probation to the preceptor?’ If the preceptor is deserving of being sent back to the beginning, an effort should be made by the co-resident disciple: ‘How might the Saṅgha send the preceptor back to the beginning?’ If the preceptor is deserving of penance, an effort should be made by the co-resident disciple: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant penance to the preceptor?’ If the preceptor is deserving of reinstatement, an effort should be made by the co-resident disciple: ‘How might the Saṅgha reinstate the preceptor?’ If the Saṅgha wishes to perform a formal act against the preceptor—whether an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—an effort should be made by the co-resident disciple: ‘How might the Saṅgha not perform the formal act against the preceptor, or how might it be changed to a lighter one?’ Or if a formal act has been performed against him by the Saṅgha—whether an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—an effort should be made by the co-resident disciple: ‘How might the preceptor conduct himself properly, humble himself, and practice for his rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha might revoke that formal act?’

“Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti[P 2.0227], saddhivihārikena dhovitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena kātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa rajanā pacitabbā hoti, saddhivihārikena pacitabbā, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ rajetabbaṃ (syā.) hoti, saddhivihārikena rajitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena rajentena (syā.) sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ.

If the preceptor's robe is to be washed, it should be washed by the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might the preceptor's robe be washed?' If the preceptor's robe is to be sewn, it should be sewn by the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might the preceptor's robe be sewn?' If dye for the preceptor is to be prepared, it should be prepared by the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might dye for the preceptor be prepared?' If the preceptor's robe is to be dyed, it should be dyed by the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might the preceptor's robe be dyed?' While dyeing the robe, one should dye it well, turning it over and over again, and one should not depart while the dripping has not ceased.

“Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā ekaccassa patto dātabbo, na ekaccassa patto paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa parikkhāro dātabbo, na ekaccassa parikkhāro paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa kesā chedetabbā chettabbā (sī.), cheditabbā (ka.), na ekaccena kesā [T 2.0253] chedāpetabbā; na ekaccassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ekaccena parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa veyyāvacco veyyāvaccaṃ (ka.) kātabbo, na ekaccena veyyāvacco kārāpetabbo; na ekaccassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ, na ekacco pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo; na ekaccassa piṇḍapāto nīharitabbo, na ekaccena piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo; na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā gāmo pavisitabbo; na susānaṃ gantabbaṃ; na disā pakkamitabbā. Sace upajjhāyo gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo[M 0.0398], vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikānaṃ upajjhāyesu vattaṃ yathā saddhivihārikehi upajjhāyesu sammā vattitabba”nti.

Without asking the preceptor, a bowl should not be given to a certain monk, nor should a bowl be received from a certain monk; a robe should not be given to a certain monk, nor should a robe be received from a certain monk; a requisite should not be given to a certain monk, nor should a requisite be received from a certain monk; the hair of a certain monk should not be cut, nor should one have one's hair cut by a certain monk; service should not be performed for a certain monk, nor should one have service performed by a certain monk; duties should not be performed for a certain monk, nor should one have duties performed by a certain monk; one should not be the junior attendant of a certain monk, nor should a certain monk be taken as a junior attendant; almsfood should not be brought out for a certain monk, nor should one have almsfood brought out by a certain monk. Without asking the preceptor, a village should not be entered; a charnel ground should not be gone to; one should not depart for another region. If the preceptor is sick, he should be attended to for life; his recovery should be awaited. This, O monks, is the duty of co-resident disciples towards their preceptors, according to which co-resident disciples should conduct themselves properly towards their preceptors.

12. Saddhivihārikavattakathā

12. The Discourse on the Duties of a Co-resident Disciple

377. Tena [V 0.0372] kho pana samayena upajjhāyā saddhivihārikesu na sammā vattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma upajjhāyā saddhivihārikesu na sammā vattissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, upajjhāyā saddhivihārikesu na sammā vattantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

377. At that time, preceptors were not behaving properly towards their co-resident disciples. Those monks who were modest... grumbled, criticized, and spread it about, saying: "How indeed can preceptors not behave properly towards their co-resident disciples?" Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One... "Is it true, monks, that preceptors are not behaving properly towards their co-resident disciples?" "It is true, Blessed One."... Having rebuked them... and given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks:

378. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, upajjhāyānaṃ saddhivihārikesu vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā upajjhāyehi saddhivihārikesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. mahāva. 67 Upajjhāyena, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ[P 2.0228]. Tatrāyaṃ [T 2.0254] sammāvattanā –

378. In that case, O monks, I will lay down the duties of preceptors towards their co-resident disciples, according to which preceptors should conduct themselves properly towards their co-resident disciples. A preceptor, O monks, should conduct himself properly towards his co-resident disciple. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

“Upajjhāyena, bhikkhave, saddhivihāriko saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā. Sace upajjhāyassa patto hoti, saddhivihārikassa patto na hoti, upajjhāyena saddhivihārikassa patto dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa patto uppajjiyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ hoti, saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ na hoti, upajjhāyena saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ uppajjiyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa parikkhāro hoti, saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro na hoti, upajjhāyena saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro uppajjiyethāti.

Monks, a preceptor should support and assist a co-resident disciple by teaching the Pali text, by teaching the commentary, by admonition, and by instruction. If the preceptor has a bowl and the co-resident disciple does not have a bowl, the preceptor should give a bowl to the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might a bowl arise for the co-resident disciple?' If the preceptor has a robe and the co-resident disciple does not have a robe, the preceptor should give a robe to the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might a robe arise for the co-resident disciple?' If the preceptor has requisites and the co-resident disciple does not have requisites, the preceptor should give requisites to the co-resident disciple, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might requisites arise for the co-resident disciple?'

“Sace saddhivihāriko gilāno hoti, kālasseva uṭṭhāya dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ [M 0.0399] datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Saddhivihārikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If a co-resident disciple is sick, one should rise early, give a tooth-stick, give water for the face, and prepare a seat. If there is rice-gruel, one should wash the vessel and offer the rice-gruel. After he has drunk the rice-gruel, one should give water, take back the vessel, and holding it low, wash it carefully without scraping it on the ground and put it away. When the co-resident disciple has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.

“Sace saddhivihāriko gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ[V 0.0373], kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā[T 2.0255], dhovitvā patto sodako dātabbo.

If a co-resident disciple wishes to enter a village, the lower robe to be worn should be given, and the lower robe that was worn should be received. A belt should be given. The outer robes, having been folded, should be given. The bowl, having been washed, should be given with water.

“Ettāvatā nivattissatīti āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Thinking, 'He will return by this time,' a seat should be prepared; foot-washing water, a footstool, and a foot-wiping potsherd should be placed nearby. One should go to meet him and receive his bowl and robe. The monastery lower robe should be given; the village lower robe should be received. If the robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the sun for a long time. The robe should be folded. While folding the robe, lifting the edge, it should be folded thinking, 'May there not be a crease in the middle.' A waistband should be placed in the fold.

“Sace piṇḍapāto hoti, saddhivihāriko ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Saddhivihāriko pānīyena pucchitabbo. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ [P 2.0229] vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Saddhivihārikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo[T 2.0256].

If there is almsfood and the co-resident wishes to eat, after giving water, the almsfood should be offered. The co-resident should be asked about drinking water. After he has eaten, water should be given, the bowl received, held low, and carefully washed without scraping it. After making it free of water, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the bowl should not be left in the sun for long. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, taking the bowl with one hand and feeling under the bench or under the seat with the other hand, the bowl should be put away. And the bowl should not be put away on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, taking the robe with one hand and wiping the robe-pole or the robe-rope with the other hand, the robe should be put away by making a fold from the near side, bringing the far end over. When the co-resident has arisen, the seat should be removed; the water for washing feet, the footstool, and the foot-wiping potsherd should be put away. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.

“Sace saddhivihāriko nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

If the co-resident wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If there is need of cold water, cold water should be prepared. If there is need of hot water, hot water should be prepared.

“Sace [M 0.0400] saddhivihāriko jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya ādāya saddhivihārikassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito (ka.) gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ, na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare saddhivihārikassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the co-resident wishes to enter the steam-room, the bath powder should be kneaded and the clay should be moistened. Taking the steam-room stool, one should go, give him the steam-room stool, receive his robe, and place it in a suitable place. The bath powder should be given, and the clay should be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam-room. When entering the steam-room, having smeared one's face with clay and having covered oneself in front and behind, one should enter. One should not sit down encroaching upon the senior monks, nor should junior monks be debarred from a seat. In the steam-room, service should be done for the co-resident. When leaving the steam-room, taking the steam-room stool and covering oneself in front and behind, one should exit from the steam-room.

“Udakepi [V 0.0374] saddhivihārikassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā saddhivihārikassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ. Saddhivihāriko pānīyena pucchitabbo.

At the bathing place also, service should be done for the co-resident. Having bathed, one should emerge from the water first, make one's own body dry, put on one's lower robe, and then the water should be wiped from the co-resident’s body. The lower robe should be given, and the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam-room stool, one should return first, prepare a seat, and place nearby water for the feet, a footstool, and a foot-wiping potsherd. The co-resident should be asked about drinking water.

“Yasmiṃ vihāre saddhivihāriko viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā [T 2.0257] ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ…pe… sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

In whichever dwelling the co-resident lives, if that dwelling is dirty, it should be cleaned if one is able. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robes should be taken out and placed in a suitable place. … If there is no water in the water-pot for rinsing, water should be poured into the water-pot for rinsing.

“Sace saddhivihārikassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, upajjhāyena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace saddhivihārikassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace saddhivihārikassa [P 2.0230] diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace saddhivihāriko garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace saddhivihāriko mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho hoti, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace saddhivihāriko mānattāraho hoti, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho [M 0.0401] saddhivihārikassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace saddhivihāriko abbhānāraho hoti, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho saddhivihārikassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa [T 2.0258] hoti saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā, ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihāriko sammā vatteyya lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If discontent has arisen for the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should assuage it, or cause it to be assuaged, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse has arisen for the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should dispel it, or cause it to be dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view has arisen for the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should dispel it, or cause it to be dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If the co-resident pupil has committed a grave offense deserving probation, the preceptor should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant probation to the co-resident pupil?’ If the co-resident pupil deserves to be sent back to the beginning, the preceptor should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha send the co-resident pupil back to the beginning?’ If the co-resident pupil deserves penance, the preceptor should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant penance to the co-resident pupil?’ If the co-resident pupil deserves reinstatement, the preceptor should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha reinstate the co-resident pupil?’ If the Saṅgha wishes to carry out a formal act against the co-resident pupil—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the preceptor should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha not carry out the formal act against the co-resident pupil, or commute it to a lighter one?’ Or if a formal act has been carried out by the Saṅgha against him—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the preceptor should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the co-resident pupil conduct himself properly, humble himself, and conduct himself for his rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha might rescind that formal act?’

“Sace saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ dhoveyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace [V 0.0375] saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ kareyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace saddhivihārikassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ paceyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ rajeyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace saddhivihāriko gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo, vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave[P 2.0231], upajjhāyānaṃ saddhivihārikesu vattaṃ yathā upajjhāyehi saddhivihārikesu sammā vattitabba”nti.

If a co-resident pupil’s robe is to be washed, the preceptor should instruct him, saying: ‘You should wash it thus,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the co-resident pupil’s robe be washed?’ If a co-resident pupil’s robe is to be made, the preceptor should instruct him, saying: ‘You should make it thus,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the co-resident pupil’s robe be made?’ If dye is to be prepared for the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should instruct him, saying: ‘You should prepare it thus,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might dye be prepared for the co-resident pupil?’ If a co-resident pupil’s robe is to be dyed, the preceptor should instruct him, saying: ‘You should dye it thus,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the co-resident pupil’s robe be dyed?’ When dyeing a robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over, and one should not depart before the dripping has ceased. If the co-resident pupil is sick, he is to be attended to for as long as he lives; his recovery should be awaited. This, O monks, is the duty for preceptors towards their co-resident pupils, according to which preceptors ought to conduct themselves properly towards their co-resident pupils.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is concluded.

13. Ācariyavattakathā

13. The Discourse on the Teacher's Duties

379. Tena [T 2.0259] kho pana samayena antevāsikā ācariyesu na sammā vattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma antevāsikā ācariyesu na sammā vattissantī”ti! Atha [M 0.0402] kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, antevāsikā ācariyesu na sammā vattantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

379. Now at that time, resident pupils were not conducting themselves properly towards their teachers. Those monks who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed can resident pupils not conduct themselves properly towards their teachers?’ Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One... ‘Is it true, as is said, O monks, that resident pupils are not conducting themselves properly towards their teachers?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’... Having rebuked them... having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

380. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, antevāsikānaṃ ācariyesu vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā antevāsikehi ācariyesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. mahāva. 78 Antevāsikena, bhikkhave, ācariyamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

380. “Therefore, monks, I will lay down the duties for resident pupils towards their teachers, so that resident pupils may conduct themselves properly towards their teachers. Monks, a resident pupil should conduct himself properly towards his teacher. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

“Kālasseva uṭṭhāya upāhanā omuñcitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena [V 0.0376] dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Ācariyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

“Having risen early, having taken off his sandals, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, a tooth-stick should be given, water for the face should be given, and a seat should be prepared. If there is gruel, having washed the bowl, the gruel should be offered.
