When he has drunk the gruel, having given water, having received the bowl, holding it low, it should be washed carefully without scraping it and put away. When the teacher has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place is dirty, that place should be swept.

“Sace ācariyo gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto [T 2.0260] sodako dātabbo. Sace ācariyo pacchāsamaṇaṃ ākaṅkhati, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā ācariyassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ. Nātidūre gantabbaṃ, nāccāsanne gantabbaṃ, pattapariyāpannaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Na ācariyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbā. Ācariyo āpattisāmantā bhaṇamāno nivāretabbo.

“If the teacher wishes to enter the village, the lower robe for wearing in the village should be given, and the lower robe for wearing in the monastery should be received. The belt should be given. Having folded them, the outer robes should be given. Having washed it, the bowl with water should be given. If the teacher desires an attendant monk, then, covering the three circles, having worn the lower robe evenly all around, having fastened the belt, having folded the outer robes and put them on, having fastened the clasp, having washed and taken the bowl, one should be the teacher's attendant monk. One should not go too far, nor too close. What has come into the bowl should be received. One should not interrupt with speech while the teacher is speaking. If the teacher is speaking in a way that borders on an offense, he should be prevented.”

“Nivattantena paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

“Upon returning, one should come before the teacher and prepare a seat. Foot-washing water, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. Having gone out to meet him, the bowl and robe should be received. The monastery lower garment should be given; the village-going lower garment should be received. If the robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the sun for a long time. The robe should be folded. When folding the robe, it should be folded leaving a four finger-breadth margin at the edge, thinking, 'Let there not be a crease in the middle.' The waistband should be placed inside the fold.

“Sace piṇḍapāto hoti, ācariyo ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Ācariyo pānīyena pucchitabbo[M 0.0403]. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ [T 2.0261] vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ācariyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

“If there is almsfood and the teacher wishes to eat, having given water, the almsfood should be offered. The teacher should be asked about drinking water. When he has finished eating, water should be given, the bowl received, held low, and carefully washed without scraping it on the ground. Having made it free of water, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the bowl should not be left in the sun for a long time. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, taking the bowl with one hand and feeling under the bed or under the stool with the other hand, the bowl should be put away. The bowl should not be put away on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, taking the robe with one hand and wiping the robe-rail or the robe-line with the other hand, making the end on the far side and the fold on the near side, the robe should be put away. When the teacher has risen, the seat should be removed; the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet should be put away. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.

“Sace ācariyo nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

“If the teacher wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If cold water is needed, cold water should be prepared. If hot water is needed, hot water should be prepared.”

“Sace [V 0.0377] ācariyo jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya ācariyassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare ācariyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the teacher wishes to enter the steam room, the aromatic powder should be mixed with water and the clay should be moistened. Taking the steam room stool, having gone behind the teacher, the steam room stool should be given, the robe should be received and placed in a suitable place. The aromatic powder should be given, and the clay should be given. If one is able, the steam room should be entered. When entering the steam room, one should smear one's face with clay, and having covered oneself in front and behind, one should enter the steam room. One should not sit down crowding the elder monks. Junior monks should not be obstructed from a seat. In the steam room, service for the teacher should be performed. When leaving the steam room, one should take the steam room stool, and having covered oneself in front and behind, one should exit from the steam room.

“Udakepi ācariyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano [T 2.0262] gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā ācariyassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ. Ācariyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Sace uddisāpetukāmo hoti, uddisitabbo. Sace paripucchitukāmo hoti, paripucchitabbo.

Also at the bathing place, service for the teacher should be performed. Having bathed, one should emerge from the water first, make one's own body dry, and put on one's lower robe. Then the water from the teacher's body should be wiped; the lower robe should be given, and the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam room stool, one should return first, prepare the seat, and place nearby the water for the feet, the footstool, and the foot-scraper. The teacher should be asked about drinking water. If he wishes to teach the Pāli, he should be asked to teach. If he wishes to be questioned on the commentary, he should be questioned.

“Yasmiṃ [M 0.0404] vihāre ācariyo viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā [T 2.0263] bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā pariphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

In the dwelling where the teacher resides, if that dwelling is untidy, and if one is able, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robe should be taken out and set aside in a suitable place; the sitting-cloth and ground-cover should be taken out and set aside in a suitable place; the mattress and pillow should be taken out and set aside in a suitable place; the bed should be handled carefully, without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-post, taken out, and set aside in a suitable place; the stool should be handled carefully, without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-post, taken out, and set aside in a suitable place; the bed-legs should be taken out and set aside in a suitable place; the spittoon should be taken out and set aside in a suitable place; the leaning-board should be taken out and set aside in a suitable place; the floor-covering should be noted as it was laid, taken out, and set aside in a suitable place. If the dwelling has cobwebs, they should first be removed from the ceiling, and the corners of the window openings should be wiped. If the walls, finished with red ochre, are mildewed, a cloth should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe them. If the floor, finished with a black color, is mildewed, a cloth should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is unfinished, it should be sprinkled with water and swept, taking care that dust does not rise in the dwelling. The sweepings should be collected and discarded in a suitable place.

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ [V 0.0378] otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā [M 0.0405] patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ [T 2.0264] vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The floor covering should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The bed legs should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in their usual place. The bed should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, and handled carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door-leaf or door-post, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The stool should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, and handled carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without knocking it against the door-leaf or door-post, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The mattress and pillow should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The sitting-cloth and ground-cover should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The spittoon should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The leaning board should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting the bowl away, one should take the bowl with one hand, feel underneath the bed or stool with the other hand, and then put the bowl down. The bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting the robe away, one should take the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-pole or robe-line with the other hand, and place the robe with its end on the far side and its fold on the near side.

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the precincts are dirty, the precincts should be swept. If the gatehouse is dirty, the gatehouse should be swept. If the service hall is dirty, the service hall should be swept. If the fire hall is dirty, the fire hall should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

“Sace ācariyassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, antevāsikena vūpakāsetabbā, vūpakāsāpetabbā, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace ācariyassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, antevāsikena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace ācariyassa diṭṭhigataṃ [V 0.0379] uppannaṃ hoti[T 2.0265], antevāsikena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace ācariyo garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, parivāsāraho, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace ācariyo mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho hoti, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace ācariyo mānattāraho hoti, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace ācariyo abbhānāraho hoti, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho ācariyassa [M 0.0406] kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyo sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If discontent has arisen for the teacher, the resident pupil should lead him away to another place, or cause him to be led away, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse has arisen for the teacher, it should be dispelled by the resident pupil, or he should cause it to be dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view has arisen for the teacher, the resident pupil should make him abandon it, or cause him to be made to abandon it, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If the teacher has committed a serious offense and is deserving of probation, the resident pupil should make an effort, thinking: 'How indeed might the Saṅgha grant probation to the teacher?' If the teacher is deserving of being sent back to the beginning, the resident pupil should make an effort, thinking: 'How indeed might the Saṅgha send the teacher back to the beginning?' If the teacher is deserving of penance, the resident pupil should make an effort, thinking: 'How indeed might the Saṅgha grant penance to the teacher?' If the teacher is deserving of rehabilitation, the resident pupil should make an effort, thinking: 'How indeed might the Saṅgha rehabilitate the teacher?' If the Saṅgha wishes to perform an act against the teacher—be it an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—the resident pupil should make an effort, thinking: 'How indeed might the Saṅgha not perform the act against the teacher, or how might it be converted to a lighter one?' Or if an act has been performed against him by the Saṅgha—be it an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—the resident pupil should make an effort, thinking: 'How indeed might the teacher behave properly, how might he humble himself, how might he conduct himself for deliverance from that act, so that the Saṅgha might revoke that act?'

“Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena dhovitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena kātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ [T 2.0266] vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace ācariyassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena pacitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena rajitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ.

If the teacher's robe is to be washed, it should be washed by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, wondering: 'How indeed might the teacher's robe be washed?' If the teacher's robe is to be made, it should be made by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, wondering: 'How indeed might the teacher's robe be made?' If dye is to be prepared for the teacher, it should be prepared by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, wondering: 'How indeed might dye be prepared for the teacher?' If the teacher's robe is to be dyed, it should be dyed by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, wondering: 'How indeed might the teacher's robe be dyed?' When dyeing the robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over, and one should not depart before the dripping of the dye has ceased.

“Na ācariyaṃ anāpucchā ekaccassa patto dātabbo, na ekaccassa patto paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa parikkhāro dātabbo, na ekaccassa parikkhāro paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa kesā cheditabbā, na ekaccena kesā chedāpetabbā; na ekaccassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ekaccena parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa veyyāvacco kātabbo, na ekaccena veyyāvacco kārāpetabbo; na ekaccassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ, na ekacco pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo; na ekaccassa piṇḍapāto nīharitabbo, na ekaccena piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo; na [V 0.0380] ācariyaṃ anāpucchā gāmo pavisitabbo; na susānaṃ gantabbaṃ; na disā pakkamitabbā. Sace ācariyo gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo[M 0.0407], vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, antevāsikānaṃ ācariyesu vattaṃ yathā [T 2.0267] antevāsikehi ācariyesu sammā vattitabba”nti.

Without asking the teacher, a bowl should not be given to another, nor should a bowl be received from another; a robe should not be given to another, nor should a robe be received from another; requisites should not be given to another, nor should requisites be received from another; hair should not be cut for another, nor should one have one's hair cut by another; a personal service should not be performed for another, nor should one have a personal service performed by another; services should not be performed for another, nor should one have services performed by another; one should not be an attendant monk to another, nor should one take another as an attendant monk; alms-food should not be brought out for another, nor should one have alms-food brought out by another. Without asking the teacher, a village should not be entered; a charnel ground should not be gone to; one should not depart to another region. If the teacher is sick, he should be attended to for as long as he lives; his recovery should be awaited. This indeed, O monks, is the duty of resident pupils towards their teachers, according to which resident pupils should conduct themselves properly towards their teachers.

14. Antevāsikavattakathā

14. The Discourse on the Duties of a Resident Pupil

381. Tena kho pana samayena ācariyā antevāsikesu na sammā vattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ācariyā antevāsikesu na sammā vattissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, ācariyā antevāsikesu na sammā vattantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

381. Now at that time, teachers were not conducting themselves properly towards their resident pupils. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can teachers not conduct themselves properly towards their resident pupils!” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this cause, on this occasion, having convened the Saṅgha of monks, questioned the monks: “Is it true, monks, as has been heard, that teachers do not conduct themselves properly towards their resident pupils?” “It is true, Blessed One.”… Having rebuked them… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

382. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, ācariyānaṃ antevāsikesu vattaṃ paññapessāmi yathā ācariyehi antevāsikesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. mahāva. 79 Ācariyena, bhikkhave, antevāsikamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

382. “Well then, monks, I will lay down the duties for teachers towards their resident pupils, how a teacher should conduct himself properly towards his resident pupils. A teacher, monks, should conduct himself properly towards a resident pupil. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

“Ācariyena, bhikkhave, antevāsiko saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā. Sace ācariyassa patto hoti, antevāsikassa patto na hoti, ācariyena antevāsikassa patto dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa patto uppajjiyethāti. Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ hoti, antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ na hoti, ācariyena antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ uppajjiyethāti. Sace ācariyassa parikkhāro hoti, antevāsikassa [T 2.0268] parikkhāro na hoti, ācariyena antevāsikassa parikkhāro dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa parikkhāro uppajjiyethāti.

“Monks, a teacher should support and help a resident pupil by recitation, by questioning, by admonition, and by instruction. If the teacher has a bowl and the resident pupil does not have a bowl, the teacher should give a bowl to the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might a bowl arise for the resident pupil?’ If the teacher has a robe and the resident pupil does not have a robe, the teacher should give a robe to the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might a robe arise for the resident pupil?’ If the teacher has requisites and the resident pupil does not have requisites, the teacher should give requisites to the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might requisites arise for the resident pupil?’”

“Sace antevāsiko gilāno hoti, kālasseva uṭṭhāya dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti[M 0.0408], bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ[V 0.0381]. Antevāsikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

“If the resident pupil is sick, one should rise early and provide a tooth-stick and water for the face, and prepare a seat. If there is gruel, one should wash the bowl and offer the gruel. After he has drunk the gruel, one should give water, receive the bowl, and holding it low, wash it carefully without scraping it, and put it away. When the resident pupil has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.”

“Sace antevāsiko gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto sodako dātabbo.

“If the resident pupil wishes to enter a village, the lower robe for going out should be given, and the lower robe for the monastery should be received. The belt should be given. Having folded them, the outer robes should be given. The bowl, having been washed, should be given with water.”

“Ettāvatā nivattissatīti āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

“Thinking, ‘He will return by this time,’ a seat should be prepared; water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. One should go to meet him and receive his bowl and robe. The lower robe for the monastery should be given, and the lower robe for the village should be received. If a robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but a robe should not be left in the sun for a long time. The robe should be folded. When folding the robe, one should fold it leaving a border of four finger-widths, thinking, ‘May there not be a crease in the middle.’ The belt should be placed in the fold.”

“Sace piṇḍapāto hoti, antevāsiko ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Antevāsiko [T 2.0269] pānīyena pucchitabbo. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena…pe… cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena…pe… pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Antevāsikamhi uṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

“If there is almsfood and the resident pupil wishes to eat, water should be given and the almsfood should be offered. The resident pupil should be asked if he requires drinking water. After he has eaten, water should be given, the bowl should be received, held low, carefully washed without scraping it, and dried of water. It should be placed in the sun for a moment, but the bowl should not be left in the sun for a long time. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl... and so on... when putting away the robe... and so on... the robe should be put away, having made a coil on this side with the end from the other side. When the resident pupil has risen, the seat should be put away; the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the foot-rubbing potsherd should be stored away. If that place is littered, that place should be swept.”

“Sace antevāsiko nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

“If the resident pupil wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If cold water is needed, cold water should be prepared. If hot water is needed, hot water should be prepared.”

“Sace antevāsiko jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya ādāya antevāsikassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito (ka.) gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena [M 0.0409] mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā[V 0.0382]. Jantāghare antevāsikassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

“If the resident pupil wishes to enter the steam room, bathing powder should be mixed with water and clay should be moistened. Taking the steam room stool, one should go, give the stool, receive the robe, and put it away in a suitable place. The bathing powder should be given, and the clay should be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam room. When entering the steam room, one should smear one's face with clay, cover oneself in front and behind, and then enter. One should not sit down encroaching upon the elder monks. Junior monks should not be prevented from taking a seat. In the steam room, service should be done for the resident pupil. When leaving the steam room, one should take the steam room stool, cover oneself in front and behind, and then leave.”

“Udakepi antevāsikassa [T 2.0270] parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā antevāsikassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, antevāsiko pānīyena pucchitabbo.

“In the bathing place also, service should be done for the resident pupil. Having bathed and come out of the water first, having made one’s own body dry and put on the lower robe, water should be wiped from the resident pupil’s body; the lower robe should be given; the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam-bath stool and having come first, a seat should be prepared; foot-washing water, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby; the resident pupil should be asked about drinking water.”

“Yasmiṃ vihāre antevāsiko viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ…pe… ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

“In whichever dwelling a resident pupil resides, if that dwelling is dirty, and if one is able, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robes should be taken out and placed in a suitable place... and so on... If there is no water in the rinsing water pot, water should be poured into the rinsing water pot.”

“Sace antevāsikassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, ācariyena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace antevāsikassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, ācariyena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace antevāsikassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, ācariyena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace antevāsiko garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, parivāsāraho, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace antevāsiko mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho hoti, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace antevāsiko mānattāraho hoti, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ [T 2.0271] – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace antevāsiko abbhānāraho hoti, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho antevāsikassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikassa kammaṃ na kareyya[M 0.0410], lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa hoti, saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsiko sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

“If discontent has arisen in a resident pupil, the teacher should lead him away to another place, or cause him to be led away, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse has arisen in a resident pupil, the teacher should dispel it, or cause it to be dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view has arisen in a resident pupil, the teacher should make him abandon it, or cause him to abandon it, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a resident pupil has committed a serious offense and is deserving of probation, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How indeed might the Saṅgha grant probation to the resident pupil?’ If a resident pupil is deserving of being sent back to the beginning, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How indeed might the Saṅgha send the resident pupil back to the beginning?’ If a resident pupil is deserving of penance, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How indeed might the Saṅgha grant penance to the resident pupil?’ If a resident pupil is deserving of rehabilitation, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How indeed might the Saṅgha rehabilitate the resident pupil?’ If the Saṅgha wishes to carry out a formal act against a resident pupil—be it an act of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the teacher should make an effort: ‘How indeed might the Saṅgha not carry out the formal act against the resident pupil, or how might it be inclined towards a lighter one?’ Or if a formal act has been carried out against him by the Saṅgha—be it an act of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the teacher should make an effort: ‘How indeed might the resident pupil conduct himself properly, humble himself, and live for his deliverance from that act, so that the Saṅgha might revoke that formal act?’”

“Sace [V 0.0383] antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ dhoveyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ kareyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace antevāsikassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ paceyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – evaṃ rajeyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ [T 2.0272] – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ. Na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace antevāsiko gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo, vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ācariyānaṃ antevāsikesu vattaṃ yathā ācariyehi antevāsikesu sammā vattitabba”nti.

“If a resident pupil’s robe needs to be washed, the teacher should instruct him: ‘You should wash it thus,’ or he should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the resident pupil’s robe be washed?’ If a resident pupil’s robe needs to be made, the teacher should instruct him: ‘You should make it thus,’ or he should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the resident pupil’s robe be made?’ If dye needs to be boiled for a resident pupil, the teacher should instruct him: ‘You should boil it thus,’ or he should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might dye be boiled for the resident pupil?’ If a resident pupil’s robe needs to be dyed, the teacher should instruct him: ‘You should dye it thus,’ or he should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the resident pupil’s robe be dyed?’ When dyeing a robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over. And one should not depart while the dye has not ceased dripping. If a resident pupil is ill, he should be attended to for as long as he lives; one should wait for his recovery. This, bhikkhus, is the duty of teachers towards their resident pupils, according to which teachers should conduct themselves properly towards their resident pupils.”

Vattakkhandhako aṭṭhamo.

The eighth Chapter on Duties is finished.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū ekūnavīsati, vattā cuddasa.

In this chapter, there are nineteen stories and fourteen duties.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Saupāhanā chattā ca, oguṇṭhi sīsaṃ pānīyaṃ;

Nābhivāde na pucchanti, ahi ujjhanti pesalā.

Wearing sandals, with an umbrella, head covered, a robe on the head, drinking water; they do not pay homage, they do not ask; a snake; the virtuous complain.

Omuñci chattaṃ khandhe ca, atarañca paṭikkamaṃ;

Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipā, patirūpañca pucchitā.

Removing the umbrella, and from the shoulder; retreating unhurriedly; laying down the bowl and robe, and asking about a suitable place.

Āsiñceyya dhovitena, sukkhenallenupāhanā;

Vuḍḍho navako puccheyya, ajjhāvuṭṭhañca gocarā.

One should sprinkle with what has been washed; with a dry and a wet cloth for the sandals; the elder should ask the junior about the residence and the alms-resort.

Sekkhā [M 0.0411] vaccā pānī pari, kattaraṃ katikaṃ tato;

Kālaṃ [T 2.0273] muhuttaṃ uklāpo, bhūmattharaṇaṃ nīhare.

Trainees, the latrine, drinking water, water for use, a staff, an agreement; then time, a moment, rubbish; one should remove the ground-covering.

Paṭipādo [V 0.0384] bhisibibbo, mañcapīṭhañca mallakaṃ;

Apassenullokakaṇṇā, gerukā kāḷa akatā.

A bed-leg support, a mattress, a pillow, a bed and a stool, and a spittoon; a leaning-board, a ceiling, corners; red ochre, black color, an unprepared floor.

Saṅkārañca bhūmattharaṇaṃ, paṭipādakaṃ mañcapīṭhaṃ;

Bhisi nisīdanampi, mallakaṃ apassena ca.

Refuse and a ground-covering, a footstool, a bed and a chair; a cushion and a sitting-mat, a spittoon, and a leaning-board.

Pattacīvaraṃ bhūmi ca, pārantaṃ orato bhogaṃ;

Puratthimā pacchimā ca, uttarā atha dakkhiṇā.

The bowl and robes, and the bare ground; the far side, a coil from the near side; the east wind and the west wind, the north wind, and then the south wind.

Sītuṇhe ca divārattiṃ, pariveṇañca koṭṭhako;

Upaṭṭhānaggi sālā ca, vattaṃ vaccakuṭīsu ca.

In cold and heat, by day and night; the monastic compound and the gatehouse; the assembly hall and the fire-hall; and the duty in the latrines.

Pānī paribhojaniyā, kumbhi ācamanesu ca;

Anopamena paññattaṃ, vattaṃ āgantukehime ve (ka. evamuparipi).

Drinking water, water for use, and a pot for water for rinsing; this duty for visiting monks was laid down by the Incomparable One.

Nevāsanaṃ na udakaṃ, na paccu na ca pāniyaṃ;

Nābhivāde napaññape, ujjhāyanti ca pesalā.

No seat is prepared, no water is set out, one does not go out to meet, and no drinking water is offered; one does not pay homage, nor prepare a seat; and the virtuous monks complain.

Vuḍḍhāsanañca udakaṃ, paccuggantvā ca pāniyaṃ;

Upāhane ekamantaṃ, abhivāde ca paññape.

A seat for the senior monk and water; having gone out to meet, and drinking water; sandals to one side; one should pay homage and prepare the seat.

Vutthaṃ [P 2.0232] gocarasekkho ca, ṭhānaṃ pāniyabhojanaṃ;

Kattaraṃ katikaṃ kālaṃ, navakassa nisinnake.

The monastery where one has stayed, the alms-round village, and the designated trainee; the place for relieving oneself, drinking water, and water for use; the staff, the regulation, the time, and the seating for a junior monk.

Abhivādaye [T 2.0274] ācikkhe, yathā heṭṭhā tathā naye;

Niddiṭṭhaṃ satthavāhena vattaṃ āvāsikehime.

One should pay homage and inform; one should conduct oneself as instructed below. This duty for resident monks has been specified by the Caravan Leader.

Gamikā dārumatti ca, vivaritvā na pucchiya;

Nassanti ca aguttañca, ujjhāyanti ca pesalā.

A departing monk, having left wooden and clay furnishings exposed and without asking anyone; they are destroyed because they are unguarded, and the virtuous monks complain.

Paṭisāmetvā [V 0.0385] thaketvā, āpucchitvāva pakkame;

Bhikkhu vā sāmaṇero vā, ārāmiko upāsako.

Having stored things away and closed up, one should depart only after taking leave of a monk, or a novice, or a monastery attendant, or a layman.

Pāsāṇakesu ca puñjaṃ, paṭisāme thakeyya ca;

Sace ussahati ussukkaṃ, anovasse tatheva ca.

One should also store away and cover the collection of things on the stones. If one is able, one should make an effort, and do likewise in a place where it does not rain.

Sabbo [M 0.0412] ovassati gāmaṃ, ajjhokāse tatheva ca;

Appevaṅgāni seseyyuṃ, vattaṃ gamikabhikkhunā.

If it rains everywhere, one should take things to the village; likewise if in the open. Even if only the frame remains, this is the duty for a departing monk.

Nānumodanti therena, ohāya catupañcahi;

Vaccito mucchito āsi, vattānumodanesume.

They do not give the blessing with the elder, having left him behind with four or five others. He was afflicted by dysentery and fainted. These are the duties concerning the giving of blessings.

Chabbaggiyā dunnivatthā, athopi ca duppārutā;

Anākappā ca vokkamma, there anupakhajjane.

The group-of-six monks were improperly dressed and also improperly covered; with incorrect deportment, they swaggered and jostled the elder monks.

Nave bhikkhū ca saṅghāṭi, ujjhāyanti ca pesalā;

Timaṇḍalaṃ [T 2.0275] nivāsetvā, kāyasaguṇagaṇṭhikā.

The virtuous monks complain about the new monks and the outer robe. One should wear the lower robe covering the three circles, with the waistband, the doubled upper robe, and the knot.

Na vokkamma paṭicchannaṃ, susaṃvutokkhittacakkhu;

Ukkhittojjagghikāsaddo, tayo ceva pacālanā.

Not swaggering, being well-covered, well-restrained with downcast eyes; not hitching up the robe, not laughing loudly, making little noise, and the three kinds of swaying.

Khambhoguṇṭhiukkuṭikā, paṭicchannaṃ susaṃvuto;

Okkhittukkhittaujjagghi, appasaddo tayo calā.

Arms akimbo, a covered head, and squatting on the heels; one should be well-covered and well-restrained, with downcast eyes, not hitching up the robe, not laughing loudly, making little sound, and avoiding the three kinds of swaying.

Khambhoguṇṭhipallatthi ca, anupakhajja nāsane;

Ottharitvāna udake, nīcaṃ katvāna siñciyā.

With hands on hips, with head covered, and sitting cross-legged with a strap; one should not sit encroaching upon a seat; having submerged [the bowl] in water and holding it low, one should sprinkle.

Paṭi sāmantā saṅghāṭi, odane ca paṭiggahe;

Sūpaṃ uttaribhaṅgena, sabbesaṃ samatitthi ca.

Nearby the double-layered outer robe, one should receive rice; curry as an extra portion, and for all, level with the brim.

Sakkaccaṃ [V 0.0386] pattasaññī ca, sapadānañca sūpakaṃ;

Na thūpato paṭicchāde, viññattujjhānasaññinā.

Respectfully and being mindful of the bowl, one should receive curry in sequence. One should not press down the top of the rice; one should cover [the curry]. One should not request with the intention of finding fault.

Mahantamaṇḍaladvāraṃ, sabbahattho na byāhare;

Ukkhepo chedanāgaṇḍa, dhunaṃ sitthāvakārakaṃ.

One should not make a very large or round mouthful, nor open the mouth wide; one should not speak with the whole hand [in the mouth]. Tossing up the mouthful, biting off mouthfuls, stuffing the cheeks, shaking the hand, and scattering rice grains are prohibited.

Jivhānicchārakañceva, capucapu surusuru;

Hatthapattoṭṭhanillehaṃ, sāmisena paṭiggahe.

And sticking out the tongue, making 'capu capu' sounds, making 'suru suru' sounds; licking the hand, scraping the bowl, licking the lips; and receiving a water vessel with a hand soiled with food are prohibited.

Yāva [T 2.0276] na sabbe udake, nīcaṃ katvāna siñciyaṃ;

Paṭi sāmantā saṅghāṭi, nīcaṃ katvā chamāya ca.

As long as not all monks have finished, one should sprinkle water holding the bowl low. One should place the bowl low on the ground near the double-layered outer robe.

Sasitthakaṃ nivattante, suppaṭicchannamukkuṭi;

Dhammarājena paññattaṃ, idaṃ bhattaggavattanaṃ.

When returning the water containing rice grains; being well-covered and squatting; this duty of the refectory was laid down by the King of Dhamma.

Dunnivatthā [M 0.0413] anākappā, asallekkhetvā ca sahasā;

Dūre acca ciraṃ lahuṃ, tatheva piṇḍacāriko.

Being badly dressed, lacking proper deportment, and being unmindful and hasty; standing too far, too near, for too long, or departing too quickly; likewise for a monk on alms-round.

Paṭicchannova [P 2.0233] gaccheyya, suṃsavutokkhittacakkhu;

Ukkhittojjagghikāsaddo, tayo ceva pacālanā.

One should go well-covered, well-restrained, with eyes cast down. Lifting the robe, laughing loudly, making noise, and the three kinds of swaying are prohibited.

Khambhoguṇṭhiukkuṭikā, sallakkhetvā ca sahasā;

Dūre acca ciraṃ lahuṃ, āsanakaṃ kaṭacchukā.

With hands on hips, with head covered, and squatting; and having taken note, hastily; too far, too near, for too long, too quickly; a seat, a ladle.

Bhājanaṃ vā ṭhapeti ca, uccāretvā paṇāmetvā;

Paṭiggahe na ulloke, sūpesupi tatheva taṃ.

Or one places a vessel; having moved it aside and having offered it, one should receive. One should not look up when receiving; that same duty applies also to curries.

Bhikkhu saṅghāṭiyā chāde, paṭicchanneva gacchiyaṃ;

Saṃvutokkhittacakkhu ca, ukkhittojjagghikāya ca;

Appasaddo tayo cālā, khambhoguṇṭhikaukkuṭi.

A monk should cover himself with the double-layered outer robe; he should go about well-covered. He should be well-restrained with eyes cast down, not lifting the robe and not laughing loudly. He should make little sound and avoid the three swayings, placing hands on hips, covering the head, and squatting.

Paṭhamāsanavakkāra[V 0.0387], pāniyaṃ paribhojanī;

Pacchākaṅkhati bhuñjeyya, opilāpeyya uddhare.

Firstly, the seat, the bowl for the first portion, drinking water, and water for use. Afterwards, if one desires, one may eat. One should pour out water and clear away.

Paṭisāmeyya [T 2.0277] sammajje, rittaṃ tucchaṃ upaṭṭhape;

Hatthavikāre bhindeyya, vattidaṃ piṇḍacārike.

One should store away and sweep; one should set up the empty vessel. One should not make gestures with the hand. This is the duty in the alms-round.

Pānī pari aggiraṇi, nakkhattadisacorā ca;

Sabbaṃ natthīti koṭṭetvā, pattaṃse cīvaraṃ tato.

Drinking water, water for use, fire, and fire-sticks; constellations, directions, and thieves. Having been struck and told, 'There is nothing at all,' then one places the bowl and robe on the shoulder.

Idāni aṃse laggetvā, timaṇḍalaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ;

Yathā piṇḍacārivattaṃ, naye āraññakesupi.

Now, having slung the bowl on the shoulder, wearing the robes to cover the three circles and be evenly round; just as the duty of the alms-round is, so too should one apply it to the duties of forest-dwellers.

Pattaṃse cīvaraṃ sīse, ārohitvā ca pāniyaṃ;

Paribhojaniyaṃ aggi, araṇī cāpi kattaraṃ.

The bowl on the shoulder, the robe on the head; and having put on sandals; also drinking water, water for use, fire, fire-sticks, and a staff.

Nakkhattaṃ sappadesaṃ vā, disāpi kusalo bhave;

Sattuttamena paññattaṃ, vattaṃ āraññakesume.

One should be skilled in the constellations and their regions, and also in the directions. By the Supreme among beings, these duties for forest-dwellers were laid down.

Ajjhokāse okiriṃsu, ujjhāyanti ca pesalā;

Sace vihāro uklāpo, paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ.

They scattered things in the open, and the monks of amiable virtue complained; if the monastery is full of rubbish, first one should secure the bowl and robe.

Bhisibibbohanaṃ mañcaṃ, pīṭhañca kheḷamallakaṃ;

Apassenullokakaṇṇā, gerukā kāḷa akatā.

A mattress, a pillow, a bedstead, a stool, and a spittoon; a leaning-board, the window has mold; the red ochre and black earth are unapplied.

Saṅkāraṃ [M 0.0414] bhikkhusāmantā, senāvihārapāniyaṃ;

Paribhojanasāmantā, paṭivāte ca aṅgaṇe.

Rubbish from the vicinity of a monk, from the lodging, the monastery, the drinking water, and from the vicinity of the water for use, should be disposed of on the downwind side and in the courtyard.

Adhovāte attharaṇaṃ, paṭipādakamañco ca;

Pīṭhaṃ [T 2.0278] bhisi nisīdanaṃ, mallakaṃ apassena ca.

Downwind, one should place the floor covering, the footstool and the bedstead, the stool, the mattress, the sitting cloth, the spittoon, and the leaning-board.

Pattacīvaraṃ [V 0.0388] bhūmi ca, pārantaṃ orato bhogaṃ;

Puratthimā ca pacchimā, uttarā atha dakkhiṇā.

The bowl and robe, and the bare ground; the far end from the near side, a fold; and from the east, west, north, then south.

Sītuṇhe ca divā rattiṃ, pariveṇañca koṭṭhako;

Upaṭṭhānaggisālā ca, vaccakuṭī ca pāniyaṃ.

In cold and heat, day and night; and the monastic compound, the gateway, the assembly hall, the fire-hall, the latrine, and the drinking water area.

Ācamanakumbhi vuḍḍhe ca, uddesapucchanā sajjhā;

Dhammo padīpaṃ vijjhāpe, na vivare napi thake.

A water pot for rinsing; and towards the elders: learning the text, questioning on the commentary, recitation, and preaching the Dhamma. Extinguishing a lamp; one should not open nor should one close doors.

Yena vuḍḍho parivatti, kaṇṇenapi na ghaṭṭaye;

Paññapesi mahāvīro, vattaṃ senāsanesu taṃ.

When moving about where an elder is, one should not touch him even with the corner of one's robe. The Great Hero laid down that duty concerning lodgings.

Nivāriyamānā dvāraṃ, mucchitujjhanti pesalā;

Chārikaṃ [P 2.0234] chaḍḍaye jantā, paribhaṇḍaṃ tatheva ca.

Being prevented at the door, they fainted; the monks of amiable virtue complained. One should discard ashes from the steam room, and likewise the rubbish.

Pariveṇaṃ koṭṭhako sālā, cuṇṇamattikadoṇikā;

Mukhaṃ purato na there, na nave ussahati sace.

The monastic compound, the gateway, the hall, the trough for powder and clay; one should not wash one's face in front of the elders, nor should one prevent the junior monks, if one is able.

Purato uparimaggo, cikkhallaṃ matti pīṭhakaṃ;

Vijjhāpetvā thaketvā ca, vattaṃ jantāgharesume.

In front, the upper path, the mud, the clay, the stool; having extinguished the fire and having closed the door, one should depart. These are the duties in the steam rooms.

Nācameti yathāvuḍḍhaṃ, paṭipāṭi ca sahasā;

Ubbhaji [T 2.0279] nitthuno kaṭṭhaṃ, vaccaṃ passāva kheḷakaṃ.

One should not fail to rinse with water, nor act out of sequence according to seniority, nor hastily lift the lower robe, nor groan. One should be mindful of the cleaning stick, the place for feces, the place for urine, and spittle.

Pharusā kūpa sahasā, ubbhaji capu sesena;

Bahi anto ca ukkāse, rajju ataramānañca.

Using a rough cleaning stick on the latrine pit; hastily lifting the lower robe; making a 'capu' sound; leaving remaining water; both outside and inside, one should clear one's throat; and one should act unhurriedly at the robe-line.

Sahasā ubbhaji ṭhite, nitthune kaṭṭha vaccañca;

Passāva kheḷa pharusā, kūpañca vaccapāduke.

Hastily lifting the lower robe while standing; groaning; improper use of the cleaning stick, the place for feces, the place for urine, and spittle; a rough cleaning stick on the pit; and on the latrine foot-stand.

Nātisahasā [V 0.0389] ubbhaji, pādukāya capucapu;

Na sesaye paṭicchāde, uhatapidharena ca.

One should not lift the lower robe too hastily; nor make a 'capu capu' sound on the foot-stand. One should not leave a remainder of water; one should cover the excrement. One should clean what is smeared with feces, and use the container for the cleaning stick.

Vaccakuṭī [M 0.0415] paribhaṇḍaṃ, pariveṇañca koṭṭhako;

Ācamane ca udakaṃ, vattaṃ vaccakuṭīsume.

The latrine, its equipment, the precinct, and the gateway; and water for rinsing—these are the duties concerning the latrines.

Upāhanā dantakaṭṭhaṃ, mukhodakañca āsanaṃ;

Yāgu udakaṃ dhovitvā, uddhāruklāpa gāma ca.

Footwear, a tooth-stick, and water for washing the face; a seat, gruel, and water; having washed, the removal of rubbish, and the village.

Nivāsanā kāyabandhā, saguṇaṃ pattasodakaṃ;

Pacchā timaṇḍalo ceva, parimaṇḍala bandhanaṃ.

The lower robe, the waistband, the double-layered outer robe, and the bowl with water; afterwards, the three circles, wearing it perfectly round, and the waistband.

Saguṇaṃ dhovitvā pacchā, nātidūre paṭiggahe;

Bhaṇamānassa āpatti, paṭhamāgantvāna āsanaṃ.

Having washed the double-layered outer robe, one should afterwards receive it in a place not too far away. An offense is incurred by one who, having gone to the seat first, speaks improperly.

Udakaṃ pīṭhakathali, paccuggantvā nivāsanaṃ;

Otāpe [T 2.0280] nidahi bhaṅgo, obhoge bhuñjitu name.

Water, a stool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet; having gone forward to meet; the lower robe; placing it in the sun; the fold of the robe; inside the coil; in order to eat, one should offer.

Pānīyaṃ udakaṃ nīcaṃ, muhuttaṃ na ca nidahe;

Pattacīvaraṃ bhūmi ca, pārantaṃ orato bhogaṃ.

Drinking water and water placed low down; for a moment, and not placing it for long. The bowl and robes, and the ground; the far end, the coil on this side.

Uddhare paṭisāme ca, uklāpo ca nahāyituṃ;

Sītaṃ uṇhaṃ jantāgharaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ mattika piṭṭhito.

One should clear away and put away rubbish. In order to bathe: cold water, hot water, the steam-bath house, bath powder, fine clay, and from behind.

Pīṭhañca cīvaraṃ cuṇṇaṃ, mattikussahati mukhaṃ;

Purato there nave ca, parikammañca nikkhame.

A stool, a robe, bath powder, and fine clay; if one is able, the face; in front of an elder and a junior monk; the act of scrubbing; and one should depart.

Purato udake nhāte, nivāsetvā upajjhāyaṃ;

Nivāsanañca saṅghāṭi, pīṭhakaṃ āsanena ca.

Beforehand; having bathed in water and having worn the lower robe; the preceptor; the lower robe and the double-layered outer robe, a stool, and a seat.

Pādo [V 0.0390] pīṭhaṃ kathaliñca, pānīyuddesapucchanā;

Uklāpaṃ susodheyya, paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ.

Water for washing the feet, a stool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet; drinking water, instruction in the Pāli, and questioning on the commentary. One should clean the rubbish well; first, the bowl and robes.

Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ, bhisi bibbohanāni ca;

Mañco pīṭhaṃ paṭipādaṃ, mallakaṃ apassena ca.

A sitting cloth and a spread, a mattress and pillows; a couch, a stool, a footstool, a spittoon, and a leaning-board.

Bhūma santāna āloka, gerukā kāḷa akatā;

Bhūmattharapaṭipādā, mañco pīṭhaṃ bibbohanaṃ.

The ground, cobwebs, the window, red ochre, black earth, and unprepared ground; a ground-covering, a footstool, a couch, a stool, and a pillow.

Nisīdattharaṇaṃ kheḷa, apasse pattacīvaraṃ;

Puratthimā [P 2.0235] pacchimā ca, uttarā atha dakkhiṇā.

A sitting cloth and spread, a spittoon, a leaning-board, the bowl and robes; wind from the east and from the west, from the north, and then from the south.

Sītuṇhañca [M 0.0416] divā rattiṃ, pariveṇañca koṭṭhako;

Upaṭṭhānaggisālā [T 2.0281] ca, vaccapāniyabhojanī.

The cold and hot seasons, day and night, the precinct and the gateway; the assembly hall and the fire-hall, the latrine, drinking water, and water for use.

Ācamaṃ anabhirati, kukkuccaṃ diṭṭhi ca garu;

Mūlamānattaabbhānaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ niyassakaṃ.

Rinsing water, discontent, remorse, and wrong view; a grave offense, sending back to the beginning, undergoing penance, rehabilitation, the act of censure, and the act of subordination.

Pabbāja paṭisāraṇī, ukkhepañca kataṃ yadi;

Dhove kātabbaṃ rajañca, raje samparivattakaṃ.

The act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the act of suspension, if it has been done. Washing should be done, and dye; one should dye it, turning it over and over.

Pattañca cīvarañcāpi, parikkhārañca chedanaṃ;

Parikammaṃ veyyāvaccaṃ, pacchā piṇḍaṃ pavisanaṃ.

The bowl and also the robes, and the requisites; shaving the hair, the act of scrubbing, and service; for the accompanying junior monk, entering for alms-food.

Na susānaṃ disā ceva, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhahe;

Saddhivihārikenetaṃ, vattupajjhāyakesume.

One should not go to the charnel ground, nor to another region. One should attend for life. This is the duty of a co-resident pupil towards the preceptors.

Ovādasāsanuddesā, pucchā pattañca cīvaraṃ;

Parikkhāro gilāno ca, na pacchāsamaṇo bhave.

Admonition, teaching, causing the Pāli to be learned, causing the commentary to be learned, the bowl and robe, requisites, and the sick monk; one should not be a following monk.

Upajjhāyesu [V 0.0391] ye vattā, evaṃ ācariyesupi;

Saddhivihārike vattā, tatheva antevāsike.

Whatever duties there are towards preceptors, so too are there towards teachers. There are duties towards a co-resident pupil, and likewise towards a resident pupil.

Āgantukesu ye vattā, puna āvāsikesu ca;

Gamikānumodanikā, bhattagge piṇḍacārike.

Whatever duties there are towards incoming monks, and again towards resident monks; duties for departing monks, for giving thanks, in the refectory, and for one going on alms-round.

Āraññakesu yaṃ vattaṃ, yañca senāsanesupi;

Jantāghare vaccakuṭī, upajjhā saddhivihārike.

The duty for forest-dwelling monks, and that which is for lodgings; in the steam-bath house, the latrine, for the preceptor, and for the co-resident pupil.

Ācariyesu [T 2.0282] yaṃ vattaṃ, tatheva antevāsike;

Ekūnavīsati vatthū, vattā cuddasa khandhake.

Whatever duty there is towards teachers, likewise it is towards a resident pupil. In the Khandhaka on Duties, there are nineteen topics and fourteen duties.

Vattaṃ aparipūrento, na sīlaṃ paripūrati;

Asuddhasīlo duppañño, cittekaggaṃ na vindati.

One who does not fulfill the duties does not perfect virtue; impure in virtue, lacking wisdom, one does not attain one-pointedness of mind.

Vikkhittacittonekaggo, sammā dhammaṃ na passati;

Apassamāno saddhammaṃ, dukkhā na parimuccati.

With a scattered mind, not one-pointed, one does not see the Dhamma rightly; not seeing the true Dhamma, one is not freed from suffering.

Yaṃ [M 0.0417] vattaṃ paripūrento, sīlampi paripūrati;

Visuddhasīlo sappañño, cittekaggampi vindati.

One who fulfills the duties also perfects virtue; pure in virtue and wise, one also attains one-pointedness of mind.

Avikkhittacitto ekaggo, sammā dhammaṃ vipassati;

Sampassamāno saddhammaṃ, dukkhā so parimuccati.

With an undistracted mind, one-pointed, one clearly sees the Dhamma rightly; seeing the true Dhamma, that one is freed from suffering.

Tasmā hi vattaṃ pūreyya, jinaputto vicakkhaṇo;

Ovādaṃ buddhaseṭṭhassa, tato nibbānamehitīti.

Therefore, a wise son of the Conqueror should fulfill the duty, the instruction of the supreme Buddha; from that, he will attain Nibbāna.

Vattakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Khandhaka on Duties is concluded.

9. Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhakaṃ

9. The Khandhaka on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha

1. Pātimokkhuddesayācanā

1. Request for the Recitation of the Pātimokkha

383. udā. 45; a. ni. 8.20 Tena [T 2.0283][P 2.0236][M 0.0418][V 0.0392] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātu pāsāde. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisinno hoti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando abhikkantāya rattiyā nikkhante paṭhame yāme uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantā, bhante, ratti, nikkhanto paṭhamo yāmo, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho. Uddisatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkha”nti. Evaṃ vutte bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando abhikkantāya rattiyā nikkhante majjhime yāme uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantā, bhante, ratti, nikkhanto majjhimo yāmo, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho. Uddisatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkha”nti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando abhikkantāya rattiyā nikkhante pacchime yāme uddhaste aruṇe nandimukhiyā rattiyā uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantā[T 2.0284], bhante, ratti, nikkhanto pacchimo yāmo, uddhastaṃ aruṇaṃ nandimukhi ratti, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho. Uddisatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkha”nti. “Aparisuddhā, ānanda, parisā”ti.

383. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, in the mansion of Migāra’s mother. Now on that occasion, on the Uposatha day, the Blessed One was seated, surrounded by the community of monks. Then, when the night had advanced, after the first watch had passed, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the night has advanced, the first watch has passed. The community of monks has been seated for a long time. Let the Blessed One recite the Pātimokkha for the monks.” When this was said, the Blessed One remained silent. For a second time, when the night had advanced, after the middle watch had passed, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the night has advanced, the middle watch has passed. The community of monks has been seated for a long time. Let the Blessed One recite the Pātimokkha for the monks.” For a second time, the Blessed One remained silent. For a third time, when the night had advanced, after the last watch had passed, as dawn was breaking and the night had a smiling face, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the night has advanced, the last watch has passed. Dawn is breaking, the night has a smiling face. The community of monks has been seated for a long time. Let the Blessed One recite the Pātimokkha for the monks.” “Ānanda, the assembly is not pure.”

Atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa etadahosi – “kaṃ nu kho bhagavā puggalaṃ sandhāya evamāha – ‘aparisuddhā, ānanda, parisā’”ti? Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sabbāvantaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ cetasā ceto paricca manasākāsi. Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṃ puggalaṃ dussīlaṃ pāpadhammaṃ asucisaṅkassarasamācāraṃ paṭicchannakammantaṃ assamaṇaṃ samaṇapaṭiññaṃ abrahmacāriṃ brahmacāripaṭiññaṃ antopūtiṃ avassutaṃ kasambujātaṃ kasambukajātaṃ (ka.) majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa nisinnaṃ. Disvāna yena so puggalo [M 0.0419] tenupasaṅkami[P 2.0237], upasaṅkamitvā taṃ puggalaṃ etadavoca – “uṭṭhehi, āvuso, diṭṭhosi bhagavatā; natthi te bhikkhūhi [V 0.0393] saddhiṃ saṃvāso”ti. Evaṃ vutte so puggalo tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṃ puggalaṃ etadavoca – “uṭṭhehi, āvuso, diṭṭhosi bhagavatā; natthi te bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ saṃvāso”ti. Dutiyampi kho so puggalo tuṇhī ahosi. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṃ puggalaṃ etadavoca – “uṭṭhehi, āvuso, diṭṭhosi bhagavatā; natthi te bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ saṃvāso”ti. Tatiyampi kho so puggalo tuṇhī ahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṃ puggalaṃ bāhāyaṃ gahetvā [T 2.0285] bahidvārakoṭṭhakā nikkhāmetvā sūcighaṭikaṃ datvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “nikkhāmito so, bhante, puggalo mayā; suddhā parisā; uddisatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkha”nti.

Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna thought: “With reference to which person did the Blessed One say, ‘Ānanda, the assembly is not pure’?” Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna surveyed the entire assembly of monks with his mind, encompassing their minds with his. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna saw that person—immoral, of evil nature, impure, of suspicious conduct, of concealed deeds, not a recluse but claiming to be a recluse, not living the holy life but claiming to live the holy life, rotten within, corrupt, and like refuse—sitting in the midst of the assembly of monks. Having seen him, he approached that person and said: “Arise, friend. You have been seen by the Blessed One; there is no communion for you with the monks.” When this was said, that person was silent. For a second time, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said to that person: “Arise, friend. You have been seen by the Blessed One; there is no communion for you with the monks.” For a second time, that person was silent. For a third time, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said to that person: “Arise, friend. You have been seen by the Blessed One; there is no communion for you with the monks.” For a third time, that person was silent. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna took that person by the arm, expelled him from outside the gatehouse, bolted the door, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, that person has been expelled by me; the assembly is pure. Let the Blessed One recite the Pātimokkha to the monks.”

“Acchariyaṃ, moggallāna, abbhutaṃ, moggallāna, yāva bāhāgahaṇāpi nāma so moghapuriso āgamessatī”ti! Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi –

“It is wonderful, Moggallāna! It is marvelous, Moggallāna, that that worthless man would wait even until being seized by the arm!” Then the Blessed One addressed the monks:

2. Mahāsamuddeaṭṭhacchariyaṃ

2. The Eight Wonders of the Great Ocean

384. udā. 45; a. ni. 8.19 “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti. Katame aṭṭha?

384. “Monks, there are these eight wonderful and marvelous qualities of the great ocean, seeing which again and again the asuras delight in the great ocean. What are the eight?

“Mahāsamuddo, bhikkhave, anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro na āyatakeneva papāto. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro na āyatakeneva papāto – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

“Monks, the great ocean gradually slopes, gradually inclines, and gradually shelves; it is not an abrupt precipice. That the great ocean, monks, gradually slopes, gradually inclines, and gradually shelves, and is not an abrupt precipice—this, monks, is the first wonderful and marvelous quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again the asuras delight in the great ocean.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṃ nātivattati. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṃ nātivattati – ayaṃ ayampi (syā.), bhikkhave, mahāsamudde dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

“Furthermore, monks, the great ocean is of a stable nature and does not transgress its bounds. That the great ocean, monks, is of a stable nature and does not transgress its bounds—this, monks, is the second wonderful and marvelous quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again the asuras delight in the great ocean.

“Puna [M 0.0420] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo na matena kuṇapena saṃvasati[T 2.0286]. Yaṃ hoti mahāsamudde mataṃ kuṇapaṃ, taṃ khippaññeva tīraṃ vāheti, thalaṃ ussāreti. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo na matena kuṇapena saṃvasati, yaṃ hoti mahāsamudde mataṃ kuṇapaṃ, taṃ khippaññeva tīraṃ [V 0.0394] vāheti, thalaṃ ussāreti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

“Furthermore, monks, the great ocean does not coexist with a dead carcass. Whatever dead carcass there is in the great ocean, it quickly carries it to the shore and casts it up onto dry land. That the great ocean, monks, does not coexist with a dead carcass, and that whatever dead carcass there is in the great ocean, it quickly carries to the shore and casts up onto dry land—this, monks, is the third wonderful and marvelous quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again the asuras delight in the great ocean.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, yā kāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, tā mahāsamuddaṃ pattā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, mahāsamuddo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchanti. Yampi, bhikkhave, yākāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, tā mahāsamuddaṃ pattā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, mahāsamuddo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchanti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde catuttho [P 2.0238] acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

“Furthermore, monks, whatever great rivers there are—namely, the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—upon reaching the great ocean, they abandon their former names and lineage and are reckoned only as 'the great ocean.' That whatever great rivers there are—namely, the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—upon reaching the great ocean, abandon their former names and lineage and are reckoned only as 'the great ocean'—this, monks, is the fourth wonderful and marvelous quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again, the asuras delight in the great ocean.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, yā ca yākāci (syā.) loke savantiyo mahāsamuddaṃ appenti, yā ca antalikkhā dhārā papatanti, na tena mahāsamuddassa ūnattaṃ vā pūrattaṃ vā paññāyati. Yampi, bhikkhave, yā ca loke savantiyo mahāsamuddaṃ appenti, yā ca [T 2.0287] antalikkhā dhārā papatanti, na tena mahāsamuddassa ūnattaṃ vā pūrattaṃ vā paññāyati – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde pañcamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

“Furthermore, monks, whatever streams in the world flow into the great ocean, and whatever streams of rain fall from the sky, by this no decrease or fullness of the great ocean is apparent. That whatever streams in the world flow into the great ocean, and whatever streams of rain fall from the sky, yet by this no decrease or fullness of the great ocean is apparent—this, monks, is the fifth wonderful and marvelous quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again, the asuras delight in the great ocean.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ekaraso loṇaraso. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ekaraso loṇaraso – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde chaṭṭho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

“Furthermore, monks, the great ocean has a single taste, the taste of salt. That the great ocean has a single taste, the taste of salt—this, monks, is the sixth wonderful and marvelous quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again, the asuras delight in the great ocean.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo bahuratano bahūtaratano (ka.) anekaratano. Tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṃ – muttā, maṇi, veḷuriyo, saṅkho, silā, pavāḷaṃ, rajataṃ, jātarūpaṃ, lohitako, masāragallaṃ. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo bahuratano anekaratano, tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṃ – muttā, maṇi, veḷuriyo, saṅkho, silā, pavāḷaṃ, rajataṃ, jātarūpaṃ, lohitako[M 0.0421], masāragallaṃ – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde sattamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.

Furthermore, O monks, the great ocean possesses many treasures, possesses various treasures. Therein are these treasures, that is to say: pearl, gem, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, ruby, and cat's eye gem. O monks, that the great ocean possesses many treasures, possesses various treasures—therein are these treasures, that is to say: pearl, gem, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, ruby, and cat's eye gem—this, O monks, is the seventh wonderful and astonishing quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again, the asuras greatly delight in the great ocean.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo mahataṃ bhūtānaṃ āvāso. Tatrime bhūtā – timi, timiṅgalo, timitimiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo (sī.), timitimiṅgalo mahātimiṅgalo (syā. kaṃ.), asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā. Santi mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, dviyojanasatikāpi [T 2.0288] attabhāvā, tiyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, catuyojanasatikāpi [V 0.0395] attabhāvā, pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo mahataṃ bhūtānaṃ āvāso, tatrime bhūtā – timi, timiṅgalo, timitimiṅgalo, asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā; santi mahāsamudde, yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā…pe… pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhirama”nti.

Furthermore, O monks, the great ocean is the abode of great beings. Therein are these beings: the timi, the timiṅgala, the timitimiṅgala, asuras, nāgas, and gandhabbas. In the great ocean, there are beings whose bodies are one hundred yojanas, beings whose bodies are two hundred yojanas, beings whose bodies are three hundred yojanas, beings whose bodies are four hundred yojanas, and beings whose bodies are five hundred yojanas. O monks, that the great ocean is the abode of great beings, and that therein are these beings—the timi, the timiṅgala, the timitimiṅgala, asuras, nāgas, and gandhabbas; and that in the great ocean there are beings whose bodies are one hundred yojanas... up to... beings whose bodies are five hundred yojanas—this, O monks, is the eighth wonderful and astonishing quality of the great ocean, seeing which again and again, the asuras greatly delight in the great ocean. These, indeed, O monks, are the eight wonderful and astonishing qualities of the great ocean, seeing which again and again, the asuras greatly delight in the great ocean.

3. Imasmiṃdhammavinayeaṭṭhacchariyaṃ

3. The Eight Wonders in this Dhamma and Vinaya

385. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti. Katame aṭṭha?

385. Just so, O monks, in this Dhamma and Vinaya there are eight wonderful and astonishing qualities, seeing which again and again, the monks greatly delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya. What are the eight?

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro na āyatakeneva papāto; evameva kho, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho. Yampi, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Monks, just as the great ocean gradually slopes, gradually inclines, and gradually deepens, and is not an abrupt precipice; even so, monks, in this Dhamma and Vinaya, there is gradual training, gradual action, and gradual practice; there is no sudden penetration to final knowledge. That in this Dhamma and Vinaya there is gradual training, gradual action, and gradual practice, and no sudden penetration to final knowledge—this, monks, is the first wonderful and astonishing quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṃ nātivattati[T 2.0289]; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ mayā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, taṃ mama sāvakā jīvitahetupi nātikkamanti. Yampi, bhikkhave, mayā mama sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ [M 0.0422] paññattaṃ, taṃ [P 2.0239] mama sāvakā jīvitahetupi nātikkamanti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Monks, just as the great ocean is of a stable nature and does not overstep its shore; even so, monks, whatever training rule has been laid down by me for my disciples, my disciples do not transgress it even for the sake of life. That, monks, whatever training rule has been laid down by me for my disciples, my disciples do not transgress it even for the sake of life—this, monks, is the second wonderful and astonishing quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo na matena kuṇapena saṃvasati, yaṃ hoti mahāsamudde mataṃ kuṇapaṃ taṃ khippameva tīraṃ vāheti, thalaṃ ussāreti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yo so puggalo dussīlo pāpadhammo asucisaṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto, na tena saṅgho saṃvasati, khippameva naṃ sannipatitvā ukkhipati, kiñcāpi kho so hoti majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa [V 0.0396] nisinno. Atha kho so ārakāva saṅghamhā, saṅgho ca tena. Yampi, bhikkhave, yo so puggalo dussīlo pāpadhammo asucisaṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto, na tena saṅgho saṃvasati, khippameva naṃ sannipūtitvā ukkhipati, kiñcāpi kho so hoti majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa nisinno, atha kho so ārakāva saṅghamhā, saṅgho ca tena – ayaṃ[T 2.0290], bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Just as, O monks, the great ocean does not dwell with a dead corpse—whatever dead corpse there is in the great ocean, it quickly carries it to the shore and casts it up on dry land—even so, O monks, the Saṅgha does not dwell with a person who is immoral, of evil nature, impure, of suspect conduct, of concealed actions, not an ascetic but claiming to be an ascetic, not practicing the holy life but claiming to practice the holy life, rotten within, drenched with defilements, and has become like refuse. Having assembled, it quickly expels him. Even though he may be seated in the midst of the assembly of monks, nevertheless, he is far from the Saṅgha, and the Saṅgha is far from him. The fact that, O monks, the Saṅgha does not dwell with a person who is immoral, of evil nature, impure, of suspect conduct, of concealed actions, not an ascetic but claiming to be an ascetic, not practicing the holy life but claiming to practice the holy life, rotten within, drenched with defilements, and has become like refuse; that having assembled, it quickly expels him; and that even though he may be seated in the midst of the assembly of monks, he is nevertheless far from the Saṅgha, and the Saṅgha is far from him—this, O monks, is the third wonderful and astonishing quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yā kāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, tā mahāsamuddaṃ pattā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, mahāsamuddo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, cattārome vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Te tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitvā pabbajitā (sī.) jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, samaṇā sakyaputtiyā tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchanti.
