Yampi, bhikkhave, cattārome vaṇṇā khattiyā brāhmaṇā vessā suddā, te tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitvā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, samaṇā sakyaputtiyā tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchanti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Just as, monks, whatever great rivers there are—namely, the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—upon reaching the great ocean, abandon their former names and clans, and are reckoned simply as 'the great ocean'; even so, monks, these four castes—Khattiyas, Brāhmaṇas, Vessas, and Suddas—having gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, abandon their former names and clans, and are reckoned simply as 'ascetics, sons of the Sakyan'. That these four castes—Khattiyas, Brāhmaṇas, Vessas, and Suddas—having gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, abandon their former names and clans, and are reckoned simply as 'ascetics, sons of the Sakyan'—this, monks, is the fourth wonderful and astonishing quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi[M 0.0423], bhikkhave, yā ca loke savantiyo mahāsamuddaṃ appenti, yā ca antalikkhā dhārā papatanti, na tena mahāsamuddassa ūnattaṃ vā pūrattaṃ vā paññāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bahū cepi bhikkhū anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyanti, na tena nibbānadhātuyā ūnattaṃ vā pūrattaṃ vā paññāyati. Yampi, bhikkhave, bahū cepi bhikkhū anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyanti[T 2.0291], na tena nibbānadhātuyā ūnattaṃ vā pūrattaṃ vā paññāyati – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pañcamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Just as, monks, whatever streams in the world flow into the great ocean, and whatever rains fall from the sky, by that no decrease or increase in the great ocean is discernible; even so, monks, even if many monks attain final Nibbāna in the Nibbāna-element without residue, by that no decrease or increase in the Nibbāna-element is discernible. That even if many monks attain final Nibbāna in the Nibbāna-element without residue, no decrease or increase in the Nibbāna-element is discernible—this, monks, is the fifth wonderful and marvelous quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ekaraso loṇaraso, evameva kho, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo ekaraso vimuttiraso. Yampi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo ekaraso vimuttiraso – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye chaṭṭho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Just as, monks, the great ocean has one taste, the taste of salt, even so, monks, this Dhamma and Vinaya has one taste, the taste of liberation. That this Dhamma and Vinaya has one taste, the taste of liberation—this, monks, is the sixth wonderful and marvelous quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi[V 0.0397], bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo bahuratano anekaratano, tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṃ – muttā, maṇi, veḷuriyo, saṅkho, silā, pavāḷaṃ, rajataṃ, jātarūpaṃ, lohitako, masāragallaṃ; evameva [P 2.0240] kho, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo bahuratano anekaratano. Tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Yampi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo bahuratano anekaratano, tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā…pe… ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye sattamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.

Just as, monks, the great ocean has many jewels, various jewels, wherein are these jewels—namely, pearl, gem, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, ruby, and cat's-eye; even so, monks, this Dhamma and Vinaya has many jewels, various jewels. Herein are these jewels: the four establishments of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the Noble Eightfold Path. That this Dhamma and Vinaya, monks, has many jewels and various jewels, wherein are these jewels—namely, the four establishments of mindfulness... and so on... the Noble Eightfold Path—this, monks, is the seventh wonderful and marvelous quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

“Seyyathāpi[T 2.0292], bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo mahataṃ bhūtānaṃ āvāso, tatrime bhūtā – timi, timiṅgalo, timitimiṅgalo, asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā, santi mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, dviyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, tiyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, catuyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo mahataṃ bhūtānaṃ āvāso. Tatrime bhūtā – sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno; sakadāgāmī, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya [M 0.0424] paṭipanno; anāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno; arahā, arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno. Yampi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo mahataṃ bhūtānaṃ āvāso, tatrime bhūtā – sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno…pe… arahā, arahataphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṃ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramanti. “Ime kho, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṃ dhammavinaye abhiramantī”ti.

Just as, monks, the great ocean is the abode of great beings—that is, the timi fish, the timiṅgala fish, the timitimiṅgala fish, asuras, nāgas, and gandhabbas. There are in the great ocean beings with bodies one hundred yojanas in size, two hundred yojanas in size, three hundred yojanas in size, four hundred yojanas in size, and five hundred yojanas in size. Even so, monks, this Dhamma and Vinaya is the abode of great beings—that is, the stream-enterer and the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry; the once-returner and the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning; the non-returner and the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning; the Arahant and the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship. That this Dhamma and Vinaya is the abode of great beings—that is, the stream-enterer and the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry... the Arahant and the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship—this, monks, is the eighth wonderful and marvelous quality in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya. These, monks, are the eight wonderful and marvelous qualities in this Dhamma and Vinaya, seeing which again and again, the monks delight in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

udā. 45 “Channamativassati suchannamativassati (ka.), vivaṭaṃ nātivassati;

Tasmā channaṃ vivaretha, evaṃ taṃ nātivassatī”ti.

What is covered is rained upon; what is uncovered is not rained upon. Therefore, uncover what is covered; thus it will not be rained upon.

4. Pātimokkhasavanāraho

4. Worthy to Hear the Pātimokkha

386. Atha [V 0.0398] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “nadānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ito [T 2.0293] paraṃ uposathaṃ karissāmi, pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmi. Tumhevadāni, bhikkhave, ito paraṃ uposathaṃ kareyyātha, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyātha. Aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṃ tathāgato aparisuddhāya parisāya uposathaṃ kareyya, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyya. Na ca, bhikkhave na ca bhikkhave bhikkhunā (syā. kaṃ.), sāpattikena pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ. Yo suṇeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yo sāpattiko pātimokkhaṃ suṇāti, tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ṭhapetabbaṃ. Tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe [P 2.0241] udāharitabbaṃ –

386. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, from now on, I will not perform the Uposatha nor recite the Pātimokkha. Monks, from now on, you yourselves should perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. It is impossible, monks, it cannot happen that a Tathāgata would perform the Uposatha or recite the Pātimokkha in an impure assembly. And, monks, one who has an offense should not listen to the Pātimokkha. Whoever should listen incurs an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow the setting aside of the Pātimokkha for one who listens while having an offense. And this, monks, is how it should be set aside. On that Uposatha day, whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth, in the midst of the Saṅgha, when that individual is present, this should be declared:

‘Suṇātu me bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo sāpattiko, tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba’nti ṭhapitaṃ hoti pātimokkha”nti.

‘Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This individual, named so-and-so, has an offense. I set aside the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.’ Thus the Pātimokkha is set aside.”

Tena [M 0.0425] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ‘nāmhe koci jānātī’ti sāpattikāva pātimokkhaṃ suṇanti. Therā bhikkhū paracittaviduno bhikkhūnaṃ ārocenti – “itthannāmo ca itthannāmo ca, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ‘nāmhe koci jānātī’ti sāpattikāva pātimokkhaṃ suṇantī”ti. Assosuṃ kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – “therā kira bhikkhū paracittaviduno amhe bhikkhūnaṃ ārocenti – itthannāmo ca itthannāmo ca, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ‘nāmhe koci [T 2.0294] jānātī’ti sāpattikāva pātimokkhaṃ suṇantī”ti.

At that time the group-of-six monks, thinking, “No one knows us,” listened to the Pātimokkha while having offenses. The elder monks, skilled in knowing the minds of others, informed the monks: “Friends, so-and-so and so-and-so, the group-of-six monks, thinking, ‘No one knows us,’ listen to the Pātimokkha while having offenses.” The group-of-six monks heard: “It is said that the elder monks, skilled in knowing the minds of others, are informing the monks about us: ‘Friends, so-and-so and so-and-so, the group-of-six monks, thinking, “No one knows us,” listen to the Pātimokkha while having offenses.’”

Te – puramhākaṃ pesalā bhikkhū pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapentīti – paṭikacceva suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapentī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ. Yo ṭhapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa”.

Thinking, 'Before the virtuous monks set aside the Pātimokkha on us,' they preemptively set aside the Pātimokkha for pure monks who were without offense, without basis and without cause. Those monks who were of few desires… criticized, condemned, and spread the word disparagingly: 'How indeed could the group-of-six monks set aside the Pātimokkha for pure monks who are without offense, without basis and without cause?' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, monks, as is said, that the group-of-six monks set aside the Pātimokkha for pure monks who are without offense, without basis and without cause?' 'It is true, Blessed One.'… Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be set aside for pure monks who are without offense, without basis and without cause. Whoever should set it aside commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

5. Dhammikādhammikapātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ

5. Righteous and Unrighteous Suspension of the Pātimokkha

387. “Ekaṃ[V 0.0399], bhikkhave, adhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ, ekaṃ dhammikaṃ; pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ ekaṃ dhammikaṃ (sī. syā.), dve adhammikāni; pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, dve dhammikāni; tīṇi adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, tīṇi dhammikāni, cattāri adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, cattāri dhammikāni; pañca adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, pañca dhammikāni; cha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, cha dhammikāni; satta adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, satta dhammikāni; aṭṭha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, aṭṭha dhammikāni; nava adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni[T 2.0295], nava dhammikāni; dasa adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, dasa dhammikāni.

387. Monks, there is one unrighteous suspension of the Pātimokkha, and one righteous suspension of the Pātimokkha; two unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and two righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; three unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and three righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; four unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and four righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; five unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and five righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; six unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and six righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; seven unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and seven righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; eight unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and eight righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; nine unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and nine righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha; ten unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha, and ten righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

“Katamaṃ [M 0.0426] ekaṃ adhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – idaṃ ekaṃ adhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ. Katamaṃ ekaṃ dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ? Samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – idaṃ ekaṃ dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“What is the one unrighteous suspension of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of virtue—this is the one unrighteous suspension of the Pātimokkha. What is the one righteous suspension of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of virtue with a basis—this is the one righteous suspension of the Pātimokkha.”

“Katamāni dve adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā [P 2.0242] pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni dve adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni dve dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni dve dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

“What are the two unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of conduct—these are the two unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the two righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of virtue with a basis, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of conduct with a basis—these are the two righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.”

“Katamāni tīṇi adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlikāya diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni tīṇi adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni tīṇi dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlikāya [T 2.0296] sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlikāya diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni tīṇi dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

“What are the three unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of conduct, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of view—these are the three unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the three righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of virtue with a basis, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of conduct with a basis, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of view with a basis—these are the three righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.”

“Katamāni cattāri adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlikāya diṭṭhivipattiyā [V 0.0400] pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlikāya ājīvavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni cattāri adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni cattāri dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlikāya diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlikāya ājīvavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni cattāri dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

“What are the four unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of conduct, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of view, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless corruption of livelihood—these are the four unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the four righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of virtue with a basis, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of conduct with a basis, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of view with a basis, one suspends the Pātimokkha for a corruption of livelihood with a basis—these are the four righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.”

“Katamāni pañca adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlakena pārājikena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlakena saṅghādisesena…pe… amūlakena pācittiyena… amūlakena pāṭidesanīyena… amūlakena dukkaṭena pātimokkhaṃ [M 0.0427] ṭhapeti – imāni pañca adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni pañca dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlakena pārājikena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlakena saṅghādisesena…pe… [T 2.0297] pācittiyena… pāṭidesanīyena… dukkaṭena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni pañca dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

“What are the five unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a groundless pārājika offense, for a groundless saṅghādisesa offense… for a groundless pācittiya offense… for a groundless pāṭidesanīya offense… for a groundless dukkaṭa offense—these are the five unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the five righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha? One suspends the Pātimokkha for a pārājika offense with a basis, for a saṅghādisesa offense with a basis… for a pācittiya offense… for a pāṭidesanīya offense… for a dukkaṭa offense—these are the five righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.”

“Katamāni cha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katāya; amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katāya; amūlikāya diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, amūlikāya diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katāya – imāni cha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni cha dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katāya; samūlikāya ācāravipattiyā…pe… diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya…pe… katāya – imāni cha dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

What are the six unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a groundless, undecided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, decided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, undecided corruption of conduct, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, decided corruption of conduct, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, undecided corruption of view, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, decided corruption of view, one suspends the Pātimokkha—these are the six unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the six lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a well-grounded, undecided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a well-grounded, decided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; and so on for a well-grounded corruption of conduct and a corruption of view—these are the six lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

“Katamāni satta adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlakena pārājikena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, amūlakena saṅghādisesena…pe… [T 2.0298] thullaccayena pācittiyena pāṭidesanīyena dukkaṭena dubbhāsitena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni satta adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni satta dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlakena pārājikena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti, samūlakena [V 0.0401] saṅghādisesena…pe… thullaccayena pācittiyena pāṭidesanīyena dukkaṭena dubbhāsitena pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti – imāni satta dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

What are the seven unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a groundless pārājika offense, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless saṅghādisesa offense… and so on… a thullaccaya offense, a pācittiya offense, a pāṭidesanīya offense, a dukkaṭa offense, or a dubbhāsita offense, one suspends the Pātimokkha—these are the seven unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the seven lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a well-grounded pārājika offense, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a well-grounded saṅghādisesa offense… and so on… a thullaccaya offense, a pācittiya offense, a pāṭidesanīya offense, a dukkaṭa offense, or a dubbhāsita offense, one suspends the Pātimokkha—these are the seven lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

“Katamāni aṭṭha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katāya; amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā [P 2.0243]…pe… diṭṭhivipattiyā…pe… ājīvavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya…pe… katāya – imāni aṭṭha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni [T 2.0299] aṭṭha dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti [M 0.0428] katāya; samūlikāya ācāravipattiyā…pe… diṭṭhivipattiyā…pe… ājīvavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya…pe… katāya. Imāni aṭṭha dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

What are the eight unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a groundless, undecided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, decided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; and so on for a groundless corruption of conduct, a corruption of view, and a corruption of livelihood—these are the eight unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the eight lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a well-grounded, undecided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a well-grounded, decided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; and so on for a well-grounded corruption of conduct, a corruption of view, and a corruption of livelihood. These are the eight lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

“Katamāni nava adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katāya, amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katākatāya; amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā…pe… diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya…pe… katāya…pe… katākatāya imāni nava adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni nava dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya, samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ [T 2.0300] ṭhapeti katāya, samūlikāya sīlavipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti katākatāya; samūlikāya ācāravipattiyā…pe… diṭṭhivipattiyā pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti akatāya…pe… katāya – katākatāya…pe… imāni nava dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

What are the nine unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a groundless, undecided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless, decided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a groundless corruption of virtue that is both decided and undecided, one suspends the Pātimokkha; and so on for a groundless corruption of conduct and a corruption of view—these are the nine unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the nine lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? By means of a well-grounded, undecided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a well-grounded, decided corruption of virtue, one suspends the Pātimokkha; by means of a well-grounded corruption of virtue that is both decided and undecided, one suspends the Pātimokkha; and so on for a well-grounded corruption of conduct and a corruption of view. These are the nine lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

“Katamāni dasa adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Na pārājiko tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti, na pārājikakathā vippakatā hoti; na sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti, na sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakathā vippakatā hoti; dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ upeti, na dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyati, na dhammikāya sāmaggiyā paccādānakathā vippakatā hoti; na sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti, na ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti, na diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti – imāni dasa adhammikāni [V 0.0402] pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Katamāni dasa dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni? Pārājiko tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti, pārājikakathā vippakatā hoti; sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti, sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakathā vippakatā hoti; dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upeti, dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ [T 2.0301] paccādiyati, dhammikāya sāmaggiyā paccādānakathā vippakatā hoti; sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti, ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti, diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti – imāni dasa dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

What are the ten unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? No one who has committed a pārājika offense is seated in that assembly, nor is the discussion about a pārājika offense unresolved; no one who has renounced the training is seated in that assembly, nor is the discussion about one who has renounced the training unresolved; a lawful agreement is approached, a lawful agreement is not rejected, nor is the discussion about rejecting a lawful agreement unresolved; one is not suspected of a corruption of virtue on the grounds of what is seen, heard, or suspected; one is not suspected of a corruption of conduct on the grounds of what is seen, heard, or suspected; one is not suspected of a corruption of view on the grounds of what is seen, heard, or suspected—these are the ten unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. What are the ten lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha? Someone who has committed a pārājika offense is seated in that assembly, and the discussion about a pārājika offense is unresolved; someone who has renounced the training is seated in that assembly, and the discussion about one who has renounced the training is unresolved; a lawful agreement is not approached, a lawful agreement is rejected, and the discussion about rejecting a lawful agreement is unresolved; one is suspected of a corruption of virtue on the grounds of what is seen, heard, or suspected; one is suspected of a corruption of conduct on the grounds of what is seen, heard, or suspected; one is suspected of a corruption of view on the grounds of what is seen, heard, or suspected—these are the ten lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

6. Dhammikapātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ

6. Lawful Suspension of the Pātimokkha

388. “Kathaṃ [M 0.0429] pārājiko tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi pārājikassa dhammassa ajjhāpatti hoti, tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpajjantaṃ. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati pārājikaṃ [P 2.0244] dhammaṃ ajjhāpajjantaṃ, api ca añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpajjantaṃ, nāpi nāpi ca (ka.) añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti, apica sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

388. “How is a bhikkhu who has incurred a pārājika offense seated in that assembly? Here, bhikkhus, by whatever modes, by whatever signs, by whatever indications a pārājika offense is incurred, by those modes, by those signs, by those indications a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu incurring a pārājika offense. A bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu incurring a pārājika offense, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so has incurred a pārājika offense.’ A bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu incurring a pārājika offense, nor does another bhikkhu inform him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so has incurred a pārājika offense,’ but that very bhikkhu himself declares to him: ‘Friend, I have incurred a pārājika offense.’ If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by that which was seen, by that which was heard, or by that suspicion, should declare on that very Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—when that person is present in the midst of the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpanno, tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte [T 2.0302] pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The person named so-and-so has incurred a pārājika offense. I suspend the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited when he is present. This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.”

389. “Bhikkhussa pātimokkhe ṭhapite parisā vuṭṭhāti, dasannaṃ antarāyānaṃ aññatarena aññatarena antarāyena (syā. kaṃ.) – rājantarāyena vā, corantarāyena vā, agyantarāyena vā, udakantarāyena vā, manussantarāyena vā, amanussantarāyena vā, vāḷantarāyena vā, sarīsapantarāyena vā, jīvitantarāyena [V 0.0403] vā, brahmacariyantarāyena vā. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ vā āvāse, aññasmiṃ vā āvāse, tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

389. “When the Pātimokkha has been suspended for a bhikkhu, the assembly rises due to one of the ten dangers: a danger from kings, a danger from thieves, a danger from fire, a danger from water, a danger from human beings, a danger from non-human beings, a danger from wild beasts, a danger from reptiles, a danger to life, or a danger to the holy life. If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, either in that monastery or in another, when that person is present, should declare in the midst of the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa puggalassa pārājikakathā vippakatā, taṃ vatthu avinicchitaṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ vinicchineyyāti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The discussion concerning the pārājika of the person named so-and-so is incomplete; that matter is undecided. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should decide that matter.”

“Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāharitabbaṃ –

“If this is obtained, it is good. If it is not obtained, then on that very Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—when that person is present, it should be declared in the midst of the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0430] me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa puggalassa pārājikakathā vippakatā, taṃ vatthu avinicchitaṃ. Tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The discussion concerning the pārājika of the person named so-and-so is incomplete; that matter is undecided. I suspend the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited when he is present. This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.”

390. “Kathaṃ sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi [T 2.0303] nimittehi sikkhā paccakkhātā hoti, tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati sikkhaṃ paccakkhantaṃ. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati sikkhaṃ paccakkhantaṃ, apica añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmena, āvuso, bhikkhunā sikkhā paccakkhātā’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati sikkhaṃ paccakkhantaṃ, nāpi añño [P 2.0245] bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmena, āvuso, bhikkhunā sikkhā paccakkhātā’ti, apica sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘mayā, āvuso, sikkhā paccakkhātā’ti. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

390. “How is one who has renounced the training seated in that assembly? Here, bhikkhus, by whatever modes, by whatever signs, by whatever indications the training is renounced, by those modes, by those signs, by those indications a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu renouncing the training. A bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu renouncing the training, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the training has been renounced by the bhikkhu named so-and-so.’ A bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu renouncing the training, nor does another bhikkhu inform him: ‘Friend, the training has been renounced by the bhikkhu named so-and-so,’ but that very bhikkhu himself informs him: ‘Friend, the training has been renounced by me.’ If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by that which was seen, by that which was heard, or by that suspicion, should declare on that very Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—when that person is present in the midst of the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmena puggalena sikkhā paccakkhātā, tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The training has been renounced by the person named so-and-so. I suspend the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited when he is present. This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.”

391. “Bhikkhussa pātimokkhe ṭhapite parisā vuṭṭhāti, dasannaṃ antarāyānaṃ aññatarena – rājantarāyena vā [V 0.0404] …pe… brahmacariyantarāyena vā, ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ vā āvāse, aññasmiṃ vā āvāse, tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

391. “When the Pātimokkha has been suspended for a bhikkhu, the assembly rises due to one of the ten dangers—a danger from kings … or a danger to the holy life. If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, either in that monastery or in another, when that person is present, should declare in the midst of the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa puggalassa sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakathā sikkhāpaccakkhātakathā (sī.) vippakatā, taṃ vatthu avinicchitaṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ vinicchineyyāti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The discussion about the renunciation of the training by the person named so-and-so is incomplete; that matter is undecided. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should decide that matter.”

“Evañcetaṃ [T 2.0304] labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāharitabbaṃ –

“If this is obtained, it is good. If it is not obtained, then on that very Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—when that person is present, it should be declared in the midst of the Saṅgha:”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0431] me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa puggalassa sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakathā vippakatā, taṃ vatthu avinicchitaṃ. Tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The discussion about the renunciation of the training by the person named so-and-so is incomplete; that matter is undecided. I suspend the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited when he is present. This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.”

392. “Kathaṃ dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upeti? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi dhammikāya sāmaggiyānupagamanaṃ hoti, tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upentaṃ. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upentaṃ, api ca añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upetī’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upentaṃ, nāpi añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upetī’ti, api ca sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upemī’ti. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā [P 2.0246] pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

392. “How does one not attain to lawful concord? Here, bhikkhus, by whatever modes, signs, and indications the non-attainment of lawful concord occurs, by those same modes, signs, and indications a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu not attaining to lawful concord. A bhikkhu does not himself see another bhikkhu not attaining to lawful concord, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so does not attain to lawful concord.’ A bhikkhu does not himself see another bhikkhu not attaining to lawful concord, nor does another bhikkhu inform him, but that very bhikkhu himself informs another bhikkhu: ‘Friend, I do not attain to lawful concord.’ If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu may, based on what he has seen, heard, or suspected, declare it on that Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—in the presence of that person in the midst of the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ na upeti[T 2.0305], tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The person named so-and-so does not attain to lawful concord. I suspend the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.” This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.

393. “Kathaṃ dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi dhammikāya sāmaggiyā paccādānaṃ hoti, tehi ākārehi [V 0.0405] tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyantaṃ na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyantaṃ, api ca añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyatī’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyantaṃ, nāpi añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyatī’ti, api ca sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyāmī’ti[M 0.0432]. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

393. “How does one reclaim lawful concord? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu reclaiming lawful concord by those modes, by those signs, by those indications by which the reclaiming of lawful concord occurs. Or, a bhikkhu does not in fact see another bhikkhu reclaiming lawful concord, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so is reclaiming lawful concord.’ Or, a bhikkhu does not in fact see another bhikkhu reclaiming lawful concord, nor does another bhikkhu inform him, but that very bhikkhu himself informs another bhikkhu: ‘Friend, I am reclaiming lawful concord.’ If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, based on what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected, may declare it on that Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—in the midst of the Saṅgha when that person is present:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo dhammikaṃ sāmaggiṃ paccādiyati, tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The person named so-and-so is reclaiming lawful concord. I suspend the Pātimokkha for him. The Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.” This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.

394. “Bhikkhussa pātimokkhe ṭhapite parisā vuṭṭhāti, dasannaṃ antarāyānaṃ aññatarena – rājantarāyena vā…pe… brahmacariyantarāyena [T 2.0306] vā. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ vā āvāse, aññasmiṃ vā āvāse, tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

394. When the Pātimokkha has been suspended for a bhikkhu, and the assembly adjourns owing to one of the ten dangers—a danger from kings … or a danger to the holy life. If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu may declare it in the midst of the Saṅgha, either in that monastery or in another, in the presence of that person:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa puggalassa dhammikāya sāmaggiyā paccādānakathā vippakatā, taṃ vatthu avinicchitaṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ vinicchineyyāti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The discussion concerning the reclaiming of lawful concord by the person named so-and-so is incomplete; that matter is undecided. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should decide that matter.”

“Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāharitabbaṃ –

If this is obtained, it is good. If it is not obtained, then on that Uposatha day, whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth, with that individual present, it should be declared in the midst of the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa puggalassa dhammikāya sāmaggiyā paccādānakathā vippakatā, taṃ vatthu avinicchitaṃ. Tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The discussion concerning the reclaiming of lawful concord by the person named so-and-so is incomplete; that matter is undecided. I suspend his Pātimokkha; the Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.” This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.

395. “Kathaṃ [V 0.0406] sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti, tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, api ca añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, nāpi añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu [T 2.0307][M 0.0433] sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito’ti, api ca sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitomhī’ti. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

395. “How is one seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue? Here, bhikkhus, by whatever modes, signs, and indications one is seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue, by those same modes, signs, and indications a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu who is seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue. A bhikkhu does not himself see another bhikkhu who is seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so is seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue.’ A bhikkhu does not himself see another bhikkhu who is seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue, nor does another bhikkhu inform him, but that very bhikkhu himself informs another bhikkhu: ‘Friend, I am seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue.’ If he wishes, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu may, based on what he has seen, heard, or suspected, declare it on that Uposatha day—whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth—in the presence of that person in the midst of the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo sīlavipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito, diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti (syā. kaṃ.) tassa pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The person named so-and-so is seen, heard, or suspected of a corruption of virtue. I suspend his Pātimokkha; the Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.” This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.

396. “Kathaṃ ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, api ca añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, nāpi añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito’ti, api ca sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitomhī’ti. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya [T 2.0308] parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

396. How is one suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard? In this Dispensation, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard, by means of those modes, marks, and signs by which one is so suspected. Or a bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so is suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard.’ Or a bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard, nor does another bhikkhu inform him, but that very bhikkhu himself informs him: ‘Friend, I am suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard.’ If he wishes, Bhikkhus, based on what he has seen, heard, or suspected, he may make a declaration in the midst of the Sangha on that Uposatha day, whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth, when that individual is present—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo ācāravipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito, tassa [V 0.0407] pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The individual named so-and-so is suspected of corruption of conduct based on what has been seen or heard. I suspend his Pātimokkha; the Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.’ This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.

397. “Kathaṃ diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti? Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi diṭṭhivipattiyā [M 0.0434] diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito hoti, tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, api ca añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito’ti. Na heva kho bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ passati diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, nāpi añño bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘itthannāmo, āvuso, bhikkhu diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito’ti, api ca sova bhikkhu bhikkhussa āroceti – ‘ahaṃ, āvuso, diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitomhī’ti. Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tena diṭṭhena tena sutena tāya parisaṅkāya tadahuposathe cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya –

397. How is one suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard? In this Dispensation, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees another bhikkhu suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard, by means of those modes, marks, and signs by which one is so suspected. Or a bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard, but another bhikkhu informs him: ‘Friend, the bhikkhu named so-and-so is suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard.’ Or a bhikkhu does not see another bhikkhu suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard, nor does another bhikkhu inform him, but that very bhikkhu himself declares to him: ‘Friend, I am suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard.’ If he wishes, Bhikkhus, based on what he has seen, heard, or suspected, he may declare it in the midst of the Sangha on that Uposatha day, whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth, with that individual present:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo diṭṭhivipattiyā diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkito, tassa [T 2.0309] pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapemi, na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti – dhammikaṃ [P 2.0247] pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The individual named so-and-so is suspected of corruption of view based on what has been seen or heard. I suspend his Pātimokkha; the Pātimokkha should not be recited while he is present.’ This is a lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha.

“Imāni dasa dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanānī”ti.

These are the ten lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is finished.

7. Attādānaaṅgaṃ

7. The Chapter on Self-Initiated Legal Issues

398. Atha kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “attādānaṃ ādātukāmena, bhante, bhikkhunā katamaṅgasamannāgataṃ kataṅgasamannāgataṃ (ka.) attādānaṃ ādātabba”nti?

398. Then the Venerable Upāli approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Upāli said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, when a bhikkhu wishes to take up a self-initiated legal issue, with what factors should that self-initiated legal issue be endowed?'

pari. 440 “Attādānaṃ [M 0.0435][V 0.0408] ādātukāmena, upāli, bhikkhunā pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ. Attādānaṃ ādātukāmena, upāli, bhikkhunā evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātukāmo, kālo nu kho imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātuṃ udāhu no’ti? Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘akālo imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātuṃ, no kālo’ti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to take up a self-initiated legal issue should take up a self-initiated legal issue endowed with five factors. Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to take up a self-initiated legal issue should reflect thus: ‘Regarding this self-initiated legal issue that I wish to take up, is it now the right time to take it up, or is it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, while reflecting, knows thus: ‘It is the wrong time to take up this self-initiated legal issue, not the right time,’ then, Upāli, that self-initiated legal issue should not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kālo imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātuṃ, no akālo’ti, tenupāli, bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātukāmo, bhūtaṃ nu kho idaṃ attādānaṃ udāhu no’ti? Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhūtaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ, no bhūta’nti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

“But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, while reflecting, knows thus: ‘It is the right time to take up this self-initiated legal issue, not the wrong time,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu should reflect further: ‘Regarding this self-initiated legal issue that I wish to take up, is it actual, or is it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, while reflecting, knows thus: ‘This self-initiated legal issue is not actual, it is unreal,’ then, Upāli, that self-initiated legal issue should not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno [T 2.0310] evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhūtaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ, no abhūta’nti, tenupāli, bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātukāmo, atthasañhitaṃ nu kho idaṃ attādānaṃ udāhu no’ti? Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anatthasañhitaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ, no atthasañhita’nti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

“But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, while reflecting, knows thus: ‘This self-initiated legal issue is actual, it is not unreal,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu should reflect further: ‘Regarding this self-initiated legal issue that I wish to take up, is it connected with benefit, or is it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, while reflecting, knows thus: ‘This self-initiated legal issue is not connected with benefit, it is without benefit,’ then, Upāli, that self-initiated legal issue should not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘atthasañhitaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ, no anatthasañhita’nti, tenupāli, bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ attādānaṃ ādiyamāno labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū dhammato vinayato pakkhe udāhu no’ti? Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ attādānaṃ ādiyamāno na labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū dhammato vinayato pakkhe’ti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflection, knows thus: ‘This undertaking is connected with benefit, not with detriment,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu should reflect further: ‘By this undertaking, will I gain bhikkhus who are seen and associated with, who are on my side in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflection, knows thus: ‘By this undertaking, I will not gain bhikkhus who are seen and associated with, who are on my side in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya,’ then, Upāli, that undertaking should not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ [P 2.0248] attādānaṃ ādiyamāno labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū dhammato vinayato pakkhe’ti, tenupāli, bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me attādānaṃ ādiyato bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ udāhu no’ti? Sace upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho me attādānaṃ [V 0.0409] ādiyato bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ [M 0.0436] saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ. Sace panupāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho me attādānaṃ ādiyato na bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho [T 2.0311] vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, ādātabbaṃ taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ. Evaṃ pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ kho, upāli, attādānaṃ ādinnaṃ, pacchāpi avippaṭisārakaraṃ bhavissatī’ti.

But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflection, knows thus: ‘By this undertaking, I will gain bhikkhus who are seen and associated with, who are on my side in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu should reflect further: ‘Due to this undertaking of mine, will there arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputes, contention, disputation, schism in the Saṅgha, a fissure in the Saṅgha, a division in the Saṅgha, or factionalism in the Saṅgha, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflection, knows thus: ‘Due to this undertaking of mine, there will arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputes, contention, disputation, schism in the Saṅgha, a fissure in the Saṅgha, a division in the Saṅgha, and factionalism in the Saṅgha,’ then, Upāli, that undertaking should not be taken up. But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflection, knows thus: ‘Due to this undertaking of mine, there will not arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputes, contention, disputation, schism in the Saṅgha, a fissure in the Saṅgha, a division in the Saṅgha, or factionalism in the Saṅgha,’ then, Upāli, that undertaking should be taken up. Thus, Upāli, an undertaking endowed with these five factors, when taken up, will cause no remorse afterward.

8. Codakenapaccavekkhitabbadhammā

8. Qualities to Be Reflected Upon by the Accuser

399. pari. 436 (a. ni. 10.44 thokaṃ visadisaṃ) “Codakena, bhante, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā paro codetabbo”ti? “Codakena, upāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā paro codetabbo.

399. “Venerable sir, a bhikkhu who wishes to accuse another, having reflected upon how many qualities within himself, should then accuse that other?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to accuse another, having reflected upon five qualities within himself, should then accuse that other.”

“Codakena, upāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘parisuddhakāyasamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi kāyasamācārena samannāgato – acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena? Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, upāli, bhikkhu parisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti, parisuddhena kāyasamācārena samannāgato – acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā kāyikaṃ sikkhassū’ti. Itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to accuse another should reflect thus: ‘Am I of pure bodily conduct, endowed with pure bodily conduct—unbroken and unblemished? Does this quality exist in me or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu is not of pure bodily conduct, not endowed with pure bodily conduct—unbroken and unblemished—then there will be those who say to him: ‘Come now, venerable sir, first train yourself in bodily conduct.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘parisuddhavacīsamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi vacīsamācārena samannāgato – acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena? Saṃvijjati nu [T 2.0312] kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, upāli, bhikkhu parisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti, parisuddhena vacīsamācārena samannāgato – acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā vācasikaṃ sikkhassū’ti. Itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to accuse another should reflect thus: ‘Am I of pure verbal conduct, endowed with pure verbal conduct—unbroken and unblemished? Does this quality exist in me or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu is not of pure verbal conduct, not endowed with pure verbal conduct—unbroken and unblemished—then there will be those who say to him: ‘Come now, venerable sir, first train yourself in verbal conduct.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘mettaṃ nu kho me cittaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṃ[P 2.0249], saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, upāli, bhikkhuno mettacittaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṃ[V 0.0410], tassa [M 0.0437] bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā sabrahmacārīsu mettacittaṃ upaṭṭhāpehī’ti. Itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to accuse another should reflect thus: ‘Is a mind of loving-kindness, free from animosity, established in me towards my fellow practitioners? Does this quality exist in me or not?’ If, Upāli, a mind of loving-kindness, free from animosity, is not established in a bhikkhu towards his fellow practitioners, then there will be those who say to him: ‘Come now, venerable sir, first establish a mind of loving-kindness towards your fellow practitioners.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘bahussuto nu khomhi, sutadharo, sutasanniccayo? Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā, sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpā me dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā? Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, upāli, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti, sutadharo, sutasanniccayo; ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā, sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ [T 2.0313] parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpassa dhammā na bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā āgamaṃ pariyāpuṇassū’ti. Itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to accuse another should reflect thus: ‘Am I learned, a bearer of the teachings, one who has accumulated learning? Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, complete with meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the entirely complete and pure holy life—are such teachings much heard by me, borne in mind, familiarized by speech, repeatedly contemplated by mind, and well penetrated by wisdom? Does this quality exist in me, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu is not learned, not a bearer of the teachings, not one who has accumulated learning; and if those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, complete with meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the entirely complete and pure holy life—if such teachings have not been much heard by him, not borne in mind, not familiarized by speech, not repeatedly contemplated by mind, and not well penetrated by wisdom, then there will be those who say to him, ‘Come, venerable sir, first you should master the scriptures.’ Thus there will be those who speak to him.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘ubhayāni kho me pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti, suvibhattāni, suppavattīni, suvinicchitāni – suttaso, anubyañjanaso? Saṃviñjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, upāli, bhikkhuno ubhayāni pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti, suvibhattāni, suppavattīni, suvinicchitāni – suttaso, anubyañjanaso, ‘idaṃ panāvuso, kattha vuttaṃ bhagavatā’ti, iti puṭṭho na sampāyati na sampādayati (ka.), tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā, vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇassū’ti. Itissa bhavanti vattāro. Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā paro codetabbo”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a monk intending to accuse another should reflect thus: ‘Are both Pātimokkhas well-mastered by me in detail, well-analyzed, well-established, and well-adjudicated, according to the text and according to the detailed explanation? Does this quality exist in me, or not?’ If, Upāli, both Pātimokkhas are not well-mastered by a monk in detail, not well-analyzed, not well-established, and not well-adjudicated, according to the text and according to the detailed explanation, and when asked, ‘Friend, where was this stated by the Blessed One?’ he cannot furnish an answer, then there will be those who say to him, ‘Come, venerable sir, first you should master the Vinaya.’ Thus there will be those who speak to him. Upāli, a monk intending to accuse another should reflect on these five qualities within himself before accusing another.

9. Codakenaupaṭṭhāpetabbadhammā

9. Qualities to Be Established by the Accuser

400. “Codakena, bhante, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo”ti? “Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo – kālena vakkhāmi, no akālena; bhūtena vakkhāmi, no [T 2.0314] abhūtena; saṇhena [M 0.0438] vakkhāmi, no pharusena; atthasaṃhitena vakkhāmi, no anatthasaṃhitena; mettacitto [V 0.0411] vakkhāmi, no dosantaroti. Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo”ti.

400. “Venerable sir, how many qualities should a monk who wishes to accuse another establish in himself before accusing another?” “Upāli, a monk who wishes to accuse another should establish five qualities in himself before accusing another: ‘I will speak at a suitable time, not at an unsuitable time; I will speak with what is true, not with what is untrue; I will speak with gentleness, not with harshness; I will speak with what is beneficial, not with what is unbeneficial; I will speak with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of ill will.’ Upāli, a monk who wishes to accuse another should establish these five qualities in himself before accusing another.”

10. Codakacuditakapaṭisaṃyuttakathā

10. Discourse Connected with the Accuser and the Accused

401. “Adhammacodakassa, bhante, bhikkhuno katīhākārehi vippaṭisāro [P 2.0250] upadahātabbo”ti? “Adhammacodakassa, upāli, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo – akālenāyasmā codesi, no kālena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; abhūtenāyasmā codesi, no bhūtena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; pharusenāyasmā codesi, no saṇhena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; anatthasaṃhitenāyasmā codesi, no atthasaṃhitena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; dosantaro āyasmā codesi, no mettacitto, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāyāti. Adhammacodakassa, upāli, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yathā na aññopi bhikkhu abhūtena codetabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

401. “Venerable sir, by how many factors should remorse be induced in a monk who accuses contrary to the Dhamma?” “Upāli, remorse should be induced in a monk who accuses contrary to the Dhamma by five factors: ‘Venerable, you accused at the wrong time, not at the right time—that is enough for your remorse; you accused with what is untrue, not with what is true—that is enough for your remorse; you accused with harshness, not with gentleness—that is enough for your remorse; you accused with what is unbeneficial, not with what is beneficial—that is enough for your remorse; you accused with a mind of ill will, not with a mind of loving-kindness—that is enough for your remorse.’ Upāli, remorse should be induced in a monk who accuses contrary to the Dhamma by these five factors. For what reason? So that another monk might not think that one should be accused with what is untrue.”

“Adhammacuditassa pana, bhante, bhikkhuno katihākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo”ti? “Adhammacuditassa, upāli, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo – akālenāyasmā cudito, no kālena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; abhūtenāyasmā cudito, no bhūtena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; pharusenāyasmā cudito[T 2.0315], no saṇhena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; anatthasaṃhitenāyasmā cudito, no atthasaṃhitena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; dosantarenāyasmā cudito, no mettacittena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāyāti. Adhammacuditassa, upāli, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo”ti.

“Venerable sir, by how many factors should freedom from remorse be brought about in a bhikkhu who has been accused contrary to the Dhamma?” “Upāli, freedom from remorse should be brought about in a bhikkhu who has been accused contrary to the Dhamma by five factors: ‘Venerable, you were accused at the wrong time, not at the right time—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you were accused with what is untrue, not with what is true—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you were accused with harsh speech, not with gentle speech—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you were accused with what is unbeneficial, not with what is beneficial—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you were accused with a mind of ill will, not with a mind of loving-kindness—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse.’ Upāli, freedom from remorse should be brought about in a bhikkhu who has been accused contrary to the Dhamma by these five factors.”

“Dhammacodakassa, bhante, bhikkhuno katihākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo”ti? “Dhammacodakassa, upāli, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo – kālenāyasmā codesi, no akālena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; bhūtenāyasmā codesi, no abhūtena[M 0.0439], alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; saṇhenāyasmā codesi, no pharusena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; atthasaṃhitenāyasmā codesi, no anatthasaṃhitena, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya; mettacitto āyasmā codesi, no dosantaro, alaṃ te avippaṭisārāyāti. Dhammacodakassa, upāli, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yathā aññopi bhikkhu bhūtena codetabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

“Venerable sir, by how many factors should freedom from remorse be brought about in a bhikkhu who accuses according to the Dhamma?” “Upāli, freedom from remorse should be brought about in a bhikkhu who accuses according to the Dhamma by five factors: ‘Venerable, you accused at the right time, not at the wrong time—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you accused with what is true, not with what is untrue—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you accused with gentle speech, not with harsh speech—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you accused with what is beneficial, not with what is unbeneficial—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse; you accused with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of ill will—that is sufficient for you to be free from remorse.’ Upāli, freedom from remorse should be brought about in a bhikkhu who accuses according to the Dhamma by these five factors. For what reason? So that another bhikkhu might also think that one ought to be accused with what is true.”

“Dhammacuditassa [V 0.0412] pana, bhante, bhikkhuno katihākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo”ti? “Dhammacuditassa, upāli, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo – kālenāyasmā cudito, no akālena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; bhūtenāyasmā cudito, no abhūtena[T 2.0316], alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; saṇhenāyasmā cudito, no pharusena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; atthasaṃhitenāyasmā cudito, no anatthasaṃhitena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāya; mettacittenāyasmā cudito, no dosantarena, alaṃ te vippaṭisārāyāti. Dhammacuditassa, upāli, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo”ti.

“But, venerable sir, by how many factors should remorse be induced in a monk who has been accused according to the Dhamma?” “Upāli, remorse should be induced in a monk who has been accused according to the Dhamma by five factors: ‘Venerable, you were accused at the right time, not at the wrong time—that is enough for your remorse; you were accused with what is true, not with what is untrue—that is enough for your remorse; you were accused with gentle speech, not with harsh speech—that is enough for your remorse; you were accused with what is beneficial, not with what is unbeneficial—that is enough for your remorse; you were accused with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of ill will—that is enough for your remorse.’ Upāli, remorse should be induced in a monk who has been accused according to the Dhamma by these five factors.”

pari. 438 “Codakena, bhante, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ manasi karitvā paro codetabbo”ti? “Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ manasi karitvā paro codetabbo – kāruññatā, hitesitā, anukampitā, anukampatā (ka.) āpattivuṭṭhānatā, vinayapurekkhāratāti. Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ [P 2.0251] manasi karitvā paro codetabbo”ti.

“Venerable sir, when a monk wishes to accuse another, how many qualities should he reflect upon internally before accusing another?” “Upāli, a monk who wishes to accuse another should reflect upon five qualities internally before accusing another: compassion, desiring his welfare, sympathetic concern, the raising from the offense, and making the Vinaya foremost. Upāli, a monk who wishes to accuse another should reflect upon these five qualities internally before accusing another.”

“Cuditena pana, bhante, bhikkhunā katisu dhammesu patiṭṭhātabba”nti? “Cuditenupāli, bhikkhunā dvīsu dhammesu patiṭṭhātabbaṃ – sacce ca akuppe cā”ti.

“But, venerable sir, in how many qualities should an accused monk be established?” “Upāli, an accused monk should be established in two qualities: in truth and in non-anger.”

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is concluded.

Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhako navamo.

The ninth chapter, on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha, is concluded.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū tiṃsa.

In this chapter, there are thirty topics.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Uposathe [T 2.0317][M 0.0440] yāvatikaṃ, pāpabhikkhu na nikkhami;

Moggallānena nicchuddho, accherā jinasāsane.

On the Uposatha, as the evil monk would not depart, he was expelled by Moggallāna. There are marvels in the Dispensation of the Conqueror.

Ninnonupubbasikkhā ca, ṭhitadhammo nātikkamma;

Kuṇapukkhipati saṅgho, savantiyo jahanti ca.

Sloping and gradual training; a stable nature not transgressed; the Saṅgha casts out a corpse, and rivers abandon their names.

Savanti parinibbanti, ekarasa vimutti ca;

Bahu dhammavinayopi, bhūtaṭṭhāriyapuggalā.

Rivers attain Parinibbāna; one taste of liberation; the Dhamma and Vinaya is also rich in treasures; great beings and the eight noble persons.

Samuddaṃ [V 0.0413] upamaṃ katvā, vācesi ṭhāpesi (ka.) sāsane guṇaṃ;

Uposathe pātimokkhaṃ, na amhe koci jānāti.

Having made the ocean a simile, He spoke of the qualities in the Dispensation; on the Uposatha day, the Pātimokkha, and the thought, “no one knows us.”

Paṭikacceva ujjhanti, eko dve tīṇi cattāri;

Pañca cha satta aṭṭhāni, navā ca dasamāni ca.

They complain right at the outset; regarding the one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten kinds of suspension.

Sīla-ācāra-diṭṭhi ca, ājīvaṃ catubhāgike;

Pārājikañca saṅghādi, pācitti pāṭidesani.

Corruption of virtue, conduct, and view, and corruption of livelihood are spoken of in the fourfold division; and Pārājika, Saṅghādisesa, Pācittiya, and Pāṭidesanīya.

Dukkaṭaṃ pañcabhāgesu, sīlācāravipatti ca;

Akatāya katāya ca, chabhāgesu yathāvidhi.

Dukkaṭa is spoken of in the fivefold division; corruption of virtue and conduct, together with an unresolved case and a resolved case, are spoken of in the sixfold division, according to the procedure.

Pārājikañca saṅghādi, thullaṃ pācittiyena ca;

Pāṭidesaniyañceva[T 2.0318], dukkaṭañca dubbhāsitaṃ.

Pārājika, Saṅghādisesa, Thullaccaya, and Pācittiya; and Pāṭidesanīya, Dukkaṭa, and Dubbhāsita are spoken of in the sevenfold division.

Sīlācāravipatti ca, diṭṭhiājīvavipatti;

Yā ca aṭṭhā katākate, tenetā sīlācāradiṭṭhiyā.

Whatever corruption of virtue and conduct there is, and whatever corruption of view and livelihood there is; these, together with a resolved and an unresolved case, are spoken of as eight.

Akatāya katāyāpi, katākatāyameva ca;

Evaṃ navavidhā vuttā, yathābhūtena ñāyato.

In the case of corruption of virtue, conduct, and view, each taken with an unresolved case, with a resolved case, and with both a resolved and an unresolved case; thus, by this method and according to reality, they are spoken of as being of nine kinds.

Pārājiko vippakatā, paccakkhāto tatheva ca;

Upeti paccādiyati, paccādānakathā ca yā.

A monk who has committed a Pārājika offense in an unresolved case; and likewise a monk who has given up the training; he approaches but is not taken back, and there is talk of taking back.

Sīlācāravipatti ca, tathā diṭṭhivipattiyā;

Diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitaṃ, dasadhā taṃ vijānātha.

In the case of corruption of virtue and conduct, and likewise corruption of view, an offense is seen, heard, or suspected. Know that suspension of the Pātimokkha to be tenfold.

Bhikkhu [M 0.0441] vipassati bhikkhuṃ, añño cārocayāti taṃ;

So yeva tassa akkhāti vipassañño cārocati; taṃ suddheva tassa akkhāti (ka.), pātimokkhaṃ ṭhapeti so.

A monk sees another monk, and another informs him about it; that very one tells it to him, and so he suspends the Pātimokkha.

Vuṭṭhāti [V 0.0414] antarāyena, rājacoraggudakā ca;

Manussaamanussā ca, vāḷasarīsapā jīvibrahmaṃ.

One gets up and leaves due to a danger: from kings, thieves, fire, and water; from humans and non-humans; from beasts of prey and reptiles; from danger to life and danger to the holy life.

Dasannamaññatarena, tasmiṃ aññataresu vā;

Dhammikādhammikā [T 2.0319] ceva, yathā maggena jānātha.

If one leaves due to one of those ten dangers, whether in that place or in another, you should know, according to the way, whether the act is lawful or unlawful.

Kālabhūtatthasaṃhitaṃ[P 2.0252], labhissāmi bhavissati;

Kāyavācasikā mettā, bāhusaccaṃ ubhayāni.

An accuser should speak what is timely, true, and beneficial; he should think, ‘I will get a chance, it will happen’; he should have loving-kindness in body and speech, great learning, and knowledge of both Pātimokkhas.

Kālabhūtena saṇhena, atthamettena codaye;

Vippaṭisāradhammena, tathā vācā tathevāpi (syā.) vinodaye.

One should accuse with what is timely, true, gentle, beneficial, and with a mind of loving-kindness. Through an unlawful accusation, for both the accuser and the one accused in the same way, remorse cannot be dispelled.

Dhammacodacuditassa, vinodeti vippaṭisāro;

Karuṇā hitānukampi, vuṭṭhānapurekkhārato.

For one who accuses according to the Dhamma and one who is accused according to the Dhamma, remorse is dispelled. This is due to: compassion, desiring his welfare, sympathy, desiring him to rise from the offense, and holding the Vinaya foremost.

Codakassa paṭipatti, sambuddhena pakāsitā;

Sacce ceva akuppe ca, cuditasseva dhammatāti.

Thus, the practice of the accuser has been declared by the Perfectly Enlightened One; and for the one accused, standing in truth and non-anger is declared as the proper nature. Thus it should be known.

Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha is concluded.

10. Bhikkhunikkhandhakaṃ

10. The Chapter on Bhikkhunīs

1. Paṭhamabhāṇavāro

1. The First Recitation Section

Mahāpajāpatigotamīvatthu

The Story of Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī

402. a. ni. 8.51 idaṃ vatthu āgataṃ Tena [T 2.0320][P 2.0253][M 0.0442][V 0.0415] samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho mahāpajāpati mahāpajāpatī (sī. syā.) gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti. “Alaṃ, gotami, mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjā”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho mahapajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti. “Alaṃ, gotami, mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjā”ti. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī – na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjanti – dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

402. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Monastery.
