Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if a woman might obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” “Enough, Gotamī, do not desire that a woman should obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” A second time… A third time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if a woman might obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” “Enough, Gotamī, do not desire that a woman should obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, thinking, “The Blessed One does not permit the going forth for a woman from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata,” being sorrowful, dejected, with a tearful face, and weeping, paid homage to the Blessed One, and having circumambulated him keeping her right side towards him, departed.

Atha kho bhagavā kapilavatthusmiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane [T 2.0321] kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī kese chedāpetvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā sambahulāhi sākiyānīhi saddhiṃ yena vesālī tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena vesālī mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā [V 0.0416] bahidvārakoṭṭhake aṭṭhāsi. Addasā kho āyasmā [P 2.0254] ānando mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhiṃ dummanaṃ assumukhiṃ rudamānaṃ bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ [M 0.0443] etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, gotami, sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitā”ti? “Tathā hi pana, bhante ānanda, na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, gotami, muhuttaṃ idheva tāva hohi, yāvāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ yācāmi mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti.

Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Kapilavatthu for as long as he wished, set out on tour to Vesālī. Touring by stages, he arrived at Vesālī. There the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, having had her hair cut off and put on ochre robes, set out for Vesālī together with many Sakyan women. Touring by stages, she arrived at Vesālī, at the Great Wood, at the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, with swollen feet, her body covered with dust, sorrowful, dejected, with tearful face, weeping, stood outside the gatehouse. Venerable Ānanda saw Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī standing outside the gatehouse with swollen feet, her body covered with dust, sorrowful, dejected, with tearful face, weeping. Having seen Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, he said this to her: “Why, Gotamī, are you standing outside the gatehouse with swollen feet, your body covered with dust, sorrowful, dejected, with tearful face, weeping?” “Because, Venerable Ānanda, the Blessed One does not permit a woman's going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” “In that case, Gotamī, wait here for a moment while I request of the Blessed One the going forth for a woman from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “esā, bhante, mahāpajāpati gotamī sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitā – na bhagavā [T 2.0322] anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjanti. Sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti. “Alaṃ, ānanda, mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjā”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti. “Alaṃ, ānanda, mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjā”ti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, here is Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, standing outside the gatehouse with swollen feet, her body covered with dust, sorrowful, dejected, with a tearful face, weeping, because the Blessed One does not permit a woman’s going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if a woman might obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” “Enough, Ānanda. Let it not be pleasing to you that a woman should go forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” For a second time… For a third time, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “It would be good, Venerable Sir, if a woman might obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.” “Enough, Ānanda. Let it not be pleasing to you that a woman should go forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando a. ni. 8.51 “atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosī”ti āgataṃ – “na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjaṃ; yaṃnūnāhaṃ aññenapi pariyāyena bhagavantaṃ yāceyyaṃ mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhabbo nu kho, bhante, mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalaṃ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ sakidāgāmiphalaṃ (syā.) vā anāgāmiphalaṃ vā arahattaphalaṃ [T 2.0323] vā sacchikātu”nti? “Bhabbo, ānanda, mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalampi sakadāgāmiphalampi [M 0.0444] anāgāmiphalampi arahattaphalampi sacchikātu”nti. “Sace, bhante, bhabbo mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalampi sakadāgāmiphalampi [V 0.0417] anāgāmiphalampi arahattaphalampi sacchikātuṃ; bahūpakārā, bhante, mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavato mātucchā āpādikā[P 2.0255], posikā, khīrassa dāyikā, bhagavantaṃ janettiyā kālaṅkatāya thaññaṃ pāyesi; sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajja”nti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda thought: “The Blessed One does not permit a woman's going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata. What if I were to request of the Blessed One by another means the going forth for a woman from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata?” Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, is a woman, having gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, capable of realizing the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arahantship?” “She is capable, Ānanda. A woman, having gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, is capable of realizing the fruit of stream-entry, and the fruit of once-returning, and the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arahantship.” “If, Venerable Sir, a woman is capable of realizing the fruit of stream-entry, and the fruit of once-returning, and the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arahantship, having gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata; then, Venerable Sir, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī has been of great service to the Blessed One. She is his maternal aunt, foster mother, nourisher, and giver of milk; when his own mother passed away, she suckled the Blessed One. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if a woman might obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”

Aṭṭhagarudhammā

The Eight Weighty Principles

403. “Sace, ānanda, mahāpajāpatī gotamī aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇhāti, sāvassā. Hotu upasampadā.

403. “Ānanda, if Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts the eight weighty principles, let that itself be her ordination.”

pāci. 149 “Vassasatūpasampannāya bhikkhuniyā tadahupasampannassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā garuṃkatvā (ka.) mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

“A bhikkhunī ordained for a hundred years is to perform salutation towards, rise up for, raise the joined palms in reverence to, and perform proper duties for a bhikkhu ordained on that very day. This principle is to be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Na bhikkhuniyā abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

“A bhikkhunī is not to spend the rains-residence in a monastery where there is no bhikkhu. This principle is also to be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Anvaddhamāsaṃ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā – uposathapucchakañca, ovādūpasaṅkamanañca. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

“Every half-month, a bhikkhunī is to expect two things from the Bhikkhu Saṅgha: the asking of the Uposatha day and the approaching for an exhortation. This principle is also to be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Vassaṃvuṭṭhāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe [T 2.0324] tīhi ṭhānehi pavāretabbaṃ – diṭṭhena vā, sutena vā, parisaṅkāya vā. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

“A bhikkhunī who has completed the rains-residence is to perform the Pavāraṇā before the dual Saṅgha on three grounds: by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. This principle is also to be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṃ caritabbaṃ. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A bhikkhunī who has transgressed a grave rule must undergo the pakkhamānatta penance before the dual Saṅgha. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya ubhatosaṅghe upasampadā pariyesitabbā. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A sikkhamānā who has trained for two years in the six rules should seek higher ordination from the dual Saṅgha. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Na [M 0.0445][V 0.0418] bhikkhuniyā kenaci pariyāyena bhikkhu akkositabbo paribhāsitabbo. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A bhikkhunī must not, for any reason whatsoever, revile or abuse a bhikkhu. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Ajjatagge ovaṭo bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūsu vacanapatho, anovaṭo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīsu vacanapatho. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

From today onwards, the admonition of bhikkhus by bhikkhunīs is forbidden, whereas the admonition of bhikkhunīs by bhikkhus is not forbidden. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Sace, ānanda, mahāpajāpati gotamī ime aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇhāti, sāvassā hotu upasampadā”ti.

“If, Ānanda, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts these eight grave principles, let that very acceptance be her higher ordination.”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato santike aṭṭha garudhamme uggahetvā yena mahāpajāpati gotamī tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavoca – “sace kho tvaṃ, gotami, aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇheyyāsi, sāva te bhavissati upasampadā.

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having learned the eight grave principles from the Blessed One, went to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī and said to her: “Gotamī, if you accept these eight grave principles, that very acceptance will be your higher ordination.”

“Vassasatūpasampannāya bhikkhuniyā tadahupasampannassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Ayampi [T 2.0325] dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A bhikkhunī ordained for a hundred years must pay homage to, rise up for, salute with joined palms, and perform respectful service for a bhikkhu ordained that very day. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Na bhikkhuniyā abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A bhikkhunī should not spend the rains-retreat in a residence where there is no bhikkhu. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Anvaddhamāsaṃ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā – uposathapucchakañca, ovādūpasaṅkamanañca. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

Every half-month, a bhikkhunī should expect two things from the Bhikkhu Saṅgha: the asking of the Uposatha day and the approaching for an exhortation. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Vassaṃvuṭṭhāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi pavāretabbaṃ – diṭṭhena vā, sutena vā, parisaṅkāya vā. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

After completing the rains-retreat, a bhikkhunī should perform the Pavāraṇā before the dual Saṅgha on three grounds: by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṃ caritabbaṃ. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A bhikkhunī who has committed a grave offense must undergo the pakkhamānatta penance before the dual Saṅgha. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Dve [V 0.0419] vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya ubhatosaṅghe upasampadā pariyesitabbā. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A sikkhamānā who has trained for two years in the six rules should seek higher ordination from the dual Saṅgha. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Na [M 0.0446] bhikkhuniyā kenaci pariyāyena bhikkhu akkositabbo paribhāsitabbo. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

A bhikkhunī must not, by any means, revile or abuse a bhikkhu. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Ajjatagge ovaṭo bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūsu vacanapatho, anovaṭo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīsu vacanapatho. Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo.

From today onwards, the admonition of bhikkhus by bhikkhunīs is forbidden, whereas the admonition of bhikkhunīs by bhikkhus is not forbidden. This principle, too, should be respected, honored, esteemed, and revered, and is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

“Sace kho tvaṃ, gotami, ime aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇheyyāsi, sāva te bhavissati [T 2.0326] upasampadā”ti.

“Gotamī, if you accept these eight grave principles, that very acceptance will be your higher ordination.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhante ānanda, itthī vā puriso vā daharo, yuvā, maṇḍanakajātiko sīsaṃnahāto uppalamālaṃ vā vassikamālaṃ vā atimuttakamālaṃ [P 2.0256] adhimattakamālaṃ (syā.) vā labhitvā ubhohi hatthehi paṭiggahetvā uttamaṅge sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhāpeyya; evameva kho ahaṃ, bhante, ānanda ime aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇhāmi yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīye”ti.

“Venerable Ānanda, just as a young woman or man, fond of adornment, having washed their head, would receive a garland of lotuses, jasmine, or atimuttaka flowers, and taking it with both hands, place it upon their head, the highest limb; even so, Venerable Ānanda, I accept these eight grave principles, not to be transgressed for as long as I live.”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭiggahitā, bhante, mahāpajāpatiyā gotamiyā aṭṭha garudhammā, upasampannā bhagavato mātucchā”ti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the eight grave principles have been accepted by Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī; the Blessed One’s maternal aunt is now ordained.”

“Sace, ānanda, nālabhissa mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjaṃ, ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, ānanda, brahmacariyaṃ abhavissa, vassasahassaṃ saddhammo tiṭṭheyya. Yato ca kho, ānanda, mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na dāni, ānanda, brahmacariyaṃ ciraṭṭhitikaṃ bhavissati. Pañceva dāni, ānanda, vassasatāni saddhammo ṭhassati.

“Ānanda, if women had not obtained the going forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the holy life, Ānanda, would have been long-lasting; the good Dhamma would have endured for a thousand years. But since, Ānanda, women have gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the holy life, Ānanda, will not now be long-lasting. Now, Ānanda, the good Dhamma will endure for only five hundred years.”

“Seyyathāpi, ānanda, yāni kānici kulāni [T 2.0327] bahutthikāni bahuitthikāni (sī. syā.) appapurisakāni, tāni suppadhaṃsiyāni [V 0.0420] honti corehi kumbhathenakehi; evameva kho, ānanda, yasmiṃ dhammavinaye labhati mātugāmo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjaṃ, na taṃ brahmacariyaṃ ciraṭṭhitikaṃ hoti.

“Just as, Ānanda, those families with many women and few men are easily plundered by burglars; even so, Ānanda, in whatever Dhamma and Discipline women obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness, that holy life is not long-lasting.”

“Seyyathāpi[M 0.0447], ānanda, sampanne sālikkhette setaṭṭikā nāma rogajāti nipatati, evaṃ taṃ sālikkhettaṃ na ciraṭṭhitikaṃ hoti; evameva kho, ānanda, yasmiṃ dhammavinaye labhati mātugāmo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjaṃ, na taṃ brahmacariyaṃ ciraṭṭhitikaṃ hoti.

“Just as, Ānanda, when a type of disease called ‘white blight’ falls upon a flourishing rice field, that rice field is not long-lasting; even so, Ānanda, in whatever Dhamma and Discipline women obtain the going forth from the household life into homelessness, that holy life is not long-lasting.”

“Seyyathāpi, ānanda, sampanne ucchukkhette mañjiṭṭhikā mañjeṭṭhikā (sī. syā.) nāma rogajāti nipatati, evaṃ taṃ ucchukkhettaṃ na ciraṭṭhitikaṃ hoti; evameva kho, ānanda, yasmiṃ dhammavinaye labhati mātugāmo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjaṃ, na taṃ brahmacariyaṃ ciraṭṭhitikaṃ hoti.

Just as, Ānanda, when a disease called red rot falls upon a flourishing sugarcane field, that sugarcane field does not last long; even so, Ānanda, in whatever Dhamma and Vinaya a woman obtains the going forth from the household life into homelessness, that holy life does not last long.

“Seyyathāpi, ānanda, puriso mahato taḷākassa paṭikacceva āḷiṃ bandheyya yāvadeva udakassa anatikkamanāya; evameva kho, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva bhikkhunīnaṃ aṭṭha garudhammā paññattā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyā”ti.

Just as, Ānanda, a man might build an embankment for a great reservoir beforehand, precisely to prevent the water from overflowing; even so, Ānanda, have I laid down beforehand these eight weighty principles for bhikkhunīs, not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.

Bhikkhunīnaṃ aṭṭha garudhammā niṭṭhitā.

The eight weighty principles for bhikkhunīs are concluded.

Bhikkhunīupasampadānujānanaṃ

The Authorization of the Higher Ordination for Bhikkhunīs

404. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā [T 2.0328] kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathāhaṃ, bhante, imāsu sākiyānīsu [P 2.0257] paṭipajjāmī”ti? Atha kho bhagavā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhuniyo upasampādetu”nti.

404. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, how should I act concerning these Sakyan women?” Then the Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī with a Dhamma talk. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, having been instructed, established, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to her right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow bhikkhunīs to be given higher ordination by bhikkhus.”

Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayyā anupasampannā, mayañcamhā upasampannā; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ bhikkhūhi bhikkhuniyo upasampādetabbā”ti. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī [M 0.0448] yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā [V 0.0421] āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “imā maṃ, bhante ānanda, bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – ‘ayyā anupasampannā, mayañcamhā upasampannā; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ bhikkhūhi bhikkhuniyo upasampādetabbā’”ti.

Then those bhikkhunīs said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī: ‘Noble Lady, you are not yet ordained with higher ordination, whereas we are. For it has been laid down by the Blessed One that bhikkhunīs are to be given higher ordination by bhikkhus.’ Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Venerable Ānanda: ‘Venerable Ānanda, these bhikkhunīs said this to me: “Noble Lady, you are not yet ordained with higher ordination, whereas we are. For it has been laid down by the Blessed One that bhikkhunīs are to be given higher ordination by bhikkhus.”’”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ [T 2.0329] etadavoca – “mahāpajāpati, bhante, gotamī evamāha – ‘imā maṃ, bhante ānanda, bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – ayyā anupasampannā, mayañcamhā upasampannā; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ bhikkhūhi bhikkhuniyo upasampādetabbā’”ti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable Sir, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī says thus: “Venerable Ānanda, these bhikkhunīs said this to me: ‘Noble Lady, you are not yet ordained with higher ordination, whereas we are. For it has been laid down by the Blessed One that bhikkhunīs are to be given higher ordination by bhikkhus.’”’”

“Yadaggena, ānanda, mahāpajāpatiyā gotamiyā aṭṭha garudhammā paṭiggahitā, tadeva sā tadevassā (ka.) upasampannā”ti.

“Ānanda, from the day that the eight weighty principles were accepted by Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, on that very day she was ordained with higher ordination.”

405. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “ekāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhagavantaṃ varaṃ yācāmi. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā anujāneyya bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikamma”nti.

405. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Venerable Ānanda: ‘Venerable Ānanda, I ask one boon of the Blessed One. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One would permit, for both bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, paying homage, rising up for, saluting with joined palms, and showing proper respect, according to seniority.’”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mahāpajāpati, bhante, gotamī evamāha – ‘ekāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhagavantaṃ varaṃ yācāmi. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā anujāneyya bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikamma’”nti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī says thus: ‘Venerable Ānanda, I ask the Blessed One for one boon. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One would permit for both bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, according to seniority, paying homage, rising up for, saluting with joined palms, and showing proper respect.’”

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ, ānanda, anavakāso[P 2.0258], yaṃ tathāgato anujāneyya mātugāmassa abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ. Imehi nāma, ānanda, aññatitthiyā durakkhātadhammā mātugāmassa abhivādanaṃ [T 2.0330] paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ [M 0.0449] sāmīcikammaṃ na karissanti[V 0.0422]; kimaṅgaṃ pana tathāgato anujānissati mātugāmassa abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikamma”nti?

“Ānanda, it is impossible, it cannot happen that the Tathāgata would permit paying homage to a woman, rising up for her, saluting her with joined palms, or showing her proper respect. Ānanda, even these other sectarians, whose doctrines are poorly expounded, do not pay homage to a woman, rise up for her, salute her with joined palms, or show her proper respect; for what reason then would the Tathāgata permit paying homage to a woman, rising up for her, saluting her with joined palms, or showing her proper respect?”

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, mātugāmassa abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, a woman is not to be paid homage to, risen up for, saluted with joined palms, or shown proper respect. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yāni tāni, bhante, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni bhikkhūhi sādhāraṇāni, kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, tesu sikkhāpadesu paṭipajjāmā”ti? “Yāni tāni, gotami, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni bhikkhūhi sādhāraṇāni, yathā bhikkhū sikkhanti tathā tesu sikkhāpadesu sikkhathā”ti. “Yāni pana tāni, bhante, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇāni, kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, tesu sikkhāpadesu paṭipajjāmā”ti? “Yāni tāni, gotami, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇāni, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu sikkhathā”ti.

Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having paid homage to him, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, as for those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are common with the bhikkhus, how should we, Venerable Sir, practice in regard to them?” “Gotamī, as for those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are common with the bhikkhus, you should train in them as the bhikkhus train.” “But, Venerable Sir, as for those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are not common with the bhikkhus, how should we, Venerable Sir, practice in regard to them?” “Gotamī, as for those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are not common with the bhikkhus, you should train in the training rules as they have been laid down.”

406. a. ni. 8.53 Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ [T 2.0331] sutvā ekā vūpakaṭṭhā appamattā ātāpinī pahitattā vihareyya”nti. “Ye kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi – ime dhammā sarāgāya saṃvattanti no virāgāya, saññogāya saṃvattanti no visaññogāya, ācayāya saṃvattanti no apacayāya, mahicchatāya saṃvattanti no appicchatāya, asantuṭṭhiyā saṃvattanti no santuṭṭhiyā, saṅgaṇikāya saṃvattanti no pavivekāya, kosajjāya saṃvattanti no vīriyārambhāya, dubbharatāya [P 2.0259] saṃvattanti no subharatāya; ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi – neso dhammo, neso vinayo, netaṃ satthusāsananti. Ye ca kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi – ime dhammā virāgāya saṃvattanti no sarāgāya, visaññogāya saṃvattanti no saññogāya, apacayāya saṃvattanti no ācayāya, appicchatāya saṃvattanti no [M 0.0450] mahicchatāya, santuṭṭhiyā saṃvattanti no asantuṭṭhiyā, pavivekāya saṃvattanti no saṅgaṇikāya, vīriyārambhāya [V 0.0423] saṃvattanti no kosajjāya, subharatāya saṃvattanti no dubbharatāya; ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi – eso dhammo, eso vinayo, etaṃ satthusāsana”nti.

406. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having paid homage to him, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.” “Gotamī, of those things you might know thus: ‘These things lead to passion, not to dispassion; they lead to bondage, not to release from bondage; they lead to accumulation, not to dissolution; they lead to great ambition, not to fewness of wishes; they lead to discontent, not to contentment; they lead to delight in company, not to seclusion; they lead to laziness, not to the arousal of energy; they lead to being difficult to support, not to being easy to support’—of such, Gotamī, you should hold with certainty: ‘This is not the Dhamma, this is not the Vinaya, this is not the Teacher’s instruction.’ But of those things you might know thus: ‘These things lead to dispassion, not to passion; they lead to release from bondage, not to bondage; they lead to dissolution, not to accumulation; they lead to fewness of wishes, not to great ambition; they lead to contentment, not to discontent; they lead to seclusion, not to delight in company; they lead to the arousal of energy, not to laziness; they lead to being easy to support, not to being difficult to support’—of such, Gotamī, you should hold with certainty: ‘This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’”

407. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ na uddisīyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… [T 2.0332] “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti.

407. At that time, the Pātimokkha was not recited for the bhikkhunīs. They reported this matter to the Blessed One... I allow, O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha to be recited for the bhikkhunīs. Then this thought arose to the bhikkhus: “By whom, indeed, should the Pātimokkha be recited for the bhikkhunīs?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. I allow, O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha to be recited for the bhikkhunīs by the bhikkhus.

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “jāyāyo imā imesaṃ, jāriyo imā imesaṃ, idāni ime imāhi saddhiṃ abhiramissantī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīhi bhikkhunīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti. Bhikkhuniyo na jānanti – “evaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ ācikkhituṃ – ‘evaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyāthā’”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus, having approached the bhikkhunīs’ dwelling, recited the Pātimokkha for the bhikkhunīs. People complained, were critical, and spread it about: “These are their wives, these are their paramours; now they will enjoy themselves with them!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should not be recited for the bhikkhunīs by bhikkhus. Whoever should recite it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha to be recited for the bhikkhunīs by the bhikkhunīs.” The bhikkhunīs did not know: “In this way the Pātimokkha should be recited.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, O bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs be instructed by the bhikkhus: ‘In this way you should recite the Pātimokkha.’”

408. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo āpattiṃ na paṭikaronti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā āpatti na paṭikātabbā. Yā na paṭikareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo na jānanti – “evaṃ āpatti paṭikātabbā”ti[T 2.0333]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ ācikkhituṃ – ‘evaṃ āpattiṃ paṭikareyyāthā’”ti. Atha [P 2.0260] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho bhikkhunīnaṃ āpatti paṭiggahetabbā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ āpattiṃ paṭiggahetu”nti.

408. At that time, the bhikkhunīs did not make amends for an offense. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not fail to make amends for an offense. Whoever does not make amends commits an offense of wrong-doing.” The bhikkhunīs did not know: “This is how an offense should be made amends for.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O bhikkhus, I allow bhikkhus to instruct the bhikkhunīs: ‘You should make amends for an offense in this way.’” Then the bhikkhus thought: “By whom should the bhikkhunīs’ offense be received?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O bhikkhus, I allow bhikkhus to receive the bhikkhunīs’ offense.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo rathikāyapi byūhepi siṅghāṭakepi bhikkhuṃ passitvā pattaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ [M 0.0451] nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā āpattiṃ paṭikaronti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “jāyāyo imā imesaṃ, jāriyo imā imesaṃ, rattiṃ vimānetvā idāni khamāpentī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0424]. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ āpatti paṭiggahetabbā. Yo paṭiggaṇheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīhi bhikkhunīnaṃ āpattiṃ paṭiggahetu”nti. Bhikkhuniyo na jānanti – “evaṃ āpatti paṭiggahetabbā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ ācikkhituṃ – ‘evaṃ āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇheyyāthā’”ti.

At that time, bhikkhunīs, upon seeing a bhikkhu on a street, in a narrow street, or at a crossroads, would place their bowl on the ground, arrange their upper robe over one shoulder, squat down, raise their joined hands, and make amends for an offense. People complained, criticized, and spread gossip, saying: “These are their wives, these are their mistresses; after misbehaving at night, now they are asking for forgiveness!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O Bhikkhus, the offense of bhikkhunīs should not be received by bhikkhus. Whoever should receive it commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, O Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs to receive the offense of bhikkhunīs.” The bhikkhunīs did not know: “In this way an offense should be received.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, O Bhikkhus, bhikkhus to instruct the bhikkhunīs: ‘You should receive an offense in this way.’”

409. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ na kariyati[T 2.0334]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ kātu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ kātabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ kātu”nti.

409. At that time, a formal act was not being performed for the bhikkhunīs. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “I allow, O Bhikkhus, a formal act to be performed for the bhikkhunīs.” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhus: “By whom, indeed, should a formal act be performed for the bhikkhunīs?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “I allow, O Bhikkhus, that a formal act be performed for the bhikkhunīs by the bhikkhus.”

Tena kho pana samayena katakammā bhikkhuniyo rathikāyapi byūhepi siṅghāṭakepi bhikkhuṃ passitvā pattaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā khamāpenti ‘evaṃ nūna kātabba’nti maññamānā. Manussā tatheva ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “jāyāyo imā imesaṃ, jāriyo imā imesaṃ, rattiṃ vimānetvā idāni khamāpentī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīhi bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ kātu”nti. Bhikkhuniyo na jānanti – “evaṃ kammaṃ kātabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ ācikkhituṃ – ‘evaṃ kammaṃ kareyyāthā’”ti.

At that time, bhikkhunīs for whom a formal act had been performed, upon seeing a bhikkhu on a street, on a narrow path, or at a crossroads, would place their bowls on the ground, arrange their upper robes over one shoulder, sit squatting, raise their joined hands, and ask for forgiveness, thinking, “Surely, it should be done thus.” People complained, scorned, and spread gossip in the same way, saying, “These are their wives, these are their mistresses; having misbehaved at night, now they ask for forgiveness.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “O Bhikkhus, a formal act should not be performed for the bhikkhunīs by the bhikkhus. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, O Bhikkhus, a formal act to be performed for the bhikkhunīs by the bhikkhunīs.” The bhikkhunīs did not know, “Thus should a formal act be performed.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “I allow, O Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus to instruct the bhikkhunīs, ‘You should perform the formal act thus.’”

410. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo saṅghamajjhe bhaṇḍanajātā [P 2.0261] kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti. Na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Bhagavato [T 2.0335] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametu”nti.

410. At that time, bhikkhunīs in the midst of the Sangha, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into disputation, were dwelling while piercing one another with verbal spears. They were not able to settle that legal issue. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “I allow, O Bhikkhus, that a legal issue for the bhikkhunīs be settled by the bhikkhus.”

Tena [M 0.0452] kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhikkhunīnaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamenti. Tasmiṃ kho pana adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne dissanti bhikkhuniyo kammappattāyopi āpattigāminiyopi. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “sādhu, bhante, ayyāva bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ karontu, ayyāva bhikkhunīnaṃ āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇhantu; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ [V 0.0425] vūpasametabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ āropetvā bhikkhunīnaṃ niyyādetuṃ – bhikkhunīhi bhikkhunīnaṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ āpattiṃ āropetvā bhikkhunīnaṃ niyyādetuṃ, bhikkhunīhi bhikkhunīnaṃ āpattiṃ paṭiggahetu”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus were settling the legal issues of bhikkhunīs. While that legal issue was being decided, bhikkhunīs who were liable for a formal act and liable for an offense were seen. The bhikkhunīs said thus: “Please, venerable sirs, may the venerable ones themselves perform the formal act for the bhikkhunīs; may the venerable ones themselves receive the offense of the bhikkhunīs. For it has been laid down by the Blessed One that the legal issues of bhikkhunīs should be settled by bhikkhus.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “I allow, O Bhikkhus, that bhikkhus, having assigned a formal act to bhikkhunīs, may hand it over to the bhikkhunīs for the bhikkhunīs to perform the formal act for bhikkhunīs; and that bhikkhus, having assigned an offense to bhikkhunīs, may hand it over to the bhikkhunīs for the bhikkhunīs to receive the offense of bhikkhunīs.”

Tena kho pana samayena uppalavaṇṇāya bhikkhuniyā antevāsinī bhikkhunī satta vassāni bhagavantaṃ anubandhā hoti vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇantī. Tassā muṭṭhassatiniyā gahito gahito mussati. Assosi kho sā bhikkhunī – “bhagavā kira sāvatthiṃ gantukāmo”ti. Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho satta vassāni bhagavantaṃ anubandhiṃ vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇantī. Tassā me muṭṭhassatiniyā gahito gahito mussati. Dukkaraṃ kho pana mātugāmena yāvajīvaṃ satthāraṃ [T 2.0336] anubandhituṃ. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ vinayaṃ vācetu”nti.

At that time, a bhikkhunī who was a pupil of the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā had been following the Blessed One for seven years, learning the Vinaya. Due to her lapsed memory, whatever she grasped, she forgot. That bhikkhunī heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, intends to go to Sāvatthī.” Then this thought arose in that bhikkhunī: “For seven years I have been following the Blessed One, learning the Vinaya. Due to my lapsed memory, whatever I grasp, I forget. It is indeed difficult for a woman to follow the Teacher for her whole life. How indeed should I proceed?” Then that bhikkhunī told this matter to the bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs told this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “I allow, O Bhikkhus, that bhikkhus may teach the Vinaya to bhikkhunīs.”

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is finished.

2. Dutiyabhāṇavāro

2. The Second Recitation Section

411. Atha kho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[P 2.0262]. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo kaddamodakena osiñcanti – appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyunti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā [M 0.0453] bhikkhuniyo kaddamodakena osiñcitabbā. Yo osiñceyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tassa bhikkhuno daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho daṇḍakammaṃ kātabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Avandiyo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena kātabbo”ti.

411. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Vesālī as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Sāvatthī. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One stayed in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks splashed the nuns with muddy water, thinking, “Perhaps they will become attracted to us.” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, a monk should not splash nuns with muddy water. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow a disciplinary action to be taken against that monk.” Then this thought occurred to the monks: “What kind of disciplinary action should be taken?” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, that monk should be made unworthy of being paid homage to by the community of nuns.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kāyaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti [V 0.0426] …pe… ūruṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, aṅgajātaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, bhikkhuniyo obhāsenti, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ sampayojenti – appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyunti. Bhagavato [T 2.0337] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā kāyo vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassetabbo, na ūru vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassetabbo, na aṅgajātaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassetabbaṃ, na bhikkhuniyo obhāsitabbā, na bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ sampayojetabbaṃ. Yo sampayojeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tassa bhikkhuno daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho daṇḍakammaṃ kātabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Avandiyo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena kātabbo”ti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks exposed their bodies to the nuns… exposed their thighs to the nuns, exposed their genitals to the nuns, flirted with the nuns, and associated with the nuns, thinking, “Perhaps they will become attracted to us.” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, a monk should not expose his body to nuns, should not expose his thighs to nuns, should not expose his genitals to nuns, should not flirt with nuns, and should not associate with nuns. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow a disciplinary action to be taken against that monk.” Then this thought occurred to the monks: “What kind of disciplinary action should be taken?” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, that monk should be made unworthy of being paid homage to by the community of nuns.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuṃ kaddamodakena osiñcanti – appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyunti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhu kaddamodakena osiñcitabbo. Yā osiñceyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tassā bhikkhuniyā daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho daṇḍakammaṃ kātabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ kātu”nti. Āvaraṇe kate na ādiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ovādaṃ ṭhapetu”nti.

At that time the group-of-six nuns splashed a monk with muddy water, thinking, 'Perhaps he might become attracted to us.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a monk should not be splashed with muddy water by a nun. Whichever nun should splash him, it is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that disciplinary action be taken against that nun.' Then the monks thought, 'What kind of disciplinary action should be taken?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, to impose a prohibition.' When the prohibition was imposed, they did not comply. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, to suspend the instruction.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo kāyaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhūnaṃ dassenti, thanaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhūnaṃ dassenti, ūruṃ vivaritvā [T 2.0338] bhikkhūnaṃ dassenti, aṅgajātaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhūnaṃ dassenti, bhikkhū obhāsenti, bhikkhūhi [P 2.0263] saddhiṃ sampayojenti – appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyunti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā kāyo vivaritvā bhikkhūnaṃ dassetabbo…pe… na thano vivaritvā [M 0.0454] bhikkhūnaṃ dassetabbo, na ūru vivaritvā bhikkhūnaṃ dassetabbo, na aṅgajātaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhūnaṃ dassetabbaṃ, na bhikkhū obhāsitabbā, na bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ sampayojetabbaṃ. Yā sampayojeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tassā bhikkhuniyā daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho daṇḍakammaṃ kātabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ kātu”nti. Āvaraṇe kate na ādiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ovādaṃ ṭhapetu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kappati nu kho ovādaṭṭhapitāya ovādaṇṭhapitāya (syā.), ovādaṃṭhapitāya (ka.) bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ uposathaṃ kātuṃ, na nu kho [V 0.0427] kappatī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādaṭṭhapitāya bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ uposatho kātabbo, yāva na taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ hotī”ti.

At that time, the nuns of the group of six exposed their bodies to the monks, exposed their breasts to the monks, exposed their thighs to the monks, and exposed their genitals to the monks; they flirted with the monks and associated with the monks, with the thought, 'Indeed, may they become attached to us.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a nun should not expose her body to monks... she should not expose her breasts to monks, she should not expose her thighs to monks, she should not expose her genitals to monks, she should not flirt with monks, she should not associate with monks. Whichever one should associate, it is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that a disciplinary action be performed for that nun.' Then it occurred to the monks, 'What disciplinary action, I wonder, should be performed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, that a prohibition be made.' When the prohibition was made, they did not heed it. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, that the instruction be suspended.' Then it occurred to the monks, 'Is it, I wonder, allowable to perform the Uposatha with a nun for whom instruction has been suspended, or is it not allowable?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the Uposatha should not be performed with a nun for whom instruction has been suspended, so long as that legal issue is not settled.'

412. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī ovādaṃ ṭhapetvā cārikaṃ [T 2.0339] pakkāmi. Bhikkhuniyo ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyo udāyī ovādaṃ ṭhapetvā cārikaṃ pakkamissatī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādaṃ ṭhapetvā cārikā pakkamitabbā. Yo pakkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

412. At that time, the Venerable Udāyī, having suspended the instruction, departed on a journey. The nuns complained, criticized, and grumbled, saying: ‘How indeed can the Venerable Udāyī set out on a journey, having suspended the instruction?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, one should not depart on a journey having suspended the instruction. Whoever should depart commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

Tena kho pana samayena tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū (syā. kaṃ.) bālā abyattā ovādaṃ ṭhapenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bālena abyattena ovādo ṭhapetabbo. Yo ṭhapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, foolish and incompetent monks were suspending the instruction. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, the instruction should not be suspended by one who is foolish and incompetent. Whoever should suspend it commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ovādaṃ ṭhapenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ovādo ṭhapetabbo. Yo ṭhapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks were suspending the instruction without a proper case and without a reason. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, the instruction should not be suspended without a proper case and without a reason. Whoever should suspend it commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ovādaṃ ṭhapetvā vinicchayaṃ na denti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādaṃ ṭhapetvā vinicchayo na dātabbo. Yo na dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks, having set aside the instruction, were not giving a judgment. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, it is not that a judgment should not be given having set aside the instruction; it should indeed be given. Whoever should not give it commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

413. pāci. 1054 Tena [M 0.0455] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ na gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā ovādo na [T 2.0340] gantabbo. Yā na gaccheyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

413. At that time, the nuns were not going for instruction. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, it is not that a nun should not go for instruction; she should indeed go. Whichever nun should not go, she is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma.’

Tena kho pana samayena sabbo bhikkhunisaṅgho ovādaṃ gacchati. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [P 2.0264] vipācenti – “jāyāyo imā imesaṃ, jāriyo imā imesaṃ, idāni ime imāhi saddhiṃ abhiramissantī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, sabbena bhikkhunisaṅghena ovādo gantabbo. Gaccheyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catūhi pañcahi bhikkhunīhi ovādaṃ gantu”nti.

At that time, the entire community of nuns was going for instruction. People complained, criticized, and grumbled, saying: ‘These are their wives, these are their mistresses! Now these men will enjoy themselves together with these women!’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, the entire community of nuns should not go for instruction. Should they go, there is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, four or five nuns to go for instruction.’

Tena kho pana samayena catasso pañca bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ gacchanti. Manussā tatheva ujjhāyanti [V 0.0428] khiyyanti vipācenti – “jāyāyo imā imesaṃ, jāriyo imā imesaṃ, idāni ime imāhi saddhiṃ abhiramissantī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, catūhi pañcahi bhikkhunīhi ovādo gantabbo. Gaccheyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve tisso bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīhi (ka.) ovādaṃ gantuṃ. Ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘bhikkhunisaṅgho, ayya, bhikkhusaṅghassa pāde vandati, ovādūpasaṅkamanañca yācati; labhatu kira, ayya, bhikkhunisaṅgho ovādūpasaṅkamana’nti. Tena bhikkhunā pātimokkhuddesako upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘bhikkhunīsaṅgho, bhante, bhikkhusaṅghassa pāde vandati, ovādūpasaṅkamanañca [T 2.0341] yācati; labhatu kira, bhante, bhikkhunisaṅgho ovādūpasaṅkamana’nti. Pātimokkhuddesakena vattabbo – ‘atthi koci bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato’ti? Sace hoti koci bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato, pātimokkhuddesakena vattabbo – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato, taṃ bhikkhunisaṅgho upasaṅkamatū’ti. Sace na hoti koci bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato, pātimokkhuddesakena vattabbo – ‘ko āyasmā ussahati bhikkhuniyo ovaditu’nti? Sace koci ussahati bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ, so ca hoti aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato, sammannitvā vattabbo – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu [M 0.0456] bhikkhunovādako sammato, taṃ bhikkhunisaṅgho upasaṅkamatū’ti. Sace na koci ussahati bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ, pātimokkhuddesakena vattabbo – ‘natthi koci bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato, pāsādikena bhikkhunisaṅgho sampādetū”ti.

At that time, four or five bhikkhunīs went for instruction. People complained, criticized, and grumbled just as before, saying: ‘These are their wives, these are their mistresses! Now these men will enjoy themselves together with these women!’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, four or five bhikkhunīs should not go for instruction. Should they go, it is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, two or three bhikkhunīs to go for instruction. Approaching a bhikkhu, arranging the upper robe over one shoulder, paying homage at his feet, squatting down, and raising their joined palms, they should say this: “Venerable sir, the Community of Bhikkhunīs pays homage at the feet of the Community of Bhikkhus and requests to approach for instruction. May the Community of Bhikkhunīs, venerable sir, indeed receive the opportunity to approach for instruction.” That bhikkhu should approach the reciter of the Pātimokkha and should say this to him: “Venerable sir, the Community of Bhikkhunīs pays homage at the feet of the Community of Bhikkhus and requests to approach for instruction. May the Community of Bhikkhunīs, venerable sir, indeed receive the opportunity to approach for instruction.” The reciter of the Pātimokkha should ask: “Is there any bhikkhu designated as an instructor of bhikkhunīs?” If there is a bhikkhu designated as an instructor of bhikkhunīs, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should say: “The bhikkhu named so-and-so is designated as an instructor of bhikkhunīs. Let the Community of Bhikkhunīs approach him.” If there is no bhikkhu designated as an instructor of bhikkhunīs, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should ask: “Which venerable one is able to instruct the bhikkhunīs?” If someone is able to instruct the bhikkhunīs and he is endowed with the eight qualities, he should be designated, and it should be said: “The bhikkhu named so-and-so is designated as an instructor of bhikkhunīs. Let the Community of Bhikkhunīs approach him.” If no one is able to instruct the bhikkhunīs, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should say: “There is no bhikkhu designated as an instructor of bhikkhunīs. Let the Community of Bhikkhunīs conduct themselves in an inspiring way.”’

414. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ovādaṃ na gaṇhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādo na gahetabbo. Yo na gaṇheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

414. At that time, monks were not accepting the instruction. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, it is not that the instruction should not be accepted; it should indeed be accepted. Whoever should not accept it commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bālo hoti. Taṃ bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “ovādaṃ, ayya, gaṇhāhī”ti[P 2.0265]. “Ahañhi, bhaginī, bālo; kathāhaṃ ovādaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti? “Gaṇhāhayya[T 2.0342], ovādaṃ; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ – bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo gahetabbo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, avasesehi ovādaṃ gahetu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk was foolish. The bhikkhunīs approached him and said: ‘Venerable sir, please accept the instruction.’ He replied: ‘Sisters, I am foolish; how can I accept the instruction?’ They said: ‘Venerable sir, please accept the instruction; for it has been laid down by the Blessed One that the instruction for the bhikkhunīs is to be accepted by the monks.’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, I allow the remaining ones, excepting the foolish one, to accept the instruction.’

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Taṃ bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā [V 0.0429] etadavocuṃ – “ovādaṃ, ayya gaṇhāhī”ti. “Ahañhi, bhaginī, gilāno; kathāhaṃ ovādaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti? “Gaṇhāhayya, ovādaṃ; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ – ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, avasesehi ovādo gahetabbo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, ṭhapetvā gilānaṃ, avasesehi ovādaṃ gahetu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk was ill. The bhikkhunīs approached him and said: ‘Venerable sir, please accept the instruction.’ He replied: ‘Sisters, I am ill; how can I accept the instruction?’ They said: ‘Venerable sir, please accept the instruction; for it has been laid down by the Blessed One: “Excepting the foolish one, the instruction is to be accepted by the remaining ones.”’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, I allow the remaining ones, excepting the foolish one and the ill one, to accept the instruction.’

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gamiko hoti. Taṃ bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “ovādaṃ, ayya, gaṇhāhī”ti. “Ahañhi, bhaginī, gamiko; kathāhaṃ ovādaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti? “Gaṇhāhayya, ovādaṃ; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ – ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, ṭhapetvā gilānaṃ, avasesehi ovādo gahetabbo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, ṭhapetvā gilānaṃ, ṭhapetvā gamikaṃ, avasesehi ovādaṃ gahetu”nti.

At that time, a certain monk was a traveler. The bhikkhunīs approached him and said: ‘Venerable sir, please accept the instruction.’ He replied: ‘Sisters, I am a traveler; how can I accept the instruction?’ They said: ‘Venerable sir, please accept the instruction; for it has been laid down by the Blessed One: “Excepting the foolish one and the ill one, the instruction is to be accepted by the remaining ones.”’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: ‘Monks, I allow the remaining ones, excepting the foolish one, the ill one, and the traveler, to accept the instruction.’

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu araññe viharati. Taṃ bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “ovādaṃ, ayya, gaṇhāhī”ti. “Ahañhi, bhaginī, araññe viharāmi; kathāhaṃ ovādaṃ [T 2.0343] gaṇhāmī”ti? “Gaṇhāhayya[M 0.0457], ovādaṃ; evañhi bhagavatā paññattaṃ – ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, ṭhapetvā gilānaṃ, ṭhapetvā gamikaṃ, avasesehi ovādo gahetabbo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āraññikena bhikkhunā ovādaṃ gahetuṃ, saṅketañca kātuṃ – atra patiharissāmī”ti.

At that time, a certain monk was dwelling in the forest. Bhikkhunīs approached him and said, 'Venerable sir, please receive the exhortation.' 'Sisters, I dwell in the forest; how can I receive the exhortation?' 'Venerable sir, please receive the exhortation; for it has been laid down by the Blessed One: "Setting aside a foolish one, setting aside a sick one, setting aside one who is traveling, the exhortation should be received by the remaining monks."' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a forest-dwelling monk to receive the exhortation and to make an appointment, saying: "I will bring it back here."

415. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ovādaṃ gahetvā na ārocenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādo na ārocetabbo. Yo na āroceyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

415. At that time, monks, having received the exhortation, did not report it. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, it is not that the exhortation should not be reported; it should indeed be reported. Whichever monk should not report it, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ovādaṃ gahetvā na paccāharanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādo na paccāharitabbo. Yo na paccāhareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, monks, having received the exhortation, did not bring it back. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, it is not that the exhortation should not be brought back; it should indeed be brought back. Whichever monk should not bring it back, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo saṅketaṃ na gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā saṅketaṃ na gantabbaṃ. Yā na gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs did not go to the appointed place. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, it is not that a bhikkhunī should not go to the appointed place; she should indeed go. Whichever bhikkhunī should not go, she incurs an offense of wrong conduct.'

416. Tena [P 2.0266][V 0.0430] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo dīghāni kāyabandhanāni dhārenti, teheva phāsukā nāmenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [T 2.0344] ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā dīghaṃ kāyabandhanaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yā dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā ekapariyākataṃ ekapariyāyakataṃ (syā.) kāyabandhanaṃ, na ca tena phāsukā nāmetabbā. Yā nāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

416. At that time, bhikkhunīs wore long waist-cords, and with them they caused their ribs to bend. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: '...just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a long waist-cord should not be worn by a bhikkhunī. Whichever one should wear it, she incurs an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, for a bhikkhunī a waist-cord made with a single wrap, but the ribs should not be made to bend with it. Whichever one should cause them to bend, she incurs an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo vilīvena vilivena (ka.) paṭṭena phāsukā nāmenti…pe… cammapaṭṭena phāsukā nāmenti. Dussapaṭṭena phāsukā nāmenti. Dussaveṇiyā phāsukā nāmenti. Dussavaṭṭiyā phāsukā nāmenti. Coḷapaṭṭena phāsukā nāmenti. Coḷaveṇiyā phāsukā nāmenti. Coḷavaṭṭiyā phāsukā nāmenti. Suttaveṇiyā phāsukā nāmenti. Suttavaṭṭiyā phāsukā nāmenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[M 0.0458]. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā vilīvena paṭṭena phāsukā nāmetabbā…pe… na suttavaṭṭiyā phāsukā nāmetabbā. Yā nāmeyya āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhunīs were causing their ribs to bend with a strip of bamboo… with a strip of leather, with a strip of cloth, with a braid of cloth, with a twisted cord of cloth, with a strip of rag, with a braid of rag, with a twisted cord of rag, with a braid of thread, and with a twisted cord of thread. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: 'Just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a bhikkhunī should not cause the ribs to bend with a strip of bamboo… nor with a twisted cord of thread. Whichever one should cause them to bend, she incurs an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo aṭṭhillena jaghanaṃ ghaṃsāpenti…pe… [T 2.0345] gohanukena jaghanaṃ koṭṭāpenti, hatthaṃ koṭṭāpenti, hatthakocchaṃ koṭṭāpenti, pādaṃ koṭṭāpenti, pādakocchaṃ koṭṭāpenti, ūruṃ koṭṭāpenti, mukhaṃ koṭṭāpenti, dantamaṃsaṃ koṭṭāpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā aṭṭhillena jaghanaṃ ghaṃsāpetabbaṃ…pe… na dantamaṃsaṃ koṭṭāpetabbaṃ. Yā koṭṭāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, bhikkhunīs were causing their hip region to be rubbed with a bone from a cow's or horse's head… causing their hip region to be scraped with a cow's jawbone, causing the hand to be scraped, causing the back of the hand to be scraped, causing the foot to be scraped, causing the back of the foot to be scraped, causing the thigh to be scraped, causing the face to be scraped, and causing the gums to be scraped. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: '…just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a bhikkhunī should not cause the hip region to be rubbed with a bone from a cow's or horse's head… nor cause the gums to be scraped. Whichever one should do so, she incurs an offense of wrong conduct.'

417. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo mukhaṃ ālimpanti…pe… mukhaṃ ummaddenti, mukhaṃ cuṇṇenti, manosilikāya mukhaṃ lañchenti, aṅgarāgaṃ karonti, mukharāgaṃ karonti, aṅgarāgamukharāgaṃ karonti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave[P 2.0267], bhikkhuniyā mukhaṃ ālimpitabbaṃ…pe… na mukhaṃ ummadditabbaṃ, na mukhaṃ cuṇṇetabbaṃ, na manosilikāya mukhaṃ lañchitabbaṃ, na aṅgarāgo kātabbo, na mukharāgo kātabbo, na aṅgarāgamukharāgo kātabbo. Yā kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

417. At that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six were anointing their faces… massaging their faces, powdering their faces, making marks on their faces with realgar, applying body-coloring, applying mouth-coloring, and applying both body-coloring and mouth-coloring. People criticized, scorned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying, ‘…just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures.’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, a bhikkhunī should not anoint her face… nor massage her face, nor powder her face, nor make marks on her face with realgar, nor apply body-coloring, nor apply mouth-coloring, nor apply both body-coloring and mouth-coloring. Whichever one should do so, she incurs an offense of wrong conduct.’”

Tena [T 2.0346][V 0.0431] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo avaṅgaṃ apāṅgaṃ (?) karonti…pe… visesakaṃ karonti, olokanakena olokenti, sāloke tiṭṭhanti; naccaṃ sanaccaṃ (sī. syā.), samajjaṃ (ka.) kārāpenti, vesiṃ vuṭṭhāpenti, pānāgāraṃ ṭhapenti, sūnaṃ ṭhapenti, āpaṇaṃ pasārenti, vaḍḍhiṃ payojenti, vaṇijjaṃ payojenti, dāsaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, dāsiṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, kammakāraṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, kammakāriṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, tiracchānagataṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, harītakapakkikaṃ harītakapaṇṇikaṃ (ka.) pakiṇanti, namatakaṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā avaṅgaṃ kātabbaṃ…pe… na visesakaṃ kātabbaṃ, na olokanakena [M 0.0459] oloketabbaṃ, na sāloke ṭhātabbaṃ, na naccaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ, na vesī vuṭṭhāpetabbā, na pānāgāraṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ, na sūnā ṭhapetabbā, na āpaṇo pasāretabbo, na vaḍḍhi payojetabbā, na vaṇijjā payojetabbā, na dāso upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na dāsī upaṭṭhāpetabbā, na kammakāro upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na kammakārī upaṭṭhāpetabbā, na tiracchānagato upaṭṭhāpetabbo, na harītakapakkikaṃ pakiṇitabbaṃ, na namatakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yā dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time the nuns of the group of six were drawing a downward-facing line… making special designs, looking out through windows, standing in the doorway; they had dances performed, set up courtesans, established liquor shops, established a butcher's shop, opened shops, engaged in lending at interest, engaged in trade, maintained male slaves, maintained female slaves, maintained male workers, maintained female workers, maintained animals, sold green and cooked produce, and wore a tight sash. People complained, criticized, and protested… saying, “Just like laywomen who indulge in sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a nun should not draw a downward-facing line… should not make special designs, should not look out through windows, should not stand in the doorway, should not arrange dances, should not set up courtesans, should not establish liquor shops, should not establish a butcher's shop, should not open shops, should not engage in lending at interest, should not engage in trade, should not maintain male slaves, should not maintain female slaves, should not maintain male workers, should not maintain female workers, should not maintain animals, should not sell green and cooked produce, and should not wear a tight sash. Whoever would wear it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.”

418. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sabbanīlakāni cīvarāni [T 2.0347] dhārenti…pe… sabbapītakāni cīvarāni dhārenti, sabbalohitakāni cīvarāni dhārenti, sabbamañjiṭṭhikāni cīvarāni dhārenti, sabbakaṇhāni cīvarāni dhārenti, sabbamahāraṅgarattāni cīvarāni dhārenti, sabbamahānāmarattāni cīvarāni dhārenti, acchinnadasāni cīvarāni dhārenti, dīghadasāni cīvarāni dhārenti, pupphadasāni cīvarāni dhārenti, phaladasāni cīvarāni dhārenti, kañcukaṃ dhārenti, tirīṭakaṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā sabbanīlakāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni…pe… na tirīṭakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yā dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

418. At that time, the nuns of the group of six were wearing entirely blue robes… wearing entirely yellow robes, wearing entirely red robes, wearing entirely madder-colored robes, wearing entirely black robes, wearing entirely crimson-colored robes, wearing entirely pale-colored robes, wearing robes with uncut fringes, wearing robes with long fringes, wearing robes with flower-fringes, wearing robes with fruit-fringes, wearing a bodice, and wearing a headband. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “They are just like laywomen who indulge in sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a nun should not wear entirely blue robes… nor should she wear a headband. Whichever nun should wear one, she commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

419. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī kālaṃ karontī evamāha – “mamaccayena mayhaṃ parikkhāro saṅghassa hotū”ti. Tattha bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca vivadanti [P 2.0268] – “amhākaṃ hoti, amhākaṃ hotī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Bhikkhunī ce, bhikkhave[T 2.0348], kālaṃ karontī evaṃ vadeyya – ‘mamaccayena mayhaṃ parikkhāro saṅghassa hotū’ti, anissaro tattha bhikkhusaṅgho, bhikkhunisaṅghassevetaṃ. Sikkhamānā ce, bhikkhave…pe… sāmaṇerī ce, bhikkhave, kālaṃ karontī evaṃ vadeyya – ‘mamaccayena mayhaṃ parikkhāro [V 0.0432] saṅghassa hotū’ti, anissaro tattha bhikkhusaṅgho, bhikkhunisaṅghassevetaṃ. Bhikkhu ce, bhikkhave, kālaṃ karonto evaṃ vadeyya – ‘mamaccayena mayhaṃ parikkhāro saṅghassa hotū’ti, anissaro tattha bhikkhunisaṅgho, bhikkhusaṅghassevetaṃ. Sāmaṇero ce, bhikkhave…pe… upāsako ce, bhikkhave…pe… upāsikā ce, bhikkhave…pe… añño ce, bhikkhave, koci kālaṃ karonto evaṃ vadeyya – ‘mamaccayena mayhaṃ parikkhāro [M 0.0460] saṅghassa hotū’ti, anissaro tattha bhikkhunisaṅgho, bhikkhusaṅghasseveta”nti.

419. Now at that time, a certain nun, as she was dying, said thus: “After my passing away, let my requisites be for the Saṅgha.” Thereupon, monks and nuns disputed, saying, “They are for us, they are for us.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, if a nun, as she is dying, should say thus: ‘After my passing away, let my requisites be for the Saṅgha,’ the Saṅgha of monks has no authority therein; it belongs solely to the Saṅgha of nuns. If a female trainee, Bhikkhus… If a female novice, Bhikkhus, as she is dying, should say thus: ‘After my passing away, let my requisites be for the Saṅgha,’ the Saṅgha of monks has no authority therein; it belongs solely to the Saṅgha of nuns. If a monk, Bhikkhus, as he is dying, should say thus: ‘After my passing away, let my requisites be for the Saṅgha,’ the Saṅgha of nuns has no authority therein; it belongs solely to the Saṅgha of monks. If a male novice, Bhikkhus… If a male lay follower, Bhikkhus… If a female lay follower, Bhikkhus… If anyone else, Bhikkhus, as they are dying, should say thus: ‘After my passing away, let my requisites be for the Saṅgha,’ the Saṅgha of nuns has no authority therein; it belongs solely to the Saṅgha of monks.”

420. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā itthī purāṇamallī bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Sā rathikāya dubbalakaṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā aṃsakūṭena pahāraṃ datvā pātesi pavaṭṭesi (sī.). Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma, bhikkhunī, bhikkhussa pahāraṃ dassatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhussa pahāro dātabbo. Yā dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā [T 2.0349] bhikkhuṃ passitvā dūratova okkamitvā maggaṃ dātu”nti.

420. At that time, a certain woman who had formerly been a wrestler had gone forth among the nuns. Seeing a weak monk on the street, she struck him with her shoulder and knocked him down. The monks complained, were annoyed, and criticized, saying: “How indeed could a nun give a blow to a monk?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a blow is not to be given by a nun to a monk. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Bhikkhus, that a nun, upon seeing a monk, is to step aside from a distance and give way.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā itthī pavutthapatikā jārena gabbhinī hoti. Sā gabbhaṃ pātetvā kulūpikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “handayye, imaṃ gabbhaṃ pattena nīharā”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī taṃ gabbhaṃ patte pakkhipitvā saṅghāṭiyā paṭicchādetvā agamāsi. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena piṇḍacārikena bhikkhunā samādānaṃ kataṃ hoti – ‘yāhaṃ paṭhamaṃ bhikkhaṃ labhissāmi, na taṃ adatvā bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā paribhuñjissāmī’ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu taṃ bhikkhuniṃ passitvā etadavoca – “handa, bhagini, bhikkhaṃ paṭiggaṇhā”ti. “Alaṃ ayyā”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho so bhikkhu taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “handa, bhagini, bhikkhaṃ paṭiggaṇhā”ti. “Alaṃ ayyā”ti. “Mayā kho, bhagini, samādānaṃ kataṃ – ‘yāhaṃ paṭhamaṃ bhikkhaṃ labhissāmi, na taṃ adatvā bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā paribhuñjissāmī’ti. Handa[P 2.0269], bhagini, bhikkhaṃ paṭiggaṇhā”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tena bhikkhunā nippīḷiyamānā nīharitvā pattaṃ dassesi – “passa, ayya, patte gabbhaṃ; mā ca kassaci ārocesī”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi [T 2.0350] nāma bhikkhunī pattena gabbhaṃ nīharissatī”ti! Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī pattena gabbhaṃ nīharissatī”ti! Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā pattena gabbho [V 0.0433] nīharitabbo. Yā [M 0.0461] nīhareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhuṃ passitvā nīharitvā pattaṃ dassetu”nti.

At that time, a certain woman, whose husband was away, became pregnant by a lover. After aborting the fetus, she said to a bhikkhunī who frequented her household: "Come, venerable one, take this fetus away in a bowl." Then that bhikkhunī placed the fetus in a bowl, covered it with her outer robe, and left. Now at that time, a certain alms-collecting bhikkhu had made a vow: "Whatever alms I receive first, I will not partake of it without giving it to a bhikkhu or a bhikkhunī." Then that bhikkhu saw the bhikkhunī and said: "Here, sister, accept alms." "Enough, sir," she replied. A second time... a third time, the bhikkhu said to the bhikkhunī: "Here, sister, accept alms." "Enough, sir," she replied. "Sister, I have made a vow: 'Whatever alms I receive first, I will not partake of it without giving it to a bhikkhu or a bhikkhunī.' Here, sister, accept alms." Pressured by the bhikkhu, the bhikkhunī took out the bowl and showed it to him, saying: "Look, sir, there is a fetus in the bowl—but do not tell anyone." Then that bhikkhu complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: "How could a bhikkhunī carry a fetus in a bowl?" He reported the matter to the bhikkhus.
