Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: "How could a bhikkhunī carry a fetus in a bowl?" They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not carry a fetus in a bowl. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī, upon seeing a bhikkhu, to take out and show the bowl."

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuṃ passitvā parivattetvā pattamūlaṃ dassenti. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuṃ passitvā parivattetvā pattamūlaṃ dassessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhuṃ passitvā parivattetvā pattamūlaṃ dassetabbaṃ. Yā dasseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhuṃ passitvā ukkujjitvā pattaṃ dassetuṃ. Yañca patte āmisaṃ hoti, tena ca bhikkhu nimantetabbo”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six, upon seeing a bhikkhu, would turn their bowls over and show the bottom. The bhikkhus complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the bhikkhunīs of the group of six, upon seeing a bhikkhu, turn their bowls over and show the bottom?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī, upon seeing a bhikkhu, should not turn her bowl over and show the bottom. Whichever bhikkhunī should show it, for her there is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī, upon seeing a bhikkhu, to turn the bowl upright and show it. And with whatever almsfood is in the bowl, the bhikkhu should be invited.”

Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ rathikāya purisabyañjanaṃ chaḍḍitaṃ hoti. Taṃ bhikkhuniyo sakkaccaṃ upanijjhāyiṃsu. Manussā ukkuṭṭhiṃ akaṃsu. Tā bhikkhuniyo maṅkū ahesuṃ. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo upassayaṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… [T 2.0351] tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo purisabyañjanaṃ upanijjhāyissantī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā purisabyañjanaṃ upanijjhāyitabbaṃ. Yā upanijjhāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time in Sāvatthī, a male organ had been discarded on the street. The bhikkhunīs carefully stared at it. The people raised an outcry. Those bhikkhunīs became ashamed. Then those bhikkhunīs, having gone to the nunnery, reported this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed could bhikkhunīs stare at a male organ?” Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not stare at a male organ. Whichever bhikkhunī should stare at it, for her there is an offense of wrong-doing.”

421. Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhikkhūnaṃ āmisaṃ denti. Bhikkhū bhikkhunīnaṃ denti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā attano paribhogatthāya [P 2.0270] dinnaṃ aññesaṃ dassanti! Mayampi na jānāma dānaṃ dātu”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, attano paribhogatthāya dinnaṃ aññesaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

421. At that time, people gave material gifts to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus gave them to the bhikkhunīs. The people complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed could the venerable sirs give to others what was given for their own use? Do we also not know how to give a gift?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, what is given for one’s own use should not be given to others. Whichever bhikkhu should give it, for him there is an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ āmisaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghassa dātu”nti. Bāḷhataraṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puggalikampi dātu”nti.

At that time, provisions were abundant for the bhikkhus. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow it to be given to the Saṅgha.' It became exceedingly abundant. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow it to be given to an individual as well.'

Tena [M 0.0462] kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ sannidhikataṃ āmisaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [V 0.0434] ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sannidhiṃ bhikkhunīhi bhikkhunīhi bhikkhūhi (sī.) paṭiggāhāpetvā paṭiggahāpetvā (ka.) paribhuñjitu”nti.

At that time, stored provisions were abundant for the bhikkhus. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow you to consume stored provisions after having them accepted by bhikkhunīs.'

Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhikkhunīnaṃ āmisaṃ denti. Bhikkhuniyo [T 2.0352] bhikkhūnaṃ denti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo attano paribhogatthāya dinnaṃ aññesaṃ dassanti! Mayampi na jānāma dānaṃ dātu”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā attano paribhogatthāya dinnaṃ aññesaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yā dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, people gave provisions to the bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs gave them to the bhikkhus. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: 'How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give to others what was given for their own consumption! Do we not also know how to give a gift?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, what is given to a bhikkhunī for her own consumption is not to be given to others. Whichever bhikkhunī should give it, for her there is an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhunīnaṃ āmisaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghassa dātu”nti. Bāḷhataraṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puggalikampi dātu”nti.

At that time, provisions were abundant for the nuns. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow it to be given to the Saṅgha.' It became exceedingly abundant. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow it to be given to an individual as well.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhunīnaṃ sannidhikataṃ āmisaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ sannidhiṃ bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi (sī.) paṭiggāhāpetvā paribhuñjitu”nti.

At that time, stored provisions were abundant for the nuns. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the nuns' stored provisions to be consumed after having them received by monks.'

422. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ ussannaṃ hoti, bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ senāsanaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) na hoti. Bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘sādhu, bhante, ayyā amhākaṃ senāsanaṃ dentu tāvakālika’nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ senāsanaṃ dātuṃ tāvakālika”nti.

422. At that time, lodgings were abundant for the bhikkhus, but not for the bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs sent a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “Venerable sirs, may the venerable ones please give us temporary lodgings.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow temporary lodgings to be given to the bhikkhunīs.”

Tena kho pana samayena utuniyo bhikkhuniyo onaddhamañcaṃ onaddhapīṭhaṃ abhinisīdantipi abhinipajjantipi. Senāsanaṃ lohitena makkhiyyati[T 2.0353]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā [P 2.0271] onaddhamañcaṃ onaddhapīṭhaṃ abhinisīditabbaṃ abhinipajjitabbaṃ. Yā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āvasathacīvara”nti. Āvasathacīvaraṃ lohitena makkhiyyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi[M 0.0463], bhikkhave, āṇicoḷaka”nti. Coḷakaṃ nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, suttakena bandhitvā ūruyā bandhitu”nti[V 0.0435]. Suttaṃ chijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṃvelliyaṃ, kaṭisuttaka”nti.

At that time, menstruating bhikkhunīs would sit or lie down on couches and chairs with interwoven straps. The lodgings became stained with blood. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bhikkhunī should not sit or lie down on a couch or chair with interwoven straps. Whoever sits or lies down on one commits an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow a menstrual cloth.” The menstrual cloth became stained with blood. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a sanitary cloth.” The sanitary cloth fell off. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow it to be tied with a string and fastened around the thigh.” The string snapped. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a loincloth wrap and a waist-string.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sabbakālaṃ kaṭisuttakaṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā sabbakālaṃ kaṭisuttakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yā dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, utuniyā kaṭisuttaka”nti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wore waist-strings at all times. People complained, grumbled, and criticized them, saying: “They are just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a bhikkhunī should not wear a waist-string at all times. Whoever wears one commits an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow a waist-string for a menstruating bhikkhunī.”

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is finished.

3. Tatiyabhāṇavāro

3. The Third Recitation Section

423. Tena kho pana samayena upasampannāyo dissanti – animittāpi, nimittamattāpi, alohitāpi, dhuvalohitāpi, dhuvacoḷāpi, paggharantīpi, sikhariṇīpi, itthipaṇḍakāpi, vepurisikāpi, sambhinnāpi, ubhatobyañjanāpi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upasampādentiyā catuvīsati antarāyike dhamme pucchituṃ. Evañca pana[T 2.0354], bhikkhave, pucchitabbā – ‘nasi animittā, nasi nimittamattā, nasi alohitā, nasi dhuvalohitā, nasi dhuvacoḷā, nasi paggharantī, nasi sikharaṇī sikhariṇī (sī. syā.), nasi itthipaṇḍakā, nasi vepurisikā, nasi sambhinnā, nasi ubhatobyañjanā? Santi te evarūpā ābādhā – kuṭṭhaṃ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro? Manussāsi, itthīsi, bhujissāsi, aṇaṇāsi, nasi rājabhaṭī? Anuññātāsi mātāpitūhi, sāmikena? Paripuṇṇavīsativassāsi, paripuṇṇaṃ te pattacīvaraṃ, kinnāmāsi, kānāmā te pavattinī”ti?

423. At that time, ordained nuns were seen who were of the following types: those without the female sign, those with only the mark of the sign, those without menstrual blood, those with constant menstrual blood, those who constantly used a sanitary cloth, those with a constant trickle of blood, those who were sikhariṇīs, those who were female paṇḍakas, those who were masculine women, those with connected passages, and those with the characteristics of both sexes. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to ask a candidate for ordination about the twenty-four obstructive conditions. And, monks, she should be asked thus: “Are you not one without the female sign? Are you not one with only the mark of the sign? Are you not one without menstrual blood? Are you not one with constant menstrual blood? Are you not one who constantly uses a sanitary cloth? Are you not one with a constant trickle of blood? Are you not a sikhariṇī? Are you not a female paṇḍaka? Are you not a masculine woman? Are you not one with connected passages? Are you not one with the characteristics of both sexes? Do you have such diseases as these: leprosy, boils, a skin disease, consumption, or epilepsy? Are you a human being? Are you a woman? Are you a free woman? Are you free from debt? Are you not in the king’s service? Have you been permitted by your parents and husband? Are you fully twenty years of age? Are your bowl and robes complete? What is your name? What is your preceptress’s name?”'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhikkhunīnaṃ antarāyike dhamme pucchanti. Upasampadāpekkhāyo vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti, na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekatoupasampannāya bhikkhunisaṅghe visuddhāya bhikkhusaṅghe upasampādetu”nti.

At that time, bhikkhus were questioning the candidates for ordination about the obstructive conditions. The candidates for ordination became embarrassed and downcast; they were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the full ordination in the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for a candidate who has been ordained on one side by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is purified.'

Tena [M 0.0464] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo ananusiṭṭhā upasampadāpekkhāyo antarāyike dhamme pucchanti. Upasampadāpekkhāyo [P 2.0272] vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti, na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato [V 0.0436] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ anusāsitvā pacchā antarāyike dhamme pucchitu”nti.

At that time, bhikkhunīs were asking uninstructed candidates for ordination about the obstructive conditions. The candidates for ordination became embarrassed and downcast; they were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to first instruct them and afterwards ask about the obstructive conditions.'

Tattheva saṅghamajjhe anusāsanti. Upasampadāpekkhāyo tatheva vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti[T 2.0355], na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekamantaṃ anusāsitvā saṅghamajjhe antarāyike dhamme pucchituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, anusāsitabbā.

They instructed them right there in the midst of the Saṅgha. The candidates for ordination still became embarrassed and downcast, and were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you to instruct them aside and then question them about the obstructive conditions in the midst of the Saṅgha. And, monks, they should be instructed thus:

424. “Paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbā. Upajjhaṃ gāhāpetvā pattacīvaraṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ayaṃ te patto, ayaṃ saṅghāṭi, ayaṃ uttarāsaṅgo, ayaṃ antaravāsako, idaṃ saṃkaccikaṃ saṅkacchikaṃ (syā.), ayaṃ udakasāṭikā; gaccha amumhi okāse tiṭṭhāhī”ti.

424. “First, she should be led to take a preceptress. Having led her to take a preceptress, the bowl and robes should be pointed out: ‘This is your bowl, this is your double-layered robe, this is your upper robe, this is your lower robe, this is your breast-cloth, this is your bathing cloth; go and stand in that spot.’”

Bālā abyattā anusāsanti. Duranusiṭṭhā upasampadāpekkhāyo vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti, na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bālāya abyattāya anusāsitabbā. Yā anusāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya anusāsitu”nti.

Foolish and inexpert bhikkhunīs gave the instruction. The candidates for ordination, being poorly instructed, became embarrassed and downcast, and were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a foolish and inexpert bhikkhunī should not give the instruction. Whoever gives it commits an offense of wrong conduct. Monks, I allow a competent and capable bhikkhunī to give the instruction.”

Asammatā anusāsanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, asammatāya anusāsitabbā. Yā anusāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sammatāya anusāsituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā – attanā vā attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ, parāya vā parā sammannitabbā.

Unauthorized bhikkhunīs gave the instruction. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, an unauthorized bhikkhunī should not give the instruction. Whoever should give it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow an authorized bhikkhunī to give the instruction. And, bhikkhus, she should be authorized thus—either she should authorize herself, or another should authorize her.”

“Kathañca attanāva attanā vā (ka.) attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ? Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo – ‘suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmaṃ anusāseyya’nti. Evaṃ attanāva [T 2.0356] attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ.

“And how should she authorize herself? A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha listen to me. So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I, so-and-so, will instruct so-and-so.’ Thus should she authorize herself.”

“Kathañca parāya parāya vā (ka.) parā sammannitabbā? Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo – ‘suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya [M 0.0465] ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmā itthannāmaṃ anusāseyyā’ti. Evaṃ parāya parā sammannitabbā.

“And how should another be authorized by another? A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha listen to me. So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, so-and-so should instruct so-and-so.’ In this way should another be authorized by another.”

“Tāya [V 0.0437] sammatāya bhikkhuniyā upasampadāpekkhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyā – ‘suṇasi itthannāme. Ayaṃ te saccakālo, bhūtakālo. Yaṃ jātaṃ taṃ saṅghamajjhe pucchante santaṃ atthīti vattabbaṃ, asantaṃ natthīti vattabbaṃ. Mā kho vitthāyi vitthāsi (ka.), mā kho maṅku ahosi. Evaṃ taṃ pucchissanti – nasi animittā, nasi nimittamattā, nasi alohitā, nasi dhuvalohitā, nasi dhuvacoḷā, nasi paggharantī, nasi sikhariṇī, nasi itthipaṇḍakā, nasi vepurisikā, nasi sambhinnā, nasi ubhatobyañjanā? Santi te evarūpā ābādhā – kuṭṭhaṃ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro? Manussāsi, itthīsi, bhujissāsi, aṇaṇāsi, nasi rājabhaṭī? Anuññātāsi mātāpitūhi, sāmikena? Paripuṇṇavīsativassāsi, paripuṇṇaṃ te pattacīvaraṃ, kinnāmāsi, kānāmā te pavattinī’ti[P 2.0273]?

That authorized bhikkhunī, having approached the candidate for higher ordination, should speak to her thus: ‘Listen, so-and-so. This is your time for truth, your time for fact. When asked in the midst of the Saṅgha about what has occurred, if it is present, it should be said, “It is”; if it is not present, it should be said, “It is not.” Do not be hesitant, do not be dismayed. They will question you thus: Are you not one without the sign? Are you not one with only the mere sign? Are you not one without menstrual blood? Are you not one with constant blood flow? Are you not one who constantly uses a sanitary cloth? Are you not one who is trickling? Are you not a sikhariṇī? Are you not a female paṇḍaka? Are you not a vepurisikā? Are you not one with connected passages? Are you not an ubhatobyañjanaka? Do you have such diseases as these: leprosy, boils, eczema, consumption, epilepsy? Are you a human being? Are you a woman? Are you a free woman? Are you without debt? Are you not in the king's service? Have you been permitted by your mother and father, and by your husband? Are you fully twenty years of age? Is your bowl and robe complete? What is your name? What is the name of your preceptress?’”

“Ekato āgacchanti. Na ekato āgantabbaṃ. Anusāsikāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā saṅgho ñāpetabbo – ‘suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya [T 2.0357] ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Anusiṭṭhā sā mayā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmā āgaccheyyā’ti. ‘Āgacchāhī’ti vattabbā.

They come together. They should not come together. The instructing bhikkhunī should come first and inform the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha listen to me. So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. I have instructed her. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, so-and-so may come.’ She should be told, ‘Come.’”

“Ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā upasampadaṃ yācāpetabbā – ‘saṅghaṃ, ayye, upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, ayye, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Dutiyampi, ayye, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, ayye, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Tatiyampi, ayye, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, ayye, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāyā’ti. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Having caused her to arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, to pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, to sit in the squatting position, and to raise her hands in añjali, she should be made to request higher ordination: ‘Venerable ladies, I request higher ordination from the Saṅgha. Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion. A second time, venerable ladies, I request higher ordination from the Saṅgha. Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion. A third time, venerable ladies, I request higher ordination from the Saṅgha. Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion.’ The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ antarāyike dhamme puccheyyanti.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would ask so-and-so about the obstructive conditions.”

“Suṇasi [M 0.0466] itthannāme. Ayaṃ te saccakālo, bhūtakālo. Yaṃ jātaṃ taṃ pucchāmi santaṃ atthīti vattabbaṃ, asantaṃ natthīti vattabbaṃ. Nasi animittā…pe… kinnāmāsi, kānāmā te pavattinīti. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Listen, so-and-so. This is your time for truth, your time for fact. I ask about what has occurred. What is present should be stated as, ‘It is;’ what is not present should be stated as, ‘It is not.’ Are you not one without the sign? … What is your name? What is the name of your preceptress?” The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

425. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassā pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyya [T 2.0358] itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Esā ñatti.

425. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. She is pure from obstructive conditions; her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should confer higher ordination on so-and-so with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā[V 0.0438]. Parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassā pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. She is pure from obstructive conditions, and her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on so-and-so with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. Whichever venerable lady approves of the higher ordination of so-and-so with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress should be silent. Whichever does not approve should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassā pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“For the second time, I speak on this matter… For the third time, I speak on this matter: Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable lady so-and-so. She is pure from obstructive conditions, and her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on so-and-so with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. Whichever venerable lady approves of the higher ordination of so-and-so with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress should be silent. Whichever does not approve should speak.”

“Upasampannā saṅghena itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

“So-and-so has been ordained by the Saṅgha with the venerable lady so-and-so as her preceptress. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

“Tāvadeva taṃ ādāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā [T 2.0359] añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā upasampadaṃ yācāpetabbā – ‘ahaṃ, ayyā, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā[P 2.0274]. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā; saṅghaṃ, ayyā, upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Ahaṃ, ayyā, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya [M 0.0467] upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Dutiyampi, ayyā, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Ahaṃ, ayyā, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Tatiyampi, ayyā, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāyā’ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then, taking her, she should be made to approach the community of monks, to arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, to pay homage at the feet of the monks, to sit in the squatting position, to raise her hands in añjali, and to request full ordination: ‘Venerable sirs, I, named so-and-so, seek full ordination from the venerable so-and-so as my preceptress. Having been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Sangha, I am pure. Venerable sirs, I request full ordination from the Sangha. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha lift me up out of compassion. A second time, venerable sirs, I, named so-and-so, seek full ordination from the venerable so-and-so as my preceptress. Having been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Sangha, I am pure. A second time, venerable sirs, I request full ordination from the Sangha. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha lift me up out of compassion. A third time, venerable sirs, I, named so-and-so, seek full ordination from the venerable so-and-so as my preceptress. Having been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Sangha, I am pure. A third time, venerable sirs, I request full ordination from the Sangha. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha lift me up out of compassion.’ A competent and capable monk should then inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0439] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyya, itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for full ordination from the venerable so-and-so. Having been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Sangha, she is pure. So-and-so requests full ordination from the Sangha, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress. If it is timely for the Sangha, the Sangha should confer full ordination on so-and-so, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmāya [T 2.0360] pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for full ordination from the venerable so-and-so. Having been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Sangha, she is pure. So-and-so requests full ordination from the Sangha, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress. The Sangha confers full ordination on so-and-so, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress. If the full ordination of so-and-so, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress, is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent; if it is not agreeable, let him speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“A second time I speak on this matter… A third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for full ordination from the venerable so-and-so. Having been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Sangha, she is pure. So-and-so requests full ordination from the Sangha, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress. The Sangha confers full ordination on so-and-so, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress. If the full ordination of so-and-so, with the venerable so-and-so as her preceptress, is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent; if it is not agreeable, let him speak.”

“Upasampannā saṅghena itthannāmā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

“So-and-so has been given full ordination by the Sangha, with so-and-so as her preceptress. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.”

“Tāvadeva chāyā metabbā, utuppamāṇaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, divasabhāgo ācikkhitabbo, saṅgīti ācikkhitabbā, bhikkhuniyo vattabbā – imissā tayo ca nissaye, aṭṭha ca akaraṇīyāni ācikkheyyāthā”ti.

“At that very moment, the shadow is to be measured, the measure of the season is to be told, the part of the day is to be told, the summary is to be told, and the bhikkhunīs are to be told: ‘You should tell this new ordinand the three resources and the eight things not to be done.’”

426. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhattagge āsanaṃ saṃkasāyantiyo kālaṃ vītināmesuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[M 0.0468]. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ, avasesānaṃ yathāgatika”nti.

426. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs, while moving seats about in the dining hall, let the proper time pass. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Bhikkhus, I allow for eight bhikkhunīs according to seniority, and for the remaining ones according to arrival.”

Tena [T 2.0361] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo – bhagavatā anuññātaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ, avasesānaṃ yathāgatikanti – sabbattha aṭṭheva bhikkhuniyo yathāvuḍḍhaṃ paṭibāhanti, avasesāyo [V 0.0440] yathāgatikaṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattagge aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ, avasesānaṃ yathāgatikaṃ; aññattha sabbattha yathāvuḍḍhaṃ aññattha yathāvuḍḍhaṃ (syā.) na paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Yā paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The Blessed One has allowed for eight bhikkhunīs according to seniority, and for the remaining ones according to arrival,” everywhere prevented the normal order, allowing only eight bhikkhunīs to be seated according to seniority and the rest according to arrival. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Bhikkhus, in the dining hall I allow for eight bhikkhunīs according to seniority, and for the remaining ones according to arrival. Elsewhere, in all places, seating according to seniority is not to be prevented. Whoever should prevent it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

427. pāci. 1050 ādayo Tena [P 2.0275] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo na pavārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā na pavāretabbaṃ. Yā na pavāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

427. At that time, the bhikkhunīs did not invite for Pavāraṇā. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Bhikkhus, it is not that a bhikkhunī should not invite for Pavāraṇā; she should indeed invite. Whichever bhikkhunī should not invite, she should be dealt with according to the Dhamma.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo attanā pavāretvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ na pavārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā attanā pavāretvā bhikkhusaṅgho na pavāretabbo. Yā na pavāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs, having invited for Pavāraṇā among themselves, did not invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Bhikkhus, it is not that a bhikkhunī, having invited among themselves, should not invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha; she should indeed invite. Whichever bhikkhunī should not invite, she should be dealt with according to the Dhamma.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ekato pavārentiyo kolāhalaṃ akaṃsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ekato pavāretabbaṃ. Yā pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs, while inviting for Pavāraṇā together with the bhikkhus, made a commotion. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not invite for Pavāraṇā together with the bhikkhus. Whichever bhikkhunī should so invite, she commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo purebhattaṃ pavārentiyo kālaṃ [T 2.0362] vītināmesuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pacchābhattaṃ bhikkhave bhikkhuniyā pacchābhattaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) pavāretu”nti. Pacchābhattaṃ pavārentiyo vikāle vikālaṃ (ka.) ahesuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ajjatanā bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ ajjatanā (sī.), ajjatanāya (ka.) pavāretvā aparajju bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāretu”nti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs, while inviting for Pavāraṇā before the meal, let the time pass. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'I allow, Bhikkhus, to invite for Pavāraṇā after the meal.' While inviting for Pavāraṇā after the meal, it became the wrong time. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'I allow, Bhikkhus, having invited the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha today, to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha on the next day.'

Tena kho pana samayena sabbo bhikkhunisaṅgho pavārento kolāhalaṃ akāsi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ byattaṃ paṭibalaṃ sammannituṃ – bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ [M 0.0469] pavāretuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunī yācitabbā, yācitvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, the entire Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, while performing Pavāraṇā, made a commotion. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'I allow, Bhikkhus, to appoint one competent, capable bhikkhunī to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā for the sake of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. And, Bhikkhus, she should be appointed in this way. First, the bhikkhunī should be requested. Having requested, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhunī:'

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammanneyya bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāretuṃ. Esā ñatti.

'Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā for the sake of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. This is the motion.'

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammannati bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāretuṃ. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā sammuti bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya [V 0.0441] bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāretuṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā for the sake of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. Whichever venerable lady approves of the appointment of the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā for the sake of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, let her be silent; whoever does not approve, let her speak.

“Sammatā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāretuṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

The bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has been appointed by the Saṅgha to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā for the sake of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

“Tāya [T 2.0363] sammatāya bhikkhuniyā bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ ādāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘bhikkhunīsaṅgho[P 2.0276], ayyā, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāreti – diṭṭhena vā, sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu vadatu maṃ (ka.), ayyā, bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ anukampaṃ upādāya, passanto paṭikarissati. Dutiyampi, ayyā…pe… tatiyampi, ayyā, bhikkhunisaṅgho bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāreti – diṭṭhena vā, sutena vā, parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu, ayyā, bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ anukampaṃ upādāya, passanto paṭikarissatī”ti.

That appointed bhikkhunī, taking the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha with her, should approach the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. Arranging her upper robe over one shoulder, she should pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise her joined palms, and speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha invites the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā regarding what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected. Venerable sirs, may the Bhikkhu Saṅgha speak to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha out of compassion; upon seeing a fault, they will make amends.’ A second time, venerable sirs… a third time, venerable sirs, the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha invites the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for Pavāraṇā regarding what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected. Venerable sirs, may the Bhikkhu Saṅgha speak to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha out of compassion; upon seeing a fault, they will make amends.’”

428. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ uposathaṃ ṭhapenti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapenti, savacanīyaṃ karonti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapenti, okāsaṃ kārenti, codenti, sārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhussa uposatho ṭhapetabbo; ṭhapitopi aṭṭhapito; ṭhapentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā; ṭhapitāpi aṭṭhapitā; ṭhapentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na savacanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ; katampi akataṃ; karontiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo; paṭṭhapitopi appaṭṭhapito; paṭṭhapentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na okāso kāretabbo[M 0.0470]; kāritopi akārito; kārentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na codetabbo; coditopi acodito; codentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa[T 2.0364]. Na sāretabbo; sāritopi asārito; sārentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

428. At that time, bhikkhunīs were suspending the bhikkhus’ Uposatha, suspending their Pavāraṇā, making them liable to admonition, initiating disputes, making them ask for permission, reproving them, and reminding them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not suspend a bhikkhu’s Uposatha; even if she suspends it, it is not suspended, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. She should not suspend his Pavāraṇā; even if it is suspended, it is not suspended, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. She should not make him liable to admonition; even if she does, it is not done, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. She should not initiate a dispute against him; even if she does, it is not initiated, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. She should not make him ask for permission; even if she does, it is not done, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. She should not reprove him; even if she does, he is not reproved, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. She should not remind him; even if she does, he is not reminded, and the bhikkhunī who does so commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhikkhunīnaṃ uposathaṃ ṭhapenti, pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapenti, savacanīyaṃ karonti, anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapenti, okāsaṃ kārenti, codenti, sārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave bhikkhunā bhikkhuniyā uposathaṃ ṭhapetuṃ; ṭhapitopi suṭṭhapito; ṭhapentassa anāpatti. Pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapetuṃ; ṭhapitāpi suṭṭhapitā; ṭhapentassa anāpatti. Savacanīyaṃ kātuṃ; katampi sukataṃ; karontassa anāpatti. Anuvādaṃ paṭṭhapetuṃ; paṭṭhapitopi suppaṭṭhapito; paṭṭhapentassa anāpatti. Okāsaṃ kāretuṃ; kāritopi sukārito; kārentassa [V 0.0442] anāpatti. Codetuṃ; coditāpi sucoditā; codentassa anāpatti. Sāretuṃ; sāritāpi susāritā; sārentassa anāpattī”ti.

At that time, bhikkhus were suspending the bhikkhunīs’ Uposatha, suspending their Pavāraṇā, making them liable to admonition, initiating disputes, making them ask for permission, reproving them, and reminding them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a bhikkhu to suspend a bhikkhunī’s Uposatha; if he does, it is well suspended, and he commits no offense. He may suspend her Pavāraṇā; if he does, it is well suspended, and he commits no offense. He may make her liable to admonition; if he does, it is well done, and he commits no offense. He may initiate a dispute against her; if he does, it is well initiated, and he commits no offense. He may make her ask for permission; if he does, it is well done, and he commits no offense. He may reprove her; if he does, she is well reproved, and he commits no offense. He may remind her; if he does, she is well reminded, and he commits no offense.”

429. pāci. 1184 Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyanti – itthiyuttenapi purisantarena, purisayuttenapi itthantarena. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… “seyyathāpi gaṅgāmahiyāyā”ti gaṅgāmahiyāti (sī.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā yānena yāyitabbaṃ. Yā yāyeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

429. At that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six were travelling by vehicle—by a vehicle yoked with a female animal and driven by a male, and by a vehicle yoked with a male animal and driven by a female. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “Just like laywomen going to the Gaṅgā and Mahī festivals.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not travel by vehicle. Whichever one does travel, she should be dealt with according to the Dhamma.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti, na sakkoti padasā gantuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi[T 2.0365], bhikkhave, gilānāya yāna”nti. Atha kho bhikkhunīnaṃ etadahosi – “itthiyuttaṃ nu kho, purisayuttaṃ nu kho”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, itthiyuttaṃ purisayuttaṃ hatthavaṭṭaka”nti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhunī was sick and unable to go on foot. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a vehicle for one who is sick.” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunīs: “Should it be a vehicle yoked with a female animal, or a vehicle yoked with a male animal?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a vehicle yoked with a female animal, a vehicle yoked with a male animal, and a hand-cart.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā bhikkhuniyā yānugghātena bāḷhataraṃ aphāsu ahosi. Bhagavato [P 2.0277] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sivikaṃ pāṭaṅki”nti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhunī experienced severe discomfort due to the jolting of the vehicle. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a palanquin and a litter.”

430. Tena [M 0.0471] kho pana samayena aḍḍhakāsī gaṇikā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Sā ca sāvatthiṃ gantukāmā hoti – ‘bhagavato santike upasampajjissāmī’ti. Assosuṃ kho dhuttā – ‘aḍḍhakāsī kira gaṇikā sāvatthiṃ gantukāmā’ti. Te magge pariyuṭṭhiṃsu. Assosi kho aḍḍhakāsī gaṇikā – ‘dhuttā kira magge pariyuṭṭhitā’ti. Bhagavato santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “ahañhi upasampajjitukāmā; kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dūtenapi upasampādetu”nti.

430. At that time, the courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs. She wanted to go to Sāvatthī, thinking, “I will receive full ordination in the presence of the Blessed One.” Rogues heard, “It is said that the courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī wants to go to Sāvatthī.” They lay in wait along the road. The courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī heard, “It is said that rogues are lying in wait along the road.” She sent a messenger to the Blessed One, saying: “I wish to receive full ordination; how now should I proceed?” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow full ordination to be conferred even by a messenger.”

Bhikkhudūtena upasampādenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhudūtena upasampādetabbā. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti. Sikkhamānadūtena [T 2.0366] upasampādenti…pe… sāmaṇeradūtena upasampādenti…pe… sāmaṇeridūtena upasampādenti…pe… bālāya abyattāya dūtena upasampādenti. “Na, bhikkhave, bālāya abyattāya dūtena upasampādetabbā. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya dūtena upasampādetunti.

They conferred the full ordination through a bhikkhu-messenger. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, full ordination should not be conferred through a bhikkhu-messenger. Whichever bhikkhunī should confer it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.' They conferred the full ordination through a sikkhamānā-messenger… through a sāmaṇera-messenger… through a sāmaṇerī-messenger… through a foolish, incompetent bhikkhunī-messenger. 'Bhikkhus, full ordination should not be conferred through a foolish, incompetent bhikkhunī-messenger. Whichever bhikkhunī should confer it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Bhikkhus, ordination to be conferred by means of a competent and able bhikkhunī as a messenger.'

“Tāya [V 0.0443] dūtāya bhikkhuniyā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘itthannāmā, ayyā, itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā, ayyā, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati. Ullumpatu taṃ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Itthannāmā, ayyā, itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Dutiyampi, ayyā, itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati. Ullumpatu taṃ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Itthannāmā, ayyā, itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Tatiyampi, ayyā, itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati. Ullumpatu taṃ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāyā’ti[T 2.0367]. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

That bhikkhunī who is the messenger should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhus, squat down, raise her joined palms, and say this: 'Venerable Sirs, so-and-so is seeking full ordination from the venerable lady so-and-so. She has been ordained on one side by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure. She does not come only because of some impediment. Venerable Sirs, so-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha. May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, raise her up. Venerable Sirs, so-and-so is seeking full ordination from the venerable lady so-and-so. She has been ordained on one side by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure. She does not come only because of some impediment. For the second time, Venerable Sirs, so-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha. May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, raise her up. Venerable Sirs, so-and-so is seeking full ordination from the venerable lady so-and-so. She has been ordained on one side by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure. She does not come only because of some impediment. For the third time, Venerable Sirs, so-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha. May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, raise her up.' A competent and able bhikkhu should then inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu [M 0.0472] me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyya itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. So-and-so is a candidate for ordination under so-and-so. She has been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure. She does not come because of some impediment. The candidate so-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha with so-and-so as her preceptor. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should ordain so-and-so with so-and-so as her preceptor. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me[P 2.0278], bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. So-and-so is a candidate for ordination under so-and-so. She has been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure. She does not come because of some impediment. The candidate so-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha with so-and-so as her preceptor. The Saṅgha ordains so-and-so with so-and-so as her preceptor. The venerable one who approves of the ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as her preceptor should remain silent; he who does not approve should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa [T 2.0368] nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“A second time I speak on this matter… and a third time I speak on this matter. Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. So-and-so is a candidate for ordination under so-and-so. She has been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure. She does not come because of some impediment. The candidate so-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha with so-and-so as her preceptor. The Saṅgha ordains so-and-so with so-and-so as her preceptor. The venerable one who approves of the ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as her preceptor should remain silent; he who does not approve should speak.”

“Upasampannā [V 0.0444] saṅghena itthannāmā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

“So-and-so has been ordained by the Saṅgha with so-and-so as her preceptor. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.”

“Tāvadeva chāyā metabbā, utuppamāṇaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, divasabhāgo ācikkhitabbo, saṅgīti ācikkhitabbā, bhikkhuniyo vattabbā – tassā tayo ca nissaye, aṭṭha ca akaraṇīyāni ācikkheyyāthā”ti.

“At that very moment, the shadow should be measured, the measure of the season should be announced, the portion of the day should be announced, the number in the assembly should be announced, and the bhikkhunīs should be told: ‘You should declare to her the three dependencies and the eight acts not to be done.’”

431. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo araññe viharanti. Dhuttā dūsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ, ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā araññe vatthabbaṃ. Yā vaseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

431. At that time, bhikkhunīs were dwelling in the wilderness. Drunkards molested them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not dwell in the wilderness. Whichever one should dwell there, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena upāsakena bhikkhunisaṅghassa uddosito dinno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uddosita”nti. Uddosito na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [M 0.0473] ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upassaya”nti. Upassayo na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, navakamma”nti. Navakammaṃ na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puggalikampi kātu”nti.

At that time, a certain lay follower had given a storeroom to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow a storeroom.' The storeroom was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow a residence.' The residence was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow new work.' The new work was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow even an individual dwelling to be made.'

432. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā itthī sannisinnagabbhā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Tassā pabbajitāya gabbho vuṭṭhāti. Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho mayā imasmiṃ dārake paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 2.0369]. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, posetuṃ, yāva so dārako viññutaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti.

432. At that time, a certain woman with an established pregnancy had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs. After she had gone forth, the pregnancy became apparent. Then this thought occurred to that bhikkhunī: 'How should I act with regard to this child?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow her to raise him until that child reaches an age of discernment.'

Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “mayā ca na labbhā ekikāya vatthuṃ, aññāya ca bhikkhuniyā na labbhā dārakena saha vatthuṃ, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammannitvā tassā [P 2.0279] bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunī yācitabbā, yācitvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then this thought occurred to that bhikkhunī: 'It is not allowable for me to live alone, and it is not allowable for another bhikkhunī to live together with the male child. How then should I act?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow that a bhikkhunī be appointed and given to that bhikkhunī as a companion. And, Bhikkhus, she is to be appointed in this way: First, the bhikkhunī should be asked. Having asked, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and able bhikkhunī:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0445] me, ayye, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammanneyya itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṃ. Esā ñatti.

Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammannati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṃ. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā sammuti itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so. To whichever venerable lady the appointment of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so is agreeable, she should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, she should speak.

“Sammatā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The bhikkhunī named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Atha kho tassā dutiyikāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho mayā imasmiṃ dārake paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā sāgāraṃ yathā aññasmiṃ purise paṭipajjanti paṭipajjati (syā.) evaṃ tasmiṃ [T 2.0370] dārake paṭipajjitu”nti.

Then this thought occurred to that bhikkhunī who was the companion: 'How indeed should I conduct myself with regard to this boy?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow that, setting aside living together under one roof, she may conduct herself with regard to that boy just as they conduct themselves with regard to another man.'

433. Tena [M 0.0474] kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannā hoti mānattacārinī. Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “mayā ca na labbhā ekikāya vatthuṃ, aññāya ca bhikkhuniyā na labbhā saha mayā vatthuṃ, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammannitvā tassā bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunī yācitabbā, yācitvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

433. At that time, a certain bhikkhunī had transgressed a grave rule and was undergoing the mānatta discipline. Then this thought occurred to that bhikkhunī: 'It is not allowable for me to dwell alone, and it is not allowable for another bhikkhunī to dwell together with me. How indeed should I conduct myself?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow that a bhikkhunī be appointed and given to that bhikkhunī as a companion. And, Bhikkhus, she is to be appointed in this way: First, the bhikkhunī should be asked. Having asked, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammanneyya itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṃ. Esā ñatti.

Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammannati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṃ. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā sammuti itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so. To whichever venerable lady the appointment of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so is agreeable, she should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, she should speak.

“Sammatā [V 0.0446] saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The bhikkhunī named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as a companion to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

434. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya vibbhami. Sā puna paccāgantvā bhikkhuniyo upasampadaṃ yāci[T 2.0371]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ; yadeva sā vibbhantā tadeva sā abhikkhunī”ti.

434. At that time, a certain bhikkhunī, having renounced the training, returned to lay life. She later returned and asked the bhikkhunīs for higher ordination. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhunī there is no renunciation of the training; for the very reason that she has returned to lay life, for that very reason she is no longer a bhikkhunī.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sakāvāsā titthāyatanaṃ saṅkami. Sā puna paccāgantvā bhikkhuniyo upasampadaṃ yāci. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Yā sā, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī sakāvāsā titthāyatanaṃ saṅkantā, sā āgatā na upasampādetabbā”ti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhunī went from her own residence to a sectarian hermitage. She later returned and asked the bhikkhunīs for higher ordination. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī who has gone from her own residence to a sectarian hermitage is not to be given higher ordination when she has returned.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo purisehi abhivādanaṃ[P 2.0280], kesacchedanaṃ, nakhacchedanaṃ, vaṇappaṭikammaṃ, kukkuccāyantā na sādiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāditu”nti sādiyituṃ (ka.).

At that time, the bhikkhunīs, being scrupulous, did not consent to the paying of homage, the cutting of hair, the cutting of nails, or the dressing of wounds by men. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow you to consent.'

435. Tena [M 0.0475] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo pallaṅkena nisīdanti paṇhīsamphassaṃ sādiyantī sādiyantā (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā pallaṅkena nisīditabbaṃ. Yā nisīdeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

435. At that time, the bhikkhunīs, while sitting cross-legged, were enjoying the contact of their heels. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī is not to sit cross-legged. Whichever one should so sit, there is an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti. Tassā vinā pallaṅkena na phāsu hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā aḍḍhapallaṅka”nti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhunī was sick. She was not comfortable without sitting cross-legged. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Bhikkhus, I allow a bhikkhunī the half-cross-legged posture.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo vaccakuṭiyā vaccaṃ karonti[T 2.0372]. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tattheva gabbhaṃ pātenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā vaccakuṭiyā vacco kātabbo. Yā kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, heṭṭhā vivaṭe uparipaṭicchanne vaccaṃ kātu”nti.

At that time the bhikkhunīs were relieving themselves in the latrine. The bhikkhunīs of the group of six aborted fetuses right there. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not relieve herself in the latrine. Whosoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow relieving oneself in a place that is open below and covered above.”

436. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo cuṇṇena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0447]. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā cuṇṇena nahāyitabbaṃ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kukkusaṃ mattika”nti.

436. At that time the bhikkhunīs were bathing with powder. People complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying, “They are just like female householders who indulge in sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not bathe with powder. Whosoever should bathe, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow powdered husked rice and clay.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo vāsitakāya mattikāya nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā vāsitakāya mattikāya nahāyitabbaṃ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pakatimattika”nti.

At that time the bhikkhunīs were bathing with perfumed clay. People complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying, “They are just like female householders who indulge in sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not bathe with perfumed clay. Whosoever should bathe, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow natural clay.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo jantāghare nahāyantiyo kolāhalaṃ akaṃsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā jantāghare nahāyitabbaṃ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs, while bathing in the steam-bath house, made a commotion. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not bathe in the steam-bath house. Whosoever should bathe, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paṭisote nahāyanti dhārāsamphassaṃ sādiyantī. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave[T 2.0373], bhikkhuniyā [M 0.0476] paṭisote nahāyitabbaṃ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs were bathing upstream, enjoying the touch of the current. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not bathe upstream. Whosoever should bathe, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo atitthe nahāyanti. Dhuttā dūsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā atitthe nahāyitabbaṃ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs were bathing at a place that was not a proper landing. Scoundrels molested them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not bathe at a place that is not a proper landing. Whosoever should bathe, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo purisatitthe nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [P 2.0281] ārocesuṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā purisatitthe nahāyitabbaṃ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mahilātitthe nahāyitu”nti.

At that time, bhikkhunīs were bathing at a men's bathing place. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them, saying, “They are just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not bathe at a men's bathing place. Whosoever should bathe, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow bathing at a women's bathing place.”

Tatiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The third recitation section is concluded.

Bhikkhunikkhandhako dasamo.

The tenth Chapter on Bhikkhunīs is concluded.

Imasmiṃ khandhake vatthū ekasataṃ.

In this chapter, there are one hundred and one topics.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Pabbajjaṃ [V 0.0448] gotamī yāci, nānuññāsi tathāgato;

Kapilavatthu vesāliṃ, agamāsi vināyako.

Gotamī requested the going forth; the Tathāgata did not permit it in Kapilavatthu. The Leader went to Vesālī.

Rajokiṇṇena koṭṭhake, ānandassa pavedayi;

Bhabboti [T 2.0374] nayato yāci, mātāti posikāti ca.

With dust-covered body, at the gatehouse, she informed Ānanda. She requested by a wise method, citing that she was his mother, his nurturer, and that she was capable.

Vassasataṃ tadahu ca, abhikkhupaccāsīsanā;

Pavāraṇā garudhammā, dve vassā anakkosanā.

One hundred years and ordination on that day; a residence without bhikkhus and expectation; the Pavāraṇā ceremony and the grave rules; two years and not reviling.

Ovaṭo ca aṭṭha dhammā, yāvajīvānuvattanā;

Garudhammapaṭiggāho sāvassā upasampadā.

Exhortation and the eight rules, to be followed for life; the acceptance of the grave rules—that itself was her higher ordination.

Vassasahassaṃ pañceva, kumbhathenakasetaṭṭi;

Mañjiṭṭhikaupamāhi, evaṃ saddhammahiṃsanā.

A thousand years and five hundred; the pot-breaking thief, the white-blight disease, and with the simile of red-rust disease; thus the decline of the good Dhamma.

Āḷiṃ bandheyya pāeva, puna saddhammasaṇṭhiti;

Upasampādetuṃ ayyā, yathāvuḍḍhābhivādanā.

One should build the embankment beforehand for the firm establishment of the good Dhamma; giving higher ordination to the venerable ladies; salutation according to seniority.

Na [M 0.0477] karissanti kimeva, sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇaṃ;

Ovādaṃ pātimokkhañca, kena nu kho upassayaṃ.

They will not act, how could I allow it?; shared and unshared offenses; exhortation, the Pātimokkha, and by whom the residence?

Na jānanti ca ācikkhi, na karonti ca bhikkhuhi;

Paṭiggahetuṃ bhikkhūhi, bhikkhunīhi paṭiggaho.

They do not know and he was informed; the bhikkhus do not act; receiving by bhikkhus, and receiving by bhikkhunīs.

Ācikkhi kammaṃ bhikkhūhi, ujjhāyanti bhikkhunīhi vā;

Ācikkhituṃ bhaṇḍanañca, ropetvā uppalāya ca.

Informing of a formal act by bhikkhus, or complaining by bhikkhunīs; to inform, and quarreling; falsely accusing, and Uppalavaṇṇā.

Sāvatthiyā kaddamoda, avandi kāya ūru ca;

Aṅgajātañca obhāsaṃ, sampayojenti vaggikā.

In Sāvatthī, dousing with muddy water; not paying homage; the body, thigh, and private parts; making an overture; the group-of-six instigate.

Avandiyo [V 0.0449] daṇḍakammaṃ, bhikkhuniyo tathā puna;

Āvaraṇañca [T 2.0375] ovādaṃ, kappati nu kho pakkami.

The punishment of not being paid homage to, and bhikkhunīs likewise; obstruction and exhortation; 'Is it allowable?' and he departed.

Bālā vatthuvinicchayā, ovādaṃ saṅgho pañcahi;

Duve tisso na gaṇhanti, bālā gilānagamikaṃ.

A foolish one and a decision on a case; exhortation, the Saṅgha, by five; two or three do not accept; a foolish one, a sick one, one going on a journey.

Āraññiko nārocenti, na paccāgacchanti ca;

Dīghaṃ vilīvacammañca, dussā ca veṇivaṭṭi ca;

Coḷaveṇi ca vaṭṭi ca, suttaveṇi ca vaṭṭikā.

Forest-dwelling monks do not inform, do not return, and do not go. A long girdle, a girdle made of bamboo strips, a girdle woven from leather, a cloth, a roll of cloth, a twisted cloth, a robe, a knot of robe-cloth, a twist of robe-cloth, thread, a knot of thread, and a twist of thread.

Aṭṭhillaṃ gohanukena, hatthakocchaṃ pādaṃ tathā;

Ūruṃ mukhaṃ dantamaṃsaṃ, ālimpomaddacuṇṇanā.

The skull of a cow or horse, with a cow's jawbone; a hand-brush, and likewise a foot-brush; the thigh, the face, and the gums; smearing, massaging, and applying fine powder.

Lañchenti aṅgarāgañca, mukharāgaṃ tathā duve;

Avaṅgaṃ visesoloko, sālokena naccena ca sāloke sanaccena ca (sī.), sālokena sanaccanaṃ (syā.).

They apply eye-makeup; coloring the limbs, coloring the mouth, and likewise coloring both; drawing lines for beauty, applying patches on the cheeks; looking through a window, standing at the window opening, and together with dancing.

Vesī [P 2.0282] pānāgāraṃ sūnaṃ, āpaṇaṃ vaḍḍhi vaṇijjā;

Dāsaṃ dāsiṃ kammakaraṃ, kammakāriṃ upaṭṭhayyuṃ.

A prostitute, a tavern, a butcher's block, a shop, lending at interest, trading; they cause a male slave, a female slave, a male worker, and a female worker to serve.

Tiracchānaharītaki, sandhārayanti namatakaṃ;

Nīlaṃ pītaṃ lohitakaṃ, mañjiṭṭhakaṇhacīvarā.

Animals, green vegetables; they wear a binding that is tied to make the ribs bend. A dark blue robe, a yellow robe, a red robe, a madder-colored robe, and a black robe.

Mahāraṅgamahānāmaacchinnā dīghameva ca;

Pupphaphalakañcukañca, tirīṭakañca dhārayuṃ.

They wore a robe dyed with mahāraṅga dye, a robe dyed with mahānāma dye, a robe with an uncut border, and one with a long border; a robe with a flower border, a robe with a fruit border, a jacket, and a robe of hemp.

Bhikkhunī [M 0.0478] sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇerāya accaye;

Niyyādite [T 2.0376] parikkhāre, bhikkhuniyova issarā.

At the time of death of a bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, or a sāmaṇerī, when the requisites have been entrusted, only the bhikkhunīs are the owners.

Bhikkhussa sāmaṇerassa, upāsakassupāsikā;

Aññesañca parikkhāre, niyyāte bhikkhuissarā.

When the requisites of a bhikkhu, a sāmaṇera, an upāsaka, an upāsikā, or of other persons have been entrusted, a bhikkhu is the owner.

Mallī [V 0.0450] gabbhaṃ pattamūlaṃ, byañjanaṃ āmisena ca;

Ussannañca bāḷhataraṃ, sannidhikatamāmisaṃ.

The wife of a wrestler, pregnancy, the bottom of the bowl, the male organ, and with material things; that which is very abundant, exceedingly abundant, and the stored material things.

Bhikkhūnaṃ yādisaṃ bhoṭṭhaṃ heṭṭhā (sī.), heṭṭhaṃ (syā.), bhutti (ka.), bhikkhunīnaṃ tathā kare;

Senāsanaṃ utuniyo, makkhīyati paṭāṇi ca.

Whatever is fit for the use of bhikkhus, one should do likewise for bhikkhunīs. The lodging is smeared with blood by menstruating bhikkhunīs; and a woman with a coarse cloth plug.

Chijjanti sabbakālañca, animittāpi dissare;

Nimittā lohitā ceva, tatheva dhuvalohitā.

It was cut off at all times; even those without the female organ appear. A bhikkhunī with only the female organ, a bhikkhunī who does not bleed, and a bhikkhunī who bleeds constantly.

Dhuvacoḷapaggharantī, sikharaṇitthipaṇḍakā;

Vepurisī ca sambhinnā, ubhatobyañjanāpi ca.

A bhikkhunī who constantly uses a coarse cloth plug, one from whom blood drips, one with a long protrusion of flesh, a female paṇḍaka, a man-turned-woman, one whose two passages are connected, and she who has the characteristics of both sexes.

Animittādito katvā, yāva ubhatobyañjanā;

Etaṃ peyyālato heṭṭhā, kuṭṭhaṃ gaṇḍo kilāso ca.

Beginning from the one without the female organ up to the one with characteristics of both sexes, all of this should be known below by way of abbreviation. Leprosy, a boil, and skin diseases.

Sosāpamāro mānusī, itthīsi bhujissāsi ca;

Aṇaṇā na rājabhaṭī, anuññātā ca vīsati.

Consumptive disease, epilepsy. Are you a human? Are you a woman? Are you a freed woman? Are you free from debt? Are you not a female servant of the king? Permission from parents and husband, and being twenty years of age.

Paripuṇṇā ca kinnāmā, kānāmā te pavattinī;

Catuvīsantarāyānaṃ, pucchitvā upasampadā.

Completeness of bowl and robes; what is your name? What is the name of your preceptor? Having asked about the twenty-four obstacles, there is higher ordination.

Vitthāyanti ananusiṭṭhā, saṅghamajjhe tatheva ca;

Upajjhāgāha saṅghāṭi, uttarantaravāsako.

Uninstructed ones are shy, and likewise in the midst of the Saṅgha. Taking a preceptor, the double-layered robe, the upper robe, and the inner robe.

Saṅkaccudakasāṭi ca, ācikkhitvāna pesaye;

Bālā [T 2.0377] asammatekato, yāce pucchantarāyikā.

The breast-cloth and bathing cloth; having explained, one should send them. A foolish, unappointed bhikkhunī asks together about the obstructions.

Ekatoupasampannā, bhikkhusaṅghe tathā puna;

Chāyā utu divasā ca, saṅgīti tayo nissaye.

Ordained on one side, and likewise again in the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. Shadow, season, day, their summation, and the three dependencies.

Aṭṭha akaraṇīyāni, kālaṃ sabbattha aṭṭheva;

Na pavārenti bhikkhunī, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ tatheva ca.

The eight things not to be done; at all times, in all matters, there are eight indeed. Bhikkhunīs do not perform pavāraṇā, and likewise not towards the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.

Kolāhalaṃ [M 0.0479][V 0.0451] purebhattaṃ, vikāle ca kolāhalaṃ;

Uposathaṃ pavāraṇaṃ, savacanīyānuvādanaṃ.

Commotion before the meal, and commotion at the wrong time; Uposatha, Pavāraṇā, admonishment, and placing in a position of authority.

Okāsaṃ code sārenti, paṭikkhittaṃ mahesinā;

Tatheva bhikkhu bhikkhunī, anuññātaṃ mahesinā.

Asking for an opportunity, accusing, and reminding—this was rejected by the Great Sage. Likewise, for a bhikkhu towards a bhikkhunī, this was permitted by the Great Sage.

Yānaṃ gilānayuttañca, yānugghātaḍḍhakāsikā;

Bhikkhu sikkhā sāmaṇera, sāmaṇerī ca bālāya.

A vehicle, and a yoked vehicle for a sick bhikkhunī; a bhikkhunī who strikes a vehicle, and Aḍḍhakāsikā; a bhikkhu, a trainee, a male novice, and a female novice as messengers for a foolish girl.

Araññe [P 2.0283] upāsakena, uddosito upassayaṃ;

Na sammati navakammaṃ, nisinnagabbhaekikā.

In the forest, a dwelling pointed out by a layman; the new work is not sufficient; a pregnant bhikkhunī sitting alone.

Sāgārañca garudhammaṃ, paccakkhāya ca saṅkami;

Abhivādanakesā ca, nakhā ca vaṇakammanā.

Living together in an enclosed dwelling; a Garudhamma; giving up the training and transferring; paying homage, shaving hair, cutting nails, and treating a wound.

Pallaṅkena gilānā ca, vaccaṃ cuṇṇena vāsitaṃ;

Jantāghare paṭisote, atitthe purisena ca.

A sick bhikkhunī sitting cross-legged; excrement scented with powder; in a steam-bath house; upstream; at a non-ford; and at a men's bathing place.

Mahāgotamī āyāci, ānando cāpi yoniso;

Parisā catasso honti, pabbajjā jinasāsane.

Mahāgotamī requested, and Ānanda also requested wisely. Because of the going forth in the Dispensation of the Jina, the four assemblies come to be.

Saṃvegajananatthāya[T 2.0378], saddhammassa ca vuddhiyā;

Āturassāva bhesajjaṃ, evaṃ buddhena desitaṃ.

For the sake of arousing spiritual urgency and for the growth of the good Dhamma; like medicine for the sick, thus was it taught by the Buddha.

Evaṃ vinītā saddhamme, mātugāmāpi itarā;

Yāyanti tāyanti (sī. syā.) accutaṃ ṭhānaṃ, yattha gantvā na socareti.

Thus trained in the good Dhamma, other women also go to the deathless state, to which place having gone, they do not grieve.

Bhikkhunikkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter on the Bhikkhunīs is finished.

11. Pañcasatikakkhandhakaṃ

11. The Chapter of the Five Hundred

1. Saṅgītinidānaṃ

1. The Account of the Council

437. Atha [T 2.0379][P 2.0284][M 0.0480][V 0.0452] kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhikkhū āmantesi – “ekamidāhaṃ, āvuso, samayaṃ pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Atha khvāhaṃ, āvuso, maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdiṃ.

437. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa addressed the bhikkhus: “On one occasion, friends, I was traveling on the long road from Pāvā to Kusinārā with a great company of bhikkhus, with about five hundred bhikkhus. Then, friends, I turned aside from the road and sat down at the foot of a certain tree.

dī. ni. 2.231 “Tena kho pana samayena aññataro ājīvako kusinārāya mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti. Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, taṃ ājīvakaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna taṃ ājīvakaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘apāvuso, amhākaṃ satthāraṃ jānāsī’ti? ‘Āmāvuso, jānāmi. Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo. Tato me idaṃ mandāravapupphaṃ gahita’nti. Tatrāvuso, ye te bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahitanti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhāti.

“At that time, a certain Ājīvaka, having taken a mandārava flower from Kusinārā, was traveling along the long road to Pāvā. I saw, friends, that Ājīvaka coming from afar. Having seen him, I said this to that Ājīvaka: ‘Friend, do you know our Teacher?’ ‘Yes, friend, I know. Today it has been seven days since the ascetic Gotama attained final Nibbāna. It was from there that this mandārava flower was taken by me.’ There, friends, those bhikkhus who were not free from passion—some of them raised their arms and wept, fell down as if their feet were cut off, rolled forwards and backwards, lamenting: ‘Too quickly has the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna! Too quickly has the Sugata attained final Nibbāna!
