Too quickly has the Eye vanished from the world!’ But those bhikkhus who were free from passion, being mindful and fully aware, endured, reflecting: ‘Conditioned things are impermanent. How, in this case, could that be obtained?’

“Atha khvāhaṃ, āvuso, te bhikkhū etadavocaṃ – ‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha; mā paridevittha. Nanvetaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi [T 2.0380] nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo. Taṃ kutettha āvuso labbhā, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti.

“Then, friends, I said to those bhikkhus: ‘Enough, friends, do not grieve; do not lament. Friends, has it not been declared from the very beginning by the Blessed One that with all that is dear and pleasing there is otherness, separation, and alteration? How, in this case, friends, could it be obtained that what is born, come to be, conditioned, and subject to perishing should not, indeed, perish? That condition is not found.’

“Tena kho panāvuso, samayena subhaddo nāma vuḍḍhapabbajito tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti[V 0.0453]. Atha kho, āvuso, subhaddo vuḍḍhapabbajito te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha; mā paridevittha. Sumuttā mayaṃ tena mahāsamaṇena[P 2.0285]; upaddutā ca mayaṃ homa – idaṃ vo kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatīti. Idāni pana mayaṃ yaṃ icchissāma taṃ karissāma, yaṃ na icchissāma na taṃ karissāmā’ti. Handa [M 0.0481] mayaṃ, āvuso, dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyāma. Pure adhammo dippati dibbati (ka.), dhammo paṭibāhiyyati; pure avinayo dippati vinayo paṭibāhiyyati; pure adhammavādino balavanto honti, dhammavādino dubbalā honti; pure avinayavādino balavanto honti, vinayavādino dubbalā hontī”ti.

“At that time, friends, an elderly monk named Subhadda was seated in that assembly. Then, friends, the elderly monk Subhadda said this to those bhikkhus: ‘Enough, friends! Do not grieve; do not lament. We are well freed from that great ascetic. We were oppressed by him, saying: “This is allowable for you, this is not allowable for you.” But now we shall do what we wish, and what we do not wish, we shall not do.’ Come, friends, let us chant the Dhamma and the Vinaya before unrighteousness shines forth and righteousness is suppressed; before indiscipline shines forth and discipline is suppressed; before those who speak unrighteousness become strong and those who speak righteousness become weak; before those who speak indiscipline become strong and those who speak discipline become weak.”

“Tena hi, bhante, thero bhikkhū uccinatū”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo ekenūnapañcaarahantasatāni uccini. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā ānando kiñcāpi sekkho, abhabbo chandā dosā mohā bhayā agatiṃ gantuṃ. Bahu ca anena bhagavato santike dhammo ca vinayo ca pariyatto. Tena hi, bhante, thero āyasmantampi ānandaṃ uccinatū”ti[T 2.0381]. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantampi ānandaṃ uccini.

“Then, venerable sir, let the Elder select the bhikkhus.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa selected four hundred and ninety-nine arahants. The bhikkhus said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Venerable sir, this Venerable Ānanda, although he is a learner, is incapable of going to a wrong course through desire, hatred, delusion, or fear. And much Dhamma and Vinaya has been learned by him in the presence of the Blessed One. Therefore, venerable sir, let the Elder also select the Venerable Ānanda.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa also selected the Venerable Ānanda.

Atha kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kattha nu kho mayaṃ dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyeyyāmā”ti? Atha kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “rājagahaṃ kho mahāgocaraṃ pahūtasenāsanaṃ, yaṃnūna mayaṃ rājagahe vassaṃ vasantā dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyeyyāma. Na aññe bhikkhū rājagahe vassaṃ upagaccheyyu”nti.

Then this thought occurred to the elder bhikkhus: “Where indeed should we rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya?” Then this thought occurred to the elder bhikkhus: “Rājagaha has a large area for alms-round and abundant lodgings. It would be good if we, while spending the rains-residence in Rājagaha, were to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya, and if other bhikkhus did not enter upon the rains-residence in Rājagaha.”

Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

Then the Venerable Mahākassapa informed the Saṅgha:

438. “Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imāni pañca bhikkhusatāni sammanneyya – rājagahe vassaṃ vasantāni dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṃ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṃ vasitabbanti. Esā ñatti.

438. “Reverend sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should authorize these five hundred bhikkhus to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya while residing for the rains-residence in Rājagaha, and that other bhikkhus should not reside for the rains-residence in Rājagaha. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Imāni pañca bhikkhusatāni sammannati – rājagahe vassaṃ vasantāni dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṃ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṃ vasitabbanti. Yassāyasmato khamati imesaṃ pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ sammuti – rājagahe vassaṃ vasantānaṃ [V 0.0454] dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṃ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṃ vasitabbanti – so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Reverend sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha authorizes these five hundred bhikkhus to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya while residing for the rains-residence in Rājagaha, and that other bhikkhus should not reside for the rains-residence in Rājagaha. To whichever venerable one the authorization of these five hundred bhikkhus to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya while residing for the rains-residence in Rājagaha, and that other bhikkhus should not reside for the rains-residence in Rājagaha, is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Sammatāni [M 0.0482] saṅghena imāni pañca bhikkhusatāni rājagahe vassaṃ vasantāni dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṃ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṃ vasitabbanti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ [T 2.0382] dhārayāmī”ti.

“These five hundred bhikkhus have been authorized by the Saṅgha to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya while residing for the rains-residence in Rājagaha, and that other bhikkhus should not reside for the rains-residence in Rājagaha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I take note of it.”

Atha [P 2.0286] kho therā bhikkhū rājagahaṃ agamaṃsu dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṃ. Atha kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā kho, āvuso, khaṇḍaphullappaṭisaṅkharaṇaṃ vaṇṇitaṃ. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, paṭhamaṃ māsaṃ khaṇḍaphullaṃ paṭisaṅkharoma; majjhimaṃ māsaṃ sannipatitvā dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyissāmā”ti.

Then the elder bhikkhus went to Rājagaha to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya. Then this thought occurred to the elder bhikkhus: “Reverend sirs, the repairing of what is broken and dilapidated has been praised by the Blessed One. Come, Reverend sirs, for the first month let us repair what is broken and dilapidated; then, having assembled in the middle month, we will rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya.”

Atha kho therā bhikkhū paṭhamaṃ māsaṃ khaṇḍaphullaṃ paṭisaṅkhariṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā ānando – sve sannipāto sannipātoti (ka.) na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ, yohaṃ sekkho samāno sannipātaṃ gaccheyyanti – bahudeva rattiṃ kāyagatāya satiyā vītināmetvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ ‘nipajjissāmī’ti kāyaṃ āvajjesi. Appattañca sīsaṃ bibbohanaṃ, bhūmito ca pādā muttā. Etasmiṃ antare anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimucci.

Then, the elder bhikkhus spent the first month repairing what was broken and dilapidated. Then the Venerable Ānanda, having reflected, 'Tomorrow is the assembly. It would not be proper for me, being a learner, to go to the assembly,' spent much of the night with mindfulness directed to the body. At dawn, thinking, 'I will lie down,' he inclined his body. Before his head reached the pillow and after his feet had lifted from the ground, in that interval, his mind was liberated from the taints without clinging.

439. Atha kho āyasmā ānando arahā samāno sannipātaṃ agamāsi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

439. Then the Venerable Ānanda, being an Arahant, went to the assembly. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ upāliṃ vinayaṃ puccheyya”nti.

“Reverend sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would question Upāli on the Vinaya.”

Āyasmā upāli saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

The Venerable Upāli informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ āyasmatā mahākassapena vinayaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyya”nti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I, being questioned on the Vinaya by the Venerable Mahākassapa, would answer.”

Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ etadavoca – “paṭhamaṃ, āvuso upāli[T 2.0383][V 0.0455], pārājikaṃ kattha paññatta”nti? “Vesāliyaṃ bhante”ti. “Kaṃ ārabbhā”ti? “Sudinnaṃ kalandaputtaṃ ārabbhā”ti. “Kismiṃ vatthusmi”nti? “Methunadhamme”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ paṭhamassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi [M 0.0483] pucchi. “Dutiyaṃ panāvuso upāli, pārājikaṃ kattha paññatta”nti? “Rājagahe bhante”ti. “Kaṃ ārabbhā”ti? “Dhaniyaṃ kumbhakāraputtaṃ ārabbhā”ti. “Kismiṃ vatthusmi”nti? “Adinnādāne”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ dutiyassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi. “Tatiyaṃ panāvuso upāli, pārājikaṃ kattha paññatta”nti? “Vesāliyaṃ bhante”ti. “Kaṃ ārabbhā”ti? “Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbhā”ti. “Kismiṃ vatthusmi”nti? “Manussaviggahe”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ [P 2.0287] tatiyassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi. “Catutthaṃ panāvuso upāli, pārājikaṃ kattha paññatta”nti? “Vesāliyaṃ bhante”ti. “Kaṃ ārabbhā”ti? “Vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū ārabbhā”ti. “Kismiṃ vatthusmi”nti? “Uttarimanussadhamme”ti. Atha kho āyasmā [T 2.0384] mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ catutthassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi. Eteneva upāyena ubhatovibhaṅge pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā upāli vissajjesi.

Then the Venerable Mahākassapa said this to the Venerable Upāli: “Friend Upāli, where was the first pārājika laid down?” “In Vesālī, venerable sir.” “Concerning whom?” “Concerning Sudinna, the son of Kalanda.” “In what matter?” “In the matter of sexual intercourse.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa asked the Venerable Upāli about the story, the origin, the person, the primary regulation, the supplementary regulation, the offense, and the non-offense of the first pārājika. “Friend Upāli, where was the second pārājika laid down?” “In Rājagaha, venerable sir.” “Concerning whom?” “Concerning Dhaniya, the potter’s son.” “In what matter?” “In the matter of taking what was not given.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa asked the Venerable Upāli about the story, the origin, the person, the primary regulation, the supplementary regulation, the offense, and the non-offense of the second pārājika. “Friend Upāli, where was the third pārājika laid down?” “In Vesālī, venerable sir.” “Concerning whom?” “Concerning many bhikkhus.” “In what matter?” “In the matter of killing a human being.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa asked the Venerable Upāli about the story, the origin, the person, the primary regulation, the supplementary regulation, the offense, and the non-offense of the third pārājika. “Friend Upāli, where was the fourth pārājika laid down?” “In Vesālī, venerable sir.” “Concerning whom?” “Concerning the bhikkhus on the bank of the Vaggumudā river.” “In what matter?” “In the matter of a superhuman state.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa asked the Venerable Upāli about the story, the origin, the person, the primary regulation, the supplementary regulation, the offense, and the non-offense of the fourth pārājika. In this very way, he asked about both Vibhaṅgas. Whenever he was asked, the Venerable Upāli answered.

440. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

440. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ ānandaṃ dhammaṃ puccheyya”nti.

“Friends, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, I would question Ānanda about the Dhamma.”

Āyasmā ānando saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

The Venerable Ānanda informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ āyasmatā mahākassapena dhammaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyya”nti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, I, being questioned about the Dhamma by the Venerable Mahākassapa, would answer.”

Atha [V 0.0456] kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “brahmajālaṃ, āvuso ānanda, kattha bhāsita”nti? “Antarā ca, bhante, rājagahaṃ antarā ca nāḷandaṃ rājāgārake ambalaṭṭhikāyā”ti. “Kaṃ ārabbhā”ti? “Suppiyañca paribbājakaṃ brahmadattañca māṇava”nti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ brahmajālassa nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi. “Sāmaññaphalaṃ panāvuso ānanda, kattha bhāsita”nti? “Rājagahe, bhante, jīvakambavane”ti. “Kena saddhi”nti? “Ajātasattunā vedehiputtena [M 0.0484] saddhi”nti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ sāmaññaphalassa nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi [T 2.0385] pucchi. Eteneva upāyena pañcapi nikāye pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā ānando vissajjesi.

Then the Venerable Mahākassapa said to the Venerable Ānanda: “Friend Ānanda, where was the Brahmajāla Sutta spoken?” “Venerable sir, between Rājagaha and Nāḷandā, at the royal rest-house in Ambalaṭṭhikā.” “With reference to whom?” “The wanderer Suppiya and the young man Brahmadatta.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa asked the Venerable Ānanda about the occasion for the Brahmajāla Sutta and the person involved. “And where, friend Ānanda, was the Sāmaññaphala Sutta spoken?” “Venerable sir, in Rājagaha, in Jīvaka’s mango grove.” “With whom?” “With King Ajātasattu, son of the Vedehan queen.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa asked the Venerable Ānanda about the occasion for the Sāmaññaphala Sutta and the person involved. In this very way, he asked about all five Nikāyas. Each time he was asked, the Venerable Ānanda answered.

2. Khuddānukhuddakasikkhāpadakathā

2. The Discussion on the Minor and Lesser Training Rules

441. Atha kho āyasmā ānando there bhikkhū etadavoca – “bhagavā maṃ, bhante, parinibbānakāle evamāha – ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhaneyyā’”ti. “Pucchi pana tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, bhagavantaṃ – ‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’”ti? “Na khohaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ pucchiṃ – ‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā[P 2.0288], terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, tiṃsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, tiṃsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā, dvenavuti pācittiye ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, tiṃsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā, dvenavuti pācittiye ṭhapetvā, cattāro pāṭidesanīye ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni [T 2.0386] sikkhāpadānī”ti.

441. Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the elder monks: “Venerable sirs, at the time of His final passing away, the Blessed One said to me: ‘Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing away it may abolish the minor and lesser training rules.’” “But did you, friend Ānanda, ask the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, which are the minor and lesser training rules?’” “No, venerable sirs, I did not ask the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, which are the minor and lesser training rules?’” Some elders said thus: “Setting aside the four Pārājikas, the remaining are the minor and lesser training rules.” Some elders said thus: “Setting aside the four Pārājikas and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the remaining are the minor and lesser training rules.” Some elders said thus: “Setting aside the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and the two Aniyatas, the remaining are the minor and lesser training rules.” Some elders said thus: “Setting aside the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the two Aniyatas, and the thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiyas, the remaining are the minor and lesser training rules.” Some elders said thus: “Setting aside the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the two Aniyatas, the thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiyas, and the ninety-two Pācittiyas, the remaining are the minor and lesser training rules.” Some elders said thus: “Setting aside the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the two Aniyatas, the thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiyas, the ninety-two Pācittiyas, and the four Pāṭidesanīyas, the remaining are the minor and lesser training rules.”

442. Atha [V 0.0457] kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

442. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Santamhākaṃ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni. Gihinopi jānanti – ‘idaṃ vo samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’ti. Sace mayaṃ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanissāma, bhavissanti [M 0.0485] vattāro – ‘dhūmakālikaṃ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Yāvimesaṃ satthā aṭṭhāsi tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṃsu. Yato imesaṃ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’ti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho appaññattaṃ nappaññapeyya, paññattaṃ na samucchindeyya, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vatteyya. Esā ñatti.

“Friends, may the Saṅgha hear me. There are training rules of ours which are known to the laity. Even the laity know: ‘This is allowable for you, the Sakyan son ascetics; this is not allowable for you.’ If we were to abolish the minor and lesser training rules, there will be those who say: ‘A training rule was laid down for the disciples by the ascetic Gotama for a temporary period. As long as their Teacher was present, they trained in the training rules. Since their Teacher has attained final Nibbāna, now they do not train in the training rules.’ If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should not lay down what has not been laid down, nor abolish what has been laid down, but should proceed by undertaking the training rules as they have been laid down. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Santamhākaṃ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni. Gihinopi jānanti – ‘idaṃ vo samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’ti. Sace mayaṃ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanissāma, bhavissanti vattāro – ‘dhūmakālikaṃ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ[T 2.0387]. Yāvimesaṃ satthā aṭṭhāsi tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṃsu. Yato imesaṃ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’ti. Saṅgho appaññattaṃ nappaññapeti, paññattaṃ na samucchindati, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattati. Yassāyasmato khamati appaññattassa appaññāpanā, paññattassa asamucchedo, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Friends, may the Saṅgha hear me. There are training rules of ours which are known to the laity. Even the laity know: ‘This is allowable for you, the Sakyan son ascetics; this is not allowable for you.’ If we were to abolish the minor and lesser training rules, there would be those who say: ‘A training rule was laid down for the disciples by the ascetic Gotama for a temporary period. As long as their Teacher was present, they trained in the training rules. Since their Teacher has attained final Nibbāna, now they do not train in the training rules.’ The Saṅgha does not lay down what has not been laid down, nor does it abolish what has been laid down, but proceeds by undertaking the training rules as they have been laid down. To whichever venerable one the non-laying down of what has not been laid down, the non-abolishing of what has been laid down, and the proceeding by undertaking the training rules as they have been laid down is agreeable, he should be silent. He to whom it is not agreeable should speak.”

“Saṅgho appaññattaṃ nappaññapeti, paññattaṃ na samucchindati, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattati. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The Saṅgha does not lay down what has not been laid down, nor does it abolish what has been laid down, but proceeds by undertaking the training rules as they have been laid down. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

443. Atha kho therā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idaṃ te, āvuso ānanda, dukkaṭaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ bhagavantaṃ na pucchi – ‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni [P 2.0289] sikkhāpadānī’ti. Desehi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, assatiyā bhagavantaṃ na pucchiṃ – ‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Nāhaṃ taṃ dukkaṭaṃ passāmi, api cāyasmantānaṃ saddhāya desemi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Idampi te, āvuso ānanda, dukkaṭaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ bhagavato vassikasāṭikaṃ akkamitvā sibbesi. Desehi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, na agāravena bhagavato vassikasāṭikaṃ akkamitvā sibbesiṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ dukkaṭaṃ passāmi, api cāyasmantānaṃ saddhāya desemi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Idampi [T 2.0388][V 0.0458] te, āvuso ānanda, dukkaṭaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ mātugāmehi bhagavato [M 0.0486] sarīraṃ paṭhamaṃ vandāpesi, tāsaṃ rodantīnaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ assukena makkhitaṃ. Desehi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. Ahaṃ kho, bhante – māyimāsaṃ māyimā (sī. syā.) vikāle ahesunti – mātugāmehi bhagavato sarīraṃ paṭhamaṃ vandāpesiṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ dukkaṭaṃ passāmi, api cāyasmantānaṃ saddhāya desemi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Idampi te, āvuso ānanda, dukkaṭaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ bhagavatā oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne, oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne, na bhagavantaṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ, bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Desehi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto na bhagavantaṃ yāciṃ – ‘tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ, bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Nāhaṃ taṃ dukkaṭaṃ passāmi, api cāyasmantānaṃ saddhāya desemi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Idampi te, āvuso ānanda, dukkaṭaṃ yaṃ tvaṃ mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye pabbajjaṃ ussukkaṃ akāsi. Desehi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti. “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, ayaṃ mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavato mātucchā āpādikā posikā khīrassa dāyikā bhagavantaṃ janettiyā kālaṅkatāya thaññaṃ pāyesīti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye pabbajjaṃ ussukkaṃ akāsiṃ. Nāhaṃ taṃ dukkaṭaṃ passāmi, api [T 2.0389] cāyasmantānaṃ saddhāya desemi taṃ dukkaṭa”nti.

443. Then the elder monks said to the Venerable Ānanda: “This is a fault for you, friend Ānanda, that you did not ask the Blessed One: ‘What, venerable sir, are the minor and lesser training rules?’ Acknowledge that fault.” “I, venerable sirs, was unmindful and did not ask the Blessed One: ‘What, venerable sir, are the minor and lesser training rules?’ I do not see that as a fault, but out of faith in the venerable ones, I acknowledge that fault.” “This too is a fault for you, friend Ānanda, that you sewed the Blessed One’s rain-robe while stepping on it. Acknowledge that fault.” “I, venerable sirs, did not sew the Blessed One’s rain-robe stepping on it disrespectfully. I do not see that as a fault, but out of faith in the venerable ones, I acknowledge that fault.” “This too is a fault for you, friend Ānanda, that you had women pay homage to the Blessed One’s body first, so that the Blessed One’s body was stained with the tears of the weeping women. Acknowledge that fault.” “I, venerable sirs, thinking, ‘Lest it become an untimely hour for them,’ had women pay homage to the Blessed One’s body first. I do not see that as a fault, but out of faith in the venerable ones, I acknowledge that fault.” “This too is a fault for you, friend Ānanda, that when the Blessed One gave a striking sign and displayed a striking radiance, you did not request the Blessed One: ‘May the Blessed One remain for an eon, may the Well-farer remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans.’ Acknowledge that fault.” “I, venerable sirs, with my mind possessed by Māra, did not request the Blessed One: ‘May the Blessed One remain for an eon, may the Well-farer remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans.’ I do not see that as a fault, but out of faith in the venerable ones, I acknowledge that fault.” “This too is a fault for you, friend Ānanda, that you made an effort to promote the going forth of women in the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata. Acknowledge that fault.” “I, venerable sirs, thinking that this Mahāpajāpati Gotamī was the Blessed One’s maternal aunt, his nurse, his foster-mother, the giver of milk, who gave him suck after his birth mother had passed away, made an effort to promote the going forth of women in the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata. I do not see that as a fault, but out of faith in the venerable ones, I acknowledge that fault.”

444. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā purāṇo dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Atha kho āyasmā purāṇo therehi bhikkhūhi dhamme ca vinaye ca saṅgīte dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena rājagahaṃ yena veḷuvanaṃ [P 2.0290] kalandakanivāpo yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā therehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammoditvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ purāṇaṃ therā bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “therehi, āvuso purāṇa, dhammo ca vinayo ca saṅgīto. Upehi taṃ saṅgīti”nti. “Susaṅgītāvuso, therehi dhammo ca vinayo ca. Apica yatheva mayā bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, tathevāhaṃ dhāressāmī”ti.

444. At that time, the Venerable Purāṇa was wandering on tour in the Dakkhiṇāgiri region with a large company of monks, about five hundred in number. Then, when the Dhamma and Vinaya had been recited by the elder monks, the Venerable Purāṇa, after staying in Dakkhiṇāgiri as long as he pleased, went to Rājagaha, to the Veḷuvana, the Squirrels' Feeding Place, where the elder monks were. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the elder monks and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the elder monks said to the Venerable Purāṇa: 'Friend Purāṇa, the Dhamma and Vinaya have been recited by the elders. Please accept this recitation.' 'Friends, the Dhamma and Vinaya have been well recited by the elders. Nevertheless, I shall bear it in mind just as I heard it in the presence of the Blessed One, just as I received it in his presence.'

3. Brahmadaṇḍakathā

3. The Story of the Brahma-Penalty

445. Atha [M 0.0487] kho āyasmā ānando there bhikkhū etadavoca – “bhagavā maṃ, bhante, parinibbānakāle evamāha – ‘tena hānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena channassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍaṃ āṇāpetū’”ti[V 0.0459]. “Pucchi pana tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, bhagavantaṃ – ‘katamo pana, bhante, brahmadaṇḍo’”ti? “Pucchiṃ khohaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ – ‘katamo pana, bhante, brahmadaṇḍo’”ti? “Channo, ānanda, bhikkhu yaṃ iccheyya taṃ vadeyya. Bhikkhūhi channo bhikkhu neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, nānusāsitabbo”ti. “Tena hāvuso ānanda, tvaṃyeva channassa bhikkhuno [T 2.0390] brahmadaṇḍaṃ āṇāpehī”ti. “Kathāhaṃ, bhante, channassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍaṃ āṇāpemi, caṇḍo so bhikkhu pharuso”ti? ‘Tena hāvuso ānanda, bahukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ gacchāhī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭissutvā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi nāvāya ujjavanikāya kosambiṃ ujjavi, nāvāya paccorohitvā rañño udenassa utenassa (ka.) uyyānassa avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena rājā udeno uyyāne paricāresi saddhiṃ orodhena. Assosi kho rañño udenassa orodho – “amhākaṃ kira ācariyo ayyo ānando uyyānassa avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinno”ti. Atha kho rañño udenassa orodho rājānaṃ udenaṃ etadavoca – “amhākaṃ kira, deva, ācariyo ayyo ānando uyyānassa avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinno. Icchāma mayaṃ, deva, ayyaṃ ānandaṃ passitu”nti. “Tena hi tumhe samaṇaṃ ānandaṃ passathā”ti.

445. Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the elder monks, “Venerable sirs, the Blessed One said to me at the time of his final passing away: ‘Therefore, Ānanda, after my passing, let the Saṅgha impose the Brahma-penalty on the monk Channa.’” “But did you ask the Blessed One, friend Ānanda, ‘What, venerable sir, is the Brahma-penalty?’” “I did ask the Blessed One, venerable sirs, ‘What, venerable sir, is the Brahma-penalty?’ ‘The monk Channa, Ānanda, may say whatever he wishes. The monks should not speak to the monk Channa, nor advise him, nor admonish him.’” “Then, friend Ānanda, you yourself should impose the Brahma-penalty on the monk Channa.” “How, venerable sirs, can I impose the Brahma-penalty on the monk Channa? He is fierce and harsh.” “Then, friend Ānanda, go with a large number of monks.” “Very well, venerable sirs,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the elder monks. Then, accompanied by a large Saṅgha of monks—some five hundred monks—he went upstream by boat to Kosambī. After disembarking from the boat, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree not far from King Udena's park. At that time, King Udena was amusing himself in the park with his women. King Udena's women heard, “Our teacher, the Venerable Ānanda, is sitting at the foot of a certain tree not far from the park.” Then King Udena's women said to King Udena, “Our teacher, the Venerable Ānanda, is sitting at the foot of a certain tree not far from the park. We wish, sire, to see the Venerable Ānanda.” “Then you may see the ascetic Ānanda.”

Atha kho rañño udenassa orodho yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rañño udenassa orodhaṃ āyasmā ānando dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi [T 2.0391] samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi[P 2.0291]. Atha kho rañño udenassa orodho āyasmatā ānandena dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito āyasmato ānandassa pañca uttarāsaṅgasatāni pādāsi. Atha [M 0.0488] kho rañño udenassa orodho āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena rājā udeno tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho rājā udeno orodhaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna orodhaṃ etadavoca – “api nu kho tumhe samaṇaṃ ānandaṃ passitthā”ti? “Apassimhā kho mayaṃ, deva, ayyaṃ ānanda”nti. “Api nu tumhe samaṇassa ānandassa kiñci adatthā”ti? “Adamhā kho mayaṃ, deva, ayyassa ānandassa pañca uttarāsaṅgasatānī”ti. Rājā udeno ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇo ānando tāva bahuṃ cīvaraṃ paṭiggahessati! Dussavāṇijjaṃ vā samaṇo ānando karissati, paggāhikasālaṃ vā pasāressatī”ti!

Then King Udena's harem approached the Venerable Ānanda, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened King Udena's harem with a Dhamma talk. Then King Udena's harem, having been instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened by the Venerable Ānanda with a Dhamma talk, offered five hundred upper robes to the Venerable Ānanda. Then King Udena's harem, having rejoiced and expressed appreciation for the Venerable Ānanda’s words, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, circumambulated him, and went to King Udena. King Udena saw the harem coming from afar. Having seen them, he said to the harem, “Did you see the ascetic Ānanda?” “Indeed, Your Majesty, we saw the Venerable Ānanda.” “Did you give anything to the ascetic Ānanda?” “Indeed, Your Majesty, we gave five hundred upper robes to the Venerable Ānanda.” King Udena became annoyed, irritated, and displeased, saying, “How can the ascetic Ānanda accept so many robes? Is the ascetic Ānanda going to engage in the cloth trade or set up a shop?”

Atha [V 0.0460] kho rājā udeno yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā udeno āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “āgamā nu [T 2.0392] khvidha, bho ānanda, amhākaṃ orodho”ti? “Āgamāsi kho te idha, mahārāja, orodho”ti. “Api pana bhoto ānandassa kiñci adāsī”ti? “Adāsi kho me, mahārāja, pañca uttarāsaṅgasatānī”ti. “Kiṃ pana bhavaṃ ānando tāva bahuṃ cīvaraṃ karissatī”ti? “Ye ye pana (ka.) te, mahārāja, bhikkhū dubbalacīvarā tehi saddhiṃ saṃvibhajissāmī”ti. “Yāni kho pana, bho ānanda, porāṇakāni dubbalacīvarāni tāni kathaṃ karissathā”ti? “Tāni, mahārāja, uttarattharaṇaṃ karissāmā”ti. “Yāni pana, bho ānanda, porāṇakāni uttarattharaṇāni tāni kathaṃ karissathā”ti? “Tāni, mahārāja, bhisicchaviyo karissāmā”ti. “Yā pana, bho ānanda, porāṇakā bhisicchaviyo tā kathaṃ karissathā”ti? “Tā, mahārāja, bhūmattharaṇaṃ karissāmā”ti. “Yāni pana, bho ānanda, porāṇakāni bhūmattharaṇāni tāni kathaṃ karissathā”ti? “Tāni, mahārāja, pādapuñchaniyo karissāmā”ti. “Yā pana, bho ānanda, porāṇakā pādapuñchaniyo tā kathaṃ karissathā”ti?. “Tā, mahārāja, rajoharaṇaṃ karissāmā”ti. “Yāni pana, bho [M 0.0489] ānanda, porāṇakāni rajoharaṇāni tāni kathaṃ karissathā”ti? “Tāni, mahārāja, koṭṭetvā cikkhallena madditvā paribhaṇḍaṃ limpissāmā”ti.

Then King Udena approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. After concluding courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Udena said this to the Venerable Ānanda: 'Venerable Ānanda, did our harem come here?' 'Indeed, great king, your harem came here.' 'And did they give anything to the Venerable Ānanda?' 'Indeed, great king, they gave me five hundred upper robes.' 'What will the Venerable Ānanda do with so many robes?' 'Great king, I will share them with those monks who have worn-out robes.' 'And what will you do with the old, worn-out robes, Venerable Ānanda?' 'Great king, we will make them into coverlets.' 'And what will you do with the old coverlets, Venerable Ānanda?' 'Great king, we will make them into mattress covers.' 'And what will you do with the old mattress covers, Venerable Ānanda?' 'Great king, we will make them into floor coverings.' 'And what will you do with the old floor coverings, Venerable Ānanda?' 'Great king, we will make them into foot-wipers.' 'And what will you do with the old foot-wipers, Venerable Ānanda?' 'Great king, we will make them into dust-cloths.' 'And what will you do with the old dust-cloths, Venerable Ānanda?' 'Great king, having pounded them and kneaded them with mud, we will apply them as plaster.'

Atha kho rājā udeno – sabbevime [P 2.0292] samaṇā sakyaputtiyā yoniso upanenti, na kulavaṃ gamentīti [T 2.0393] – āyasmato ānandassa aññānipi pañca dussasatāni pādāsi. Ayañcarahi āyasmato ānandassa paṭhamaṃ cīvarabhikkhā uppajji cīvarasahassaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena ghositārāmo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmā channo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ channaṃ āyasmā ānando etadavoca – “saṅghena te, āvuso channa, brahmadaṇḍo āṇāpito”ti.

Then King Udena, thinking, 'All these recluses, sons of the Sakyans, use things with proper consideration; they do not bring them to ruin,' gave the Venerable Ānanda another five hundred cloths. Indeed, this was the first robe-alms that arose for the Venerable Ānanda: a thousand robes. Then the Venerable Ānanda went to Ghosita’s Park; having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the Venerable Channa went to where the Venerable Ānanda was; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, he sat down to one side. To the Venerable Channa, who was seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this: 'Friend Channa, the brahma-penalty has been imposed upon you by the Saṅgha.'

“Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, brahmadaṇḍo āṇāpito”ti? “Tvaṃ, āvuso channa, bhikkhū yaṃ iccheyyāsi taṃ vadeyyāsi. Bhikkhūhi tvaṃ neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, nānusāsitabbo”ti. “Nanvāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, hato ettāvatā, yatohaṃ bhikkhūhi neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, nānusāsitabbo”ti tattheva mucchito papato. Atha kho āyasmā channo [V 0.0461] brahmadaṇḍena aṭṭīyamāno harāyamāno jigucchamāno eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ [T 2.0394] brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā channo arahataṃ ahosi. Atha kho āyasmā channo arahattaṃ patto yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “paṭippassambhehi dāni me, bhante ānanda, brahmadaṇḍa”nti. “Yadaggena tayā, āvuso channa, arahattaṃ sacchikataṃ tadaggena te brahmadaṇḍo paṭippassaddho”ti. Imāya kho pana vinayasaṅgītiyā pañca bhikkhusatāni anūnāni anadhikāni ahesuṃ. Tasmā ayaṃ vinayasaṅgīti “pañcasatikā”ti vuccatīti.

“Venerable Ānanda, what then is the brahma-penalty?” “Friend Channa, you may say to the monks whatever you wish. You are not to be spoken to by the monks, not to be admonished, not to be instructed.” “Venerable Ānanda, by this much, am I not slain, in that I am not to be spoken to by the monks, not to be admonished, not to be instructed?” And right there he fainted and fell. Then the Venerable Channa, being tormented, ashamed, and disgusted by the brahma-penalty, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, with a mind directed to Nibbāna, before long, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, that supreme culmination of the holy life, he dwelt having realized it for himself with higher knowledge in this very life. He knew: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ And the Venerable Channa became one of the Arahants. Then the Venerable Channa, having attained Arahantship, approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Venerable Ānanda, now revoke the brahma-penalty for me.” “Friend Channa, from the day you realized Arahantship, from that day your brahma-penalty was revoked.” At this Vinaya recitation, there were five hundred monks, not less, not more. Therefore, this Vinaya recitation is called ‘the recitation of the five hundred’.”

Pañcasatikakkhandhako ekādasamo.

The Eleventh Chapter on the Five Hundred.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū tevīsati.

In this chapter, there are twenty-three topics.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Parinibbute [M 0.0490] sambuddhe, thero kassapasavhayo;

Āmantayi bhikkhugaṇaṃ, saddhammamanupālako;

Pāvāyaddhānamaggamhi, subhaddena paveditaṃ;

Saṅgāyissāma [P 2.0293] saddhammaṃ, adhammo pure dippati.

When the Fully Enlightened One had attained Parinibbāna, the Elder named Kassapa, protector of the good Dhamma, addressed the assembly of monks. On the long road from Pāvā, it was declared by Subhadda. Let us recite the good Dhamma before the false Dhamma shines forth.

Ekenūna pañcasataṃ, ānandampi ca uccini;

Dhammavinayasaṅgītiṃ, vasanto guhamuttame.

Five hundred less one, and Ānanda too, were chosen. Dwelling in the excellent cave, they made the recitation of the Dhamma and Vinaya.

Upāliṃ [T 2.0395] vinayaṃ pucchi, suttantānandapaṇḍitaṃ;

Piṭakaṃ tīṇi saṅgītiṃ, akaṃsu jinasāvakā.

They asked Upāli about the Vinaya; they asked the wise Ānanda about the Suttanta. The disciples of the Conqueror held the council for the three Piṭakas.

Na pucchi akkamitvāna, vandāpesi na yāci ca.

He did not ask; having stepped upon, he caused homage to be paid; and he did not request.

Pabbajjaṃ [V 0.0462] mātugāmassa, saddhāya dukkaṭāni me;

Purāṇo brahmadaṇḍañca, orodho udenena saha.

The going forth of women; my wrongdoings through faith; the elder Purāṇa and the brahma-penalty; the harem together with Udena.

Tāva bahu dubbalañca, uttarattharaṇā bhisi;

Bhūmattharaṇā puñchaniyo, rajo cikkhallamaddanā.

So many and weak robes; upper coverings and mattresses; ground coverings and wipers; a dust-cloth and the kneading of clay.

Sahassacīvaraṃ uppajji, paṭhamānandasavhayo;

Tajjito brahmadaṇḍena, catussaccaṃ apāpuṇi;

Vasībhūtā pañcasatā, tasmā pañcasatī iti.

A thousand robes arose for the first time for the one named Ānanda; threatened by the brahma-penalty, he attained the four truths. Five hundred had attained mastery; therefore, it is called the Council of the Five Hundred.

Pañcasatikakkhandhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter of the Five Hundred is concluded.

12. Sattasatikakkhandhakaṃ

12. The Chapter of the Seven Hundred

1. Paṭhamabhāṇavāro

1. The First Recitation Section

446. Tena [T 2.0396][P 2.0294][M 0.0491][V 0.0463] kho pana samayena vassasataparinibbute bhagavati vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū vesāliyaṃ dasa vatthūni dīpenti – kappati siṅgiloṇakappo, kappati dvaṅgulakappo, kappati gāmantarakappo, kappati āvāsakappo, kappati anumatikappo, kappati āciṇṇakappo, kappati amathitakappo, kappati jaḷogiṃ pātuṃ, kappati adasakaṃ nisīdanaṃ, kappati jātarūparajatanti.

446. At that time, when one hundred years had passed since the Blessed One’s Parinibbāna, the Vajjian monks from Vesālī made known ten points in Vesālī: the practice of storing salt in a horn is allowable; the practice of eating when the shadow is two fingers wide past noon is allowable; the practice concerning going to another village is allowable; the practice concerning residences is allowable; the practice concerning consent is allowable; the practice concerning custom is allowable; the practice of consuming milk that is not yet curd is allowable; it is allowable to drink toddy; a sitting-cloth without a border is allowable; gold and silver are allowable.

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vajjīsu cārikaṃ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū tadahuposathe kaṃsapātiṃ kaṃsacāṭiṃ (syā.) udakena pūretvā majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa ṭhapetvā āgatāgate vesālike upāsake evaṃ vadanti – “dethāvuso, saṅghassa kahāpaṇampi aḍḍhampi pādampi māsakarūpampi. Bhavissati saṅghassa parikkhārena karaṇīya”nti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vesālike upāsake etadavoca – “māvuso, adattha saṅghassa kahāpaṇampi aḍḍhampi pādampi māsakarūpampi. Na [T 2.0397] kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ; na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; na paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā”ti. Evampi kho vesālikā upāsakā āyasmatā yasena kākaṇḍakaputtena vuccamānā adaṃsuyeva saṅghassa kahāpaṇampi aḍḍhampi pādampi māsakarūpampi.

At that time, the Venerable Yasa, the son of the brahmin Kākaṇḍaka, was wandering on tour in the Vajjian country when he arrived at Vesālī. There, the Venerable Yasa, the son of the brahmin Kākaṇḍaka, stayed in Vesālī at the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. At that time, on the Uposatha day, the Vajjian monks of Vesālī filled a bronze bowl with water and placed it in the midst of the community of monks. As the lay followers of Vesālī arrived, they said, “Give, Sirs, a kahāpaṇa, half a kahāpaṇa, a quarter, or a māsaka coin to the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha will have a need for requisites.” When this was said, the Venerable Yasa, the son of the brahmin Kākaṇḍaka, addressed the lay followers of Vesālī: “Do not give, Sirs, a kahāpaṇa, half a kahāpaṇa, a quarter, or a māsaka coin to the Saṅgha. Gold and silver is not allowable for the Sakyan ascetics; the Sakyan ascetics do not consent to gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics do not receive gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics have rejected jewels and gold and are free from gold and silver.” Though the lay followers of Vesālī were spoken to thus by the Venerable Yasa, the son of the brahmin Kākaṇḍaka, they still gave a kahāpaṇa, half a kahāpaṇa, a quarter, or a māsaka coin to the Saṅgha.

Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū tassā rattiyā accayena taṃ hiraññaṃ bhikkhaggena bhikkhuggena (syā.) [V 0.0464] paṭivīsaṃ paṭiviṃsaṃ (sī.), paṭivisaṃ (syā.) ṭhapetvā bhājesuṃ. Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ yasaṃ kākaṇḍakaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “eso [P 2.0295] te, āvuso yasa, hiraññassa paṭivīso”ti. “Natthi, me āvuso, hiraññassa paṭivīso, nāhaṃ hiraññaṃ sādiyāmī”ti. Atha [M 0.0492] kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū – “ayaṃ āvuso yaso kākaṇḍakaputto upāsake saddhe pasanne akkosati, paribhāsati, appasādaṃ karoti; handassa mayaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karomā”ti te. Tassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ akaṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vesālike vajjiputtake bhikkhū etadavoca – “bhagavatā, āvuso, paññattaṃ – ‘paṭisāraṇīyakammakatassa bhikkhuno anudūto dātabbo’ti. Detha me, āvuso, anudūtaṃ bhikkhu”nti.

Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī, when that night had passed, distributed that gold, setting aside a share for each monk. Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī said this to the Venerable Yasa, the son of Kākaṇḍaka: “Friend Yasa, this is your share of the gold.” “Friends, I have no share of the gold; I do not consent to gold.” Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī said: “Friends, this Yasa, the son of Kākaṇḍaka, reviles and abuses the faithful, devoted lay followers, and causes them displeasure. Come, let us carry out the act of reconciliation against him.” They carried out the act of reconciliation against him. Then the Venerable Yasa, the son of Kākaṇḍaka, said this to the Vajjian monks of Vesālī: “Friends, it has been laid down by the Blessed One: ‘An escort monk is to be given to a monk upon whom the act of reconciliation has been carried out.’ Friends, give me an escort monk.”

Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ sammannitvā āyasmato yasassa kākaṇḍakaputtassa anudūtaṃ adaṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto [T 2.0398] anudūtena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vesāliṃ pavisitvā vesālike upāsake etadavoca – “ahaṃ kirāyasmante upāsake saddhe pasanne akkosāmi, paribhāsāmi, appasādaṃ karomi; yohaṃ adhammaṃ adhammoti vadāmi, dhammaṃ dhammoti vadāmi, avinayaṃ avinayoti vadāmi, vinayaṃ vinayoti vadāmi.

Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī, having appointed a monk, gave him as an escort monk to the Venerable Yasa, the son of Kākaṇḍaka. Then the Venerable Yasa, the son of Kākaṇḍaka, together with the escort monk, entered Vesālī and said this to the lay followers of Vesālī: “It is said that I revile, abuse, and cause displeasure to the venerable lay followers, who are faithful and devoted; I who declare what is not the Dhamma as ‘not the Dhamma’ and the Dhamma as ‘the Dhamma,’ what is not the Discipline as ‘not the Discipline’ and the Discipline as ‘the Discipline.’”

447. “Ekamidaṃ, āvuso, samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho, āvuso, bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – a. ni. 4.50 ‘cattārome, bhikkhave, candimasūriyānaṃ upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhā candimasūriyā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Katame cattāro? Abbhaṃ, bhikkhave, candimasūriyānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā candimasūriyā na tapanti, na bhāsanti na virocanti. Mahikā, bhikkhave, candimasūriyānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā candimasūriyā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti, dhūmarajo, bhikkhave, candimasūriyānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā candimasūriyā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Rāhu, bhikkhave, asurindo candimasūriyānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā candimasūriyā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro candimasūriyānaṃ upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhā candimasūriyā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cattārome samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ [T 2.0399] upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Katame cattāro? Santi, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā [V 0.0465] suraṃ pivanti, merayaṃ pivanti, surāmerayapānā appaṭiviratā – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā na [M 0.0493] tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā methunaṃ [P 2.0296] dhammaṃ paṭisevanti, methunadhammā appaṭiviratā – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyo samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā jātarūparajataṃ sādiyanti, jātarūparajatappaṭiggahaṇā appaṭiviratā – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyo samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā micchājīvena jīvitaṃ kappenti; micchājīvā appaṭiviratā – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, catuttho samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapanti, na bhāsanti, na virocanti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapanti, na bhāsanti[T 2.0400], na virocanti’. “Idamavocāvuso, bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

447. “At one time, friends, the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There, friends, the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Monks, there are these four defilements of the moon and sun, by which, being defiled, the moon and sun do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. What are the four? Clouds, monks, are a defilement of the moon and sun, by which defilement, being defiled, the moon and sun do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. Frost, monks, is a defilement of the moon and sun, by which defilement, being defiled, the moon and sun do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. Smoke and dust, monks, are a defilement of the moon and sun, by which defilement, being defiled, the moon and sun do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. Rāhu, the lord of the asuras, monks, is a defilement of the moon and sun, by which defilement, being defiled, the moon and sun do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. These, monks, are the four defilements of the moon and sun, by which, being defiled, the moon and sun do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. In the very same way, monks, there are these four defilements of ascetics and brahmins, by which, being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. What are the four? There are, monks, some ascetics and brahmins who drink liquor and intoxicants, and do not abstain from drinking liquor and intoxicants—this, monks, is the first defilement of ascetics and brahmins, by which defilement, being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. Furthermore, monks, there are some ascetics and brahmins who engage in sexual intercourse, and do not abstain from sexual intercourse—this, monks, is the second defilement of ascetics and brahmins, by which defilement, being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. Furthermore, monks, there are some ascetics and brahmins who consent to gold and silver, and do not abstain from the acceptance of gold and silver—this, monks, is the third defilement of ascetics and brahmins, by which defilement, being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. Furthermore, monks, there are some ascetics and brahmins who make their living by wrong livelihood, and do not abstain from wrong livelihood—this, monks, is the fourth defilement of ascetics and brahmins, by which defilement, being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate. These, monks, are the four defilements of ascetics and brahmins, by which, being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not shine, do not blaze, and do not radiate.’ This, friends, is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Rāgadosaparikliṭṭhā, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā;

Avijjānivuṭā avijjānīvutā (syā.) posā, piyarūpābhinandino.

“Some ascetics and brahmins, afflicted by lust and hatred, beings veiled by ignorance, delight in agreeable forms.

“Suraṃ pivanti merayaṃ, paṭisevanti methunaṃ;

Rajataṃ jātarūpañca, sādiyanti aviddasū.

They drink liquor and intoxicants, they engage in sexual intercourse; the unwise consent to silver and gold.

“Micchājīvena jīvanti, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā;

Ete upakkilesā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

Some ascetics and brahmins make a living by wrong livelihood; these defilements were spoken of by the Buddha, kinsman of the sun.

“Yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhā, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā;

Na tapanti na bhāsanti, asuddhā sarajā magā.

Defiled by these defilements, some ascetics and brahmins neither shine nor glow; they are impure, dusty, like wild deer.

“Andhakārena onaddhā, taṇhādāsā sanettikā;

Vaḍḍhenti kaṭasiṃ ghoraṃ, ādiyanti punabbhavanti.

Bound by darkness, slaves to craving, with craving as their guide, they increase the dreadful charnel ground and take up renewed existence.”

“Evaṃvādī [M 0.0494][V 0.0466] kirāhaṃ āyasmante upāsake saddhe pasanne akkosāmi, paribhāsāmi, appasādaṃ karomi; yohaṃ adhammaṃ adhammoti vadāmi, dhammaṃ dhammoti vadāmi, avinayaṃ avinayoti vadāmi, vinayaṃ vinayoti vadāmi.

Speaking thus, it is said that I revile and abuse the faithful, devoted, venerable lay followers, and cause them displeasure—I who say that what is not the Dhamma is not the Dhamma, that the Dhamma is the Dhamma, that what is not the Vinaya is not the Vinaya, and that the Vinaya is the Vinaya.

448. saṃ. ni. 4.362 idaṃ vatthu āgataṃ “Ekamidaṃ, āvuso, samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena rājantepure rājaparisāyaṃ sannisinnānaṃ [T 2.0401] sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarakathā udapādi – ‘kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ; sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajata’nti. Tena kho panāvuso samayena, maṇicūḷako gāmaṇī tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho, āvuso, maṇicūḷako gāmaṇī taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – ‘mā ayyā evaṃ avacuttha. Na kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ; na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; na paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā [P 2.0297] samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā’ti. Asakkhi kho, āvuso, maṇicūḷako gāmaṇī taṃ parisaṃ saññāpetuṃ.

448. On one occasion, friends, the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary. At that time, in the royal palace, this topic of conversation arose among the royal assembly who were sitting together: ‘Gold and silver is allowable for the Sakyan ascetics; the Sakyan ascetics consent to gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics accept gold and silver.’ At that time, friends, the headman Maṇicūḷaka was sitting in that assembly. Then, friends, the headman Maṇicūḷaka said this to that assembly: ‘Do not say this, sirs. Gold and silver is not allowable for the Sakyan ascetics; the Sakyan ascetics do not consent to gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics do not accept gold and silver. The Sakyan ascetics have put aside gems and gold; they are rid of gold and silver.’ The headman Maṇicūḷaka, friends, was able to convince that assembly.

“Atha kho, āvuso, maṇicūḷako gāmaṇī taṃ parisaṃ saññāpetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, āvuso, maṇicūḷako gāmaṇī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘idha, bhante, rājantepure rājaparisāyaṃ sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarakathā udapādi – kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ; sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajatanti. Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ bhante, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – mā ayyā evaṃ avacuttha. Na kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ; na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ[T 2.0402]; na paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatāti. Asakkhiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ parisaṃ saññāpetuṃ. Kaccāhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva bhagavato homi, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāmi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaromi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’ti? ‘Taggha tvaṃ, gāmaṇi, evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me hosi; na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhasi [M 0.0495] pārā. 582, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarosi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati. Na hi, gāmaṇi, kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ; na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā [V 0.0467] jātarūparajataṃ; na paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ; nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā. Yassa kho, gāmaṇi, jātarūparajataṃ kappati, pañcapi tassa kāmaguṇā kappanti. Yassa pañca kāmaguṇā kappanti ekaṃsenetaṃ, gāmaṇi, dhāreyyāsi – assamaṇadhammo asakyaputtiyadhammoti. Api cāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, evaṃ vadāmi tiṇaṃ tiṇatthikena pariyesitabbaṃ; dāru dārutthikena pariyesitabbaṃ; sakaṭaṃ sakaṭatthikena pariyesitabbaṃ; puriso purisatthikena pariyesitabbo. Na tvevāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, kenaci pariyāyena jātarūparajataṃ sāditabbaṃ pariyesitabbanti [T 2.0403] vadāmī’ti.

Then the headman Maṇicūḷaka, having informed that assembly, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the headman Maṇicūḷaka said to the Blessed One: ‘Here, venerable sir, in the royal palace, among the assembled royal council, this discussion arose: “It is allowable for the Sakyan ascetics; the Sakyan ascetics consent to gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics accept gold and silver.” When this was said, venerable sir, I addressed that assembly thus: “Do not say so, sirs. It is not allowable for the Sakyan ascetics; the Sakyan ascetics do not consent to gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics do not accept gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics have laid aside gems and gold, they are rid of gold and silver.” Venerable sir, I was able to convince that assembly. Am I, venerable sir, speaking in accordance with the Blessed One’s teaching when I declare thus, not misrepresenting the Blessed One with falsehood, explaining the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and in such a way that no principled statement and counter-statement provides grounds for censure?’ ‘Indeed, headman, when you declare thus, you are speaking in accordance with my teaching, not misrepresenting me with falsehood, explaining the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and in such a way that no principled statement and counter-statement provides grounds for censure. Indeed, headman, it is not allowable for the Sakyan ascetics; they do not consent to gold and silver; they do not accept gold and silver; the Sakyan ascetics have laid aside gems and gold, they are rid of gold and silver. Headman, for whom gold and silver are allowable, for him the five strands of sensual pleasure are also allowable. For whom the five strands of sensual pleasure are allowable, you can be certain of this, headman: “This is not the practice of a recluse, not the practice of a son of the Sakyan.” Moreover, headman, I say this: grass should be sought by one who needs grass; wood should be sought by one who needs wood; a cart should be sought by one who needs a cart; a person should be sought by one who needs a person. But in no way, headman, do I say that gold and silver should be consented to or sought.’

“Evaṃvādī kirāhaṃ āyasmante upāsake saddhe pasanne akkosāmi, paribhāsāmi, appasādaṃ karomi; yohaṃ adhammaṃ adhammoti vadāmi, dhammaṃ dhammoti vadāmi, avinayaṃ avinayoti vadāmi, vinayaṃ vinayoti vadāmi.

Speaking thus, do I indeed revile and abuse the faithful and devoted venerable lay followers, and cause them displeasure—I who declare what is not the Dhamma as 'not the Dhamma,' the Dhamma as 'the Dhamma,' what is not the Vinaya as 'not the Vinaya,' and the Vinaya as 'the Vinaya'?

449. “Ekamidaṃ, āvuso, samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha jātarūparajataṃ paṭikkhipi, sikkhāpadañca paññapesi. Evaṃvādī kirāhaṃ āyasmante upāsake saddhe pasanne akkosāmi, paribhāsāmi, appasādaṃ karomi; yohaṃ adhammaṃ [P 2.0298] adhammoti vadāmi, dhammaṃ dhammoti vadāmi, avinayaṃ avinayoti vadāmi, vinayaṃ vinayoti vadāmī”ti.

449. Friends, at one time in Rājagaha, the Blessed One, on account of the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, prohibited gold and silver and also laid down a training rule. Speaking thus, do I indeed revile and abuse the faithful and devoted venerable lay followers, and cause them displeasure—I who declare what is not the Dhamma as 'not the Dhamma,' the Dhamma as 'the Dhamma,' what is not the Vinaya as 'not the Vinaya,' and the Vinaya as 'the Vinaya'?

Evaṃ vutte vesālikā upāsakā āyasmantaṃ yasaṃ kākaṇḍakaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ekova bhante, ayyo yaso kākaṇḍakaputto samaṇo sakyaputtiyo. Sabbevime assamaṇā asakyaputtiyā. Vasatu, bhante, ayyo yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vesāliyaṃ. Mayaṃ ayyassa yasassa kākaṇḍakaputtassa ussukkaṃ karissāma cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna”nti. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vesālike upāsake saññāpetvā anudūtena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ārāmaṃ agamāsi.

When this was said, the lay followers of Vesālī said this to the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta: ‘Venerable sir, only the noble Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta is a Sakyan ascetic. All these others are not Sakyan ascetics. Let the noble Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta stay in Vesālī, venerable sir. We will be zealous in providing the noble Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta with robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick.’ Then, having informed the lay followers of Vesālī, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta went to the monastery with the messenger monk.

Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū anudūtaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchiṃsu – “khamāpitāvuso, yasena kākaṇḍakaputtena vesālikā upāsakā”ti[T 2.0404][M 0.0496]? “Upāsakehi pāpikaṃ no, āvuso, kataṃ. Ekova yaso kākaṇḍakaputto samaṇo sakyaputtiyo kato. Sabbeva mayaṃ assamaṇā asakyaputtiyā katā”ti. Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū – “ayaṃ, āvuso, yaso kākaṇḍakaputto amhehi asammato gihīnaṃ pakāsesi; handassa mayaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ [V 0.0468] karomā”ti. Te tassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kattukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā kosambiyaṃ paccuṭṭhāsi.

Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī asked the accompanying messenger monk: “Friend, have the lay followers of Vesālī been reconciled by Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta?” “Friends, the lay followers have done us wrong. Only Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta has been made out to be a recluse, a son of the Sakyan. All of us have been made out to be non-recluses, not sons of the Sakyan.” Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī said: “Friends, this Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, without being authorized by us, has revealed this to the laity. Come, let us perform the act of suspension against him.” Wishing to perform the act of suspension against him, they assembled. Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, having risen up into the air, established himself in Kosambī.

450. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto pāveyyakānañca pāṭheyyakānañca (syā.) avantidakkhiṇāpathakānañca bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “āgacchantu āyasmantā; imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ādiyissāma. Pure adhammo dippati, dhammo paṭibāhiyyati; avinayo dippati, vinayo paṭibāhiyyati; pure adhammavādino balavanto honti, dhammavādino dubbalā honti; avinayavādino balavanto honti, vinayavādino dubbalā hontī”ti.

450. Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta sent a messenger to the monks of Pāveyyaka and of Avanti-Dakkhiṇāpatha, saying: “May the venerable sirs come; let us take up this legal question. Before the non-Dhamma shines forth and the Dhamma is obstructed; before the non-Vinaya shines forth and the Vinaya is obstructed; before the speakers of non-Dhamma become powerful and the speakers of Dhamma become weak; before the speakers of non-Vinaya become powerful and the speakers of Vinaya become weak.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī ahogaṅge pabbate paṭivasati. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto yena ahogaṅgo pabbato, yenāyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sambhūtaṃ sāṇavāsiṃ [T 2.0405] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto āyasmantaṃ sambhūtaṃ sāṇavāsiṃ etadavoca – “ime, bhante, vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū vesāliyaṃ dasa vatthūni dīpenti – kappati siṅgiloṇakappo, kappati dvaṅgulakappo, kappati gāmantarakappo, kappati āvāsakappo, kappati anumatikappo, kappati āciṇṇakappo, kappati amathitakappo, kappati jaḷogiṃ pātuṃ, kappati adasakaṃ nisīdanaṃ, kappati jātarūparajatanti. Handa [P 2.0299] mayaṃ, bhante, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ādiyissāma. Pure adhammo dippati, dhammo paṭibāhiyyati; avinayo dippati, vinayo paṭibāhiyyati; pure adhammavādino balavanto honti, dhammavādino dubbalā honti; avinayavādino balavanto honti, vinayavādino dubbalā hontī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī āyasmato yasassa kākaṇḍakaputtassa paccassosi. Atha [M 0.0497] kho saṭṭhimattā pāveyyakā bhikkhū – sabbe āraññikā, sabbe piṇḍapātikā, sabbe paṃsukūlikā, sabbe tecīvarikā, sabbeva arahanto – ahogaṅge pabbate sannipatiṃsu. Aṭṭhāsītimattā avantidakkhiṇāpathakā bhikkhū – appekacce āraññikā, appekacce piṇḍapātikā, appekacce paṃsukūlikā, appekacce tecīvarikā, sabbeva arahanto – ahogaṅge pabbate sannipatiṃsu. Atha [T 2.0406] kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mantayamānānaṃ etadahosi – “idaṃ kho adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷañca, vāḷañca; kaṃ nu kho mayaṃ pakkhaṃ labheyyāma, yena mayaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe balavantatarā assāmā”ti.

Now at that time, the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī was dwelling on Mount Ahogaṅga. Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta went to where Mount Ahogaṅga was, to where the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī was, and approached him. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta said this to the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī: “Venerable sir, these Vajjiputtaka monks of Vesālī are proclaiming ten points in Vesālī: it is allowable to store salt in a horn; it is allowable to eat when the shadow is two finger-breadths past noon; it is allowable to eat again in another village after having set out; it is allowable to hold separate Uposatha ceremonies within the same monastic boundary; it is allowable to carry out an act and seek consent for it afterward; it is allowable to follow the practice of one’s preceptors; it is allowable to consume partially-curdled milk; it is allowable to drink palm-toddy; it is allowable to use a sitting cloth without a border; it is allowable to accept gold and silver. Come, venerable sir, let us take up this legal question before the non-Dhamma shines forth and the Dhamma is obstructed; before the non-Vinaya shines forth and the Vinaya is obstructed; before those who speak non-Dhamma become strong and those who speak Dhamma become weak; before those who speak non-Vinaya become strong and those who speak Vinaya become weak.” “Very well, friend,” the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī consented to the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta. Then sixty monks from Pāveyya—all forest-dwellers, all alms-food eaters, all rag-robe wearers, all triple-robe wearers, all of them arahants—assembled on Mount Ahogaṅga. Eighty-eight monks from Avanti and the Southern Region—some forest-dwellers, some alms-food eaters, some rag-robe wearers, some triple-robe wearers, all of them arahants—assembled on Mount Ahogaṅga. Then, as the elder monks were conferring, this thought occurred to them: “This legal question is indeed harsh and fierce. What faction might we obtain, by which we would be stronger in this legal question?”

451. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā revato soreyye paṭivasati – bahussuto āgatāgamo [V 0.0469] dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Atha kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā revato soreyye paṭivasati – bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Sace mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pakkhaṃ labhissāma, evaṃ mayaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe balavantatarā assāmā”ti. Assosi kho āyasmā revato – dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya – therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mantayamānānaṃ. Sutvānassa etadahosi – “idaṃ kho adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷañca vāḷañca. Na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ yohaṃ evarūpe adhikaraṇe osakkeyyaṃ. Idāni ca pana te bhikkhū āgacchissanti. Sohaṃ tehi ākiṇṇo na phāsu gamissāmi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ paṭikacceva gaccheyya”nti. Atha kho āyasmā revato soreyyā saṅkassaṃ agamāsi.

451. Now at that time, the Venerable Revata was dwelling at Soreyya—learned, one who has mastered the traditions, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikās, wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and eager for training. Then this thought occurred to the elder monks: “This Venerable Revata is dwelling at Soreyya—learned, one who has mastered the traditions, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikās, wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and eager for training. If we can gain the Venerable Revata’s support, we will be much stronger in this legal question.” The Venerable Revata heard—with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human—the elder monks deliberating. Having heard, this thought occurred to him: “This legal question is indeed harsh and fierce. It is not proper for me that I should shrink back from such a legal question. But now those monks will come. And I, being crowded by them, will not be able to proceed at ease. What if I were to go beforehand?” Then the Venerable Revata went from Soreyya to Saṅkassa.

Atha kho therā bhikkhū soreyyaṃ gantvā pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ āyasmā revato”ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – “esāyasmā revato saṅkassaṃ [T 2.0407] gato”ti. Atha kho āyasmā revato saṅkassā kaṇṇakujjaṃ kannakujjaṃ (sī.) agamāsi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū saṅkassaṃ gantvā pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ āyasmā revato”ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – “esāyasmā revato kaṇṇakujjaṃ gato”ti. Atha kho āyasmā revato kaṇṇakujjā udumbaraṃ [M 0.0498] agamāsi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū kaṇṇakujjaṃ gantvā pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ āyasmā revato”ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – “esāyasmā revato udumbaraṃ gato”ti. Atha [P 2.0300] kho āyasmā revato udumbarā aggaḷapuraṃ agamāsi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū udumbaraṃ gantvā pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ āyasmā revato”ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – “esāyasmā revato aggaḷapuraṃ gato”ti. Atha kho āyasmā revato aggaḷapurā sahajātiṃ sahaṃjātiṃ (ka.) agamāsi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū aggaḷapuraṃ gantvā pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ āyasmā revato”ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – “esāyasmā revato sahajātiṃ gato”ti. Atha kho therā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ revataṃ sahajātiyaṃ sambhāvesuṃ.

Then the elder monks, having gone to Soreyya, asked, “Where is the Venerable Revata?” They said, “This Venerable Revata has gone to Saṅkassa.” Then the Venerable Revata went from Saṅkassa to Kaṇṇakujja. Then the elder monks, having gone to Saṅkassa, asked, “Where is the Venerable Revata?” They said, “This Venerable Revata has gone to Kaṇṇakujja.” Then the Venerable Revata went from Kaṇṇakujja to Udumbara. Then the elder monks, having gone to Kaṇṇakujja, asked, “Where is the Venerable Revata?” They said, “This Venerable Revata has gone to Udumbara.” Then the Venerable Revata went from Udumbara to Aggaḷapura. Then the elder monks, having gone to Udumbara, asked, “Where is the Venerable Revata?” They said, “This Venerable Revata has gone to Aggaḷapura.” Then the Venerable Revata went from Aggaḷapura to Sahajāti. Then the elder monks, having gone to Aggaḷapura, asked, “Where is the Venerable Revata?” They said, “This Venerable Revata has gone to Sahajāti.” Then the elder monks met the Venerable Revata in Sahajāti.

452. Atha kho āyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī āyasmantaṃ yasaṃ kākaṇḍakaputtaṃ etadavoca – “ayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmā revato bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Sace mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pañhaṃ pucchissāma, paṭibalo āyasmā revato ekeneva pañhena sakalampi rattiṃ vītināmetuṃ. Idāni ca panāyasmā revato [T 2.0408] antevāsikaṃ antevāsiṃ (syā.) sarabhāṇakaṃ bhikkhuṃ ajjhesissati. So tvaṃ tassa bhikkhuno sarabhaññapariyosāne āyasmantaṃ revataṃ upasaṅkamitvā imāni [V 0.0470] dasa vatthūni puccheyyāsī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto āyasmato sambhūtassa sāṇavāsissa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā revato antevāsikaṃ sarabhāṇakaṃ bhikkhuṃ ajjhesi. Atha kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto tassa bhikkhuno sarabhaññapariyosāne yenāyasmā revato tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ revataṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca – “kappati, bhante, siṅgiloṇakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, siṅgiloṇakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, siṅginā loṇaṃ pariharituṃ – yattha aloṇakaṃ bhavissati tattha paribhuñjissāmī”ti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, dvaṅgulakappo”ti[M 0.0499]? “Ko so, āvuso, dvaṅgulakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, dvaṅgulāya chāyāya vītivattāya, vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjitu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, gāmantarakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, gāmantarakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante – idāni gāmantaraṃ gamissāmīti – bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjitu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, āvāsakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, āvāsakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, sambahulā āvāsā samānasīmā nānuposathaṃ kātu”nti? “Nāvuso[T 2.0409], kappatī”ti. “Kappati[P 2.0301], bhante, anumatikappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, anumatikappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, vaggena saṅghena kammaṃ kātuṃ – āgate bhikkhū anumānessāmā”ti anujānissāmāti, anujānessāmāti, anumatiṃ ānessāmāti (ka.)? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, āciṇṇakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, āciṇṇakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, idaṃ me upajjhāyena ajjhāciṇṇaṃ, idaṃ me ācariyena ajjhāciṇṇaṃ, taṃ ajjhācaritu”nti? “Āciṇṇakappo kho, āvuso, ekacco kappati, ekacco na kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, amathitakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, amathitakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, yaṃ taṃ khīraṃ khīrabhāvaṃ vijahitaṃ, asampattaṃ dadhibhāvaṃ, taṃ bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ pātu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti? “Kappati, bhante, jaḷogiṃ pātu”nti? “Kā sā, āvuso, jaḷogī”ti? “Kappati, bhante, yā sā surā āsutā, asampattā majjabhāvaṃ, sā pātu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, adasakaṃ nisīdana”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Kappati, bhante, jātarūparajata”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. “Ime, bhante, vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū vesāliyaṃ imāni dasa vatthūni dīpenti. Handa mayaṃ, bhante, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ādiyissāma. Pure adhammo dippati, dhammo paṭibāhiyyati; avinayo [T 2.0410] dippati, vinayo paṭibāhiyyati; pure adhammavādino balavanto honti, dhammavādino dubbalā [V 0.0471] honti; avinayavādino balavanto honti, vinayavādino dubbalā hontī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā revato āyasmato yasassa kākaṇḍakaputtassa paccassosi.

452. Then the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī said to the Venerable Yasa, son of Kākaṇḍaka: 'Friend, this Venerable Revata is of great learning, has mastered the transmitted scriptures, is a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikās, wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training. If we were to ask the Venerable Revata a question, he is capable of spending the entire night on just one question. And now the Venerable Revata will request a reciting monk, his resident pupil. You, when that monk has finished his recitation, should approach the Venerable Revata and ask about these ten points.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' replied the Venerable Yasa, son of Kākaṇḍaka, in assent to the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī. Then the Venerable Revata requested a reciting monk, his resident pupil. Then, at the conclusion of that monk's recitation, the Venerable Yasa, son of Kākaṇḍaka, approached the Venerable Revata, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Yasa, son of Kākaṇḍaka, said to the Venerable Revata: 'Venerable sir, is the salt-in-horn practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the salt-in-horn practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable to carry salt in a horn, thinking: "Where there is no salt, I will partake there"?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is the two-finger practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the two-finger practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable to eat a meal at an unseasonable time, when the shadow has passed two finger-breadths?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is the village-to-village practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the village-to-village practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable for one who has finished eating and has refused more food, thinking, "I will now go to another village," to eat food that has not been made a leftover?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is the residence practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the residence practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable for many residences within the same boundary to perform separate Uposatha ceremonies?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is the approval practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the approval practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable for an incomplete assembly of the Saṅgha to perform a formal act, thinking: "We will obtain the approval of the monks when they arrive"?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is the habitual practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the habitual practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable to practice that which was habitually practiced by my preceptor and that which was habitually practiced by my teacher?' 'Friend, some habitual practices are allowable, some are not.' 'Venerable sir, is the unchurned practice allowable?' 'What, friend, is the unchurned practice?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable for one who has finished eating and has refused more food to drink, without it having been made a leftover, that which has left the state of milk but has not yet reached the state of curds?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink fermented liquor?' 'What, friend, is fermented liquor?' 'Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink that alcoholic beverage which has been brewed but has not yet reached the state of an intoxicant?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is a sitting cloth without a border allowable?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, is gold and silver allowable?' 'No, friend, it is not allowable.' 'Venerable sir, these Vajjian monks of Vesālī proclaim these ten points in Vesālī.
