Come, venerable sir, let us take up this issue, before what is contrary to the Dhamma prevails and the Dhamma is suppressed; before what is contrary to the Vinaya prevails and the Vinaya is suppressed; before the proponents of non-Dhamma become strong and the proponents of Dhamma become weak; before the proponents of non-Vinaya become strong and the proponents of Vinaya become weak.' 'Yes, friend,' replied the Venerable Revata in assent to the Venerable Yasa, son of Kākaṇḍaka.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is finished.

2. Dutiyabhāṇavāro

2. The Second Recitation Section

453. Assosuṃ [M 0.0500] kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū – “yaso kira kākaṇḍakaputto idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ādiyitukāmo pakkhaṃ pariyesati, labhati ca kira pakkha”nti. Atha kho vesālikānaṃ vajjiputtakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “idaṃ kho adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷañca vāḷañca. Kaṃ nu kho mayaṃ pakkhaṃ labheyyāma, yena mayaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe balavantatarā assāmā”ti.

453. The Vajjian monks of Vesālī heard: 'It is said that Yasa, son of Kākaṇḍaka, desiring to take up this legal issue, seeks a faction, and it is said that he is also obtaining a faction.' Then this thought occurred to the Vajjian monks of Vesālī: 'Indeed, this legal issue is harsh and fierce. What faction might we obtain, by which we might become more powerful in this legal issue?'

Atha kho vesālikānaṃ vajjiputtakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā revato bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Sace mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pakkhaṃ labheyyāma, evaṃ mayaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe balavantatarā assāmā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to the Vajjian monks of Vesālī: 'Indeed, this Venerable Revata is of great learning, has the transmitted scriptures, is a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikās, is wise, clever, intelligent, modest, scrupulous, and desirous of the training. If we were to obtain Venerable Revata for our faction, thus we would be more powerful in this legal issue.'

Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū pahūtaṃ sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ paṭiyādesuṃ – pattampi, cīvarampi, nisīdanampi, sūcigharampi, kāyabandhanampi, parissāvanampi, dhammakaraṇampi. Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū taṃ sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ ādāya nāvāya sahajātiṃ ujjaviṃsu; nāvāya paccorohitvā [P 2.0302] aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle [T 2.0411] bhattavissaggaṃ karonti. Atha kho āyasmato sāḷhassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “ke nu kho dhammavādino – pācīnakā vā bhikkhū, pāveyyakā vā”ti? Atha kho āyasmato sāḷhassa, dhammañca vinayañca cetasā paccavekkhantassa, etadahosi – “adhammavādino pācīnakā bhikkhū, dhammavādino pāveyyakā pāṭheyyakā (syā.) bhikkhū”ti.

Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī prepared abundant requisites for ascetics—a bowl, a robe, a sitting cloth, a needle case, a belt, a water strainer, and a Dhamma-filter. Taking those requisites for ascetics, the Vajjian monks of Vesālī went upstream by boat to Sahajāti. Having disembarked from the boat, they took their meal at the foot of a certain tree. Then, to the Venerable Sāḷha, who had gone to a secluded place and was dwelling in solitude, this thought arose in his mind: 'Who, indeed, are the speakers of the Dhamma—the monks of the East, or the monks of Pāveyya?' Then, as the Venerable Sāḷha was reflecting on the Dhamma and the Vinaya with his mind, it occurred to him: 'The monks of the East are speakers of non-Dhamma; the monks of Pāveyya are speakers of the Dhamma.'

Atha kho aññatarā suddhāvāsakāyikā devatā āyasmato sāḷhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ sammiñjeyya, evameva suddhāvāsesu devesu antarahitā – āyasmato sāḷhassa [V 0.0472] sammukhe pāturahosi. Atha kho sā devatā āyasmantaṃ sāḷhaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante sāḷha, adhammavādī pācīnakā bhikkhū, dhammavādī pāveyyakā bhikkhū. Tena hi, bhante sāḷha, yathādhammo tathā tiṭṭhāhī”ti. “Pubbepi cāhaṃ, devate, etarahi ca yathādhammo tathā ṭhito[M 0.0501]; api cāhaṃ na tāva diṭṭhiṃ āvi karomi, appeva nāma maṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe sammanneyyā”ti.

Then a certain deity of the Pure Abodes, knowing with her mind the thought in the Venerable Sāḷha’s mind—just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm, or bend his stretched-out arm—so too did she disappear from among the devas of the Pure Abodes and appear in the presence of the Venerable Sāḷha. Then that deity said this to the Venerable Sāḷha: “It is good, Venerable Sāḷha. The monks of the East are speakers of non-Dhamma; the monks of Pāveyya are speakers of Dhamma. Therefore, Venerable Sāḷha, stand as the Dhamma is.” “Deity, both previously and now, I stand as the Dhamma is. However, I do not yet make my view apparent; it may be that they will appoint me in this dispute.”

454. Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū taṃ sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ ādāya yenāyasmā revato tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavocuṃ – “paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, thero sāmaṇakaṃ [T 2.0412] parikkhāraṃ – pattampi, cīvarampi, nisīdanampi, sūcigharampi, kāyabandhanampi, parissāvanampi, dhammakaraṇampī”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, paripuṇṇaṃ me pattacīvara”nti na icchi paṭiggahetuṃ.

454. Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī, taking those monastic requisites, approached the Venerable Revata. Having approached, they said this to the Venerable Revata: “Venerable sir, may the Elder accept the monastic requisites: the bowl, the robe, the sitting-cloth, the needle-case, the waistband, the water-strainer, and the water pot.” Saying, “Enough, friends, my bowl and robe are complete,” he did not wish to accept them.

Tena kho pana samayena uttaro nāma bhikkhu vīsativasso āyasmato revatassa upaṭṭhāko hoti. Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū yenāyasmā uttaro tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ uttaraṃ etadavocuṃ – “paṭiggaṇhātu āyasmā uttaro sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ – pattampi, cīvarampi, nisīdanampi, sūcigharampi, kāyabandhanampi, parissāvanampi, dhammakaraṇampī”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, paripuṇṇaṃ me pattacīvara”nti na icchi paṭiggahetuṃ. “Manussā kho, āvuso uttara, bhagavato sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ upanāmenti. Sace bhagavā paṭiggaṇhāti, teneva te attamanā honti. No ce bhagavā paṭiggaṇhāti, āyasmato āyasmato ca (syā.) ānandassa upanāmenti – paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, thero sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ. Yathā bhagavatā paṭiggahito, evameva so bhavissatīti. Paṭiggaṇhātu āyasmā uttaro sāmaṇakaṃ [P 2.0303] parikkhāraṃ. Yathā therena paṭiggahito, evameva so bhavissatī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā uttaro vesālikehi vajjiputtehi bhikkhūhi nippīḷiyamāno ekaṃ cīvaraṃ aggahesi. “Vadeyyātha, āvuso, yena attho”ti. “Ettakaṃ āyasmā uttaro theraṃ [T 2.0413] vadetu; ettakañca, bhante, thero saṅghamajjhe vadetu – ‘puratthimesu janapadesu buddhā bhagavanto uppajjanti. Dhammavādī pācīnakā bhikkhū, adhammavādī pāveyyakā bhikkhū’”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā uttaro vesālikānaṃ vajjiputtakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭissutvā yenāyasmā revato tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca – “ettakaṃ, bhante, thero saṅghamajjhe vadetu – ‘puratthimesu janapadesu buddhā bhagavanto uppajjanti[M 0.0502]. Dhammavādī pācīnakā bhikkhū, adhammavādī [V 0.0473] pāveyyakā bhikkhū’”ti. “Adhamme maṃ tvaṃ, bhikkhu, niyojesī”ti thero āyasmantaṃ uttaraṃ paṇāmesi.

At that time, a monk named Uttara, with twenty years of seniority, was the attendant of the Venerable Revata. Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī approached the Venerable Uttara. Having approached, they said to him: 'Venerable Uttara, please accept the monastic requisites—a bowl, a robe, a sitting-cloth, a needle-case, a waistband, a water-strainer, and a water pot.' 'Enough, friends, my bowl and robe are complete,' he said, not wishing to accept them. 'Venerable Uttara, people offer monastic requisites to the Blessed One. If the Blessed One accepts them, they are pleased by that. If the Blessed One does not accept them, they offer them to the Venerable Ānanda, saying: "Venerable sir, may the Elder accept the monastic requisites. As it is accepted by the Blessed One, so shall it be." Venerable Uttara, please accept the monastic requisites. As it is accepted by the Elder, so shall it be.' Then, being pressured by the Vajjian monks of Vesālī, the Venerable Uttara accepted one robe and said, 'Friends, say what is needed.' They said: 'Let the Venerable Uttara say this much to the Elder, and let the Elder say this much in the midst of the Sangha: "In the eastern districts, Blessed Buddhas arise. The eastern monks are speakers of the Dhamma, while the monks of Pāveyya are speakers of non-Dhamma."' 'Very well, friends,' replied the Venerable Uttara to the Vajjian monks of Vesālī. Having agreed, he approached the Venerable Revata and, having approached, said to him: 'Venerable sir, may the Elder say this much in the midst of the Sangha: "In the eastern districts, Blessed Buddhas arise. The eastern monks are speakers of the Dhamma, while the monks of Pāveyya are speakers of non-Dhamma."' 'Monk, you are urging me toward unrighteousness,' said the Elder, dismissing the Venerable Uttara.

Atha kho vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ uttaraṃ etadavocuṃ – “kiṃ, āvuso uttara, thero āhā”ti? “Pāpikaṃ no, āvuso, kataṃ. ‘Adhamme maṃ tvaṃ, bhikkhu, niyojesī’”ti thero maṃ paṇāmesīti. “Nanu tvaṃ, āvuso āvuso uttara (syā. kaṃ.), vuḍḍho vīsativassosī”ti? “Āmāvuso, api ca mayaṃ garunissayaṃ gaṇhāmā”ti.

Then the Vajjian monks of Vesālī said to the Venerable Uttara: “What, friend Uttara, did the Elder say?” “An evil thing has been done to us, friends. Saying, ‘You, monk, urged me in what is not the Dhamma,’ the Elder dismissed me.” “But are you not, friend, a senior of twenty years’ standing?” “Yes, friends, but we still take dependence on a teacher.”

455. Atha kho saṅgho taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinitukāmo sannipati. Atha kho āyasmā revato saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

455. Then the Sangha, wishing to settle that dispute, assembled. Then the Venerable Revata informed the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Sace mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ idha vūpasamessāma, siyāpi mūlādāyakā mūladāyakā (sī.) bhikkhū punakammāya ukkoṭeyyuṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, yatthevimaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuppannaṃ, saṅgho tatthevimaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ [T 2.0414] vūpasameyyā”ti.

“May the Sangha listen to me, Venerables. If we were to settle this dispute here, it might be that the monks who were the original accusers would agitate to re-open the matter for a formal act. If it seems fitting to the Sangha, the Sangha should settle this dispute in the very place where it arose.”

Atha kho therā bhikkhū vesāliṃ agamaṃsu – taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinitukāmā.

Then the elder monks went to Vesālī, desiring to settle that dispute.

Tena kho pana samayena sabbakāmī nāma pathabyā saṅghatthero vīsavassasatiko upasampadāya, āyasmato ānandassa saddhivihāriko, vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati. Atha kho āyasmā revato āyasmantaṃ sambhūtaṃ sāṇavāsiṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ, āvuso, yasmiṃ vihāre sabbakāmī thero viharati, taṃ vihāraṃ upagacchāmi. So tvaṃ kālasseva āyasmantaṃ sabbakāmiṃ upasaṅkamitvā imāni dasa vatthūni puccheyyāsī”ti.

At that time, one named Sabbakāmī, the Sangha's Elder on earth, of one hundred and twenty years' standing since his higher ordination, a co-resident pupil of the Venerable Ānanda, was dwelling in Vesālī. Then the Venerable Revata said this to the Venerable Sambhūta of Sāṇa: “Friend, I will go to the monastery where the Elder Sabbakāmī dwells. You should approach the Venerable Sabbakāmī early and ask him about these ten points.”

“Evaṃ bhante”ti kho āyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī āyasmato revatassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā revato, yasmiṃ vihāre sabbakāmī thero viharati, taṃ vihāraṃ upagacchi. Gabbhe āyasmato sabbakāmissa senāsanaṃ paññattaṃ hoti, gabbhappamukhe āyasmato revatassa. Atha kho āyasmā revato – ayaṃ thero [P 2.0304] mahallako na nipajjatīti – na seyyaṃ kappesi. Āyasmā sabbakāmī – ayaṃ bhikkhu āgantuko kilanto na nipajjatīti – na seyyaṃ kappesi. Atha kho āyasmā [M 0.0503] sabbakāmī rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca – “katamena tvaṃ bhūmi vihārena etarahi bahulaṃ viharasī”ti? “Mettāvihārena kho ahaṃ[V 0.0474], bhante, etarahi bahulaṃ viharāmī”ti. “Kullakavihārena kira tvaṃ bhūmi etarahi bahulaṃ viharasi[T 2.0415]. Kullakavihāro eso heso (syā.) bhūmi yadidaṃ mettā”ti. “Pubbepi me, bhante, gihibhūtassa āciṇṇā mettā. Tenāhaṃ etarahipi mettāvihārena bahulaṃ viharāmi, api ca kho mayā cirappattaṃ arahatta”nti. “Thero pana, bhante, katamena vihārena etarahi bahulaṃ viharatī”ti? “Suññatāvihārena kho ahaṃ bhūmi etarahi bahulaṃ viharāmī”ti. “Mahāpurisavihārena kira, bhante, thero etarahi bahulaṃ viharati. Mahāpurisavihāro eso, bhante, yadidaṃ suññatā”ti. “Pubbepi me bhūmi gihibhūtassa āciṇṇā suññatā. Tenāhaṃ etarahipi suññatāvihārena bahulaṃ viharāmi, api ca mayā cirappattaṃ arahatta”nti. Ayañcarahi therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ antarākathā vippakatā, athāyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī tasmiṃ anuppatto hoti. Atha kho āyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī yenāyasmā sabbakāmī tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sabbakāmiṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sambhūto sāṇavāsī āyasmantaṃ sabbakāmiṃ etadavoca – “ime, bhante, vesālikā vajjiputtakā bhikkhū vesāliyaṃ dasa vatthūni dīpenti – kappati siṅgiloṇakappo, kappati dvaṅgulakappo, kappati gāmantarakappo, kappati āvāsakappo, kappati anumatikappo, kappati āciṇṇakappo, kappati amathitakappo, kappati jaḷogiṃ[T 2.0416], pātuṃ kappati adasakaṃ nisīdanaṃ, kappati jātarūparajatanti. Therena, bhante, upajjhāyassa mūle bahudhammo ca vinayo ca pariyatto. Therassa bhante, dhammañca vinayañca paccavekkhantassa kathaṃ hoti? Ke nu kho dhammavādino – pācīnakā vā bhikkhū, pāveyyakā vā”ti? “Tayāpi kho, āvuso, upajjhāyassa mūle bahu dhammo ca vinayo ca pariyatto. Tuyhaṃ pana, āvuso, dhammañca vinayañca paccavekkhantassa kathaṃ hoti? Ke nu kho dhammavādino – pācīnakā vā bhikkhū, pāveyyakā vā”ti? “Mayhaṃ kho, bhante, dhammañca vinayañca paccavekkhantassa evaṃ hoti – adhammavādī pācīnakā bhikkhū, dhammavādī pāveyyakā bhikkhūti; api cāhaṃ na [M 0.0504] tāva diṭṭhiṃ āvi karomi, appeva nāma maṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe sammanneyyā”ti. “Mayhampi kho, āvuso, dhammañca vinayañca paccavekkhantassa evaṃ hoti [P 2.0305] – adhammavādī pācīnakā bhikkhū, dhammavādī pāveyyakā bhikkhūti; api cāhaṃ na tāva diṭṭhiṃ āvi karomi, appeva nāma maṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe sammanneyyā”ti.

“Very well, venerable sir,” the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī assented to the Venerable Revata. Then the Venerable Revata approached the monastery where the Elder Sabbakāmī was dwelling. The lodging for the Venerable Sabbakāmī was prepared in the inner chamber, and the lodging for the Venerable Revata was prepared at the entrance to the inner chamber. Then the Venerable Revata, thinking, “This elder is old and is not lying down,” did not lie down to sleep. The Venerable Sabbakāmī, thinking, “This monk is a visitor and is weary, and he is not lying down,” did not lie down to sleep. Then, having risen at dawn, the Venerable Sabbakāmī said this to the Venerable Revata: “Good sir, by which abiding do you now mostly dwell?” “Venerable sir, I now mostly dwell by the abiding of loving-kindness.” “Good sir, it seems you now mostly dwell by a lesser abiding. For this, good sir, that which is loving-kindness, is a lesser abiding.” “Venerable sir, even in the past when I was a householder, loving-kindness was practiced by me. Therefore, even now I mostly dwell by the abiding of loving-kindness. And moreover, Arahantship was attained by me long ago.” “But the Elder, venerable sir, by which abiding does he now mostly dwell?” “Good sir, I now mostly dwell by the abiding of emptiness.” “Venerable sir, it seems the Elder now mostly dwells by the abiding of a great man. For this, venerable sir, that which is emptiness, is the abiding of a great man.” “Good sir, even in the past when I was a householder, emptiness was practiced by me. Therefore, even now I mostly dwell by the abiding of emptiness. And moreover, Arahantship was attained by me long ago.” While this conversation between the elder monks was still unfinished, the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī arrived there. Then the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī approached the Venerable Sabbakāmī. Having approached and paid homage, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī said this to the Venerable Sabbakāmī: “Venerable sir, these Vajjiputtaka monks of Vesālī proclaim these ten points in Vesālī: ‘The practice of storing salt in a horn is allowable. The practice of eating after midday when the shadow is two finger-breadths long is allowable. The practice of going to another village after having finished eating is allowable. The practice of holding separate Uposathas within the same monastic boundary is allowable. The practice of carrying out an act and obtaining consent for it afterwards is allowable. The practice of following the teacher's custom is allowable. The practice of consuming milk that is not yet curd is allowable. To drink palm wine that is not yet fermented is allowable. A sitting cloth without a border is allowable. Gold and silver are allowable.’ Venerable sir, much Dhamma and Vinaya has been learned by the Elder at the feet of his preceptor. Venerable sir, for the Elder, when reflecting on the Dhamma and Vinaya, how does it seem? Who, indeed, are the speakers of the Dhamma—the monks of the East, or the monks of Pāvā?” “Friend, much Dhamma and Vinaya has also been learned by you at the feet of your preceptor. But for you, friend, when reflecting on the Dhamma and Vinaya, how does it seem? Who, indeed, are the speakers of the Dhamma—the monks of the East, or the monks of Pāvā?” “Venerable sir, for me, when reflecting on the Dhamma and Vinaya, it seems thus: the monks of the East are speakers of non-Dhamma, and the monks of Pāvā are speakers of the Dhamma. And moreover, I do not yet make my view manifest, for it may be that I will be appointed in this legal case.” “Friend, for me also, when reflecting on the Dhamma and Vinaya, it seems thus: the monks of the East are speakers of non-Dhamma, and the monks of Pāvā are speakers of the Dhamma. And moreover, I do not yet make my view manifest, for it may be that I will be appointed in this legal case.”

456. Atha kho saṅgho taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinitukāmo sannipati. Tasmiṃ kho pana adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anaggāni ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa bhāsitassa attho viññāyati. Atha kho āyasmā revato saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

456. Then the Saṅgha, wishing to settle that legal issue, assembled. While that legal issue was being settled, endless discussions arose, and the meaning of any single statement was not understood. Then the Venerable Revata informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0475] me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ [T 2.0417] imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anaggāni ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa bhāsitassa attho viññāyati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ubbāhikāya vūpasameyyā”ti. Saṅgho cattāro pācīnake bhikkhū, cattāro pāveyyake bhikkhū uccini. Pācīnakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ – āyasmantañca sabbakāmiṃ, āyasmantañca sāḷhaṃ, āyasmantañca khujjasobhitaṃ, āyasmantañca vāsabhagāmikaṃ; pāveyyakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ – āyasmantañca revataṃ, āyasmantañca sambhūtaṃ sāṇavāsiṃ, āyasmantañca yasaṃ kākaṇḍakaputtaṃ, āyasmantañca sumananti. Atha kho āyasmā revato saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to my words. While this legal issue is being settled among us, endless discussions arise, and the meaning of any single statement is not understood. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, may the Saṅgha settle this legal issue by means of referral.” The Saṅgha selected four monks from the east and four monks from Pāvā. Of the monks from the east: the Venerable Sabbakāmi, the Venerable Sāḷha, the Venerable Khujjasobhita, and the Venerable Vāsabhagāmika. Of the monks from Pāvā: the Venerable Revata, the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī, the Venerable Yasa son of Kākaṇḍaka, and the Venerable Sumana. Then the Venerable Revata informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anaggāni ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa bhāsitassa attho viññāyati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho cattāro pācīnake bhikkhū, cattāro pāveyyake bhikkhū sammanneyya ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to my words. While this legal issue is being settled among us, endless discussions arise, and the meaning of any single statement is not understood. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, may the Saṅgha appoint four monks from the east and four monks from Pāvā by means of referral to settle this legal issue. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchiyamāne anaggāni ceva bhassāni jāyanti, na cekassa bhāsitassa attho viññāyati. Saṅgho cattāro pācīnake bhikkhū, cattāro pāveyyake bhikkhū sammannati ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati catunnaṃ pācīnakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, catunnaṃ pāveyyakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sammuti, ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ[T 2.0418], so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. While this legal issue of ours is being decided, endless discussions arise, and the meaning of any single statement is not understood. The Saṅgha appoints four monks from the East and four monks from Pāvā by means of referral to settle this legal issue. To whichever venerable one the appointment of four monks from the East and four monks from Pāvā by means of referral to settle this legal issue is agreeable, let him be silent; whoever does not agree should speak.”

“Sammatā [M 0.0505] saṅghena cattāro pācīnakā bhikkhū, cattāro pāveyyakā bhikkhū, ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Four monks from the East and four monks from Pāvā have been appointed by the Saṅgha by means of referral to settle this legal issue. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Tena kho pana samayena ajito nāma bhikkhu dasavasso saṅghassa pātimokkhuddesako hoti. Atha kho saṅgho āyasmantampi ajitaṃ sammannati – therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āsanapaññāpakaṃ. Atha kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kattha nu kho mayaṃ imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyāmā”ti? Atha kho therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [P 2.0306] etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho vālikārāmo ramaṇīyo appasaddo appanigghoso. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ vālikārāme imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyāmā”ti.

Now at that time, a monk named Ajita, who had ten rains, was the Saṅgha's reciter of the Pātimokkha. Then the Saṅgha appointed the Venerable Ajita as the arranger of seats for the elder monks. Then this thought occurred to the elder monks: “Where, indeed, should we settle this legal issue?” Then this thought occurred to the elder monks: “This Vālikārāma is delightful, with little sound and little noise. What if we were to settle this legal issue in the Vālikārāma?”

457. Atha [V 0.0476] kho therā bhikkhū vālikārāmaṃ agamaṃsu – taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinitukāmā. Atha kho āyasmā revato saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

457. Then the elder monks went to the Vālikārāma, desiring to decide that legal issue. Then the Venerable Revata informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ āyasmantaṃ sabbakāmiṃ vinayaṃ puccheyya”nti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would question the Venerable Sabbakāmī concerning the Vinaya.”

Āyasmā sabbakāmī saṅghaṃ ñāpesi –

The Venerable Sabbakāmī informed the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ revatena vinayaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyya”nti.

“Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I, being questioned by Revata concerning the Vinaya, would answer.”

Atha kho āyasmā revato āyasmantaṃ sabbakāmiṃ etadavoca – “kappati, bhante, siṅgiloṇakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, siṅgiloṇakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, siṅginā loṇaṃ pariharituṃ – yattha aloṇakaṃ bhavissati [T 2.0419] tattha paribhuñjissāmā”ti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti. pāci. 254 ādayo “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Sāvatthiyaṃ, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Sannidhikārakabhojane pācittiya”nti.

Then the Venerable Revata said this to the Venerable Sabbakāmī: “Venerable Sir, is the salt-horn practice allowable?” “What, friend, is that salt-horn practice?” “Venerable Sir, is it allowable to carry salt in a horn, having considered, ‘Where there is no salt, there I will consume it’?” “No, friend, it is not allowable.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Sāvatthī, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense is incurred?” “A pācittiya offense for consuming what has been stored.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This first matter has been decided by the Saṅgha. For this reason also, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher's instruction. I cast this first voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, dvaṅgulakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, dvaṅgulakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, dvaṅgulāya chāyāya vītivattāya vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjitu”nti[M 0.0506]? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti pāci. 245. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Rājagahe, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? Vikālabhojane pācittiya”nti.

“Venerable Sir, is the two-finger-breadth practice allowable?” “What, friend, is that two-finger-breadth practice?” “Venerable Sir, is it allowable to consume food at the wrong time when the shadow has passed by two finger-breadths?” “No, friend, it is not allowable.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Rājagaha, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense is incurred?” “A pācittiya offense for eating at the wrong time.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This second matter has been decided by the Saṅgha. For this reason also, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher's instruction. I cast this second voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, gāmantarakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, gāmantarakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante – idāni gāmantaraṃ gamissāmīti – bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ bhojanaṃ [V 0.0477] bhuñjitu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti pāci. 234. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Sāvatthiyaṃ, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Anatirittabhojane pācittiya”nti.

“Venerable Sir, is the going-to-another-village practice allowable?” “What, friend, is that going-to-another-village practice?” “Venerable Sir, is it allowable for one who has eaten and has been formally satisfied to consume food that has not been made a leftover, thinking, ‘Now I will go to another village’?” “No, friend, it is not allowable.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Sāvatthī, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense is incurred?” “A pācittiya offense for eating food that has not been made a leftover.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This third matter has been decided by the Saṅgha. For this reason also, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher's instruction. I cast this third voting ticket.”

“Kappati[T 2.0420], bhante, āvāsakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, āvāsakappo”ti? “Kappati bhante, sambahulā āvāsā samānasīmā nānuposathaṃ kātu”nti. “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti mahāva. 141 ādayo. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Rājagahe, uposathasaṃyutte”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Vinayātisāre dukkaṭa”nti.

“Venerable sir, is the procedure regarding residences permissible?” “What, friend, is this procedure regarding residences?” “Venerable sir, is it permissible for many residences that have a common boundary to perform the Uposatha separately?” “No, friend, it is not permissible.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Rājagaha, in the chapter connected with the Uposatha.” “What offense does one incur?” “One incurs a dukkaṭa offense for transgressing the Vinaya.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ catutthaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ catutthaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This fourth matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this fourth voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, anumatikappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, anumatikappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, vaggena saṅghena kammaṃ kātuṃ – āgate bhikkhū anumānessāmā”ti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti [P 2.0307] mahāva. 383 ādayo. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Campeyyake, vinayavatthusmi”nti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Vinayātisāre dukkaṭa”nti.

“Venerable sir, is the procedure of consent permissible?” “What, friend, is this procedure of consent?” “Venerable sir, is it permissible for an incomplete Sangha to perform a formal act, thinking, ‘We will obtain the consent of the monks when they have arrived’?” “No, friend, it is not permissible.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In the Campeyyaka chapter, concerning a Vinaya matter.” “What offense does one incur?” “One incurs a dukkaṭa offense for transgressing the Vinaya.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This fifth matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this fifth voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, āciṇṇakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, āciṇṇakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante – idaṃ me upajjhāyena ajjhāciṇṇaṃ, idaṃ me ācariyena [M 0.0507] ajjhāciṇṇaṃ – taṃ ajjhācaritu”nti? “Āciṇṇakappo kho, āvuso, ekacco kappati, ekacco na kappatī”ti.

“Venerable sir, is the practice based on custom permissible?” “What, friend, is this practice based on custom?” “Venerable sir, is it permissible to practice that which was habitually practiced by my preceptor and that which was habitually practiced by my teacher?” “Friend, some practices based on custom are permissible, and some are not permissible.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ[T 2.0421]. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This sixth matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this sixth voting ticket.”

“Kappati[V 0.0478], bhante, amathitakappo”ti? “Ko so, āvuso, amathitakappo”ti? “Kappati, bhante, yaṃ taṃ khīraṃ khīrabhāvaṃ vijahitaṃ, asampattaṃ dadhibhāvaṃ, taṃ bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ pātu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti pāci. 234. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Sāvatthiyaṃ, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Anatirittabhojane pācittiya”nti.

“Venerable sir, is the procedure regarding unstirred milk permissible?” “What, friend, is this procedure regarding unstirred milk?” “Venerable sir, is it permissible for one who has finished eating and has declined further food to drink, without it having been made a leftover, that milk which has left its state as milk but has not yet reached the state of curd?” “No, friend, it is not permissible.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Sāvatthī, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense does one incur?” “One incurs a pācittiya offense for eating what has not been made a leftover.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ sattamaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ sattamaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This seventh matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this seventh voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, jaḷogiṃ pātu”nti? “Kā sā, āvuso, jaḷogī”ti? “Kappati, bhante, yā sā surā āsutā asampattā majjabhāvaṃ, sā pātu”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti pāci. 326. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Kosambiyaṃ, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti. “Surāmerayapāne pācittiya”nti.

“Venerable sir, is it permissible to drink jaḷogī?” “What, friend, is jaḷogī?” “Venerable sir, is it permissible to drink that liquor which has been brewed but has not yet reached the state of an intoxicant?” “No, friend, it is not permissible.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Kosambī, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense does one incur?” “One incurs a pācittiya offense for drinking intoxicants.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This eighth matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this eighth voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, adasakaṃ nisīdana”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti pāci. 531 ādayo. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti? “Sāvatthiyaṃ, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Chedanake pācittiya”nti.

“Venerable sir, is a sitting-cloth without a border permissible?” “No, friend, it is not permissible.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Sāvatthī, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense does one incur?” “One incurs a pācittiya offense involving cutting.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ navamaṃ vatthu [T 2.0422] saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ navamaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi”.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This ninth matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this ninth voting ticket.”

“Kappati, bhante, jātarūparajata”nti? “Nāvuso, kappatī”ti pārā. 580 ādayo. “Kattha paṭikkhitta”nti. “Rājagahe, suttavibhaṅge”ti. “Kiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇe pācittiya”nti.

“Venerable sir, is gold and silver permissible?” “No, friend, it is not permissible.” “Where was it prohibited?” “In Rājagaha, in the Suttavibhaṅga.” “What offense does one incur?” “One incurs a nissaggiya pācittiya offense for accepting gold and silver.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0508] me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ dasamaṃ vatthu saṅghena vinicchitaṃ. Itipidaṃ vatthu uddhammaṃ, ubbinayaṃ, apagatasatthusāsanaṃ. Idaṃ dasamaṃ salākaṃ nikkhipāmi.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This tenth matter has been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, this matter is not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and is devoid of the Teacher’s instruction. I cast this tenth voting ticket.”

“Suṇātu [V 0.0479] me, bhante, saṅgho. Imāni dasa vatthūni saṅghena vinicchitāni. Itipimāni dasavatthūni uddhammāni, ubbinayāni, apagatasatthusāsanānī”ti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. These ten matters have been decided by the Sangha. For this reason, these matters are not the Dhamma, not the Vinaya, and are devoid of the Teacher’s instruction.”

458. “Nihatametaṃ, āvuso, adhikaraṇaṃ, santaṃ vūpasantaṃ suvūpasantaṃ. Api ca maṃ tvaṃ, āvuso, saṅghamajjhepi imāni dasa vatthūni puccheyyāsi – tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ saññattiyā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā revato āyasmantaṃ sabbakāmiṃ saṅghamajjhepi imāni dasa vatthūni pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā sabbakāmī vissajjesi. Imāya kho pana vinayasaṅgītiyā satta bhikkhusatāni anūnāni anadhikāni ahesuṃ, tasmāyaṃ vinayasaṅgīti “sattasatikā”ti vuccatīti.

458. “Friends, this legal question has been settled, pacified, especially pacified, well and especially pacified. Nevertheless, friend, you should ask me about these ten matters even in the midst of the Sangha, so that those monks may be made to understand.” Then the Venerable Revata asked the Venerable Sabbakāmī about these ten matters even in the midst of the Sangha. Being asked again and again, the Venerable Sabbakāmī answered. At this recital of the Vinaya, there were seven hundred arahant monks, no fewer and no more. Therefore, this recital of the Vinaya is called the ‘Sattasatikā’.”

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The second recitation section is finished.

Sattasatikakkhandhako dvādasamo.

The twelfth chapter, the Sattasatikakkhandhaka, is finished.

Imamhi [P 2.0308] khandhake vatthū pañcavīsati.

In this chapter, there are twenty-five matters.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Dasa [T 2.0423] vatthūni pūretvā, kammaṃ dūtena pāvisi;

Cattāro puna rūpañca, kosambi ca pāveyyako.

The ten matters having been fulfilled, the formal act entered by means of a messenger; four, and again four, gold and silver, Kosambī, and the monk from Pāvā.

Maggo soreyyaṃ saṅkassaṃ, kaṇṇakujjaṃ udumbaraṃ;

Sahajāti ca majjhesi, assosi kaṃ nu kho mayaṃ.

The road, Soreyya, Saṅkassa, Kaṇṇakujja, Udumbara, and Sahajāti; the request, one heard: “Whom indeed do we…?”

Pattanāvāya ujjavi, rahosi upanāmayaṃ dūratopi udapādi (ka.);

Garu dāruṇaṃ (syā.) saṅgho ca vesāliṃ, mettā saṅgho ubbāhikāti.

The bowl by boat went upstream; in secret bringing near; the harsh matter, the Sangha, and Vesālī; loving-kindness, the Sangha, and the selection committee.

Sattasatikakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Chapter of the Seven Hundred is finished.

Cūḷavaggo cullavaggo (sī.) niṭṭhito.

The Cūḷavagga is finished.

Cūḷavaggapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Cūḷavagga is finished.
